entries.zh: 長興中，以與明宗有舊，常貯入相之意，從容謂時相曰：「唐祚中興，宜敦敘宗室，才高者合居相位。
entries.en: In Changxing, with old ties to Mingzong, he often hoped for the chancellorship and told the chancellors, "The Tang restoration should honor the clan; the able should hold the highest office.
entries.literal: In Changxing, because of old ties with Mingzong, he often harbored intent to enter the chancellorship and casually told the chancellors: "The Tang restoration should honor the imperial clan; the talented ought to hold the highest office.

entries.zh: 仆雖不才，曾事莊宗霸府，見今上於藩邸時。
entries.en: Though I lack talent, I served Zhuangzong's headquarters and knew the present emperor in his princely days.
entries.literal: Though I am without talent, I once served Zhuangzong's hegemonic headquarters and saw the present emperor in his princely residence.

entries.zh: 家代重侯累相，靖安李氏，不在諸族之下；
entries.en: For generations my house produced marquises and chancellors; the Jing'an Li are not beneath other clans;
entries.literal: For generations my house produced heavy marquises and chancellors; the Jing'an Li family is not beneath the other clans;

entries.zh: 論才較藝，何讓眾人。
entries.en: in talent and skill, why should I yield to others?
entries.literal: comparing talent and skill, why yield to others.

entries.zh: 久置仆於朝行，諸君安乎？」
entries.en: Keeping me so long in routine posts—are you at ease?"
entries.literal: Long placing me in court ranks—are you gentlemen at ease?"

entries.zh: 馮道、趙鳳每怒其僭。
entries.en: Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were angered each time by his presumption.
entries.literal: Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were each time angered by his presumption.

entries.zh: 有頃，鏻因淮南細人言事，乃謂樞密使安重誨曰：「偽吳欲歸國久矣，若朝廷先遣使諭之，則旋踵而至矣。」
entries.en: Soon, on a Huainan informer's report, he told An Chonghui, "Wu has long wished to submit; if the court sends an envoy, they will come at once."
entries.literal: Before long, because of a petty man from Huainan reporting affairs, he told Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui: "False Wu has long wished to return to the state; if the court first sends an envoy to instruct them, they will come in a trice."

entries.zh: 重誨然之，以玉帶與細人，令往淮南為信，久而不反，由是出鏻為兗州行軍司馬。
entries.en: Chonghui agreed and gave the man a jade belt as envoy to Huainan; he never returned; Lin was sent out as Yan prefecture marching adjutant.
entries.literal: Chonghui agreed, gave the petty man a jade belt to go to Huainan as envoy; he did not return for a long time; on that account Lin was sent out as marching adjutant of Yan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 得代歸闕，復為戶部尚書，尋轉兵部尚書，有頃兼判太常卿事。
entries.en: Returning to court he was again minister of revenue, soon minister of war, and before long acting director of imperial sacrifices.
entries.literal: When his replacement returned to court, he was again minister of revenue, soon transferred to minister of war, and before long concurrently acted as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 嘗權典選部，銓綜失序，物論非之。
entries.en: He once ran personnel selection; his judgments were disorderly and opinion condemned him.
entries.literal: He once held selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel; his evaluation was disorderly and public opinion condemned it.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，守太子少保。
entries.en: In Jin's Tianfu era he was junior tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he held the post of junior tutor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 開運中，遷太子太保。
entries.en: In Kaiyun he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In Kaiyun he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 高祖至闕，授守司徒，數月而卒，年八十八。
entries.en: When Gaozu reached court he was made acting minister of works; he died several months later at eighty-eight.
entries.literal: When the Gaozu reached court he was appointed acting Minister of Works; several months later he died at age eighty-eight.

entries.zh: 詔贈太傅。
entries.en: An edict posthumously made him grand tutor.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 李崧，深州饒陽人。
entries.en: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父舜卿，本州錄事參軍。
entries.en: His father Shunqing had been recording officer and military adjutant of that prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Shunqing served as recording officer and military adjutant of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 崧幼而聰敏，十餘歲為文，家人奇之。
entries.en: From childhood Song was quick-witted; by his mid-teens he was already writing essays, and his family marveled at him.
entries.literal: Song was clever from childhood; in his teens he could compose essays, and his family regarded him as extraordinary.

entries.zh: 弱冠，本府署為參軍。
entries.en: At twenty he took a post as military adjutant in the local prefectural office.
entries.literal: At the age of twenty he was appointed military adjutant in the prefectural office.

entries.zh: 其父嘗謂宗人李鏻曰：「大醜生處，形奇氣異，前途應不居徒勞之地，賴吾兄誨激之。」
entries.en: His father once told his kinsman Li Lin, "Where Dachou was born, the boy's looks were odd and his spirit unlike others; he is not meant to waste his life in drudgery—it will be up to my elder brother to teach and urge him on."
entries.literal: His father once said to his clansman Li Lin: "Where Dachou was born, his form was strange and his spirit unusual; his future should not lie in vain toil—it depends on my elder brother to instruct and spur him."

entries.zh: 大醜即崧之小字也。
entries.en: Dachou was Song's childhood name.
entries.literal: Dachou was Song's childhood name.

entries.zh: 同光初，魏王繼岌為興聖宮使，兼領鎮州節鉞，崧以參軍從事。
entries.en: Early in the Tongguang reign, Prince of Wei Jiji served as director of the Xingsheng Palace while also holding the military commission of Zhen Prefecture, and Song went with him as adjutant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era, Prince of Wei Jiji was Director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the military commission of Zhen Prefecture; Song accompanied him as adjutant.

entries.zh: 時推官李蕘掌書，崧見其起草不工，密謂掌事呂柔曰：「令公皇子，天下瞻望，至於尺牘往來，章表論列，稍須文理合宜。
entries.en: The judicial officer Li Rao then handled correspondence, and Song, finding his drafts clumsy, quietly told the steward Lü Rou, "His Lordship is an imperial prince, the hope of the realm; whatever letters and memorials go out should at least be literate and apt.
entries.literal: At the time the judicial officer Li Rao managed documents; Song saw that his drafting was unskilled and secretly told the steward Lü Rou: "His Lordship is an imperial prince, watched by all under Heaven; as for letters exchanged and memorials submitted, the prose ought at least to be literate and fitting.

entries.zh: 李侍御起草，未能盡善。」
entries.en: Censor Li's drafts are not quite up to the mark."
entries.literal: Censor Li's drafts are not fully adequate."

entries.zh: 呂曰：「公試代為之。」
entries.en: Lü replied, "Why don't you try drafting them yourself?"
entries.literal: Lü said: "Sir, try drafting them yourself."

entries.zh: 呂得崧所作，示盧質、馮道，皆稱之。
entries.en: Lü took what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao, and both praised it.
entries.literal: Lü obtained what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao; both praised it.

entries.zh: 繇是擢為興聖宮巡官，獨掌奏記。
entries.en: On that account he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and given sole charge of memorials and reports.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and alone managed memorials and reports.

entries.zh: 莊宗入洛，授太常寺協律郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Song was made harmonizing officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Song was appointed harmonizing officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 王師伐蜀，繼岌為都統，以崧掌書記。
entries.en: When the imperial forces marched against Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song served as his chief secretary.
entries.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song served as chief secretary.

entries.zh: 蜀平，樞密使郭崇韜為宦官誣構，繼岌遂殺崇韜父子，外尚未知。
entries.en: After Shu fell, eunuchs framed Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Chongtao, and Jiji killed Chongtao and his son; the news had not yet spread beyond their camp.
entries.literal: After Shu was pacified, the eunuchs slandered the Commissioner of Military Affairs Guo Chongtao, and Jiji thereupon killed Chongtao and his son; those outside still did not know.

entries.zh: 崧白繼岌曰：「王何為作此危事？
entries.en: Song said to Jiji, "Your Highness, why do this reckless thing?
entries.literal: Song told Jiji: "Your Highness, why commit this perilous act?

entries.zh: 至於不容崇韜，至洛誅之未晚。
entries.en: If Chongtao cannot be tolerated, you could still put him to death after you reach Luoyang.
entries.literal: As for not tolerating Chongtao, it would not be too late to execute him after reaching Luoyang.

entries.zh: 今懸軍五千里，無咫尺書詔，便殺重臣，非謀也。」
entries.en: Your army is five thousand li from home with no word from the throne, yet you have killed a great minister—that is no sound policy."
entries.literal: Now the army is isolated five thousand li away, without the slightest imperial edict, yet a great minister is killed—this is not sound planning."

entries.zh: 繼岌曰：「吾亦悔之。」
entries.en: Jiji said, "I regret it as well."
entries.literal: Jiji said: "I too regret it."

entries.zh: 崧召書吏三四人，登樓去梯，取黃紙矯寫詔書，倒使都統印發之。
entries.en: Song called three or four clerks, had them climb a tower and pull up the ladder, forged an edict on yellow paper, and had it issued with the overall commander's seal impressed upside down.
entries.literal: Song summoned three or four clerks, went up a tower and removed the ladder, took yellow paper and forged an edict, and had the overall commander's seal impressed upside down to issue it.

entries.zh: 翌日，告諸軍，軍情稍定。
entries.en: The next day he announced it to the troops, and army morale gradually settled.
entries.literal: The next day he announced it to the armies, and morale gradually steadied.

entries.zh: 及自蜀還，明宗革命，任圜以宰相判三司，用崧為鹽鐵推官，賜緋。
entries.en: After the return from Shu, Emperor Mingzong took the throne; Ren Huan, serving as chancellor in charge of the Three Departments, appointed Song salt-and-iron investigating officer and gave him crimson robes.
entries.literal: When he returned from Shu, Emperor Mingzong seized power; Ren Huan, as chancellor overseeing the Three Departments, employed Song as salt and iron investigating officer and granted him crimson robes.

entries.zh: 丁內艱，歸鄉里。
entries.en: When his mother died he went into mourning and returned home.
entries.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and returned to his home district.

entries.zh: 服闋，鎮帥範延光奏署掌書記。
entries.en: After mourning he was appointed chief secretary on Fan Yanguang's recommendation as military governor.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, the military governor Fan Yanguang memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.

entries.zh: 延光為樞密使，拜拾遺，直樞密院，遷補闕、起居郎、尚書郎，充職如故。
entries.en: When Yanguang became military affairs commissioner, Song was made remonstrance official and attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs; he rose through censor, recorder of the ruler's movements, and secretariat posts while keeping his original duties.
entries.literal: When Yanguang became Commissioner of Military Affairs, Song was appointed remonstrance official and served in the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was promoted to censor, recorder of the ruler's movements, and secretary in the Secretariat, while continuing in his duties as before.

entries.zh: 長興末，改翰林學士。
entries.en: Near the end of the Changxing reign he was made a Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: At the end of the Changxing era he was made Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 清泰初，拜端明殿學士、戶部侍郎。
entries.en: Early in the Qingtai reign he was made Duanming Hall academician and vice minister of revenue.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue.

entries.zh: 高祖車駕至闕，以重威為宋州節度使，加守太尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu's court reached the capital, Chongwei was appointed military governor of Songzhou and acting Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu's imperial carriage reached the capital, Chongwei was made military governor of Song Prefecture and additionally acting Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 重威懼，閉城拒命，詔高行周率兵攻討，重威遣其子宏遂等告急於鎮州州麻答，乞師救援，旦以宏遂為質，麻答遣蕃將楊兗赴之。
entries.en: Terrified, Chongwei shut the gates and defied the court. Gao Xingzhou was ordered to attack. Chongwei sent his son Hongsui to beg Maduo, governor of Zhenzhou, for relief, offering Hongsui as hostage that same day. Maduo dispatched the tribal general Yang Yan.
entries.literal: Chongwei was afraid, shut the city and refused orders. An edict ordered Gao Xingzhou to lead troops to attack. Chongwei sent his son Hongsui and others to plead urgently with Maduo, military governor of Zhen Prefecture, begging for rescue troops and offering Hongsui as hostage that very morning. Maduo sent the tribal general Yang Yan to go to his aid.

entries.zh: 未幾，鎮州軍逐滿達勒，楊兗至洺州而回。
entries.en: Before long the Zhenzhou garrison expelled Manduole, and Yang Yan turned back when he reached Mozhou.
entries.literal: Before long the army of Zhen Prefecture drove out Manduole; Yang Yan reached Mo Prefecture and turned back.

entries.zh: 十月，高祖親征，車駕至鄴城之下，遣給事中陳觀等賫詔入城，許其歸命，重威不納。
entries.en: In the tenth month Gaozu marched in person. When the court reached Yecheng he sent Supervising Secretary Chen Guan with an edict offering mercy if Chongwei submitted. Chongwei refused.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Emperor Gaozu personally campaigned; the imperial carriage reached below the walls of Yecheng. He sent Supervising Secretary Chen Guan and others to carry an edict into the city, promising acceptance of surrender, but Chongwei would not receive it.

entries.zh: 數日，高祖親率諸軍攻其壘，不克，王師傷夷者萬餘人。
entries.en: Days later Gaozu led the assault himself but failed to break the defenses. Imperial casualties exceeded ten thousand.
entries.literal: Several days later Gaozu personally led the armies to assault his fortifications but could not take them; the imperial forces had more than ten thousand killed and wounded.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·杜漢徽傳》云：從高行周討杜重威於鄴城，屢為流矢所中，身被重創，猶力戰，觀者壯之。）〉
entries.en: (History of Song, biography of Du Hanhui: Serving under Gao Xingzhou against Du Chongwei at Yecheng, he was hit again and again by stray arrows and badly wounded, yet kept fighting until onlookers marveled at his courage.)〉
entries.literal: (History of Song, biography of Du Hanhui: He followed Gao Xingzhou in attacking Du Chongwei at Yecheng, was repeatedly struck by stray arrows, bore grave wounds, yet still fought fiercely—onlookers admired his valor.)〉

entries.zh: 高祖駐軍數旬，城中糧盡，屑麹餅以給軍士，吏民逾壘而出者甚眾，皆無人色。
entries.en: Gaozu besieged the city for weeks until provisions ran out and the garrison lived on bran cakes. Officials and townspeople slipped over the walls in crowds, their faces gray with hunger.
entries.literal: Gaozu encamped for several weeks; grain in the city was exhausted and bran cakes were issued to feed the soldiers. Many officials and people climbed over the walls to get out, all without human color in their faces.

entries.zh: 至是，重威牙將詣行宮請降，復遣節度判官王敏奉表請罪，賜優詔敦勉，許其如初。
entries.en: At last a junior officer came to Gaozu's camp to offer surrender, and Chongwei sent circuit judge Wang Min with a memorial begging pardon. An edict of clemency arrived, promising him his former standing.
entries.literal: At this point Chongwei's junior officer went to the temporary palace to request surrender; he again sent circuit judge Wang Min with a memorial begging pardon. A gracious edict was bestowed encouraging him, and he was permitted to return to his former status.

entries.zh: 重威即遣其子宏遂、妻石氏出候高祖，重威繼踵出降，素服俟罪，復其衣冠，賜見，即日制授檢校太師、守太傅、兼中書令。
entries.en: Chongwei sent his son Hongsui and Lady Shi out to greet Gaozu, then followed to surrender in plain dress. Restored to court dress, he was received that same day and appointed acting Grand Preceptor, acting Grand Tutor, and Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Chongwei at once sent his son Hongsui and his wife Lady Shi out to wait upon Gaozu; Chongwei followed close behind to surrender. In plain dress he awaited judgment, then resumed his robes and cap and was granted audience. That same day he was appointed by decree acting Grand Preceptor, acting Grand Tutor, and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 鄴城士庶，殍殕者十之六七。
entries.en: Six or seven people in ten among Yecheng's populace had starved to death.
entries.literal: Among the people of Yecheng, six or seven in ten died of starvation.

entries.zh: 先是，契丹遣幽州指揮使張璉，以部下軍二千餘人屯鄴，時亦有燕軍一千五百人在京師，會高祖至闕，有上變者，言燕軍謀亂，盡誅於繁臺之下，咸稱其冤。
entries.en: Earlier the Khitan had posted Zhang Lian of Youzhou at Ye with more than two thousand men, while another fifteen hundred Yan troops were in the capital. When Gaozu entered the capital, an informer claimed the Yan garrison meant to rebel, and every man was executed below Fantai—a killing widely called a miscarriage of justice.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Khitan had sent Zhang Lian, commander of You Prefecture, with more than two thousand troops under his command to garrison Ye; at the time there were also fifteen hundred Yan troops in the capital. When Gaozu reached the capital, someone reported a plot of rebellion among the Yan troops, and they were all executed below Fantai—all said it was unjust.

entries.zh: 有逃奔於鄴者，備言其事，故張璉等懼死，與重威膠固守城，略無叛誌。
entries.en: Fugitives reached Ye with the full story, and Zhang Lian and his men, fearing the same fate, clung to Chongwei and held the walls with no thought of treason—only terror.
entries.literal: Some who had fled to Ye told the whole story in detail; therefore Zhang Lian and the others, fearing death, clung to Chongwei and held the city fast, with not the slightest thought of rebellion.

entries.zh: 高祖亦悔其前失，累令宣諭，許以不死。
entries.en: Gaozu too regretted the massacre and repeatedly proclaimed that they would not be executed.
entries.literal: Gaozu also regretted his earlier mistake and repeatedly sent proclamations assuring them they would not be put to death.

entries.zh: 璉等於城上揚言曰：「繁臺之誅，燕軍何罪？
entries.en: From the walls Zhang Lian shouted, "What crime did the Yan troops commit at Fantai?
entries.literal: Zhang Lian and the others shouted from atop the wall, "At the Fantai slaughter, what crime had the Yan troops committed?

entries.zh: 既無生理，以死為期。」
entries.en: With no hope of life left, we choose death as our end."
entries.literal: Having no hope of life, we take death as our term."

entries.zh: 璉一軍在圍中，重威推食解衣，盡力姑息。
entries.en: Trapped in the siege, Zhang Lian's men were fed from Chongwei's own stores and clothed from his wardrobe as he tried every means to keep them loyal.
entries.literal: Zhang Lian's whole army was within the siege; Chongwei shared his food and gave up his clothing, doing all he could to soothe them.

entries.zh: 燕軍驕悍，憑陵吏民，子女金帛，公行豪奪。
entries.en: The Yan soldiers were brutal and overbearing, robbing officials and commoners alike of daughters, gold, and silk without restraint.
entries.literal: The Yan troops were arrogant and fierce; they bullied officials and people, openly seizing daughters, silk, and gold by force.

entries.zh: 及重威請命，璉等邀朝廷信誓，詔許璉等卻歸本土。
entries.en: When Chongwei sued for mercy, Zhang Lian demanded a sworn promise from the throne, and an edict allowed him and his men to return home.
entries.literal: When Chongwei begged to submit, Zhang Lian and the others demanded a sworn pledge from the court; an edict permitted Zhang Lian and the others to return to their native lands.

entries.zh: 及出降，盡誅璉等將數十人，其什長已下放歸幽州，將出漢境，剽略而去。
entries.en: After the surrender dozens of Zhang Lian's officers were put to death. Squad leaders already sent back toward Youzhou looted the countryside as soon as they crossed out of Han territory.
entries.literal: When they came out to surrender, Zhang Lian and several dozen of his officers were all executed. Their squad leaders had already been sent down and returned to You Prefecture; as they were about to leave Han territory they plundered and departed.

entries.zh: 高祖遣三司使王章、樞密副使郭威，錄重威部下將吏盡誅之，籍其財產與重威私帑，分給將士。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Wang Zhang of the Three Departments and Deputy Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Wei to list every officer under Chongwei, execute them, seize their goods together with Chongwei's private hoard, and divide the spoils among the troops.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Commissioner of the Three Departments Wang Zhang and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Guo Wei to register Chongwei's subordinate officers and execute them all, seizing their property together with Chongwei's private treasury and distributing it among the troops.

entries.zh: 車駕還宮，高祖不豫，既而大漸。
entries.en: After the court returned to the palace Gaozu fell ill and soon lay dying.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage returned to the palace; Gaozu was unwell, and soon entered his final decline.

entries.zh: 顧命之際，謂近臣將佐曰：「善防重威。」
entries.en: On his deathbed he told his closest ministers and generals, "Guard yourselves against Chongwei."
entries.literal: At the moment of his final charge he said to his close ministers and military aides, "Take good care to guard against Chongwei."

entries.zh: 帝崩，遂收重威，重威子宏璋、宏璉、宏傑誅之。
entries.en: When the emperor died, Chongwei was arrested and executed together with his sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongjie.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, Chongwei was seized, and his sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongjie were executed with him.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「杜重威猶貯禍心，未悛逆節，梟音不改，虺性難馴。
entries.en: The edict read: "Du Chongwei still nurses treason in his heart and has not repented his rebellion. His nature remains that of an owl and a viper, impossible to tame.
entries.literal: An edict said, "Du Chongwei still harbors a treacherous heart and has not repented his rebellious conduct; his owl-like cry has not changed, his viper nature is hard to tame.

entries.zh: 昨朕小有不安，罷朝數日，而重威父子潛肆兇言，怨謗大朝，扇惑小輩；
entries.en: When I was briefly unwell and court was suspended for several days, Chongwei and his sons secretly spread vicious talk, reviling the throne and stirring up lesser men;
entries.literal: Yesterday We were slightly unwell and suspended court for several days, yet Chongwei father and son secretly uttered murderous words, slandering the great court and inciting lesser men;

entries.zh: 今則顯有陳告，備驗奸期。
entries.en: informers have now come forward with proof of their plot.
entries.literal: now there are open denunciations, fully verifying their treacherous designs.

entries.zh: 既負深恩，須置極法，其杜重威父子並處斬。
entries.en: Having betrayed deep favor, they must suffer the utmost penalty: Du Chongwei and his sons are all to be executed.
entries.literal: Having betrayed deep grace, they must receive the extreme penalty: Du Chongwei father and son are all to be beheaded.

entries.zh: 所有晉朝公主及外親族，一切如常，仍與供給。」
entries.en: The princesses of Later Jin and all related kin shall be treated as before and continue to receive support."
entries.literal: As for the princesses of the Jin dynasty and all collateral kin, everything is to remain as before, and provisions are still to be supplied."

entries.zh: 重威父子已誅，陳屍於通衢，都人聚觀者詬罵蹴擊，軍吏不能禁，屍首狼籍，斯須而盡。
entries.en: After the executions their bodies were displayed in the street. Crowds cursed them, kicked them, and tore them apart before the guards could stop it—the corpses vanished in moments.
entries.literal: After Chongwei father and son were executed, their corpses were displayed in the main thoroughfare. The people of the capital who gathered to watch cursed, kicked, and struck them; military officers could not restrain them, and the corpses were torn to pieces in an instant.

entries.zh: 李守貞，河陽人也。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen was a native of Heyang.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen was a man of Heyang.

entries.zh: 少桀黠落魄，事本部為牙將。
entries.en: In his youth he was sharp, unruly, and down on his luck, serving his command as a junior officer.
entries.literal: In youth he was fierce, cunning, and down on his luck; he served his command as a junior officer.

entries.zh: 晉高祖鎮河陽，用為典客，後移數鎮，皆從之。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin governed Heyang he made Shouzhen his protocol officer, and Shouzhen followed him through every subsequent posting.
entries.literal: When Jin's Emperor Gaozu governed Heyang he employed him as protocol officer; afterward, as he moved through several commands, Shouzhen followed him to each.

entries.zh: 及即位，累遷至客省使。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne Shouzhen rose steadily to commissioner of the guest bureau.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, Shouzhen was repeatedly promoted until he became commissioner of the guest bureau.

entries.zh: 天福中，李金全以安州叛，淮夷入寇，晉高祖命馬全節討之，守貞監護其軍，賊平，守貞為宣徽使。
entries.en: During Tianfu, Li Jinquan rebelled at Anzhou and Huai tribes raided the borders. Gaozu sent Ma Quanjie to suppress them with Shouzhen as army supervisor. After victory Shouzhen became palace secretariat commissioner.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era Li Jinquan rebelled with An Prefecture and the Huai tribes invaded; Jin's Emperor Gaozu ordered Ma Quanjie to suppress them. Shouzhen supervised the army; when the rebels were pacified he became commissioner of the palace secretariat.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，授滑州節度兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使，未幾，改侍衛都虞候。
entries.en: When the Young Emperor came to the throne he was made military governor of Huazhou and commander of the palace guard cavalry, then soon afterward deputy commander of the palace guard.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made military governor of Hua Prefecture and concurrently commander of the palace guard cavalry; before long he was changed to deputy commander of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 開運元年春，敵眾犯澶、魏，少帝幸澶州，契丹遣將麻答以奇兵由鄆州馬家口濟河，立柵於東岸，守貞率師自澶州馳赴之。
entries.en: In the spring of the first Kaiyun year the enemy struck Chan and Wei, and the Young Emperor went to Chanzhou in person. The Khitan general Maduo crossed at Majiakou in Yunzhou with a flanking force and fortified the east bank. Shouzhen raced from Chanzhou to meet him.
entries.literal: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun the enemy masses invaded Chan and Wei; the Young Emperor went in person to Chan Prefecture. The Khitan sent the general Maduo with a surprise force to cross the river at Majiakou in Yun Prefecture and erect palisades on the east bank. Shouzhen led troops in a rush from Chan Prefecture to meet them.

entries.zh: 契丹大敗，溺死者數千人，獲馬數百匹，偏裨七十餘人。
entries.en: The Khitan were routed. Several thousand drowned, hundreds of horses were captured, and more than seventy officers were taken.
entries.literal: The Khitan suffered a great defeat; several thousand drowned, several hundred horses were captured, and more than seventy officers were taken.

entries.zh: 有頃，敵退。
entries.en: Before long the enemy withdrew.
entries.literal: Before long the enemy withdrew.

entries.zh: 晉少帝還京，以守貞為兗州節度使，依前侍衛都虞候。
entries.en: The Young Emperor returned to the capital and appointed Shouzhen military governor of Yanzhou while keeping him as deputy commander of the palace guard.
entries.literal: Jin's Young Emperor returned to the capital and made Shouzhen military governor of Yan Prefecture while retaining him as before as deputy commander of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 五月，以守貞為青州行營都部署，率兵二萬東討楊光遠，命符彥卿為副。
entries.en: In the fifth month he was made overall commander of the eastern expedition with twenty thousand troops against Yang Guangyuan, and Fu Yanqing was named his deputy.
entries.literal: In the fifth month he was made overall commander of the Qing Prefecture campaign headquarters, leading twenty thousand troops east to attack Yang Guangyuan, with Fu Yanqing appointed as his deputy.

entries.zh: 十一月，光遠子承勛等乞降，守貞入城，害光遠於別第。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Guangyuan's son Chengxun sued for surrender. Shouzhen entered the city and killed Guangyuan in his private quarters.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Yang Guangyuan's son Chengxun and others begged to surrender; Shouzhen entered the city and killed Guangyuan at a separate residence.

entries.zh: 光遠有孔目官吏宋顏者，盡以光遠財寶、名姬、善馬告於守貞，得之置於帳下。
entries.en: A clerk named Song Yan revealed all of Guangyuan's treasure, celebrated concubines, and fine horses to Shouzhen, who seized them for his own camp.
entries.literal: Guangyuan had a clerical officer named Song Yan who reported all of Guangyuan's treasures, famous beauties, and fine horses to Shouzhen; obtaining them, Shouzhen placed them in his own camp.

entries.zh: 近例，官軍克復城隍，必降德音，洗滌瑕穢，時樞密使桑維翰以光遠同惡數十輩潛竄未出，搜索甚急，故制書久不下。
entries.en: By custom, recaptured cities received an amnesty edict clearing lesser offenders. Military Affairs Commissioner Sang Weihan, still hunting dozens of Guangyuan's accomplices in hiding, delayed the proclamation.
entries.literal: By recent precedent, when government troops recovered a walled city an amnesty edict was always issued to wash away faults. At that time Military Affairs Commissioner Sang Weihan, because several dozen of Guangyuan's accomplices were still in hiding and the search was very urgent, delayed the edict for a long time.

entries.zh: 或有告宋顏匿於守貞處者，朝廷取而殺之，守貞由是怨維翰。
entries.en: When someone reported that Song Yan was hidden in Shouzhen's camp, the court seized and executed him, and Shouzhen came to resent Sang Weihan.
entries.literal: Someone reported that Song Yan was hidden at Shouzhen's quarters; the court took him and executed him, and from this Shouzhen bore resentment toward Weihan.

entries.zh: 時行營將士所給賞賜，守貞盡以黦茶、染木、姜藥之類分給之，軍中大怨，乃以帛包所得物，如人首級，目之為守貞頭，懸於樹以詛之。
entries.en: When rewards reached the camp Shouzhen handed out only dark tea, dyewood, ginger, and medicines. The army erupted in anger, wrapped the goods in cloth shaped like severed heads, called them "Shouzhen's heads," and hung them from trees in mockery.
entries.literal: At that time the rewards given to the campaign troops—Shouzhen distributed them entirely as dark tea, dyewood, ginger, and medicines of that sort. Great resentment arose in the army; they wrapped what they had received in cloth like human heads, called them "Shouzhen's heads," and hung them on trees to curse him.

entries.zh: 守貞班師，加同平章事，以楊光遠東京第賜之。
entries.en: When Shouzhen returned in triumph he was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and given Yang Guangyuan's mansion in the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Shouzhen returned the army in triumph and was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery; Yang Guangyuan's mansion in the Eastern Capital was bestowed on him.

entries.zh: 守貞因取連宅軍營，以廣其第，大興土木，治之歲餘，為京師之甲。
entries.en: He seized adjoining barracks to expand the estate and spent more than a year on construction until his mansion ranked first in the capital.
entries.literal: Shouzhen thereupon took adjoining military barracks to enlarge his residence, undertaking great construction for more than a year until it was the finest in the capital.

entries.zh: 行幸賜宴，恩禮無比。
entries.en: When the emperor traveled he was honored with banquets and favor beyond any peer.
entries.literal: On imperial progresses he was granted banquets; favor and ceremony were without parallel.

entries.zh: 開運二年春，契丹以全軍南下，前鋒至相州湯陰縣，詔守貞屯滑州。
entries.en: In the spring of the second Kaiyun year the Khitan advanced south with their full army. Their vanguard reached Tangyin in Xiangzhou, and Shouzhen was ordered to hold Huazhou.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaiyun the Khitan marched south with their full army; the vanguard reached Tangyin County in Xiang Prefecture, and an edict ordered Shouzhen to garrison Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少帝再幸澶州，以守貞為北面行營都監，與招討使杜重威北伐，洎獲陽城之捷，遂收軍而還。
entries.en: The Young Emperor again went to Chanzhou in person and made Shouzhen overall supervisor of the northern campaign, marching north with pacification commissioner Du Chongwei. After the victory at Yangcheng they withdrew.
entries.literal: The Young Emperor again went in person to Chan Prefecture and made Shouzhen overall supervisor of the northern campaign headquarters; together with pacification commissioner Du Chongwei he marched north. After gaining the victory at Yangcheng he gathered the army and returned.

entries.zh: 四月，車駕還京，以守貞為侍衛副都指揮使，移鎮宋州，加檢校太師。
entries.en: In the fourth month the court returned to the capital. Shouzhen became deputy commander of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou, and was given the acting title of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: In the fourth month the imperial carriage returned to the capital; Shouzhen was made deputy commander of the palace guard, transferred to govern Song Prefecture, and additionally made acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 三年春，詔守貞率師巡邊。
entries.en: In the spring of the third year he was ordered to lead a border patrol.
entries.literal: In the spring of the third year an edict ordered Shouzhen to lead troops on a border patrol.

entries.zh: 至衡水，獲鄚州刺史趙思英而還。
entries.en: At Hengshui he captured Zhao Siying, prefect of Mozhou, and returned.
entries.literal: Reaching Hengshui, he captured Mo Prefecture's prefect Zhao Siying and returned.

entries.zh: 居無何，代高行周為侍衛親軍都指揮使，移鎮鄆州，意頗觖望。
entries.en: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace guard and was posted to Yunzhou, nursing considerable resentment.
entries.literal: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces and was transferred to govern Yun Prefecture, his mind rather resentful and dissatisfied.

entries.zh: 會宰臣李崧加侍中，守貞謂樞密使直學士殷鵬曰：「樞密何功，便加正相！」
entries.en: When chief minister Li Song was made Palace Attendant, Shouzhen told Military Affairs academician Yin Peng, "What has the Bureau of Military Affairs done to deserve the chief ministership?"
entries.literal: It happened that chief minister Li Song was made Palace Attendant; Shouzhen said to Military Affairs academician-direct Yin Peng, "What merit has the Bureau of Military Affairs that they should be given the chief ministership!"

entries.zh: 先是，桑維翰以元勛舊德為樞密使，守貞位望素處其下，每憚之，與李彥韜、馮玉輩協力排斥，維翰竟罷樞務。
entries.en: Earlier Sang Weihan, a founding minister of long service, had held the Bureau of Military Affairs. Shouzhen had always ranked below him and feared him. With Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and others he worked to oust him until Weihan was finally removed.
entries.literal: Earlier, Sang Weihan, by merit of founding service and old virtue, was Military Affairs Commissioner; Shouzhen's rank and prestige had always been below his, and he feared him each time. Together with Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and their like he worked to drive him out, and Weihan was finally removed from Military Affairs duties.

entries.zh: 李崧事分疏遠，守貞得以淩蔑。
entries.en: Li Song stood at a remove from military affairs, and Shouzhen took to despising him.
entries.literal: Li Song's duties were separate and distant, so Shouzhen was able to look down on him.

entries.zh: 其年夏，契丹寇邊，以守貞為北面行營都部署。
entries.en: That summer, when the Khitan raided the frontier, Shouzhen was made overall commander of the northern campaign.
entries.literal: That summer the Khitan raided the border, and Shouzhen was made overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 少帝開曲宴於內殿，以寵其行，教坊令人獻語云：「天子不須憂北寇，守貞面上管幽州。」
entries.en: The Young Emperor gave him a private farewell banquet in the inner hall. A director of the Music Office offered a verse: "Let the Son of Heaven not fear the northern foe—Shouzhen's face alone governs Youzhou."
entries.literal: The Young Emperor held an informal banquet in the inner hall to honor his departure; a director of the Music Office presented a saying: "The Son of Heaven need not worry about northern invaders—on Shouzhen's face he governs You Prefecture."

entries.zh: 既罷，守貞有自負之色，以其言誇詫於外。
entries.en: Afterward Shouzhen looked thoroughly pleased with himself and repeated the verse abroad as boast.
entries.literal: When it was over, Shouzhen wore a self-satisfied look and boasted of these words outside.

entries.zh: 既而率兵至定州北，與契丹偏師遇，斬蕃將嘉哩而還。
entries.en: He then marched north of Dingzhou, met a Khitan detachment, beheaded the tribal general Jiali, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Before long he led troops north of Ding Prefecture, met a Khitan detached force, beheaded the tribal general Jiali, and returned.

entries.zh: 九月，加兼侍中。
entries.en: In the ninth month he was additionally made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he was additionally made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 會契丹遣瀛州刺史偽降於少帝，請發大軍應接，朝廷信之。
entries.en: The Khitan then sent the prefect of Yingzhou in a feigned surrender, asking for a large army to join him, and the court believed the ruse.
entries.literal: It happened that the Khitan sent Ying Prefecture's prefect in a false surrender to the Young Emperor, requesting that a great army be sent to link up; the court believed it.

entries.zh: 十月，詔杜重威為北面行營招討使，以守貞為兵馬都監，知幽州行府事。
entries.en: In the tenth month Du Chongwei was made northern pacification commissioner, with Shouzhen as army supervisor and head of the Youzhou field headquarters.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Du Chongwei was ordered as northern campaign pacification commissioner, with Shouzhen as overall supervisor of horse and foot forces and in charge of the You Prefecture field headquarters.

entries.zh: 先是，守貞領兵再由鄴都，杜重威厚加贈遺，曲意承迎，守貞悅之，每於帝前稱舉，請委征討之柄。
entries.en: Earlier, when Shouzhen's troops passed through Ye again, Du Chongwei showered him with gifts and flattery. Delighted, Shouzhen praised him repeatedly at court and urged that the expedition command be given to him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Shouzhen led troops through Yecheng again, Du Chongwei gave lavish gifts and bent every courtesy to welcome him. Shouzhen was pleased and repeatedly praised him before the emperor, asking that the command of the expedition be entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 至是，守貞、重威等會兵於鄴，遂趨瀛州，瀛州不應。
entries.en: Shouzhen and Chongwei then united at Ye and marched on Yingzhou, which did not respond.
entries.literal: At this point Shouzhen, Chongwei, and the others joined forces at Ye and hurried toward Ying Prefecture, but Ying did not respond.

entries.zh: 貝州節度使梁漢璋為蕃將高牟翰所敗，死之，王師遂還。
entries.en: Liang Hanzhang, military governor of Beizhou, was defeated and killed by the tribal general Gao Mouhan, and the imperial army withdrew.
entries.literal: Bei Prefecture's military governor Liang Hanzhang was defeated by the tribal general Gao Mouhan and died; the imperial army then withdrew.

entries.zh: 師至深州，聞契丹大至，乃西趨鎮州，至滹沲之中渡，與敵相遇，官軍營於滹水之南。
entries.en: At Shenzhou they heard the Khitan were advancing in force and turned west to Zhenzhou. At Zhongdu on the Hutuo they met the enemy and pitched camp south of the river.
entries.literal: When the army reached Shen Prefecture and heard that the Khitan were coming in force, they hurried west toward Zhen Prefecture. At Zhongdu on the Hutuo they met the enemy, and the government troops encamped south of the Hutuo.

entries.zh: 未幾，敵騎潛渡至欒城，斷我糧路，尋則王清戰死，杜重威遂與守貞歸命契丹，授守貞司徒，依前鄆州節度使，從契丹至汴。
entries.en: Soon enemy cavalry crossed secretly to Luancheng and severed the supply lines. Wang Qing was killed in battle, and Du Chongwei surrendered with Shouzhen to the Khitan. Shouzhen was made Minister of Education and kept Yunzhou, then followed the Khitan to Bian.
entries.literal: Before long enemy horsemen secretly crossed to Luancheng and cut our supply routes; soon Wang Qing died in battle, and Du Chongwei then surrendered with Shouzhen to the Khitan. Shouzhen was appointed Minister of Education and remained military governor of Yun Prefecture as before, following the Khitan to Bian.

entries.zh: 時京輦之下，契丹充斥，都人士庶，若在塗炭。
entries.en: The capital swarmed with Khitan troops, and its people suffered as though in fire and flood.
entries.literal: At that time below the imperial capital the Khitan swarmed everywhere; the people of the capital were as if in fire and boiling water.

entries.zh: 二帥出入揚揚，市人詬之，略無慚色。
entries.en: The two commanders swaggered through the streets while townspeople cursed them, yet they showed no shame.
entries.literal: The two commanders went in and out with swaggering airs; the townspeople cursed them, yet they showed hardly a trace of shame.

entries.zh: 有頃，河北及京東草寇大起，澶州浮橋為群賊所斷，契丹主甚恐，乃命諸帥各歸本鎮，守貞遂赴汶陽。
entries.en: Soon bandits rose across Hebei and eastern China, and the floating bridge at Chanzhou was cut. Terrified, the Khitan khan ordered the commanders back to their posts, and Shouzhen returned to Wenyang.
entries.literal: Before long bandits rose in great numbers in Hebei and east of the capital; the floating bridge at Chan Prefecture was cut by bandit gangs. The Khitan ruler was greatly afraid and ordered each commander to return to his own command. Shouzhen then went to Wenyang.

entries.zh: 高祖入汴，守貞懼而來朝，授守貞太保，移鎮河中。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered Bian, Shouzhen came to court in fear. He was made Grand Guardian and transferred to Hezhong.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Bian, Shouzhen, afraid, came to court; he was made Grand Guardian and transferred to govern Hezhong.

entries.zh: 居無何，高祖晏駕，杜重威被誅，守貞愈不自安，乃潛畜異計。
entries.en: Before long Gaozu died and Du Chongwei was executed. Shouzhen grew ever more uneasy and began secretly plotting rebellion.
entries.literal: Before long Gaozu died; Du Chongwei was executed, and Shouzhen grew ever more ill at ease, secretly harboring rebellious designs.

entries.zh: 乾祐元年三月，先致書於權臣，布求保證，而完城郭，繕甲兵，晝夜不息。
entries.en: In the third month of the first Qianyou year he wrote first to powerful ministers seeking assurances, while fortifying the walls and arming his troops day and night without pause.
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Qianyou he first sent letters to powerful ministers, openly seeking guarantees, while completing walls and gates, repairing armor and weapons, day and night without rest.

entries.zh: 守貞以漢室新造，嗣君才立，自謂舉無遺策，又有僧總倫者，以占術幹守貞，謂守貞有人君之位，
entries.en: With the Han dynasty newly founded and a young heir on the throne, Shouzhen believed his plans flawless. A monk named Zonglun won his ear with divination, declaring that he was destined for the throne,
entries.literal: Shouzhen, because the Han house was newly founded and the heir had only just been established, believed his plans left nothing out. There was also the monk Zonglun, who by divination approached Shouzhen and said Shouzhen had the position of a sovereign,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：浚儀人趙修己，素善術數，自守貞鎮滑州，署司戶參軍，累從移鎮。
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhao Xiuji of Junyi was skilled in divination. When Shouzhen governed Huazhou he appointed him revenue aide and took him to every new posting.
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhao Xiuji of Junyi was skilled in numerology and fate-calculation. From the time Shouzhen governed Hua Prefecture he was appointed revenue section aide and followed him through successive transfers.

entries.zh: 為守貞言：「時命不可妄動。」
entries.en: He warned Shouzhen, "Do not move rashly against the times."
entries.literal: He told Shouzhen, "The times and fate must not be rashly stirred."

entries.zh: 前後切諫非一，守貞不聽，乃稱疾歸裏。）〉
entries.en: He remonstrated again and again, but Shouzhen would not listen, and at last he pleaded illness and went home.)〉
entries.literal: He remonstrated urgently more than once, but Shouzhen would not listen, so he claimed illness and returned home.)〉

entries.zh: 未幾，趙思綰以京兆叛，遣使奉表送禦衣於守貞，守貞自謂天時人事合符於己，乃潛結草賊，令所在竊發，遣兵據潼關。
entries.en: Soon Zhao Siwan rebelled at Jingzhao and sent envoys with a memorial and imperial robes for Shouzhen. Convinced that heaven and men alike favored him, Shouzhen secretly stirred bandits to rise everywhere and sent troops to seize Tong Pass.
entries.literal: Before long Zhao Siwan rebelled in Jingzhao and sent envoys with a memorial, presenting imperial robes to Shouzhen. Shouzhen believed heaven's timing and human affairs all matched himself, and secretly linked with bandits, ordering outbreaks everywhere and sending troops to seize Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·王繼勛傳》：李守貞之叛，令繼勛據潼關，為郭從義所破。）〉
entries.en: (History of Song, biography of Wang Jixun: During Li Shouzhen's rebellion he ordered Jixun to hold Tong Pass, but Guo Congyi defeated him.)〉
entries.literal: (History of Song, biography of Wang Jixun: In Li Shouzhen's rebellion he ordered Jixun to hold Tong Pass, but Jixun was defeated by Guo Congyi.)〉

entries.zh: 朝廷命白文珂、常思等領兵問罪，復遣樞密使郭威西征。
entries.en: The court sent Bai Wenke, Chang Si, and others to punish him, and dispatched Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Wei on a western campaign.
entries.literal: The court ordered Bai Wenke, Chang Si, and others to lead troops to punish him, and again sent Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Wei on a western campaign.

entries.zh: 官軍初至，守貞以諸軍多曾隸於麾下，自謂素得軍情，坐俟扣城迎己，及軍士詬噪，大失所望。
entries.en: When the imperial army arrived, Shouzhen assumed that many of its men had once served under him and would welcome him at the gates. Instead the soldiers cursed and jeered, and his hopes collapsed.
entries.literal: When the government army first arrived, Shouzhen thought that many of the troops had once served under him and believed he had long held the soldiers' hearts. He sat waiting for them to knock on the walls and welcome him—when the troops cursed and clamored instead, he was deeply disappointed.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·馬全義傳》：李守貞鎮河中，召置帳下。
entries.en: (History of Song, biography of Ma Quanyi: When Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong he took Quanyi into his service.
entries.literal: (History of Song, biography of Ma Quanyi: When Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong he summoned Quanyi and placed him in his command.

entries.zh: 及守貞叛，周主討之，全義每率敢死士夜出攻周祖壘，多所殺傷。
entries.en: When Shouzhen rebelled and the Zhou ruler marched against him, Quanyi repeatedly led suicide squads out by night to strike the Zhou founder's camps and inflict heavy losses.
entries.literal: When Shouzhen rebelled, the Zhou ruler attacked him; Quanyi often led dare-to-die troops out by night to assault the Zhou founder's camps, killing and wounding many.

entries.zh: 守貞貪而無謀，性多忌刻，全義累為畫策，皆不能用。）〉
entries.en: Shouzhen was greedy, shortsighted, and jealous. Quanyi offered plan after plan, but he would use none of them.)〉
entries.literal: Shouzhen was greedy and without strategy, his nature jealous and harsh; Quanyi repeatedly devised plans for him, but none could be used.)〉

entries.zh: 俄而王景崇據岐下，與趙思綰遣使推奉，守貞乃自號秦王，思綰、景崇皆受守貞署置。
entries.en: Soon Wang Jingchong held the Qi region. He and Zhao Siwan sent envoys to proclaim Shouzhen King of Qin, and both accepted appointments from him.
entries.literal: Before long Wang Jingchong held the Qi region; together with Zhao Siwan he sent envoys to elevate Shouzhen, who thereupon styled himself King of Qin. Siwan and Jingchong both accepted appointments from Shouzhen.

entries.zh: 又遣人賫蠟彈於吳、蜀、契丹，以求應援。
entries.en: He also sent sealed messages to Wu, Shu, and the Khitan seeking aid.
entries.literal: He also sent men bearing sealed wax balls to Wu, Shu, and the Khitan to seek reinforcements.

entries.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書·朱元傳》：守貞以河中反，漢命周太祖討之，元與李平奉守貞表來乞師，未復而守貞敗。）〉
entries.en: (Ma Ling, Southern Tang History, biography of Zhu Yuan: When Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, Han ordered the Zhou founder against him. Yuan and Li Ping brought Shouzhen's plea for troops, but before any answer came Shouzhen was defeated.)〉
entries.literal: (Ma Ling, Southern Tang History, biography of Zhu Yuan: When Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong, Han ordered the Zhou founder to suppress him. Yuan and Li Ping brought Shouzhen's memorial to beg for troops, but before a reply came Shouzhen was defeated.)〉

entries.zh: 既而城中糧盡，殺人為食。
entries.en: Before long the city's grain ran out and the garrison turned to cannibalism.
entries.literal: Before long grain in the city was exhausted and people were killed for food.

entries.zh: 召總倫詰其休咎，總倫至曰：「王自有天分，人不能奪。
entries.en: He summoned Zonglun to ask his fate. Zonglun said, "Your Highness has heaven's mandate; no one can take it from you.
entries.literal: He summoned Zonglun to question him about fortune and misfortune. Zonglun arrived and said, "Your Highness has heaven's portion by nature; no man can take it away.

entries.zh: 然分野災變，俟磨滅將盡，存留一人一騎，即王鵲起之際也。」
entries.en: But calamity hangs over this region. Wait until the destruction is nearly complete—when only one man and one horse remain, that will be the hour when you rise like a magpie."
entries.literal: Yet in the astral zones there are disasters and changes; wait until the grinding away is nearly complete—when only one man and one horse remain, that will be the moment Your Highness rises like a magpie."

entries.zh: 守貞深以為信。
entries.en: Shouzhen believed him utterly.
entries.literal: Shouzhen believed it deeply.

entries.zh: 洎攻城，守貞欲發石以拒外軍，炮竿子不可得，無何，上遊泛一筏至，其木悉可為炮竿，守貞以為神助。
entries.en: During the siege he needed poles for stone-throwers but could find none. Then a raft drifted downriver with timber fit for every catapult, and Shouzhen took it as a sign from heaven.
entries.literal: When the siege began, Shouzhen wished to launch stones against the outside army but could not obtain catapult poles. Before long a raft floated down from upstream; its timber could all serve as catapult poles, and Shouzhen took it as divine aid.

entries.zh: 又嘗因宴會將佐，守貞執弧矢，遙指一虎舐掌圖曰：「我若有非常之事，當中虎舌。」
entries.en: At another banquet with his officers he took up bow and arrow, aimed at a painting of a tiger licking its paw, and said, "If extraordinary fortune is mine, I shall strike the tiger's tongue."
entries.literal: Again, at a banquet with his officers, Shouzhen took bow and arrow, pointed from afar at a painting of a tiger licking its paw, and said, "If I am to have extraordinary fortune, I shall hit the tiger's tongue."

entries.zh: 引弓一發中之，左右拜賀，守貞亦自負焉。
entries.en: One shot struck true. His attendants bowed in congratulation, and Shouzhen swelled with pride.
entries.literal: He drew the bow and with one shot hit it; those beside him bowed in congratulation, and Shouzhen too was proud of himself.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·吳虔裕傳》：周祖討三叛，以虔裕為河中行營都監，率護聖諸軍五千以往。
entries.en: (History of Song, biography of Wu Qianyu: Campaigning against the three rebels, the Zhou founder made Qianyu supervisor of the Hezhong field headquarters with five thousand Imperial Guard troops.
entries.literal: (History of Song, biography of Wu Qianyu: The Zhou founder campaigned against the three rebels and made Qianyu overall supervisor of the Hezhong field headquarters, leading five thousand troops of the Imperial Guard.

entries.zh: 李守貞出兵五千餘，設梯橋，分五路於長連城西北以禦周祖。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen sent out more than five thousand men with scaling bridges, dividing into five columns northwest of the long walls to meet the Zhou founder.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen sent out more than five thousand troops, set up scaling bridges, and divided into five routes northwest of the long linked walls to oppose the Zhou founder.

entries.zh: 周祖令虔裕率大軍橫擊之，蒲人敗走，奪其梯橋，殺傷大半。）〉
entries.en: The Zhou founder ordered Qianyu to strike them in the flank. The Hezhong troops fled, losing their bridges, and more than half were killed or wounded.)〉
entries.literal: The Zhou founder ordered Qianyu to lead the main force in a lateral strike; the men of Pu were defeated and fled, their scaling bridges were seized, and more than half were killed or wounded.)〉

entries.zh: 及周光遜以西寨降，其勢益窘，人情離散。
entries.en: When Zhou Guangxun surrendered the western camp, their position grew desperate and morale collapsed.
entries.literal: When Zhou Guangxun surrendered the western camp, their situation grew still more desperate and hearts scattered.

entries.zh: 官軍攻城愈急，守貞乃潛於衙署多積薪芻，為自焚之計。
entries.en: As the imperial siege tightened, Shouzhen secretly piled firewood and straw in his headquarters, preparing to burn himself alive.
entries.literal: As the government army pressed the siege ever harder, Shouzhen secretly piled much firewood and straw in the yamen, planning self-immolation.

entries.zh: 二年七月，城陷，舉家蹈火而死。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the second year the city fell. His entire household perished in the flames.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the second year the city fell; the whole household entered the fire and died.

entries.zh: 王師入城，於煙中獲其屍，斷其首函之，並獲數子二女，與其黨俱獻於闕下。
entries.en: The imperial troops entered, recovered his body from the smoke, severed and boxed the head, and captured several sons and two daughters together with his followers, all sent to court.
entries.literal: The imperial army entered the city, recovered his corpse from the smoke, severed the head and boxed it, and also captured several sons and two daughters, presenting them together with his faction at the capital.

entries.zh: 隱帝御明德樓受俘馘，宣露布，百僚稱賀。
entries.en: Emperor Yindi received the captives and heads at the Tower of Bright Virtue, proclaimed victory, and the officials offered congratulations.
entries.literal: Emperor Yindi ascended the Tower of Bright Virtue to receive captives and severed heads, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 禮畢，以俘馘徇於都城，守貞首級梟於南市，諸子並賊黨孫願、劉芮、張延嗣、劉仁裕、僧總倫、靖余、張球、王廷秀、焦文傑、安在欽等並磔於西市，餘皆斬之。
entries.en: After the rites the captives were paraded through the capital. Shouzhen's head was displayed in the southern market. His sons and followers—including Sun Yuan, Liu Rui, Zhang Yansi, Liu Renyu, the monk Zonglun, Jing Yu, Zhang Qiu, Wang Tingxiu, Jiao Wenjie, and An Zaiqin—were dismembered at the western market, and the rest were beheaded.
entries.literal: When the rites were complete, the captives and heads were paraded through the capital; Shouzhen's head was displayed in the southern market. His sons and rebel associates Sun Yuan, Liu Rui, Zhang Yansi, Liu Renyu, the monk Zonglun, Jing Yu, Zhang Qiu, Wang Tingxiu, Jiao Wenjie, An Zaiqin, and others were all dismembered at the western market; the rest were beheaded.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：符後先適河中節度使李守貞之子崇訓。
entries.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu Hou had first married Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun.
entries.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Fu Hou had first been married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen, the military governor of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 守貞嘗得術士，善聽聲，知人貴賤，守貞舉族悉令術士聽之，獨言後大富貴，當母儀天下。
entries.en: Shouzhen once found a man skilled at judging rank by the sound of voices. He had every member of his clan tested; only Hou, he said, would rise to supreme wealth and become mother of the realm.
entries.literal: Shouzhen once obtained a technician skilled in listening to voices and knowing men's noble or base rank. Shouzhen had his whole clan listened to by the technician; only of Hou did he say she would be greatly noble and wealthy and should be mother to the realm.

entries.zh: 守貞信之，因曰：「吾婦尚為皇后，吾可知也。」
entries.en: Shouzhen believed him and said, "If my daughter-in-law is to be empress, what then am I destined for?"
entries.literal: Shouzhen believed it and therefore said, "If my daughter-in-law is yet to be empress, what may be known of me?"

entries.zh: 遂謀叛。
entries.en: He then plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: He then plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 及城陷，後獨免，周祖為世宗娶之，顯德中，冊為後。）〉
entries.en: When the city fell she alone was spared. The Zhou founder had her marry his heir Shizong, and in the Xiande era she was made empress.)〉
entries.literal: When the city fell, Hou alone was spared. The Zhou founder had her marry Shizong, and in the Xiande era she was enfeoffed as empress.)〉

entries.zh: 趙思綰，魏府人也。
entries.en: Zhao Siwan was a native of Weifu.
entries.literal: Zhao Siwan was a man of Weifu.

entries.zh: 唐同光末，趙在禮之據魏城也，思綰隸於帳下，累從之。
entries.en: At the end of the Tongguang era, when Zhao Zaili seized Weicheng, Siwan served in his command and followed him through every campaign.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang's Tongguang era, when Zhao Zaili held Weicheng, Siwan served under his command and followed him repeatedly.

entries.zh: 在禮卒，趙延壽籍其部曲，盡付於其子贊，思綰即其首領也。
entries.en: After Zaili's death Zhao Yanshou took over his troops and gave them to his son Zan, with Siwan as their leader.
entries.literal: When Zaili died, Zhao Yanshou registered his troops and handed them all to his son Zan; Siwan was their leader.

entries.zh: 高祖定河、洛，贊自河中移京兆尹。
entries.en: After Gaozu secured the heartland, Zan moved from Hezhong to become metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
entries.literal: When Gaozu secured the Yellow River and Luoyang regions, Zan moved from Hezhong to become metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 贊以久事契丹，常慮國家終不能容，乃與鳳翔侯益謀，引蜀兵為援，又令判官李恕入朝請覲，趙贊不待報赴闕，留思綰等數百人在京兆。
entries.en: Having long served the Khitan, Zan feared the court would never trust him. He plotted with Hou Yi of Fengxiang to bring in Shu troops and sent his aide Li Shu to request an audience. Zan left for court without waiting for permission, leaving Siwan and several hundred men in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Zan, having long served the Khitan, constantly feared the state would never tolerate him. He plotted with Fengxiang's Hou Yi to bring in Shu troops as aid, and also had his aide Li Shu enter court to request an audience. Zhao Zan did not wait for a reply but went to court, leaving Siwan and several hundred men in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 會高祖遣王景崇等西赴鳳翔，行次京兆，時思綰等數百人在焉。
entries.en: Gaozu then sent Wang Jingchong west toward Fengxiang. Passing through Jingzhao, they found Siwan and his several hundred men still there.
entries.literal: It happened that Gaozu sent Wang Jingchong and others west toward Fengxiang; marching through Jingzhao, Siwan and several hundred men were there at the time.

entries.zh: 思綰等比是趙在禮禦士，本不刺面，景崇、齊藏珍既至京兆，欲令文面，以防逋逸。
entries.en: Siwan's men had been Zhao Zaili's personal guards and bore no facial tattoos. When Jingchong and Qi Zangzhen reached Jingzhao they wanted to tattoo their faces to prevent desertion.
entries.literal: Siwan and the others had been Zhao Zaili's personal guards and had not originally been tattooed on the face. When Jingchong and Qi Zangzhen reached Jingzhao they wished to have them facially marked to prevent desertion.

entries.zh: 景崇微露風旨，思綰厲聲先請自刺，以率其下，景崇壯之。
entries.en: Jingchong hinted at the plan. Siwan loudly volunteered to be tattooed first, to set an example for his men, and Jingchong admired his spirit.
entries.literal: Jingchong subtly revealed the intent; Siwan loudly asked first to tattoo himself, to lead his subordinates, and Jingchong admired this.

entries.zh: 藏珍竊言曰：「思綰粗暴難制，不如殺之。」
entries.en: Zangzhen whispered, "Siwan is violent and ungovernable. Better kill him."
entries.literal: Zangzhen whispered, "Siwan is brutal and hard to control—better to kill him."

entries.zh: 景崇不聽，但率之同赴鳳翔。
entries.en: Jingchong refused and led them on toward Fengxiang.
entries.literal: Jingchong would not listen and only led them together toward Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 朝廷聞之，遣供奉官王益部署思綰等赴闕。
entries.en: When the court learned of this it sent Palace Attendant Wang Yi to escort Siwan and his men to the capital.
entries.literal: The court heard of this and sent Palace Attendant Wang Yi to arrange for Siwan and the others to proceed to court.

entries.zh: 思綰既發，行至途中，謂其黨常彥卿曰：「小太尉已入他手，吾輩至，則並死矣。」
entries.en: On the road Siwan told his follower Chang Yanqing, "The Little Grand Guardian is already in their hands. When we reach the capital we will all die together."
entries.literal: After Siwan set out, on the road he said to his follower Chang Yanqing, "The Little Grand Guardian is already in others' hands—when we arrive we will all die together."

entries.zh: 小太尉蓋謂趙贊也。
entries.en: The Little Grand Guardian meant Zhao Zan.
entries.literal: The Little Grand Guardian meant Zhao Zan.

entries.zh: 彥卿曰：「臨機制變，子勿復言！」
entries.en: Yanqing said, "Act on the moment—say no more!"
entries.literal: Yanqing said, "Seize the moment and change the plan—say no more!"

entries.zh: 既行，至永興，副使安友規、巡檢使喬守溫出迎，於郊外離亭置酒。
entries.en: They reached Yongxing, where Deputy Commissioner An Yougui and Inspection Commissioner Qiao Shouwen met them with wine at a roadside pavilion outside the city.
entries.literal: After they set out and reached Yongxing, Deputy Commissioner An Yougui and Inspection Commissioner Qiao Shouwen came out to welcome them and set out wine at a roadside pavilion beyond the suburbs.

entries.zh: 思綰前曰：「部下軍士已在城東安下，緣家屬在城，欲各將家今夜便宿城東。」
entries.en: Siwan stepped forward and said, "My men are already encamped east of the city. Our families are inside, and each man wishes to bring them out to camp east of the walls tonight."
entries.literal: Siwan stepped forward and said, "My troops are already encamped east of the city. Because our families are in the city, each man wishes to bring his family out and lodge east of the city tonight."

entries.zh: 守溫等然之。
entries.en: Shouwen and the others agreed.
entries.literal: Shouwen and the others agreed.

entries.zh: 思綰等辭去，與部下並無兵仗，才入西門，有州校坐門側，思綰遽奪其佩劍，即斬之。
entries.en: Siwan and his men left unarmed. Just inside the west gate a prefectural officer sat by the gate; Siwan snatched his sword and killed him on the spot.
entries.literal: Siwan and the others took their leave. They and their followers carried no weapons. Just inside the west gate a prefectural officer sat beside the gate; Siwan suddenly seized his girdle sword and at once beheaded him.

entries.zh: 其眾持白挺殺守門軍士十餘人，分眾守捉諸門。
entries.en: His men seized white clubs, killed more than ten gate guards, and seized every gate.
entries.literal: His followers took white clubs and killed more than ten gate-guard soldiers, then divided forces to seize and hold the various gates.

entries.zh: 思綰劫庫兵以授之，遂據其城，時乾祐元年三月二十四日也。
entries.en: Siwan seized the armory and armed his men, then took the city on the twenty-fourth day of the third month of the first Qianyou year.
entries.literal: Siwan plundered the armory weapons and distributed them, then seized the city—it was the twenty-fourth day of the third month in the first year of Qianyou.

entries.zh: 翌日，集城中丁壯得四千餘人，浚池隍，修樓櫓，旬浹之間，戰守皆備。
entries.en: The next day he mustered more than four thousand able-bodied men, dredged the moats, repaired the towers, and within ten days the city was ready for siege or defense.
entries.literal: The next day he gathered able-bodied men in the city, obtaining more than four thousand; he dredged moats and ditches and repaired towers and palisades, and within ten days both attack and defense were ready.

entries.zh: 尋遣人送款於河中，李守貞遣使賫偽詔授思綰晉昌軍節度使、檢校太尉。
entries.en: He soon sent envoys to submit to Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, who replied with a forged edict making him military governor of Jinchang and acting Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Before long he sent men with submission to Hezhong; Li Shouzhen sent envoys bearing a false edict appointing Siwan military governor of the Jinchang army and acting Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 朝廷聞之，命郭從義、王峻帥師伐之。
entries.en: The court then ordered Guo Congyi and Wang Jun to lead troops against him.
entries.literal: When the court heard of this it ordered Guo Congyi and Wang Jun to lead troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 及攻其城，王師傷者甚眾，乃以長塹圍之。
entries.en: The assault cost the imperial army heavy casualties, and they settled instead for a long encircling trench.
entries.literal: When they attacked the city, imperial casualties were very heavy, so they surrounded it with a long trench.

entries.zh: 經年糧盡，遂殺人充食。
entries.en: After a year the grain ran out and the garrison turned to cannibalism.
entries.literal: After a year grain was exhausted and people were killed to serve as food.

entries.zh: 思綰嘗對眾取人膽以酒吞之，告眾曰：「吞此至一千，即膽氣無敵矣。」
entries.en: Siwan once swallowed a human gall bladder in wine before his troops and declared, "Swallow a thousand of these and your courage will know no match."
entries.literal: Siwan once before the assembly took a human gall bladder and swallowed it in wine, telling the crowd, "When you have swallowed a thousand of these, your gall and spirit will be without match."

entries.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》：賊臣趙思綰自倡亂至敗，凡食人肝六十六，無不面剖而膾之。）〉
entries.en: (Taiping guangji: From rebellion to defeat the traitor Zhao Siwan ate sixty-six human livers, each time slicing the flesh from the face.)〉
entries.literal: (Taiping guangji: The rebel minister Zhao Siwan, from raising rebellion to defeat, ate sixty-six human livers in all, each time cutting open the face and slicing the flesh fine.)〉

entries.zh: 杜重威，其先朔州人，近世徙家於太原。
entries.en: Du Chongwei came from Shuozhou stock; in recent generations his family had settled in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Du Chongwei—his ancestors were men of Shuozhou; in recent generations the family moved its residence to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 祖興，振武牙將。
entries.en: His grandfather Xing had served as a junior officer in the Zhenwu army.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xing was a junior officer of the Zhenwu command.

entries.zh: 父堆金，事唐武皇為先鋒使。
entries.en: His father Duijin had served Emperor Wu of Tang as vanguard commissioner.
entries.literal: His father Duijin served Tang's Martial Emperor as vanguard commissioner.

entries.zh: 重威少事明宗，自護聖軍校領防州刺史。
entries.en: In his youth Chongwei entered the service of Emperor Mingzong, advancing from a guardsman in the Imperial Guard to acting prefect of Fangzhou.
entries.literal: When young, Chongwei served Emperor Mingzong, rising from a guardsman of the Imperial Guard to acting prefect of Fang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 其妻即晉高祖妹也，累封宋國大長公主。
entries.en: His wife was a younger sister of Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin, and was eventually enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Song.
entries.literal: His wife was the younger sister of Jin's Emperor Gaozu; she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Song.

entries.zh: 天福初，命重威典禁軍，遙授舒州刺史。
entries.en: Early in the Tianfu era he was placed in command of the palace guard and given the concurrent title of prefect of Shuzhou, though he did not take up the post.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, Chongwei was ordered to command the palace guard and was concurrently appointed, in absentia, prefect of Shu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 二年，張從賓構亂，據汜水，晉高祖遣重威與候益率眾破之，以功授潞州節度使。
entries.en: In the second year Zhang Congbin rebelled and held Sishui. Emperor Gaozu dispatched Chongwei and Hou Yi to crush the revolt, and for this service Chongwei was appointed military governor of Luzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year, Zhang Congbin raised a rebellion and seized Sishui; Jin's Emperor Gaozu sent Chongwei and Hou Yi to lead troops and defeat him, and for this merit Chongwei was made military governor of Lu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 與楊光遠降範延光於鄴城，改許州節度使，兼侍衛親軍馬步軍副指揮使，尋加同平章事。
entries.en: With Yang Guangyuan he forced Fan Yanguang to surrender at Yecheng. He was then transferred to Xu Prefecture as military governor, made deputy commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, and soon afterward elevated to co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
entries.literal: Together with Yang Guangyuan he compelled Fan Yanguang to surrender at Yecheng; he was then made military governor of Xu Prefecture, and concurrently deputy commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces; shortly afterward he was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 未幾，移鎮鄆州，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Before long he was reassigned to Yunzhou and promoted to commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to govern at Yun Prefecture and promoted to commander of the palace guard's horse and foot forces.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：馮道、李崧屢薦重威之能，以為都指揮使，充隨駕御營使。）〉
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly praised Chongwei's abilities; he was appointed commander and also served as commissioner of the imperial escort camp.)〉
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly recommended Chongwei's ability, and he was made commander and also served as commissioner of the imperial escort camp.)〉

entries.zh: 及鎮州安重榮稱兵向闕，命重威禦之，敗重榮於宗城。
entries.en: When An Chongrong of Zhenzhou raised an army and marched on the capital, Chongwei was sent against him and defeated him at Zongcheng.
entries.literal: When An Chongrong of Zhen Prefecture raised troops and marched on the capital, Chongwei was ordered to oppose him and defeated Chongrong at Zongcheng.

entries.zh: 重榮奔據常山，重威尋拔其城，斬重榮首傳於闕下，授成德軍節度使。
entries.en: Chongrong fled to Changshan, which Chongwei soon captured. He beheaded Chongrong and sent the head to court, and in reward was made military governor of Chengde.
entries.literal: Chongrong fled and held Changshan; Chongwei soon took the city, beheaded Chongrong and sent his head to the capital, and was appointed military governor of the Chengde army.

entries.zh: 所得重榮家財及常山公帑，悉歸於己，晉高祖知而不問。
entries.en: He appropriated all of Chongrong's family wealth and the public treasury of Changshan for himself. Emperor Gaozu knew but said nothing.
entries.literal: The property taken from Chongrong's household and the public funds of Changshan he kept entirely for himself; Jin's Emperor Gaozu knew of it but did not inquire.

entries.zh: 至鎮，復重斂於民，稅外加賦，境內苦之
entries.en: Once installed in his circuit he taxed the people even more harshly, piling surcharges on top of regular levies until the region groaned under his rule.
entries.literal: On reaching his post he again levied heavily on the people, imposing surcharges beyond the regular taxes, and those within his circuit suffered bitterly.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：重威所至黷貨，民多逃亡，嘗出過市，謂左右曰：「人言我驅盡百姓，何市人之多也！」）〉
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Wherever Chongwei was posted he extorted wealth until the people fled in droves. Once, passing through the market, he remarked to his attendants, "They say I have driven away every last commoner—then why is the market so crowded?")〉
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Wherever Chongwei went he plundered for gain; many of the people fled. Once when he went out through the market he said to those beside him, "People say I have driven away all the commoners—why are there so many people in the market!")〉

entries.zh: 戊辰，前曹州防禦使何福進受宣權許州節度使，前復州防禦使王彥超受宣權徐州節度使，前澶州節度使李洪義受宣權宋州節度使。
entries.en: On wuchen, former Caozhou Defender He Fujin was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Xu Prefecture; former Fuzhou Defender Wang Yanchao was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Xuzhou; former Chanzhou Military Governor Li Hongyi was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Songzhou.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen, the former Defender of Caozhou He Fujin received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Xu Prefecture; the former Defender of Fuzhou Wang Yanchao received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Xuzhou; the former Military Governor of Chanzhou Li Hongyi received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Songzhou.

entries.zh: 己巳，上漢太后尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
entries.en: On jisi the Han Empress Dowager was given the honorific title Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
entries.literal: On the day jisi, the honorific title Zhaosheng Empress Dowager was bestowed upon the Han Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 是日，詔有司擇日為故主發哀。
entries.en: That day an edict ordered the relevant offices to set a date for mourning the former sovereign.
entries.literal: That day an edict ordered the relevant offices to choose a day to proclaim mourning for the former sovereign.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載原敕云：漢高祖為義帝發喪，魏明帝正禪陵尊號，一時達禮，千古所稱，況朕久事前朝，常參大政，雖遷虞事夏，見奪於群情，而四海九州，咸知予夙志。
entries.en: (The Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties records the original edict: Han Gaozu proclaimed mourning for Emperor Yi; Wei Mingdi corrected the honorific of the Zen tomb — both timely fulfillment of ritual, praised through the ages. I long served the previous dynasty and regularly participated in great affairs. Though yielding Yu to serve Xia, I was displaced by public sentiment, yet all the realm knows my longstanding intent.
entries.literal: (The "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties" records the original edict as saying: Han Gaozu proclaimed mourning for the Emperor Yi; Wei Mingdi corrected the honorific title of the Zen tomb — timely fulfillment of ritual, praised through the ages; moreover I long served the previous dynasty and regularly participated in great affairs; though yielding Yu to serve Xia, I was displaced by public sentiment, yet the four seas and nine provinces all know my longstanding intent.

entries.zh: 宜令所司擇日為故主舉哀，仍備山陵葬禮。）〉
entries.en: Let the relevant offices choose a day to proclaim mourning for the former sovereign and provide full mountain-tomb burial rites.) (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: The relevant offices should be ordered to choose a day to proclaim mourning for the former sovereign, and also to provide full mountain-tomb burial rites.) (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 辛未，有司上言：「皇帝為故主舉哀日，服縞素，直領深衣、腰绖等。
entries.en: On xinwei the relevant offices submitted: "On the day the Emperor proclaims mourning for the former sovereign, he shall wear unbleached hemp, a straight-collared deep robe, and a waist mourning sash.
entries.literal: On the day xinwei, the relevant offices submitted a memorial saying: "On the day the Emperor proclaims mourning for the former sovereign, he shall wear unbleached hemp, a straight-collared deep robe, a waist mourning sash, and the like.

entries.zh: 成服畢祭奠，不視朝七日，坊市禁音樂。
entries.en: After the mourning garments are complete and offerings performed, he shall not hold court for seven days, and music shall be forbidden in the wards and markets.
entries.literal: When the mourning garments are complete and the offerings performed, he shall not hold court for seven days, and music shall be forbidden in wards and markets.

entries.zh: 文武內外臣僚成服後，每日赴太平宮臨，三日止，七日釋服。
entries.en: After civil and military officials complete their mourning garments, they shall attend daily mourning rites at Taiping Palace for three days, then cease; on the seventh day they shall lay mourning aside.
entries.literal: After civil and military officials within and without complete their mourning garments, they shall daily attend mourning rites at Taiping Palace for three days, then cease; on the seventh day they shall remove mourning dress.

entries.zh: 至山陵啟攢塗日，服初服，盾車出城，班辭釋服。」
entries.en: On the day the mountain tomb is opened and the coffin sealed, he shall wear initial mourning dress; the shield carriage departs the city, and after the farewell ceremony he shall lay mourning aside."
entries.literal: On the day the mountain tomb is opened and the coffin sealed, he shall wear initial mourning dress; the shield carriage departs the city, and after the farewell ceremony mourning dress is removed."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: The memorial was approved.

entries.zh: 壬申，前博州刺史李筠受宣權滑州節度使。
entries.en: On renshen, former Bozhou Prefect Li Yun was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Huazhou.
entries.literal: On the day renshen, the former Prefect of Bozhou Li Yun received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Huazhou.

entries.zh: 癸酉，樞密使、檢校太傅王峻加同平章事；
entries.en: On guiyou, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jun, Grand Preceptor by special appointment, was made Grand Councilor;
entries.literal: On the day guiyou, Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Preceptor by special appointment, was made Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以前澶州節度使李洪義為宋州節度使，加同平章事。
entries.en: former Chanzhou Military Governor Li Hongyi was made Military Governor of Songzhou and appointed Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: the former Military Governor of Chanzhou Li Hongyi was made Military Governor of Songzhou and appointed Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 以滑州節度副使陳觀為左散騎常侍，鄴都留守判官王溥為左諫議大夫，並充樞密院直學士。
entries.en: Huazhou Deputy Military Governor Chen Guan was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and Yedu Garrison Aide Wang Pu was made Left Remonstrance Grandee — both appointed Direct Academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Chen Guan, deputy military governor of Huazhou, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Wang Pu, administrative aide to the Yedu garrison commander, was made Left Remonstrance Grandee — both appointed Direct Academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 以元從都押衙鄭仁誨為客省使，知客押牙向訓為宮苑使。
entries.en: Original-follower Chief Yamen Officer Zheng Renhui was made Commissioner of the Reception Bureau, and Reception Officer Xiang Xun was made Commissioner of the Palace Parks.
entries.literal: Zheng Renhui, chief yamen officer of the original followers, was made Commissioner of the Reception Bureau; Xiang Xun, reception officer and yamen guard, was made Commissioner of the Palace Parks.

entries.zh: 北京留守劉崇遣押牙鞏廷美致書，求劉赟歸藩。
entries.en: Northern Capital Garrison Commander Liu Chong sent his yamen guard Gong Tingmei with a letter requesting Liu Yun's return to his post.
entries.literal: Liu Chong, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, sent his yamen guard Gong Tingmei with a letter requesting that Liu Yun be returned to his frontier post.

entries.zh: 帝報曰：「朕在澶州之時，軍情推戴之際，先差來直省李光美備見，必想具言，而況遐邇所聞，在後盡當知悉。
entries.en: The Emperor replied: "When I was at Chanzhou and the army urged my elevation, I first dispatched Palace Attendant Li Guangmei, who witnessed everything — you must have heard the full account by now. What near and far have heard will all become clear in time.
entries.literal: The Emperor replied: "When I was at Chanzhou, at the moment the army urged my elevation, I first dispatched the palace attendant Li Guangmei, who witnessed everything in full — you must surely have heard the full account; moreover what near and far have heard will all become known in time.

entries.zh: 湘陰公比在宋州駐泊，見令般取赴京，但勿憂疑，必令得所。
entries.en: The Lord of Xiangyin is presently at Songzhou and has been ordered brought to the capital. Do not worry — he will surely be properly provided for.
entries.literal: The Lord of Xiangyin is presently stationed at Songzhou; he has now been ordered brought to the capital — but do not worry or doubt; he will surely be properly provided for.

entries.zh: 惟公在彼，固請安心，若能同力扶持，別無顧慮，即當便封王爵，永鎮北門，鐵券丹書，必無愛惜。
entries.en: As for you there, set your mind at ease. If you lend your strength in joint support without other concern, I shall at once enfeoff you as prince and charge you forever with guarding the northern gate — iron certificates and cinnabar writs will be granted without stint.
entries.literal: As for you there, I earnestly ask you to set your mind at ease; if you can jointly lend your strength in support, with no other concern, I shall at once enfeoff you with princely rank, forever guarding the northern gate — iron certificates and cinnabar writs will surely be granted without stint.

entries.zh: 其諸情素，並令來人口宣。」
entries.en: All these matters shall also be conveyed orally by the envoy."
entries.literal: As for all these circumstances, they shall also be orally proclaimed by the envoy who comes."

entries.zh: 遣千牛衛將軍未憲充入契丹使。
entries.en: He dispatched Qianniu Guard General Zhu Xian to serve as envoy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: He dispatched Qianniu Guard General Zhu Xian to serve as envoy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 先是，去年契丹永康王烏裕寇邢、趙，陷內丘，及回，兀裕遣使與漢隱帝書，
entries.en: Earlier, the year before, Khitan Prince Yongkang Wuyu had raided Xing and Zhao and captured Neiqiu. On his return Wuyu sent an envoy with a letter to the Hidden Emperor of Han,
entries.literal: Previously, in the previous year the Khitan Prince of Yongkang Wuyu raided Xing and Zhao, captured Neiqiu, and upon his return Wuyu dispatched an envoy with a letter to the Hidden Emperor of Han,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹之攻內丘也，死傷頗多，又值月食，軍中多妖異，契丹主不敢深入，引兵還，遣使請和於漢。）〉
entries.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that in the attack on Neiqiu Khitan casualties were heavy; a lunar eclipse followed, and strange omens multiplied in the camp. The Khitan ruler dared not advance further, withdrew his army, and sent an envoy to sue for peace with Han.) (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: (From the "Comprehensive Mirror": when the Khitan attacked Neiqiu, dead and wounded were many; moreover a lunar eclipse occurred and many strange omens appeared in the army.
