The Khitan ruler dared not press deep, withdrew his forces, and dispatched an envoy to sue for peace with Han.) (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 使至境上，會朝廷有蕭墻之變，帝定京城，回至澶州，遇蕃使至，遂與入朝。
entries.en: When the envoy reached the border, the court was convulsed by internal strife. After the Emperor secured the capital he returned to Chan Prefecture, met the arriving Khitan envoy, and entered court with him.
entries.literal: When the envoy reached the frontier, the court was struck by internal turmoil; after the Emperor secured the capital he returned to Chan Prefecture, met the barbarian envoy arriving, and entered court together with him.

entries.zh: 至是，遣朱憲伴送來使歸蕃，兼致書敘革命之由，仍以金酒器一副、玉帶一遺兀裕。
entries.en: At this point he sent Zhu Xian to escort the Khitan envoy home, with a letter explaining the change of dynasty, and presented Wuyu with a set of gold wine vessels and a jade belt.
entries.literal: At this time he dispatched Zhu Xian to escort the incoming envoy back to the barbarians, also sending a letter explaining the reason for the dynastic change, and presenting Wuyu with one set of gold wine vessels and one jade belt.

entries.zh: 晉州節度使王晏殺行軍司馬徐建，以通河東聞。
entries.en: Jin Prefecture Military Governor Wang Yan killed March Chief of Staff Xu Jian and notified Hedong.
entries.literal: Jin Prefecture Military Governor Wang Yan killed March Chief of Staff Xu Jian and reported the act to Hedong.

entries.zh: 司天上言：「今國家建號，以木德代水，準經法國以姓墓為臘，請以未日為臘。」
entries.en: The Directorate of Astronomy submitted: "Now that the state has been founded, Wood replaces Water as the ruling element. By canonical law the La festival follows the tomb day of the dynastic surname — we request that the wei day be observed as La."
entries.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy submitted a memorial saying: "Now that the state has established its title, Wood virtue replaces Water; according to canonical law the state takes the surname tomb day as the La festival — we request that the wei day be taken as La."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: The request was approved.

entries.zh: 時議者曰：「昔武王勝殷，歲集於房，國家受命，金、木集於房。
entries.en: Commentators of the time said: "When King Wu conquered Yin, the year star gathered in Fang; when the state received the Mandate, Metal and Wood gathered there as well.
entries.literal: Commentators of the time said: "In antiquity when King Wu conquered Yin, the year star gathered in Fang; when the state received the Mandate, Metal and Wood gathered in Fang.

entries.zh: 文王厄羑裏，而卦遇明夷，帝脫於鄴，大衍之數，復得明夷，則周為國號，符於文、武矣。」
entries.en: King Wen suffered at Youli and drew the hexagram Mingyi; the Emperor escaped at Ye and the Great Evolution numbers again yielded Mingyi — thus the state title Zhou accorded with King Wen and King Wu."
entries.literal: King Wen suffered hardship at Youli, and the hexagram encountered Mingyi; the Emperor escaped at Ye, and in the numbers of the Great Evolution Mingyi was obtained again — thus Zhou as the state title accorded with Wen and Wu."

entries.zh: 先是，丁未年夏六月，土、金、木、火四星聚於張，占者雲，當有帝王興於周者。
entries.en: Earlier, in the sixth month of summer in the dingwei year, the Earth, Metal, Wood, and Fire stars gathered in Zhang; diviners declared that an emperor would rise under the name Zhou.
entries.literal: Earlier, in summer, the sixth month of the dingwei year, Earth, Metal, Wood, and Fire stars gathered in Zhang; diviners said that an emperor or king would rise in Zhou.

entries.zh: 故漢祖建國，由平陽、陜服趨洛陽以應之，及隱帝將嗣位，封周王以符其事。
entries.en: Therefore when Han's founder established the dynasty, he moved from Pingyang and Shanfu toward Luoyang to fulfill the omen; when Emperor Yin was about to succeed, he enfeoffed a Prince of Zhou to match it.
entries.literal: Therefore when Han's ancestor established the state, he moved from Pingyang and Shanfu toward Luoyang to accord with it; when Emperor Yin was about to succeed the throne, he enfeoffed the Prince of Zhou to match the matter.

entries.zh: 而帝以姬虢之胄，復繼宗周，而天下之契炳然矣。
entries.en: Now the Emperor, as a scion of Ji and Guo, has restored the Zhou line — and Heaven's design for the realm stands plain.
entries.literal: Yet the Emperor, as a scion of Ji and Guo, again succeeded the ancestral Zhou — and the accord of all under Heaven was luminous.

entries.zh: 昔武王以木德王天下，宇文周亦承木德，而三朝皆以木代水，不其異乎！
entries.en: King Wu once ruled the realm under Wood; the Yuwen Zhou also claimed Wood — yet three dynasties all replaced Water with Wood. What a remarkable pattern!
entries.literal: In antiquity King Wu ruled all under Heaven with Wood virtue; the Yuwen Zhou also inherited Wood virtue — yet three dynasties all used Wood to replace Water; is this not strange!

entries.zh: 又詔在朝文武臣僚，各上封事，凡有益國利民之事，速具以聞。
entries.en: Another edict ordered civil and military officials at court each to submit sealed memorials on any matter benefiting state or people, reporting at once.
entries.literal: Another edict ordered civil and military officials at court each to submit sealed memorials; whatever benefits the state and benefits the people, report quickly.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：詔曰：朕生長軍旅，不親學問，未知治天下之道。
entries.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records the edict: I was reared in the army and never pursued learning myself; I do not know how to govern the realm.
entries.literal: (From the "Comprehensive Mirror": the edict stated: I was reared in the army and did not personally pursue learning; I do not know the Way of governing all under heaven.

entries.zh: 文武官有益國利民之術，各具封事以聞，咸宜直書其事，勿事辭藻。）〉
entries.en: Any civil or military official with policies that benefit state or people should submit sealed memorials; write plainly of the matter and do not trouble over literary ornament.) (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: Civil and military officials who have policies benefiting the state and the people should each submit sealed memorials; all should write plainly of the matter — do not trouble over literary ornament.) (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 辛巳，鎮州武行德、晉州王晏、相州張彥成、潞州常思、邠州候章並加兼侍中；
entries.en: On xinsi Wu Xingde of Zhen Prefecture, Wang Yan of Jin Prefecture, Zhang Yancheng of Xiang Prefecture, Chang Si of Lu Prefecture, and Hou Zhang of Bin Prefecture were all made concurrent Palace Secretary;
entries.literal: On the day xinsi, Zhen Prefecture Wu Xingde, Jin Prefecture Wang Yan, Xiang Prefecture Zhang Yancheng, Lu Prefecture Chang Si, and Bin Prefecture Hou Zhang were all additionally appointed concurrent Palace Secretary;

entries.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使、果州防禦使、檢校太保郭崇為洋州節度使、檢校太傅，典軍如故；
entries.en: Palace Guard Cavalry Commander and Defender of Guo Prefecture Guo Chong was appointed Military Governor of Yang Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, retaining command of his troops;
entries.literal: Palace Guard Cavalry Commander, Defender of Guo Prefecture, and Honorary Grand Guardian Guo Chong was appointed Military Governor of Yang Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, command of troops as before;

entries.zh: 以侍衛步軍都指揮使、岳州防禦使曹英為利州節度使、檢校太傅，典軍如故。
entries.en: Palace Guard Infantry Commander and Defender of Yue Prefecture Cao Ying was appointed Military Governor of Li Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, retaining command of his troops.
entries.literal: Palace Guard Infantry Commander and Defender of Yue Prefecture Cao Ying was appointed Military Governor of Li Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, command of troops as before.

entries.zh: 癸未，涇州史懿、延州高允權、滄州王景、永興郭從義、定州孫方簡並加兼侍中，鄜州楊信、同州薛懷讓、貝州王繼宏並加同平章事。
entries.en: On guiwei Shi Yi of Jing Prefecture, Gao Yunquan of Yan Prefecture, Wang Jing of Cang Prefecture, Guo Congyi of Yongxing, and Sun Fangjian of Ding Prefecture were made concurrent Palace Secretary; Yang Xin of Fu Prefecture, Xue Huairang of Tong Prefecture, and Wang Jihong of Bei Prefecture were made concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: On the day guiwei, Jing Prefecture Shi Yi, Yan Prefecture Gao Yunquan, Cang Prefecture Wang Jing, Yongxing Guo Congyi, and Ding Prefecture Sun Fangjian were all additionally appointed concurrent Palace Secretary; Fu Prefecture Yang Xin, Tong Prefecture Xue Huairang, and Bei Prefecture Wang Jihong were all additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 乙酉，華州王饒、河中扈彥珂、鄧州折從阮、邢州劉詞並加同平章事。
entries.en: On yiyou Wang Rao of Hua Prefecture, Hu Yanke of Hezhong, Zhe Congruan of Deng Prefecture, and Liu Ci of Xing Prefecture were made concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: On the day yiyou, Hua Prefecture Wang Rao, Hezhong Hu Yanke, Deng Prefecture Zhe Congruan, and Xing Prefecture Liu Ci were all additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 丙戌，幸西莊。
entries.en: On bingxu the Emperor visited the Western Villa.
entries.literal: On the day bingxu, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.

entries.zh: 潞州奏，得石會關使王延美報，河東劉崇於正月十六日僭號。
entries.en: Lu Prefecture reported that Shihui Pass Commissioner Wang Yanmei had notified them that Liu Chong of Hedong had usurped the imperial title on the sixteenth of the first month.
entries.literal: Lu Prefecture memorialized that it had received a report from Shihui Pass Commissioner Wang Yanmei that Hedong Liu Chong on the sixteenth day of the first month usurped the imperial title.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以前澶州節度使李洪義為宋州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: On dinghai former Chan Prefecture Military Governor Li Hongyi was appointed Military Governor of Song Prefecture and made concurrent Grand Councilor;
entries.literal: On the day dinghai, the former Military Governor of Chan Prefecture Li Hongyi was appointed Military Governor of Song Prefecture and additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以曹州防禦使、北面行營馬步都排陣使何福進為許州節度使，加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Defender of Cao Prefecture and Northern Expeditionary Chief Array Marshal He Fujin was appointed Military Governor of Xu Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor;
entries.literal: Defender of Cao Prefecture and Chief Array Marshal of the Northern Expeditionary Camp for Horse and Foot He Fujin was appointed Military Governor of Xu Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor;

entries.zh: 以博州刺史、北面行營右廂排陣使李筠為滑州節度使，加檢校太保。
entries.en: Prefect of Bo Prefecture and Northern Expeditionary Right Wing Array Marshal Li Jun was appointed Military Governor of Hua Prefecture and Honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Prefect of Bo Prefecture and Right Wing Array Marshal of the Northern Expeditionary Camp Li Jun was appointed Military Governor of Hua Prefecture and Honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 戊子，有司上言：「準赦書，以晉、漢之胄為二王後，其唐五廟仲祀合廢。」
entries.en: On wuzi the relevant offices submitted: "Under the amnesty, descendants of Jin and Han are appointed heirs of the two dynasties; the mid-year sacrifice at the Five Temples of Tang should be abolished."
entries.literal: On the day wuzi, the relevant offices submitted a memorial saying: "According to the amnesty, descendants of Jin and Han are to serve as heirs of the two dynasties; the mid-year sacrifice at the Five Temples of Tang should jointly be abolished."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: It was ordered.

entries.zh: 庚寅，宗正寺奏：「請以晉、漢故事，遷漢七廟神主入升平宮，行仲享之禮，以漢宗子為三獻。」
entries.en: On gengyin the Office of the Imperial Clan submitted: "Following Jin and Han precedent, we request that the spirit tablets of Han's seven temples be moved to Shengping Palace for the mid-year offering, with a Han imperial clansman serving as thrice-presenter."
entries.literal: On the day gengyin, the Office of the Imperial Clan submitted a memorial saying: "Following the precedents of Jin and Han, we request that the spirit tablets of the seven temples of Han be moved into Shengping Palace to perform the mid-year offering, with a Han imperial clansman serving as thrice-presenter."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: It was ordered.

entries.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝，姓郭氏，諱威，字文仲，邢州堯山人也。
entries.en: Taizu, the Sagely Divine, Respectful, Solemn, Martial, Literary, and Filial Emperor, was of the Guo clan. His personal name was Wei, his courtesy name Wenzhong, and his home was Yao Mountain in Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Taizu, the Sagely Divine Respectful Solemn Martial Literary Filial Emperor, bore the surname Guo; his taboo name was Wei, his style Wenzhong, and he was a native of Yao Mountain in Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 或云本常氏之子，幼隨母適郭氏，故冒其姓焉。
entries.en: Some accounts hold that he was born a Chang, followed his mother into the Guo household as a child, and thereafter bore the Guo surname.
entries.literal: Some say he was originally a son of the Chang clan; in youth he followed his mother in marrying into the Guo clan, and therefore took their surname.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：周虢叔之後。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, the house descended from Guo Shu of Zhou.)
entries.literal: (From the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties": a descendant of Guo Shu of Zhou.)

entries.zh: 高祖諱璟，廣順初，追尊為睿和皇帝，廟號信祖，陵曰溫陵；
entries.en: The high ancestor, taboo name Jing, was posthumously enthroned as Emperor Ruihe at the opening of Guangshun, with the temple name Xizu and the mausoleum Wenling;
entries.literal: The High Ancestor's taboo name was Jing; at the beginning of the Guangshun era he was posthumously honored as Emperor Ruihe, with temple name Xizu and mausoleum called Wenling;

entries.zh: 高祖妣張氏，追謚睿恭皇后。
entries.en: The High Ancestor's consort, Lady Zhang, received the posthumous title Empress Ruigong.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor's consort, née Zhang, was posthumously given the title Empress Ruigong.

entries.zh: 曾祖諱諶，漢贈太保，追尊為明憲皇帝，廟號僖祖，陵曰齊陵；
entries.en: The great-grandfather, taboo name Chen, was made Grand Guardian under the Han and later raised to Emperor Mingxian, with the temple name Xizu and the mausoleum Qiling;
entries.literal: The great-grandfather's taboo name was Chen; the Han posthumously made him Grand Guardian, and he was later honored as Emperor Mingxian, with temple name Xizu and mausoleum Qiling;

entries.zh: 曾祖妣鄭國夫人申氏，追謚明孝皇后。
entries.en: Lady Shen of Zheng was posthumously styled Empress Mingxiao.
entries.literal: The great-grandmother, Lady Shen, Lady of Zheng, was posthumously given the title Empress Mingxiao.

entries.zh: 祖諱蘊，漢贈太傅，追尊為翼順皇帝，廟號義祖，陵曰節陵；
entries.en: The grandfather, taboo name Yun, was made Grand Tutor under the Han and later raised to Emperor Yishun, with the temple name Yizu and the mausoleum Jieling;
entries.literal: The grandfather's taboo name was Yun; the Han posthumously made him Grand Tutor, and he was later honored as Emperor Yishun, with temple name Yizu and mausoleum Jieling;

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：溫陵、齊陵、節陵皆無陵所，遙申朝拜。）〉
entries.en: (The Institutional Compendium notes that Wenling, Qiling, and Jieling had no physical burial sites; rites were performed by distant petition.)
entries.literal: (From the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties": Wenling, Qiling, and Jieling all had no actual tomb sites; worship was offered from afar.)

entries.zh: 祖妣陳國夫人韓氏，追謚翼敬皇后。
entries.en: Lady Han of Chen received the posthumous title Empress Yijing.
entries.literal: The grandmother, Lady Han, Lady of Chen, was posthumously given the title Empress Yijing.

entries.zh: 皇考諱簡，漢贈太師，追尊為章肅皇帝，廟號慶祖，陵曰欽陵；
entries.en: His father, taboo name Jian, was made Grand Preceptor under the Han and later raised to Emperor Zhangsu, with the temple name Qingzu and the mausoleum Qinling;
entries.literal: The Imperial Father's taboo name was Jian; the Han posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, and he was later honored as Emperor Zhangsu, with temple name Qingzu and mausoleum Qinling;

entries.zh: 皇妣燕國夫人王氏，追謚為章德皇后。
entries.en: His mother, Lady Wang of Yan, was posthumously styled Empress Zhangde.
entries.literal: The Imperial Mother, Lady Wang, Lady of Yan, was posthumously given the title Empress Zhangde.

entries.zh: 後以唐天祐元年甲子歲七月二十八日，生帝於堯山之舊宅。
entries.en: On the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month in the first Tianyou year of Tang (jiazi), he was born at the family's old home on Yao Mountain.
entries.literal: Later, on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month in the first year of Tianyou of Tang, the year jiazi, the Emperor was born at the old residence on Yao Mountain.

entries.zh: 載誕之夕，赤光照室，有聲如爐炭之裂，星火四迸。
entries.en: On the night he was born, a crimson glow filled the room, charcoal seemed to crackle in the brazier, and sparks burst outward on every side.
entries.literal: On the night of his birth, red light filled the chamber; there was a sound like charcoal splitting in a brazier, and sparks flew in all directions.

entries.zh: 廣順元年春二月癸巳朔，以樞密副使、尚書戶部侍郎範質為兵部侍郎，依前充職；
entries.en: In the first year of Guangshun, on the new moon of the second month of spring, on guisi day, Fan Zhi, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Revenue, was appointed Vice Minister of War while retaining his existing duties;
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangshun, on the new moon of the second month of spring, on the day guisi, Fan Zhi, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Revenue in the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed Vice Minister of War, continuing in his previous office;

entries.zh: 以陳州刺史、判三司李穀為戶部侍郎，判三司；
entries.en: Li Gu, Prefect of Chen and Commissioner of the Three Offices, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and continued as Commissioner of the Three Offices;
entries.literal: Li Gu, Prefect of Chen prefecture and Commissioner of the Three Offices, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of the Three Offices;

entries.zh: 以右金吾大將軍、充街使翟光鄴為左千牛衛上將軍，充宣徽北院使；
entries.en: Zhai Guangye, General of the Right Golden Guard and Street Commissioner, was appointed General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard and Commissioner of the North Bureau of the Palace Secretariat;
entries.literal: Zhai Guangye, General of the Right Golden Guard and Street Commissioner, was made General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard and Commissioner of the North Bureau of the Palace Secretariat;

entries.zh: 以宣徽北院使袁鳷為左武衛上將軍，充宣徽南院使；
entries.en: Yuan Zhi, Commissioner of the North Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner of the South Bureau;
entries.literal: Yuan Zhi, Commissioner of the North Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner of the South Bureau of the Palace Secretariat;

entries.zh: 以左右金吾大將軍、充街使符彥琳為右監門上將軍。
entries.en: Fu Yanlin, General of the Left and Right Golden Guard and Street Commissioner, was appointed General of the Right Gate Guard.
entries.literal: Fu Yanlin, General of the Left and Right Golden Guard and Street Commissioner, was made General of the Right Gate Guard.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以皇子天雄軍牙內都指揮使、檢校右僕射、貴州刺史榮起復為澶州節度使、檢校太保，以右金吾上將軍薛可言為右龍武統軍，以左神武統軍安審約為左羽林統軍，以左驍衛上將軍趙贊為右羽林統軍，以太子太師致仕宋彥筠為左衛上將軍。
entries.en: On dingyou day, Prince Rong, Inner Commander of the Tianxiong Army guard and Acting Right Vice Director, Prefect of Gui, was restored as Military Commissioner of Chan and Acting Grand Guardian; Xue Keyan, General of the Right Golden Guard, became Commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard; An Shenyue, Commander of the Left Divine Martial Guard, became Commander of the Left Forest Feather Guard; Zhao Zan, General of the Left Swift Horse Guard, became Commander of the Right Forest Feather Guard; and Song Yanyun, retired Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, was appointed General of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: On the day dingyou, the prince Rong, Inner Commander of the Tianxiong Army's personal guard and Acting Right Vice Director, Prefect of Gui prefecture, was restored to office as Military Commissioner of Chan prefecture and Acting Grand Guardian; Xue Keyan, General of the Right Golden Guard, was made Commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard; An Shenyue, Commander of the Left Divine Martial Guard, was made Commander of the Left Forest Feather Guard; Zhao Zan, General of the Left Swift Horse Guard, was made Commander of the Right Forest Feather Guard; Song Yanyun, retired Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, was made General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 詔移生吐渾族帳於潞州長子縣江豬嶺。
entries.en: An edict ordered the Tuyuhun encampments moved to Jiangzhu Ridge in Changzi county, Luzhou.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the relocation of the living Tuyuhun tribal encampments to Jiangzhu Ridge in Changzi county, Luzhou.

entries.zh: 己亥，以左武衛上將軍劉遂凝為左神武統軍，以左衛上將軍焦繼勛為右神武統軍，以左領軍衛上將軍史佺為右衛上將軍。
entries.en: On jihai day, Liu Suining, General of the Left Martial Guard, was appointed Commander of the Left Divine Martial Guard; Jiao Jixun, General of the Left Guard, became Commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard; and Shi Quan, General of the Left Military Guard, became General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: On the day jihai, Liu Suining, General of the Left Martial Guard, was made Commander of the Left Divine Martial Guard; Jiao Jixun, General of the Left Guard, was made Commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard; Shi Quan, General of the Left Military Guard, was made General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 庚子，故吳國夫人張氏追贈貴妃；
entries.en: On gengzi day, the late Lady Zhang of Wu was posthumously created Noble Consort;
entries.literal: On the day gengzi, the late Lady Zhang, Lady of the State of Wu, was posthumously honored as Noble Consort;

entries.zh: 故皇第三女追封樂安公主；
entries.en: the late third imperial daughter was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Le'an;
entries.literal: the late third imperial daughter was posthumously created Princess of Le'an;

entries.zh: 故第二子青哥贈太保，賜名侗；
entries.en: the late second son Qingge received the posthumous rank of Grand Guardian and the name Tong;
entries.literal: the late second son Qingge was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the name Tong;

entries.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信；
entries.en: the third son Yige received the posthumous rank of Minister of Works and the name Xin;
entries.literal: the third son Yige was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the name Xin;

entries.zh: 故長婦劉氏追封彭城郡夫人。
entries.en: the late eldest daughter-in-law, Lady Liu, was posthumously created Lady of Pengcheng commandery.
entries.literal: the late eldest daughter-in-law, née Liu, was posthumously created Lady of Pengcheng commandery.

entries.zh: 皇侄三人：守筠贈左領軍將軍，改名願；
entries.en: Three imperial nephews: Shoujun received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Military Guard and was renamed Yuan;
entries.literal: Three imperial nephews: Shoujun was posthumously made General of the Left Military Guard and renamed Yuan;

entries.zh: 奉超贈左監門將軍；
entries.en: Fengchao received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Gate Guard;
entries.literal: Fengchao was posthumously made General of the Left Gate Guard;

entries.zh: 定哥贈左千牛衛將軍，賜名遜。
entries.en: Dingge received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard and the name Xun.
entries.literal: Dingge was posthumously made General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard and given the name Xun.

entries.zh: 故皇孫三人：宜哥贈左驍衛大將軍，賜名誼；
entries.en: Three late imperial grandsons: Yige received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Swift Horse Guard and the name Yi;
entries.literal: Three late imperial grandsons: Yige was posthumously made General of the Left Swift Horse Guard and given the name Yi;

entries.zh: 喜哥贈武衛大將軍，賜名誠；
entries.en: Xige received the posthumous rank of General of the Martial Guard and the name Cheng;
entries.literal: Xige was posthumously made General of the Martial Guard and given the name Cheng;

entries.zh: 三哥贈左領衛大將軍，賜名諴。
entries.en: Sange received the posthumous rank of General of the Left Military Guard and the name Yan.
entries.literal: Sange was posthumously made General of the Left Military Guard and given the name Yan.

entries.zh: 辛丑，西州回鶻遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On xinchou day, the Uyghurs of Xizhou sent tribute envoys with local products.
entries.literal: On the day xinchou, the Uyghurs of Xizhou sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 前開封尹、魯國公侯益進封楚國公，前西京留守、莒國公李從敏進封秦國公，前西京留守王守恩進封莒國公。
entries.en: Former Kaifeng Prefect Hou Yi, Duke of Lu, was promoted to Duke of Chu; former Western Capital Military Governor Li Congmin, Duke of Ju, to Duke of Qin; and former Western Capital Military Governor Wang Shou'en to Duke of Ju.
entries.literal: The former Prefect of Kaifeng and Duke of Lu, Hou Yi, was advanced to Duke of Chu; the former Western Capital Military Governor and Duke of Ju, Li Congmin, was advanced to Duke of Qin; the former Western Capital Military Governor Wang Shou'en was advanced to Duke of Ju.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以前中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事李濤為太子賓客。
entries.en: On guimao day, former Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Tao, who had also served as Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor, was appointed Advisor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: On the day guimao, the former Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, and Grand Councilor Li Tao was made Advisor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 詔宣徽南院使袁鳷權知開封府事，以太子太保和凝為太子太傅。
entries.en: An edict named Yuan Zhi, Commissioner of the South Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, acting Prefect of Kaifeng, and appointed He Ning, Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince, as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Yuan Zhi, Commissioner of the South Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, acting Prefect of Kaifeng, and made He Ning, Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince, Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 丙午，晉州王晏奏，河東劉崇遣偽招討使劉鈞、副招討使白截海，率步騎萬餘人來攻州城，以今月五日五道齊攻，率州兵拒之，賊軍傷死甚眾。
entries.en: On bingwu day, Wang Yan of Jin reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had sent the rebel Pacification Commissioner Liu Jun and Vice Commissioner Bai Jiehai with more than ten thousand foot and horse to assault the city; on the fifth of the month they attacked along five routes, and Yan led the garrison in defense, killing and wounding a great many of the enemy.
entries.literal: On the day bingwu, Wang Yan of Jin prefecture memorialized that Liu Chong of Hedong had sent the false Pacification Commissioner Liu Jun and Vice Pacification Commissioner Bai Jiehai at the head of more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the prefectural city; on the fifth of this month they attacked together along five routes, and he led the prefectural troops to resist them, inflicting very heavy casualties on the rebel army.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·王晏傳》：劉崇侵晉州，晏閉關不出，設伏城上。
entries.en: (According to the History of Song biography of Wang Yan, when Liu Chong invaded Jin, Yan shut the gates and held his men in reserve on the ramparts.
entries.literal: (From the "Biography of Wang Yan" in the History of Song: when Liu Chong invaded Jin prefecture, Yan closed the gates and did not come out, setting ambushes atop the walls.

entries.zh: 並人以為怯，競攀堞而登，晏麾伏兵擊之，顛死者甚眾，遂焚橋遁。
entries.en: The Bing soldiers took him for a coward and scrambled up the parapets; Yan signaled his ambush, and a great many fell to their deaths; the enemy then burned the bridge and fled.
entries.literal: The Bing troops thought him cowardly and vied to climb the battlements; Yan waved his hidden troops to strike them, and very many fell headlong to their deaths; they then burned the bridge and fled.

entries.zh: 晏遣子漢倫追北數十里，斬首百餘級。）〉
entries.en: Yan sent his son Hanlun in pursuit for several tens of li and took more than a hundred heads.) (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: Yan sent his son Hanlun in pursuit north for several tens of li and took more than a hundred heads.) (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 內出寶玉器及金銀結縷、寶裝床幾、飲食之具數十，碎之於殿庭。
entries.en: Several dozen pieces of precious jade, gold and silver filigree, jewel-mounted beds and tables, and dining ware were brought out from the inner palace and smashed in the courtyard.
entries.literal: From within the palace were brought out several tens of precious jades, gold and silver filigree work, jewel-inlaid beds and tables, and dining utensils, and they were smashed in the palace courtyard.

entries.zh: 帝謂侍臣曰：「凡為帝王，安用此！」
entries.en: The emperor told his attendants, "What use has a ruler for such things!"
entries.literal: The emperor said to his attending officials: "What need has one who would be emperor for such things!"

entries.zh: 仍詔所司，凡珍華悅目之物，不得入宮。
entries.en: He also ordered that no rare or ornamental objects meant merely to please the eye were to enter the palace.
entries.literal: He further ordered the responsible offices that whatever rare and splendid objects pleasing to the eye must not be brought into the palace.

entries.zh: 先是，回鶻間歲入貢，禁民不得與蕃人市易寶貨，至是一聽私便交易，官不禁詰。
entries.en: Previously, when the Uyghurs sent tribute in alternate years, commoners were barred from trading valuables with foreigners; now private trade was freely allowed and officials no longer prohibited or investigated it.
entries.literal: Previously, when the Uyghurs presented tribute every other year, the people were forbidden to trade precious goods with foreigners; now private trade was entirely permitted at convenience, and the authorities did not prohibit or investigate it.

entries.zh: 丁未，左千牛將軍朱憲使契丹回。
entries.en: On dingwei day, Zhu Xian, General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard, returned from his embassy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On the day dingwei, Zhu Xian, General of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard, returned from his mission to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 契丹主烏裕遣使郭濟獻良馬一駟，賀登極。
entries.en: The Khitan ruler Wuyu sent the envoy Guo Ji with a team of fine horses to congratulate the emperor on his accession.
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler Wuyu sent the envoy Guo Ji presenting a team of fine horses in congratulations on the assumption of the throne.

entries.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「朕祗膺景命，奄有中區，每思順物之情，從眾之欲。
entries.en: On wushen day, an edict declared: "Having reverently received Heaven's mandate and come to rule the central realm, We constantly seek to align with the natural order and heed the people's wishes.
entries.literal: On the day wushen, an edict said: "We reverently received the luminous mandate and suddenly hold the central realm; we constantly think to accord with the disposition of things and follow the desires of the multitude.

entries.zh: 將使照臨之下，多寄食僦舍之徒；
entries.en: We would not have so many under Our rule living as lodgers in rented quarters;
entries.literal: We wish that under Our illumination there may not be so many who lodge and take meals in rented quarters;

entries.zh: 歲月之間，動懷土念家之思。
entries.en: year after year burdened with homesickness and longing for their native places.
entries.literal: as the months and years pass, they are constantly moved by thoughts of native soil and longing for home.

entries.zh: 宜循大體，用革前規。
entries.en: It is right to act on broad principle and reform the old rules.
entries.literal: It is fitting to follow the great principle and reform the former regulations.

entries.zh: 應諸道州府，有前資朝官居住，如未赴京，不得發遣。
entries.en: In every circuit and prefecture, former capital officials residing locally who have not been summoned to court must not be compelled to leave.
entries.literal: In all circuits and prefectures, where former capital officials of prior service reside, if they have not gone to the capital they must not be sent away.

entries.zh: 其行軍副使已下，幕職州縣官等，得替求官，自有月限，年月未滿，一聽外居。
entries.en: For army deputy commissioners and below, and for prefectural, county, and staff officials seeking new posts after leaving office, the prescribed waiting period applies; until it is complete, they may all live outside the capital.
entries.literal: As for army deputy commissioners and below, staff of prefectures and counties, and the like, when relieved of office and seeking new appointment they have their own monthly limits; if the term of months and years is not complete, they are entirely permitted to reside outside the capital.

entries.zh: 如非時詔征，不在此限。」
entries.en: Extraordinary summons by edict are excepted from this rule."
entries.literal: If there is an extraordinary edict summoning them, this limit does not apply."

entries.zh: 己酉，有司議立四親廟，從之。
entries.en: On jiyou day, the responsible offices proposed establishing a temple to four generations of ancestors, and the court approved.
entries.literal: On the day jiyou, the responsible offices debated establishing a temple to four generations of forebears, and the proposal was approved.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以太子少傅楊凝式為太子少師，以太常卿張昭為戶部尚書，以尚書左丞王易為禮部尚書，以兵部侍郎邊蔚為太常卿，以翰林學士、中書舍人魚崇諒為工部侍郎充職，以戶部侍郎韋勛為兵部侍郎，以刑部侍郎邊歸讜為戶部侍郎，以禮部侍郎司徒詡為刑部侍郎，以秘書監趙上交為禮部侍郎，以兵部尚書王仁裕為太子少保，以翰林學士、禮部尚書張沆為刑部尚書充職，以尚書右丞田敏為左丞，以吏部侍郎段希堯為工部尚書，以太子詹事馬裔孫為太子賓客。
entries.en: On xinhai day, Yang Ningshi moved from Junior Tutor to Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince; Zhang Zhao from Director of Imperial Sacrifices to Minister of Revenue; Wang Yi from Left Vice Director of State Affairs to Minister of Rites; Bian Wei from Vice Minister of War to Director of Imperial Sacrifices; Yu Chongliang, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafting Official, to Vice Minister of Works; Wei Xun from Vice Minister of Revenue to Vice Minister of War; Bian Guichan from Vice Minister of Justice to Vice Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu from Vice Minister of Rites to Vice Minister of Justice; Zhao Shangjiao from Director of the Palace Library to Vice Minister of Rites; Wang Renyu from Minister of War to Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince; Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician and Minister of Rites, to Minister of Justice; Tian Min from Right to Left Vice Director of State Affairs; Duan Xiyao from Vice Minister of Personnel to Minister of Works; and Ma Yisun from Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent to Advisor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: On the day xinhai, Yang Ningshi, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, was made Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince; Zhang Zhao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Minister of Revenue; Wang Yi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Minister of Rites; Bian Wei, Vice Minister of War, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Yu Chongliang, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafting Official, was made Vice Minister of Works in his office; Wei Xun, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Minister of War; Bian Guichan, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice; Zhao Shangjiao, Director of the Palace Library, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Wang Renyu, Minister of War, was made Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince; Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician and Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Justice in his office; Tian Min, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Left Vice Director; Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Personnel, was made Minister of Works; Ma Yisun, Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent, was made Advisor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 前鄜州節度使劉重進、前滑州節度使宋延渥，並加食邑。
entries.en: Former Military Commissioners Liu Chongjin of Fu and Song Yanwo of Hua both received increases to their fief income.
entries.literal: The former Military Commissioners of Fu prefecture, Liu Chongjin, and of Hua prefecture, Song Yanwo, were both granted additional fief income.

entries.zh: 吐渾府留後王全德加檢校太保，充憲州刺史。
entries.en: Wang Quande, Acting Commissioner of the Tuyuhun Prefecture, was appointed Acting Grand Guardian and Prefect of Xian.
entries.literal: Wang Quande, Acting Commissioner of the Tuyuhun Prefecture, was made Acting Grand Guardian and appointed Prefect of Xian prefecture.

entries.zh: 隰州刺史許遷奏，河東賊軍劉筠自晉州引兵來攻州城，尋以州兵拒之，賊軍傷死者五百人，信宿遁去。
entries.en: Xu Qian, Prefect of Xi, reported that Liu Jun's Hedong rebels had marched from Jin to attack the city; he led the garrison in defense, killing or wounding five hundred of the enemy, who withdrew after a day and a night.
entries.literal: Xu Qian, Prefect of Xi prefecture, memorialized that the Hedong rebel army under Liu Jun had led troops from Jin prefecture to attack the prefectural city; shortly afterward he led the prefectural troops to resist them, and five hundred of the rebel army were killed or wounded; after one night and day they fled.

entries.zh: 丁已，以尚書左丞田敏充契丹國信使。
entries.en: On dingsi day, Tian Min, Left Vice Director of State Affairs, was appointed credentialed envoy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On the day dingsi, Tian Min, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed envoy bearing the state's credentials to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 回鶻遣使貢方物。
entries.en: The Uyghurs sent tribute envoys with local products.
entries.literal: The Uyghurs sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 己未，天德軍節度使、虢國公郭勛加同平章事，以前宗正卿劉皞為衛尉卿。
entries.en: On jiwei day, Guo Xun, Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army and Duke of Guo, was made Concurrent Grand Councilor; former Director of the Imperial Clan Court Liu Hao became Chamberlain for the Guards.
entries.literal: On the day jiwei, Guo Xun, Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army and Duke of Guo, was made Concurrent Grand Councilor; the former Director of the Imperial Clan Court Liu Hao was made Chamberlain for the Guards.

entries.zh: 辛酉，以衛尉卿邊光範為秘書監，以前吏部侍郎李詳為吏部侍郎，以前戶部侍郎顏衎為尚書右丞。
entries.en: On xinyou day, Bian Guangfan moved from Chamberlain for the Guards to Director of the Palace Library; former Vice Minister of Personnel Li Xiang returned as Vice Minister of Personnel; and former Vice Minister of Revenue Yan Kan became Right Vice Director of State Affairs.
entries.literal: On the day xinyou, Bian Guangfan, Chamberlain for the Guards, was made Director of the Palace Library; the former Vice Minister of Personnel Li Xiang was made Vice Minister of Personnel; the former Vice Minister of Revenue Yan Kan was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 三月壬戌朔，前西京留守李從敏卒。
entries.en: In the third month, on the new moon of renxu day, former Western Capital Military Governor Li Congmin died.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the new moon of the day renxu, the former Western Capital Military Governor Li Congmin died.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以前左武衛上將軍李懷忠為太子太傅致仕，以前邢州節度使安審暉為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: On wuchen day, former General of the Left Martial Guard Li Huaizhong was granted retirement as Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince, and former Military Commissioner of Xing, An Shenhui, as retired Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen, the former General of the Left Martial Guard Li Huaizhong was made retired Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince; the former Military Commissioner of Xing prefecture An Shenhui was made retired Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 辛未，幸南莊。
entries.en: On xinwei day, the emperor visited the Southern Estate.
entries.literal: On the day xinwei, the emperor visited the Southern Estate.

entries.zh: 壬申，詔曰：「諸州府先差散從親事官等，前朝創置，蓋出權宜，茍便一時，本非舊貫。
entries.en: On renshen day, an edict declared: "The personal attendants and intimate staff officials previously assigned by prefectures and districts were a creation of the prior dynasty—expedients for the moment, not part of long-standing practice.
entries.literal: On the day renshen, an edict said: "The various prefectures and districts had previously been assigned personal attendants and intimate staff officials and the like; these were created by the previous dynasty as expedients, merely for temporary convenience, and were not originally part of established practice.

entries.zh: 近者遍詢群議，兼采封章，且言前件抽差，於理不甚允當，一則礙州縣之色役，一則妨春夏之耕耘，貧乏者困於供須，豪富者幸於影庇，既為煩擾，須至改更，況當東作之時，宜罷不急之務。
entries.en: We have lately consulted widely and reviewed memorials stating that such requisitioning is unjust: it blocks local corvée obligations and disrupts spring and summer farming; the poor are burdened with supplies while the wealthy profit from sheltering dependents. Because the practice is oppressive, it must be changed—and now, at the height of the planting season, nonessential duties should cease.
entries.literal: Recently we have broadly inquired of collective opinion and also taken up memorials, which state that the aforesaid requisitioning is not very reasonable in principle: on the one hand it obstructs the corvée duties of prefectures and counties, on the other it hinders spring and summer plowing and sowing; the poor are distressed by supplies demanded of them, while the wealthy profit from sheltering others under their names; since it is vexatious, reform is necessary; moreover, as it is the season of eastern cultivation, inessential tasks should be halted.

entries.zh: 其諸州所差散從親事官等，並宜放散。」
entries.en: All personal attendants and intimate staff officials assigned by the prefectures are to be dismissed."
entries.literal: The personal attendants and intimate staff officials assigned by the various prefectures should all be dismissed."

entries.zh: 詔下，公私便之。
entries.en: Once the edict was promulgated, officials and commoners alike found relief.
entries.literal: When the edict was issued, it was convenient for both public and private interests.

entries.zh: 徐州行營都部署王彥超馳奏，收復徐州。
entries.en: Wang Yanchao, Commander-in-Chief of the Xuzhou field headquarters, urgently reported the recapture of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Yanchao, Commander-in-Chief of the Xuzhou Field Headquarters, sent an urgent memorial reporting the recovery of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 「城內逆首楊溫及親近徒黨並處斬。
entries.en: "The rebel leader Yang Wen in the city and his close followers were all executed.
entries.literal: "The rebel leader Yang Wen within the city and his close associates were all executed.

entries.zh: 其餘無名目人及本城軍都將校、職掌吏民等，雖被脅從，本非同惡，並釋放。
entries.en: All others—unranked men, garrison commanders and officers, clerks, and townspeople—though coerced, were not true accomplices and were released.
entries.literal: The rest—persons without formal status, the army commanders and officers of the city, clerks and commoners in office, and the like—although coerced, were not originally of one mind with the wicked, and were all released.

entries.zh: 兼知自前楊溫招喚草賊，同力守把，朕以村墅小民，偶被扇誘，念其庸賤，特與含容，其招入城草賊，並放歸農，仍倍加安撫。
entries.en: It is also known that Yang Wen had earlier recruited rural bandits to help defend the city. We regard these village folk as having been misled in passing; mindful of their humble station, We extend special leniency: the rural recruits brought into the city are all sent home to farm and given extra reassurance.
entries.literal: It is also known that previously Yang Wen had summoned bandits from the countryside to join in holding the defenses together; We regard these village and hamlet commoners as having been incidentally incited, and considering their low and mean station, We specially extend forbearance; the bandits summoned into the city are all released to return to farming, and are to receive doubled reassurance.

entries.zh: 湘陰公夫人並骨肉在彼，仰差人安撫守護，勿令驚恐。」
entries.en: The Duchess of Xiangyin and her family who remain there are to be reassured and protected by dispatched officials, without alarm."
entries.literal: The lady of Duke of Xiangyin and her kin who are there—officials are ordered to send persons to reassure and protect them, and not to let them be frightened."

entries.zh: 以右散騎常侍張煦、給事中王延藹並為左散騎常侍，以前大名府少尹李瓊為將作監，以前彰武軍節度使周密為太子太師致仕，以衛尉卿劉皞充漢隱帝山陵部署。
entries.en: Zhang Xu, Regular Attendant of the Right Cavalry, and Wang Yan'ai, Drafting Official, were both appointed Regular Attendants of the Left Cavalry; former Junior Prefect of Daming Li Qiong became Director of Palace Construction; former Military Commissioner of the Zhangwu Army Zhou Mi received retirement as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; and Liu Hao, Chamberlain for the Guards, was placed in charge of arrangements for Hidden Emperor of Han's mausoleum.
entries.literal: Zhang Xu, Regular Attendant of the Right Cavalry, and Wang Yan'ai, Drafting Official in the Secretariat, were both made Regular Attendants of the Left Cavalry; the former Junior Prefect of Daming Fu Li Qiong was made Director of Palace Construction; the former Military Commissioner of the Zhangwu Army Zhou Mi was made retired Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; Liu Hao, Chamberlain for the Guards, was appointed to the arrangements for the mausoleum of Emperor Yin of Han.

entries.zh: 丙子，以太子少保致仕王延為太子少傅，以戶部尚書致仕盧損、左驍衛上將軍致仕李肅並為太子少保，兵部尚書致仕韓昭允為尚書右僕射，太子太師致仕盧文紀為司空。
entries.en: On bingzi day, Wang Yan moved from retired Junior Guardian to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince; Lu Sun, retired Minister of Revenue, and Li Su, retired General of the Left Swift Horse Guard, both became Junior Guardians of the Crown Prince; Han Zhaoyun, retired Minister of War, became Right Vice Director of State Affairs; and Lu Wenji, retired Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, became Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On the day bingzi, Wang Yan, retired Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, was made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince; Lu Sun, retired Minister of Revenue, and Li Su, retired General of the Left Swift Horse Guard, were both made Junior Guardians of the Crown Prince; Han Zhaoyun, retired Minister of War, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Lu Wenji, retired Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 自延而下，並依前致仕。
entries.en: From Yan downward, all remained in retirement as before.
entries.literal: From Yan downward, all continued in retirement as before.

entries.zh: 故散騎常侍裴羽贈戶部尚書，故太子賓客蕭願贈禮部尚書，以司農卿致仕薛仁謙為鴻臚卿，以將作監致仕烏昭為太府卿，以太常少卿致仕王禧為少府監，以秘書少監致仕段颙為將作監。
entries.en: The late Regular Attendant Pei Yu was posthumously created Minister of Revenue; the late Crown Prince's Advisor Xiao Yuan, Minister of Rites; Xue Renqian, retired Director of the Imperial Granaries, became Chamberlain for Dependencies; Wu Zhao, retired Director of Palace Construction, Chamberlain for the Imperial Household; Wang Xi, retired Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Palace Workshop; and Duan Yong, retired Vice Director of the Palace Library, Director of Palace Construction.
entries.literal: The late Regular Attendant Pei Yu was posthumously made Minister of Revenue; the late Advisor to the Crown Prince Xiao Yuan was posthumously made Minister of Rites; Xue Renqian, retired Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, was made Chamberlain for Dependencies; Wu Zhao, retired Director of Palace Construction, was made Chamberlain for the Imperial Household; Wang Xi, retired Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Director of the Palace Workshop; Duan Yong, retired Vice Director of the Palace Library, was made Director of Palace Construction.

entries.zh: 自仁謙而下，並依前致仕。
entries.en: From Renqian downward, all remained in retirement as before.
entries.literal: From Renqian downward, all continued in retirement as before.

entries.zh: 詔沿淮州縣軍鎮，今後自守疆土，不得縱一人一騎擅入淮南地分。
entries.en: An edict commanded prefectures, counties, and garrisons along the Huai hereafter to hold their own borders and not allow any man or horse to cross into Huainan without authorization.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the prefectures, counties, and garrisons along the Huai to guard their own territories hereafter and not to allow a single man or horse to enter the Huainan region on their own authority.

entries.zh: 己卯，潞州奏，涉縣所擒河東將士二百餘人，部送赴闕。
entries.en: On jimao day, Luzhou reported that more than two hundred Hedong officers and soldiers captured in She county were being escorted to court.
entries.literal: On the day jimao, Luzhou memorialized that more than two hundred Hedong officers and soldiers captured in She county were being escorted to the court.

entries.zh: 詔給衫袴巾屨，放歸本土。
entries.en: An edict supplied them with clothing and footwear and sent them home.
entries.literal: An edict provided them with jackets, trousers, headcloths, and shoes, and released them to their native regions.

entries.zh: 甲申，鎮州武行德移鎮許州，何福進移鎮鎮州。
entries.en: On jiashen day, Wu Xingde transferred from Zhen to Xu, and He Fujin from his post to Zhen.
entries.literal: On the day jiashen, Wu Xingde of Zhen prefecture was transferred to Xu prefecture, and He Fujin was transferred to Zhen prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以襄州節度副使郭令圖為宗正卿。
entries.en: On bingxu day, Guo Lingtu, Deputy Military Commissioner of Xiang, was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
entries.literal: On the day bingxu, Guo Lingtu, Deputy Military Commissioner of Xiang prefecture, was made Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「故蘇逢吉、劉銖，頃在漢朝，與朕同事。
entries.en: An edict declared: "The late Su Fengji and Liu Zhu once served with Us in the Han court.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The late Su Fengji and Liu Zhu, who not long ago in the Han dynasty served together with Us,

entries.zh: 朕自平禍亂，不念仇讎，尋示優宏，與全家屬。
entries.en: Since We pacified the turmoil, We have not held old grudges and soon showed their whole families generous mercy.
entries.literal: since We pacified the turmoil have not borne old enmities in mind, and soon showed generous magnanimity toward their entire families.

entries.zh: 尚以幼稚無托，衣食是艱，將行矜恤之恩，俾獲生存之路，報怨以德，非我負人。
entries.en: Yet their young children are unsupported and lack food and clothing; We will extend compassionate care so they may survive—repaying enmity with kindness, for We have not wronged others.
entries.literal: Yet because their young children are without support and food and clothing are hard to obtain, We shall extend compassionate care so that they may gain a path to survival; to repay enmity with virtue—We have not wronged others.

entries.zh: 賜逢吉骨肉洛京莊宅各一，賜劉銖骨肉陜州莊宅各一。」
entries.en: We grant Fengji's kin an estate each in the Luoyang capital, and Liu Zhu's kin an estate each in Shan."
entries.literal: We grant to Fengji's kin one estate in the Luoyang capital each, and to Liu Zhu's kin one estate in Shan prefecture each."

entries.zh: 己丑，幸南莊。
entries.en: On jichou day, the emperor visited the Southern Estate.
entries.literal: On the day jichou, the emperor visited the Southern Estate.

entries.zh: 庚寅，唐故郇國公李從益追封許王，唐明宗淑妃王氏追贈賢妃。
entries.en: On gengyin day, Li Congyi, late Duke of Xun of Tang, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xu; and Virtuous Consort Wang of Tang Emperor Mingzong was posthumously created Worthy Consort.
entries.literal: On the day gengyin, Li Congyi, the late Duke of Xun of Tang, was posthumously created Prince of Xu; the late Virtuous Consort Wang of Tang Emperor Mingzong was posthumously honored as Worthy Consort.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔：「諸道節度副使、行軍司馬、兩京少尹、留守判官，並許差定當直，人力不得過十五人；
entries.en: On xinmao day, an edict declared: "Deputy military commissioners, army marshals, junior prefects of the two capitals, and military governors' judicial assessors may assign fixed duty attendants, but not more than fifteen persons;
entries.literal: On the day xinmao, an edict said: "Deputy military commissioners of the circuits, army marshals, junior prefects of the two capitals, and military governors' judicial assessors are all permitted to assign fixed duty attendants, and manpower must not exceed fifteen persons;

entries.zh: 諸府少尹、書記、支使、防禦團練副使，不得過十人；
entries.en: junior prefects, secretaries, branch commissioners, and deputy defense and training commissioners may not exceed ten;
entries.literal: junior prefects of prefectures, secretaries, branch commissioners, and deputy commissioners of defense and training regiments must not exceed ten persons;

entries.zh: 節度推官、防卸團練軍事判官，不得過七人，逐處系帳收管。
entries.en: judicial reviewers of military commissioners and military assessors of defense and training regiments may not exceed seven, and each post must keep them on the official rolls.
entries.literal: judicial reviewers of military commissioners and military judicial assessors of defense and training regiments must not exceed seven persons; in each place they are to be registered and kept on the rolls.

entries.zh: 此外如敢額外影占人戶，其本官當行朝典。」
entries.en: Anyone who covertly registers extra households beyond these limits shall face court discipline against the responsible official."
entries.literal: Beyond this, if anyone dares to take additional households under covert registration, the responsible official shall be subject to court punishment."

entries.zh: 先是，漢隱帝時，有人上言：「州府從事令錄，皆請料錢，自合雇人驅使，不合差遣百姓丁戶。」
entries.en: Earlier, under Hidden Emperor of Han, a memorial had argued that prefectural staff and recorders, who received stipends, should hire their own servants and not requisition commoners for corvée."
entries.literal: Previously, in the time of Hidden Emperor of Han, someone submitted a memorial saying: "Prefectural and district staff officials and recorders all receive stipends and should hire persons to serve them themselves; they ought not requisition commoners' corvée households."

entries.zh: 秉政者然之，乃下詔州府從事令錄，本處先差職役，並放歸農。
entries.en: The authorities agreed and ordered that corvée laborers previously assigned to prefectural staff and recorders be released to farming.
entries.literal: Those holding power approved this, and an edict was issued that the staff officials and recorders of prefectures and districts who had previously been assigned corvée duties locally were all released to return to farming.

entries.zh: 自是官吏有獨行趨府縣者，帝頗知之，故有是命。
entries.en: Afterward officials were seen traveling alone to prefectures and counties, which the emperor well knew—hence this order.
entries.literal: From this time officials were seen going alone to prefectures and districts, which the emperor knew quite well, and therefore there was this order.

entries.zh: 夏四月壬辰朔，詔沿淮州縣，許淮南人就淮北糴易糇糧，時淮南饑故也。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of renchen day, an edict allowed Huainan people to buy dry grain north of the Huai, as Huainan was then in famine.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of the day renchen, an edict ordered the prefectures and counties along the Huai to permit people of Huainan to come to Huaibei to purchase and exchange dry provisions, because Huainan was then suffering famine.

entries.zh: 甲午，以夫人董氏為德妃，仍令所司備禮冊命。
entries.en: On jiawu day, Lady Dong was created Virtuous Consort, and the responsible offices were ordered to prepare investiture rites.
entries.literal: On the day jiawu, Lady Dong was made Virtuous Consort, and the responsible offices were ordered to prepare the rites of investiture.

entries.zh: 己亥，改侍衛馬步軍軍額。
entries.en: On jihai day, the designations of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies were changed.
entries.literal: On the day jihai, the designations of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies were changed.

entries.zh: 馬軍舊稱護聖，今改為龍捷；
entries.en: The horse army, formerly Guard of the Sage, was renamed Dragon Swift;
entries.literal: the horse army, formerly called Guard of the Sage, was now changed to Dragon Swift;

entries.zh: 步軍舊稱奉國，今改為虎捷。
entries.en: the foot army, formerly Serving the State, was renamed Tiger Swift.
entries.literal: the foot army, formerly called Serving the State, was now changed to Tiger Swift.

entries.zh: 壬寅，詔唐莊宗、明宗、晉高祖三處陵寢，各有守陵宮人，並放逐便。
entries.en: On renyin day, an edict ordered the palace women guarding the mausoleums of Tang Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Jin Gaozu all dismissed and sent away.
entries.literal: On the day renyin, an edict ordered that at the three mausoleum sites of Tang Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Jin Gaozu, each of which had palace women guarding the tombs, they were all to be dismissed and sent away as convenient.

entries.zh: 如願在陵所者，依舊供給。
entries.en: Those who wished to remain at the tombs were to be supplied as before.
entries.literal: Those who wished to remain at the mausoleum sites were to be supplied as before.

entries.zh: 甲辰，相州張彥成移鎮鄧州，折從阮移鎮滑州，李筠移鎮相州。
entries.en: On jiachen day, Zhang Yancheng transferred from Xiang to Deng, Zhe Congruan to Hua, and Li Jun to Xiang.
entries.literal: On the day jiachen, Zhang Yancheng of Xiang prefecture was transferred to Deng prefecture, Zhe Congruan was transferred to Hua prefecture, and Li Jun was transferred to Xiang prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙午，亳州防卸使王重裔卒。
entries.en: On bingwu day, Wang Chongyi, Defense Commissioner of Bozhou, died.
entries.literal: On the day bingwu, Wang Chongyi, Commissioner of Defense of Bozhou, died.

entries.zh: 戊申，幸南莊。
entries.en: On wushen day, the emperor visited the Southern Estate.
entries.literal: On the day wushen, the emperor visited the Southern Estate.

entries.zh: 庚戌，皇第四女封壽安公主。
entries.en: On gengxu day, the fourth imperial daughter was enfeoffed as Princess of Shou'an.
entries.literal: On the day gengxu, the fourth imperial daughter was created Princess of Shou'an.

entries.zh: 辛亥，故許州節度使劉信追封蔡王。
entries.en: On xinhai day, Liu Xin, late Military Commissioner of Xu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai.
entries.literal: On the day xinhai, Liu Xin, the late Military Commissioner of Xu prefecture, was posthumously created Prince of Cai.

entries.zh: 丙辰，詔曰：「牧守之任，委遇非輕，分憂之務既同，制祿之數宜等。
entries.en: On bingchen day, an edict declared: "The office of prefect and governor is no light trust; since their burden of shared governance is the same, their regulated salaries ought to be equal.
entries.literal: On the day bingchen, an edict said: "The charge of prefects and governors is no light commission; since the duty of sharing cares is the same, the regulated salary amounts ought to be equal.

entries.zh: 自前有富庶之郡，請給則優，或邊侄之州，俸料素薄。
entries.en: Formerly wealthy prefectures received generous allowances on request, while some border prefectures had always had meager salaries.
entries.literal: From of old wealthy and populous commanderies received generous allowances when requested, while some border prefectures had always had thin salaries.

entries.zh: 以至遷除之際，擬議亦難，既論資敘之高低，又患祿秩之升降。
entries.en: At transfers and promotions deliberation was difficult, weighing both seniority and the rise and fall of salary grades.
entries.literal: Thus at the time of transfers and promotions deliberation was also difficult, for one must consider both the high and low of seniority and rank, and also worry over the rise and fall of salary grades.

entries.zh: 所宜分多益寡，均利同恩，冀無黨無偏，以勸勛效。
entries.en: The court should take from the abundant to aid the meager, equalize benefits and share favor alike, and seek impartiality so as to encourage loyal service.
entries.literal: It is fitting to take from the many to benefit the few, equalize profit and share grace alike, hoping for neither faction nor partiality, so as to encourage meritorious service.

entries.zh: 今定諸防禦使料錢二百貫，祿粟一百石，食鹽五石，馬十匹草粟，元隨三十人衣糧；
entries.en: Defense commissioners were now fixed at two hundred strings of stipend cash, one hundred piculs of salary grain, five piculs of salt, fodder for ten horses, and provisions for thirty personal attendants;
entries.literal: Now it is fixed that defense commissioners receive two hundred strings of stipend cash, one hundred piculs of salary grain, five piculs of salt for consumption, fodder for ten horses, and provisions for thirty original followers;

entries.zh: 團練使一百五十貫，祿粟七十石，鹽五石，馬十匹，元隨三十人；
entries.en: training regiment commissioners at one hundred fifty strings, seventy piculs of salary grain, five piculs of salt, ten horses, and thirty attendants;
entries.literal: training regiment commissioners one hundred fifty strings, seventy piculs of salary grain, five piculs of salt, ten horses, and thirty original followers;

entries.zh: 刺史一百貫，祿粟五十石，鹽五石，馬五匹，元隨二十人」云。
entries.en: and prefects at one hundred strings, fifty piculs of salary grain, five piculs of salt, five horses, and twenty attendants," the edict concluded.
entries.literal: prefects one hundred strings, fifty piculs of salary grain, five piculs of salt, five horses, and twenty original followers," it was said.

entries.zh: 丁巳，尚書左丞田敏使契丹回。
entries.en: On dingsi day, Tian Min, Left Vice Director of State Affairs, returned from his embassy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On the day dingsi, Tian Min, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, returned from his mission to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 契丹主兀欲遣。
entries.en: The Khitan ruler Wuyu sent
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler Wuyu sent

entries.zh: 使耨姑報命，並獻碧玉金塗銀裹鞍勒各一副，弓矢、器仗、貂裘等，土產馬三十匹、土產漢馬十匹。
entries.en: the envoy Nuguga to report in reply, together with jade saddles with gold inlay and silver mountings, bows and arrows, arms and armor, sable furs, thirty native horses, and ten native Han horses.
entries.literal: the envoy Nuguga to report in reply, and also presented one set each of jade-and-gold-inlaid silver-mounted saddles and bridles, bows and arrows, weapons and armor, sable furs, and the like, thirty native horses and ten native Han horses.

entries.zh: 庚申，帝為故貴妃張氏舉哀於舊宮，輟視朝三日。
entries.en: On gengshen day, the emperor mourned the late Noble Consort Zhang at the former palace and suspended court for three days.
entries.literal: On the day gengshen, the emperor conducted mourning for the late Noble Consort Zhang at the former palace and suspended court audiences for three days.

entries.zh: 辛酉，司空致仕盧文紀卒。
entries.en: On xinyou day, Lu Wenji, retired Minister of Works, died.
entries.literal: On the day xinyou, Lu Wenji, retired Minister of Works, died.

entries.zh: 八月辛卯，漢隱帝梓宮發引，帝詣太平宮臨奠，詔群臣出祖於西郊。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on xinmao day, Hidden Emperor of Han's coffin was sent forth; the emperor went to the Palace of Great Peace to mourn and ordered the ministers to perform farewell rites at the western suburb.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on xinmao day, the coffin of Hidden Emperor of Han was sent forth; the emperor went to the Palace of Great Peace to offer libations and ordered the ministers to perform the farewell rites at the western suburb.

entries.zh: 是歲，幽州饑，流人散入滄州界。
entries.en: That year You prefecture suffered famine, and refugees scattered into Cang prefecture.
entries.literal: That year, You prefecture suffered famine, and refugees scattered into the borders of Cang prefecture.

entries.zh: 詔流人至者，口給鬥粟，仍給無主土田，令取便種蒔，放免差稅。
entries.en: An edict ordered that arriving refugees receive a dou of grain per person, be granted ownerless land to plant as they chose, and be exempted from corvée and taxes.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that refugees who arrived be given a dou of grain per person, and also granted ownerless land for them to plant as convenient, with corvée and tax obligations waived.

entries.zh: 癸已，虎入西京修行寺傷人，市民殺之。
entries.en: On guisi day, a tiger entered Xingxing Temple in the Western Capital and injured people; townspeople killed it.
entries.literal: On the day guisi, a tiger entered the Xingxing Temple in the Western Capital and injured people; townspeople killed it.

entries.zh: 乙未，幸班荊館。
entries.en: On yiwei day, the emperor visited the Lodge for Parting Guests.
entries.literal: On the day yiwei, the emperor visited the Lodge for Parting Guests.

entries.zh: 壬寅，契丹遣幽州牙將曹繼筠來歸故晉中書令趙瑩之喪，詔贈太傅，仍賜其子絹五百匹，以備喪事，歸葬於華陰故裏。
entries.en: On renyin day, the Khitan sent You military adjutant Cao Jijun to return the remains of late Jin Director of the Secretariat Zhao Ying; the court posthumously created him Grand Mentor, granted his son five hundred bolts of silk for the funeral, and ordered burial in his native Huayin.
entries.literal: On the day renyin, the Khitan sent Cao Jijun, a military adjutant of You prefecture, to return the remains of the late Jin Director of the Secretariat Zhao Ying; an edict posthumously made him Grand Mentor and also granted his son five hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses, with burial in his old home in Huayin.

entries.zh: 乙巳，幸西莊。
entries.en: On yisi day, the emperor visited the Western Estate.
entries.literal: On the day yisi, the emperor visited the Western Estate.

entries.zh: 壬子，晉州王晏移鎮徐州，滄州王景移鎮河中，定州孫方簡移鎮華州，永興郭從義移鎮許州，貝州王繼宏移鎮河陽，李暉移鎮滄州。
entries.en: On renzi day, Wang Yan transferred from Jin to Xu, Wang Jing from Cang to Hezhong, Sun Fangjian from Ding to Hua, Guo Congyi from Yongxing to Xu, Wang Jihong from Bei to Heyang, and Li Hui to Cang.
entries.literal: On the day renzi, Wang Yan of Jin prefecture was transferred to Xu prefecture, Wang Jing of Cang to Hezhong, Sun Fangjian of Ding to Hua, Guo Congyi of Yongxing to Xu, Wang Jihong of Bei to Heyang, and Li Hui to Cang.

entries.zh: 以許州節度使武行德為西京留守，滑州折從阮移鎮陜州，河中扈彥珂移鎮滑州，陜州李洪信移鎮永興，華州王饒移鎮貝州，徐州王彥超移鎮晉州。
entries.en: Wu Xingde, Military Commissioner of Xu, became Military Governor of the Western Capital; Zhe Congruan transferred from Hua to Shan; Hu Yanke from Hezhong to Hua; Li Hongxin from Shan to Yongxing; Wang Rao from Hua to Bei; and Wang Yanchao from Xu to Jin.
entries.literal: Wu Xingde, Military Commissioner of Xu prefecture, was made Military Governor of the Western Capital; Zhe Congruan of Hua was transferred to Shan prefecture; Hu Yanke of Hezhong to Hua; Li Hongxin of Shan to Yongxing; Wang Rao of Hua to Bei; and Wang Yanchao of Xu to Jin.

entries.zh: 丙辰，尚食李氏等宮官八人並封縣君，司記劉氏等六人並封郡夫人，尚宮皇甫氏等三人並封國夫人。
entries.en: On bingchen day, eight palace officials including Li of Imperial Food were created county ladies; six including Liu of Records, commandery ladies; and three including Huangfu of Palace Attendants, state ladies.
entries.literal: On the day bingchen, eight palace officials including Li of the Bureau of Imperial Food were all created Ladies of a county; six including Liu of the Bureau of Records were all created Ladies of a commandery; and three including Huangfu of the Palace Attendants Bureau were all created Ladies of a state.

entries.zh: 唐制有內官、宮官，各有司存，更不加郡國之號，近代加之，非舊典也。
entries.en: Under Tang institutions, inner and palace officials each had their own bureaus and were not given commandery or state titles; recent times have added such titles, which is not the old standard.
entries.literal: The Tang system had inner officials and palace officials, each with its own office, and did not further add titles of commandery or state; recent times have added them—this is not the old standard.

entries.zh: 以易州刺史孫行友為定州留後。
entries.en: Sun Xingyou, Prefect of Yi, was appointed Acting Commissioner of Ding.
entries.literal: Sun Xingyou, Prefect of Yi prefecture, was made Acting Commissioner of Ding prefecture.

entries.zh: 戊午，故夫人柴氏追立為皇后，仍令所司定謚，備禮冊命。
entries.en: On wuwu day, the late Lady Chai was posthumously enthroned as empress, and the responsible offices were ordered to fix her posthumous title and prepare investiture rites.
entries.literal: On the day wuwu, the late Lady Chai was posthumously established as empress, and the responsible offices were ordered to fix her posthumous title and prepare the rites of investiture.

entries.zh: 十二月丙戌，權武平軍留後劉言遣牙將張崇嗣入奏，於十月十三日，與節度副使王進逵、行軍司馬何敬貞、指揮使周行逢等，同共部領戰棹，攻收湖南，偽節度使邊鎬當夜出奔，王進逵等已入潭州。
entries.en: On bingxu in the twelfth month acting Wuiping deputy Liu Yan sent adjutant Zhang Chongsi to report: on the thirteenth of the tenth month he, vice governor Wang Jinkui, chief of staff He Jingzhen, commander Zhou Xingfeng, and others led war boats to retake Hunan; puppet governor Bian Hao fled that night and Wang Jinkui entered Tanzhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army, sent adjutant general Zhang Chongsi to report to court that on the thirteenth day of the tenth month, together with vice military governor Wang Jinkui, campaign chief of staff He Jingzhen, commander Zhou Xingfeng, and others, they jointly led war boats, attacked and recovered Hunan; the puppet military governor Bian Hao fled that same night, and Wang Jinkui and the others had already entered Tan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王逵傳》：逵，朗州武陵人，或名進逵。
entries.en: (Per the Chronicles of the Nine States biography of Wang Kui: Kui was from Wuling in Langzhou, also known as Jinkui.
entries.literal: (Chronicles of the Nine States, Biography of Wang Kui: Kui was a native of Wuling in Lang Prefecture, also called Jinkui.

entries.zh: 邊鎬為武安軍節度使，召劉言入覲，言不行，謀於逵曰：「江南召我，不往，必加兵於我矣，為之奈何！」
entries.en: Bian Hao, Wu'an Army governor, summoned Liu Yan to court; Yan refused and asked Kui: "If Jiangnan summons me and I stay away, they will attack—what can we do!"
entries.literal: Bian Hao served as military governor of the Wu'an Army and summoned Liu Yan to court for an audience; Yan did not go and consulted Kui, saying: "The Jiangnan court summons me—if I do not go, they will surely send troops against me. What is to be done!

entries.zh: 逵曰：「鎬之此來，以制置潭、朗為名，公如速行，正入其算。
entries.en: Kui replied: "Hao's mission is to control Tan and Lang—if you hurry to court, you play into his hand.
entries.literal: Kui said: "Hao comes on the pretext of administering Tan and Lang. If you go quickly, you walk straight into his plan.

entries.zh: 武陵負江湖之阻，帶甲百萬，乃欲拱手臣異姓乎？
entries.en: Wuling has rivers for defense and a million men under arms—will you meekly bow to outsiders?
entries.literal: Wuling lies behind the barrier of rivers and lakes, with a million armed men—will you simply bow and submit to a surname not your own?

entries.zh: 鎬新至長沙，經略未定，乘人心憤怒，引兵攻鎬，可一鼓而擒也。」
entries.en: Hao has just reached Changsha and is unsettled—strike while men are angry, attack Hao, and you can take him in one rush."
entries.literal: Hao has newly reached Changsha and his control is not yet settled; seize this moment while hearts are angry, lead troops to attack Hao, and he can be taken in a single assault."

entries.zh: 言然之，乃遣與何景真等同起兵於武陵，號十指揮使，以攻邊鎬。
entries.en: Yan agreed and dispatched him with He Jingzhen and others to raise troops at Wuling under the title Ten-Command Commander, to attack Bian Hao.
entries.literal: Yan agreed, then sent him together with He Jingzhen and others to raise troops at Wuling, styling themselves Ten-Command Commanders to attack Bian Hao.

entries.zh: 逵率舟師南上，至長沙，邊鎬大駭，以所部奔歸江南，諸州屯守皆罷之，盡復湖外之地。）〉
entries.en: Kui led his fleet south to Changsha; terrified, Bian Hao fled with his troops back to Jiangnan, garrisons in every prefecture were withdrawn, and all territory beyond the lakes was recovered.)〉
entries.literal: Kui led a fleet south to Changsha; Bian Hao was greatly terrified, fled with his division back to Jiangnan, garrison posts in all prefectures were abolished, and all lands beyond the lakes were recovered.)〉

entries.zh: 癸巳，太子太師致仕安叔千卒。
entries.en: On guisi, An Shuqian, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, died.
entries.literal: On guisi, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent An Shuqian died.

entries.zh: 甲午，詔今後諸侯入朝，不得進奉買宴。
entries.en: On jiawu, an edict forbade feudatory lords who came to court from presenting tribute to purchase banquets.
entries.literal: On jiawu, an edict said that hereafter when feudatory lords came to court they might not present tribute to purchase banquets.

entries.zh: 丁酉，皇子澶州節度使榮落起復，加同平章事。
entries.en: On dingyou, Prince Rong, military governor of Cao Prefecture, left mourning restoration and was appointed co-equal Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Prince Rong, military governor of Cao Prefecture, left mourning restoration and was made co-equal Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 戊戌，太子少傅致仕王延卒。
entries.en: On wuxu, Wang Yan, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, died.
entries.literal: On wuxu, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wang Yan died.

entries.zh: 壬寅，幸西莊。
entries.en: On renyin, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.
entries.literal: On renyin, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.

entries.zh: 乙巳，以端明殿學士顏衎權知開封府事。
entries.en: On yisi, Palace Attendant Academician Yan Kan was appointed acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
entries.literal: On yisi, Palace Attendant Academician Yan Kan was made acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 御史臺奏：「請改左右衛復為左右屯衛。」
entries.en: The Censorate submitted: "We request that the Left and Right Guards be restored to the Left and Right Garrison Guards."
entries.literal: The Censorate submitted: "We request that the Left and Right Guards be changed back to the Left and Right Garrison Guards.

entries.zh: 從之，避御名也。
entries.en: The request was granted, to avoid the imperial taboo name.
entries.literal: The request was granted, to avoid the imperial taboo name.

entries.zh: 是冬無雪。
entries.en: That winter brought no snow.
entries.literal: That winter there was no snow.

entries.zh: 廣順元年冬十月己丑朔，宰臣王峻獻唐張蘊古《大寶箴》、謝偃《惟皇誡德賦》二圖。
entries.en: On the jichou new moon in the tenth month of winter, Guangshun 1, Chief Minister Wang Jun presented two Tang-era illustrated texts: Zhang Yungu's Great Treasure Admonition and Xie Yan's Admonition on the Emperor's Virtue.
entries.literal: On the jichou new moon of the tenth month in winter, Guangshun year 1, Chief Minister Wang Jun presented two illustrated works from Tang: Zhang Yungu's Great Treasure Admonition and Xie Yan's Admonition on the Emperor's Virtue.

entries.zh: 詔報曰：「朕生長軍戎，勤勞南北，雖用心於《鈐》、《匱》，且無暇於《詩》、《書》，世務時艱，粗經閱歷，前言往行，未甚討尋。
entries.en: The Emperor replied by edict: "I was raised in the military and labored north and south; though I studied the war manuals Qian and Kui, I never had time for the Odes and Documents; I have only a rough acquaintance with the troubles of the times and have scarcely explored the wisdom of the past.
entries.literal: An edict in reply said: "I grew up amid armies and toiled north and south; though I applied myself to the military manuals Qian and Kui, I had no leisure for the Odes and Documents; the affairs of the age and their hardships I have only roughly experienced, and the words and deeds of former ages I have not much investigated.

entries.zh: 卿有佐命立國之勛，居代天調鼎之任，恒慮眇德，未及古人。
entries.en: You aided the founding of the dynasty and now regulate the realm in Heaven's stead; I constantly worry that my limited virtue cannot match the ancients.
entries.literal: You have merit in aiding the Mandate and founding the state, and hold the charge of regulating the realm on Heaven's behalf; I always fear my slight virtue falls short of the ancients.

entries.zh: 於是采掇箴規，弼諧寡昧，披文閱理，懌意怡神，究為君治國之源，審修己御人之要。
entries.en: You have gathered these admonitions to guide my ignorance; reading them delights the spirit and clarifies the roots of rulership and the essentials of self-cultivation and governing others.
entries.literal: Therefore you gathered admonitions and regulations to assist my dim understanding; reading the text and examining its principles delights the mind and settles the spirit, probing the source of governing the state as ruler and discerning the essentials of cultivating oneself and commanding others.

entries.zh: 帝王之道，盡在於茲，辭翰俱高，珠寶何貴！
entries.en: The way of kings is fully contained in these works—both texts are superb; no jewel could be more valuable!
entries.literal: The Way of emperors and kings is all here—both writings are lofty; what treasure could be more precious!

entries.zh: 再三省覽，深用愧嘉。
entries.en: I have read them again and again and am deeply moved—both humbled and grateful.
entries.literal: On repeated examination I am deeply moved to shame and approval.

entries.zh: 其所進圖，已令於行坐處張懸，所冀出入看讀，用為鑒戒。」
entries.en: I have ordered your illustrations hung where I pass my days, so that I may read them coming and going and take them as my mirror and warning."
entries.literal: The illustrations you presented have been ordered hung where I walk and sit, so that passing in and out I may read them as a mirror and warning.

entries.zh: 壬辰，潞州奏，巡檢使陳思讓、監軍向訓破河東賊軍於虒亭。
entries.en: On renchen Luzhou reported that inspector Chen Sirang and army supervisor Xiang Xun had routed Hedong rebels at Siting.
entries.literal: On renchen, Luzhou reported: Inspector Chen Siyang and army supervisor Xiang Xun defeated Hedong rebel forces at Sixiting.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以刑部侍郎司徒詡為戶部侍郎，以左散騎常侍張煦為刑部侍郎，以給事中呂咸休為左散騎常侍。
entries.en: On guisi Situ Xu moved from Punishments to Revenue; Zhang Xu took Punishments; and Lü Xianxiu became Left Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: On guisi, Vice Minister of Punishments Situ Xu was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Zhang Xu was made Vice Minister of Punishments; and Secretariat Drafter Lü Xianxiu was made Left Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 甲午，絳州防禦使孫漢英卒。
entries.en: On jiawu Jiangzhou defense commissioner Sun Hanying died.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Jiangzhou defense commissioner Sun Hanying died.

entries.zh: 辛丑，荊南奏，湖南亂，大將軍陸孟俊執偽節度使馬希萼遷於衡州，立希萼弟希崇為留後，將吏二千餘人，遇害者半，牙署庫藏焚燒殆盡。
entries.en: On xinchou Jingnan reported turmoil in Hunan: Grand General Lu Mengjun seized puppet governor Ma Xi'e, exiled him to Hengzhou, and installed his brother Xichong; of over two thousand officials and troops, half were killed and the headquarters treasury was nearly burned out.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Jingnan reported: Hunan is in turmoil; Grand General Lu Mengjun seized the puppet military governor Ma Xie and moved him to Hengzhou, installing Xie's brother Xichong as acting commissioner; of more than two thousand officers and clerks, half were killed, and the headquarters treasury was burned nearly clean.

entries.zh: 乙巳，詔並吏部三銓為一銓，委本司長官通判。
entries.en: On yisi an edict combined the Personnel Ministry's three selection boards into one, with the ministry chief overseeing all reviews.
entries.literal: On yisi, an edict merged the Ministry of Personnel's three review boards into one, entrusting joint adjudication to the ministry's chief.

entries.zh: 丙午，晉州巡檢王萬敢奏，河東劉崇入寇，營於州北。
entries.en: On bingwu Jinzhou inspector Wang Wangan reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had invaded and camped north of the prefecture.
entries.literal: On bingwu, Jinzhou inspector Wang Wangan reported: Hedong's Liu Chong invaded and encamped north of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 辛亥，潞州奏，河東賊軍寇境。
entries.en: On xinhai Luzhou reported Hedong rebel raids on the border.
entries.literal: On xinhai, Luzhou reported Hedong rebel forces raiding the border.

entries.zh: 乙卯，荊南奏，淮南遣鄂州節度使劉仁贍，以戰船二百艘於今月二十五日入岳州。
entries.en: On yimao Jingnan reported that Huainan had sent Ezhou governor Liu Renzan with two hundred warships into Yuezhou on the twenty-fifth of this month.
entries.literal: On yimao, Jingnan reported: Huainan sent Ezhou military governor Liu Renzan with two hundred warships, which entered Yuezhou on the twenty-fifth of this month.

entries.zh: 丙辰，詔樞密使王峻率兵援晉州。
entries.en: On bingchen an edict ordered Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun to march to Jinzhou's relief.
entries.literal: On bingchen, an edict ordered Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun to lead troops to relieve Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 丁巳，以左衛將軍申師厚為河西軍節度使、檢校太保。
entries.en: On dingsi Left Guard general Shen Shihou was appointed Hexi military governor and acting Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: On dingsi, Left Guard General Shen Shihou was made military governor of the Hexi Army and Acting Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 師厚素與王峻善，及峻貴，師厚羈旅無依，日於峻馬前望塵而拜，會西涼請帥，帝令擇之，無欲去者，峻乃以師厚奏之，師厚亦欣然求往，尋自前鎮將授左衛將軍、檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: Shihou and Wang Jun were old friends; after Jun's rise, the homeless Shihou bowed to him in the dust before his horse every day. When the Western Liang post opened and no one wanted it, Jun nominated Shihou, who eagerly accepted—he had just been made Left Guard general and acting Works minister.
entries.literal: Shihou had long been friendly with Wang Jun; when Jun rose to power, Shihou, destitute and without support, daily bowed to him in the dust before his horse. When Liangzhou requested a commander, the Emperor ordered a selection, but none wished to go; Jun therefore recommended Shihou, and Shihou also gladly sought the post; shortly before he had been appointed from his former post as Left Guard General and Acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 翌日，乃有涼州之命，賜旌節、駝馬、繒帛以遣之。
entries.en: The next day he received the Liangzhou appointment and was sent off with insignia, camels, horses, and silks.
entries.literal: The next day came the appointment to Liangzhou, and he was sent off with banners of authority, camels, horses, and silks.

entries.zh: 廣順三年春三月庚辰朔，以相州留後白重贊為滑州節度使，以鄭州防禦使王進為相州節度使，以前兗州防禦使索萬進為延州節度使，以亳州防禦使張鐸為同州節度使。
entries.en: On the gengchen new moon in the third month of spring, Guangshun 3, Bai Chongzan (acting Xiangzhou) was appointed Huazhou military governor; Wang Jin (Zhengzhou) took Xiangzhou; former Yanzhou defense commissioner Suo Wanjin took Yan Prefecture (Yanzhou); and Bozhou's Zhang Duo took Tongzhou.
