entries.literal: In spring of Guangshun year 3, third month, gengchen new moon: Bai Chongzan, acting commissioner of Xiangzhou, was made military governor of Huazhou; Wang Jin, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou; Suo Wanjin, former defense commissioner of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Yan Prefecture; and Zhang Duo, defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made military governor of Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 甲申，以皇子澶州節度使榮為開封尹兼功德使，封晉王，仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。
entries.en: On jiashen Prince Rong, Chanzhou military governor, was named Kaifeng mayor and merit commissioner, enfeoffed Prince of Jin, with orders to schedule his formal investiture.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the imperial son Rong, military governor of Chanzhou, was made Mayor of Kaifeng and concurrently Merit Commissioner, enfeoffed as Prince of Jin, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day and prepare the ritual investiture.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以宣徽北院使兼樞密副使鄭仁誨為澶州節度使，以殿前都指揮使李重進領泗州防禦使，以客省使向訓為內客省使。
entries.en: On bingxu Zheng Renhui (Northern Palace Secretariat and vice military affairs commissioner) took Chanzhou; Palace Front commander Li Chongjin took Sizhou; and reception commissioner Xiang Xun became inner reception commissioner.
entries.literal: On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military governor of Chanzhou; Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was given charge of Sizhou as defense commissioner; and Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, was made commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.

entries.zh: 己丑，以棣州團練使王仁鎬為右衛大將軍，充宣徽北院使兼樞密副使。
entries.en: On jichou Dizhou regimental trainer Wang Renhao was promoted to Right Guards general and named Northern Palace Secretariat commissioner with a concurrent vice military affairs post.
entries.literal: On jichou, Wang Renhao, regimental trainer of Dizhou, was made General of the Right Guards and appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 庚寅，端明殿學士、尚書兵部侍郎顏衎落職守本官。
entries.en: On gengyin Duanming academician and Vice Minister of War Yan Yan was stripped of his concurrent posts and kept only his base rank.
entries.literal: On gengyin, Yan Yan, academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of War, was stripped of his concurrent academician post and retained only his original office.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·顏衎傳》：衎權知開封府，王峻敗，衎罷職，守兵部侍郎。）〉
entries.en: (Per the 《History of Song》 biography of Yan Yan: he had been acting Kaifeng mayor; after Wang Jun's downfall he was removed and kept only his vice ministry of war post.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Biography of Yan Yan》 in the 《History of Song》 says: Yan was acting mayor of Kaifeng; when Wang Jun fell, Yan was dismissed and retained only the post of Vice Minister of War.)〉

entries.zh: 以翰林學士、中書舍人王溥為戶部侍郎充職，以左司郎中、充樞密直學士景範為左諫議大夫充職。
entries.en: Wang Pu (Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter) was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue; Jing Fan (Left Department director and military affairs direct academician) was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor.
entries.literal: Wang Pu, Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter, was made Vice Minister of Revenue to fill the post; Jing Fan, Left Department director and concurrently direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Left Remonstrance Counselor to fill the post.

entries.zh: 秘書監陳觀責授左贊善大夫，留司西京，坐王峻黨也。
entries.en: Secretariat Director Chen Guan was demoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and left on duty in Luoyang as a member of Wang Jun's faction.
entries.literal: Chen Guan, Director of the Secretariat, was demoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and ordered to remain on duty in the Western Capital, for belonging to Wang Jun's faction.

entries.zh: 癸巳，大風雨土。
entries.en: On guisi a fierce wind drove dust like rain.
entries.literal: On guisi, a great wind rained earth.

entries.zh: 戊申，幸南莊。
entries.en: On wushen the emperor visited the South Manor.
entries.literal: On wushen, the Emperor visited the South Manor.

entries.zh: 夏四月甲寅，禁沿邊民戶鬻兵仗與蕃人。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on jiayin, border households were forbidden to sell arms to non-Chinese peoples.
entries.literal: In summer, fourth month, jiayin: it was forbidden for households along the borders to sell weapons to barbarians.

entries.zh: 戊辰，河中節度使王景移鎮鳳翔，宋州節度使常思移鎮青州，鳳翔節度使趙暉移鎮宋州，河陽節度使王彥超移鎮河中。
entries.en: On wuchen Wang Jing (Hezhong) moved to Fengxiang, Chang Si (Songzhou) to Qingzhou, Zhao Hui (Fengxiang) to Songzhou, and Wang Yanchao (Heyang) to Hezhong.
entries.literal: On wuchen, Wang Jing, military governor of Hezhong, was transferred to Fengxiang; Chang Si of Songzhou to Qingzhou; Zhao Hui of Fengxiang to Songzhou; and Wang Yanchao of Heyang to Hezhong.

entries.zh: 賜朗州劉言絹三百匹，以兵革之後匱乏故也。
entries.en: Liu Yan of Langzhou received three hundred bolts of silk, as he was impoverished after the fighting.
entries.literal: Three hundred bolts of silk were bestowed on Liu Yan of Langzhou, because after the warfare he was destitute.

entries.zh: 詔在京諸軍將士持支救接。
entries.en: An edict granted advance pay relief to capital garrison troops.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that officers and soldiers of the armies in the capital receive advance pay relief.

entries.zh: 秋七月戊寅朔，徐州言，龍出豐縣村民井中，即時澍雨，漂沒城邑。
entries.en: On the wuyin new moon in the seventh month of autumn Xuzhou reported a dragon rising from a villager's well in Feng County, followed at once by downpour that washed away towns.
entries.literal: In autumn, seventh month, wuyin new moon, Xuzhou reported that a dragon emerged from a villager's well in Feng County; timely rain followed, and cities were washed away.

entries.zh: 癸未，太子賓客馬裔孫卒。
entries.en: On guiwei heir-apparent guest Ma Yisun died.
entries.literal: On guiwei, Ma Yisun, Guest of the Heir Apparent, died.

entries.zh: 甲申，鄴都王殷奏乞朝覲，凡三上章，允之。
entries.en: On jiashen Wang Yin of Yedu petitioned three times for an audience and was granted permission.
entries.literal: On jiashen, Wang Yin of Yedu memorialized requesting an audience at court; after three memorials permission was granted.

entries.zh: 尋以北邊奏契丹事機，詔止其行。
entries.en: Soon afterward Khitan activity on the northern frontier prompted an edict canceling his trip.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, because the northern border reported Khitan military developments, an edict halted his journey.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以左金吾上將軍安審信為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: On bingxu Left Golden Crow general An Shenxin retired as grand mentor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: On bingxu, An Shenxin, General of the Left Golden Crow Guards, was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以右金吾上將軍張從恩為左金吾上將軍，以前鄧州節度使張彥成為右金吾上將軍。
entries.en: On dinghai Right Golden Crow general Zhang Congen took the Left Golden Crow post; former Dengzhou military governor Zhang Yancheng took the Right Golden Crow post.
entries.literal: On dinghai, Zhang Congen, General of the Right Golden Crow Guards, was made General of the Left Golden Crow Guards; Zhang Yancheng, former military governor of Dengzhou, was made General of the Right Golden Crow Guards.

entries.zh: 己丑，以虎捷左廂都指揮使、永州防禦使韓通為陜州留後。
entries.en: On jichou Left Tiger Swift commander and Yongzhou defense commissioner Han Tong was named acting Shaanzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: On jichou, Han Tong, commander of the Left Tiger Swift Division and defense commissioner of Yongzhou, was made acting commissioner of Shaanzhou.

entries.zh: 庚寅，太府卿、判司天監趙延乂卒。
entries.en: On gengyin imperial storehouse director and acting astronomy director Zhao Yanyi died.
entries.literal: On gengyin, Zhao Yanyi, Director of the Imperial Storehouse and acting overseer of the Directorate of Astronomy, died.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以前西京副留守盧價為太子賓客。
entries.en: On xinmao former Luoyang deputy regent Lu Jia became heir-apparent guest.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Lu Jia, former deputy regent of the Western Capital, was made Guest of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 乙未，以御史中丞邊光範為禮部侍郎，以刑部侍郎張煦為御史中丞，以翰林學士承旨、尚書禮部侍郎徐臺符為刑部侍郎充職。
entries.en: On yiwei censor-in-chief Bian Guangfan took the vice ministry of rites; vice minister of justice Zhang Xu became censor-in-chief; and Hanlin chief academician Xu Taifu took the vice ministry of justice.
entries.literal: On yiwei, Bian Guangfan, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Zhang Xu, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Censor-in-Chief; and Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief and Vice Minister of Rites of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Justice to fill the post.

entries.zh: 丙申，太子太師致仕安審信卒。
entries.en: On bingshen retired grand mentor An Shenxin died.
entries.literal: On bingshen, An Shenxin, retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, died.

entries.zh: 丁酉，詔曰：「京兆、鳳翔府、同、華、邠、延、鄜、耀等州所管州縣軍鎮，頃因唐末藩鎮殊風，久歷歲時，未能厘革，政途不一，何以教民。
entries.en: On dingyou an edict declared: "The counties and garrison towns under Jingzhao, Fengxiang, Tong, Hua, Bin, Yan, Fu, and Yao still bear the tangled customs of late-Tang warlords; long unreformed, their divided administration cannot teach the people.
entries.literal: On dingyou, an edict said: "The prefectures, counties, and garrison towns under the jurisdiction of Jingzhao, Fengxiang, Tong, Hua, Bin, Yan, Fu, and Yao, because of the divergent customs of the late-Tang military governors, have for many years not been reformed; with administration not unified, how can the people be instructed?

entries.zh: 其婚田爭訟、賦稅丁徭，合是令佐之職。
entries.en: Marriage disputes, land suits, taxes, and corvée belong to magistrates and their assistants.
entries.literal: Marriage, land disputes, taxes, and corvée labor should fall within the duties of magistrates and assistants.

entries.zh: 其擒奸捕盜、庇護部民，合是軍鎮警察之職。
entries.en: Arresting criminals, catching bandits, and protecting the populace belong to garrison policing.
entries.literal: Apprehending traitors, catching bandits, and protecting local people should fall within the policing duties of the garrison towns.

entries.zh: 今後各守職分，專切提撕，如所職疏遣，各行按責，其州府不得差監征軍將下縣。」
entries.en: Henceforth each office must keep to its role and be held strictly accountable; neglect will be punished separately, and circuits may no longer send military tax supervisors into counties."
entries.literal: Henceforth each shall keep to his duties and be strictly urged; if duties are neglected, each shall be investigated on its own authority; prefectures and circuits may not dispatch supervising tax-collecting military officers into the counties."

entries.zh: 戊戌，衛尉少卿李溫美責授房州司戶參軍。
entries.en: On wuxu Court of Imperial Regalia vice director Li Wenmei was demoted to Fangzhou revenue clerk.
entries.literal: On wuxu, Li Wenmei, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia, was demoted to Revenue Clerk of Fangzhou.

entries.zh: 溫美奉使祭海，便道歸家，家在壽光縣，為縣吏馮勛所訟，故黜之。
entries.en: Wenmei had been sent to sacrifice at the sea but detoured home to Shouguang, where county clerk Feng Xun sued him, leading to his dismissal.
entries.literal: Wenmei had been on a mission to sacrifice to the sea and took a detour home; his family was in Shouguang County, and he was sued by the county clerk Feng Xun, for which he was dismissed.

entries.zh: 供奉官武懷贊棄市，坐盜馬價入己也。
entries.en: Palace attendant Wu Huaizan was executed for pocketing horse purchase funds.
entries.literal: Wu Huaizan, a palace attendant, was executed in the marketplace, for embezzling horse prices into his own possession.

entries.zh: 壬寅，以鴻臚少卿趙修己為司天監。
entries.en: On renyin reception court vice director Zhao Xiuji became astronomy director.
entries.literal: On renyin, Zhao Xiuji, Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, was made Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

entries.zh: 八月己酉，幸南莊。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on jiyou, the emperor visited the South Manor.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, jiyou, the Emperor visited the South Manor.

entries.zh: 丙辰，內衣庫使齊藏珍除名，配沙門島。
entries.en: On bingchen inner garment storehouse commissioner Qi Cangzhen was expelled and exiled to Shamen Island.
entries.literal: On bingchen, Qi Cangzhen, commissioner of the Inner Garment Storehouse, was struck from the rolls and exiled to Shamen Island.

entries.zh: 藏珍奉詔修河，不於役所部轄，私至近縣止宿，及報堤防危急，安寢不動，遂致橫流，故有是責。
entries.en: Ordered to repair the river, Cangzhen left his work site to lodge in a nearby county and, when dikes were reported critical, did nothing as the flood broke through—hence his punishment.
entries.literal: Cangzhen had received an edict to repair the river but, instead of remaining within the jurisdiction of his work site, privately went to a nearby county to lodge; when the dikes were reported in critical danger he did not stir from rest, and flooding spread—hence this punishment.

entries.zh: 庚申，邢州節度使劉詞移鎮河陽。
entries.en: On gengshen Xingzhou military governor Liu Ci moved to Heyang.
entries.literal: On gengshen, Liu Ci, military governor of Xingzhou, was transferred to Heyang.

entries.zh: 辛酉，以龍捷左廂都指揮使、閬州防禦使田景鹹為邢州留後。
entries.en: On xinyou Left Dragon Swift commander and Langzhou defense commissioner Tian Jingxian was named acting Xingzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: On xinyou, Tian Jingxian, commander of the Left Dragon Swift Division and defense commissioner of Langzhou, was made acting commissioner of Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 丁卯，河決河陰，京師霖雨不止。
entries.en: On dingmao the Yellow River broke through at Heyin while unending rain fell on the capital.
entries.literal: On dingmao, the Yellow River burst its banks at Heyin; in the capital the rains did not cease.

entries.zh: 給賜諸軍將士薪芻有差。
entries.en: Troops received graded allotments of fuel and fodder.
entries.literal: Fuel and fodder were granted to the officers and soldiers of the armies in varying amounts.

entries.zh: 癸酉，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎王溥為端明殿學士。
entries.en: On guiyou Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu became a Duanming Hall academician.
entries.literal: On guiyou, Wang Pu, Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made academician of the Duanming Hall.

entries.zh: 甲戌，潭州王進逵奏：「朗州劉言與淮賊通連，差指揮使鄭交部領兵士，欲並當道。
entries.en: On jiaxu Tanzhou's Wang Jinkui reported: "Langzhou's Liu Yan is colluding with Huai rebels; he sent Commander Zheng Jiao with troops to seize our circuit.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, Wang Jinkui of Tanzhou memorialized: "Liu Yan of Langzhou is in contact with Huai bandits; he dispatched Commander Zheng Jiao leading troops intending to annex this circuit.

entries.zh: 鄭交為軍眾所執，奔入武陵，劉言尋為諸軍所廢，臣已至朗州安撫訖。」
entries.en: The troops seized Zheng Jiao, who fled to Wuling; the armies soon deposed Liu Yan; I have already pacified Langzhou."
entries.literal: Zheng Jiao was seized by the troops and fled into Wuling; Liu Yan was soon deposed by the armies; I have already reached Langzhou and completed pacification."

entries.zh: 詔劉言勒歸私第，委王進逵取便安置。
entries.en: An edict sent Liu Yan home and left his disposition to Wang Jinkui.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Liu Yan to return to his private residence and entrusted Wang Jinkui to dispose of him as convenient.

entries.zh: 是月所在州郡奏，霖雨連綿，漂沒田稼，損壞城郭廬舍。
entries.en: That month prefectures across the realm reported endless rain that drowned crops and damaged walls and houses.
entries.literal: That month prefectures everywhere reported that continuous rains had washed away crops and damaged city walls and dwellings.

entries.zh: 冬十月戊申朔，詔以來年正月一日有事於南郊，諸道州府不得以進奉南郊為名，輒有率斂。
entries.en: On the wushen new moon in the tenth month of winter an edict set southern suburb rites for New Year's Day next year and forbade circuits and prefectures to extort funds in its name.
entries.literal: In winter, tenth month, wushen new moon, an edict announced that on the first day of the first month of the coming year rites would be held at the Southern Suburbs; circuits and prefectures were forbidden to levy exactions under the pretext of offerings for the Southern Suburbs.

entries.zh: 己酉，右金吾上將軍張彥成卒。
entries.en: On jiyou Right Golden Crow general Zhang Yancheng died.
entries.literal: On jiyou, Zhang Yancheng, General of the Right Golden Crow Guards, died.

entries.zh: 庚戌，以前同州節度使薛懷讓為左屯衛上將軍，以尚書左丞兼判國子監田敏權判太常卿，以禮部尚書王易權兵部尚書。
entries.en: On gengxu former Tongzhou military governor Xue Huairang took the Left Encampment Guards; Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent overseer of the Directorate of Education Tian Min became acting director of imperial sacrifices; and Minister of Rites Wang Yi became acting Minister of War.
entries.literal: On gengxu, Xue Huairang, former military governor of Tongzhou, was made General of the Left Encampment Guards; Tian Min, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently overseer of the Directorate of Education, was made acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and Wang Yi, Minister of Rites, was made acting Minister of War.

entries.zh: 太常奏，郊廟社稷壇位制度，請下所司修奉，從之。
entries.en: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted regulations for suburban, ancestral, and soil-and-grain altars and asked the relevant offices to restore them; the request was approved.
entries.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized on the regulations for suburban, temple, and altar of soil and grain positions, requesting that the responsible offices repair and maintain them; the request was approved.

entries.zh: 以中書令馮道為南郊大禮使，以開封尹、晉王榮為頓遞使，權兵部尚書王易為鹵簿使，御史中丞張煦為儀仗使，權判太常卿田敏為禮儀使，以前潁州防禦使郭瓊為權宗正卿。
entries.en: Feng Dao (director of the Secretariat) headed the southern suburbs rites; Prince of Jin and Kaifeng mayor Rong managed the procession; acting Minister of War Wang Yi oversaw the imperial insignia cortege; censor-in-chief Zhang Xu oversaw ceremonial arms; acting sacrifices director Tian Min handled ritual; and former Yingzhou defense commissioner Guo Qiong served as acting imperial clan director.
entries.literal: Feng Dao, Director of the Secretariat, was made Grand Master of the Southern Suburbs Rites; Rong, Prince of Jin and Mayor of Kaifeng, was made Escort Commissioner; Wang Yi, acting Minister of War, was made Armor Guard Commissioner; Zhang Xu, Censor-in-Chief, was made Ceremonial Arms Commissioner; Tian Min, acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Ritual Commissioner; and Guo Qiong, former defense commissioner of Yingzhou, was made acting Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 甲寅，以前光祿卿丁知浚復為光祿卿。
entries.en: On jiayin former entertainments director Ding Zhijun was reappointed to that post.
entries.literal: On jiayin, Ding Zhijun, former Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was restored as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 丙辰，幸南莊、西莊。
entries.en: On bingchen the emperor visited the South and West Manors.
entries.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor visited the South Manor and West Manor.

entries.zh: 己未，前寧州刺史張建武責授右司禦副率，以野雞族失利故也。
entries.en: On jiwei former Ningzhou prefect Zhang Jianwu was demoted to deputy leader of the Right Imperial Guard for the Wild Chicken campaign defeat.
entries.literal: On jiwei, Zhang Jianwu, former prefect of Ningzhou, was demoted to Deputy Leader of the Right Imperial Guard, because of the defeat involving the Wild Chicken tribe.

entries.zh: 以前翰林學士、工部侍郎魚崇諒為禮部侍郎，充翰林學士。
entries.en: Former Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Works Yu Chongliang was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: Yu Chongliang, former Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Works, was made Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 時崇諒解職於陜州就養，至是再除禁職，仍賜詔召之，令本州給行裝鞍馬，侍親歸朝。
entries.en: Chongliang had resigned to care for his parents in Shaanzhou; now he was recalled to a palace post with an edict ordering the prefecture to supply travel gear and mounts so he could escort his parents to court.
entries.literal: At the time Chongliang had left office and was supporting his parents at Shaanzhou; now he was again given a palace post, and an edict was bestowed summoning him, ordering the prefecture to provide travel gear and saddle horses so he might attend his parents and return to court.

entries.zh: 以太子賓客張昭為戶部尚書，以太子賓客李濤為刑部尚書。
entries.en: Heir-apparent guest Zhang Zhao became Minister of Revenue; heir-apparent guest Li Tao became Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhao, Guest of the Heir Apparent, was made Minister of Revenue; Li Tao, Guest of the Heir Apparent, was made Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 詔中書令馮道赴西京迎奉太廟神主。
entries.en: An edict sent Secretariat director Feng Dao to Luoyang to escort the ancestral temple spirit tablets.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Feng Dao, Director of the Secretariat, to go to the Western Capital to escort the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 甲子，中書令馮道率百官上尊號曰聖明文武仁德皇帝，答詔不允，凡三上章，允之，仍俟郊禮畢施行。
entries.en: On jiazi Feng Dao led the officials in offering the title Sagely, Illumined, Civil and Martial, Benevolent and Virtuous Emperor; the emperor refused twice before accepting on the third petition, to take effect after the suburban rites.
entries.literal: On jiazi, Feng Dao, Director of the Secretariat, led the hundred officials in offering the honorific title Sagely, Illumined, Civil and Martial, Benevolent and Virtuous Emperor; the rescript reply did not consent; after three memorials consent was granted, to take effect only after the suburban rites were completed.

entries.zh: 壬申，鄴都、邢、洺等州皆上言地震，鄴都尤甚。
entries.en: On renshen Yedu, Xing, Ming, and other prefectures reported earthquakes, worst at Yedu.
entries.literal: On renshen, Yedu, Xing, Ming, and other prefectures all reported earthquakes; Yedu was especially severe.

entries.zh: 十二月戊申，雨木冰。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on wushen, glaze ice coated the trees.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, wushen, rain froze on the trees.

entries.zh: 是日，四廟神主至西郊，帝郊迎奠饗，奉神主入於太廟，設奠安神而退。
entries.en: That day the four temples' spirit tablets reached the western suburbs; the emperor welcomed them with offerings, installed them in the ancestral temple, performed the settling rites, and withdrew.
entries.literal: That day the spirit tablets of the four temples reached the western suburbs; the Emperor went to the suburbs to welcome them, offered libations, escorted the tablets into the Imperial Ancestral Temple, set out offerings to settle the spirits, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 壬子，前單州刺史趙鳳賜死，坐為民所訟故也。
entries.en: On renzi former Shanzhou prefect Zhao Feng was sentenced to death after suits by the populace.
entries.literal: On renzi, Zhao Feng, former prefect of Shanzhou, was granted death, for having been sued by the people.

entries.zh: 甲寅，詔諸道州府縣鎮城內人戶，舊請蠶鹽征價，起今後並停。
entries.en: On jiayin an edict ended the old silk-and-salt surcharge levied on urban households in circuits, prefectures, counties, and garrison towns.
entries.literal: On jiayin, an edict ordered that for households within the cities of circuits, prefectures, counties, and garrison towns, the old collection of silk-and-salt tax prices was henceforth to cease entirely.

entries.zh: 甲子，鎮州節度使何福進來朝。
entries.en: On jiazi Zhenzhou military governor He Fujin arrived at court.
entries.literal: On jiazi, He Fujin, military governor of Zhenzhou, came to court.

entries.zh: 乙丑，鄴都留守王殷來朝。
entries.en: On yichou Yedu regent Wang Yin arrived at court.
entries.literal: On yichou, Wang Yin, regent of Yedu, came to court.

entries.zh: 丙寅，禮儀使奏：「皇帝郊廟行事，請以晉王榮為亞獻，通攝終獻行事。」
entries.en: On bingyin the ritual commissioner proposed that Prince of Jin Rong serve as secondary offerer and also oversee the final offering when the emperor performed suburban and temple rites.
entries.literal: On bingyin, the Ritual Commissioner memorialized: "When the Emperor performs suburban and temple rites, the Prince of Jin Rong is requested as secondary offerer, comprehensively overseeing the final offering as well."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 己巳，左補闕王伸停任，坐檢田於亳州，虛憑紐配故也。
entries.en: On jisi Left Remonstrance aide Wang Shen was suspended for falsifying land-registry matches during a field inspection at Bozhou.
entries.literal: On jisi, Wang Shen, Left Remonstrance Aide, was suspended from office, for while inspecting fields at Bozhou he had falsely relied on registry matching.

entries.zh: 辛未，鄴都留守、侍衛親軍都指揮使王殷削奪在身官爵，長流登州，尋賜死於北郊。
entries.en: On xinwei Yedu regent and Palace Guards commander Wang Yin was stripped of rank, exiled to Dengzhou, and soon ordered to die at the northern suburbs.
entries.literal: On xinwei, Wang Yin, regent of Yedu and commander-in-chief of the Palace Guards, was stripped of all ranks and offices he held, exiled far to Dengzhou, and soon granted death at the northern suburbs.

entries.zh: 其家人骨肉，並不問罪。
entries.en: His family was not prosecuted.
entries.literal: His family and kin were not prosecuted.

entries.zh: 癸酉，帝宿齋於崇元殿，為來年正月一日親祀南郊也。
entries.en: On guiyou the emperor fasted in Chongyuan Hall ahead of his personal southern suburb sacrifice on New Year's Day.
entries.literal: On guiyou, the Emperor kept fast in the Chongyuan Hall, for on the first day of the first month of the coming year he would personally sacrifice at the Southern Suburbs.

entries.zh: 時帝已不豫。
entries.en: The emperor was already gravely ill.
entries.literal: At the time the Emperor was already unwell.

entries.zh: 甲戌，宿於太廟。
entries.en: On jiaxu he lodged at the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, he lodged at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 乙亥質明，帝親饗太廟，自齋宮乘步輦至廟庭，被袞冕，令近臣翼侍升階，止及一室行禮，俯首而退，餘命晉王率有司終其禮。
entries.en: At dawn on yihai the emperor personally sacrificed at the ancestral temple, rode from the fasting palace in a palanquin, donned full regalia, ascended with close ministers' aid only as far as one chamber, bowed and withdrew, and left Prince of Jin to finish the rites with the responsible offices.
entries.literal: At dawn on yihai the Emperor personally offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; from the fasting palace he rode a palanquin to the temple court, donned imperial robes and cap, ordered close ministers to assist him up the steps, performed rites only as far as one chamber, bowed his head and withdrew, and left the Prince of Jin to lead the responsible offices in completing the rites.

entries.zh: 是日，車駕赴郊宮。
entries.en: That day the imperial procession went to the suburban palace.
entries.literal: That day the imperial carriage proceeded to the suburban palace.

entries.zh: 十一月辛巳，廢共城稻田務，任人佃蒔。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on xinsi, the Gongcheng rice office was abolished and tenants were free to farm the fields.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, xinsi, the Gongcheng rice-field office was abolished and people were allowed to rent and plant as they wished.

entries.zh: 乙酉，日南至，帝不受朝賀。
entries.en: On yiyou, the winter solstice, the emperor declined congratulatory audience.
entries.literal: On yiyou, the winter solstice; the Emperor did not receive congratulatory audience.

entries.zh: 庚寅，鎮州節度使何福進奏乞朝覲，三奏，允之。
entries.en: On gengyin Zhenzhou military governor He Fujin petitioned three times for an audience and was granted permission.
entries.literal: On gengyin, He Fujin, military governor of Zhenzhou, memorialized requesting an audience at court; after three memorials permission was granted.

entries.zh: 詔侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英權知鎮州軍府事。
entries.en: An edict named Palace Foot Guards commander Cao Ying acting overseer of Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Cao Ying, commander-in-chief of the Palace Foot Guards, to act as overseer of Zhenzhou military administration.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以將作監李瓊為濟州刺史。
entries.en: On guisi works director Li Qiong was appointed Jizhou prefect.
entries.literal: On guisi, Li Qiong, Director of the Directorate of Works, was made prefect of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 壬寅，詔：「重定天下縣邑，除畿赤外，其餘三千戶已上為望縣，二千戶已上為緊縣，一千戶已上為上縣，五百戶以上為中縣，不滿五百戶為中下縣。」
entries.en: On renyin an edict reclassified counties nationwide: outside the capital core, 3,000+ households made a "esteemed" county, 2,000+ a "pressing" county, 1,000+ an upper county, 500+ a middle county, and under 500 a lower-middle county.
entries.literal: On renyin, an edict said: "The counties of the realm are to be reclassified; apart from the capital and its red districts, those with three thousand households and above are to be esteemed counties, two thousand and above are pressing counties, one thousand and above are upper counties, five hundred and above are middle counties, and fewer than five hundred are lower-middle counties."

entries.zh: 顯德元年春正月丙子朔，帝親祀圜丘，禮畢，詣郊宮受賀。
entries.en: On the bingzi new moon in spring, Xiande 1, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound, then went to the suburban palace to receive congratulations.
entries.literal: In spring of Xiande year 1, first month, bingzi new moon, the Emperor personally sacrificed at the Round Mound; when the rites were completed he went to the suburban palace to receive congratulations.

entries.zh: 車駕還宮，禦明德樓，宣制：「大赦天下，改廣順四年為顯德元年。
entries.en: Returning to the palace, he took Bright Virtue Tower and proclaimed: "A great amnesty for the realm; Guangshun 4 is renamed Xiande 1.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage returned to the palace; taking the Bright Virtue Tower, he proclaimed: "A great amnesty for the realm; Guangshun year 4 is changed to Xiande year 1.

entries.zh: 自正月一日昧爽已前，應犯罪人，常赦所不原者，咸赦除之。
entries.en: All offenders before dawn on New Year's Day, including those normally beyond amnesty, were pardoned.
entries.literal: From before dawn on the first day of the first month, all offenders, including those normally excluded from amnesty, were wholly pardoned.

entries.zh: 內外將士各優給，文武職官並與加恩，內外命婦並與進封。
entries.en: Troops at court and in the field received preferential grants; civil and military officials received added favors; and titled ladies received advanced enfeoffments.
entries.literal: Officers and soldiers within and without were each given preferential grants; civil and military officials all received added favor; titled ladies within and without all received advanced enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 寺監攝官七周年已上者，同明經出身，今後諸寺監不得以白身署攝。
entries.en: Acting directorate officials with seven or more years of service were treated as classics graduates; directorates could no longer appoint untitled men to acting posts.
entries.literal: Acting officials of directorates who had served seven full years or more were treated as graduates of the classics examination; henceforth directorates might not appoint acting posts to men without office.

entries.zh: 升朝官兩任已上，著綠十五周年與賜緋，著緋十五年與賜紫。
entries.en: Court officials with two or more terms: fifteen years in green earned crimson robes; fifteen years in crimson earned purple.
entries.literal: Court officials with two terms or more: after fifteen years wearing green, crimson was granted; after fifteen years wearing crimson, purple was granted.

entries.zh: 州縣官曾經五度參選，雖未及十六考，與授朝散大夫階，年七十已上，授優散官，賜緋。
entries.en: Prefectural and county officials who had stood for selection five times, though short of sixteen evaluations, received the rank of Grand Master of Palace Gentility; those seventy or older received superior scattered office and crimson robes.
entries.literal: Prefectural and county officials who had stood for selection five times, though not yet reaching sixteen evaluations, were granted the rank of Grand Master of Palace Gentility; those seventy years and above were granted superior scattered office and bestowed crimson.

entries.zh: 應奉郊廟職掌人員，並與恩澤。
entries.en: All staff who served the suburban and temple rites received favors.
entries.literal: All personnel charged with suburban and temple service received favors.

entries.zh: 今後不得以梁朝及清泰朝為偽朝偽主，天下帝王陵廟及名臣墳墓無後，官為檢校」云。
entries.en: Henceforth the Liang and Qingtai reigns may not be called false dynasties; and the state shall maintain imperial tombs and famous ministers' graves that lack heirs," the proclamation said.
entries.literal: Henceforth the Liang dynasty and the Qingtai reign may not be treated as a false dynasty and false rulers; imperial tombs and temples and the graves of famous ministers without heirs throughout the realm shall be inspected and maintained by the state," it said.

entries.zh: 宣赦畢，帝御崇元殿受冊尊號，禮畢，群臣稱賀。
entries.en: After the amnesty the emperor took Chongyuan Hall to receive his honorific title; when the rites ended the officials congratulated him.
entries.literal: When the amnesty proclamation was finished, the Emperor took the Chongyuan Hall to receive investiture of the honorific title; when the rites were completed the hundred officials offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 時帝郊祀，禦樓受冊，有司多略其禮，以帝不豫故也。
entries.en: During the suburban rites and tower investiture the responsible offices curtailed much of the ceremony because the emperor was ill.
entries.literal: At the time the Emperor performed suburban sacrifice and took the tower to receive investiture; the responsible offices largely abbreviated the rites, because the Emperor was unwell.

entries.zh: 先是，有占者言：「鎮星在氐、房，乃鄭、宋之分，當京師之地；
entries.en: Earlier a diviner had said: "The Seat Star stands in Di and Fang—the Zheng and Song regions, corresponding to the capital—
entries.literal: Earlier, a diviner had said: "The Seat Star is in Di and Fang, the territories of Zheng and Song, corresponding to the capital region;

entries.zh: 兼氐宿主帝王路寢。
entries.en: and Di governs the imperial sleeping chamber.
entries.literal: Moreover Di governs the imperial sleeping chamber.

entries.zh: 若散財以致福，遷幸以避災，庶幾可以驅禳矣。」
entries.en: Dispersing wealth for blessing and moving the capital to avoid disaster might drive the omen away."
entries.literal: If wealth is dispersed to bring blessing and the capital moved to avoid calamity, perhaps the evil may be driven away."

entries.zh: 帝以遷幸煩費，不可輕議，散財可矣，故有郊禋之命。
entries.en: The emperor judged a capital move too costly to consider and chose dispersing wealth instead—hence the order for suburban sacrifice.
entries.literal: The Emperor held that moving the capital would be troublesome and costly and could not be lightly discussed; dispersing wealth would suffice—hence the order for suburban sacrifice.

entries.zh: 洎歲暮，帝疾增劇，郊廟之禮蓋勉而行之耳。
entries.en: By year's end his illness had worsened, and the suburban and temple rites were carried out only with great effort.
entries.literal: By year's end the Emperor's illness grew severe; the suburban and temple rites were performed only with effort.

entries.zh: 戊寅，詔廢鄴都依舊為天雄軍，大名府在京兆府之下。
entries.en: On wuyin an edict abolished Yedu as a capital, restored the Tianxiong Army, and ranked Daming below Jingzhao.
entries.literal: On wuyin, an edict abolished Yedu as a capital and restored it as the Tianxiong Army; Daming Prefecture was placed below Jingzhao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚辰，制皇子開封尹、晉王榮可開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼侍中，行開封尹、功德使，判內外兵馬事。
entries.en: On gengchen an order named Prince of Jin and Kaifeng mayor Rong Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent palace attendant, continuing as Kaifeng mayor and merit commissioner with authority over all military affairs.
entries.literal: On gengchen, an order declared that the imperial son, Mayor of Kaifeng and Prince of Jin Rong, was approved as Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, acting as Mayor of Kaifeng and Merit Commissioner, with jurisdiction over internal and external military affairs.

entries.zh: 襄州安審琦進封陳王；
entries.en: An Shenqi of Xiangzhou was advanced to Prince of Chen;
entries.literal: An Shenqi of Xiangzhou was advanced to Prince of Chen;

entries.zh: 鄆州符彥卿進封衛王，移鎮天雄軍；
entries.en: Fu Yanqing of Yanzhou was advanced to Prince of Wei and transferred to the Tianxiong Army;
entries.literal: Fu Yanqing of Yanzhou was advanced to Prince of Wei and transferred to command the Tianxiong Army;

entries.zh: 荊南高保融進封南平王；
entries.en: Gao Baorong of Jingnan was advanced to Prince of Nanping;
entries.literal: Gao Baorong of Jingnan was advanced to Prince of Nanping;

entries.zh: 夏州李彜興進封西平王。
entries.en: Li Yixing of Xiazhou was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
entries.literal: Li Yixing of Xiazhou was advanced to Prince of Xiping.

entries.zh: 甲申，宋州趙暉進封韓國公，青州常思進封萊國公，徐州王晏進封滕國公，鄧州侯章進封申國公，西京武行德進封譙國公，許州郭從義加檢校太師，鳳翔王景進封褒國公，華州孫方諫進封蕭國公。
entries.en: On jiashen Zhao Hui of Songzhou became Duke of Han; Chang Si of Qingzhou, Duke of Lai; Wang Yan of Xuzhou, Duke of Teng; Hou Zhang of Dengzhou, Duke of Shen; Wu Xingde of Luoyang, Duke of Qiao; Guo Congyi of Xu Prefecture was made acting grand preceptor; Wang Jing of Fengxiang, Duke of Bao; and Sun Fangjian of Huazhou, Duke of Xiao.
entries.literal: On jiashen, Zhao Hui of Songzhou was advanced to Duke of Han; Chang Si of Qingzhou to Duke of Lai; Wang Yan of Xuzhou to Duke of Teng; Hou Zhang of Dengzhou to Duke of Shen; Wu Xingde of the Western Capital to Duke of Qiao; Guo Congyi of Xu Prefecture was made Acting Grand Preceptor; Wang Jing of Fengxiang was advanced to Duke of Bao; and Sun Fangjian of Huazhou to Duke of Xiao.

entries.zh: 自趙暉已下並加開府儀同三司。
entries.en: From Zhao Hui downward all received Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: From Zhao Hui downward all were given Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 乙酉，分命朝臣往諸州開倉，減價出糶，以濟饑民。
entries.en: On yiyou court ministers were sent to open granaries across the prefectures and sell grain cheaply to relieve famine victims.
entries.literal: On yiyou, court ministers were separately dispatched to the prefectures to open granaries and sell grain at reduced prices to relieve the famine-stricken.

entries.zh: 詔潭州依舊為大都督府，在朗州、桂州之上。
entries.en: An edict restored Tanzhou as a great metropolitan prefecture, ranking above Langzhou and Guizhou.
entries.literal: An edict restored Tanzhou as a great metropolitan prefecture, ranking above Langzhou and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以澶州節度使鄭仁誨為樞密使，加同平章事；
entries.en: On bingxu Chanzhou military governor Zheng Renhui became military affairs commissioner and grand councilor;
entries.literal: On bingxu, Zheng Renhui, military governor of Chanzhou, was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 鄜州楊信加開府儀同三司，進封杞國公；
entries.en: Yang Xin of Fuzhou received Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies and was advanced to Duke of Qi;
entries.literal: Yang Xin of Fuzhou was given Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies and advanced to Duke of Qi;

entries.zh: 邠州折從阮加開府儀同三司，改封鄭國公；
entries.en: Zhe Congruan of Binzhou received Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Zheng;
entries.literal: Zhe Congruan of Binzhou was given Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Zheng;

entries.zh: 滄州李暉加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Li Hui of Cangzhou was made acting grand commandant;
entries.literal: Li Hui of Cangzhou was made Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 安州李洪義加檢校太師；
entries.en: Li Hongyi of Anzhou was made acting grand preceptor;
entries.literal: Li Hongyi of Anzhou was made Acting Grand Preceptor;

entries.zh: 貝州王饒加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Wang Rao of Beizhou was made acting grand commandant;
entries.literal: Wang Rao of Beizhou was made Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 以陳州節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使郭崇為澶州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: Chenzhou military governor and Palace Horse Guards commander Guo Chong took Chanzhou and became grand councilor;
entries.literal: Guo Chong, military governor of Chenzhou and commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guards, was made military governor of Chanzhou and given concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以曹州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英為鎮州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: Caozhou military governor and Palace Foot Guards commander Cao Ying took Zhenzhou and became grand councilor;
entries.literal: Cao Ying, military governor of Caozhou and commander-in-chief of the Palace Foot Guards, was made military governor of Zhenzhou and given concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 潭州王進逵加特進、兼侍中；
entries.en: Wang Jinkui of Tanzhou received special advancement and a concurrent palace attendant post;
entries.literal: Wang Jinkui of Tanzhou was given special advancement and made Concurrent Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 河陽劉詞加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Liu Ci of Heyang was made acting grand commandant;
entries.literal: Liu Ci of Heyang was made Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 河中王彥超加同平章事；
entries.en: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong became grand councilor;
entries.literal: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was given concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以鎮州節度使何福進為鄆州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: Zhenzhou military governor He Fujin took Yanzhou and became grand councilor;
entries.literal: He Fujin, military governor of Zhenzhou, was made military governor of Yanzhou and given concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 潞州李筠加同平章事。
entries.en: Li Yun of Luzhou became grand councilor.
entries.literal: Li Yun of Luzhou was given concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 戊子，晉州藥元福、滑州白重贊、相州王進、同州張鐸並加檢校太傅；
entries.en: On wuzi Yao Yuanfu of Jinzhou, Bai Chongzan of Huazhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Zhang Duo of Tongzhou were all made acting grand mentors;
entries.literal: On wuzi, Yao Yuanfu of Jinzhou, Bai Chongzan of Huazhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Zhang Duo of Tongzhou were all made Acting Grand Mentor;

entries.zh: 以延州節度使索萬進為曹州節度使，加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Yanzhou military governor Suo Wanjin took Caozhou and was made acting grand mentor;
entries.literal: Suo Wanjin, military governor of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Caozhou and given Acting Grand Mentor;

entries.zh: 定州留後孫行友、邢州留後田景鹹、陜州留後韓通、靈武留後馮繼業並正授節度使。
entries.en: Acting commissioners Sun Xingyou of Dingzhou, Tian Jingxian of Xingzhou, Han Tong of Shaanzhou, and Feng Jiye of Lingwu were all formally appointed military governors.
entries.literal: Sun Xingyou, acting commissioner of Dingzhou; Tian Jingxian of Xingzhou; Han Tong of Shaanzhou; and Feng Jiye of Lingwu were all formally appointed military governors.

entries.zh: 庚寅夜，東北有大星墜，其聲如雷。
entries.en: On the night of gengyin a great star fell in the northeast with a thunderous roar.
entries.literal: On the night of gengyin a great star fell in the northeast with a sound like thunder.

entries.zh: 壬辰，宰臣馮道加守太師，範質加尚書左僕射，監修國史李穀加右僕射、集賢殿大學士。
entries.en: On renchen chief minister Feng Dao received acting grand preceptor; Fan Zhi became left vice director of the Department of State Affairs; and national history supervisor Li Gu became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and assembled worthies academician.
entries.literal: On renchen, Feng Dao, chief minister, was given acting Grand Preceptor; Fan Zhi was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; and Li Gu, supervisor of the national history, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

entries.zh: 以端明殿學士、尚書戶部侍郎王溥為中書侍郎、平章事。
entries.en: Duanming academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Pu was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and councilor.
entries.literal: Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Councilor.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：太祖將大漸，促召學士草制，以溥為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: (Per the 《Summary of Affairs of the Eastern Capital》: as Taizu was dying he urgently summoned an academician to draft Pu's appointment as vice director and councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.)
entries.literal: (The 《Summary of Affairs of the Eastern Capital》 says: As the Grand Ancestor was near death he urgently summoned an academician to draft an order appointing Pu Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.)

entries.zh: 已宣制，太祖曰：「吾無恨矣。」）〉
entries.en: When the order was proclaimed Taizu said, "I have no regrets.")〉
entries.literal: When the order had been proclaimed, the Grand Ancestor said: "I have no regrets.")〉

entries.zh: 司徒竇貞固進封汧國公，司空蘇禹珪進封莒國公，並加開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Minister of Education Dou Zhengu was advanced to Duke of Qian; Minister of Works Su Yugui to Duke of Ju; both received Commissioner with Protocol of the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Education, was advanced to Duke of Qian; Su Yugui, Minister of Works, to Duke of Ju; both were given Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 以宣徽南院使、知永興軍府事袁鳷為延州節度使；
entries.en: Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner and Yongxing overseer Yuan Zhi took Yanzhou;
entries.literal: Yuan Zhi, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and overseer of Yongxing military administration, was made military governor of Yanzhou;

entries.zh: 以宣徽北院使兼樞密副使王仁鎬為永興軍節度使；
entries.en: Northern Palace Secretariat commissioner and vice military affairs commissioner Wang Renhao took Yongxing;
entries.literal: Wang Renhao, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military governor of Yongxing;

entries.zh: 以前安州節度使王令溫為陳州節度使；
entries.en: Former Anzhou military governor Wang Lingwen took Chenzhou;
entries.literal: Wang Lingwen, former military governor of Anzhou, was made military governor of Chenzhou;

entries.zh: 以殿前都指揮使、泗州防禦使李重進為武信軍節度使、檢校太保，典軍如故；
entries.en: Palace Front commander and Sizhou defense commissioner Li Chongjin took the Wuxin Army as acting grand guardian while continuing to command troops;
entries.literal: Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division and defense commissioner of Sizhou, was made military governor of the Wuxin Army and Acting Grand Guardian, continuing to command the army as before;

entries.zh: 以龍捷左廂都指揮使、睦州防禦使樊愛能為侍衛馬軍都指揮使、洋州節度使，加檢校太保；
entries.en: Left Dragon Swift commander and Muzhou defense commissioner Fan Aineng became Palace Horse Guards commander and Yangzhou military governor with acting grand guardian;
entries.literal: Fan Aineng, commander of the Left Dragon Swift Division and defense commissioner of Muzhou, was made commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guards and military governor of Yangzhou, with Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以虎捷左廂都指揮使、果州防禦使何徽為侍衛步軍都指揮使、利州節度使，加檢校太保；
entries.en: Left Tiger Swift commander and Guozhou defense commissioner He Hui became Palace Foot Guards commander and Lizhou military governor with acting grand guardian;
entries.literal: He Hui, commander of the Left Tiger Swift Division and defense commissioner of Guozhou, was made commander-in-chief of the Palace Foot Guards and military governor of Lizhou, with Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以樞密承旨魏仁浦為樞密副使。
entries.en: Military affairs chief academician Wei Renpu became vice military affairs commissioner.
entries.literal: Wei Renpu, academician-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 是日巳時，帝崩於滋德殿，聖壽五十一。
entries.en: That day at the si hour the emperor died in the Hall of Nourishing Virtue at the age of fifty-one.
entries.literal: That day at the si hour the Emperor died in the Hall of Nourishing Virtue, aged fifty-one.

entries.zh: 秘不發喪。
entries.en: His death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.
entries.literal: The death was kept secret and mourning not announced.

entries.zh: 乙未，遷神柩於萬歲殿，召文武百官班於殿廷，宣遺制：「晉王榮可於柩前即皇帝位，服紀月日一如舊制」云。
entries.en: On yiwei the coffin was moved to the Hall of Ten Thousand Years; officials were summoned to court and the testament was proclaimed: "Prince of Jin Rong shall take the throne before the coffin; mourning shall follow the old regulations," it said.
entries.literal: On yiwei the coffin was moved to the Hall of Ten Thousand Years; civil and military officials were summoned to line the court, and the testamentary order was proclaimed: "The Prince of Jin Rong may take the imperial throne before the coffin; the period of mourning shall follow the old regulations," it said.

entries.zh: 是歲，自正月朔日後，景色昏晦，日月多暈，及嗣君即位之日，天氣晴朗，中外肅然。
entries.en: That year, after the first-month new moon, the sky stayed dim and halos ringed the sun and moon; on the day the heir took the throne the weather cleared and the realm grew solemn.
entries.literal: That year, from after the new moon of the first month, the sky was dim and the sun and moon often haloed; on the day the successor took the throne the weather was clear and within and without were solemn.

entries.zh: 帝自郊禋後，其疾乍瘳乍劇，晉王省侍，不離左右。
entries.en: After the suburban rites his illness alternately eased and worsened; Prince of Jin attended him without leaving his side.
entries.literal: After the suburban sacrifice the Emperor's illness alternately eased and worsened; the Prince of Jin attended him and did not leave his side.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：李重進，周太祖之甥，母即福慶長公主。
entries.en: (Per the 《Summary of Affairs of the Eastern Capital》: Li Chongjin was Zhou Taizu's nephew; his mother was the Princess of Fortune and Celebration.)
entries.literal: (The 《Summary of Affairs of the Eastern Capital》 says: Li Chongjin was a nephew of the Zhou Grand Ancestor; his mother was the Princess of Fortune and Celebration.)

entries.zh: 重進年長於世宗，及太祖寢疾，召重進受顧命，令拜世宗，以定君臣之分。）〉
entries.en: Chongjin was older than Shizong; when Taizu fell ill he summoned Chongjin for the deathbed charge and ordered him to bow to Shizong, fixing their ruler-subject roles.)〉
entries.literal: Chongjin was older than Shizong; when the Grand Ancestor lay ill he summoned Chongjin to receive the final charge and ordered him to bow to Shizong, thereby fixing the distinction between ruler and subject.)〉

entries.zh: 累諭晉王曰：「我若不起此疾，汝即速治山陵，不得久留殿內。
entries.en: He repeatedly told Prince of Jin: "If I do not recover, prepare my tomb quickly and do not linger in the palace halls.
entries.literal: He repeatedly instructed the Prince of Jin: "If I do not recover from this illness, you must quickly prepare my tomb and not linger long in the palace halls.

entries.zh: 陵所務從儉素，應緣山陵役力人匠，並須和雇，不計近遠，不得差配百姓。
entries.en: Keep the tomb frugal; hire all tomb labor and craftsmen at fair wages, near or far, and do not conscript the people.
entries.literal: The tomb must be kept frugal and plain; all laborers and craftsmen for the tomb works must be hired at fair wages, regardless of distance, and the people may not be conscripted.

entries.zh: 陵寢不須用石柱，費人功，只以磚代之。
entries.en: Do not use stone pillars in the tomb chamber—they waste labor; use brick instead.
entries.literal: The tomb chamber need not use stone pillars, which waste human labor; use only brick in their place.

entries.zh: 用瓦棺紙衣。
entries.en: Use a pottery coffin and paper shrouds.
entries.literal: Use a pottery coffin and paper garments.

entries.zh: 臨入陵之時，召近稅戶三十家為陵戶，下事前揭開瓦棺，遍視過陵內，切不得傷他人命。
entries.en: When interment comes, appoint thirty nearby tax households as tomb keepers; before burial open the pottery coffin and inspect the tomb, and harm no one's life.
entries.literal: When the time comes to enter the tomb, summon thirty nearby tax households as tomb keepers; before interment open the pottery coffin and inspect the entire tomb interior, and on no account harm another person's life.

entries.zh: 勿修下宮，不要守陵宮人，亦不得用石人石獸，只立一石記子，鐫字云：『大周天子臨晏駕，與嗣帝約，緣平生好儉素，只令著瓦棺紙衣葬。』
entries.en: Build no lower palace, keep no tomb-guarding attendants, and use no stone figures or beasts; set up only a stone marker reading: "The Son of Heaven of Great Zhou, facing death, agreed with the heir that, loving frugality all his life, he would be buried only in a pottery coffin and paper shrouds."
entries.literal: Do not build a lower palace, do not keep tomb-guarding palace attendants, and do not use stone human figures or stone beasts; erect only a stone marker inscribed: "The Son of Heaven of Great Zhou, facing death, agreed with the heir emperor that, because he loved frugality and plainness all his life, he ordered burial only in a pottery coffin and paper garments."

entries.zh: 若違此言，陰靈不相助。」
entries.en: If this word is violated, his shade will not assist you."
entries.literal: If this word is violated, the shade-spirit will not assist."

entries.zh: 又言：「朕攻收河府時，見李家十八帝陵園，廣費錢物人力，並遭開發。
entries.en: He also said: "When I took the He prefectures I saw the Li family's eighteen imperial tombs, which had cost vast wealth and labor and were all looted.
entries.literal: He also said: "When I attacked and took the He prefectures I saw the eighteen imperial tombs of the Li family, which had expended vast wealth and labor and were all opened and looted.

entries.zh: 汝不聞漢文帝儉素，葬在霸陵原，至今見在。
entries.en: Have you not heard that Emperor Wen of Han was frugal, buried on Ba Mound plain, and remains intact to this day?
entries.literal: Have you not heard that Emperor Wen of Han was frugal and plain, buried on the plain of Ba Mound, and is still intact to this day?

entries.zh: 如每年寒食無事時，即仰量事差人灑掃，如無人去，只遙祭。
entries.en: Each Cold Food festival, if nothing else presses, send men to sweep the tomb as needed; if no one can go, offer from afar.
entries.literal: Each year at Cold Food, if there is nothing else to do, send men as the occasion warrants to sweep and tend it; if no one goes, perform only a distant offering.

entries.zh: 兼仰於河府、魏府各葬一副劍甲，澶州葬通天冠、絳紗袍，東京葬一副平天冠、袞龍服。
entries.en: Also bury a set of sword and armor each at the He and Wei prefectures; at Chanzhou bury the imperial cap and crimson gauze robe; and at the Eastern Capital bury a level-heaven cap and dragon robe.
entries.literal: Moreover bury one set of sword and armor each at the He and Wei prefectures; at Chanzhou bury the imperial cap and crimson gauze robe; at the Eastern Capital bury one set of the level-heaven cap and dragon robe.

entries.zh: 千萬千萬，莫忘朕言。」
entries.en: Again and again—do not forget my words."
entries.literal: Again and again, do not forget my words."

entries.zh: 秋七月癸酉朔，前河西軍節度使申師厚責授右監門衛率府副率。
entries.en: On the guiyou new moon of the seventh month of autumn, former Hexi military governor Shen Shihou was demoted to vice leader of the Right Gate Guards of the Supervisory Army.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, guiyou new moon, Shen Shihou, former military governor of the Hexi Army, was demoted and appointed Vice Leader of the Right Gate Guards of the Supervisory Army.

entries.zh: 師厚在涼州歲餘，以所部艱食，蕃情反覆，奏乞入朝，尋留其子為留後，不俟詔離任，故責之。
entries.en: Shihou had been at Liangzhou for more than a year. His troops lacked food and the tribes were unreliable, so he memorialized asking to come to court. He soon left his son as acting commissioner, left his post without awaiting an edict, and was punished for it.
entries.literal: Shihou had been at Liangzhou for more than a year; because his command lacked food and the tribal disposition was inconstant, he memorialized begging to enter court; soon he left his son as acting commissioner without awaiting an edict and left his post—hence the punishment.

entries.zh: 乙亥，天雄軍節度使、衛王府彥卿進位守太傅，改封魏王；
entries.en: On yihai Tianxiong military governor and Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was advanced to Defender Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wei;
entries.literal: On yihai, Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong Army and Prince of Wei, was advanced to Defender Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Wei;

entries.zh: 鄆州郭從義加兼中書令；
entries.en: Yanzhou's Guo Congyi was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
entries.literal: Guo Congyi of Yanzhou was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

entries.zh: 河陽劉詞移鎮永興軍，加兼侍中；
entries.en: Heyang's Liu Ci was transferred to Yongxing and additionally made palace attendant;
entries.literal: Liu Ci of Heyang was transferred to the Yongxing Army and additionally made Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 潞州李筠加兼侍中；
entries.en: Luzhou's Li Jun was additionally made palace attendant;
entries.literal: Li Jun of Luzhou was additionally made Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 河中王彥超移鎮許州，加兼侍中；
entries.en: Hezhong's Wang Yanchao was transferred to Xuzhou and additionally made palace attendant;
entries.literal: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was transferred to Xuzhou and additionally made Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 許州節度、侍衛都虞候李重進移鎮宋州，加同平章事兼侍衛親軍都指揮使；
entries.en: Xuzhou military governor and palace guard chief of staff Li Chongjin was transferred to Songzhou, made councilor, and appointed commander-in-chief of the imperial guard;
entries.literal: Li Chongjin, military governor of Xuzhou and chief of staff of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou, made concurrent Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and appointed commander-in-chief of the imperial guard;

entries.zh: 以武信軍節度使兼殿前都指揮使張永德為滑州節度使，加檢校太傅，典軍如故；
entries.en: Wuxin military governor and Palace Front commander Zhang Yongde was made Huazhou military governor, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor, and kept army command as before;
entries.literal: Zhang Yongde, military governor of the Wuxin Army and commander-in-chief of the Palace Front Division, was made military governor of Huazhou, promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor, and retained command of the army as before;

entries.zh: 同州藥元福移鎮陜州，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Tongzhou's Yao Yuanfu was transferred to Shaanzhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;
entries.literal: Yao Yuanfu of Tongzhou was transferred to Shaanzhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;

entries.zh: 鄜州白重贊移鎮河陽，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Yongzhou's Bai Chongzan was transferred to Heyang and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;
entries.literal: Bai Chongzan of Yongzhou was transferred to Heyang and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander;

entries.zh: 陜州韓通移鎮曹州，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: Shaanzhou's Han Tong was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Han Tong of Shaanzhou was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 帝即位之初，覃慶於諸侯，是賞從征之功也。
entries.en: At the beginning of his reign he had extended rewards widely to the feudal lords; this round rewarded those who had joined the campaign.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Emperor's accession he had bestowed rewards widely upon the feudal lords; this was to reward merit from the campaign.

entries.zh: 丙子，以前禮部侍郎邊光範為刑部侍郎，權判開封府事。
entries.en: On bingzi former Vice Minister of Rites Bian Guangfan was made Vice Minister of Justice and acting mayor of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: On bingzi, Bian Guangfan, former Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice and acting mayor of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 丁丑，天下兵馬元帥、吳越國王錢俶加天下兵馬都元帥；
entries.en: On dingchou Wu-Yue king and Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven Qian Chu was additionally made Marshal-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;
entries.literal: On dingchou, Qian Chu, King of Wu-Yue and Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven, was additionally made Marshal-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;

entries.zh: 襄州節度使、陳王安審琦加守太尉。
entries.en: Xiangzhou military governor and Prince of Chen Wang Shenqi was advanced to Defender Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Wang Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou and Prince of Chen, was advanced to Defender Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 戊寅，右散騎常侍張可復卒。
entries.en: On wuyin Right Regular Attendant Zhang Kefu died.
entries.literal: On wuyin, Zhang Kefu, Right Regular Attendant, died.

entries.zh: 以前亳州防禦使李萬金為鄜州留後。
entries.en: Former Bozhou defense commissioner Li Wanjin was made acting commissioner of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Li Wanjin, former defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made acting commissioner of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 庚辰，幸南莊。
entries.en: On gengchen the emperor visited the South Manor.
entries.literal: On gengchen, the Emperor visited the South Manor.

entries.zh: 辛巳，荊南節度使、南平王高保融加守中書令，夏州節度使、西平王李彜興加守太保，西京留守武行德、徐州王晏、鄧州侯章並加兼中書令。
entries.en: On xinsi Jingnan military governor and Prince of Nanping Gao Baorong was advanced to Defender Councilor; Xiazhou military governor and Prince of Xiping Li Yixing was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde, Xuzhou's Wang Yan, and Dengzhou's Hou Zhang were all additionally made councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
entries.literal: On xinsi, Gao Baorong, military governor of Jingnan and Prince of Nanping, was advanced to Defender Councilor; Li Yixing, military governor of Xiazhou and Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Defender Grand Guardian; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, Wang Yan of Xuzhou, and Hou Zhang of Dengzhou were all additionally made Councilors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 癸未，湖南王進逵加兼中書令；
entries.en: On guimao Hunan's Wang Jinkui was additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
entries.literal: On guimao, Wang Jinkui of Hunan was additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

entries.zh: 天德軍節度使郭勛、邠州折從阮、安州李洪義並加兼侍中；
entries.en: Tiande military governor Guo Xun, Binzhou's Zhe Congruan, and Anzhou's Li Hongyi were all additionally made palace attendants;
entries.literal: Guo Xun, military governor of the Tiande Army, Zhe Congruan of Binzhou, and Li Hongyi of Anzhou were all additionally made Palace Attendants;

entries.zh: 以前華州節度使孫方諫為同州節度使，加兼中書令；
entries.en: Former Hua military governor Sun Fangjian was appointed military governor of Tong and additionally made councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;
entries.literal: Previously Sun Fangjian, military governor of Hua, was made military governor of Tong, additionally made Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery;

entries.zh: 以前永興軍節度使王仁鎬為河中節度使，加檢校太尉。
entries.en: Former Yongxing military governor Wang Rengao was appointed military governor of Hezhong and promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.
entries.literal: Previously Wang Rengao, military governor of the Yongxing Army, was made military governor of Hezhong, promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.

entries.zh: 乙酉，滄州李暉、貝州王饒、鎮州曹英並加兼侍中，涇州張鐸、相州王進、延州袁鳷並加檢校太尉。
entries.en: On yiyou Cangzhou's Li Hui, Beizhou's Wang Rao, and Zhenzhou's Cao Ying were all additionally made palace attendants; Jingzhou's Zhang Duo, Xiangzhou's Wang Jin, and Yanzhou's Yuan Zhi were all promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.
entries.literal: On yiyou, Li Hui of Cangzhou, Wang Rao of Beizhou, and Cao Ying of Zhenzhou were all additionally made Palace Attendants; Zhang Duo of Jingzhou, Wang Jin of Xiangzhou, and Yuan Zhi of Yanzhou were all promoted to Honorary Grand Commander.

entries.zh: 壬辰，百僚上表，請以九月二十四日誕聖日為天清節，從之。
entries.en: On renchen the officials memorialized to make the emperor's birthday, the twenty-fourth of the ninth month, the Tianqing Festival. The request was granted.
entries.literal: On renchen, the hundred officials submitted a memorial requesting that the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day of the sage's birth, be established as the Tianqing Festival; it was approved.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以左僕射兼門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史範質為守司徒兼門下侍郎、平章事、宏文館大學士；
entries.en: On guisi Left Vice Minister, Secretariat Chamberlain, councilor, and supervisor of state history Fan Zhi was advanced to Defender Grand Mentor, retaining his posts as Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, and made Grandee of the Hongwen Academy;
entries.literal: On guisi, Fan Zhi, Left Vice Minister concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of state history, was made Defender Grand Mentor concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and Grandee of the Hongwen Academy;

entries.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：周太祖嘗令世宗詣範質，時為親王，軒車高大，門不能容，世宗即下馬步入。
entries.en: (The Guolao Tanyuan records that Zhou Taizu once sent Shizong to visit Fan Zhi when the latter was still a prince. Shizong's carriage was so tall the gate would not take it, so he dismounted and entered on foot.
entries.literal: (The 《Guolao Tanyuan》 states: Zhou Taizu once had Shizong go to Fan Zhi's residence; he was then a prince. His carriage was tall and the gate could not admit it; Shizong at once dismounted and walked in on foot.

entries.zh: 及嗣位，從容語質曰：「卿所居舊宅耶，門樓一何小哉。」
entries.en: After he took the throne, he said to Fan Zhi with easy familiarity, "Is this your old house? What a tiny gate-tower!"
entries.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, he said to Fan Zhi in an easy manner: "Is this the old residence in which you dwell? How very small the gate-tower is!"

entries.zh: 遂為治第。）〉
entries.en: He then had a new residence built for him.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon a mansion was built for him.)〉

entries.zh: 以左僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士、判三司李穀為守司徒兼門下侍朗、平章事，監修國史；
entries.en: Left Vice Minister, Secretariat Chamberlain, councilor, Jixian Hall Grandee, and overseer of the Three Offices Li Gu was advanced to Defender Grand Mentor, retaining his posts as Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, and made supervisor of state history;
entries.literal: Li Gu, Left Vice Minister concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, Jixian Hall Grandee, and overseer of the Three Offices, was made Defender Grand Mentor concurrently Secretariat Chamberlain, Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of state history;

entries.zh: 以中書侍郎、平章事王溥為中書侍郎兼禮部尚書、平章事、集賢殿大學士；
entries.en: Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor Wang Pu was made Secretariat Chamberlain and Minister of Rites, councilor, and Jixian Hall Grandee;
entries.literal: Wang Pu, Secretariat Chamberlain and Councilor, was made Secretariat Chamberlain concurrently Minister of Rites, Councilor, and Jixian Hall Grandee;

entries.zh: 以樞密院學士、工部侍郎景範為中書侍郎、平章事，判三司；
entries.en: Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works Jing Fan was made Secretariat Chamberlain and councilor, with charge of the Three Offices;
entries.literal: Jing Fan, Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works, was made Secretariat Chamberlain and Councilor, overseeing the Three Offices;

entries.zh: 樞密使、檢校太保、同平章事鄭仁誨加兼侍中；
entries.en: Privy Commissioner, Honorary Grand Guardian, and concurrent councilor Zheng Renhui was additionally made palace attendant;
entries.literal: Zheng Renhui, Privy Commissioner, Honorary Grand Guardian, and Concurrent Councilor, was additionally made Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 靈武馮繼業、定州孫行友、邢州田景鹹並加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Lingwu's Feng Jiye, Dingzhou's Sun Xingyou, and Xingzhou's Tian Jingxian were all promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: Feng Jiye of Lingwu, Sun Xingyou of Dingzhou, and Tian Jingxian of Xingzhou were all promoted to Honorary Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 晉州楊廷璋加檢校太保；
entries.en: Jinzhou's Yang Tingzhang was promoted to Honorary Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: Yang Tingzhang of Jinzhou was promoted to Honorary Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以太子詹事趙上交為太子賓客。
entries.en: Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Zhao Shangjiao was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Zhao Shangjiao, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 乙未，以樞密副使、右監門衛大將軍魏仁浦為樞密使、檢校太保。
entries.en: On yiwei Deputy Privy Commissioner and Right Imperial Insignia Guard Major General Wei Renpu was made Privy Commissioner and Honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: On yiwei, Wei Renpu, Deputy Privy Commissioner and Major General of the Right Imperial Insignia Guard, was made Privy Commissioner and Honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略》云：議者以仁浦不由科第進，世宗曰：「顧才何如耳！」
entries.en: (The Dongdu Shilue records that critics objected that Renpu had not risen through the examination system. Shizong replied, "What matters is ability, does it not!"
entries.literal: (The 《Dongdu Shilue》 states: Discussants held that Renpu had not advanced through the civil service examinations. Shizong said: "What matters is talent, does it not!"

entries.zh: 遂用之。）〉
entries.en: He was appointed.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon he was appointed.)〉

entries.zh: 丙申，以中書舍人史館修撰、判館事劉溫叟為禮部侍郎，判館如故。
entries.en: On bingshen Secretariat Drafter, History Bureau compiler, and bureau director Liu Wen'ou was made Vice Minister of Rites while retaining his bureau duties.
entries.literal: On bingshen, Liu Wen'ou, Secretariat Drafter, History Bureau compiler, and director of the bureau, was made Vice Minister of Rites; his duties at the bureau remained as before.

entries.zh: 丁酉，相州節度使王進卒。
entries.en: On dingyou Xiangzhou military governor Wang Jin died.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Wang Jin, military governor of Xiangzhou, died.

entries.zh: 冬十月甲辰，左羽林大將軍孟漢卿賜死，坐監納厚取耗餘也。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on jiachen Left Feathered Forest Major General Meng Hanqing was ordered to take his own life for skimming excess grain while supervising tax collection.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, Meng Hanqing, Major General of the Left Feathered Forest, was granted death for supervising collection and taking a heavy surplus in collection.

entries.zh: 丙午，以安州節度使李洪義為青州節度使，以貝州節度使王饒為相州節度使，以徐州節度使王晏為西京留守，以西京留守武行德為徐州節度使。
entries.en: On bingwu Anzhou military governor Li Hongyi was moved to Qingzhou; Beizhou military governor Wang Rao to Xiangzhou; Xuzhou military governor Wang Yan to Western Capital defender; and Western Capital defender Wu Xingde to Xuzhou military governor.
entries.literal: On bingwu, Li Hongyi, military governor of Anzhou, was made military governor of Qingzhou; Wang Rao, military governor of Beizhou, was made military governor of Xiangzhou; Wang Yan, military governor of Xuzhou, was made Western Capital resident defender; Wu Xingde, Western Capital resident defender, was made military governor of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 戊申，以龍捷左廂都指揮使、泗州防禦使韓令坤為洋州節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使；
entries.en: On wushen Dragon Swift Left Wing commander and Sizhou defense commissioner Han Lingkun was made Yangzhou military governor and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry;
entries.literal: On wushen, Han Lingkun, commander of the Dragon Swift Left Wing and defense commissioner of Sizhou, was made military governor of Yangzhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry;

entries.zh: 以虎捷右廂都指揮使、永州防禦使李繼勛為利州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Tiger Swift Right Wing commander and Yongzhou defense commissioner Li Jixun was made Lizhou military governor and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard infantry.
entries.literal: Li Jixun, commander of the Tiger Swift Right Wing and defense commissioner of Yongzhou, was made military governor of Lizhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the palace guard infantry.

entries.zh: 己酉，太子太保致仕楊凝式卒。
entries.en: On jiyou retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yang Ningshi died.
entries.literal: On jiyou, Yang Ningshi, retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, died.

entries.zh: 詔安、貝二州依舊為防禦州，其軍額並停。
entries.en: An edict restored An and Bei to defense prefectures as before and abolished their military designations.
entries.literal: An edict restored An and Bei prefectures to defense prefectures as before; their army designations were all abolished.

entries.zh: 壬子，以今上為永州防禦使，依前殿前都虞候。
entries.en: On renzi the present sovereign was made Yongzhou defense commissioner while retaining his post as chief of staff of the Palace Front Division.
entries.literal: On renzi, the present sovereign was made defense commissioner of Yongzhou, retaining his former post as chief of staff of the Palace Front Division.

entries.zh: 戊午，監修國史李穀等上言曰：「竊以自古王者鹹建史官，君臣獻替之謀皆須備載，家國安危之道得以直書。
entries.en: On wuwu Li Gu and the other supervisors of state history submitted a memorial: "We observe that since antiquity every conquering sovereign has established historiographers, so that counsel offered and withdrawn between ruler and minister might all be fully recorded and the paths of national safety and peril written without distortion.
entries.literal: On wuwu, Li Gu and others, supervisors of the compilation of state history, submitted saying: "We venture to observe that since antiquity conquering kings have all established historiographers; the counsel of ruler and minister, whether offered or withdrawn, must all be fully recorded, and the paths of the state's safety and peril can thereby be written straight.

entries.zh: 歷代已來，其名不一。
entries.en: Through the ages their titles have varied.
entries.literal: Through the generations their titles have not been uniform.

entries.zh: 人君言動，則起居註創於累朝；
entries.en: The ruler's words and deeds were recorded in the Diaries of Activity and Repose, instituted dynasty after dynasty;
entries.literal: For the ruler's words and deeds there is the Diaries of Activity and Repose, instituted across successive reigns;

entries.zh: 輔相經綸，則時政記興於前代。
entries.en: the chancellor's governance in the Record of Current Administration, which arose in earlier times.
entries.literal: for the chancellor's governance, the Record of Current Administration arose in former ages.

entries.zh: 然後采其事實，編作史書。
entries.en: Only then were the facts gathered and compiled into formal histories.
entries.literal: Only then were the facts gathered and compiled into historical books.

entries.zh: 蓋緣聞見之間須有來處，記錄之際得以審詳。
entries.en: This was because what the historians heard and saw had to come from somewhere, so that what they recorded could be thorough and exact.
entries.literal: This was because between what was heard and seen there had to be a source, and at the time of recording one could be thorough and exact.

entries.zh: 今之左右起居郎，即古之左右史也。
entries.en: Today's Left and Right Diarists are the ancient Left and Right Historians.
entries.literal: Today's Left and Right Diarists are the ancient Left and Right Historians.

entries.zh: 唐文宗朝，命其官執筆，立於殿階螭頭之下，以紀政事。
entries.en: Under Tang Wenzong these officers were ordered to take up their brushes and stand below the dragon-head steps of the throne hall to record affairs of state.
entries.literal: In the reign of Tang Wenzong, these officers were ordered to hold the brush and stand below the dragon-head steps of the hall to record government affairs.

entries.zh: 後則明宗朝，命端明殿及樞密直學士，皆輪修日曆，旋送史官，以備纂修。
entries.en: Later, under Mingzong, Duanming Hall scholars and Privy Council direct academicians were ordered to compile the court calendar in rotation and send it promptly to the historiographers for use in compilation.
entries.literal: Later, in the reign of Mingzong, the Duanming Hall and direct academicians of the Privy Council were all ordered to take turns compiling the court calendar, which was promptly sent to the historiographers to supply material for compilation.

entries.zh: 及近朝，此事皆廢，史官惟憑百司報狀，館司但取兩省制書，此外雖有訪聞，例非端的。
entries.en: In recent times this practice had been abandoned entirely. Historiographers relied only on reports from the ministries, and the History Bureau took only edicts from the two secretariats. Whatever else they heard was, as a rule, unreliable.
entries.literal: By recent times this practice had all been abandoned; historiographers relied only on reports from the hundred offices, and the institute took only edicts from the two secretariats; beyond this, though there might be inquiries and hearsay, as a rule it was not reliable.

entries.zh: 伏自先皇帝創開昌運，及皇帝陛下纘嗣丕基，其聖德武功、神謀睿略，而皆萬幾宥密，丹禁深嚴，非外臣之所知，豈庶僚之可訪。
entries.en: Since the late emperor opened this flourishing age and Your Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation, his sagely virtue, martial achievement, divine stratagems, and keen plans all lie within the myriad affairs of the inner court, deep within the vermilion forbidden precincts. These are not matters outer ministers can know, nor subjects common officials may inquire into.
entries.literal: We bow before the fact that the late emperor opened a flourishing age, and Your Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation; his sagely virtue and martial achievement, divine stratagems and keen plans—all lie within the myriad affairs of the inner court, deep and secret within the vermilion forbidden precincts, not what outer ministers can know, how could common officials be consulted?

entries.zh: 此後欲望以諮詢之事、裁制之規，別命近臣旋具抄錄，每當修撰日曆，即令封付史臣，庶國事無漏略之文，職業免疏遺之咎。」
entries.en: Henceforth we ask that matters of consultation and rules of decision be specially entrusted to nearby ministers to copy at once, and that whenever the court calendar is compiled these copies be sealed and delivered to the historiographers, so that state affairs suffer no omissions and the historiographers escape the charge of negligence."
entries.literal: Hereafter we desire that on matters of consultation and rules of decision special orders be given to nearby ministers to prepare copies at once; whenever the court calendar is compiled, let these be sealed and delivered to the historiographers, so that state affairs may have no omitted passages and the profession may escape the fault of negligence."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 因命樞密直學士，起今後於樞密使處，逐月抄錄事件，送付史館。
entries.en: Privy Council direct academicians were accordingly ordered, beginning immediately, to copy monthly from the Privy Commissioner's records and deliver the copies to the History Bureau.
entries.literal: Accordingly Privy Council direct academicians were ordered, beginning from now at the Privy Commissioner's office, to copy events month by month and send them to the History Bureau.

entries.zh: 己未，供奉官郝光庭棄市，坐在葉縣巡檢日，挾私斷殺平人也。
entries.en: On jiwei palace service official Hao Guangting was executed in the marketplace for killing a commoner in a private judgment while serving as patrol inspector of Ye County.
entries.literal: On jiwei, Hao Guangting, palace service official, was executed in the marketplace for, while serving as patrol inspector of Ye County, killing a commoner in a private judgment.

entries.zh: 是日大閱，帝親臨之。
entries.en: That day a grand military review was held, and the emperor attended in person.
entries.literal: That day there was a great review; the emperor personally attended it.

entries.zh: 帝自高平之役，睹諸軍未甚嚴整，遂有退卻，至是命今上一概簡閱，選武藝超絕者，署為殿前諸班，因是有散員、散指揮使、內殿直、散都頭、鐵騎、控鶴之號。
entries.en: Since Gaoping the emperor had seen how poorly disciplined the armies were and how readily they fell back. He now ordered the present sovereign to review them all, selecting men of outstanding martial skill for the various companies of the Palace Front. Hence came the designations Loose Companies, Loose Commanders, Inner Hall Direct, Loose Squad Chiefs, Iron Cavalry, and Crane Control.
entries.literal: Since the campaign at Gaoping the emperor had seen that the various armies were not very strict and orderly and had withdrawn; at this time he ordered the present sovereign to review them all comprehensively, selecting those of surpassing martial skill and appointing them to the various companies of the Palace Front; hence there came to be the designations Loose Companies, Loose Commanders, Inner Hall Direct, Loose Squad Chiefs, Iron Cavalry, and Crane Control.

entries.zh: 復命總戎者，自龍捷、虎捷以降，一一選之，老弱羸小者去之，諸軍士伍，無不精當。
entries.en: He also ordered the army commanders, from Dragon Swift and Tiger Swift downward, to inspect their troops one by one, removing the old, weak, and stunted until every company in every army was fit and exact.
entries.literal: He again ordered the commanders-in-chief, from Dragon Swift and Tiger Swift downward, to select one by one; the old, weak, emaciated, and small were removed, and in every army company nothing was not exact and proper.

entries.zh: 由是兵甲之盛，近代無比，且減冗食之費焉。
entries.en: The army's arms and armor were thereafter unmatched in recent memory, and the cost of feeding useless mouths was reduced as well.
entries.literal: By this the abundance of arms and armor had no parallel in recent times, and moreover superfluous consumption of provisions was reduced.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：顯德元年，上謂侍臣曰：「侍衛兵士老少相半，強懦不分，蓋徇人情，不能選練。
entries.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties records that in the first year of Xiande the emperor told his ministers, "Our palace guards are half old men and half young, with no distinction between the strong and the weak. We indulge personal ties and cannot drill them properly.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》: In the first year of Xiande, the emperor said to his attending ministers: "The palace guard soldiers are half old and half young, strong and weak undistinguished; this indulges personal feeling and cannot select and drill.

entries.zh: 今春朕在高平，與劉崇及蕃軍相遇，臨敵有指使不前者，茍非朕親當堅陣，幾至喪敗。
