entries.en: This spring at Gaoping I met Liu Chong and the Khitan army. Some of my officers would not advance when ordered. Had I not personally held the line, we would nearly have been destroyed.
entries.literal: This spring I was at Gaoping and met Liu Chong and the barbarian army; facing the enemy there were those under command who would not advance; if I had not personally taken the firm line, we would nearly have suffered defeat.

entries.zh: 況百戶農夫，未能贍一甲士，且兵在精不在眾，宜令一一點選，精銳者升在上軍，怯懦者任從安便，庶期可用，又不虛費。」
entries.en: A hundred farming households cannot even support one armored soldier. Soldiers depend on quality, not numbers. Each man should be inspected: the elite raised into the upper armies, the timid allowed to go where they will, so that what we keep is useful and nothing is wasted."
entries.literal: Moreover, a hundred farming households cannot support one armored soldier; moreover, in soldiers quality matters, not numbers; it is fitting to order selection one by one—the sharp and elite to be raised into the upper armies, the timid and weak allowed to go where they please, so that we may expect usefulness and not waste in vain."

entries.zh: 先是，上按於高平，觀其退縮，慨然有懲革之志。
entries.en: Earlier, when he inspected the troops at Gaoping and watched them fall back, he had resolved to reform them.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the emperor inspected at Gaoping and saw them withdraw, he sighed and had the will to punish and reform.

entries.zh: 又以驍勇之士，多為外諸侯所占，如是召募天下豪傑，不以草澤為阻，在於闕下，躬親試閱，選武藝超絕及有身首者，分署為殿前諸班。）〉
entries.en: Bold warriors had also been snapped up by regional lords, so he recruited heroes from across the realm without regard to humble birth. At court he personally tested them, selecting men of outstanding skill and imposing stature for the various companies of the Palace Front.)〉
entries.literal: Moreover, because bold and brave men were mostly taken by outer feudal lords, he therefore recruited heroes throughout the empire, not obstructed by commoners in the wilds; at the court he personally tested and reviewed them, selecting those of surpassing martial skill and of stature, and assigning them in divisions to the various companies of the Palace Front.)〉

entries.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，諱榮，太祖之養子，蓋聖穆皇后之侄也。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong, posthumously known as Ruiwu Xiaowen, bore the personal name Rong. He was Taizu's adopted son and a nephew of Empress Shengmu.
entries.literal: The Emperor Shizong, posthumously titled Ruiwu Xiaowen, whose personal name was Rong, was the adopted son of Taizu and was in fact a nephew of Empress Shengmu.

entries.zh: 本姓柴氏，父守禮，太子少保致仕。
entries.en: He was born into the Chai family. His father Shouli had retired from the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: His original surname was the Chai clan; his father was Shouli, who had retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 〈（《隆平集》：柴翁者，嘗獨居室，人以為司冥事。
entries.en: (According to the Longpingji, an elder of the Chai clan once lived alone in his room, and people believed he had dealings with the realm of the dead.
entries.literal: (The Longpingji states: There was an Old Man Chai who once lived alone in his room, and people thought he dealt with matters of the underworld.

entries.zh: 一日，笑不止，妻問其故，不答。
entries.en: One day he could not stop laughing. When his wife asked why, he refused to say.
entries.literal: One day he laughed without stopping; his wife asked the reason, but he would not answer.

entries.zh: 翁嗜飲，妻醉之以酒，乃曰：「上帝有命，郭郎為天子。」
entries.en: The old man loved wine, so his wife plied him with drink until he blurted out: "Heaven has decreed that Master Guo shall become emperor."
entries.literal: The old man loved drink; his wife made him drunk with wine, and then he said: "Heaven has commanded that Master Guo shall become Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 考柴翁即守禮之父，史佚其名。）〉
entries.en: It is held that this Old Man Chai was Shouli's father, though the history does not give his name.)〉
entries.literal: Investigation shows that Old Man Chai was the father of Shouli; the history does not record his name.)〉

entries.zh: 帝以唐天祐十八年，歲在辛巳，九月二十四日丙午，生於邢州之別墅。
entries.en: He was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (bingwu) in Tianyou 18 of Tang (xinsi year), at a country estate in Xingzhou.
entries.literal: The Emperor was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, bingwu, in the eighteenth year of Tang Tianyou, the year xinsi, at a villa in Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 年未童冠，因侍聖穆皇后，在太祖左右。
entries.en: While still a boy, he attended Empress Shengmu and remained close to Taizu.
entries.literal: Before he had reached the age of the capping ceremony, he attended Empress Shengmu and was at Taizu's side.

entries.zh: 時太祖無子，家道淪落，然以帝謹厚，故以庶事委之。
entries.en: Taizu had no sons of his own, and the household had fallen on hard times, but he found the boy conscientious and dependable and began entrusting him with day-to-day affairs.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu had no son, and the family's fortunes had declined; yet because the Emperor was careful and sincere, Taizu entrusted him with household affairs.

entries.zh: 帝悉心經度，資用獲濟，太祖甚憐之，乃養為己子。
entries.en: The boy managed everything with care, kept the household supplied, and won Taizu's deep affection; Taizu eventually adopted him as his son.
entries.literal: The Emperor devoted himself to planning and management, and supplies were made adequate; Taizu cherished him greatly and therefore adopted him as his own son.

entries.zh: 漢初，太祖以佐命功為樞密副使，帝始授左監門衛將軍。
entries.en: Early in the Han dynasty Taizu became vice commissioner of military affairs for his founding service, and the future emperor received his first commission as general of the Left Gate Guards.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Han, Taizu was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs for his merit in assisting the founding, and the Emperor was first appointed General of the Left Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：周世宗在漢為諸衛將軍，嘗遊畿甸，謁縣令，忘其姓名，令方聚邑客蒱博，勿得見，世宗頗銜之。
entries.en: (The Guolao tanyuan records that while serving as a general of the guards under Han, the future Zhou Shizong once toured the capital region and called on a county magistrate whose name is lost to us. The magistrate was hosting a gambling party for local guests and refused to see him, and Shizong never forgot the slight.
entries.literal: (The Guolao tanyuan says: When Zhou Shizong was a general of the guards under Han, he once traveled in the capital region and called on a county magistrate, whose name is forgotten; the magistrate was just gathering local guests for gambling and would not receive him, and Shizong bore considerable resentment.

entries.zh: 及即位，令因部夫犯贓數百匹，宰相範質以具獄上奏，世宗曰：「親民之官，贓狀狼籍，法當處死。」
entries.en: After he took the throne, that same magistrate was implicated when laborers under his command embezzled hundreds of bolts of cloth. Chief minister Fan Zhi submitted the completed case. Shizong said, "An official charged with caring for the people, and his corruption this brazen—the law calls for death."
entries.literal: When he acceded to the throne, that magistrate, because laborers under his command had embezzled several hundred bolts of cloth, had the full case submitted by the chief minister Fan Zhi; Shizong said: "An official close to the people, with corruption so flagrant—by law he should be put to death."

entries.zh: 質奏曰：「受所監臨財物有罪，上贓雖多，法不至死。」
entries.en: Fan Zhi replied, "Embezzling property under one's supervision is indeed a crime, but even with a large sum involved, the statute does not prescribe death."
entries.literal: Fan Zhi memorialized: "Taking property under one's supervision is a crime, but though the amount embezzled is large, the law does not reach death."

entries.zh: 世宗怒，厲聲曰：「法者自古帝王之所制，本以防奸，朕立法殺贓吏，非酷刑也。」
entries.en: Shizong flared up and said sharply, "Law is what rulers have fashioned since antiquity to keep wrongdoing in check. When I use the law to execute corrupt officials, that is not cruelty."
entries.literal: Shizong grew angry and said in a stern voice: "Law is what emperors and kings have made since antiquity, originally to guard against wrongdoing; that I make law to kill corrupt officials is not cruel punishment."

entries.zh: 質曰：「陛下殺之則可，若付有司，臣不敢署敕。」
entries.en: Fan Zhi said, "Your Majesty may execute him if you insist, but if the case goes through the regular judiciary, I cannot sign the edict."
entries.literal: Fan Zhi said: "Your Majesty may kill him if you wish, but if the case is handed to the responsible offices, your servant dares not sign the edict."

entries.zh: 遂貸其命。）〉
entries.en: In the end his life was spared.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon his life was spared.)〉

entries.zh: 二年，太祖鎮鄴，改天雄軍牙內都指揮使，領貴州刺史、檢校右僕射。
entries.en: In the second year, when Taizu took command at Ye, he was made commander of the Tianxiong Army's inner guard, given Guizhou as his prefecture, and granted the honorary title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: In year 2, when Taizu was stationed at Ye, he was changed to commander of the inner guard of the Tianxiong Army, and given charge of Guizhou as governor while serving as honorary Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 三年冬，太祖入平內難，留帝守鄴城。
entries.en: That winter Taizu marched into the capital to settle the internal crisis and left him to hold Yecheng.
entries.literal: In winter of year 3, when Taizu entered the capital to quell the internal crisis, he left the Emperor to guard Yecheng.

entries.zh: 顯德二年春正月辛未朔，帝不受朝賀。
entries.en: On the xinwei new moon of the first month of spring in Xiande 2, the Emperor declined the usual court congratulations.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year of Xiande, on the first day of the first month (day xinwei, new moon), the Emperor did not accept court congratulations.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔：「在朝文班，各舉堪為令錄者一人，雖姻族近親，亦無妨嫌。
entries.en: On xinmao an edict stated: “Each civil official at court shall nominate one person qualified for county magistrate or recorder—even a close kinsman by marriage is not barred.
entries.literal: On day xinmao, an edict: "Among the civil officials at court, each shall recommend one person fit to serve as county magistrate or recorder; even close relatives by marriage need not be excluded.

entries.zh: 授官之日，各署舉主姓名，若在官貪濁不任、懦弱不理，並量事狀重輕，連坐舉主。」
entries.en: At appointment each nominee’s recommender shall be named on record; if the appointee proves corrupt, incompetent, timid, or neglectful in office, the recommender shall share liability according to the gravity of the offense.”
entries.literal: On the day of appointment, each shall record the recommender's name; if the appointee while in office is corrupt and unfit, or timid and unable to govern, the severity of the case shall be weighed, and the recommender shall be punished by association."

entries.zh: 乙未，詔：「應逃戶莊田，並許人請射承佃，供納稅租：如三周年內本戶來歸者，其莊田不計荒熟，並交還一半；
entries.en: On yiwei an edict declared: “Estate fields left by absconding households may be bid for and leased by others, who shall pay tax and rent; if the original household returns within three years, half the fields—whether fallow or cultivated—shall be restored to them;
entries.literal: On day yiwei, an edict: "As to estate fields of absconding households, all are permitted to be bid for and leased by others, who shall pay taxes and rent: if the original household returns within three years, its estate fields, whether waste or cultivated, shall be returned in half;

entries.zh: 五周年內歸業者，三分交還一分；
entries.en: if they resume farming within five years, one-third shall be returned;
entries.literal: if they return to their occupation within five years, one part in three shall be returned;

entries.zh: 如五周年外歸業者，其莊田除本戶墳塋外，不在交付之限。
entries.en: if they return after five years, the fields need not be returned except for the family burial grounds.
entries.literal: if they return to their occupation after five years, their estate fields, except for the original household's graves, are not within the limit of delivery.

entries.zh: 其近北地諸州，應有陷蕃人戶，自蕃界來歸業者：五周年內來者，三分交還二分；
entries.en: In northern border prefectures, households lost to the Khitan who return from beyond the frontier: if they come back within five years, two-thirds of their land shall be restored;
entries.literal: In the northern border prefectures, as to households that fell into the barbarians' hands and return from the barbarian frontier to resume their occupation: those who come within five years shall have two parts in three returned;

entries.zh: 十周年內來者，交還一半；
entries.en: within ten years, half shall be returned;
entries.literal: those who come within ten years shall have half returned;

entries.zh: 十五周年來者，三分交還一分；
entries.en: within fifteen years, one-third shall be returned;
entries.literal: those who come within fifteen years shall have one part in three returned;

entries.zh: 十五周年外來者，不在交還之限。」
entries.en: after fifteen years, no land need be returned.”
entries.literal: those who come after fifteen years are not within the limit of return."

entries.zh: 二月戊申，遣使赴西京，賜太子太師致仕侯益、白文珂、宋彥筠等茶藥錢帛各有差，仍降詔存問。
entries.en: On wushen in the second month envoys were dispatched to the Western Capital with tea, medicine, cash, and silk for the retired Grand Preceptor Hou Yi, Bai Wenke, Song Yanyun, and others in varying amounts, together with an edict of imperial concern.
entries.literal: In the second month, on day wushen, envoys were sent to the Western Capital to bestow tea, medicine, money, and silks on the retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Hou Yi, Bai Wenke, Song Yanyun, and others, each in differing amounts, and an edict of inquiry was also issued.

entries.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：
entries.en: On renxu an edict proclaimed:
entries.literal: On day renxu, an edict stated:

entries.zh: 應內外文武臣僚，今後或有所見所聞，並許上章論諫。
entries.en: Henceforth all civil and military officials, at court or in the provinces, may memorialize on anything they see or hear.
entries.literal: All civil and military officials within and without, hereafter if they have anything seen or heard, are all permitted to submit memorials to discuss and remonstrate.

entries.zh: 若朕躬之有闕失，得以盡言；
entries.en: Speak fully of any fault in my person;
entries.literal: If there are faults in Our person, they may speak fully;

entries.zh: 時政之有瑕疵，勿宜有隱。
entries.en: and do not conceal flaws in current policy.
entries.literal: if there are flaws in current policy, they should not be concealed.

entries.zh: 方求名實，豈尚虛華，茍或素不工文，但可直書其事。
entries.en: I seek substance, not ornament; if you are no stylist, write plainly of the facts.
entries.literal: We seek substance and reality—how could We esteem empty show? If one is by nature unskilled in writing, he need only write the matter plainly.

entries.zh: 辭有謬誤者，固當舍短，言涉傷忤者，必與留中，所冀盡情，免至多慮。
entries.en: Errors in wording I will overlook; words that offend I will keep confidential. Speak freely, without undue fear.
entries.literal: If the wording has errors, We shall of course overlook the faults; if the words touch on offense, We shall certainly retain them within, hoping that all may speak freely and be spared excessive anxiety.

entries.zh: 諸有司局公事者，各宜舉職，事有不便者，革之可也，理有可行者，舉之可也，勿務因循，漸成訛謬。
entries.en: Every office should perform its duty: reform what is harmful, propose what is sound, and do not cling to routine until error accumulates.
entries.literal: All offices and bureaus with public duties should each perform their functions; where affairs are inconvenient, they may be reformed; where principle permits action, it may be proposed—do not cling to routine and gradually create error.

entries.zh: 臣僚有出使在外回者，茍或知黎庶之利病，聞官吏之優劣，當具敷奏，以廣聽聞。
entries.en: Officials returning from missions abroad should fully report what they know of the people’s welfare and of officials’ merit or failings, so that my hearing may be broadened.
entries.literal: Officials who return from missions abroad, if they know the benefits and harms affecting the common people or hear of the excellence or defects of officials, should fully memorialize so as to broaden what is heard.

entries.zh: 班行職位之中，遷除改轉之際，即當考陳力之輕重，較言事之否臧，奉公切直者當議甄升，臨事蓄縮者須期抑退。
entries.en: At promotions and transfers, weigh each man’s service and the soundness of his counsel: advance the dutiful and forthright, demote the timid in crisis.
entries.literal: Among the ranks in office, at the time of promotion, removal, or transfer, one should examine the weight of their exertion of strength and compare whether their words on affairs are right or wrong; those devoted to public duty and forthright should be considered for advancement, those who shrink before affairs should be expected to be demoted.

entries.zh: 翰林學士、兩省官職居侍從，乃論思諫諍之司；
entries.en: Hanlin academicians and Two-Department officials in close attendance are charged with deliberation and remonstrance;
entries.literal: Hanlin academicians and officials of the Two Departments who attend in close service are the offices for deliberation, reflection, remonstrance, and admonition;

entries.zh: 御史臺官任處憲綱，是擊搏糾彈之地。
entries.en: Censorate officials uphold the law; theirs is the duty of investigation and impeachment.
entries.literal: Censorate officials bear the constitutional net; it is the place for striking, seizing, and impeachment.

entries.zh: 論其職分，尤異群臣，如逐任官內，所獻替啟發彈舉者，至月限滿合遷轉時，宜令中書門下先奏取進止。
entries.en: Their duties set them apart: at each term’s end, when promotion is due, the Secretariat and Chancellery shall first report their memorials and impeachments and obtain imperial approval.
entries.literal: In their duties they differ especially from the multitude of officials; for each term in office, the proposals for replacement, enlightenment, and impeachment they submit—when the monthly term is full and transfer is due, the Secretariat and Chancellery should first memorialize and obtain approval.

entries.zh: 三月辛未，以李晏口為靜安軍，其軍南距冀州百里，北距深州三十里，夾胡盧河為壘。
entries.en: On xinwei in the third month Liyankou was established as Jing'an Army, one hundred li south of Jizhou and thirty li north of Shenzhou, with fortifications along the Hulu River.
entries.literal: In the third month, on day xinwei, Liyankou was made Jing'an Army; the army was one hundred li south of Jizhou and thirty li north of Shenzhou, with fortresses straddling the Hulu River.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：浚胡盧河在正月，至三月始建軍額。）〉
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian notes: the Hulu was dredged in the first month, but the army designation was not created until the third month.))〉
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: The dredging of the Hulu River was in the first month; only in the third month was the army designation established.))〉

entries.zh: 先是，貝、冀之境密邇戎疆，居常敵騎涉河而南，馳突往來洞無阻礙，北鄙之地民不安居。
entries.en: Earlier the Bei–Ji border lay hard against the frontier; enemy horsemen routinely crossed the river to raid at will, and northern villagers could not live in peace.
entries.literal: Previously, the border of Bei and Ji closely adjoined the barbarian frontier; enemy cavalry commonly crossed the river southward and rode in sudden raids back and forth with no obstruction, and the people of the northern marches could not live in peace.

entries.zh: 帝乃按圖定策，遣許州節度使王彥超、曹州節度使韓通等領兵他徙，築壘於李晏口，以兵戍守，功未畢，契丹眾尋至，彥超等擊退之。
entries.en: The Emperor studied the maps and sent Xuzhou commissioner Wang Yanchao, Caozhou commissioner Han Tong, and others to relocate troops and build fortresses at Liyankou. Before the work was finished Khitan forces arrived; Yanchao and his colleagues repulsed them.
entries.literal: The Emperor then consulted maps and fixed strategy, sending Wang Yanchao, military governor of Xuzhou, Han Tong, military governor of Caozhou, and others to lead troops elsewhere, build fortresses at Liyankou, and garrison them with troops; the work was not yet complete when Khitan forces soon arrived, and Yanchao and the others drove them back.

entries.zh: 及壘成，頗扼要害，自是敵騎雖至，不敢涉河，邊民稍得耕牧焉。
entries.en: When the fortresses were finished they commanded the key points; thereafter enemy horsemen dared not cross the river, and border folk could gradually farm and herd again.
entries.literal: When the fortresses were completed, they largely controlled the strategic points; from then on, though enemy cavalry came, they did not dare cross the river, and border people gradually were able to farm and herd.

entries.zh: 壬辰，尚書禮部貢院進新及第進士李覃等一十六人所試詩賦、文論、策文等。
entries.en: On renchen the Ministry of Rites examination hall presented the poetry, fu, essays, and policy papers of the sixteen newly passed jinshi led by Li Tan.
entries.literal: On day renchen, the Examination Hall of the Ministry of Rites of the Secretariat presented the poetry, fu, literary essays, and policy essays submitted by the sixteen newly passed jinshi including Li Tan.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「國家設貢舉之司，求英俊之士，務詢文行，方中科名。
entries.en: An edict declared: “The state holds examinations to seek outstanding men and weighs both learning and conduct before granting the degree.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The state has established the office of tribute examinations to seek outstanding men; it inquires into literary accomplishment and conduct, and only then grants the degree name.

entries.zh: 比聞近年以來，多有濫進，或以年勞而得第，或因媒勢以出身。
entries.en: Lately we have heard that many have passed improperly—some through seniority alone, others through patronage.
entries.literal: We have lately heard that in recent years there have been many who advanced improperly, some gaining the degree through years of service, others entering office through patronage and influence.

entries.zh: 今歲所放舉人，試令看驗，果見紕繆，須至去留。
entries.en: This year’s candidates were re-examined; flaws were found, and some must be kept while others are removed.
entries.literal: The candidates passed this year were tested and examined; flaws were indeed found, and retention or removal was necessary.

entries.zh: 其李覃、何嚴、楊徽之、趙鄰幾等四人，宜放及第。
entries.en: Li Tan, He Yan, Yang Huizhi, and Zhao Linji—the four of them—shall be confirmed as jinshi.
entries.literal: Li Tan, He Yan, Yang Huizhi, Zhao Linji, and three others—four men in all—should be granted passage of the degree.

entries.zh: 其嚴說、武允成、王汾、閭邱舜卿、任惟吉、周度、張慎徽、王翥、馬文、劉選、程浩然、李震等一十二人，藝學未精，並宜勾落，且令苦學，以俟再來。
entries.en: Yan Shuo, Wu Yuncheng, Wang Fen, Lüqiu Shunqing, Ren Weiji, Zhou Du, Zhang Shenhui, Wang Zhu, Ma Wen, Liu Xuan, Cheng Haoran, and Li Zhen—the twelve of them—lack sufficient mastery; all shall be struck from the rolls and told to study hard and try again.
entries.literal: Yan Shuo, Wu Yuncheng, Wang Fen, Lüqiu Shunqing, Ren Weiji, Zhou Du, Zhang Shenhui, Wang Zhu, Ma Wen, Liu Xuan, Cheng Haoran, Li Zhen, and nine others—twelve men in all—their arts and learning not refined, should all be struck from the list and ordered to study hard, awaiting their return.

entries.zh: 禮部侍郎劉溫叟失於選士，頗屬因循，據其過尤，合行譴謫，尚視寬恕，特與矜容，劉溫叟放罪，其將來貢舉公事，仍令所司別具條理以聞。」
entries.en: Vice Minister of Rites Liu Wensou failed in selecting candidates and was unduly lax; by rights he should be punished, but I show leniency and release him from blame. Future examination rules shall be drawn up separately and reported.”
entries.literal: Liu Wensou, Vice Minister of Rites, failed in selecting scholars and was quite negligent; according to his faults he should be censured and demoted, but in view of leniency We specially grant indulgence: Liu Wensou is released from punishment; as to future examination affairs, the responsible offices are still ordered to draw up separate regulations and report."

entries.zh: 夏四月庚戌，以內客省使李彥頵為延州留後。
entries.en: On gengxu in the fourth month of summer, inner reception commissioner Li Yanbin was appointed acting Yanzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day gengxu, Li Yanbin, commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau, was made acting commissioner of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 辛亥，詔：「應自外新除御史，未經朝謝，行過州府，不得受館驛供給及所在公禮。」
entries.en: On xinhai an edict ordered: “Newly appointed censors from the provinces who have not yet attended court may not accept post-station provisions or local official gifts while traveling through prefectures.”
entries.literal: On day xinhai, an edict: "Newly appointed censors from outside who have not yet attended court thanksgiving, when passing through prefectures and districts on their journey, must not receive post-station supplies or local official gifts."

entries.zh: 乙卯，詔於京城四面別築羅城，期以來春興役。
entries.en: On yimao an edict ordered outer walls built on all four sides of the capital, with work to begin the following spring.
entries.literal: On day yimao, an edict ordered construction of outer walls on all four sides of the capital, with labor to begin the coming spring.

entries.zh: 戊午，以翰林學士、給事中竇儀為禮部侍郎，依前充職；
entries.en: On wuwu Hanlin academician and supervising secretary Dou Yi was named Vice Minister of Rites while retaining his existing posts;
entries.literal: On day wuwu, Dou Yi, Hanlin academician and Supervising Secretary, was made Vice Minister of Rites, continuing in his former concurrent duties;

entries.zh: 以禮部侍郎劉溫叟為太子詹事。
entries.en: and Liu Wensou (Vice Minister of Rites) became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Liu Wensou, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以翰林學士、中書舍人楊昭儉為御史中丞。
entries.en: On guihai Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter Yang Zhaojian was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: On day guihai, Yang Zhaojian, Hanlin academician and Secretariat Drafter, was made Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 是月，詔翰林學士承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》各一首，帝親覽之。
entries.en: That month the Emperor ordered Hanlin chief Xu Taifu and more than twenty colleagues each to write an essay On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and Minister and a Border-Pacification Stratagem, which he read personally.
entries.literal: That month, an edict ordered Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief, and more than twenty others below him each to compose one treatise On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister and one Border-Pacification Stratagem; the Emperor personally reviewed them.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·陶蒨傳》：世宗謂宰相曰：「朕觀歷代君臣治平之道，誠為不易，又念唐、晉失德之後，亂臣黠將，僭竊者多。
entries.en: (Song Shi, biography of Tao Qian: Shizong told his chief ministers: “I see how hard it is for ruler and minister together to bring order; and after Tang and Jin lost their virtue, rebellious ministers and cunning generals usurped power in great numbers.
entries.literal: (Song Shi, Biography of Tao Qian: The Emperor Shizong said to the chief ministers: "We observe the way of rulers and ministers through the ages in achieving order and peace—it is truly not easy; We also recall that after Tang and Jin lost virtue, rebellious ministers and cunning generals who usurped were many.

entries.zh: 今中原甫定，吳、蜀、幽、并尚未平附，聲教未能遠被，宣令近臣各為論策，宜導經濟之略。」
entries.en: The Central Plain is only now settled; Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet subdued, and imperial influence does not yet reach far. I order my close advisers each to submit policy essays pointing toward practical statecraft.”
entries.literal: Now the Central Plain has just been settled, but Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet pacified and attached; civilizing instruction cannot yet reach far. We proclaim that close ministers each compose discourses and stratagems, guiding toward policies of statecraft."

entries.zh: 乃命承旨徐臺符已下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》以進。
entries.en: He then ordered chief academician Xu Taifu and more than twenty others each to submit the two essays named above.
entries.literal: He then ordered Xu Taifu, academician-in-chief, and more than twenty others below him each to compose On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister and Border-Pacification Stratagem and present them.

entries.zh: 其略率以修文德、來遠人為意，惟蒨與竇儀、楊昭儉、王樸以封疆密邇江、淮，當用師取之。
entries.en: Most argued for civil virtue and winning distant peoples; only Tao Qian, with Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu, urged military action because the frontier lay close to the Yangzi and Huai.
entries.literal: Their summaries mostly took cultivating civil virtue and drawing distant peoples as their intent; only Qian, with Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu, held that since the frontier closely adjoined the Yangzi and Huai, troops should be used to take it.

entries.zh: 世宗自克高平，常訓兵講武，思混一天下，及覽其策，欣然聽納，由是平南之意益堅矣。）〉
entries.en: Since his victory at Gaoping, Shizong had trained troops and dreamed of unifying the realm; reading these essays he gladly accepted them, and his resolve to conquer the south grew firmer still.))〉
entries.literal: Shizong, since conquering Gaoping, had constantly trained troops and reviewed arms, thinking to unify all under Heaven; when he read their stratagems he gladly accepted them, and from this his intent to pacify the south grew firmer.))〉

entries.zh: 五月辛未，回鶻遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On xinwei in the fifth month Uyghur envoys presented tribute goods.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on day xinwei, the Uyghurs sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 鳳翔節度使王景上言：「奉詔攻收秦、鳳二州，已於今月一日領軍由大散關路進軍次。」
entries.en: Fengxiang commissioner Wang Jing reported: “By imperial order to recover Qin and Feng, on the first of this month I led the army through Dasanguan pass and am advancing.”
entries.literal: Wang Jing, military governor of Fengxiang, memorialized: "In obedience to an edict to attack and recover Qin and Feng prefectures, on the first of this month I have led the army by the Dasanguan route and am advancing."

entries.zh: 先是，晉末契丹入晉，秦州節度使何建以秦、成、階三州入蜀，蜀人又取鳳州。
entries.en: Earlier, at the end of Later Jin the Khitan invaded; Qinzhou commissioner He Jian surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Shu, and Shu also seized Fengzhou.
entries.literal: Previously, at the end of Jin the Khitan entered Jin; He Jian, military governor of Qinzhou, surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu, and the Shu people also took Fengzhou.

entries.zh: 至是，秦、鳳人戶怨蜀之苛政，相次詣闕，乞舉兵收復舊地，乃詔景與宣徽南院使向訓率師赴焉。
entries.en: Now the people of Qin and Feng, resenting Shu’s harsh rule, came in succession to court begging for troops to recover their lands; the Emperor ordered Wang Jing and Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Xiang Xun to lead armies there.
entries.literal: At this time the households of Qin and Feng resented Shu’s harsh government and came one after another to court, begging that troops be raised to recover their old territory; an edict then ordered Jing and Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, to lead armies there.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·王溥傳》：世宗將討秦、鳳，溥薦向拱，遂平之。
entries.en: (Dongdu Shilüe, biography of Wang Pu: When Shizong prepared to attack Qin and Feng, Pu recommended Xiang Gong, and the region was pacified.
entries.literal: (Dongdu Shilüe, Biography of Wang Pu: When Shizong was about to campaign against Qin and Feng, Pu recommended Xiang Gong, and they were pacified.

entries.zh: 世宗因宴酌卮酒賜之，曰：「成吾邊功，卿擇帥之力也。」）〉
entries.en: At a banquet Shizong poured him a cup of wine and said: “Our frontier success is owed to your choice of commander.”))〉
entries.literal: Shizong at a banquet poured a cup of wine and bestowed it on him, saying: "You have accomplished Our frontier achievement—the power is in your choosing the commander."))〉

entries.zh: 甲戌，詔曰：
entries.en: On jiaxu an edict proclaimed:
entries.literal: On day jiaxu, an edict stated:

entries.zh: 諸道府州縣鎮村坊，應有敕額寺院，一切仍舊，其無敕額者，並仰停廢，所有功德佛像及僧尼，並騰並於合留寺院內安置。
entries.en: In every circuit, prefecture, county, garrison, village, and ward: monasteries with imperial charters shall remain; those without shall be abolished, and their images, monks, and nuns consolidated into permitted monasteries.
entries.literal: In all circuits, prefectures, counties, garrisons, villages, and wards: monasteries with imperial patent shall all remain as before; those without patent shall all be ordered abolished; all merit images of Buddha and monks and nuns shall be transferred and placed within monasteries permitted to remain.

entries.zh: 天下諸縣城郭內，若無敕額寺院，只於合停廢寺院內，選功德屋宇最多者，或寺院僧尼各留一所，若無尼住，只留僧寺院一所。
entries.en: Within county seats lacking chartered monasteries, choose from those to be abolished the one with the most merit halls—or retain one monastery each for monks and nuns; where no nuns reside, retain only one monks’ monastery.
entries.literal: Within the walls of all counties under Heaven, if there is no monastery with patent, only from among monasteries to be abolished choose the one with the most merit halls, or leave one monastery each for monks and nuns; if no nuns reside there, leave only one monks’ monastery.

entries.zh: 諸軍鎮坊郭及二百戶已上者，亦依諸縣例指揮。
entries.en: Garrison towns and settlements of two hundred households or more shall follow the same rules as counties.
entries.literal: Military garrisons, ward settlements, and places with two hundred households or more shall likewise follow the county precedent in their orders.

entries.zh: 如邊遠州郡無敕額寺院處，於停廢寺院內僧尼各留兩所。
entries.en: In remote border prefectures without chartered monasteries, retain two each for monks and nuns from among those abolished.
entries.literal: In remote border prefectures where there are no monasteries with patent, from among abolished monasteries leave two each for monks and nuns.

entries.zh: 今後並不得創造寺院蘭若。
entries.en: Henceforth no new monasteries or hermitages may be built.
entries.literal: Hereafter none may newly build monasteries or hermitages.

entries.zh: 王公戚裏諸道節刺已下，今後不得奏請創造寺院及請開置戒壇。
entries.en: Princes, imperial affines, military commissioners, prefects, and all below may no longer petition to build monasteries or open ordination platforms.
entries.literal: Princes, dukes, imperial affines, circuit commissioners, prefects, and all below—hereafter they may not memorialize requesting construction of monasteries or requesting establishment of ordination platforms.

entries.zh: 男子女子如有誌願出家者，並取父母、祖父母處分，已孤者取同居伯叔兄處分，候聽許方得出家。
entries.en: Men and women wishing to take vows must obtain consent from parents and grandparents—or, if orphaned, from uncles and elder brothers in the household—and may leave home only after permission is granted.
entries.literal: Men and women who wish to leave home must all obtain disposition from parents and grandparents; if orphaned, from uncles and elder brothers of the same household; only after permission is heard may they leave home.

entries.zh: 男年十五已上，念得經文一百紙，或讀得經文五百紙，女年十三已上，念得經文七十紙，或讀得經文三百紙者，經本府陳狀乞剃頭，委錄事參軍本判官試驗經文。
entries.en: Men fifteen or older must recite one hundred sheets of scripture or read five hundred; women thirteen or older must recite seventy or read three hundred. They shall petition the prefecture for tonsure and be examined by the recording secretary and military aide.
entries.literal: Men aged fifteen or above who can recite one hundred sheets of scripture or read five hundred sheets; women aged thirteen or above who can recite seventy sheets or read three hundred sheets—after petitioning the prefecture for tonsure, the recording secretary and military aide of the prefecture shall test the scriptures.

entries.zh: 其未剃頭間，須留發髻，如有私剃頭者，卻勒還俗，其本師主決重杖勒還俗，仍配役三年。
entries.en: Before formal tonsure they must keep their hair; illicit tonsure shall force return to lay life, and the master shall be beaten, forced back to lay life, and assigned three years’ corvée.
entries.literal: Before tonsure they must keep their topknots; if anyone tonsures privately, he shall be compelled to return to lay life; his original master shall be sentenced to heavy beating and compelled to return to lay life, and still assigned corvée for three years.

entries.zh: 兩京、大名府、京兆府、青州各處置戒壇，候受戒時，兩京委祠部差官引試，其大名府等三處，只委本判官錄事參軍引試。
entries.en: Ordination platforms shall be established in the Two Capitals, Daming, Jingzhao, and Qingzhou. In the Two Capitals the Bureau of Sacrifices shall examine candidates; at Daming and the other three, the prefectural military aide and recording secretary shall examine them.
entries.literal: The Two Capitals, Daming prefecture, Jingzhao prefecture, and Qingzhou shall each establish ordination platforms; when receiving precepts, the Two Capitals shall commission the Bureau of Sacrifices to dispatch officials to conduct examinations; at Daming and the other three places, only the prefectural military aide and recording secretary shall conduct examinations.

entries.zh: 如有私受戒者，其本人、師主、臨壇三綱、知事僧尼，並同私剃頭例科罪。
entries.en: Illicit ordination shall punish the candidate, his master, the three presiding officers, and the managing monks and nuns under the same rules as illicit tonsure.
entries.literal: If anyone receives precepts privately, the person himself, his master, the three ranks presiding at the platform, and the managing monks and nuns shall all be punished under the precedent for private tonsure.

entries.zh: 應合剃頭受戒人等，逐處聞奏，候敕下，委祠部給付憑由，方得剃頭受戒。
entries.en: Qualified candidates shall be reported from each locality; only after imperial approval and credentials from the Bureau of Sacrifices may tonsure and ordination proceed.
entries.literal: Those who should receive tonsure and precepts shall be reported from each place; after awaiting the edict’s issuance, the Bureau of Sacrifices shall issue credentials, and only then may they receive tonsure and precepts.

entries.zh: 應男女有父母、祖父母在，別無兒息侍養，不聽出家。
entries.en: Men and women with living parents or grandparents and no other children to support them may not take vows.
entries.literal: Men and women who have living parents or grandparents and no other sons or daughters to serve them are not permitted to leave home.

entries.zh: 曾有罪犯，遭官司刑責之人，及棄背父母、逃亡奴婢、奸人細作、惡逆徒黨、山林亡命、未獲賊徒、負罪潛竄人等，並不得出家剃頭。
entries.en: Former criminals punished by the courts, those who abandoned parents, fugitive slaves, spies, traitors, outlaws, uncaptured bandits, and fugitives from justice may not take vows or receive tonsure.
entries.literal: Those who have committed crimes and suffered official punishment, who abandoned parents, fugitive slaves, traitors and spies, parties of great wickedness, outlaws in mountains and forests, uncaptured bandits, and those who fled while bearing guilt—all may not leave home or receive tonsure.

entries.zh: 如有寺院輒容受者，其本人及師主、三綱、知事僧尼、鄰房同住僧，並仰收捉禁勘，申奏取裁。
entries.en: Monasteries that accept such persons shall have the offender, his master, the three officers, managing monks and nuns, and neighboring monks seized, imprisoned, and reported for imperial decision.
entries.literal: If any monastery rashly accepts them, the person himself, his master, the three ranks, managing monks and nuns, and monks dwelling in neighboring cells shall all be ordered seized, imprisoned, and interrogated, with memorial to obtain decision.

entries.zh: 是歲，諸道供到帳籍，所存寺院凡二千六百九十四所，廢寺院凡三萬三百三十六，僧尼系籍者六萬一千二百人。
entries.en: That year the circuits reported registers showing 2,694 monasteries retained, 30,336 abolished, and 61,200 registered monks and nuns.
entries.literal: That year, registers supplied from all circuits showed monasteries retained numbering 2,694 in all, monasteries abolished numbering 30,336 in all, and monks and nuns on the registers numbering 61,200 persons.

entries.zh: 戊寅，以刑部侍郎邊光範為戶部侍郎，以前御史中丞裴巽為刑部侍郎。
entries.en: On wuyin Bian Guangfan (Vice Minister of Punishments) became Vice Minister of Revenue, and former Censor-in-Chief Pei Xun became Vice Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: On day wuyin, Bian Guangfan, Vice Minister of Punishments, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Pei Xun, former Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 己卯，刑部員外郎陳渥賜死，坐檢齊州臨邑縣民田失實也。
entries.en: On jimao Chen Wo, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, was sentenced to death for falsifying his report on civilian fields in Linyi county, Qizhou.
entries.literal: On day jimao, Chen Wo, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments, was granted death; he sat because in inspecting civilian fields in Linyi county, Qizhou, his report was untrue.

entries.zh: 渥為人清苦，臨事有守，以微累而當極刑，時論惜之。
entries.en: Wo lived plainly and held firm in office, yet for a minor offense he suffered capital punishment, and public opinion mourned him.
entries.literal: Wo was a man of pure hardship; in affairs he had integrity, yet for a slight offense he received extreme punishment, and contemporary opinion pitied him.

entries.zh: 戊子，以沙州留後曹元忠為沙州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事。
entries.en: On wuzi acting Shazhou commissioner Cao Yuanzhong was appointed Shazhou military governor, honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent chief councilor.
entries.literal: On day wuzi, Cao Yuanzhong, acting commissioner of Shazhou, was made military governor of Shazhou, Grand Preceptor by inspection, and Concurrent Councilor of the Hall of Equal Affairs.

entries.zh: 丙申，禮部侍郎竇儀奏，請廢童子、明經二科及條貫考試次第，從之。
entries.en: On bingshen Vice Minister of Rites Dou Yi asked to abolish the Child Prodigy and Clarified Classics examinations and their examination regulations; the request was approved.
entries.literal: On day bingshen, Dou Yi, Vice Minister of Rites, memorialized requesting abolition of the Child Prodigy and Clarified Classics examinations and the regulations for examination order; it was approved.

entries.zh: 十一月乙未朔，以宰臣李穀為淮南道前軍行營都部署，知廬、壽等州行府事；
entries.en: On the yimao new moon of the eleventh month chief minister Li Gu was named overall commander of the Huainan vanguard field army with charge of the mobile headquarters at Lu, Shou, and neighboring prefectures;
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yimao new moon, Chief Minister Li Gu was made Overall Commander of the Vanguard Field Army of Huainan Circuit and given charge of the mobile headquarters affairs of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures;

entries.zh: 以許州節度使王彥超為行營副部署；
entries.en: Xuzhou commissioner Wang Yanchao was named deputy overall commander;
entries.literal: Wang Yanchao, military governor of Xuzhou, was made Deputy Overall Commander of the field army;

entries.zh: 命侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤等一十二將，各帶征行之號以從焉。
entries.en: and twelve generals led by Palace Cavalry commander Han Lingkun were ordered to follow, each bearing a campaign title.
entries.literal: Han Lingkun, commander of the Palace Cavalry of the Guard, and eleven other generals were ordered, each bearing a campaign title, to follow.

entries.zh: 己亥，諭淮南州縣，詔曰：
entries.en: On jihai an edict was issued to the Huainan prefectures and counties:
entries.literal: On day jihai, Huainan prefectures and counties were addressed; an edict stated:

entries.zh: 今則推輪命將，鳴鼓出師，征浙右之樓船，下朗陵之戈甲，東西合勢，水陸齊攻。
entries.en: Now we appoint generals, beat the drums, and march: tower ships from western Zhe and arms from Langling shall converge east and west, attacking by land and sea together.
entries.literal: Now We set the war chariot rolling and appoint generals, beat drums and march forth, summon tower ships of the right of Zhe, descend with spears and armor from Langling, combine forces east and west, and attack together by land and water.

entries.zh: 吳孫皓之計窮，自當歸命；
entries.en: When Sun Hao of Wu was at his wits’ end, he submitted;
entries.literal: When Sun Hao of Wu's stratagems were exhausted, he naturally submitted;

entries.zh: 陳叔寶之數盡，何處偷生！
entries.en: when Chen Shubao’s fate was spent, where could he hide!
entries.literal: when Chen Shubao's fate was spent, where could he steal life!

entries.zh: 應淮南將士軍人百姓等，久隔朝廷，莫聞聲教，雖從偽俗，應樂華風，必須善擇安危，早圖去就。
entries.en: Officers, soldiers, and people of Huainan, long cut off from court though you follow a bogus regime, should welcome Chinese civilization, weigh safety and danger wisely, and decide your course early.
entries.literal: All Huainan officers, soldiers, and common people, long cut off from court and hearing no civilizing instruction—though you follow a bogus custom, you should delight in Chinese culture; you must wisely choose safety and danger and early plan departure or staying.

entries.zh: 如能投戈獻款，舉郡來降，具牛酒以犒師，納圭符而請命，車服玉帛豈吝旌酬，土地山河誠無愛惜。
entries.en: If you cast down arms and submit whole prefectures, offering oxen and wine to reward our troops and jade tallies to swear allegiance—carriages, robes, jade, and silk we shall not withhold, nor lands and rivers begrudge.
entries.literal: If you can cast aside weapons and offer allegiance, surrender whole prefectures, provide oxen and wine to reward the army, and present jade tallies to request commands—carriages, robes, jade, and silks, how could We be stingy in reward? Lands, mountains, and rivers We truly do not begrudge.

entries.zh: 刑賞之令，信若丹青，茍或執迷，寧免後悔。
entries.en: Punishment and reward shall be as sure as written law; cling to delusion and you will regret it.
entries.literal: Orders of punishment and reward are trustworthy as black and red ink; if you cling to delusion, how can you escape regret?

entries.zh: 王師所至，軍政甚明，不犯秋毫，有如時雨，百姓父老各務安居，剽擄焚燒必令禁止雲。
entries.en: Where the imperial army goes discipline shall be strict, harming not a hair, gentle as timely rain; the people shall live in peace, and plunder and burning are strictly forbidden.
entries.literal: Where the royal army arrives, military government is very clear, not violating the slightest, like timely rain; common people and elders each strive for peaceful dwelling; plunder, abduction, and burning are strictly forbidden.

entries.zh: 閏月壬子，西南面招討使王景奏，大破西川賊軍於黃花谷，擒偽命都監王巒、孫韜等一千五百餘人。
entries.en: On renzi in the intercalary month Wang Jing reported a great victory over Western Shu rebels at Huanghua Valley, capturing over 1,500 men including bogus overall supervisors Wang Luan and Sun Tao.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on day renzi, Wang Jing, southwestern pacification commissioner, memorialized that he had greatly defeated Western Shu rebel troops at Huanghua Valley and captured more than 1,500 men including the bogus-appointed overall supervisor Wang Luan and Sun Tao.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·李廷珪傳》：周師攻秦、鳳，以廷珪為北路行營都統，高彥儔、呂彥珂為招討。
entries.en: (Jiuguo Zhi, biography of Li Tinggui: When Zhou attacked Qin and Feng, Tinggui was named northern route commander, with Gao Yanchou and Lü Yanke as pacification commissioners.
entries.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi, Biography of Li Tinggui: When Zhou troops attacked Qin and Feng, Tinggui was made overall commander of the northern route field army, and Gao Yanchou and Lü Yanke were made pacification commissioners.

entries.zh: 廷珪遣先鋒指揮使李進以兵據馬嶺，分兵出斜谷，營於白澗，將腹背以攻周師；
entries.en: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin to hold Maling, detached troops through Xiegu pass, and encamped at Baijian to attack the Zhou from front and rear;
entries.literal: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin with troops to hold Maling, divided troops to exit Xiegu, and encamped at Baijian, intending to attack Zhou troops from front and rear;

entries.zh: 又遣染院使王巒領兵出唐倉，與周師遇，蜀師敗走，王巒死之。
entries.en: He also sent dye-house commissioner Wang Luan through Tangcang; the Shu army was defeated and Wang Luan was killed.
entries.literal: He also sent dye-house commissioner Wang Luan to lead troops out of Tangcang; they met Zhou troops, Shu troops were defeated and fled, and Wang Luan died.

entries.zh: 而馬嶺、斜谷之兵聞之皆退奔，高彥儔與諸將謀退守青泥嶺。
entries.en: Hearing this, the troops at Maling and Xiegu fled; Gao Yanchou and his generals planned to withdraw to Qingni Ridge.
entries.literal: When the troops at Maling and Xiegu heard this they all retreated in flight; Gao Yanchou and the generals planned to withdraw and hold Qingni Ridge.

entries.zh: 由是秦、鳳、階、成之地，皆陷於周矣。）〉
entries.en: Thus Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng all fell to Zhou.))〉
entries.literal: Thus the lands of Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng all fell to Zhou.))〉

entries.zh: 癸丑，秦州偽命觀察判官趙比以本城降，詔以比為郢州刺史。
entries.en: On guichou bogus Qinzhou investigating aide Zhao Bi surrendered the city and was appointed Yingzhou prefect.
entries.literal: On day guichou, Zhao Bi, bogus-appointed investigating aide of Qinzhou, surrendered the city; an edict made Bi prefect of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·趙比傳》：高彥儔出師救援，未至，聞軍敗，因潰歸。
entries.en: (Song Shi, biography of Zhao Bi: Gao Yanchou marched to the rescue but, hearing of defeat before he arrived, fled in rout.
entries.literal: (Song Shi, Biography of Zhao Bi: Gao Yanchou marched out to rescue but had not arrived when he heard the army was defeated and therefore fled back in rout.

entries.zh: 比閉門不納，召官屬諭之曰：「今中朝兵甲無敵於天下，自用師西征，戰無不勝，蜀中所遣將皆武勇者，卒皆驍健者，然殺戮遁逃之外，幾無孑遺。
entries.en: Bi shut the gates against him and told his staff: “The central court’s arms are unmatched; since the western campaign began they have won every battle. Shu sent its bravest generals and fiercest troops—yet scarcely a man survives slaughter and flight.
entries.literal: Bi closed the gates and would not admit him, summoned the officials and addressed them: "Now the central court's arms are unmatched under Heaven; since troops were sent west on campaign, in battle there has been no defeat; the generals Shu sent were all brave warriors, the soldiers all fierce and strong—yet apart from slaughter and flight, scarcely one survivor remains.

entries.zh: 我輩安忍坐受其禍，去危就安，當在今日。」
entries.en: How can we sit still and suffer this disaster? We must leave danger for safety—today.”
entries.literal: How can we bear to sit and receive this calamity? Leaving danger for safety should be today."

entries.zh: 眾皆俯伏聽命，比遂以城歸順。
entries.en: All bowed and obeyed, and Bi surrendered the city.
entries.literal: All bowed prostrate and obeyed; Bi then surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 世宗欲命以藩鎮，宰相範質不可，乃授郢州刺史。）〉
entries.en: Shizong wished to give him a military governorship, but Chief Minister Fan Zhi objected, and he received only the Yingzhou prefecture.))〉
entries.literal: Shizong wished to appoint him to a military governorship, but Chief Minister Fan Zhi objected, and he was therefore made prefect of Yingzhou.))〉

entries.zh: 先是，帝以西師久次，艱於糧運，命今上乘驛赴軍前，以觀攻戰之勢。
entries.en: Earlier, because the western army had camped long and supply was difficult, the Emperor sent His present Majesty by post relay to the front to observe the campaign.
entries.literal: Previously, because the western army had long been stationed and grain transport was difficult, the Emperor ordered His present Majesty to ride post-horses to the army front to observe the situation of attack and battle.

entries.zh: 及回，具以事勢上奏，帝甚悅，至是果成功焉。
entries.en: On his return he reported fully on the situation; the Emperor was greatly pleased, and success followed as he had foreseen.
entries.literal: When he returned, he fully memorialized the situation; the Emperor was very pleased, and at this time success was indeed achieved.

entries.zh: 甲子，秘書少監許遜責授蔡州別駕，坐先假竇氏圖書隱而不還也。
entries.en: On jiazi library vice director Xu Xun was demoted to Caizhou vice prefect for failing to return books borrowed from the Dou family.
entries.literal: On day jiazi, Xu Xun, Vice Director of the Secretariat Library, was demoted and appointed Vice Prefect of Caizhou, sitting because he had earlier borrowed books from the Dou clan and concealed them without returning them.

entries.zh: 冬十月庚午，召近臣射於苑中，賜金器鞍馬有差。
entries.en: On gengwu in the tenth month of winter the Emperor summoned close ministers to archery in the park and granted gold vessels, saddles, and horses in varying amounts.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day gengwu, close ministers were summoned to shoot in the park, and gold vessels, saddles, and horses were bestowed in differing amounts.

entries.zh: 辛未，成州歸順。
entries.en: On xinwei Chengzhou submitted.
entries.literal: On day xinwei, Chengzhou submitted.

entries.zh: 癸酉，以給事中王敏為工部侍郎。
entries.en: On guiyou supervising secretary Wang Min was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On day guiyou, Wang Min, Supervising Secretary, was made Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 戊寅，高麗國遣使朝貢。
entries.en: On wuyin Koryŏ sent tribute envoys to court.
entries.literal: On day wuyin, Koryŏ sent envoys to court with tribute.

entries.zh: 丁丑，右散騎常侍康澄責授環州別駕，左司郎中史又元責授商州長史，左驍衛大將軍元霸責授均州別駕，右驍衛將軍林延禔責授登州長史。
entries.en: On dingchou Kang Cheng (right regular attendant) was demoted to Huanzhou vice prefect; Shi Youyuan (left bureau director) to Shangzhou senior recorder; Yuan Ba (left Brave Guards general) to Junzhou vice prefect; and Lin Yanti (right Brave Guards general) to Dengzhou senior recorder.
entries.literal: On day dingchou, Kang Cheng, Regular Attendant of the Right, was demoted to Vice Prefect of Huanzhou; Shi Youyuan, Director of the Left Bureau, was demoted to Senior Recorder of Shangzhou; Yuan Ba, Great General of the Left Brave Guards, was demoted to Vice Prefect of Junzhou; Lin Yanti, General of the Right Brave Guards, was demoted to Senior Recorder of Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 澄等奉使浙中，回日以私便停留，逾時復命，故有是責。
entries.en: Cheng and his colleagues, returning from a mission to Zhe, had delayed for private reasons and reported late; hence the demotions.
entries.literal: Cheng and the others had been on mission to Zhe, and on returning delayed for private convenience, reporting back beyond the deadline; therefore they received this punishment.

entries.zh: 右諫議大夫李知損配流沙門島，坐妄貢章疏，斥讟貴近，及求使兩浙故也。
entries.en: Remonstrance grandee Li Zhisun was exiled to Liushamen Island for rash memorials slandering high officials and seeking a mission to the Two Zhes.
entries.literal: Li Zhisun, Remonstrance Grandee of the Right, was exiled to Liushamen Island, sitting because he had rashly submitted memorials slandering the eminent and near, and because he had sought a mission to the Two Zhes.

entries.zh: 己丑，前太常卿邊蔚卒。
entries.en: On jichou former Imperial Sacrifices Minister Bian Wei died.
entries.literal: On day jichou, Bian Wei, former Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, died.

entries.zh: 是月始議南征。
entries.en: That month plans for the southern campaign were first discussed.
entries.literal: That month discussion of the southern campaign first began.

entries.zh: 善操理者不能有全功，善處身者不能無過失。
entries.en: Even the ablest administrator cannot achieve perfection, and even the most prudent man cannot avoid error.
entries.literal: One who is skilled in governance cannot achieve complete success; one who is skilled in self-conduct cannot be without faults.

entries.zh: 雖堯、舜、禹、湯之上聖，文、武、成康之至明，尚猶思逆耳之言，求苦口之藥，何況後人之不逮哉！
entries.en: Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were supreme sages; Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were supremely enlightened—yet they still welcomed unwelcome counsel and sought bitter medicine for the state. How much more must lesser rulers do so!
entries.literal: Although Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were supreme sages, and Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were supremely enlightened, they still sought words that grated on the ear and medicine bitter to the mouth—how much more must those who come after and do not reach them!

entries.zh: 六月己酉，以曹州節度使韓通充西南面行營都虞候。
entries.en: On jiyou in the sixth month Caozhou commissioner Han Tong was named chief adjutant of the southwestern field army.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on day jiyou, Han Tong, military governor of Caozhou, was appointed Chief Adjutant of the Southwestern Field Army.

entries.zh: 丙辰，以亳州防禦使陳思讓為邢州留後。
entries.en: On bingchen Bozhou defense commissioner Chen Sirang was appointed acting Xingzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: On day bingchen, Chen Sirang, defense commissioner of Bozhou, was made acting commissioner of Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 庚申，詔：「兩京及諸道府州，不得奏薦留守判官、兩使判官、少尹、防禦團練軍事判官，如是隨幕已曾任此職者聽奏。
entries.en: On gengshen an edict ordered: “The Two Capitals and all circuits may not recommend acting commissioners’ aides, bureau aides, vice prefects, or defense and training aides—except those who have already held such posts on a commissioner’s staff.
entries.literal: On day gengshen, an edict: "The Two Capitals and all circuit prefectures and districts may not memorialize recommending acting commissioners' aides, commissioners' aides of the two bureaus, vice prefects, or military aides of defense and training commissioners; if they have already held such posts while on staff, memorializing is permitted.

entries.zh: 防禦團練刺史州，各置推官一員。」
entries.en: Each defense, training, and prefectural state shall appoint one investigating official.”
entries.literal: Defense, training, and prefectural states shall each establish one investigating official."

entries.zh: 辛酉，廢景州為定遠軍。
entries.en: On xinyou Jingzhou was abolished and redesignated Dingyuan Army.
entries.literal: On day xinyou, Jingzhou was abolished and made Dingyuan Army.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以前延州節度使袁鳷為滄州節度使，以前邢州節度使田景鹹為鄧州節度使。
entries.en: On guihai former Yanzhou commissioner Yuan Zhi took Cangzhou, and former Xingzhou commissioner Tian Jingxian took Dengzhou.
entries.literal: On day guihai, Yuan Zhi, former military governor of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Cangzhou; Tian Jingxian, former military governor of Xingzhou, was made military governor of Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 秋七月丁卯朔，以鳳翔節度使王景兼西南面行營都招討使，以宣徽南院使、鎮安軍節度使向訓兼西南面行營都監。
entries.en: On the dingmao new moon of the seventh month of autumn, Fengxiang commissioner Wang Jing was named overall pacification commander of the southwestern field army, and Southern Palace Secretariat commissioner Xiang Xun (Zhen'an Army) was named overall supervisor.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the dingmao new moon, Wang Jing, military governor of Fengxiang, was made concurrent Overall Commander for Pacification of the Southwestern Field Army; Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Zhen'an Army, was made concurrent Overall Supervisor of the Southwestern Field Army.

entries.zh: 戊辰，太子太傅、魯國公和凝卒。
entries.en: On wuchen Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Lu He Ning died.
entries.literal: On day wuchen, He Ning, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Lu, died.

entries.zh: 高麗國王王昭加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，依前使持節元菟州都督、大義軍使，王如故。
entries.en: Koryŏ King Wang Zhao was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor with Grand Master of the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, retaining his commission as Yuantu prefect and Dayi Army commissioner; his kingship was unchanged.
entries.literal: Wang Zhao, King of Koryŏ, was given Grand Master of the Office with Equal Ceremony to the Three Excellencies and Grand Preceptor by inspection, continuing as before as commissioner holding the staff of Yuantu Prefecture and commissioner of the Dayi Army; his kingship was as before.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以前滄州節度使李暉為邠州節度使。
entries.en: On xinhai former Cangzhou commissioner Li Hui was appointed Binzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: On day xinhai, Li Hui, former military governor of Cangzhou, was made military governor of Binzhou.

entries.zh: 壬子，潞州奏，破河東賊軍於祁縣。
entries.en: On renzi Luzhou reported defeating Hedong rebel troops at Qixian.
entries.literal: On day renzi, Luzhou memorialized that Hedong rebel troops were defeated at Qixian.

entries.zh: 癸丑，西南面行營都部署王景奏，收復鳳州，獲偽命節度使王環。
entries.en: On guichou southwestern field army commander Wang Jing reported recovering Fengzhou and capturing bogus commissioner Wang Huan.
entries.literal: On day guichou, Wang Jing, overall commander of the southwestern field army, memorialized that Fengzhou was recovered and the bogus-appointed military governor Wang Huan was captured.

entries.zh: 乙卯。
entries.en: On yimao.
entries.literal: On day yimao.

entries.zh: 曲赦秦、鳳、階、成等州管內罪人，自顯德二年十一月已前，凡有罪犯，無問輕重，一切釋放。
entries.en: A partial amnesty was granted for criminals in Qin, Feng, Jie, Cheng, and related prefectures: all offenses before the eleventh month of Xiande 2, whatever their severity, were pardoned.
entries.literal: A partial amnesty was granted for criminals within the jurisdictions of Qin, Feng, Jie, Cheng, and other prefectures; from before the eleventh month of Xiande 2, all who had committed crimes, regardless of severity, were entirely released.

entries.zh: 丁巳，前邠州節度使折從阮卒。
entries.en: On dingsi former Binzhou commissioner Zhe Congruan died.
entries.literal: On day dingsi, Zhe Congruan, former military governor of Binzhou, died.

entries.zh: 己未，邢州奏，河東劉崇死。
entries.en: On jiwei Xingzhou reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had died.
entries.literal: On day jiwei, Xingzhou memorialized that Liu Chong of Hedong had died.

entries.zh: 壬戌，淮南前軍都部署李穀奏，先鋒都指揮使白延遇破淮賊於來遠鎮。
entries.en: On renxu Huainan vanguard commander Li Gu reported that vanguard commander Bai Yanyu had defeated Huai rebels at Laiyuan town.
entries.literal: On day renxu, Li Gu, overall commander of the Huainan vanguard army, memorialized that Bai Yanyu, vanguard commander, had defeated Huai rebels at Laiyuan town.

entries.zh: 十二月丙寅，以左金吾大將軍蓋萬為右監門上將軍。
entries.en: On bingyin in the twelfth month left Golden Crow general Gai Wan was appointed senior right Gate Watch general.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on day bingyin, Gai Wan, Great General of the Left Golden Crow, was made Senior General of the Right Gate Watch.

entries.zh: 丁卯，淄州奏，前中書侍郎、同平章事景範卒。
entries.en: On dingmao Zizhou reported that former secretariat vice director and chief councilor Jing Fan had died.
entries.literal: On day dingmao, Zizhou memorialized that Jing Fan, former Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Councilor, had died.

entries.zh: 庚午，右金吾衛上將軍王守恩卒。
entries.en: On gengwu right Golden Crow senior general Wang Shou'en died.
entries.literal: On day gengwu, Wang Shou'en, Senior General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, died.

entries.zh: 辛未，安州奏，盜殺防禦使張穎。
entries.en: On xinwei Anzhou reported that bandits had killed defense commissioner Zhang Ying.
entries.literal: On day xinwei, Anzhou memorialized that bandits had killed Zhang Ying, defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 是日，翰林學士承旨徐臺符卒。
entries.en: That same day Hanlin chief academician Xu Taifu died.
entries.literal: That day, Xu Taifu, Hanlin academician-in-chief, died.

entries.zh: 甲戌，李穀奏，破淮賊二千人於壽州城下。
entries.en: On jiaxu Li Gu reported defeating two thousand Huai rebels below Shouzhou.
entries.literal: On day jiaxu, Li Gu memorialized that two thousand Huai rebels were defeated below the walls of Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 丙子，以左諫議大夫、權知開封府事王樸為左散騎常侍，充端明殿學士，依前權知開封府事。
entries.en: On bingzi remonstrance grandee and acting Kaifeng mayor Wang Pu was named left regular attendant and Duanming Hall academician while retaining acting charge of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: On day bingzi, Wang Pu, Remonstrance Grandee of the Left and acting mayor of Kaifeng, was made Regular Attendant of the Left, appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, and continued as before as acting mayor of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 永興軍奏，節度使劉詞卒。
entries.en: Yongxing Army reported that commissioner Liu Ci had died.
entries.literal: Yongxing Army memorialized that Liu Ci, military commissioner, had died.

entries.zh: 己卯，李穀奏，破淮賊千餘人於山口鎮。
entries.en: On jimao Li Gu reported defeating over a thousand Huai rebels at Shankou town.
entries.literal: On day jimao, Li Gu memorialized that more than a thousand Huai rebels were defeated at Shankou town.

entries.zh: 丙戌，樞密使鄭仁誨卒。
entries.en: On bingxu Military Affairs commissioner Zheng Renhui died.
entries.literal: On day bingxu, Zheng Renhui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, died.

entries.zh: 辛卯，西南面行營都部署王景，差人部送所獲偽鳳翔節度使王環至闕。
entries.en: On xinmao southwestern field army commander Wang Jing sent men to escort captured bogus Fengxiang commissioner Wang Huan to court.
entries.literal: On day xinmao, Wang Jing, overall commander of the southwestern field army, dispatched men to escort the captured bogus Fengxiang military governor Wang Huan to court.

entries.zh: 詔釋之，仍賜鞍馬衣服，尋授右驍衛
entries.en: An edict released him, granted saddle, horse, and clothing, and soon appointed him to the Right Brave Guards
entries.literal: An edict released him and still bestowed saddle, horse, and clothing; soon he was appointed to the Right Brave Guards

entries.zh: 〈（按：原本闕一字。）〉
entries.en: (Note: one character is missing in the original text.))〉
entries.literal: (Note: the original text lacks one character.))〉

entries.zh: 大將軍。
entries.en: Great General.
entries.literal: Great General.

entries.zh: 是冬，命起居郎陶文舉征殘租於宋州。
entries.en: That winter attendant Tao Wenju was ordered to collect overdue rent in Songzhou.
entries.literal: That winter, Tao Wenju, Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Chambers, was ordered to collect overdue rent in Songzhou.

entries.zh: 文舉本酷吏也，宋民被其刑者凡數千，冤號之聲聞於道路，有悼髦之輩，不勝其刑而死者數人，物議以為不允。
entries.en: Wenju was a notorious harsh official; thousands in Song suffered under him, and cries of injustice filled the roads. Several youths died under his punishments, and public opinion condemned the methods as unjust.
entries.literal: Wenju was originally a harsh official; Song common people punished by him numbered several thousand, and cries of injustice were heard on the roads; there were youths in mourning who could not bear his punishments and several died; public opinion held this unjust.

entries.zh: 九月丙寅朔，詔禁天下銅器，始議立監鑄錢。
entries.en: On the bingyin new moon of the ninth month bronze vessels were banned empire-wide and a mint bureau was first proposed.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the bingyin new moon, an edict prohibited bronze vessels throughout the realm and first discussed establishing a bureau to cast coin.

entries.zh: 癸未，以太子賓客趙上交為吏部侍郎，以吏部侍郎於德辰、司徒詡並為太子賓客。
entries.en: On guiwei Heir Apparent mentor Zhao Shangjiao became Vice Minister of Personnel, while Vice Ministers Yu Dechen and Situ Xu became Heir Apparent mentors.
entries.literal: On day guiwei, Zhao Shangjiao, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Yu Dechen and Situ Xu, Vice Ministers of Personnel, were both made Mentors of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 乙酉，詔文武百僚，今後遇天清節，依近臣例各賜衣服。
entries.en: On yiyou an edict granted all civil and military officials festival clothing on Tianqing Day, following the precedent for close ministers.
entries.literal: On day yiyou, an edict ordered that civil and military officials of all ranks, hereafter on encountering the Tianqing Festival, should each be granted clothing according to the precedent for close ministers.

entries.zh: 辛卯，西南面招討使王景，部送所獲西川軍校姜暉已下三百人至闕。
entries.en: On xinmao southwestern pacification commissioner Wang Jing escorted three hundred captured Western Shu officers led by Jiang Hui to court.
entries.literal: On day xinmao, Wang Jing, pacification commissioner of the southwest, escorted to court the three hundred captured Western Shu military officers including Jiang Hui and below.

entries.zh: 甲午，潞州部送先擒到河東兵馬監押程支等二百人至闕。
entries.en: On jiawu Luzhou escorted two hundred previously captured Hedong officers led by military supervisor Cheng Zhi to court.
entries.literal: On day jiawu, Luzhou escorted to court the two hundred men previously captured, including Cheng Zhi, military supervisor of Hedong horse and troops.

entries.zh: 詔所獲西川、河東軍校已下並釋之，各賜錢帛有差。
entries.en: An edict released all captured Western Shu and Hedong officers and granted each cash and silk in varying amounts.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that all captured Western Shu and Hedong military officers and below be released, each granted money and silks in differing amounts.

entries.zh: 六月甲子，以鳳翔節度使王景為秦州節度使，兼西面沿邊都部署；
entries.en: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Jing of Fengxiang was made Qinzhou governor and overall western frontier commander;
entries.literal: In the sixth month, day jiazi, the military governor of Fengxiang Wang Jing was made military governor of Qinzhou and overall commander of the western frontier;

entries.zh: 以宣徽南院使、陳州節度使向訓為淮南節度使，依前南院宣徽使，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Xiang Xun was confirmed as Huainan governor, retaining his commissioner post, with the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor;
entries.literal: the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau and military governor of Chenzhou Xiang Xun was made military governor of Huainan, retaining his former post as Southern Bureau commissioner, with the added title of Grand Preceptor by inspection;

entries.zh: 以曹州節度使韓通為許州節度使，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Han Tong of Caozhou was transferred to Xuzhou with the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor;
entries.literal: the military governor of Caozhou Han Tong was made military governor of Xuzhou, with the added title of Grand Preceptor by inspection;

entries.zh: 以亳州防禦使王全斌為隴州防禦使，遙領利州昭武軍兩使留後。
entries.en: Wang Quanbin of Bozhou was made Longzhou defense commissioner and concurrently acting commissioner of Lizhou Zhaowu Army.
entries.literal: the defense commissioner of Bozhou Wang Quanbin was made defense commissioner of Longzhou and held concurrently the post of acting commissioner of the two offices of Lizhou Zhaowu Army.

entries.zh: 丙寅，許州王彥超移鎮永興軍，鄧州田景鹹移鎮鄜州。
entries.en: On bingyin Wang Yanchao was transferred from Xuzhou to Yongxing, and Tian Jingxian from Dengzhou to Fuzhou.
entries.literal: On day bingyin, Wang Yanchao of Xuzhou was transferred to Yongxing Army, and Tian Jingxian of Dengzhou was transferred to Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 御史中丞楊昭儉、知雜侍御史趙礪、侍御史張糾並停任，坐鞫獄失實也。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, supervising censor Zhao Li, and attendant censor Zhang Jiu were suspended for mishandling criminal cases.
entries.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, the supervising attendant censor Zhao Li, and the attendant censor Zhang Jiu were all suspended for errors in conducting criminal investigations.

entries.zh: 丁卯，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎陶穀為兵部侍郎，充翰林學士承旨；
entries.en: On dingmao Tao Gu was made Vice Minister of War and chief Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: On day dingmao, the Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Tao Gu was made Vice Minister of War and Chief Hanlin academician;

entries.zh: 以水部員外郎知制誥扈載、度支員外郎王著，並本官充翰林學士；
entries.en: Hu Zai of the Water Bureau and Wang Zhu of the Revenue Bureau were appointed Hanlin academicians while keeping their posts;
entries.literal: the Vice Director of the Water Bureau and drafter of edicts Hu Zai and the Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau Wang Zhu were both made Hanlin academicians while retaining their original offices;

entries.zh: 以給事中高防為右散騎常侍；
entries.en: Supervising Secretary Gao Fang was made Right Regular Attendant;
entries.literal: the Supervising Secretary Gao Fang was made Right Regular Attendant;

entries.zh: 以前都官郎中、知制誥薛居正為左諫議大夫，充昭文館學士，判館事。
entries.en: former Bureau of Justice director Xue Juzheng was made Left Remonstrance Grand Master, Zhaowen Hall academician, and hall administrator.
entries.literal: the former Director of the Bureau of Justice and drafter of edicts Xue Juzheng was made Left Remonstrance Grand Master, Hanlin academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and administrator of the hall's affairs.

entries.zh: 壬申，曲赦淮南道諸州見禁罪人，自今年六月十一日已前，凡有違犯，無問輕重，並不窮問。
entries.en: On renshen a partial amnesty covered all prisoners in Huainan prefectures for offenses before the eleventh of the sixth month, without regard to severity.
entries.literal: On day renshen, a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners under detention in all prefectures of the Huainan circuit. For offenses before the eleventh day of the sixth month of this year, regardless of severity, no further investigation would be pursued.

entries.zh: 先屬江南之時，應有非理科徭，無名配率，一切停罷雲。
entries.en: All improper levies imposed under Jiangnan rule were abolished.
entries.literal: For the period when they had belonged to Jiangnan, all improper corvée levies and nameless additional assessments were to be entirely halted.

entries.zh: 戊寅，以右衛上將軍扈彥珂為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: On wuyin Hu Yanke, general of the Right Guard, was made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and retired.
entries.literal: On day wuyin, the General of the Right Guard Hu Yanke was made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and retired.

entries.zh: 庚辰，以西京留守王晏為鳳翔節度使。
entries.en: On gengchen Western Capital regent Wang Yan was appointed military governor of Fengxiang.
entries.literal: On day gengchen, the Western Capital regent Wang Yan was made military governor of Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 戊子，升贍國軍為濱州。
entries.en: On wuzi Shanguo Army was elevated to Bin Prefecture.
entries.literal: On day wuzi, Shanguo Army was promoted to Bin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 淮南道招討使李重進奏，壽州賊軍攻南寨，王師不利。
entries.en: Li Chongjin reported that Shouzhou rebels had attacked the southern camp and the imperial army had suffered a setback.
entries.literal: The Huainan campaign commander Li Chongjin memorialized that the Shouzhou rebel army had attacked the southern stockade and the imperial army had fared badly.

entries.zh: 先是，詔步軍都指揮使李繼勛營於壽州之南，攻賊壘。
entries.en: Earlier Li Jixun, commander of the foot army, had been ordered to camp south of Shouzhou and assault the rebel works.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Commander of the Foot Army Li Jixun had been ordered to encamp south of Shouzhou and attack the rebel fortifications.

entries.zh: 是日，賊軍出城來攻我軍，破柵而入，其攻城之具並為賊所焚，將士死者數百人。
entries.en: That day the rebels sallied, broke into the camp, burned the siege equipment, and killed several hundred men.
entries.literal: That day the rebel army came out of the city to attack our army, broke through the palisade and entered, and all siege equipment was burned by the rebels; several hundred officers and soldiers died.

entries.zh: 李重進在東寨，亦不能救。
entries.en: Li Chongjin in the eastern camp could not relieve them.
entries.literal: Li Chongjin was in the eastern stockade and likewise could not rescue them.

entries.zh: 時城堅未下，師老於外，加之暑毒，糧運不繼。
entries.en: The city still held; the army was weary, summer heat was severe, and supplies ran short.
entries.literal: At that time the city walls were strong and had not fallen; the army was weary from long campaigning abroad, and in addition there was summer heat and poison; grain transport did not keep up.

entries.zh: 李繼勛喪失之後，軍無固誌，諸將議欲退軍，賴今上自六合領兵歸闕，過其城下，因為駐留旬日，王師復振。
entries.en: After Jixun's defeat morale collapsed and officers talked of retreat. Zhao Kuangyin, returning from Liuhe, halted below the city for ten days and restored the army's spirit.
entries.literal: After Li Jixun's defeat the army had no firm resolve; the generals discussed withdrawing. Thanks to Zhao Kuangyin leading troops back to the capital from Liuhe and passing below the city, he stayed for ten days on that account, and the imperial army revived.

entries.zh: 顯德三年春正月乙未朔，帝不受朝賀。
entries.en: On New Year's Day in spring of the third year of Xiande, the Emperor declined the usual New Year court congratulations.
entries.literal: On the first day of the first month in spring of the third year of Xiande (day yiwei), the Emperor did not accept court congratulations.

entries.zh: 前司空蘇禹珪卒。
entries.en: Su Yugui, the former Minister of Works, died.
entries.literal: The former Minister of Works Su Yugui died.

entries.zh: 丁酉，李穀奏，破淮賊於上窯。
entries.en: On dingyou, Li Gu reported a victory over the Huainan rebels at Shangyao.
entries.literal: On day dingyou, Li Gu memorialized that the Huainan rebels had been defeated at Shangyao.

entries.zh: 戊戌，發丁夫十萬城京師羅城。
entries.en: On wuxu, the court drafted one hundred thousand laborers to fortify the capital's outer ramparts.
entries.literal: On day wuxu, one hundred thousand corvée laborers were mobilized to build the outer wall of the capital.

entries.zh: 庚子，詔取此月八日幸淮南。
entries.en: On gengzi, an edict scheduled the Emperor's departure for Huainan on the eighth of the month.
entries.literal: On day gengzi, an edict set the eighth day of this month for an imperial visit to Huainan.

entries.zh: 殿中監馬從赟免所居官，坐幹沒外孫女霍氏之資產，為人所訟故也。
entries.en: Ma Congyun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, was dismissed after being sued for embezzling the property of his maternal granddaughter née Huo.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Ma Congyun was removed from office for embezzling the assets of his maternal granddaughter née Huo, because he had been sued by others.

entries.zh: 辛丑，以宣徽南院使向訓為權東京留守，以端明殿學士王樸為副留守。
entries.en: On xinchou, Xiang Xun of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was appointed acting regent of the Eastern Capital, with Wang Pu, Academician of Duanming Hall, as his deputy.
entries.literal: On day xinchou, the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting Eastern Capital regent, and the Academician of Duanming Hall Wang Pu was made deputy regent.

entries.zh: 壬寅，車駕發京師，丁未，李穀奏，自壽州引軍退守正陽。
entries.en: On renyin the Emperor left the capital. On dingwei, Li Gu reported that he had pulled his forces back from Shouzhou to defend Zhengyang.
entries.literal: On day renyin, the imperial carriage departed the capital. On day dingwei, Li Gu memorialized that he had withdrawn his army from Shouzhou to hold Zhengyang.

entries.zh: 辛亥，李重進奏，大破淮賊於正陽，斬首二萬餘級，伏屍三十里，臨陣斬賊大將劉彥貞，生擒偏將鹹師朗已下，獲戎甲三十萬副、馬五百匹。
entries.en: On xinhai, Li Chongjin reported a great victory at Zhengyang: over twenty thousand enemy dead, bodies strewn for thirty li along the field. He killed the rebel commander Liu Yanzhen in the fighting, took Deputy General Xian Shilang and others alive, and captured three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.
entries.literal: On day xinhai, Li Chongjin memorialized that he had routed the Huainan rebels at Zhengyang, taking more than twenty thousand heads; corpses lay for thirty li; in battle he slew the rebel general Liu Yanzhen and captured alive the deputy generals Xian Shilang and others, seizing three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.

entries.zh: 先是，李穀駐軍於壽春城下，以攻其城，既而淮南援軍大至，乃與將佐謀曰：「賊軍舟棹將及正陽，我師無水戰之備，萬一橋梁不守，則大軍隔絕矣，不如全師退守正陽浮橋，以俟鑾輅。」
entries.en: Earlier Li Gu had besieged Shouchun. When strong Huainan reinforcements arrived, he told his commanders: "The enemy fleet is nearing Zhengyang, and we are not equipped for river fighting. If the bridge falls, the army will be stranded. We should pull back intact to the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang and wait for the Emperor."
entries.literal: Earlier, Li Gu had encamped below Shouchun city to attack it. When large Huainan relief forces arrived, he consulted his officers and said: "The rebel fleet will soon reach Zhengyang. Our army is not prepared for naval combat. If the bridge should not be held, the main force would be cut off. It would be better to withdraw the whole army to defend the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang and await the imperial carriage."

entries.zh: 諸將皆以為然，遂燔其糧草而退。
entries.en: The officers all agreed, so they burned their stores and retreated.
entries.literal: All the generals agreed, and they burned their grain and fodder and withdrew.

entries.zh: 軍回之際無復嚴整，公私之間頗多亡失，淮北役夫亦有陷於賊境者。
entries.en: The withdrawal was disorderly, with heavy losses of government and private property, and some laborers from north of the Huai were captured behind enemy lines.
entries.literal: On the march back discipline was no longer maintained; both public and private property suffered considerable losses, and corvée laborers north of the Huai also fell into enemy territory.

entries.zh: 帝聞之，急詔侍衛都指揮使李重進率師赴之。
entries.en: On hearing this, the Emperor urgently ordered Li Chongjin, Commander of the Palace Guards, to march to their relief.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he urgently ordered the Commander of the Palace Guards Li Chongjin to lead troops there.

entries.zh: 時淮賊乘李穀退軍之勢，發戰棹數百艘沿淮而上，且張斷橋之勢，彥貞以大軍列陣而進。
entries.en: The Huainan rebels exploited Li Gu's retreat, sending hundreds of warships up the Huai while positioning to cut the bridge; Liu Yanzhen advanced with his main force in battle order.
entries.literal: At that time the Huainan rebels, taking advantage of Li Gu's withdrawal, sent several hundred warships up the Huai and also deployed to sever the bridge; Liu Yanzhen advanced with a large army in battle formation.

entries.zh: 李重進既至正陽，聞淮軍在近，率諸將渡橋而進，與賊軍遇，重進等合勢擊之，一鼓而敗之。
entries.en: Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang, learned the enemy was close, and led his officers across the bridge. They met the rebel force and, joining their strength in one assault, broke them at the first charge.
entries.literal: When Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang and heard the Huainan army was near, he led his generals across the bridge to advance, met the rebel army, and Li Chongjin and the others combined their strength and attacked; at the first drum they routed them.

entries.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》：世宗親征，行至圉鎮，聞蒨軍卻，意唐兵必追之，遣李重進急趨正陽，曰：「唐兵且至，宜急擊之。」
entries.en: (Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang records that during Shizong's personal campaign, at Yuzhen he heard Qian's army had pulled back and expected Tang troops to pursue. He sent Li Chongjin urgently to Zhengyang with the order: "Tang troops are about to arrive; attack them at once."
