entries.literal: (From Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang: When Shizong campaigned in person and reached Yuzhen, he heard that Qian's army had withdrawn and expected Tang troops would pursue. He sent Li Chongjin in haste to Zhengyang, saying: "Tang troops are about to arrive; you should strike them quickly."

entries.zh: 彥貞等聞蒨退軍，皆以為怯，裨將鹹師朗曰：「追之可大獲。」
entries.en: Liu Yanzhen and his officers took Qian's withdrawal as a sign of cowardice. Deputy General Xian Shilang urged: "A pursuit would bring rich spoils."
entries.literal: When Liu Yanzhen and the others heard that Qian's army had withdrawn, they all thought it showed cowardice. Deputy General Xian Shilang said: "If we pursue them we can gain a great prize."

entries.zh: 劉仁贍使人喻之曰：「君來赴援，未交戰而敵人退，不可測也，慎勿追逐。
entries.en: Liu Renshan sent a messenger warning him: "You came as reinforcements. The enemy retreated without fighting—that is suspicious. Do not pursue.
entries.literal: Liu Renshan sent someone to instruct him: "You came to give aid. The enemy withdrew before any battle was joined—this is unpredictable. Be careful not to pursue.

entries.zh: 君為大將，安危以之，脫有不利，大事去矣。」
entries.en: You are the commander-in-chief; the fate of the campaign rests on you. One setback could ruin everything."
entries.literal: As the supreme commander, the army's safety or peril rests on you. If anything goes wrong, the great enterprise will be lost."

entries.zh: 前軍張全約亦曰：「不可追。」
entries.en: Vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue likewise advised against pursuit."
entries.literal: The vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue also said: "Do not pursue."

entries.zh: 彥貞曰：「軍容在我，汝輩何知？
entries.en: Liu Yanzhen snapped: "I command this army—what do you know?
entries.literal: Liu Yanzhen said: "Military bearing is mine to decide—what do you people know?

entries.zh: 沮吾事者斬！」
entries.en: Anyone who stands in my way will be executed!"
entries.literal: Whoever discourages my plan shall be beheaded!"

entries.zh: 比至正陽，而重進先至，未及食而戰。
entries.en: When they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin was already there; the armies clashed before the southerners could even take a meal.
entries.literal: By the time they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin had already arrived; before they could eat, battle was joined.

entries.zh: 彥貞施利刃於拒馬，又刻木為獸，號捷馬牌，以皮囊布鐵蒺藜於地。
entries.en: Yanzhen armed his abatis with blades, set up carved wooden beasts called Swift Horse Boards, and strewed the ground with bagged caltrops.
entries.literal: Liu Yanzhen fitted chevaux-de-frise with sharp blades, carved wooden beasts called "Swift Horse Boards," and spread caltrops on the ground in leather bags.

entries.zh: 周兵見而知其怯，一鼓而敗之，彥貞死於陣。）〉
entries.en: The Zhou soldiers saw these tricks and knew their foe lacked nerve; one charge broke them, and Yanzhen fell in battle.)〉
entries.literal: The Zhou troops saw these devices and knew their enemy was timid; at one drum they routed them, and Yanzhen died on the field.)〉

entries.zh: 殺獲之外，降者三千餘人，皆為我將趙晁所殺。
entries.en: Beyond the dead and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were slaughtered by the Zhou general Zhao Chao.
entries.literal: Apart from those killed and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were all put to death by our general Zhao Chao.

entries.zh: 甲寅，車駕至正陽。
entries.en: On jiayin the Emperor arrived at Zhengyang.
entries.literal: On day jiayin, the imperial carriage reached Zhengyang.

entries.zh: 以侍衛都指揮使李重進為淮南道行營都招討使，命宰臣李穀判壽州行府事。
entries.en: Li Chongjin, Commander of the Palace Guards, was appointed overall commander of the Huainan campaign, and Chief Minister Li Gu was assigned to run the field headquarters at Shouzhou.
entries.literal: The Commander of the Palace Guards Li Chongjin was made overall commander of the Huainan campaign headquarters, and the chief minister Li Gu was ordered to administer affairs at the Shouzhou field headquarters.

entries.zh: 乙卯，車駕渡淮。
entries.en: On yimao the Emperor crossed the Huai River.
entries.literal: On day yimao, the imperial carriage crossed the Huai.

entries.zh: 丙辰，至壽州城下，營於州西北淝水之陽，詔移正陽浮橋於下蔡。
entries.en: On bingchen he camped south of the Fei River below Shouzhou and ordered the Zhengyang pontoon bridge relocated to Xiacai.
entries.literal: On day bingchen, he reached below Shouzhou city and encamped on the south bank of the Fei River northwest of the prefecture. An edict ordered the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang moved to Xiacai.

entries.zh: 庚申，耀兵於城下。
entries.en: On gengshen the army paraded in strength before the city walls.
entries.literal: On day gengshen, troops were displayed in force below the city.

entries.zh: 〈（《春明退朝錄》云：家有《範魯公雜錄》，記世宗親征忠正，駐蹕城下，中夜有白虹自淝水起，亙數丈，下貫城中，數刻方沒。）〉
entries.en: (The Record of Leaving Court at Chunming notes that Fan the Duke of Lu's Miscellaneous Records describes Shizong's siege of Shouzhou: at midnight a white rainbow rose from the Fei, spanned several zhang, and plunged into the city before fading after some time.)〉
entries.literal: (The Record of Leaving Court at Chunming states: Our family has Fan the Duke of Lu's Miscellaneous Records, which records that when Shizong campaigned in person against Zhongzheng and halted below the city, at midnight a white rainbow rose from the Fei River, stretched several zhang, and pierced down into the city; only after several quarters did it vanish.)〉

entries.zh: 壬戌，今上奏，破淮賊萬餘眾於渦口，斬偽兵馬都監何延錫等，獲戰船五十艘。
entries.en: On renxu Zhao Kuangyin reported victory at Wokou over ten thousand Huainan troops, the execution of the enemy Director of Horse and Foot He Yanxi, and the capture of fifty warships.
entries.literal: On day renxu, Zhao Kuangyin memorialized that he had defeated more than ten thousand Huainan rebels at Wokou, beheaded the false Director of Horse and Foot He Yanxi and others, and captured fifty warships.

entries.zh: 顯德四年春正月己丑朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如儀。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Xiande, on the new moon of the first month of spring, the Emperor presided in the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive New Year congratulations, with guards and escort arrayed according to ritual.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, spring, first month, on the day jichou (the new moon), the Emperor took his seat in the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive court congratulations; guards and escort followed the prescribed ritual.

entries.zh: 詔天下見禁罪人，除大辟外，一切釋放。
entries.en: An edict ordered the release of all prisoners held in custody empire-wide, save those sentenced to death.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that all prisoners currently under detention throughout the realm, except those guilty of capital offenses, were to be released entirely.

entries.zh: 壬寅，兵部尚書張昭上言：「奉詔編修太祖實錄及梁、唐二末主實錄。
entries.en: On renyin, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial: "By imperial order I am compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu and the veritable records of the last two rulers of Liang and Tang.
entries.literal: On the day renyin, Minister of War Zhang Zhao memorialized: "By edict I am compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu and the Veritable Records of the two final rulers of Liang and Tang.

entries.zh: 伏以撰《漢書》者先為項籍，編《蜀記》首序劉璋，貴神器之傳授有因，歷數之推遷得序。
entries.en: It is customary, as when the Book of Han began with Xiang Yu and the Shu Annals opened with Liu Zhang, to show that the transfer of the Mandate has its logic and that dynastic succession follows a proper sequence.
entries.literal: Humbly considering that the compiler of the Book of Han began with Xiang Yu, and the Shu Annals opened with Liu Zhang — this honors that the transmission of the regalia has its reasons, and the succession of dynastic mandate follows proper order.

entries.zh: 伏緣漢隱帝君臨在太祖之前，歷試之績，並在隱帝朝內，請先修隱帝實錄，以全太祖之事功。
entries.en: Because Emperor Yin of Han reigned before Taizu and Taizu's early trials all belong to Yin's reign, I ask that the Veritable Records of Emperor Yin be compiled first, so that Taizu's achievements may be set forth completely.
entries.literal: Humbly, because Emperor Yin of Han reigned before Taizu, and Taizu's trials and achievements all fell within the reign of Emperor Yin, I request first compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Yin to complete Taizu's record of deeds.

entries.zh: 又以唐末主之前有閔帝，在位四月，出奔於衛，亦未編紀，請修閔帝實錄。
entries.en: Likewise, before the last Tang ruler there was Emperor Min, who reigned four months and fled to Wei; no record has been made of him either — please compile his veritable records.
entries.literal: Further, before the final Tang ruler was Emperor Min, who held the throne four months and fled to Wei — also not yet recorded — please compile Veritable Records of Emperor Min.

entries.zh: 其清泰帝實錄，請書為廢帝實錄。」
entries.en: As for the Veritable Records of Emperor Qingtai, please entitle them the Veritable Records of the Deposed Emperor."
entries.literal: As for the Veritable Records of Emperor Qingtai, please title them Veritable Records of the Deposed Emperor."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: His request was granted.

entries.zh: 〈（案：自「唐末主」以上，原文疑有脫誤。
entries.en: (Note: From the passage on "the final Tang ruler" upward, the received text appears corrupt or incomplete.
entries.literal: (Note: From "the final Tang ruler" upward, the original text is suspected of lacunae and errors.

entries.zh: 據《五代會要》云：梁末主之上有郢王友珪，篡弒居位，未有紀錄，請依《宋書》劉劭例，書為「元兇友珪」，其末主請依古義書曰後梁實錄。
entries.en: The Five Dynasties Essentials states that above the last Liang ruler stood Prince of Ying Yougui, who seized power by regicide and has no chronicle; following the Song History treatment of Liu Shao, he should be styled "the arch-criminal Yougui," while the last ruler should be recorded, in classical fashion, as the Later Liang Veritable Records.
entries.literal: According to the Five Dynasties Essentials: above the final Liang ruler was Prince of Ying Yougui, who usurped the throne by regicide and has no record; please follow the Song History precedent on Liu Shao and write him as "the arch-criminal Yougui"; the final ruler should be written according to ancient usage as the Later Liang Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 又，唐末主之前有應順帝，在位四月出奔，亦未編紀，請書為前廢帝，清泰主為後廢帝，其書並為實錄。）〉
entries.en: Before the last Tang ruler there was also Emperor Yingshun, who reigned four months and fled, likewise unrecorded; he should be styled the Former Deposed Emperor and the Qingtai ruler the Latter Deposed Emperor, each to receive a veritable record.)〉
entries.literal: Further, before the final Tang ruler was Emperor Yingshun, who reigned four months and fled — also unrecorded — please write him as the Former Deposed Emperor and the Qingtai ruler as the Latter Deposed Emperor; both works to be veritable records.)〉

entries.zh: 丁未，淮南道招討使李重進奏，破淮賊五千人於壽州北。
entries.en: On dingwei, Li Chongjin, pacification commissioner for Huainan, reported that he had routed five thousand Huai rebels north of Shouzhou.
entries.literal: On the day dingwei, Li Chongjin, Pacification Commissioner of the Huainan Circuit, reported defeating five thousand Huai bandits north of Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 先是，李景遣其弟偽齊王達率全軍來援壽州，達留駐濠州，遣其將許文縝、邊鎬、朱元領兵數萬，溯淮而上，至紫金山，設十餘寨，與城內烽火相應。
entries.en: Earlier Li Jing had sent his brother, the puppet Prince of Qi Da, at the head of the full Southern Tang army to relieve Shouzhou. Da stayed at Haozhou and dispatched Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of men up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, where they pitched more than ten camps linked by beacon fire to the besieged city.
entries.literal: Earlier, Li Jing had sent his younger brother, the unrecognized Prince of Qi, Da, leading the full army to relieve Shouzhou; Da remained at Haozhou and sent his generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of troops up the Huai to Purple Gold Mountain, establishing more than ten camps in beacon contact with the city.

entries.zh: 又築夾道數里，將抵壽春，為運糧之路，至是為重進所敗。
entries.en: They also built a walled supply corridor several li long, nearly reaching Shouchun; Chongjin now defeated this force.
entries.literal: They also built a walled corridor several li long, nearly reaching Shouchun as a grain transport route; at this time they were defeated by Chongjin.

entries.zh: 戊申，詔取來月幸淮南。
entries.en: On wushen, an edict announced that the Emperor would tour Huainan the following month.
entries.literal: On the day wushen, an edict ordered that the following month the Emperor would visit Huainan.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·李蒨傳》：師老無功，時請罷兵為便，世宗令範質、王溥就蒨謀之。
entries.en: (The Song History, Biography of Li Qian: With the campaign dragging on without victory, many urged withdrawal; Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to seek Qian's counsel.
entries.literal: (The Song History, Biography of Li Qian: The army was weary without success; many then urged that ceasing the campaign would be expedient; Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Qian.

entries.zh: 蒨手疏請親征，有必勝之利者三，世宗大悅，用其策。）〉
entries.en: Qian wrote in his own hand urging a personal expedition and set forth three reasons for certain victory; Shizong was delighted and adopted his plan.)〉
entries.literal: Qian personally memorialized requesting a personal campaign, citing three advantages that assured victory; Shizong was greatly pleased and adopted his plan.)〉

entries.zh: 十一月癸未朔，以內客省使昝居潤為宣徽北院使，權東京留守。
entries.en: On the new moon of the eleventh month, Zan Jurun of the Inner Service Bureau was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and acting regent of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On the new moon of the eleventh month, the day guiwei, Zan Jurun, commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau, was made Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and acting Eastern Capital regent.

entries.zh: 丙戌，車駕至濠州城下。
entries.en: On bingxu, the Emperor arrived below the walls of Haozhou.
entries.literal: On the day bingxu, the imperial carriage reached below the walls of Haozhou.

entries.zh: 戊子，親破十八里灘。
entries.en: On wuzi, the Emperor personally overran the Eighteen-li Shoals camp.
entries.literal: On the day wuzi, he personally broke the Eighteen-li Shoals.

entries.zh: 寨在濠州東北淮水之中，四面阻水，上令甲土數百人跨駝以濟。
entries.en: The camp lay in the Huai northeast of Haozhou, surrounded by water on all sides; the Emperor ordered several hundred armored men to cross on camels.
entries.literal: The camp was in the Huai waters northeast of Haozhou, blocked by water on all sides; the Emperor ordered several hundred armored soldiers to cross on camels.

entries.zh: 今上以騎軍浮水而渡，遂破其寨，擄其戰艦而回。
entries.en: The present sovereign led the cavalry across the water, overran the camp, captured the enemy warships, and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Present Lord led the cavalry across floating on the water, broke the camp, captured their warships, and returned.

entries.zh: 癸巳，帝親率諸軍攻濠州，奪關城，破水寨，賊眾大敗，焚戰艦七十餘艘，斬首二千級，進軍攻羊馬城。
entries.en: On guisi, the Emperor led the armies against Haozhou, took the pass city and water camp, and routed the enemy — burning more than seventy warships, taking two thousand heads, and advancing against the Sheep-and-Horse City.
entries.literal: On the day guisi, the Emperor personally led the armies to attack Haozhou, seized the pass city, broke the water camp; the bandit host was greatly defeated, more than seventy warships were burned, two thousand heads were taken, and the army advanced to attack the Sheep-and-Horse City.

entries.zh: 丙申夜，偽濠州團練使郭廷謂上表陳情，且言家在江南，欲遣人稟命於李景，從之。
entries.en: On the night of bingshen, the Southern Tang-appointed Haozhou commissioner Guo Tingyu petitioned, explaining that his family remained in Jiangnan and asking leave to send envoys to Li Jing for instructions; the request was granted.
entries.literal: On the night of bingshen, Guo Tingyu, regimental commissioner of Haozhou by usurper appointment, submitted a memorial stating his case and saying his family was in Jiangnan; he wished to send someone to report to Li Jing for orders — this was granted.

entries.zh: 辛丑，帝自濠州率大軍水陸齊進，循淮而下，命今上率精騎為前鋒。
entries.en: On xinchou, the Emperor led the main force by land and water down the Huai from Haozhou, with the present sovereign commanding the elite cavalry vanguard.
entries.literal: On the day xinchou, the Emperor from Haozhou led the great army forward together by land and water down the Huai, ordering the Present Lord to lead elite cavalry as vanguard.

entries.zh: 癸卯，大破淮賊於渦口，斬首五千級，收降卒二千餘人，奪戰船三百艘，遂鼓行而東，以追奔寇，晝夜不息，沿淮城柵，所至皆下。
entries.en: On guimao, the army routed the Huai rebels at Wokou — five thousand killed, more than two thousand captured, three hundred warships taken — then pressed east in relentless pursuit; every fortified post along the Huai fell in turn.
entries.literal: On the day guimao, the Huai bandits were greatly defeated at Wokou; five thousand heads were taken, more than two thousand surrendered troops were received, three hundred warships were seized; then with drums beating they marched east in pursuit of the fleeing bandits without cease day or night; along the Huai every walled camp they reached fell.

entries.zh: 乙巳，至泗州。
entries.en: On yisi, the army reached Sizhou.
entries.literal: On the day yisi, they reached Sizhou.

entries.zh: 今上乘勢麾軍，焚郭門，奪月城，帝親冒矢石以攻其壘。
entries.en: The present sovereign pressed the attack, burning the outer gate and seizing the outer rampart while the Emperor himself braved arrow and stone fire against the main fortifications.
entries.literal: The Present Lord took advantage of the momentum to command the army, burned the outer gate, seized the moon city; the Emperor personally braved arrows and stones to attack the fortifications.

entries.zh: 丙午，日南至，從臣拜賀於月城之上。
entries.en: On bingwu, the winter solstice, the Emperor's attendants offered congratulations from atop the outer rampart.
entries.literal: On the day bingwu, the winter solstice, attending ministers offered congratulations atop the moon city.

entries.zh: 十二月乙卯，泗州守將範再遇以其城降，授再遇宿州團練使。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Sizhou defender Fan Zaiyu surrendered the city and was made regimental commissioner of Suzhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day yimao, Fan Zaiyu, defender of Sizhou, surrendered his city; Zaiyu was made regimental commissioner of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 戊午，帝自泗州率眾東下，命今上領兵行於南岸，與帝夾淮而進。
entries.en: On wuwu, the Emperor led the army east from Sizhou while the present sovereign commanded troops on the south bank, the two wings advancing on either side of the Huai.
entries.literal: On the day wuwu, the Emperor from Sizhou led the host eastward and ordered the Present Lord to lead troops along the south bank, advancing on both sides of the Huai with the Emperor.

entries.zh: 己未，至清口，追及淮賊，軍行鼓噪之聲聞數十里。
entries.en: On jiwei, they reached Qingkou and overtook the Huai rebels; the army's drums and shouts were heard for dozens of li.
entries.literal: On the day jiwei, they reached Qingkou, overtook the Huai bandits; the sound of marching drums and clamor was heard for several tens of li.

entries.zh: 辛酉，至楚州西北，大破賊眾，水陸俱奔，有賊船數艘，順流而逸，帝率驍騎與今上追之數十里，今上擒賊大將偽保義軍節度使、江北都應援使陳承昭以獻。
entries.en: On xinyou, northwest of Chuzhou, the army routed the enemy on land and water. Several rebel ships fled downriver; the Emperor and the present sovereign pursued for dozens of li, and the present sovereign captured Chen Chengzhao, the Southern Tang-appointed Baoyi commissioner and overall relief commander north of the river, and presented him to the Emperor.
entries.literal: On the day xinyou, they reached the northwest of Chuzhou and greatly defeated the bandit host; land and water forces all fled; several bandit ships escaped downriver; the Emperor led elite cavalry with the Present Lord in pursuit for several tens of li; the Present Lord captured the bandit general Chen Chengzhao, military commissioner of Baoyi Army by usurper appointment and overall relief commander north of the river, and presented him.

entries.zh: 收獲舟船，除焚蕩外得三百餘艘，將士除殺溺外得七千餘人。
entries.en: Apart from those burned, more than three hundred ships were captured; apart from those killed or drowned, more than seven thousand enemy troops were taken.
entries.literal: Warships taken numbered more than three hundred aside from those burned; soldiers taken aside from those killed or drowned numbered more than seven thousand.

entries.zh: 初，帝之渡淮也，比無水戰之備，每遇賊之戰棹，無如之何，敵人亦以此自恃，有輕我之意。
entries.en: When the Emperor first crossed the Huai, the army had no naval force; whenever rebel warships appeared the northerners were helpless, and the enemy took confidence from this.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor crossed the Huai, there had been no preparation for naval warfare; whenever they met the bandits' war boats they were at a loss, and the enemy also relied on this and looked down on them.

entries.zh: 帝即於京師大集工徒，修成艛艦，逾歲得數百艘，兼得江、淮舟船，遂令所獲南軍教北人習水戰出沒之勢，未幾，舟師大備。
entries.en: The Emperor then mobilized craftsmen in the capital to build tower ships; within a year he had several hundred, along with Yangtze and Huai vessels, and had captured southern sailors train northern troops in naval tactics; soon the fleet was fully ready.
entries.literal: The Emperor then at the capital gathered craftsmen on a large scale and built tower ships; in more than a year several hundred were obtained; he also obtained Yangtze and Huai boats, and then had captured southern troops teach northerners the tactics of naval advance and retreat; before long the fleet was fully prepared.

entries.zh: 至是水陸皆捷，故江南大震。
entries.en: Victories on land and water alike now shook Jiangnan to its core.
entries.literal: At this time victories came on land and water alike, and therefore Jiangnan was greatly shaken.

entries.zh: 壬戌，偽命濠州團練使郭廷謂以城歸順。
entries.en: On renxu, the Southern Tang-appointed Haozhou commissioner Guo Tingyu surrendered the city.
entries.literal: On the day renxu, Guo Tingyu, regimental commissioner of Haozhou by usurper appointment, submitted his city in allegiance.

entries.zh: 乙丑，雄武軍使崔萬迪以漣水歸順。
entries.en: On yichou, Cui Wandi of the Xiongwu Army surrendered Lianshui.
entries.literal: On the day yichou, Cui Wandi, commissioner of the Xiongwu Army, submitted Lianshui in allegiance.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以郭廷謂為亳州防禦使，
entries.en: On bingyin, Guo Tingyu was made defender of Bozhou,
entries.literal: On the day bingyin, Guo Tingyu was made defender of Bozhou,

entries.zh: 〈（《隆平集》：廷謂望金陵大慟，再拜，然後以城降。
entries.en: (The Longping Collection records that Tingyu gazed toward Jinling, wept, bowed twice, and only then surrendered the city.
entries.literal: (The Longping Collection: Tingyu looked toward Jinling and wept greatly, bowed twice, and then surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「江南諸將，惟卿斷渦口僑，破定遠寨，足以報李景祿矣。
entries.en: Shizong said, "Among Jiangnan's generals, only you severed the Wokou bridge and broke the Dingyuan camp — enough to repay what Li Jing paid you.
entries.literal: Shizong said: "Among the generals of Jiangnan, only you cut off the Wokou bridge and broke the Dingyuan camp — enough to repay Li Jing's salary.

entries.zh: 濠上使李景自守，亦何能為！」
entries.en: Let Li Jing hold Haozhou himself — what can he accomplish!"
entries.literal: Let Li Jing defend Haozhou himself — what can he do!"

entries.zh: 乃授以亳州防禦使。）〉
entries.en: He was then appointed defender of Bozhou.)〉
entries.literal: He was then appointed defender of Bozhou.)〉

entries.zh: 以偽命濠州兵馬都監陳遷為沂州團練使，以偽命保義軍節度使陳承昭為右監門上將軍。
entries.en: Chen Qian, the Southern Tang-appointed Haozhou army supervisor, was made regimental commissioner of Yizhou; Chen Chengzhao, the Baoyi commissioner, was made senior general of the Right Gate Guards.
entries.literal: Chen Qian, army supervisor of Haozhou by usurper appointment, was made regimental commissioner of Yizhou; Chen Chengzhao, military commissioner of Baoyi Army by usurper appointment, was made senior general of the Right Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 江南李景遣兵驅擄揚州士庶渡江，焚其州郭而去。
entries.en: Li Jing of the Southern Tang sent troops to drive Yangzhou's population across the river, burned the city, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Li Jing of Jiangnan sent troops to drive and carry off the gentry and commoners of Yangzhou across the river, burned the prefectural city, and departed.

entries.zh: 丙子，故同州節度使白延遇贈太尉，故濠州刺史唐景思贈武清軍節度使。
entries.en: On bingzi, the late Tongzhou commissioner Bai Yanyu was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal, and the late Haozhou prefect Tang Jingsi as military commissioner of the Wuqing Army.
entries.literal: On the day bingzi, the late military commissioner of Tongzhou Bai Yanyu was posthumously made Grand Marshal; the late Prefect of Haozhou Tang Jingsi was posthumously made military commissioner of the Wuqing Army.

entries.zh: 丁丑，泰州平。
entries.en: On dingchou, Taizhou was pacified.
entries.literal: On the day dingchou, Taizhou was pacified.

entries.zh: 三月壬午朔，幸泰州。
entries.en: On the renwu new moon in the third month the emperor visited Taizhou.
entries.literal: On the renwu new moon of the third month the emperor visited Taizhou.

entries.zh: 丁亥，復幸廣陵。
entries.en: On dinghai he returned to Guangling.
entries.literal: On dinghai he again visited Guangling.

entries.zh: 辛卯，幸迎鑾江口。
entries.en: On xinmao he visited the mouth of the Yingluan River.
entries.literal: On xinmao he visited the mouth of the Yingluan River.

entries.zh: 遣右武衛大將軍李繼勛率舟師至江島以觀寇。
entries.en: Right Martial Guard grand general Li Jixun was sent to lead the fleet to the river isles and reconnoiter the enemy.
entries.literal: Right Martial Guard grand general Li Jixun was dispatched to lead the fleet to the river isles to observe the enemy.

entries.zh: 癸巳，帝臨江望見賊船數十艘，命今上帥戰棹以追之，賊軍退去，今上直抵南岸，焚其營柵而回。
entries.en: On guisi the emperor looked across the river and saw several dozen enemy ships. He ordered Zhao Kuangyin to lead battle vessels in pursuit. The enemy withdrew, and Zhao Kuangyin pressed straight to the south bank, burned their camps and palisades, and returned.
entries.literal: On guisi the emperor looked across the river and saw several tens of rebel ships; he ordered the present sovereign to lead battle vessels in pursuit; the rebel army withdrew; the present sovereign went straight to the south bank, burned their camps and palisades, and returned.

entries.zh: 甲午，以右武衛大將軍李繼勛為左領軍上將軍。
entries.en: On jiawu Right Martial Guard grand general Li Jixun was promoted to Left Leading Army upper general.
entries.literal: On jiawu Right Martial Guard grand general Li Jixun was made Left Leading Army upper general.

entries.zh: 乙未，殿前都虞候慕容延釗奏，大破賊軍於東㳍州。
entries.en: On yiwei Palace Front chief inspector Murong Yanzhao reported a great victory over the enemy at East Dongjia Prefecture.
entries.literal: On yiwei Palace Front chief inspector Murong Yanzhao reported a great defeat of the rebel army at East Dongjia Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙申，江南李景遣其臣兵部侍郎陳覺奉表陳情，兼貢羅縠紬絹三千匹，乳茶三千斤，及香藥犀象等。
entries.en: On bingshen Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his minister, Vice Minister of War Chen Jue, to present a memorial stating his case, together with tribute of three thousand bolts of gauze and silk, three thousand jin of milk tea, and aromatics, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and the like.
entries.literal: On bingshen Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his minister, Vice Minister of War Chen Jue, to present a memorial stating his case, together with tribute of three thousand bolts of gauze, silk, and thin silk, three thousand jin of milk tea, and aromatics, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and the like.

entries.zh: 覺至行在，睹樓船戰棹已泊於江岸，以為自天而降，愕然大駭。
entries.en: When Jue reached the field headquarters and saw tower ships and battle vessels already moored on the riverbank, he thought they had descended from heaven and was utterly stunned.
entries.literal: When Jue reached the mobile court and saw tower ships and battle vessels already moored on the riverbank, he thought they had descended from heaven and was greatly shocked in astonishment.

entries.zh: 丁酉，荊南高保融奏，本道舟師已至鄂州。
entries.en: On dingyou Gao Baorong of Jingnan reported that his circuit's fleet had reached E Prefecture.
entries.literal: On dingyou Gao Baorong of Jingnan reported that this circuit's fleet had reached E Prefecture.

entries.zh: 戊戌，兩浙錢俶奏，差發戰棹四百艘，水軍萬七千人，已泊江岸，請師期。
entries.en: On wuxu Qian Chu of the Two Zhes reported that he had dispatched four hundred battle vessels and seventeen thousand naval troops, already moored on the riverbank, and asked for a date to join the campaign.
entries.literal: On wuxu Qian Chu of the Two Zhes reported dispatching four hundred battle vessels and seventeen thousand naval troops, already moored on the riverbank, and requesting a date for the campaign.

entries.zh: 己亥，今上率水軍破賊船百餘只於瓜步。
entries.en: On jihai Zhao Kuangyin led the navy and destroyed more than a hundred enemy ships at Guabu.
entries.literal: On jihai the present sovereign led the navy and destroyed more than a hundred rebel ships at Guabu.

entries.zh: 是日，李景遣其臣劉承遇奉表以廬、舒、蘄、黃等四州來獻，且請以江為界，帝報曰：「皇帝恭問江南國主。
entries.en: That same day Li Jing sent his minister Liu Chengyu to offer the four prefectures of Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang and to request that the Yangtze serve as the boundary. The emperor replied: "The emperor respectfully inquires after the ruler of Jiangnan.
entries.literal: That same day Li Jing sent his minister Liu Chengyu to present a memorial offering Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang and the other four prefectures, and also requesting that the Yangtze serve as the boundary. The emperor replied: "The emperor respectfully inquires after the ruler of Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 使人至，省奏請分割舒、廬、蘄、黃等州，畫江為界者。
entries.en: Your envoy has arrived, and I have read your memorial requesting the cession of Shu, Lu, Qi, Huang, and other prefectures and the drawing of the Yangtze as the boundary.
entries.literal: Your envoy has arrived; I have read your memorial requesting the partition of Shu, Lu, Qi, Huang, and other prefectures and the drawing of the Yangtze as the boundary.

entries.zh: 頃逢多事，莫通玉帛之歡，適自近年，遂構干戈之役，兩地之交兵未息，蒸民之受弊斯多。
entries.en: For some time troubles have prevented the exchange of diplomatic courtesies; only in recent years did war break out. Hostilities between our two lands have not ceased, and the common people have suffered greatly.
entries.literal: For some time we have met with many troubles and could not exchange the courtesies of silk and jade; only in recent years did we raise the campaign of arms; hostilities between our two lands have not ceased, and the common people have suffered greatly thereby.

entries.zh: 一昨再辱使人，重尋前意，將敦久要，須盡縷陳。
entries.en: Only yesterday you again sent an envoy and renewed your earlier intent. Wishing to strengthen our long-standing bond, I must set forth the matter in full.
entries.literal: Just yesterday you again honored us with an envoy and renewed your earlier intent; wishing to strengthen our long-standing bond, I must set forth the matter in full detail.

entries.zh: 今者承遇爰來，封函復至，請割州郡，仍定封疆，猥形信誓之辭，備認始終之意，既能如是，又復何求。
entries.en: Now Chengyu has come and sealed letters have again arrived, requesting the cession of prefectures and the fixing of the frontier. You have set forth solemn pledges and fully acknowledged your intent from beginning to end. Since you offer this, what more could be asked?
entries.literal: Now Chengyu has come, and sealed letters have again arrived, requesting the cession of prefectures and commanderies and the fixing of the frontier; you have humbly set forth words of sworn faith and fully acknowledged your intent from beginning to end—since you can do thus, what more could be sought?

entries.zh: 邊陲頓靜於煙塵，師旅便還於京闕，永言欣慰，深切誠懷。
entries.en: The frontier will soon be quiet of war's dust and the armies will return to the capital. My satisfaction and sincere goodwill are profound.
entries.literal: The frontier is suddenly quiet of war's dust; the armies will soon return to the capital; I speak forever of gratification and deep sincere feeling.

entries.zh: 其常、潤一路及沿江兵棹，今已指揮抽退；
entries.en: The Chang and Run route and the military vessels along the river have now been ordered to withdraw;
entries.literal: The Chang and Run route and the military vessels along the river have now been ordered withdrawn;

entries.zh: 兼兩浙、荊南、湖南水陸兵士，各令罷兵；
entries.en: and the land and naval forces of the Two Zhes, Jingnan, and Hunan have each been ordered to stand down;
entries.literal: together with the land and naval forces of the Two Zhes, Jingnan, and Hunan, each has been ordered to cease hostilities;

entries.zh: 其廬、黃、蘄三路將士，亦遣抽拔近內，候彼中起揭逐處將員及軍都家口丁畢，只請差人勾喚在彼將校，交割州城」云。
entries.en: the troops on the Lu, Huang, and Qi routes will also be withdrawn inland. When on your side the officers and army households at each place have all been mustered out, you need only send men to summon the officers there and hand over the prefectural cities."
entries.literal: the troops of the Lu, Huang, and Qi three routes will also be withdrawn nearer inward; when on your side the officers and army households at each place have all been mustered out, you need only send men to summon the officers and commanders there and hand over the prefectural cities."

entries.zh: 淮南平，凡得州十四、縣六十、戶二十二萬六千五百七十四。
entries.en: When Huainan was pacified, the court gained fourteen prefectures, sixty counties, and 226,574 households in all.
entries.literal: When Huainan was pacified, in all there were gained fourteen prefectures, sixty counties, and 226,574 households.

entries.zh: 先是，李景以江南危蹙，謀欲傳位於世子，使附庸於我，故遣陳覺上表陳敘。
entries.en: Earlier, seeing Jiangnan in peril, Li Jing had planned to abdicate in favor of his heir and become a vassal of the Zhou court, and therefore sent Chen Jue to present a memorial stating his case.
entries.literal: Earlier, because Li Jing saw Jiangnan in peril and crisis, he planned to transmit the throne to his heir and make himself a vassal to us; therefore he sent Chen Jue to present a memorial stating his case.

entries.zh: 至是帝以既許其通好，乃降書以答之，曰：「別睹來章，備形縟旨，敘此日傳讓之意，述向來高尚之懷。
entries.en: At this point, since the emperor had already agreed to friendly relations, he issued a letter in reply: "I have read your incoming document, which fully sets forth your intent to abdicate on this day and describes your long-held lofty sentiments.
entries.literal: At this point, since the emperor had already agreed to friendly relations, he issued a letter in reply, saying: "I have separately seen your incoming document, fully setting forth your elaborate intent, narrating your wish to transmit the throne on this day and describing your long-held lofty sentiments.

entries.zh: 仍以數歲已還。
entries.en: You also speak of the years already past.
entries.literal: You also speak of the years already past.

entries.zh: 交兵不息，備論追悔之事，無非克責之辭，雖古人有引咎責躬，因災致懼，亦無以過此也。
entries.en: You note that hostilities have not ceased and fully discuss your repentance in language of self-reproach. Though the ancients took blame upon themselves and, encountering calamity, were moved to fear, none could surpass this.
entries.literal: Hostilities have not ceased; you fully discuss matters of repentance; there is nothing that is not language of self-reproach; though the ancients took blame upon themselves and, encountering calamity, were moved to fear, none could surpass this.

entries.zh: 況君血氣方剛，春秋甚富，為一方之英主，得百姓之歡心。
entries.en: Moreover, you are still in the prime of life, an outstanding ruler of your region who has won the hearts of the people.
entries.literal: Moreover, my lord's vital force is still vigorous and your years are still abundant; you are an outstanding ruler of one region and have won the hearts of the people.

entries.zh: 即今南北才通，疆埸甫定，是玉帛交馳之始，乃干戈載戢之初，豈可高謝君臨，輕辭世務，與其慕希夷之道，曷若行康濟之心。
entries.en: North and south have only just reopened relations and the frontier has only just been settled. This is the beginning of diplomatic exchange and the sheathing of arms. How can you loftily decline rule and lightly abandon worldly affairs? Rather than admiring silent withdrawal, how much better to act on a heart intent on bringing relief and order.
entries.literal: Just now north and south have only just opened communication and the frontier has only just been settled—this is the beginning of the exchange of silk and jade and the beginning of the sheathing of arms; how can you loftily decline sovereign rule and lightly abandon worldly affairs? Rather than admiring the way of silent nonaction, how much better to act on a heart intent on bringing relief and order.

entries.zh: 重念天災流行，分野常事，前代賢哲所不能逃。
entries.en: Remember too that natural calamities spread widely—a constant matter in every realm—and even sage worthies of former ages could not escape them.
entries.literal: I think again that natural calamities spread widely—a constant matter of territorial divisions—and even sage worthies of former ages could not escape them.

entries.zh: 茍盛德之日新，則景福之彌遠，勉修政理，勿倦經綸，保高義於初終，垂遠圖於家國，流芳貽慶，不亦美乎！」
entries.en: If your great virtue daily renews itself, your blessings will extend ever farther. Strive to govern well and do not weary of statecraft. Preserve lofty integrity from beginning to end and hand down far-reaching plans to your state and house. To leave a fragrant name and bequeath blessings—is this not beautiful!"
entries.literal: If your great virtue daily renews itself, then your bright blessings will extend ever farther; strive to govern well, do not weary of statecraft, preserve lofty integrity from beginning to end, and hand down far-reaching plans to state and family—leaving a fragrant name and bequeathing blessings: is this not beautiful!"

entries.zh: 庚子，詔曰：「比者以近年貢舉，頗事因循，頻詔有司精加試練，所冀去留無濫，優劣昭然。
entries.en: On gengzi an edict stated: "Recently the civil examinations have been handled in a perfunctory way. Edicts have repeatedly ordered the responsible offices to test candidates with care, so that retention and rejection would not be indiscriminate and excellence and inferiority would be clearly evident.
entries.literal: On gengzi an edict stated: "Recently, in the civil examinations of recent years, matters have been quite perfunctory; edicts have repeatedly ordered the responsible offices to test and examine with care, hoping that retention and rejection would not be indiscriminate and that excellence and inferiority would be clearly evident.

entries.zh: 昨據貢院奏，今年新及第進士等，所試文字或有否臧，爰命辭臣再令考覆，庶涇、渭之不雜，免玉石之相參。
entries.en: Yesterday, according to a memorial from the examination bureau, among this year's newly passed jinshi the examination writings showed faults and flaws. I therefore ordered literary officials to re-examine them, so that the pure would not be mixed with the impure and jade would not be confused with common stone.
entries.literal: Yesterday, according to a memorial from the examination bureau, among this year's newly passed jinshi and others, the writings submitted for examination had some faults and flaws; I therefore ordered literary officials to examine them again, hoping that Jing and Wei would not be mixed and that jade and stone would not be confused together.

entries.zh: 其劉坦、戰貽慶、李頌、徐緯、張覲等詩賦稍優，宜放及第；
entries.en: Liu Tan, Zhan Yiqing, Li Song, Xu Wei, Zhang Jing, and others wrote poetry and fu of somewhat superior quality and should be allowed to pass;
entries.literal: Liu Tan, Zhan Yiqing, Li Song, Xu Wei, Zhang Jing, and others had poetry and fu somewhat superior and should be allowed to pass;

entries.zh: 王汾據其文辭，亦未精當，念以頃曾剝落，特與成名；
entries.en: Wang Fen's compositions were also not quite refined, but considering that he had recently been stripped of his degree, he is specially granted completion of the degree;
entries.literal: Wang Fen, judging by his literary compositions, was also not quite refined and apt, but considering that he had recently been stripped of his degree, he is specially granted completion of the degree;

entries.zh: 熊若谷、陳保衡皆是遠人，深可嗟念，亦放及第；
entries.en: Xiong Ruogu and Chen Baoheng are both men from distant regions and deeply worthy of sympathy; they are also allowed to pass;
entries.literal: Xiong Ruogu and Chen Baoheng are both men from distant regions, deeply worthy of sympathy, and are also allowed to pass;

entries.zh: 郭峻、趙保雍、楊丹、安元度、張昉、董咸則、杜思道等未甚苦辛，並從退黜，更宜修進，以俟將來。
entries.en: Guo Jun, Zhao Baoyong, Yang Dan, An Yuandu, Zhang Fang, Dong Xianze, Du Sidao, and others did not show sufficient diligence. All are dismissed from passing and should further cultivate themselves to await a future examination.
entries.literal: Guo Jun, Zhao Baoyong, Yang Dan, An Yuandu, Zhang Fang, Dong Xianze, Du Sidao, and others did not show great diligence; all are dismissed from passing and should further cultivate themselves to await the future.

entries.zh: 知貢舉、右諫議大夫劉濤選士不當，有失用心，責授右贊善大夫，俾令省過，以戒當官。」
entries.en: Examination supervisor, Right Remonstrance Counselor Liu Tao, selected scholars improperly and failed in conscientious effort. He is demoted to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent so that he may reflect on his faults as a warning to those in office."
entries.literal: Examination supervisor, Right Remonstrance Counselor Liu Tao, selected scholars improperly and failed in conscientious effort; he is demoted and appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, so that he may reflect on his faults as a warning to those in office."

entries.zh: 先是，濤於東京放榜後，引新及第進士劉坦已下一十五人赴行在，帝命翰林學士李昉覆試，故有是命。
entries.en: Earlier, after Tao posted the results in the Eastern Capital he led the fifteen newly passed jinshi from Liu Tan downward to the field headquarters. The emperor ordered Hanlin academician Li Fang to re-examine them, and therefore issued this order.
entries.literal: Earlier, after Tao posted the results in the Eastern Capital he led the fifteen newly passed jinshi from Liu Tan downward to the mobile court; the emperor ordered Hanlin academician Li Fang to re-examine them, and therefore there was this order.

entries.zh: 壬寅，復幸揚州，改廬州軍額為保信軍。
entries.en: On renyin he again visited Yangzhou and changed Luzhou's army designation to Baoxin Army.
entries.literal: On renyin he again visited Yangzhou and changed Luzhou's army designation to Baoxin Army.

entries.zh: 甲辰，以右龍武統軍趙贊為廬州節度使，以殿前都虞候慕容延釗為淮南節度使兼殿前副指揮使。
entries.en: On jiachen Right Dragon Martial commander-in-chief Zhao Zan was appointed Luzhou military governor, and Palace Front chief inspector Murong Yanzhao was appointed Huainan military governor and concurrent Palace Front deputy commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: On jiachen Right Dragon Martial commander-in-chief Zhao Zan was made Luzhou military governor, and Palace Front chief inspector Murong Yanzhao was made Huainan military governor and concurrent Palace Front deputy commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 遣鹽城監使申屠諤賫書及御馬一十匹、金銀銜全、散馬四十匹、羊千口，賜江南李景。
entries.en: Yancheng supervisor Shentu E was sent with a letter and ten imperial horses with complete gold and silver bridles, forty unbridled horses, and a thousand sheep as gifts for Li Jing of Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Yancheng supervisor Shentu E was dispatched bearing a letter and ten imperial horses with complete gold and silver bridles, forty unbridled horses, and a thousand sheep, to be bestowed on Li Jing of Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 諤先為王師所俘，故遣之。
entries.en: E had earlier been captured by the imperial army and was therefore sent back.
entries.literal: E had earlier been captured by the imperial army; therefore he was sent.

entries.zh: 丙午，江南李景遣所署宰相馮延巳獻犒軍銀十萬兩、絹十萬匹、錢十萬貫、茶五十萬斤、米麥二十萬石。
entries.en: On bingwu Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his appointed chief minister Feng Yanji to present rewards for the army: one hundred thousand taels of silver, one hundred thousand bolts of silk, one hundred thousand strings of cash, five hundred thousand jin of tea, and two hundred thousand shi of rice and wheat.
entries.literal: On bingwu Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his appointed chief minister Feng Yanji to present army-reward silver of one hundred thousand taels, one hundred thousand bolts of silk, one hundred thousand strings of cash, five hundred thousand jin of tea, and two hundred thousand shi of rice and wheat.

entries.zh: 庚戌，詔：「故淮南節度使楊行密、故升府節度使徐溫各給守冢戶，應江南臣僚有先代墳墓在江北者，委所在長吏差人檢校。」
entries.en: On gengxu an edict ordered: "The former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi and the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen shall each be granted tomb-guarding households, and where Jiangnan officials had ancestral tombs north of the river the local chief officials should dispatch men to inspect and maintain them."
entries.literal: On gengxu an edict stated: "The former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi and the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen shall each be granted tomb-guarding households; as for Jiangnan officials and staff who have ancestral tombs north of the river, the local chief officials where they lie are charged to dispatch men to inspect and maintain them."

entries.zh: 辛亥，李景遣所署臨汝郡公徐遼進買宴錢二百萬並遣伶官五十人與遼俱來獻壽觴。
entries.en: On xinhai Li Jing sent his appointed Duke of Linru, Xu Liao, to present two million in funds for a banquet and also sent fifty entertainers with Liao to offer birthday toasts.
entries.literal: On xinhai Li Jing sent his appointed Duke of Linru, Xu Liao, to present two million in banquet-purchase funds and also sent fifty entertainers together with Liao to come and offer birthday toasts.

entries.zh: 夏四月癸丑，宴從臣及江南進奉使馮延巳等於行宮，徐遼代李景捧壽觴以獻，進金酒器、禦衣、犀帶、金銀、錦綺、鞍馬等。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on guichou, the emperor feasted his attending officials and the Jiangnan tribute envoys Feng Yanji and others at the field palace. Xu Liao, on Li Jing's behalf, raised and presented a birthday toast, along with gold wine vessels, imperial robes, rhinoceros-horn belts, gold and silver, brocade and silk, saddles and horses, and the like.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on guichou, attending officials and the Jiangnan tribute envoys Feng Yanji and others were feasted at the mobile palace; Xu Liao, on Li Jing's behalf, raised the birthday toast and presented it; he also presented gold wine vessels, imperial robes, rhinoceros-horn belts, gold and silver, brocade and silk, saddles and horses, and the like.

entries.zh: 乙卯，車駕發揚州還京。
entries.en: On yimao the emperor departed Yangzhou and returned to the capital.
entries.literal: On yimao the imperial carriage departed Yangzhou and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 丙辰，太常博士、權知宿州軍州事趙礪除名，坐推劾弛慢也。
entries.en: On bingchen Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Li, acting administrator of Su Prefecture's military and civil affairs, was stripped of his name and office for laxity in investigation and prosecution.
entries.literal: On bingchen Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhao Li, acting administrator of Suzhou's military and civil affairs, was stripped of his name and office, the offense being laxity in investigation and prosecution.

entries.zh: 先是，翰林醫官馬道元進狀，訴壽州界被賊殺卻男，獲正賊，見在宿州，本州不為勘斷。
entries.en: Earlier, Hanlin medical officer Ma Daoyuan submitted a petition complaining that within Shou Prefecture's borders his son had been killed by bandits. The actual culprit had been captured and was held in Suzhou, but the prefecture would not investigate and adjudicate the case.
entries.literal: Earlier, Hanlin medical officer Ma Daoyuan submitted a petition complaining that within Shou Prefecture's borders his son had been killed by bandits; the actual culprit had been captured and was presently in Suzhou, but the prefecture would not investigate and adjudicate.

entries.zh: 帝大怒，遣端明殿學士竇儀乘驛往按之，及獄成，坐族死者二十四人。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly angered and dispatched Duanming Hall academician Dou Yi by post relay to investigate. When the case was completed, twenty-four persons were sentenced to clan-extinction death.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and dispatched Duanming Hall academician Dou Yi, traveling by post relay, to investigate; when the case was completed, twenty-four persons were sentenced to clan-extinction death.

entries.zh: 儀奉辭之日，帝旨甚峻，故儀之用刑傷於深刻。
entries.en: On the day Yi received his orders the emperor's intent was very stern, and therefore his application of punishment was excessively harsh.
entries.literal: On the day Yi received his orders the emperor's intent was very stern; therefore Yi's application of punishment was excessively harsh.

entries.zh: 戊午，以前延州留後李彥頵為滄州留後。
entries.en: On wuwu former Yanzhou acting military governor Li Yanjun was appointed Cangzhou acting military governor.
entries.literal: On wuwu former Yanzhou acting military governor Li Yanjun was made Cangzhou acting military governor.

entries.zh: 庚申，新太廟成，遷五廟神主入於其室。
entries.en: On gengshen the new Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed and the spirit tablets of the five temples were moved into its chambers.
entries.literal: On gengshen the new Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed; the spirit tablets of the five temples were moved into its chambers.

entries.zh: 壬申，至自淮南。
entries.en: On renshen he returned from Huainan.
entries.literal: On renshen he arrived from Huainan.

entries.zh: 癸酉，命宣徽北院使昝居潤判開封府事。
entries.en: On guiyou Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Zan Jurun was ordered to administer Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
entries.literal: On guiyou Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Zan Jurun was ordered to administer Kaifeng prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 甲戌，澶州節度使張永德準詔赴北邊，以契丹犯境故也。
entries.en: On jiaxu Chan Prefecture military governor Zhang Yongde, pursuant to edict, went to the northern frontier because the Khitan had violated the border.
entries.literal: On jiaxu Chan Prefecture military governor Zhang Yongde, pursuant to edict, went to the northern frontier because the Khitan had violated the border.

entries.zh: 丁丑，兩浙奏，四月十九日杭州火，廬舍府署延燒殆盡。
entries.en: On dingchou the Two Zhes reported that on the nineteenth day of the fourth month Hangzhou caught fire and dwellings and government offices were burned almost completely.
entries.literal: On dingchou the Two Zhes reported that on the nineteenth day of the fourth month Hangzhou caught fire and dwellings and government offices were burned almost completely.

entries.zh: 五月辛巳朔，上御崇元殿受朝，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the xinsi new moon in the fifth month the emperor held court in Chongyuan Hall and received homage with full ceremonial guard.
entries.literal: On the xinsi new moon of the fifth month the emperor held court in Chongyuan Hall and received homage; guard and escort followed the prescribed form.

entries.zh: 詔：「侍衛諸軍及諸道將士，各賜等第優給。
entries.en: An edict ordered: "The Palace Guard armies and military officers of all circuits shall each receive graded preferential rewards.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The Palace Guard armies and military officers of all circuits shall each be granted graded preferential rewards.

entries.zh: 應行營將士歿於王事者，各與贈官；
entries.en: Campaign officers and soldiers who died in the service of the state shall each receive posthumous office;
entries.literal: Campaign officers and soldiers who died in the service of the state shall each be granted posthumous office;

entries.zh: 親的子孫，並量才錄用；
entries.en: sons and grandsons of the deceased shall all be appointed according to their talents;
entries.literal: sons and grandsons of the deceased shall all be appointed according to their talents;

entries.zh: 傷夷殘廢者，別賜救接。
entries.en: those wounded, maimed, or disabled shall separately receive relief and support.
entries.literal: those wounded, maimed, or disabled shall separately be granted relief and support.

entries.zh: 淮南諸州及徐、宿、宋、亳、陳、潁、許、蔡等州，所欠去年秋夏稅物，並與除放」云。
entries.en: For the various prefectures of Huainan and the prefectures of Xu, Su, Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Xu, and Cai, last year's autumn and summer tax arrears shall all be remitted."
entries.literal: For the various prefectures of Huainan and the prefectures of Xu, Su, Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Xu, and Cai, the autumn and summer tax goods owed from last year shall all be remitted."

entries.zh: 丙戌，命端明殿學士竇儀判河南府兼知西京留守事。
entries.en: On bingxu Duanming Hall academician Dou Yi was ordered to administer Henan Prefecture and concurrently manage the Western Capital garrison affairs.
entries.literal: On bingxu Duanming Hall academician Dou Yi was ordered to administer Henan Prefecture and concurrently manage the Western Capital's garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以襄州節度使安審琦為青州節度使；
entries.en: On xinmao Xiang Prefecture military governor An Shenqi was appointed Qing Prefecture military governor;
entries.literal: On xinmao Xiang Prefecture military governor An Shenqi was made Qing Prefecture military governor;

entries.zh: 以許州節度使韓通為宋州節度使，依前兼侍衛馬步都虞候；
entries.en: Xu Prefecture military governor Han Tong was appointed Song Prefecture military governor, continuing as Palace Guard cavalry-and-infantry chief inspector;
entries.literal: Xu Prefecture military governor Han Tong was made Song Prefecture military governor, continuing as before as concurrent Palace Guard cavalry-and-infantry chief inspector;

entries.zh: 以宋州節度使向訓為襄州節度使；
entries.en: Song Prefecture military governor Xiang Xun was appointed Xiang Prefecture military governor;
entries.literal: Song Prefecture military governor Xiang Xun was made Xiang Prefecture military governor;

entries.zh: 以今上為忠武軍節度使，依前殿前都指揮使。
entries.en: Zhao Kuangyin was appointed Zhongwu Army military governor while continuing as Palace Front commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: The present sovereign was made Zhongwu Army military governor, continuing as before as Palace Front commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 淮南之役，今上之功居最，及是命之降，雖雲酬勛，止於移鎮而已，賞典太輕，物議不以為允。
entries.en: In the Huainan campaign Zhao Kuangyin's merit ranked highest. When this appointment was issued, though it was said to reward merit, it amounted only to a transfer of command— the reward was too light, and public opinion did not consider it adequate.
entries.literal: In the Huainan campaign the present sovereign's merit ranked highest; when this appointment was issued, though it was said to reward merit, it amounted only to a transfer of commandery— the scale of reward was too light, and public opinion did not consider it adequate.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以左武衛上將軍武行德為鄜州節度使，以右神武統軍宋延渥為滑州節度使，
entries.en: On guisi Left Martial Guard upper general Wu Xingde was appointed Fu Prefecture military governor, and Right Divine Martial commander-in-chief Song Yanwo was appointed Hua Prefecture military governor,
entries.literal: On guisi Left Martial Guard upper general Wu Xingde was made Fu Prefecture military governor, and Right Divine Martial commander-in-chief Song Yanwo was made Hua Prefecture military governor,

entries.zh: 〈（《小畜集·宋延渥神道碑》云：五月，授義成軍節度使，其制略曰：「長驅下瀨之師，若涉無人之境。
entries.en: (The 《Collected Writings of the Small Herdsman》, Spirit Way stele of Song Yanwo, records that in the fifth month he was appointed Yicheng Army military governor. The appointment text in brief reads: "The army that drove straight down the rapids passed as if through an empty land.
entries.literal: (The 《Collected Writings of the Small Herdsman》, Spirit Way stele of Song Yanwo, states: In the fifth month he was appointed Yicheng Army military governor; the appointment text in brief reads: "The army that drove straight down the rapids was as if passing through a land without men.

entries.zh: 除兇戡難，爾既立夫殊庸，礪嶽盟河，予豈忘於豐報。
entries.en: In eliminating the wicked and quelling calamity you have already established extraordinary merit. Grinding mountains and swearing by rivers—how could I forget a rich reward?
entries.literal: In eliminating the wicked and quelling calamity you have already established extraordinary merit; grinding mountains and swearing by rivers—how could I forget a rich reward.

entries.zh: 南燕舊邦，北闕伊邇。
entries.en: The old domain of Southern Yan lies near the northern capital.
entries.literal: The old domain of Southern Yan, the northern capital is near at hand.

entries.zh: 河壖作翰，遙臨白馬之津；
entries.en: On the riverbank you serve as a frontier pillar, gazing from afar upon the ford of White Horse;
entries.literal: On the river's bank you serve as a frontier pillar, gazing from afar upon the ford of White Horse;

entries.zh: 穰下統戎，即鎮臥龍之地。」）〉
entries.en: At Rangxia you command the army, guarding the land of the Reclining Dragon." )〉
entries.literal: At Rangxia you command the army, guarding at once the land of the Reclining Dragon." )〉

entries.zh: 以前同州留後王暉為相州留後。
entries.en: Former Tong Prefecture acting military governor Wang Hui was appointed Xiang Prefecture acting military governor.
entries.literal: Former Tong Prefecture acting military governor Wang Hui was made Xiang Prefecture acting military governor.

entries.zh: 乙未，立東京羅城諸門名額，東二門曰寅賓、延春，南三門曰朱明、景風、畏景，西二門曰迎秋、肅政，北三門曰元德、長景、愛景。
entries.en: On yiwei the name plaques of the Eastern Capital's outer wall gates were established: the two eastern gates Yinbin and Yanchun; the three southern gates Zhuming, Jingfeng, and Weijing; the two western gates Yingqiu and Suzheng; and the three northern gates Yuande, Changjing, and Aijing.
entries.literal: On yiwei the name plaques of the gates of the Eastern Capital's outer wall were established: the two eastern gates were called Yinbin and Yanchun; the three southern gates were called Zhuming, Jingfeng, and Weijing; the two western gates were called Yingqiu and Suzheng; the three northern gates were called Yuande, Changjing, and Aijing.

entries.zh: 辛丑，幸懷信驛。
entries.en: On xinchou the emperor visited Huaixin Post Station.
entries.literal: On xinchou the emperor visited Huaixin Post Station.

entries.zh: 乙巳，詔在朝文資官各再舉堪為幕職令錄一人。
entries.en: On yisi an edict ordered that each civil official at court again nominate one person qualified to serve as a staff officer, prefectural aide, or county recorder.
entries.literal: On yisi an edict ordered that each civil official at court again nominate one person qualified to serve as a staff officer, prefectural aide, or county recorder.

entries.zh: 戊申，以襄州節度使向訓兼西南面水陸發運招討使。
entries.en: On wushen Xiang Prefecture military governor Xiang Xun was additionally appointed Southwest land-and-water transport and pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: On wushen Xiang Prefecture military governor Xiang Xun was additionally made Southwest land-and-water transport and pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 己酉，以太府卿馮延魯充江南國信使，以衛尉少卿鐘謨為副。
entries.en: On jiyou Grand Steward Feng Yanlu was appointed Jiangnan state-trust envoy, with Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhong Mo as deputy.
entries.literal: On jiyou Grand Steward Feng Yanlu was appointed Jiangnan state-trust envoy, with Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhong Mo as deputy.

entries.zh: 賜李景禦衣、玉帶、錦綺羅縠帛共十萬匹、金器千兩、銀器萬兩、御馬五匹、金玉鞍轡全、散馬百匹、羊三百口。
entries.en: Li Jing was granted imperial robes, jade belts, and one hundred thousand bolts of brocade, silk, gauze, and thin silk, one thousand taels of gold vessels, ten thousand taels of silver vessels, five imperial horses with complete gold and jade saddles and bridles, one hundred unbridled horses, and three hundred sheep.
entries.literal: Li Jing was granted imperial robes, jade belts, brocade, silk, gauze, and thin silk totaling one hundred thousand bolts, one thousand taels of gold vessels, ten thousand taels of silver vessels, five imperial horses with complete gold and jade saddles and bridles, one hundred unbridled horses, and three hundred sheep.

entries.zh: 賜江南世子李宏冀器幣鞍馬等。
entries.en: Jiangnan heir Li Hongji was granted vessels, silks, saddles, horses, and the like.
entries.literal: Jiangnan heir Li Hongji was granted vessels, silks, saddles, horses, and the like.

entries.zh: 別賜李景書曰：「皇帝恭問江南國主。
entries.en: A separate letter was bestowed on Li Jing: "The emperor respectfully inquires after the ruler of Jiangnan.
entries.literal: A separate letter was bestowed on Li Jing, saying: "The emperor respectfully inquires after the ruler of Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 煮海之利，在彼海濱，屬疆壤之初分，慮供食之有闕。
entries.en: The profit of boiling seawater for salt lies on your seacoast. Since the frontier was first divided, I feared there might be a shortfall in provisions.
entries.literal: The profit of boiling sea water for salt lies on your seacoast; since the frontier was first divided, I feared there might be a shortfall in provisions.

entries.zh: 江左諸郡素號繁饒，然於川澤之間，舊無斥鹵之地，曾承素旨，常在所懷，願均收積之餘，以助軍旅之用。
entries.en: The commanderies of the Jiang left have long been called prosperous, yet among rivers and marshes there was formerly no saline land. I have always kept your longstanding intent in mind and wish to share the surplus of accumulated stores to aid the army.
entries.literal: The various commanderies of the Jiang left have long been called prosperous and abundant, yet among rivers and marshes there was formerly no saline land; I once received your longstanding intent and have always kept it in mind, wishing to share the surplus of accumulated stores to aid military use.

entries.zh: 已下三司，逐年支撥供軍食鹽三十萬石。」
entries.en: Orders have been issued to the Three Departments to allocate three hundred thousand shi of army-supply salt each year."
entries.literal: Orders have been issued to the Three Departments to allocate three hundred thousand shi of army-supply salt each year."

entries.zh: 又賜李景今年曆日一軸。
entries.en: Li Jing was also granted one scroll of this year's calendar.
entries.literal: Li Jing was also granted one scroll of this year's calendar.

entries.zh: 八月庚辰，延州奏，溠溪水漲，壞州城，溺死者百餘人。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Yan Prefecture reported that the Zha Stream had risen in flood and destroyed the prefectural wall; more than a hundred persons drowned.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Yan Prefecture reported that the Zha Stream had risen in flood, destroying the prefectural wall; more than a hundred persons drowned.

entries.zh: 己丑，太子太師致仕宋彥筠卒。
entries.en: On jichou retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Song Yanjun died.
entries.literal: On jichou retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Song Yanjun died.

entries.zh: 辛丑，江南李景上表乞降，詔書不允。
entries.en: On xinchou Li Jing of Jiangnan submitted a memorial begging to surrender; an edict letter did not grant it.
entries.literal: On xinchou Li Jing of Jiangnan submitted a memorial begging to surrender; an edict letter did not grant it.

entries.zh: 九月丁巳，以太府卿馮延魯為刑部侍郎，以衛尉少卿鐘謨為給事中，並放歸江南。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Grand Steward Feng Yanlu was appointed Vice Minister of Justice, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhong Mo was appointed Supervising Secretary, and both were released to return to Jiangnan.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Grand Steward Feng Yanlu was made Vice Minister of Justice, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhong Mo was made Supervising Secretary, and both were released to return to Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 時延魯、鐘謨自江南復命，李景復奏欲傳位於其世子宏冀，帝亦以書答之。
entries.en: At the time Yanlu and Zhong Mo returned from reporting in Jiangnan. Li Jing again memorialized wishing to abdicate in favor of his heir Hongji, and the emperor also replied with a letter.
entries.literal: At the time Yanlu and Zhong Mo returned from reporting in Jiangnan; Li Jing again memorialized wishing to transmit the throne to his heir Hongji, and the emperor also replied with a letter.

entries.zh: 甲子，賜江南羊萬口、馬三百匹、橐駝三十頭，賜兩浙錢俶羊五千口、馬二百匹、橐駝二十頭。
entries.en: On jiazi Jiangnan was granted ten thousand sheep, three hundred horses, and thirty camels; Qian Chu of the Two Zhes was granted five thousand sheep, two hundred horses, and twenty camels.
entries.literal: On jiazi Jiangnan was granted ten thousand sheep, three hundred horses, and thirty camels; the Two Zhes' Qian Chu was granted five thousand sheep, two hundred horses, and twenty camels.

entries.zh: 乙丑，賜宰臣、樞密使及近臣宴於玉津園。
entries.en: On yichou chief ministers, Military Affairs commissioners, and close officials were granted a banquet in Jade Ford Garden.
entries.literal: On yichou chief ministers, Military Affairs commissioners, and close officials were granted a banquet in Jade Ford Garden.

entries.zh: 己巳，占城國王釋利因德漫遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On jisi the king of Champa, Shili Yinde Man, dispatched envoys presenting local products.
entries.literal: On jisi the king of Champa, Shili Yinde Man, dispatched envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 壬子，天清節，群臣詣廣德殿上壽。
entries.en: On renzi, the Tianqing Festival, the assembled ministers went to Guangde Hall to offer birthday congratulations.
entries.literal: On renzi, the Tianqing Festival, the assembled ministers went to Guangde Hall to offer birthday congratulations.

entries.zh: 江南進奉使商崇義代李景捧壽觴以獻。
entries.en: Jiangnan tribute envoy Shang Chongyi, on Li Jing's behalf, raised and presented the birthday toast.
entries.literal: Jiangnan tribute envoy Shang Chongyi, on Li Jing's behalf, raised the birthday toast and presented it.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋類苑》云：湯悅，父殷舉，唐末有才名。
entries.en: (The 《Song Anecdotes Collection》 records that Tang Yue's father Yin Ju had a reputation for talent at the end of Tang.
entries.literal: (The 《Song Anecdotes Collection》 states: Tang Yue's father Yin Ju had a reputation for talent at the end of Tang.

entries.zh: 本名崇義，建隆初，避宣祖諱改姓湯。
entries.en: His original name was Chongyi. At the beginning of Jianlong, to avoid the taboo name of the Founding Ancestor he changed his surname to Tang.
entries.literal: His original name was Chongyi; at the beginning of Jianlong, to avoid the taboo name of the Founding Ancestor he changed his surname to Tang.

entries.zh: 初在吳為舍人，受詔撰揚州《孝先寺碑》，世宗親往，駐蹕此寺，讀其文賞嘆。
entries.en: At first in Wu he was a palace aide. By edict he composed the Yangzhou Xiaoxian Temple stele. Shizong personally went there, halted at the temple, read his text, and praised it in admiration.
entries.literal: At first in Wu he was a palace aide; by edict he composed the Yangzhou Xiaoxian Temple stele; Shizong personally went there, halted at this temple, read his text and praised it in admiration.

entries.zh: 及畫江議定，後主遣悅入貢，世宗為之加禮。
entries.en: When the agreement to draw the Yangtze as boundary was settled, the Later Lord sent Yue to present tribute, and Shizong treated him with added courtesy.
entries.literal: When the agreement to draw the Yangtze as boundary was settled, the Later Lord sent Yue to present tribute; Shizong treated him with added courtesy.

entries.zh: 自淮上用兵，凡書詔多悅之作，特為典贍，切於事情。
entries.en: From the time of military action on the Huai, most edicts and proclamations were Yue's compositions—classical and ample, closely fitted to the matter at hand.
entries.literal: From the time of military action on the Huai, most edicts and proclamations were Yue's compositions; they were especially classical and ample, closely fitted to the matter at hand.

entries.zh: 世宗每覽江南文字，形於嗟嘆。
entries.en: Whenever Shizong read Jiangnan writings, sighs of admiration appeared on his face.
entries.literal: Whenever Shizong read Jiangnan writings, sighs of admiration appeared on his face.

entries.zh: 當時沈遇、馬士元皆不稱職，復用陶蒨、李昉於舍人，其後用扈載，率由此也。）〉
entries.en: At the time Shen Yu and Ma Shiyuan were both unfit for their posts. Tao Qian and Li Fang were again used as palace aides, and afterward Hu Zai was used—all largely for this reason.)〉
entries.literal: At the time Shen Yu and Ma Shiyuan were both unfit for their posts; Tao Qian and Li Fang were again used as palace aides; afterward Hu Zai was used—all largely for this reason.)〉

entries.zh: 冬十月己卯，以戶部侍郎高防為西南面水陸轉運使，將用師於巴、邛故也。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on jimao, Vice Minister of Revenue Gao Fang was appointed Southwest land-and-water transport commissioner because troops were about to be used in Ba and Qiong.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on jimao, Vice Minister of Revenue Gao Fang was made Southwest land-and-water transport commissioner, because troops were about to be used in Ba and Qiong.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·高防傳》：世宗謀伐蜀，以防為西南面水陸轉運制置使，屢發芻糧赴鳳州，為征討之備。）〉
entries.en: (The 《History of Song》, biography of Gao Fang, records that Shizong planned to attack Shu and made Fang Southwest land-and-water transport planning commissioner. He repeatedly dispatched fodder and grain to Feng Prefecture as preparation for the campaign.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《History of Song》, biography of Gao Fang: Shizong planned to attack Shu and made Fang Southwest land-and-water transport planning commissioner; he repeatedly dispatched fodder and grain to Feng Prefecture as preparation for the campaign.)〉

entries.zh: 丙戌，邠州李暉移鎮鳳翔。
entries.en: On bingxu Li Hui of Bin Prefecture was transferred to garrison Fengxiang.
entries.literal: On bingxu Li Hui of Bin Prefecture was transferred to garrison Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 戊子，幸迎春苑。
entries.en: On wuzi the emperor visited Welcome Spring Park.
entries.literal: On wuzi the emperor visited Welcome Spring Park.

entries.zh: 己丑，太常卿司徒詡以本官致仕。
entries.en: On jichou Grand Master of Ceremonies Situ Xu retired from office in his original rank.
entries.literal: On jichou Grand Master of Ceremonies Situ Xu retired from office in his original rank.

entries.zh: 壬辰，帝狩於近郊。
entries.en: On renchen the emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
entries.literal: On renchen the emperor hunted in the near suburbs.

entries.zh: 癸巳，前相州節度使王饒卒。
entries.en: On guisi former Xiang Prefecture military governor Wang Rao died.
entries.literal: On guisi former Xiang Prefecture military governor Wang Rao died.

entries.zh: 甲午，左監門上將軍許文縝、右千牛上將軍邊鎬、衛尉卿周延構並歸江南。
entries.en: On jiawu Left Gate Guard upper general Xu Wenzhen, Right Thousand-Ox Guard upper general Bian Hao, and Court of Imperial Regalia director Zhou Yangou all returned to Jiangnan.
entries.literal: On jiawu Left Gate Guard upper general Xu Wenzhen, Right Thousand-Ox Guard upper general Bian Hao, and Court of Imperial Regalia director Zhou Yangou all returned to Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 乙未，詔淮南諸州鄉軍，並放歸農。
entries.en: On yiwei an edict ordered that local militia of the various Huainan prefectures all be released to return to farming.
entries.literal: On yiwei an edict ordered that local militia of the various Huainan prefectures all be released to return to farming.

entries.zh: 丁酉，遣左散騎常侍艾穎等均定河南六十州稅賦。
entries.en: On dingyou Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Ai Ying and others were dispatched to equalize and fix the taxes of the sixty prefectures of Henan.
entries.literal: On dingyou Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Ai Ying and others were dispatched to equalize and fix the taxes of the sixty prefectures of Henan.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載賜諸道均田詔曰：「朕以干戈既弭，寰海漸寧，言念地征，罕臻藝極，須並行均定，所冀永適重輕。
entries.en: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records the edict bestowing equal-field charts on the circuits: "Since arms have been laid down and the realm is gradually at peace, I reflect on land tax and find it rarely reaches the utmost standard. Equalization must be carried out together, the hope being to fix light and heavy burdens permanently.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records the edict bestowing equal-field charts on the circuits: "I, since arms have been laid down and the realm is gradually at peace, reflect on land tax and find it rarely reaches the utmost standard; equalization must be carried out together, the hope being to fix light and heavy burdens permanently.

entries.zh: 卿受任方隅，深窮治本，必須副寡昧平分之意，察鄉閭治弊之原，明示條章，用分寄任，佇令集事，允屬推公。
entries.en: You, charged in your region, must deeply investigate the root of governance, match my intent of equal division, examine the origins of abuses in village and lane, clearly set forth regulations, divide entrusted responsibility, and await the completion of the task—all properly belonging to impartial promotion.
entries.literal: You, charged in your region, must deeply investigate the root of governance, surely match my humble intent of equal division, examine the origins of abuses in village and lane, clearly set forth regulations, use them to divide entrusted responsibility, and await the completion of the task—all properly belonging to impartial promotion.

entries.zh: 今差使臣往彼檢括，餘從別敕。」）〉
entries.en: Envoys are now dispatched there to inspect and compile; the rest follows separate edicts.")〉
entries.literal: Now envoys are dispatched there to inspect and compile; the rest follows separate edicts.")〉

entries.zh: 十二月丁丑朔，郎州奏，醴陵縣玉仙觀山門中，舊有田二萬頃，久為山石閉塞，今年七月十七日夜，暴雷劈開，其路復通。
entries.en: On the dingchou new moon in the twelfth month, Lang Prefecture reported that within the mountain gate of Yuxian Abbey in Liling County there had formerly been twenty thousand qing of fields long blocked by mountain rock. On the night of the seventeenth day of the seventh month of this year a violent thunderbolt split it open and the path was restored.
entries.literal: On the dingchou new moon of the twelfth month, Lang Prefecture reported that within the mountain gate of Yuxian Abbey in Liling County there had formerly been twenty thousand qing of fields, long blocked by mountain rock; on the night of the seventeenth day of the seventh month of this year a violent thunderbolt split it open and the path was restored.

entries.zh: 己卯，楚州兵馬都監武懷恩棄市，坐擅殺降軍四人也。
entries.en: On jimao Chuzhou cavalry-and-infantry inspector Wu Huaien was executed in the marketplace for unauthorized killing of four surrendered soldiers.
entries.literal: On jimao Chuzhou cavalry-and-infantry inspector Wu Huaien was executed in the marketplace, the offense being unauthorized killing of four surrendered soldiers.

entries.zh: 丙戌，詔重定諸道州府幕職令錄佐官料錢，其州縣官俸戶宜停。
entries.en: On bingxu an edict ordered a redetermination of the salary stipends of staff officers, prefectural aides, and county assistants in the circuits and prefectures. The salary households of prefectural and county officials should be discontinued.
entries.literal: On bingxu an edict ordered a redetermination of the salary stipends of staff officers, prefectural aides, and county assistants in the circuits and prefectures; the salary households of prefectural and county officials should be discontinued.

entries.zh: 己丑，楚州防禦使張順賜死，坐在任隱落榷稅錢五十萬、官絲綿二千兩也。
entries.en: On jichou Chuzhou defense commissioner Zhang Shun was granted death by imperial favor for concealing and withholding five hundred thousand in monopoly tax funds and two thousand taels of official silk and cotton while in office.
entries.literal: On jichou Chuzhou defense commissioner Zhang Shun was granted death by imperial favor, the offense being while in office concealing and withholding five hundred thousand in monopoly tax funds and two thousand taels of official silk and cotton.

entries.zh: 壬辰，詔兩京及五府少尹司參軍各省一員，六曹判司內只直戶法二曹，余及諸州觀察支使、兩蕃判官並省。
entries.en: On renchen an edict ordered that in the Two Capitals and the Five Prefectures one assistant prefect and one administrative aide each be reduced. Among the six bureau review clerks only the Household and Law bureaus would be retained; the rest, together with observation envoys of the various prefectures and frontier judges, would all be reduced.
entries.literal: On renchen an edict ordered that in the Two Capitals and the Five Prefectures one assistant prefect and one administrative aide each be reduced; among the six bureau review clerks only the Household and Law bureaus be retained; the rest, together with observation envoys of the various prefectures and frontier judges, all be reduced.

entries.zh: 甲午，帝狩於近郊。
entries.en: On jiawu the emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
entries.literal: On jiawu the emperor hunted in the near suburbs.

entries.zh: 乙未，鄧州劉重進移鎮邠州，滑州宋延渥移鎮鄧州，以前河中節度使王仁鎬為邢州節度使，以邢州留後陳思讓為滑州留後。
entries.en: On yiwei Liu Chongjin of Deng Prefecture was transferred to garrison Bin Prefecture; Song Yanwo of Hua Prefecture was transferred to garrison Deng Prefecture; former Hezhong military governor Wang Renhao was appointed Xing Prefecture military governor; and Xing Prefecture acting military governor Chen Sirang was appointed Hua Prefecture acting military governor.
entries.literal: On yiwei Liu Chongjin of Deng Prefecture was transferred to garrison Bin Prefecture; Song Yanwo of Hua Prefecture was transferred to garrison Deng Prefecture; former Hezhong military governor Wang Renhao was made Xing Prefecture military governor; and Xing Prefecture acting military governor Chen Sirang was made Hua Prefecture acting military governor.

entries.zh: 己亥，詔翰林學士，今後逐日起居，當直者仍赴晚朝。
entries.en: On jihai an edict ordered that Hanlin academicians henceforth attend daily court and that those on duty should still attend the evening audience.
entries.literal: On jihai an edict ordered that Hanlin academicians henceforth attend daily court; those on duty should still attend the evening audience.

entries.zh: 是月，江南李景殺其臣偽太傅中書令宋齊丘、偽兵部侍郎陳覺、偽鎮南軍節度副使李徵古等。
entries.en: That month Li Jing of Jiangnan killed his ministers the illegitimately styled Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister Song Qiqiu, illegitimately styled Vice Minister of War Chen Jue, illegitimately styled Pacifying South Army deputy military governor Li Zhenggu, and others.
entries.literal: That month Li Jing of Jiangnan killed his ministers the rebel-appointed Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister Song Qiqiu, rebel-appointed Vice Minister of War Chen Jue, rebel-appointed Pacifying South Army deputy military governor Li Zhenggu, and others.

entries.zh: 初，帝之南征也，吳人大懼，覺與徵古皆齊丘門人，因進說於景，請委國事於齊丘，景繇是銜之。
entries.en: Initially, when the emperor campaigned south, the Wu people were greatly afraid. Jue and Zhenggu were both disciples of Qiqiu and therefore urged Jing to entrust state affairs to Qiqiu. Jing thereby harbored resentment against him.
entries.literal: Initially, when the emperor campaigned south, the Wu people were greatly afraid; Jue and Zhenggu were both disciples of Qiqiu and therefore advanced a proposal to Jing to entrust state affairs to Qiqiu; Jing thereby harbored resentment against him.

entries.zh: 及吳人遣鐘謨、李德明奉表至行在，帝尋遣德明復命於金陵，德明因說李景請割江南之地求和於我，而陳覺、李徵古等以德明為賣國，請戮之，景遂殺德明。
entries.en: When the Wu people sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming to present a memorial at the field headquarters, the emperor soon sent Deming back to report at Jinling. Deming therefore urged Li Jing to cede Jiangnan territory and seek peace with the Zhou court. But Chen Jue, Li Zhenggu, and others regarded Deming as selling out the state and requested his execution, and Jing then killed Deming.
entries.literal: When the Wu people sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming to present a memorial at the mobile court, the emperor soon sent Deming back to report at Jinling; Deming therefore urged Li Jing to cede Jiangnan territory and seek peace with us; but Chen Jue, Li Zhenggu, and others regarded Deming as selling out the state and requested his execution; Jing then killed Deming.

entries.zh: 及江南內附，帝放鐘謨南歸，謨本德明之黨也，因譖齊丘等，故齊丘等得罪。
entries.en: When Jiangnan submitted to the court, the emperor released Zhong Mo to return south. Mo had originally been of Deming's faction and therefore slandered Qiqiu and the others, and Qiqiu and the others were punished.
entries.literal: When Jiangnan submitted internally, the emperor released Zhong Mo to return south; Mo had originally been of Deming's faction and therefore slandered Qiqiu and the others, so Qiqiu and the others were punished.

entries.zh: 放齊丘歸九華山，覺等貶官，尋並害之。
entries.en: Qiqiu was released to Mount Jiuhua; Jue and others were demoted, and soon all were killed.
entries.literal: Qiqiu was released to return to Mount Jiuhua; Jue and others were demoted in office, and soon all were killed.

entries.zh: 景既誅齊丘等，令鐘謨到闕，具言其事，故書。
entries.en: After Jing had executed Qiqiu and the others, he ordered Zhong Mo to come to court and fully report the matter; hence this record.
entries.literal: After Jing had executed Qiqiu and the others, he ordered Zhong Mo to come to court and fully report the matter; hence this record.

entries.zh: 顯德五年春正月癸未朔，帝在楚州城下，從臣詣行宮稱賀。
entries.en: On the guiwei new moon in the first month of spring, Xiande 5, the emperor was encamped beneath the walls of Chuzhou, and his attending officials went to the field palace to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xiande, on the guiwei new moon of the first month of spring, the emperor was below the walls of Chuzhou; attending officials went to the mobile palace to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 〈（《隆平集·馬仁瑀傳》：世宗征淮南，登楚州水寨飛樓，距城百步，城卒詬罵，左右射莫能及。
entries.en: (The 《Longping Collection》, biography of Ma Renyu, records that when Shizong campaigned in Huainan he climbed the flying tower of Chuzhou's water fort, a hundred paces from the city wall.
