Garrison soldiers hurled abuse at him, and though his attendants shot back, none of their arrows could reach the wall.
entries.literal: (Per the 《Longping Collection》, biography of Ma Renyu: When Shizong campaigned in Huainan he climbed the flying tower of Chuzhou's water fort, a hundred paces from the city; garrison soldiers cursed and reviled him, and though those at his side shot arrows none could reach them.

entries.zh: 召仁瑀至，應弦而斃。）〉
entries.en: Ma Renyu was summoned forward and, at the twang of the bowstring, struck them dead.)〉
entries.literal: Renyu was summoned; at the twang of the bowstring they were struck dead.)〉

entries.zh: 乙酉，降同州為郡。
entries.en: On yiyou Tong Prefecture was demoted to commandery status.
entries.literal: On yiyou Tong Prefecture was reduced in rank to a commandery.

entries.zh: 右驍衛將軍王環卒。
entries.en: Right Brave Guards general Wang Huan died.
entries.literal: Right Brave Guards general Wang Huan died.

entries.zh: 丙戌，右龍武將軍王漢璋奏，攻海州。
entries.en: On bingxu Right Dragon Martial general Wang Hanzhang reported that he was attacking Haizhou.
entries.literal: On bingxu Right Dragon Martial general Wang Hanzhang reported an attack on Haizhou.

entries.zh: 戊子，詔：「諸道幕職州縣官，並以三周年為考限，閏月不在其內，州府不得差攝官替正官」云。
entries.en: On wuzi an edict ordered: "Staff officials throughout the circuits, prefectures, and counties should serve three full calendar years before merit review, with intercalary months excluded, and prefectural governments must not appoint acting officials to replace the regular incumbents."
entries.literal: On wuzi an edict stated: "Staff officials of circuits, prefectures, and counties alike shall take three calendar years as the term for merit review; intercalary months are not counted; prefectures and prefectural governments may not appoint acting officials to replace the regular incumbents."

entries.zh: 己丑，詔侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤權知揚州軍府事。
entries.en: On jichou an edict named Palace Horse Army commander-in-chief Han Lingkun acting administrator of the Yangzhou military government.
entries.literal: On jichou an edict appointed Palace Horse Army commander-in-chief Han Lingkun acting administrator of Yangzhou's military government.

entries.zh: 庚寅，發楚州管內丁壯，開鸛河以通運路。
entries.en: On gengyin corvée laborers from Chuzhou's jurisdiction were mobilized to dredge the Stork River and open a supply route.
entries.literal: On gengyin corvée labor from within Chuzhou's jurisdiction was mobilized to open the Stork River and link the transport route.

entries.zh: 乙巳，帝親攻楚州。
entries.en: On yisi the emperor personally assaulted Chuzhou.
entries.literal: On yisi the emperor personally attacked Chuzhou.

entries.zh: 時今上在楚州城北，晝夜不解甲胄，親冒矢石，麾兵以登城。
entries.en: At the time the present sovereign was north of Chuzhou city. Day and night he kept his armor on, braved arrows and stones himself, and led troops up onto the wall.
entries.literal: At the time the present sovereign was north of Chuzhou city; day and night he did not remove his armor, personally braved arrows and stones, and commanded troops up onto the wall.

entries.zh: 丙午，拔之，斬偽守將張彥卿等，六軍大掠，城內軍民死者萬餘人，廬舍焚之殆盡。
entries.en: On bingwu the city fell. The Southern Tang defending generals Zhang Yanqing and others were beheaded. The six armies looted on a vast scale; more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians in the city were killed, and dwellings were burned almost to the last.
entries.literal: On bingwu the city was taken; rebel defending generals Zhang Yanqing and others were beheaded; the six armies looted on a great scale; more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians within the city died; dwellings were burned almost completely.

entries.zh: 〈（陸遊《南唐書·張彥卿傳》云：保大末，周世宗南侵，彥卿為楚州防禦使。
entries.en: (Lu You's 《History of Southern Tang》, biography of Zhang Yanqing, records that at the end of the Baoda era, when Zhou Shizong invaded the south, Yanqing was defense commissioner of Chuzhou.
entries.literal: (Lu You's 《History of Southern Tang》, biography of Zhang Yanqing, states: At the end of the Baoda era, when Zhou Shizong invaded south, Yanqing was defense commissioner of Chuzhou.

entries.zh: 周師銳甚，旬日間，海、泰州、靜海軍皆破，元宗亦命焚東都宮寺民廬，徙其民渡江。
entries.en: Zhou forces pressed hard. Within ten days Hai Prefecture, Taizhou, and the Jinghai Army all fell. Yuanzong also ordered the eastern capital's palaces, temples, and common dwellings burned and the people moved across the Yangtze.
entries.literal: Zhou forces were very sharp; within ten days Hai Prefecture, Taizhou, and the Jinghai Army were all taken; Yuanzong also ordered the burning of the eastern capital's palaces, temples, and common dwellings, and the relocation of the people across the Yangtze.

entries.zh: 世宗親禦旗鼓攻楚州，自城以外皆已下，發州民浚老鸛河，遣齊雲戰艦數百，自淮入江，勢如震霆烈焰。
entries.en: Shizong personally directed the assault on Chuzhou. Everything beyond the city had already fallen. He mobilized the prefecture's people to dredge the Old Stork River and sent several hundred Cloud-Level warships from the Huai into the Yangtze with the force of thunder and fire.
entries.literal: Shizong personally directed flags and drums in the attack on Chuzhou; everything outside the city had already fallen; he mobilized the prefecture's people to dredge the Old Stork River and dispatched several hundred Cloud-Level warships from the Huai into the Yangtze, with momentum like thunder and blazing flame.

entries.zh: 彥卿獨不為動。
entries.en: Yanqing alone stood firm.
entries.literal: Yanqing alone was unmoved.

entries.zh: 及梯沖臨城，鑿城為窟室，實薪而焚之，城皆摧圯，遂陷。
entries.en: When siege towers and battering rams reached the wall, the attackers dug chambers into it, packed them with firewood, and set them ablaze. The wall crumbled and the city fell.
entries.literal: When siege towers and rams reached the wall, they dug into the wall to make chambers, filled them with firewood and burned them; the wall was all destroyed and collapsed, and the city then fell.

entries.zh: 彥卿猶結陣城內，誓死奮擊，謂之巷鬥。
entries.en: Yanqing still formed ranks inside the city and fought to the death in what came to be called street fighting.
entries.literal: Yanqing still formed ranks within the city, vowing to die in fierce combat; this was called street fighting.

entries.zh: 日暮，轉至州廨，長短兵皆盡，彥卿猶取繩床搏戰，及兵馬都監鄭昭業等千餘人皆死之，無一人生降者。
entries.en: At dusk the fighting moved to the prefectural yamen. Long and short weapons were spent, yet Yanqing still seized a rope bed and fought on. Cavalry-and-infantry inspector Zheng Zhaoye and more than a thousand others died with him; not one surrendered alive.
entries.literal: At dusk the fighting shifted to the prefectural yamen; long and short weapons were all exhausted; Yanqing still took a rope bed and fought on; together with cavalry-and-infantry inspector Zheng Zhaoye and more than a thousand others all died; not one man surrendered alive.

entries.zh: 周兵死傷亦甚眾，世宗怒，盡屠城中居民，焚其室廬，然得彥卿子光祐不殺也。
entries.en: Zhou casualties were also very heavy. Shizong in his rage slaughtered the city's inhabitants and burned their dwellings, yet when Yanqing's son Guangyou was captured he was spared.
entries.literal: Zhou troops also suffered very heavy casualties; Shizong was enraged and slaughtered all residents within the city and burned their dwellings; yet when Yanqing's son Guangyou was captured he was not killed.

entries.zh: 又，趙鼎臣《竹隱畸士集》云：當城中之危也，彥卿方與諸將立城上，因泣諫以周、唐強弱，勢不足以相支，又城危甚，而外無一人援，恐旦夕徒死無益，勸彥卿趣降。
entries.en: Zhao Dingchen's 《Collected Writings of the Eccentric Gentleman of Bamboo Retreat》 also records that when the city was in peril Yanqing was standing on the wall with his generals. One of them wept and urged surrender, arguing that Zhou and Tang were too mismatched in strength to hold out, that the city was in grave danger with no relief coming from outside, and that they would only die in vain if they waited.
entries.literal: Moreover, Zhao Dingchen's 《Collected Writings of the Eccentric Gentleman of Bamboo Retreat》 states: When the city was in peril, Yanqing was standing on the wall with his generals; one of them wept and remonstrated, citing the relative strength of Zhou and Tang, saying their force was insufficient to hold out, that the city was in extreme danger and no one outside would aid them, fearing they would die in vain before long, and urging Yanqing to hurry and surrender.

entries.zh: 彥卿頷之，因顧諸將指曰：「視彼！」
entries.en: Yanqing nodded, then turned to the generals and pointed, saying: "Look there!"
entries.literal: Yanqing nodded, then turned to the generals and pointed, saying: "Look there!"

entries.zh: 諸將方回顧，彥卿則抽劍斷其子首，擲諸地，慷慨泣謂諸將曰：「此彥卿子，勸彥卿降周，彥卿受李家厚恩，誼不降，此城吾死所也。
entries.en: As the generals turned to look, Yanqing drew his sword and cut off his son's head, flung it to the ground, and with tears told them: "This is my son, who urged me to surrender to Zhou. I have received great favor from the Li house and cannot in honor yield. This city is where I shall die.
entries.literal: As the generals were just turning to look, Yanqing drew his sword and severed his son's head, cast it to the ground, and with passionate tears told the generals: "This is Yanqing's son, who urged Yanqing to surrender to Zhou. Yanqing has received great favor from the Li house and in duty cannot surrender. This city is where I shall die.

entries.zh: 諸軍欲降任降，第勿勸我，勸我者同此子矣。」
entries.en: If any of you wish to surrender, do so—but do not urge me. Whoever urges me will share this boy's fate."
entries.literal: If any in the army wish to surrender, let them surrender; only do not urge me—whoever urges me shall share this son's fate."

entries.zh: 於是諸將愕眙亦泣，莫敢言降。）〉
entries.en: The generals stared in shock and wept; none dared speak of surrender again.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon the generals stared in shock and wept as well; none dared speak of surrender.)〉

entries.zh: 六月乙亥朔，潞州李筠奏，攻下遼州，獲偽刺史張丕旦。
entries.en: On the first day of the sixth month, yihai, Li Jun of Luzhou reported the capture of Liao Prefecture and the Northern Han-appointed prefect Zhang Pidan.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on yihai the first day of the month, Li Jun of Luzhou memorialized that Liao Prefecture had been taken and the Northern Han-appointed prefect Zhang Pidan captured.

entries.zh: 丙子，以皇女薨輟朝三日。
entries.en: On bingzi, court was suspended for three days upon the death of an imperial daughter.
entries.literal: On bingzi, because an imperial daughter had died, court was suspended for three days.

entries.zh: 戊寅，鳳翔奏，節度使李暉卒。
entries.en: On wuyin, Fengxiang reported the death of military commissioner Li Hui.
entries.literal: On wuyin, Fengxiang reported that Military Commissioner Li Hui had died.

entries.zh: 鄭州奏，河決原武，詔宣徽南院使吳延祚發近縣丁夫二萬人以塞之。
entries.en: Zheng Prefecture reported a breach of the Yellow River at Yuanwu; Wu Yanzuo was ordered to mobilize twenty thousand corvée laborers from nearby counties to stem it.
entries.literal: Zheng Prefecture reported that the Yellow River had breached its banks at Yuanwu; an edict ordered Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Southern Court Wu Yanzuo to mobilize twenty thousand corvée laborers from nearby counties to block it.

entries.zh: 庚辰，命宣徽北院使昝居潤判開封府事。
entries.en: On gengchen, Zan Jurun of the northern court was assigned to administer Kaifeng.
entries.literal: On gengchen, Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Northern Court Zan Jurun was ordered to judge Kaifeng prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 晉州節度使楊廷璋奏，率兵入河東界，招降堡寨一十三所。
entries.en: Yang Tingzhang of Jin reported that he had led troops into the Hedong frontier and induced thirteen fortified strongholds to surrender.
entries.literal: Jin Prefecture Military Commissioner Yang Tingzhang memorialized that he had led troops into the Hedong frontier and induced thirteen fortified strongholds to surrender.

entries.zh: 癸未，立魏王符彥卿女為皇后，仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。
entries.en: On guiwei, the daughter of Fu Yanqing, Prince of Wei, was installed as empress, and the responsible offices were ordered to choose a day for the investiture ceremony.
entries.literal: On guiwei, the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was installed as empress; the responsible offices were further ordered to choose a day and prepare the rites of investiture.

entries.zh: 以皇長子宗訓為特進左衛上將軍，封梁王；
entries.en: The eldest son Zongxun was made specially advanced general of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;
entries.literal: The eldest imperial son Zongxun was made specially advanced General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;

entries.zh: 以第二子宗讓為左驍衛上將軍，封燕國公。
entries.en: the second son Zongrang was made general of the Left Tiger Swift Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
entries.literal: the second son Zongrang was made General of the Left Tiger Swift Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

entries.zh: 賜江南進奉使李從善錢二萬貫、絹二萬匹、銀一萬兩，賜兩浙進奉使吳延福錢三千貫、絹五千匹、銀器三十兩。
entries.en: Li Congshan, the Jiangnan tribute envoy, received twenty thousand strings of cash, twenty thousand bolts of silk, and ten thousand taels of silver; Wu Yanfu of the Two Zhes received three thousand strings of cash, five thousand bolts of silk, and thirty taels of silver vessels.
entries.literal: Li Congshan, Jiangnan tribute envoy, was granted twenty thousand strings of cash, twenty thousand bolts of silk, and ten thousand taels of silver; Wu Yanfu, Two Zhes tribute envoy, was granted three thousand strings of cash, five thousand bolts of silk, and thirty taels of silver vessels.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以前青州節度使李洪義為永興軍節度使，永興軍節度使王彥超移鎮鳳翔。
entries.en: On dinghai, former Qingzhou commissioner Li Hongyi became commissioner of Yongxing Army, and Wang Yanchao of Yongxing was transferred to Fengxiang.
entries.literal: On dinghai, former Qingzhou Military Commissioner Li Hongyi was made Yongxing Army military commissioner; Yongxing Army Military Commissioner Wang Yanchao was transferred to Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 戊子，潞州部送所獲遼州刺史張丕旦等二百四十五人以獻，詔釋之。
entries.en: On wuzi, Luzhou sent up two hundred forty-five captives including Zhang Pidan, prefect of Liao; an edict ordered them released.
entries.literal: On wuzi, Luzhou forwarded two hundred forty-five captives including Liao Prefecture prefect Zhang Pidan to present them; an edict ordered their release.

entries.zh: 己丑，宰臣範質、王溥並參知樞密院事。
entries.en: On jichou, grand councilors Fan Zhi and Wang Pu were both made participants in the Grand Council.
entries.literal: On jichou, Grand Councilors Fan Zhi and Wang Pu were both made participants in the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 以樞密使魏仁浦為中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士，依前充樞密使；
entries.en: Wei Renpu, grand councilor, was made vice director of the secretariat, concurrent grand councilor, and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, while retaining his grand council post;
entries.literal: Grand Councilor Wei Renpu was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, continuing as Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以宣徽南院使吳延祚為樞密使，行左驍衛上將軍；
entries.en: Wu Yanzuo of the southern court was made grand councilor with acting rank as general of the Left Tiger Swift Guard;
entries.literal: Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Southern Court Wu Yanzuo was made Grand Councilor, acting General of the Left Tiger Swift Guard;

entries.zh: 以宋州節度使、侍衛都虞候韓通為侍衛親軍副都指揮使，加檢校太尉、同平章事；
entries.en: Han Tong of Songzhou, deputy director of the palace guards, was made deputy director of the palace guards with acting grand marshal and concurrent grand councilor;
entries.literal: Songzhou Military Commissioner and Palace Guard Deputy Director Han Tong was made Deputy Director of the Palace Guards, with the added ranks of acting Grand Marshal and Concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 澶州節度使兼殿前都點檢、駙馬都尉張永德落軍職，加檢校太尉、同平章事；
entries.en: Zhang Yongde of Chanzhou, director of the palace front and imperial son-in-law, was relieved of his military posts and given acting grand marshal and concurrent grand councilor;
entries.literal: Cangzhou Military Commissioner, Concurrent Director of the Palace Front, and Imperial Son-in-Law Zhang Yongde was stripped of his military posts and given acting Grand Marshal and Concurrent Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以今上為殿前都點檢，加檢校太傅，依前忠武軍節度使。
entries.en: The present sovereign was made director of the palace front with acting grand tutor, while remaining military commissioner of Zhongwu Army.
entries.literal: The present sovereign was made Director of the Palace Front, with the added rank of acting Grand Tutor, remaining Zhongwu Army military commissioner.

entries.zh: 帝之北征也，凡供軍之物，皆令自京遞送行在。
entries.en: During the northern campaign, all military supplies were relayed from the capital to the temporary court.
entries.literal: On the Emperor's northern campaign, all supplies for the army were ordered relayed from the capital to the temporary court.

entries.zh: 一日，忽於地中得一木，長二三尺，如人之揭物者，其上卦全題云：「點檢做」，觀者莫測何物也。
entries.en: One day a piece of wood two or three feet long was unearthed, shaped like a figure holding something aloft; inscribed on it in full was "Inspector-General's post," and none who saw it could tell what it portended.
entries.literal: One day a piece of wood two or three chi long was suddenly found in the ground, shaped like a person holding something aloft; on it a full hexagram inscription read "Inspector-General's post," and onlookers could not fathom what it meant.

entries.zh: 至是，今上始受點檢之命，明年春，果自此職以副人望，則「點檢做」之言乃神符也。
entries.en: Now the present sovereign first received the inspector-general's appointment; the following spring he did indeed rise from that post to fulfill men's hopes—so the inscription "Inspector-General's post" was a divine omen.
entries.literal: At this time the present sovereign first received the appointment as inspector-general; the following spring he did indeed rise from this post to fulfill men's expectations—so the words "Inspector-General's post" were a divine token.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以宣徽北院使、判開封事昝居潤為左領軍上將軍，充宣徽南院使；
entries.en: On xinmao, Zan Jurun of the northern court, who was administering Kaifeng, was made general of the Left Lead Army and palace domestic commissioner of the southern court;
entries.literal: On xinmao, Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Northern Court and Kaifeng judge Zan Jurun was made General of the Left Lead Army and appointed Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Southern Court;

entries.zh: 以三司使、左領衛大將軍張美為左監門衛上將軍，充宣徽北院使，判三司。
entries.en: Zhang Mei, commissioner of the three departments and great general of the Left Lead Guard, was made general of the Left Gate Guard, palace domestic commissioner of the northern court, and assigned to administer the three departments.
entries.literal: Commissioner of the Three Departments and Great General of the Left Lead Guard Zhang Mei was made General of the Left Gate Guard, appointed Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Northern Court, and assigned to judge the Three Departments.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張美傳》：美少為三司小吏、澶州糧料使，世宗鎮澶州，每有求取，美悉力應之，及即位，連歲征討，糧饋無乏，美之力也。
entries.en: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: Mei began as a petty clerk of the three departments and grain commissary at Chanzhou. While Shizong was stationed there, Mei met every request; after his enthronement, supplies never failed through years of campaigning—thanks to Mei.
entries.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: in youth Mei was a petty clerk of the Three Departments and grain commissary of Cangzhou. When Shizong was stationed at Cangzhou, whenever he made demands Mei did his utmost to meet them; after the enthronement, year after year of campaigns went without shortage of provisions—Mei's doing.

entries.zh: 然每思澶州所為，終不以公忠待之。）〉
entries.en: Yet Shizong often recalled what had passed at Chanzhou and never treated him with full trust and favor.)〉
entries.literal: Yet he often recalled what had been done at Cangzhou and never treated him with full public loyalty.)〉

entries.zh: 癸巳，帝崩於萬歲殿，聖壽三十九。
entries.en: On guisi, the Emperor died in Wansui Hall at the age of thirty-nine.
entries.literal: On guisi, the Emperor died in Wansui Hall; his sacred age was thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 甲午，宣遺制，梁王於柩前即皇帝位，服紀月日一依舊制。
entries.en: On jiawu, the testamentary edict was proclaimed; the Prince of Liang took the throne before the bier, with mourning observances following the established calendar.
entries.literal: On jiawu, the testamentary edict was proclaimed; the Prince of Liang assumed the imperial throne before the bier, and the mourning calendar of months and days followed the old regulations.

entries.zh: 是日，群臣奉梁王即位於殿東楹，中外發哀。
entries.en: That day the officials installed the Prince of Liang at the hall's eastern pillar, and mourning was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: That day the officials installed the Prince of Liang at the eastern pillar of the hall; court and country raised mourning.

entries.zh: 其年八月，翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼上謚曰睿武孝文皇帝，廟號世宗。
entries.en: In the eighth month of that year, Dou Yan, Hanlin academician and administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, proposed the posthumous title Emperor Ruiwu Xiaowen, with the temple name Shizong.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Hanlin Academician and judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Yan submitted the posthumous title Emperor Ruiwu Xiaowen, with temple name Shizong.

entries.zh: 十一月壬寅朔，葬於慶陵。
entries.en: On the first day of the eleventh month, renyin, he was buried at Qingling.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on renyin the first day of the month, he was buried at Qingling.

entries.zh: 宰臣魏仁浦撰謚冊文，王溥撰哀冊文雲。
entries.en: Grand Councilor Wei Renpu composed the posthumous inscription and Wang Pu the lamentation text.
entries.literal: Grand Councilor Wei Renpu composed the posthumous inscription, and Wang Pu composed the lamentation text.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：世宗在民間，嘗與鄴中大商頡跌氏，忘其名，往江陵販賣茶貨。
entries.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: while still a commoner, Shizong once traveled with a wealthy merchant of Ye surnamed Xiedie, whose personal name is lost, to Jiangling to trade in tea.
entries.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: while Shizong was among the people, he once went with a great merchant of Ye surnamed Xiedie, whose given name is forgotten, to Jiangling to sell tea.

entries.zh: 至江陵，見有卜者王處士，其術如神，世宗因頡跌氏同往問焉。
entries.en: At Jiangling they met a diviner, Recluse Wang, whose skill seemed supernatural; Shizong went with Xiedie to consult him.
entries.literal: At Jiangling they saw a diviner, Recluse Wang, whose art was like that of a spirit; Shizong went with Xiedie to consult him.

entries.zh: 方布卦，忽有一蓍躍出，卓然而立，卜者大驚曰：「吾家筮法十餘世矣，常記曾祖以來遺言，凡卜筮而蓍自躍而出者，其人貴不可言，況又卓立不倒，得非為天下之主乎！」
entries.en: As he cast the hexagram, a yarrow stalk suddenly leaped out and stood upright. The diviner cried in alarm: "Our divination art has passed down more than ten generations. I remember my ancestors' teaching: when a stalk leaps out on its own, that person's rank is beyond telling—and here it stands without falling. Surely he is destined to rule all under Heaven!"
entries.literal: As he was laying out the hexagram, a stalk suddenly leaped out and stood upright. The diviner cried in alarm: "Our family's method of divination has passed down more than ten generations. I have always remembered the words left from my great-grandfather onward: whenever in divination a stalk leaps out of its own accord, that person's nobility is beyond words—and here it stands upright without falling. Could he not be lord of all under Heaven!"

entries.zh: 遽起再拜。
entries.en: He rose at once and bowed twice.
entries.literal: He rose at once and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 世宗雖佯為詰責，而私心甚喜。
entries.en: Shizong pretended to reprove him but was secretly delighted.
entries.literal: Shizong feigned rebuke but inwardly rejoiced greatly.

entries.zh: 於逆旅中夜置酒，與頡跌氏半酣，戲曰：「王處士以我當為天子，若一旦到此，足下要何官，請言之。」
entries.en: At an inn that night he set out wine and, half drunk with Xiedie, jested: "Recluse Wang says I am destined to be emperor. If that day comes, what office would you want? Tell me plainly."
entries.literal: At an inn that night he set out wine and, half drunk with Xiedie, jested: "Recluse Wang says I am destined to be Son of Heaven. If that day should come, what office would you want? Speak plainly."

entries.zh: 頡跌氏曰：「某三十年作估來，未有不由京洛者，每見稅官坐而獲利，一日所入，可以敵商賈數月，私心羨之。
entries.en: Xiedie said: "I have traded for thirty years and every route passed through the capital. I have seen how tax officers sit and profit—a single day's take equals a merchant's months. I have long envied that.
entries.literal: Xiedie said: "I have been a merchant for thirty years and never passed through the capital without noting how tax officers sit and reap profit—a single day's intake can equal a merchant's earnings for months. I have envied them in my heart.

entries.zh: 若大官為天子，某願得京洛稅院足矣。」
entries.en: If you become emperor, I would be content with the capital tax bureau."
entries.literal: If Your Excellency becomes Son of Heaven, I would be content with the capital tax bureau."

entries.zh: 世宗笑曰：「何望之卑耶！」
entries.en: Shizong laughed: "How modest your ambition!"
entries.literal: Shizong laughed: "How low your ambition!"

entries.zh: 及承郭氏之後踐祚，頡跌猶在，召見，竟如初言以與之。
entries.en: When he succeeded the Guo house and took the throne, Xiedie was still alive; summoned to court, he received exactly what had been promised in jest.
entries.literal: When after succeeding the Guo house he took the throne, Xiedie was still alive; he was summoned and received exactly what had been promised in jest.

entries.zh: 世宗之征東也，駐蹕於高平，劉崇兼契丹之眾來迎戰。
entries.en: On Shizong's eastern campaign he halted at Gaoping; Liu Chong came to battle with Khitan allies as well.
entries.literal: On Shizong's eastern campaign he halted at Gaoping; Liu Chong, with Khitan forces as well, came to give battle.

entries.zh: 時帥多持兩端，而王師不利。
entries.en: Many commanders wavered, and the imperial army was faring badly.
entries.literal: At the time many commanders wavered, and the imperial army fared badly.

entries.zh: 親軍帥樊愛能等各退衄，世宗赫怒，躍馬入陣，引五十人直沖崇之牙帳。
entries.en: Guard commanders such as Fan Aineng fell back in defeat. Shizong blazed with anger, spurred his horse into the line, and with fifty men charged straight at Chong's headquarters.
entries.literal: The guard commanders Fan Aineng and others each fell back in defeat. Shizong blazed with anger, leaped his horse into the battle line, and with fifty men charged straight at Chong's headquarters tent.

entries.zh: 崇方張樂飲酒，以示閑暇，及其奄至，莫不驚駭失次，世宗因以奮擊，遂敗之，追奔於城下。
entries.en: Chong was feasting with music to show his ease; when Shizong burst upon him, his men panicked. Shizong pressed the attack, routed the enemy, and pursued them to the city wall.
entries.literal: Chong was just spreading music and drinking wine to show ease; when Shizong suddenly arrived, all were struck with terror and lost order. Shizong pressed the attack and routed them, pursuing in flight to the foot of the city wall.

entries.zh: 凱旋，駐蹕潞州，且欲出其不意以誅退衄者，乃置酒高會，指樊愛能等數人責之曰：「汝輩皆累朝宿將，非不能用兵者也，然退衄者無他，誠欲將寡人作物貨賣與劉崇爾。
entries.en: Returning in triumph, he halted at Luzhou and planned to catch the defeated commanders off guard. At a grand banquet he pointed at Fan Aineng and several others and rebuked them: "You are veteran generals of successive reigns, not men who cannot fight—yet you fell back because you wished to sell me to Liu Chong like goods on the market.
entries.literal: Returning in triumph, he halted at Luzhou and wished to take by surprise those who had retreated in defeat. He set a grand banquet and, pointing at Fan Aineng and several others, rebuked them: "You are all veteran generals of successive reigns, not men unable to use troops—yet you fell back for no other reason than truly wishing to sell me as merchandise to Liu Chong.

entries.zh: 不然，何寡人親戰而劉崇始敗耶？
entries.en: Otherwise, why was Liu Chong defeated only when I fought in person?
entries.literal: Otherwise, why was it only when I fought in person that Liu Chong was first defeated?

entries.zh: 如此則卿等雖萬死不足以謝天下，宜其曲膝引頸以待斧誅。」
entries.en: For this, ten thousand deaths would not suffice to answer to the realm; bend your knees and offer your necks to the axe."
entries.literal: In such a case, though you died ten thousand deaths it would not suffice to answer to the realm; you should bend your knees and stretch your necks to await the axe."

entries.zh: 言訖，命行刑壯士擒出皆斬之。
entries.en: When he had finished, executioners seized them and all were beheaded.
entries.literal: When he had spoken, he ordered executioners to seize them and all were beheaded.

entries.zh: 於是立功士以次行賞，自行伍拔於軍廂者甚眾，其恩威並著，皆此類也。
entries.en: Meritorious soldiers were then rewarded in turn, and many were raised from the ranks to guard posts; his blend of mercy and severity was always of this kind.
entries.literal: Thereupon meritorious soldiers were rewarded in turn, and very many were raised from the ranks to posts in the guard; his favor and severity alike were manifest—matters of this kind.

entries.zh: 初，劉崇求援於契丹，得騎數千，及睹世宗兵少，侮之，曰：「吾觀周師易與爾，契丹之眾宜勿用，但以我軍攻戰，自當萬全。
entries.en: Earlier Liu Chong had sought Khitan aid and obtained several thousand horsemen. Seeing Shizong's small force, he despised it and said: "The Zhou army is easy prey. Best not use the Khitan; let my army alone fight and all will be secure.
entries.literal: Earlier, Liu Chong had sought aid from the Khitan and obtained several thousand horsemen. Seeing that Shizong's troops were few, he despised them and said: "I see the Zhou army is easy to deal with. The Khitan host had best not be used; let only my army fight, and all will be secure.

entries.zh: 如此則不惟破敵，亦足使契丹見而心服，一舉而有兩利，兵之機也。」
entries.en: Thus we defeat the enemy and make the Khitan see and submit—one stroke, two gains: the art of war."
entries.literal: Thus we will not only break the enemy but also make the Khitan see and submit in heart—one stroke with two gains: the opportunity of war."

entries.zh: 諸將以為然，乃使人謂契丹主將曰：「柴氏與吾，主客之勢，不煩足下余刃，敢請勒兵登高觀之可也。」
entries.en: The generals agreed and sent word to the Khitan commander: "Between the Chai house and us this is a contest of host and guest; spare your blades. We ask only that you array your troops on the heights and watch."
entries.literal: The generals agreed and sent word to the Khitan commander: "The Chai house and we are host and guest in this contest; we need not trouble you with the rest of the blades. We venture to ask that you array your troops on the heights and watch."

entries.zh: 契丹不知其謀，從之。
entries.en: The Khitan, unaware of the plot, complied.
entries.literal: The Khitan did not know the plot and complied.

entries.zh: 洎世宗之陣也，三軍皆賈勇爭進，無不一當百，契丹望而畏之，故不救而崇敗。
entries.en: When Shizong formed his line, all three armies vied to advance, each man fighting as ten; the Khitan looked on in fear and did not intervene, and Chong was defeated.
entries.literal: When Shizong formed his battle line, the three armies all vied in valor to advance, each man matching a hundred; the Khitan looked on in fear and did not rescue, and Chong was defeated.

entries.zh: 論者曰：「世宗患諸將之難制也久矣，思欲誅之，未有其釁，高平之役，可謂天假，故其斬決而無貸焉。
entries.en: Commentators say: "Shizong had long chafed at unruly generals and wished to execute them but lacked occasion. The Gaoping campaign was heaven's gift; hence he beheaded them without mercy.
entries.literal: Commentators say: "Shizong had long been troubled by the difficulty of controlling his generals and wished to execute them but had no occasion. The Gaoping campaign may be called heaven's gift; hence he beheaded them without mercy.

entries.zh: 自是姑息之政不行，朝廷始尊大，自非英主，其孰能為之哉！」
entries.en: From then indulgent governance ceased and the court grew formidable. Who but an heroic ruler could have done this!"
entries.literal: From this indulgent governance ceased; the court began to stand in awe. Unless an heroic ruler, who else could have done it!"

entries.zh: 世宗既下江北，駐蹕於建安，以書召偽主。
entries.en: After Shizong had crossed to the north bank of the Yangzi, he halted at Jian'an and summoned the Southern Tang ruler by letter.
entries.literal: After Shizong had descended on the north of the Yangzi, he halted at Jian'an and summoned the false ruler by letter.

entries.zh: 偽主惶恐，命鐘謨、李德明為使，以見世宗。
entries.en: The Southern Tang ruler was alarmed and sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming as envoys to see Shizong.
entries.literal: The false ruler was fearful and appointed Zhong Mo and Li Deming as envoys to see Shizong.

entries.zh: 德明素有詞辯，以利害說世宗使罷兵。
entries.en: Deming was known for eloquence and sought to persuade Shizong by arguments of advantage and harm to halt the campaign.
entries.literal: Deming was known for eloquence and sought to persuade Shizong by advantage and harm to halt the army.

entries.zh: 世宗且知之，乃盛陳兵師，排旗幟戈戟，為鹿項道以湊禦，然後引德明等入見。
entries.en: Shizong already knew this and arrayed his troops in full display, with banners, spears, and halberds, forming an avenue of barriers for the imperial approach before admitting Deming and the others to audience.
entries.literal: Shizong already knew this and therefore arrayed his forces in full display, setting out banners, spears, and halberds, forming an avenue of deer-antler barriers for the imperial approach, and only then led Deming and the others in to audience.

entries.zh: 世宗謂之曰：「汝江南自以為唐之後，衣冠禮樂世無比，何故與寡人隔一帶水，更不發一使奉書相問，惟泛海以通契丹，舍內事外，禮將安在？
entries.en: Shizong said to them: "You of Jiangnan call yourselves heirs of Tang, with rites and music unmatched in the age—yet separated from me by only a strip of water, you send no envoy with a letter of greeting, but cross the sea to deal with the Khitan, abandoning kin for outsiders. Where is propriety in that?
entries.literal: Shizong said to them: "You of Jiangnan consider yourselves heirs of Tang, with rites and music unmatched in the age—why then, separated from me by only a belt of water, do you not send a single envoy with a letter of inquiry, but cross the sea to communicate with the Khitan, abandoning the inner for the outer? Where is propriety?

entries.zh: 今又聞汝以詞說寡人罷兵，是將寡人比六國時一群癡漢，何不知人之甚也！
entries.en: Now I hear you use words to persuade me to halt the army—you take me for one of the witless lords of the Warring States. How little you know your man!
entries.literal: Now I hear you use words to persuade me to halt the army—you take me for one of the witless fools of the Six States era. How greatly you misjudge men!

entries.zh: 汝慎勿言，當速歸報汝主，令徑來跪寡人兩拜，則無事矣。
entries.en: Say no more. Return at once and tell your lord to come straightway and kneel before me in two prostrations, and all will be well.
entries.literal: Take care not to speak further. Return quickly and report to your lord: let him come straightway and kneel before me in two prostrations, and all will be well.

entries.zh: 不然，則寡人須看金陵城，借府庫以犒軍，汝等得無悔乎！」
entries.en: Otherwise I shall have to visit Jinling and borrow its treasury to reward my army—will you not regret it!"
entries.literal: Otherwise I must visit Jinling city and borrow its treasury to reward the army—will you not regret it!"

entries.zh: 於是德明等戰懼，不能措一辭，即日告歸。
entries.en: Deming and the others trembled with fear and could not utter a word; that same day they asked leave to return.
entries.literal: Thereupon Deming and the others trembled with fear and could not set forth a single word; that same day they asked to return.

entries.zh: 及見偽主，具陳世宗英烈之狀，非四方所能敵。
entries.en: When they saw their ruler, they described Shizong's heroic bearing in full—not to be matched anywhere under heaven.
entries.literal: When they saw the false ruler, they fully described Shizong's heroic and fierce bearing—not to be matched in the four quarters.

entries.zh: 偽主計無所出，遂上表服罪，且乞保江南之地，以奉宗廟、修職貢，其詞甚哀。
entries.en: Their ruler could devise no plan and submitted a memorial confessing guilt, begging to keep Jiangnan to serve his ancestral temple and maintain tribute; the wording was deeply plaintive.
entries.literal: The false ruler could devise no plan and submitted a memorial confessing guilt, begging moreover to keep the lands of Jiangnan to serve the ancestral temple and maintain tribute duties; the wording was very plaintive.

entries.zh: 世宗許之，因曰：「叛則征，服則懷，寡人之心也。」
entries.en: Shizong granted it and said: "Rebellion brings war; submission brings mercy—that is my policy."
entries.literal: Shizong granted it and said: "Rebellion brings campaign; submission brings embrace—that is my heart."

entries.zh: 於是遣使者賫書安之，然後凱還。
entries.en: He then sent envoys with a letter of reassurance and returned in triumph.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys bearing a letter to reassure them, and then returned in triumph.

entries.zh: 論者以世宗加兵於江南，不獨臨之以威，抑亦諭之以禮，可謂得大君之體矣。
entries.en: Commentators hold that in bringing force against Jiangnan, Shizong confronted them with might yet also instructed them in propriety—the manner of a great prince.
entries.literal: Commentators hold that in applying force to Jiangnan, Shizong not only confronted them with might but also instructed them in propriety—truly the manner of a great prince.

entries.zh: 陳摶，陜西人，能為詩，數舉不第，慨然有塵外之趣，隱居華山，自是其名大振。
entries.en: Chen Tuan of Shaanxi could compose poetry; having failed the examinations several times, he turned to life beyond the world and retired to Mount Hua, whence his fame spread widely.
entries.literal: Chen Tuan was a native of Shaanxi, able to compose poetry; he failed the examinations several times and, stirred, took to tastes beyond the dust, retiring to Mount Hua—from then his fame greatly spread.

entries.zh: 世宗之在位也，以四方未服，思欲牢籠英傑，且以摶曾踐場屋，不得志而隱，必有奇才遠略，於是召到闕下，拜左拾遺。
entries.en: While Shizong reigned, with the realm not yet united, he wished to win outstanding men; because Tuan had entered the examinations, failed to advance, and retired, he must possess rare talent—so Tuan was summoned to court and made Left Remonstrance and Policy Adviser.
entries.literal: While Shizong held the throne, the four quarters not yet subdued, he wished to win over outstanding men; and because Tuan had once entered the examination halls, failed to achieve his aim, and retired, he must possess rare talent and far-reaching design—therefore he was summoned to court and made Left Remonstrance and Policy Adviser.

entries.zh: 摶不就，堅乞歸山，世宗許之。
entries.en: Tuan declined and firmly begged to return to the mountains; Shizong granted his request.
entries.literal: Tuan would not accept and firmly begged to return to the mountains; Shizong granted it.

entries.zh: 未幾，賜之書：「敕陳摶，朕以汝高謝人寰，棲心物外，養太浩自然之氣，應少微處士之星，既不屈於王侯，遂甘隱於巖壑，樂我中和之化，慶乎下武之期，而能遠涉山塗，暫來城闕，浹旬延遇，宏益居多，白雲暫駐於帝鄉，好爵難縻於達士。
entries.en: Before long he granted him a letter: "To Chen Tuan: You have loftily withdrawn from the world and dwell beyond things, nurturing primordial breath and answering to the star of the recluse. Refusing princes, you hide in cliffs and ravines, delighting in our culture of harmony and rejoicing in this age of martial virtue; yet you crossed mountain paths to visit the capital. For more than ten days we received you, and the benefit was mostly ours. White clouds briefly rested at court; fine rank cannot bind the man of attainment.
entries.literal: Before long he granted him a letter: "Imperial order to Chen Tuan: We hold that you have loftily withdrawn from the human realm and dwell with heart beyond things, nurturing the breath of great primordial nature and answering to the star of the Recluse of Shaowei. Having refused to bow to princes and lords, you gladly hide in cliffs and ravines, delighting in our culture of central harmony and rejoicing in the age when martial virtue descends; yet you could traverse mountain paths and come briefly to the capital. For more than ten days we received you, and the great benefit was mostly ours. White clouds briefly rested in the imperial domain; fine rank cannot bind the man of attainment.

entries.zh: 昔唐堯之至聖，有巢、許為外臣，朕雖寡薄，庶遵前鑒。
entries.en: Of old the sage Yao had Youchao and Xu as ministers beyond the court; We, though meager, would follow that example.
entries.literal: Of old the utmost sage Yao of Tang had Youchao and Xu as outer ministers; We, though meager, would follow that earlier mirror.

entries.zh: 恐山中所闕，已令華州刺史每事供須。
entries.en: Fearing want in the mountains, We have ordered the prefect of Huazhou to supply your every need.
entries.literal: Fearing want in the mountains, We have ordered the Huazhou prefect to supply your every need.

entries.zh: 乍反故山，履茲春序，緬懷高尚，當適所宜，故茲撫問，想宜知悉。」
entries.en: Having returned to your mountain in this spring season, We think fondly of your lofty withdrawal, which suits you well; therefore We send this greeting—may you know Our mind."
entries.literal: Having suddenly returned to your old mountain, treading this spring season, We think fondly of your lofty withdrawal, which should suit you well; therefore We send this inquiry of care—may you know Our mind."

entries.zh: 即陶穀之詞也。
entries.en: These were the words of Tao Gu.
entries.literal: These were the words of Tao Gu.

entries.zh: 初，摶之被召，嘗為詩一章云：「草澤吾皇詔，圖南摶姓陳。
entries.en: When Tuan was first summoned, he composed a poem: "From the wilds comes Our Emperor's edict; plotting southward is Chen surnamed Tuan.
entries.literal: When Tuan was first summoned, he once composed a poem that said: "From the wilds and marshes comes Our Emperor's edict; plotting southward is Chen surnamed Tuan.

entries.zh: 三峰十年客，四海一閑人。
entries.en: A guest of the three peaks for ten years, one idle man under all heaven.
entries.literal: A guest of the three peaks for ten years, one idle man in the four seas.

entries.zh: 世態從來薄，詩情自得真。
entries.en: The world's ways have ever been shallow; in poetry feeling finds its truth.
entries.literal: The world's ways have ever been shallow; in poetry feeling finds its truth.

entries.zh: 超然居物外，何必使為臣。」
entries.en: Transcendent, dwelling beyond things—why must one serve as minister?"
entries.literal: Transcendent, dwelling beyond things—why must one serve as minister?"

entries.zh: 好事者欣然謂之答詔詩。
entries.en: Those fond of such things gladly called it his poem in reply to the edict.
entries.literal: Those fond of such things gladly called it his poem in reply to the edict.

entries.zh: 世宗以張昭遠好古直，甚重之，因問曰：「朕欲一賢相，卿試為言朝廷誰可。」
entries.en: Shizong greatly valued Zhang Zhaoyuan for his love of antiquity and upright character and asked: "I want a worthy grand councilor. Tell me who in court will serve."
entries.literal: Shizong, because Zhang Zhaoyuan loved antiquity and was upright, greatly valued him and asked: "I desire one worthy grand councilor. Try telling me who in court will do."

entries.zh: 昭遠對曰：「以臣所見，莫若李濤。」
entries.en: Zhaoyuan replied: "In my view, none is better than Li Tao."
entries.literal: Zhaoyuan replied: "In my view, none is better than Li Tao."

entries.zh: 世宗常薄濤之為人，聞昭遠之舉甚驚，曰：「李濤本非重厚，朕以為無大臣體，卿首舉此何也？」
entries.en: Shizong had always disdained Tao's character; hearing the recommendation he was surprised and said: "Li Tao is not grave by nature; I consider him without the bearing of a great minister. Why recommend him first?"
entries.literal: Shizong had always held Tao's character in low esteem; hearing Zhaoyuan's recommendation he was greatly surprised and said: "Li Tao is by nature not grave and weighty; I consider him without the bearing of a great minister. Why do you first recommend this man?"

entries.zh: 昭遠曰：「陛下所聞止名行，曾不問才略如何耳。
entries.en: Zhaoyuan said: "What Your Majesty has heard concerns only reputation and conduct; you have never asked about his talent and strategy.
entries.literal: Zhaoyuan said: "What Your Majesty has heard concerns only reputation and conduct; you have never asked what his talent and strategy are like.

entries.zh: 且濤事晉高祖，曾上疏論邠州節度使張彥澤蓄無君心，宜早圖之，不然則為國患。
entries.en: Moreover, Tao served Gaozu of Later Jin and once memorialized that Zhang Yanzhe, military commissioner of Bin, harbored disloyal intent and should be dealt with early, or he would become a national calamity.
entries.literal: Moreover, Tao served Gaozu of Jin and once submitted a memorial arguing that Bin Prefecture Military Commissioner Zhang Yanzhe harbored a heart without regard for his lord and should be dealt with early; otherwise he would become a national calamity.

entries.zh: 晉祖不納，其後契丹南侵，彥澤果有中渡之變，晉社殲焉。
entries.en: Gaozu did not accept it; afterward the Khitan invaded south, Yanzhe brought about the disaster at Zhongdu, and the Jin state perished.
entries.literal: Jin Gaozu did not accept it; afterward the Khitan invaded south, and Yanzhe indeed brought about the Zhongdu catastrophe, and the Jin state perished.

entries.zh: 先帝潛龍時，亦上疏請解其兵權，以備非常之變，少主不納，未幾先帝遂有天下。
entries.en: When Taizu was still in obscurity, Tao also memorialized to strip him of military authority against extraordinary change; the young lord did not accept it, and before long Taizu possessed the realm.
entries.literal: When the late emperor was still in obscurity, he too submitted a memorial asking that military authority be removed to guard against extraordinary change; the young lord did not accept it, and before long the late emperor came to possess the realm.

entries.zh: 以國家安危未兆間，濤已先見，非賢而何？
entries.en: When the state's safety and peril gave no sign, Tao had already foreseen—if that is not worthiness, what is?
entries.literal: At a time when the state's safety and peril gave no sign, Tao had already foreseen—if not worthy, what then?

entries.zh: 臣所以首舉之者，正為此也。」
entries.en: That is precisely why I recommended him first."
entries.literal: The reason your servant first recommended him is precisely this."

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「今卿言甚公，然此人終不可於中書安置。」
entries.en: Shizong said: "What you say is fair, yet this man can never be placed in the Secretariat."
entries.literal: Shizong said: "What you say now is very fair, yet this man can in the end not be placed in the Secretariat."

entries.zh: 居無何，濤亦卒。
entries.en: Before long Tao also died.
entries.literal: Before long Tao also died.

entries.zh: 濤為人不拘禮法，與弟浣雖甚雍睦，然聚語之際，不典之言，往往間作。
entries.en: Tao did not bind himself to ritual propriety. Though very close to his younger brother Huan, when they gathered to talk, unseemly words often slipped in.
entries.literal: Tao as a man did not bind himself to ritual law. With his younger brother Huan he was very harmonious, yet when they gathered to speak, uncanonical words often slipped in.

entries.zh: 浣娶禮部尚書竇寧固之女，年甲稍高，成婚之夕，竇女出參，濤輒望塵下拜，浣驚曰：「大哥風狂耶？
entries.en: Huan married the daughter of Dou Ninggu, minister of rites, who was somewhat advanced in years. On the wedding night, when the bride came out to pay respects, Tao bowed low in the dust. Huan cried: "Elder brother, are you mad?
entries.literal: Huan married the daughter of Minister of Rites Dou Ninggu, who was somewhat advanced in years. On the wedding night, when the Dou girl came out to pay respects, Tao at once bowed in the dust. Huan cried in alarm: "Elder brother, are you mad?

entries.zh: 新婦參阿伯，豈有答禮儀！」
entries.en: When a new bride pays respects to her husband's elder brother, is there any ritual of reply!"
entries.literal: When a new bride pays respects to her husband's elder brother, is there any ritual of reply!"

entries.zh: 濤應曰：「我不風，只將謂是親家母。」
entries.en: Tao replied: "I am not mad—I took her for my mother-in-law."
entries.literal: Tao replied: "I am not mad—I took her for my mother-in-law."

entries.zh: 浣且漸且怒。
entries.en: Huan was both ashamed and angry.
entries.literal: Huan was both ashamed and angry.

entries.zh: 既坐，竇氏復拜，濤又叉手當胸，作歇後語曰：「慚無竇建，繆作梁山，喏喏喏！」
entries.en: When they were seated, the Dou woman bowed again; Tao clasped his hands at his chest and made a rhyming quip: "Ashamed to lack Dou Jian, wrongly playing Liangshan—yes, yes, yes!"
entries.literal: When they were seated, the Dou woman bowed again; Tao again clasped his hands at his chest and made a postpositional quip: "Ashamed to lack Dou Jian, wrongly playing Liangshan—yes, yes, yes!"

entries.zh: 時聞者莫不絕倒。
entries.en: Those who heard it all collapsed with laughter.
entries.literal: Those who heard it all collapsed with laughter.

entries.zh: 凡濤於閨門之內，不存禮法也如此，世宗以為無大臣體，不復任用，宜哉！
entries.en: Such was Tao's disregard for propriety even within the family; that Shizong held him unfit for high office and did not employ him again was fitting!
entries.literal: In all such ways Tao within the inner quarters did not preserve ritual law; that Shizong held him without the bearing of a great minister and did not employ him again was fitting!

entries.zh: 世宗志在四方，常恐運祚速而功業不就，以王樸精究術數，一旦從容問之曰：「朕當得幾年？」
entries.en: Shizong's ambition lay in the four quarters; he often feared his allotted years would pass before his work was done. Because Wang Pu was expert in divination, one day he asked him casually: "How many years shall I have?"
entries.literal: Shizong's ambition lay in the four quarters; he often feared that fortune would pass swiftly and his achievements not be completed. Because Wang Pu was expert in numbers and fate, one day he asked him at ease: "How many years shall I have?"

entries.zh: 對曰「陛下用心，以蒼生為念，天高聽卑，自當蒙福。
entries.en: He replied: "Your Majesty's heart is set on the people; Heaven is high yet hears the lowly—you will surely be blessed.
entries.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty's heart is set on the common people; Heaven is high yet hears the lowly—you will surely receive blessing.

entries.zh: 臣固陋，輒以所學推之，三十年後非所知也。」
entries.en: I am crude and dull; applying what I have learned, what lies beyond thirty years I cannot tell."
entries.literal: Your servant is crude and dull; rashly applying what I have learned to infer, what lies beyond thirty years is not known to me."

entries.zh: 世宗喜曰：「若如卿言，寡人當以十年開拓天下，十年養百姓，十年致太平足矣。」
entries.en: Shizong rejoiced and said: "If it is as you say, I shall use ten years to conquer the realm, ten years to nurture the people, and ten years to bring great peace—that will suffice."
entries.literal: Shizong rejoiced and said: "If it is as you say, I shall use ten years to open and expand the realm, ten years to nurture the people, and ten years to bring great peace—that will suffice."

entries.zh: 其後自瓦橋關回戈，未到關而晏駕，計在位止及五年餘六個月，五六乃三十之成數也，蓋樸婉而言之。
entries.en: Afterward, turning back from Waqiao Pass, he died before reaching it. His reign amounted to only five years and six months—five and six make thirty; Pu had spoken euphemistically.
entries.literal: Afterward, turning back from Waqiao Pass, before reaching the pass he died on the journey. Counting his time on the throne, it amounted to only five years and a little more than six months—five and six are the product of thirty; thus Pu had spoken euphemistically.

entries.zh: 世宗末年，大舉以取幽州，契丹聞其親征，君臣恐懼，沿邊城壘皆望風而下，凡蕃部之在幽州者，亦連宵遁去。
entries.en: In Shizong's last years he launched a great campaign against Youzhou. The Khitan, hearing he was campaigning in person, were terrified; border fortresses submitted at sight, and tribal groups at Youzhou fled overnight.
entries.literal: In Shizong's last years he launched a great campaign to take Youzhou. The Khitan, hearing that he was campaigning in person, were fearful in court and country; border fortresses all submitted at the mere sight of the army, and all tribal groups at Youzhou fled by night as well.

entries.zh: 車駕至瓦橋關，探邏是實，甚喜，以為大勛必集，登高阜，因以觀六師。
entries.en: The imperial procession reached Waqiao Pass; scouts confirmed the reports, and he rejoiced, thinking great triumph was at hand. He ascended a high mound to review the armies.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage reached Waqiao Pass; scouts confirmed it was true, and he rejoiced greatly, thinking great merit would surely be gathered. He ascended a high mound and thereupon reviewed the six armies.

entries.zh: 頃之，有父老百餘輩持牛酒以獻，世宗問曰：「此地何名？」
entries.en: Before long more than a hundred elders came with oxen and wine. Shizong asked: "What is this place called?"
entries.literal: Before long more than a hundred elders came bearing oxen and wine as gifts. Shizong asked: "What is this place called?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「歷世相傳，謂之病龍臺。」
entries.en: They replied: "From age to age it has been called Sick Dragon Terrace."
entries.literal: They replied: "From age to age it has been handed down that it is called Sick Dragon Terrace."

entries.zh: 默然，遽上馬馳去。
entries.en: He fell silent, mounted at once, and galloped away.
entries.literal: He fell silent, mounted his horse at once, and galloped away.

entries.zh: 是夜，聖體不豫，翌日病亟，有詔回戈，未到關而晏駕。
entries.en: That night he fell ill; the next day his illness grew acute. An edict ordered the army to turn back; before reaching the pass he died.
entries.literal: That night his sacred person was indisposed; the next day his illness was acute. An edict ordered the army to turn back; before reaching the pass he died on the journey.

entries.zh: 先是，世宗之在民間也，常夢神人以大傘見遺，色如郁金，加《道經》一卷，其後遂有天下。
entries.en: Earlier, while still a commoner, Shizong often dreamed that a divine man gave him a great umbrella colored like saffron, together with a volume of the Daoist Classic; afterward he came to possess the realm.
entries.literal: Earlier, while Shizong was among the people, he often dreamed that a divine man gave him a great umbrella colored like turmeric, together with one volume of the Daoist Classic; afterward he came to possess the realm.

entries.zh: 及瓦橋不豫之際，復夢向之神人來索傘與經，夢中還之而驚起，謂近侍曰：「吾夢不祥，豈非天命將去耶！」
entries.en: When he fell ill at Waqiao, he dreamed again that the divine man came to reclaim the umbrella and the classic; in the dream he returned them and woke in alarm, telling his attendants: "My dream is ill-omened—is Heaven's mandate about to depart!"
entries.literal: When he fell ill at Waqiao, he again dreamed that the former divine man came to demand back the umbrella and the classic; in the dream he returned them and started up in alarm, saying to his close attendants: "My dream is ill-omened—is not the Mandate of Heaven about to depart!"

entries.zh: 遂召大臣，戒以後事。
entries.en: He then summoned the great ministers and charged them regarding what was to follow.
entries.literal: He then summoned the great ministers and charged them regarding affairs to come.

entries.zh: 初，幽州聞車駕將至，父老或有竊議曰：「此不足憂。
entries.en: When Youzhou first heard the imperial procession was coming, some elders whispered: "This is not worth worry.
entries.literal: When Youzhou first heard that the imperial carriage was coming, some elders whispered among themselves: "This is not worth worry.

entries.zh: 且天子姓柴，幽州為燕，燕者亦煙火之謂也，此柴入火不利之兆，安得成功。」
entries.en: Moreover the emperor's surname is Chai; Youzhou is Yan, and yan also means flame—Chai entering fire is an ill omen; how could he succeed?"
entries.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven's surname is Chai; Youzhou is Yan, and yan also means smoke and fire—this is an omen of Chai entering fire, an ill sign; how could he succeed?"

entries.zh: 卒如其言。）〉
entries.en: In the end it was exactly as they said.)〉
entries.literal: In the end it was exactly as they said.)〉

entries.zh: 三月庚申，樞密使王樸卒。
entries.en: In the third month, on gengshen, Grand Councilor Wang Pu died.
entries.literal: In the third month, on gengshen, Grand Councilor Wang Pu died.

entries.zh: 甲子，詔以北境未復，取此月內幸滄州。
entries.en: On jiazi, an edict announced that because the northern frontier had not yet been recovered, the Emperor would visit Cangzhou before the month was out.
entries.literal: On jiazi, an edict stated that because the northern frontier had not yet been recovered, within this month he would visit Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 以宣徽南院使吳延祚為權東京留守，判開封府事；
entries.en: Wu Yanzuo, palace domestic commissioner of the southern court, was made acting regent of the Eastern Capital and assigned to administer Kaifeng;
entries.literal: Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Southern Court Wu Yanzuo was made acting regent of the Eastern Capital and assigned to judge Kaifeng prefectural affairs;

entries.zh: 以宣徽北院使昝居潤為副使；
entries.en: Zan Jurun of the northern court was named his deputy;
entries.literal: Palace Domestic Commissioner of the Northern Court Zan Jurun was made deputy;

entries.zh: 以三司使張美為大內都部署。
entries.en: Zhang Mei, commissioner of the three departments, was made chief deployer of the inner palace.
entries.literal: Commissioner of the Three Departments Zhang Mei was made chief deployer of the inner palace.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張美傳》：世宗北征，以美為大內都點檢。）〉
entries.en: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: on Shizong's northern campaign, Mei was made chief inspector of the inner palace.)〉
entries.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: when Shizong campaigned north, Mei was made chief inspector of the inner palace.)〉

entries.zh: 命諸將各領馬步諸軍及戰棹赴滄州。
entries.en: Each general was ordered to lead his cavalry, infantry, and war vessels to Cangzhou.
entries.literal: The generals were ordered each to lead cavalry and infantry units and war vessels to Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 己巳，濠州奏，鐘離縣饑民死者五百九十有四。
entries.en: On jisi, Haozhou reported that five hundred ninety-four people had died of famine in Zhongli County.
entries.literal: On jisi, Haozhou reported that in Zhongli County five hundred ninety-four starving people had died.

entries.zh: 癸酉，詔廢諸州銅魚。
entries.en: On guiyou, an edict abolished the bronze tally-fish used by prefectures.
entries.literal: On guiyou, an edict abolished the bronze tally-fish of all prefectures.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：顯德六年，敕諸道牧守，每遇除移，特降制書，何假符契，其請納銅魚，宜廢之。）〉
entries.en: (Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties: in the sixth year of Xiande, an order to circuit governors declared that on each appointment or transfer a special edict is issued—what need for tally tokens? The requirement of bronze tally-fish should be abolished.)〉
entries.literal: (Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties: in the sixth year of Xiansi, an order to prefectural governors in all circuits stated that on each appointment or transfer a special edict is issued—what need is there for tally tokens? The practice of requiring bronze tally-fish should be abolished.)〉

entries.zh: 甲戌，車駕發京師。
entries.en: On jiaxu, the imperial procession left the capital.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, the imperial carriage departed the capital.

entries.zh: 顯德六年春正月丁未朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the first day of the first month of spring in the sixth year of Xiande, dingwei, the Emperor held audience in Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year's felicitations, with the ceremonial guard arrayed according to regulation.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Xiansi, on dingwei the first day of the first month of spring, the Emperor took the throne in Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations; the guard of honor followed the prescribed formation.

entries.zh: 壬子，高麗國王王昭遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On renzi, Wang Zhao, king of Goryeo, sent envoys bearing tribute goods.
entries.literal: On renzi, King Wang Zhao of Goryeo sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 己卯，以翰林學士、中書舍人申文炳為左散騎常侍。
entries.en: On jimao, Shen Wenbing, Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter, was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
entries.literal: On jimao, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Shen Wenbing was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

entries.zh: 辛酉，女真國遣使貢獻。
entries.en: On xinyou, the Jurchen sent envoys bearing tribute.
entries.literal: On xinyou, the Jurchen state sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 壬戌，青州奏，節度使、陳王安審琦為部曲所殺。
entries.en: On renxu, Qing Prefecture reported that An Shenqi, military commissioner and Prince of Chen, had been killed by his own troops.
entries.literal: On renxu, Qing Prefecture reported that Military Commissioner and Prince of Chen An Shenqi had been killed by his retainers.

entries.zh: 乙丑，賜諸將射於內鞠場。
entries.en: On yichou, the Emperor granted the generals an archery contest in the inner polo ground.
entries.literal: On yichou, the generals were granted archery in the inner polo ground.

entries.zh: 戊辰，幸迎春苑。
entries.en: On wuchen, the Emperor visited Yingchun Park.
entries.literal: On wuchen, he visited Yingchun Park.

entries.zh: 甲戌，詔：「每年新及第進士及諸科聞喜宴，宜令宣徽院指揮排比。」
entries.en: On jiaxu, an edict ordered: "Each year the celebratory banquet for newly passed jinshi and other examination graduates be arranged under the direction of the Palace Domestic Service."
entries.literal: On jiaxu, an edict stated: "Each year the celebratory banquet for newly passed jinshi and candidates of other examination categories should be arranged under the direction of the Palace Domestic Service."

entries.zh: 乙亥，詔：「禮部貢院今後及第舉人，依逐科等第定人數姓名，並所試文學奏聞，候敕下放榜」云。
entries.en: On yihai, a further edict declared: "Henceforth successful candidates at the Ministry of Rites examination compound must have their numbers and names set by rank within each category, with their examination essays reported to the throne; the list is to be posted only after imperial approval."
entries.literal: On yihai, an edict stated: "Henceforth successful candidates at the Ministry of Rites examination compound shall have their numbers and names fixed by rank within each category, together with their examination compositions reported to the throne, and the list shall be posted only after an imperial order."

entries.zh: 是月，樞密使王樸詳定雅樂十二律旋相為宮之法，並造律準，上之。
entries.en: That month, Grand Councilor Wang Pu completed a detailed scheme for the twelve pitches of court music and their cyclical modulation, fashioned pitch pipes to match, and presented them to the throne.
entries.literal: That month, Grand Councilor Wang Pu worked out in detail the method by which the twelve pitches of court music rotate to form the modes, and also made pitch pipes; he presented them.

entries.zh: 詔尚書省集百官詳議，亦以為可，語在《樂志》。
entries.en: The Secretariat was ordered to convene the officials for full discussion; they too approved the proposal. The details appear in the 《Treatise on Music》.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to assemble the officials for detailed deliberation; they too deemed it acceptable. The account is in the 《Treatise on Music》.

entries.zh: 五月乙巳朔，帝駐蹕於瓦橋關。
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month, yisi, the Emperor halted at Waqiao Pass.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi the first day of the month, the Emperor halted the imperial procession at Waqiao Pass.

entries.zh: 侍衛親軍都指揮使李重進及諸將相繼至行在，瀛州刺史高彥暉以本城歸順。
entries.en: Li Chongjin, director of the palace guards, and the other generals reached the temporary court in turn, and Gao Yanhui, prefect of Ying, submitted his city.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Guards Li Chongjin and the generals arrived at the temporary court in succession; Ying Prefecture prefect Gao Yanhui submitted his city in allegiance.

entries.zh: 關南平，凡得州三、縣十七、戶一萬八千三百六十。
entries.en: The region south of the passes was pacified, yielding three prefectures, seventeen counties, and eighteen thousand three hundred sixty households.
entries.literal: The region south of the passes was pacified; in all three prefectures, seventeen counties, and eighteen thousand three hundred sixty households were gained.

entries.zh: 是役也，王師數萬，不亡一矢，邊界城邑皆望風而下。
entries.en: In this campaign the imperial armies, tens of thousands strong, did not lose a single man to enemy fire; every border town submitted at the first sight of the banners.
entries.literal: In this campaign the imperial armies numbered tens of thousands yet did not lose a single arrow; border cities and towns all submitted at the mere sight of the army.

entries.zh: 丙午，帝與諸將議攻幽州，諸將皆以為未可，帝不聽。
entries.en: On bingwu, the Emperor consulted the generals about attacking Youzhou; they all urged that the time was not right, but he would not heed them.
entries.literal: On bingwu, the Emperor discussed with the generals an attack on Youzhou; the generals all held that it was not yet feasible, but the Emperor would not listen.

entries.zh: 是夜，帝不豫，乃止。
entries.en: That night the Emperor fell ill, and the attack was called off.
entries.literal: That night the Emperor fell ill, and the plan was halted.

entries.zh: 戊申，定州節度使孫行友奏，攻下易州，擒偽命刺史李在欽來獻，斬於軍市。
entries.en: On wushen, Sun Xingyou, military commissioner of Dingzhou, reported the capture of Yi Prefecture; the Northern Han-appointed prefect Li Zaiqin was taken and presented, then beheaded in the army market.
entries.literal: On wushen, Dingzhou Military Commissioner Sun Xingyou memorialized that Yi Prefecture had been taken, the Northern Han-appointed prefect Li Zaiqin captured and presented, and beheaded in the army market.

entries.zh: 己酉，以瓦橋關為雄州，
entries.en: On jiyou, Waqiao Pass was established as Xiong Prefecture,
entries.literal: On jiyou, Waqiao Pass was made Xiong Prefecture,

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·陳思讓傳》：得瓦橋關為雄州，命思讓為都部署，率兵戍守。）〉
entries.en: (History of Song, Biography of Chen Sirang: Waqiao Pass was made Xiong Prefecture; Sirang was appointed chief deployer to garrison it with troops.)〉
entries.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Chen Sirang: Waqiao Pass was taken and made Xiong Prefecture; Sirang was ordered as chief deployer to lead troops to garrison it.)〉

entries.zh: 以益津關為霸州。
entries.en: Yijin Pass was established as Ba Prefecture.
entries.literal: Yijin Pass was made Ba Prefecture.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·韓令坤傳》：為霸州都部署，率所部兵戍之。）〉
entries.en: (History of Song, Biography of Han Lingkun: he was made chief deployer of Ba and led his troops to garrison it.)〉
entries.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Han Lingkun: he was made chief deployer of Ba Prefecture and led his troops to garrison it.)〉

entries.zh: 是日，先鋒都指揮使張藏英破契丹數百騎於瓦橋關北，攻下固安縣。
entries.en: That day, Vanguard Director Zhang Zangying routed several hundred Khitan cavalry north of Waqiao Pass and captured Gu'an County.
entries.literal: That day, Vanguard Director Zhang Zangying routed several hundred Khitan horsemen north of Waqiao Pass and took Gu'an County.

entries.zh: 詔發濱、棣二州丁夫城霸州。
entries.en: Corvée laborers from Bin and Di were mobilized to build fortifications at Ba Prefecture.
entries.literal: An edict mobilized corvée laborers from Bin and Di prefectures to fortify Ba Prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚戌，遣侍衛都指揮使李重進率兵出土門，入河東界。
entries.en: On gengxu, Li Chongjin, director of the palace guards, was dispatched through Tumen Pass into the Hedong frontier.
entries.literal: On gengxu, Palace Guard Director Li Chongjin was sent to lead troops out through Tumen Pass into the Hedong frontier.

entries.zh: 壬子，車駕發雄州，還京。
entries.en: On renzi, the imperial procession left Xiong Prefecture for the capital.
entries.literal: On renzi, the imperial carriage departed Xiong Prefecture and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 泉州節度使劉從效遣別駕王禹錫奉貢於行在，帝以泉州比臣江南，李景方歸奉國家，不欲奪其所屬，但錫詔褒美而已。
entries.en: Liu Congxiao of Quanzhou sent Vice Prefect Wang Yuxi with tribute to the temporary court. The Emperor judged that Quanzhou stood in the same relation as a Jiangnan subject, and since Li Jing had only just returned to allegiance, he did not wish to seize another's domain and merely issued an edict of commendation.
entries.literal: Quanzhou Military Commissioner Liu Congxiao sent Vice Prefect Wang Yuxi to present tribute at the temporary court. The Emperor held that Quanzhou was comparable to a subject of Jiangnan, and Li Jing had just returned to allegiance to the state; he did not wish to seize what belonged to another and merely granted an edict of praise.

entries.zh: 丁卯，西京奏，太常卿致仕司徒詡卒。
entries.en: On dingmao, the Western Capital reported the death of the retired director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Situ Xu.
entries.literal: On dingmao, the Western Capital reported that retired Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Situ Xu had died.

entries.zh: 己巳，侍衛都指揮使李重進奏，破河東賊軍於百井，斬首二千級。
entries.en: On jisi, Li Chongjin reported a victory over the Hedong rebels at Baijing with two thousand enemy heads taken.
entries.literal: On jisi, Palace Guard Director Li Chongjin memorialized that he had defeated the Hedong rebel army at Baijing, taking two thousand heads.

entries.zh: 甲戌，上至自雄州。
entries.en: On jiaxu, the Emperor returned from Xiong Prefecture.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, the Emperor returned from Xiong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 〈（《卻掃編》：周世宗既定三關，遇疾而退，至澶淵遲留不行，雖宰輔近臣問疾者皆莫得見，中外洶懼。
entries.en: (Retreat and Sweep: after Shizong secured the three passes he fell ill and withdrew; at Chanyuan he lingered and would not move on. Grand councilors and close ministers who came to inquire after his health were none of them admitted, and alarm spread through court and country.
entries.literal: (Que sao bian: after Zhou Shizong had secured the three passes he fell ill and withdrew; at Chanyuan he lingered and would not proceed. Though grand councilors and close ministers came to inquire after his health, none could see him, and court and country were in alarm.

entries.zh: 時張永德為澶州節度使，永德尚周太祖之女，以親故，獨得至臥內，於是群臣因永德言曰：「天下未定，根本空虛，四方諸侯惟幸京師之有變。
entries.en: Zhang Yongde was then military commissioner of Chanzhou; having married a daughter of Taizu of Zhou, he alone was admitted to the sickroom by reason of kinship. The officials therefore spoke through Yongde: "The realm is not yet settled and the capital lies exposed; the regional lords all hope for upheaval in the capital.
entries.literal: At that time Zhang Yongde was military commissioner of Cangzhou; Yongde had married a daughter of Zhou Taizu, and by reason of kinship alone was admitted to the sickroom. Thereupon the officials spoke through Yongde, saying: "The realm is not yet settled; the foundation is empty; the feudatories in the four quarters only hope for trouble in the capital.

entries.zh: 今澶、汴相去甚邇，不速歸以安人情，顧憚旦夕之勞而遲回於此，如有不可諱，奈宗廟何！」
entries.en: Chan and Bian are very near; if you do not return at once to steady men's hearts but linger here for fear of a day's travel, and the worst should befall—what of the imperial altars!"
entries.literal: Now Cang and Bian are very close; if you do not return swiftly to reassure men's hearts but hesitate here for fear of a day's fatigue, and if the worst should come—what of the imperial altars!"

entries.zh: 永德然之，乘間為世宗言如群臣旨，世宗問：「誰使汝為此言？」
entries.en: Yongde agreed and at an opportune moment relayed the officials' plea to Shizong. Shizong asked, "Who put you up to this?"
entries.literal: Yongde agreed and seized an opportunity to speak to Shizong as the officials wished. Shizong asked: "Who told you to say this?"

entries.zh: 永德對以群臣之意皆願為此，世宗熟思久之，嘆曰：「吾固知汝必為人所教，獨不喻吾意哉！
entries.en: Yongde replied that all the officials wished it. Shizong thought long and sighed: "I knew someone had coached you—you alone fail to grasp what I mean!
entries.literal: Yongde replied that all the officials wished this. Shizong pondered long and sighed: "I knew all along that someone must have coached you—you alone fail to grasp my intent!

entries.zh: 然觀汝之窮薄，惡足當此！」
entries.en: Yet look at your meager means—how could you be fit for such a role!"
entries.literal: Yet looking at your paltry resources, how could you be equal to this!"

entries.zh: 即日趣駕歸京師。）〉
entries.en: That same day he hastened the imperial procession back to the capital.)〉
entries.literal: That same day he hastened the imperial carriage back to the capital.)〉

entries.zh: 夏四月辛卯，車駕次滄州，以前左諫議大夫薛居正為刑部侍郎。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on xinmao, the imperial procession halted at Cangzhou, and former Left Remonstrance and Policy Adviser Xue Juzheng was appointed vice minister of justice.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on xinmao, the imperial carriage halted at Cangzhou; former Left Remonstrance and Policy Adviser Xue Juzheng was made Vice Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 是日，帝率諸軍北征。
entries.en: That same day the Emperor led the armies north.
entries.literal: That day, the Emperor led the armies on the northern campaign.

entries.zh: 壬辰，至乾寧軍，偽寧州刺史王洪以城降。
entries.en: On renchen, the army reached Qianning Army, and Wang Hong, the Liao-appointed prefect of Ningzhou, surrendered the city.
entries.literal: On renchen, he reached Qianning Army; the Northern Han-appointed prefect of Ningzhou, Wang Hong, surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 丁酉，駕御龍舟，率舟師順流而北，首尾數十里。
entries.en: On dingyou, the Emperor boarded his dragon boat and led the fleet downstream; the column stretched bow to stern for several tens of li.
entries.literal: On dingyou, he boarded the dragon boat and led the fleet downstream to the north; bow to stern the line stretched several tens of li.

entries.zh: 辛丑，至益津關。
entries.en: On xinchou, the army reached Yijin Pass.
entries.literal: On xinchou, he reached Yijin Pass.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：至益津關，契丹守將終廷暉以城降。）〉
entries.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: at Yijin Pass, the Khitan garrison commander Zhong Tinghui surrendered the city.)〉
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: at Yijin Pass, the Khitan garrison commander Zhong Tinghui surrendered the city.)〉

entries.zh: 自此以西，水路漸隘，舟師難進，乃舍舟登陸。
entries.en: West of this point the waterway narrowed and the fleet could not proceed, so the army abandoned the boats and marched overland.
entries.literal: From here westward the waterway gradually narrowed and the fleet could not advance; they therefore abandoned the boats and went ashore.

entries.zh: 壬寅，宿於野次。
entries.en: On renyin, the Emperor encamped in the open field.
entries.literal: On renyin, he lodged in an open camp.

entries.zh: 時帝先期而至，大軍未集，隨駕之士不及一旅，賴今上率材官騎士以衛乘輿。
entries.en: The Emperor had arrived ahead of the main army; those with the imperial train numbered less than a regiment. The present sovereign led the skilled cavalry to guard the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: At that time the Emperor had arrived ahead of schedule; the main army had not yet assembled, and those accompanying him did not amount to a full regiment. It was thanks to the present sovereign leading the skilled cavalry officers to guard the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 癸卯，今上先至瓦橋關，偽守將姚內斌以城降。
entries.en: On guimao, the present sovereign reached Waqiao Pass first, and the Khitan garrison commander Yao Neibin surrendered the city.
entries.literal: On guimao, the present sovereign reached Waqiao Pass first; the Northern Han garrison commander Yao Neibin surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 〈（《隆平集》：姚內斌，平州人也。
entries.en: (Longping Collection: Yao Neibin was a native of Ping Prefecture.
entries.literal: (Longping Collection: Yao Neibin was a native of Ping Prefecture.

entries.zh: 世宗北征，將兵至瓦橋關，內斌為關使，開門請降，世宗以為汝州刺史。）〉
entries.en: When Shizong campaigned north and brought troops to Waqiao Pass, Neibin was pass commander; he opened the gate and offered surrender, and Shizong appointed him prefect of Ru.)〉
entries.literal: When Shizong campaigned north and led troops to Waqiao Pass, Neibin was pass commander; he opened the gate and requested surrender, and Shizong made him prefect of Ru.)〉

entries.zh: 甲辰，鄚州刺史劉楚信以州來降。
entries.en: On jiachen, Liu Chuxin, prefect of Mo, surrendered his prefecture.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Mo Prefecture prefect Liu Chuxin surrendered the prefecture.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：世宗頃在仄微，尤務韜晦，及天命有屬，嗣守鴻業，不日破高平之陣，逾年復秦、鳳之封，江北、燕南，取之如拾芥，神武雄略，乃一代之英主也。
entries.en: The historian writes: Shizong was lately in obscurity and practiced concealment; when Heaven's mandate fell to him, he inherited the great enterprise. Within days he broke the Gaoping line; within a year he recovered Qin and Feng. North of the Yangzi and south of Yan he took territory as one picks up mustard seeds. Divine in martial prowess and heroic in strategy, he was the heroic ruler of his age.
entries.literal: The historian says: Shizong was lately in low estate and especially practiced concealment; when Heaven's mandate was his, he succeeded to the great enterprise. Within days he broke the Gaoping line; within a year he recovered the territories of Qin and Feng. North of the Yangzi and south of Yan he took lands as one picks up mustard seeds. Divine in martial prowess and heroic in strategy, he was an heroic ruler of a generation.

entries.zh: 加以留心政事，朝夕不倦，摘伏辯奸，多得其理。
entries.en: Moreover he gave his mind to government, unwearied morning and evening; in exposing hidden wrongs and distinguishing treachery he usually got to the heart of the matter.
entries.literal: Moreover he gave his mind to government affairs, unwearied morning and evening; in exposing hidden wrongs and distinguishing treachery he often hit the right principle.

entries.zh: 臣下有過，必面折之，常言太祖養成二王之惡，以致君臣之義，不保其終，故帝駕馭豪傑，失則明言之，功則厚賞之，文武參用，莫不服其明而懷其恩也。
entries.en: When subordinates erred, he rebuked them to their faces. He often said that Taizu had nurtured the wickedness of the two princes, so that the bond between ruler and minister could not be preserved to the end. Therefore he controlled bold spirits: faults he named plainly, merit he rewarded richly; civil and military alike he employed, and all submitted to his clarity and cherished his grace.
entries.literal: When subordinates had faults, he always rebuked them to their faces. He often said that Taizu had nurtured the wickedness of the two princes, so that the righteousness between ruler and minister could not be preserved to the end. Therefore the Emperor controlled bold spirits: when they erred he spoke plainly, when they achieved merit he rewarded them richly; civil and military he employed together, and none failed to submit to his clarity and cherish his grace.

entries.zh: 所以仙去之日，遠近號慕。
entries.en: Therefore when he departed this life, near and far mourned him with cries of longing.
entries.literal: Therefore on the day he ascended as an immortal, near and far cried out in longing.

entries.zh: 然稟性傷於太察，用刑失於太峻，及事行之後，亦多自追悔。
entries.en: Yet his nature was marred by excessive keenness of perception, and his punishments erred on the side of severity; after the fact he often regretted them himself.
entries.literal: Yet his inborn nature suffered from excessive keenness of perception, and his use of punishments erred on the side of severity; after matters were carried out, he often regretted them himself.

entries.zh: 逮至末年，漸用寬典，知用兵之頻並，憫黎民之勞苦，蓋有意於康濟矣。
entries.en: In his last years he gradually employed lenient measures, knowing how frequent warfare had become and pitying the people's toil—he surely aimed at healing and relief.
entries.literal: By his last years he gradually employed lenient measures, knowing how frequent warfare had become and pitying the toil and suffering of the common people—he surely had in mind the aim of healing and relief.

entries.zh: 而降年不永，美誌不就，悲夫！
entries.en: Yet his years were cut short and his fine purpose unfulfilled—how lamentable!
entries.literal: Yet his allotted years were not long, and his fine purpose was not fulfilled—how lamentable!

entries.zh: 二月庚辰，發徐、宿、宋、單等州丁夫數萬浚汴河。
entries.en: In the second month, on gengchen, tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Xu, Su, Song, Shan, and other prefectures were mobilized to dredge the Bian Canal.
entries.literal: In the second month, on gengchen, tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Xu, Su, Song, Shan, and other prefectures were mobilized to dredge the Bian Canal.

entries.zh: 甲申，發滑、亳二州丁夫浚五丈河，東流於定陶，入於濟，以通青、鄆水運之路。
entries.en: On jiashen, corvée laborers from Hua and Bo were set to dredge the Wuzhang River so that it would run east through Dingtao into the Ji, opening the water route to Qing and Yun.
entries.literal: On jiashen, corvée laborers from Hua and Bo prefectures were mobilized to dredge the Wuzhang River, which was to flow east at Dingtao and enter the Ji, thereby opening the water transport route to Qing and Yun.

entries.zh: 又疏導蔡河，以通陳、潁水運之路。
entries.en: The Cai River was also cleared and channeled to open transport routes to Chen and Ying.
entries.literal: The Cai River was also dredged and guided to open the water transport route to Chen and Ying.

entries.zh: 乙酉，詔諸道應差攝官各支半俸。
entries.en: On yiyou, an edict directed that acting appointees in every circuit were to receive half pay.
entries.literal: On yiyou, an edict ordered that acting appointees in all circuits should each receive half salary.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以翰林學士承旨、尚書兵部侍郎陶穀為尚書吏部侍郎充職。
entries.en: On bingxu, Tao Gu, Hanlin academician-in-chief and vice minister of war, was appointed vice minister of personnel to fill the post.
entries.literal: On bingxu, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Minister of War in the Secretariat Tao Gu was made Minister of Personnel in the Secretariat to fill the post.

entries.zh: 詔升湖州為節鎮，以宣德軍為軍額，以湖州刺史錢偡為本州節度使，從兩浙錢俶之請也。
entries.en: Huzhou was promoted to a full military commission under the army name Xuande, and its prefect Qian Yi was made military commissioner, at the request of Qian Chu of the Two Zhes.
