entries.literal: An edict promoted Huzhou to a military commission, taking Xuande Army as the army designation, and made Huzhou prefect Qian Yi military commissioner of that prefecture, acceding to the request of Qian Chu of the Two Zhes.

entries.zh: 辛丑，幸迎春苑。
entries.en: On xinchou, the Emperor again visited Yingchun Park.
entries.literal: On xinchou, he visited Yingchun Park.

entries.zh: 甲辰，右補闕王德成謫授右贊善大夫，坐舉官不當也。
entries.en: On jiachen, Wang Decheng, Right Remonstrance Councillor, was demoted to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent for having recommended an unfit official.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Right Remonstrance Councillor Wang Decheng was demoted and appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, on the charge of improper recommendation of an official.

entries.zh: 詔賜諸道州府供用糧草有差。
entries.en: An edict granted grain and fodder for official use to prefectures throughout the circuits, with amounts set by rank.
entries.literal: An edict granted grain and fodder for supply use to prefectures in all circuits in varying amounts.

entries.zh: 恭帝，諱宗訓，世宗子也。
entries.en: Emperor Gong, whose personal name was Zongxun, was Shizong's son.
entries.literal: Emperor Gong, taboo name Zongxun, was the son of Shizong.

entries.zh: 廣順三年，歲在癸丑，八月四日，生於澶州之府第。
entries.en: In the third year of Guangshun (guichou), on the fourth day of the eighth month, he was born at the prefectural residence in Chanzhou.
entries.literal: In the third year of Guangshun, the year being guichou, on the fourth day of the eighth month, he was born at the official residence in Chanzhou.

entries.zh: 顯德六年六月癸未，制授特進左衛上將軍，封梁王，食邑三千戶，實封五百戶。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Xiande, on guiwei, he was ordered to receive Special Advancement and made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Liang with a nominal fief of three thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of five hundred.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande, on guiwei of the sixth month, by imperial order he was granted Special Advancement and General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Liang with a fief of three thousand households and an actual seal of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 癸巳，世宗崩。
entries.en: On guisi Shizong died.
entries.literal: On guisi, Shizong died.

entries.zh: 甲午，內出遺制，命帝柩前即皇帝位。
entries.en: On jiawu the late emperor's testament was read from within the palace, commanding the heir to take the throne before the coffin.
entries.literal: On jiawu, the late emperor's testament was issued from within the palace, ordering the Emperor to ascend the throne before the coffin.

entries.zh: 是日，群臣奉帝即位而退。
entries.en: That day the ministers presented him for enthronement and then withdrew.
entries.literal: That day the ministers presented the Emperor to ascend the throne, then withdrew.

entries.zh: 丁酉，北面兵馬都部署韓令坤奏，敗契丹五百騎於霸州北。
entries.en: On dingyou Han Lingkun, northern armies commissioner, reported defeating five hundred Khitan horsemen north of Bazhou.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Han Lingkun, Director-in-Chief of Northern Armies and Cavalry, memorialized that five hundred Khitan horsemen had been defeated north of Bazhou.

entries.zh: 戊戌，文武百僚、宰臣範質等上表請聽政，表三上，允之。
entries.en: On wuxu Fan Zhi and the civil and military officials submitted three memorials asking him to take up governance, and he assented.
entries.literal: On wuxu, the civil and military officials and chief minister Fan Zhi and others submitted a memorial requesting that he assume governance; they submitted three times, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 壬寅，文武臣僚上表，請以八月四日為天壽節，從之。
entries.en: On renyin the officials memorialized to make the fourth day of the eighth month the imperial birthday festival, and he agreed.
entries.literal: On renyin, civil and military officials submitted a memorial requesting that the fourth day of the eighth month be made the Birthday Festival; the request was accepted.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以司徒、平章事範質為山陵使，以翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼為禮儀使，以兵部尚書張昭為鹵簿使，以御史中丞邊歸讜為儀仗使，以宣徽南院使、判開封府事昝居潤為橋道頓遞使。
entries.en: On guimao Fan Zhi was named tomb commissioner; Hanlin academician Dou Yan, ritual commissioner; Minister of War Zhang Zhao, regalia commissioner; Vice Censor-in-Chief Bian Guichan, arms commissioner; and acting Kaifeng administrator Zan Jurun, bridges-and-relay commissioner.
entries.literal: On guimao, Fan Zhi, Minister of Education and Councilor of the Second Rank, was made commissioner for the imperial tomb; Dou Yan, Hanlin Academician and Administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made ritual commissioner; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, was made commissioner for the imperial regalia; Bian Guichan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was made commissioner for ceremonial arms; and Zan Jurun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Directorate and acting Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture, was made commissioner for bridges, roads, and relay stations.

entries.zh: 是月，州郡十六奏大雨連旬不止。
entries.en: That month sixteen prefectures reported unrelenting heavy rains for more than ten days.
entries.literal: That month, sixteen prefectures and commanderies reported that heavy rain had continued for more than ten days without stopping.

entries.zh: 秋七月丁未，以戶部尚書李濤為山陵副使，以度支郎中盧億為山陵判官。
entries.en: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn, Li Tao, Minister of Revenue, was made deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb and Lu Yi, bureau director of expenditures, judge for the tomb.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingwei, Li Tao, Minister of Revenue, was appointed deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb, and Lu Yi, bureau director of expenditures, was appointed judge for the imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 辛亥，左散騎常侍申文炳卒。
entries.en: On xinhai Shen Wenbing, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, died.
entries.literal: On xinhai, Shen Wenbing, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, died.

entries.zh: 乙卯，右拾遺徐雄奪三任官，坐誣奏雷澤縣令虛破戶也。
entries.en: On yimao Xu Xiong, Remonstrance Censor of the Right, was stripped of three ranks for falsely accusing the magistrate of Leize of fraudulently reducing registered households.
entries.literal: On yimao, Remonstrance Censor Xu Xiong was stripped of three ranks of office for falsely memorializing that the magistrate of Leize County had fraudulently reduced registered households.

entries.zh: 丁巳，百僚釋服。
entries.en: On dingsi the officials ended their mourning dress.
entries.literal: On dingsi, the hundred officials laid aside mourning dress.

entries.zh: 尚輦奉御金彥英，本高麗人也，奉使高麗，稱臣於其王，故及於罪。
entries.en: Jin Yanying of the Imperial Carriage, a native of Goryeo, was punished because on a mission home he had prostrated himself as subject to the Goryeo king.
entries.literal: Jin Yanying, Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, was originally a man of Goryeo; on a mission to Goryeo he declared himself subject to its king, and therefore incurred guilt.

entries.zh: 庚申，以邢州節度使王仁鎬為襄州節度使，進封開國公；
entries.en: On gengshen Wang Renhao of Xingzhou became Xiangzhou commissioner and was made Duke Who Opens the State;
entries.literal: On gengshen, Xingzhou military commissioner Wang Renhao was made Xiangzhou military commissioner and advanced to Duke Who Opens the State;

entries.zh: 以侍衛步軍都指揮使、曹州節度使、檢校太保袁彥為陜州節度使、加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Yuan Yan, director of the Palace Foot Guards and Caozhou commissioner, became Shanzhou commissioner with the added rank of acting Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: Yuan Yan, Director-in-Chief of the Palace Foot Guards, Caozhou military commissioner, and acting Grand Guardian, was made Shanzhou military commissioner and given acting Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以右羽林統軍、權知邢州事、檢校太保李繼勛為邢州節度使，加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Li Jixun, commander of the Right Forest Cavalry and acting Xingzhou administrator, became Xingzhou commissioner with acting Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: Li Jixun, Commander of the Right Forest of Cavalry, acting Xingzhou administrator, and acting Grand Guardian, was made Xingzhou military commissioner and given acting Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以滑州留後、檢校太保陳思讓為滄州節度使；
entries.en: Chen Sirang, acting Huazhou administrator, became Cangzhou commissioner;
entries.literal: Chen Sirang, acting Huazhou administrator and acting Grand Guardian, was made Cangzhou military commissioner;

entries.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使、陳州節度使、檢校太傅韓令坤為侍衛馬步都虞候，依前陳州節度使，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Han Lingkun, director of the Palace Horse Guards and Chenzhou commissioner, became deputy director of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, kept Chenzhou, and was given acting Grand Marshal;
entries.literal: Han Lingkun, Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse Guards, Chenzhou military commissioner, and acting Grand Tutor, was made Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, remaining Chenzhou military commissioner, and given acting Grand Marshal;

entries.zh: 以虎捷左廂都指揮使、岳州防禦使、檢校司徒高懷德為夔州節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保；
entries.en: Gao Huaide of the Tiger Swift Left Wing and Yuezhou became Kuizhou commissioner and director of the Palace Horse Guards with acting Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: Gao Huaide, Commander of the Left Wing of the Tiger Swift Guards, Yuezhou defense commissioner, and acting Minister of Education, was made Kuizhou military commissioner, filling the post of Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse Guards and acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以虎捷左廂都指揮使、常州防禦使、檢校司空張鐸為遂州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使、檢校太保，仍改名令鐸。
entries.en: Zhang Duo of the Tiger Swift Left Wing and Changzhou became Suizhou commissioner and director of the Palace Foot Guards with acting Grand Guardian, and was renamed Lingduo.
entries.literal: Zhang Duo, Commander of the Left Wing of the Tiger Swift Guards, Changzhou defense commissioner, and acting Minister of Works, was made Suizhou military commissioner, filling the post of Director-in-Chief of the Palace Foot Guards and acting Grand Guardian, and was further renamed Lingduo.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·張令鐸傳》云：本名鐸，以與河中張鐸同姓名，故賜今名。）〉
entries.en: (History of Song, Biography of Zhang Lingduo: his original name was Duo; because Zhang Duo of Hezhong shared the name, he was granted Lingduo.)〉
entries.literal: (The Biography of Zhang Lingduo in the History of Song states: his original name was Duo; because it was the same as Zhang Duo of Hezhong, he was granted his present name.)〉

entries.zh: 壬戌，以鄆州節度使、充侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、檢校太傅、兼侍中李重進為淮南節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中，依前侍衛馬步軍都指揮使；
entries.en: On renxu Li Chongjin of Yanzhou, director of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, became Huainan commissioner with acting Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant, keeping his guard command;
entries.literal: On renxu, Li Chongjin, Yanzhou military commissioner, Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, acting Grand Tutor, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Huainan military commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, remaining Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards;

entries.zh: 以襄州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事向拱為河南尹，充西京留守，加檢校太師、兼侍中；
entries.en: Xiang Gong of Xiangzhou, acting Grand Marshal and grand councilor, became Intendant of Henan and Western Capital regent with acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant;
entries.literal: Xiang Gong, Xiangzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, and Concurrent Grand Councilor, was made Intendant of Henan, filling the post of Western Capital regent, and given acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：向拱即向訓也，避恭帝名改焉。）〉
entries.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: Xiang Gong was Xiang Xun, renamed to avoid Emperor Gong's taboo.)〉
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Xiang Gong is Xiang Xun, renamed to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Gong.)〉

entries.zh: 以宋州節度使、充侍衛馬步軍副都指揮、檢校太尉、同平章事韓通為鄆州節度使，依前侍衛親軍馬步軍副都指揮使；
entries.en: Han Tong of Songzhou, deputy director of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, became Yanzhou commissioner while keeping his deputy guard command;
entries.literal: Han Tong, Songzhou military commissioner, Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, acting Grand Marshal, and Concurrent Grand Councilor, was made Yanzhou military commissioner, remaining Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Palace Personal Army Horse and Foot Guards;

entries.zh: 以澶州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事、附馬都尉張永德為許州節度使，進封開國公；
entries.en: Zhang Yongde of Chanzhou, imperial son-in-law and grand councilor, became Xuzhou commissioner and was made Duke Who Opens the State;
entries.literal: Zhang Yongde, Chanzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Imperial Son-in-Law, was made Xuzhou military commissioner and advanced to Duke Who Opens the State;

entries.zh: 以今上為宋州節度使，依前檢校太尉、殿前都點檢，進封開國侯；
entries.en: The present sovereign was made Songzhou commissioner, kept acting Grand Marshal and Director of the Palace Front, and was advanced to Marquis Who Opens the State;
entries.literal: The Present Lord was made Songzhou military commissioner, remaining acting Grand Marshal and Director of the Palace Front, and advanced to Marquis Who Opens the State;

entries.zh: 以淮南節度使兼殿前副都點檢、檢校太保慕容延釗為澶州節度使、檢校太傅，依前殿前副都點檢，進封開國伯；
entries.en: Murong Yanzhao of Huainan, deputy director of the Palace Front, became Chanzhou commissioner with acting Grand Tutor, kept his front-director post, and was made Earl Who Opens the State;
entries.literal: Murong Yanzhao, Huainan military commissioner, Concurrent Deputy Director of the Palace Front, and acting Grand Guardian, was made Chanzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Tutor, remaining Deputy Director of the Palace Front, and advanced to Earl Who Opens the State;

entries.zh: 以殿前都指揮使、江州防禦使、檢校司空石守信為滑州節度使、檢校太保，依前殿前都指揮使。
entries.en: Shi Shouxin, director of the Palace Front and Jiangzhou defense commissioner, became Huazhou commissioner with acting Grand Guardian while keeping command of the Palace Front.
entries.literal: Shi Shouxin, Director-in-Chief of the Palace Front, Jiangzhou defense commissioner, and acting Minister of Works, was made Huazhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian, remaining Director-in-Chief of the Palace Front.

entries.zh: 丙寅，制大赦天下。
entries.en: On bingyin a great amnesty was proclaimed for the realm.
entries.literal: On bingyin, an edict proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 庚午，翰林學士、判太常寺竇儼撰進大行皇帝太室歌酌獻辭，舞曰《定功之舞》，歌辭不錄。
entries.en: On gengwu Dou Yan, Hanlin academician and overseer of the Directorate of Ceremonies, presented the libation hymn for the late emperor's Grand Chamber offering, with the dance Establishing Merit; the lyrics are not recorded.
entries.literal: On gengwu, Dou Yan, Hanlin Academician and overseer of the Directorate of Ceremonies, drafted and presented the libation text for offering to the Grand Chamber of the late emperor, with the dance titled Dance of Establishing Merit; the song text is not recorded.

entries.zh: 是月，諸道相繼奏，大雨，所在川渠漲溢，漂溺廬舍，損害苗稼。
entries.en: That month circuits reported in turn that heavy rains had swollen rivers and canals everywhere, flooding homes and damaging crops.
entries.literal: That month, the various circuits reported in succession that heavy rain had caused rivers and canals everywhere to swell and overflow, drowning dwellings, and harming the grain in the fields.

entries.zh: 八月甲戌朔，以光祿卿致仕柴守禮為太子太保致仕。
entries.en: On the first day jiaxu of the eighth month, Chai Shouli, retired Director of the Imperial Household, was made retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day jiaxu, Chai Shouli, retired Director of the Imperial Household, was made retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 乙亥，翰林學士兼判太常寺竇儼撰進大行皇帝尊謚曰睿武孝文皇帝，廟號世宗，從之。
entries.en: On yihai Dou Yan presented the late emperor's posthumous title Sagacious Martial Filial Cultured Emperor and temple name Shizong; the court approved.
entries.literal: On yihai, Dou Yan, Hanlin Academician and Concurrent overseer of the Directorate of Ceremonies, drafted and presented the honorific posthumous title of the late emperor as Sagacious Martial Filial Cultured Emperor, with temple name Shizong; it was approved.

entries.zh: 庚辰，天下兵馬都元帥、守尚書令、兼中書令、吳越國王錢俶加食邑一千戶，實封四百戶，改賜功臣；
entries.en: On gengchen Qian Chu of Wuyue, commander-in-chief of all armies, received an added thousand fief households and four hundred enfeoffed households and a new meritorious-subject designation;
entries.literal: On gengchen, Qian Chu, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies and Horses under Heaven, Defender of the Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Secretariat Director, and King of Wuyue, was given an additional thousand households in his fief income and four hundred households in actual enfeoffment, and was granted a new designation of meritorious subject;

entries.zh: 天雄軍節度使、檢校太師、守太傅、兼中書令、魏王符彥卿加守太尉；
entries.en: Fu Yanqing of Tianxiong, Prince of Wei, was advanced to Defender of Grand Marshal;
entries.literal: Fu Yanqing, Tianxiong Army military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, Defender of Grand Tutor, Concurrent Secretariat Director, and Prince of Wei, was given Defender of Grand Marshal;

entries.zh: 夏州節度使、檢校太師、守太保、兼中書令、西平王李彜興加守太傅；
entries.en: Li Yixing of Xiazhou, Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Defender of Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: Li Yixing, Xiazhou military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, Defender of Grand Guardian, Concurrent Secretariat Director, and Prince of Xiping, was given Defender of Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 荊南節度使、檢校太師、守中書令、南平王高保融加守太保。
entries.en: Gao Baorong of Jingnan, Prince of Nanping, was advanced to Defender of Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Gao Baorong, Jingnan military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, Defender of Secretariat Director, and Prince of Nanping, was given Defender of Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 壬午，山陵使範質撰進大行皇帝陵名曰慶陵，從之。
entries.en: On renwu Fan Zhi, tomb commissioner, proposed Qingling as the late emperor's tomb name; the court approved.
entries.literal: On renwu, Fan Zhi, commissioner for the imperial tomb, drafted and presented the name of the late emperor's tomb as Qingling; it was approved.

entries.zh: 秦州節度使、西面沿邊都部署、檢校太師、守中書令、褒國公王景進封涼國公，徐州節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令郭從義加開府儀同三司，鄜州節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、邢國公武行德進封宋國公，永興軍節度使、檢校太師、兼侍中李洪義加開府儀同三司，鳳翔節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中郭崇加檢校太師，潞州節度使、檢校太傅、兼侍中李筠加檢校太尉，朗州節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中周行逢加檢校太師。
entries.en: Wang Jing of Qinzhou, Duke of Bao, was made Duke of Liang; Guo Congyi of Xuzhou received Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; Wu Xingde of Fuzhou, Duke of Xing, was made Duke of Song; Li Hongyi of Yongxing Army received the same grand-master honor; Guo Chong of Fengxiang was advanced to acting Grand Preceptor; Li Jun of Luzhou to acting Grand Marshal; and Zhou Xingfeng of Langzhou to acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Wang Jing, Qinzhou military commissioner, Western Frontier Commander-in-Chief, acting Grand Preceptor, Defender of Secretariat Director, and Duke of Bao, was advanced to Duke of Liang; Guo Congyi, Xuzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, and Concurrent Secretariat Director, was given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; Wu Xingde, Fuzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Secretariat Director, and Duke of Xing, was advanced to Duke of Song; Li Hongyi, Yongxing Army military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; Guo Chong, Fengxiang military commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was given acting Grand Preceptor; Li Jun, Luzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Tutor, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was given acting Grand Marshal; Zhou Xingfeng, Langzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Marshal, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was given acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 甲申，壽州節度使、檢校太師、同平章事、韓國公楊信封魯國公；
entries.en: On jiashen Yang Xin of Shouzhou, Duke of Han, was made Duke of Lu;
entries.literal: On jiashen, Yang Xin, Shouzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Duke of Han, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu;

entries.zh: 邠州節度使、檢校太師劉重進，廬州節度使、檢校太尉趙贊，鄧州節度使、檢校太尉宋延渥，並加開府儀同三司；
entries.en: Liu Chongjin of Binzhou, Zhao Zan of Luzhou, and Song Yanwo of Dengzhou all received Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon;
entries.literal: Liu Chongjin, Binzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Preceptor; Zhao Zan, Luzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Marshal; and Song Yanwo, Dengzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Marshal, were all given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon;

entries.zh: 涇州節度使、檢校太尉白重贊，河中節度使、檢校太尉張鐸，並加階爵。
entries.en: Bai Chongzan of Jingzhou and Zhang Duo of Hezhong were both advanced in noble rank.
entries.literal: Bai Chongzan, Jingzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Marshal, and Zhang Duo, Hezhong military commissioner and acting Grand Marshal, were both given higher noble ranks.

entries.zh: 丙戌，易定節度使孫行友、靈州節度使馮繼業、府州節度使折德扆，並自檢校太保加檢校太傅，進階爵。
entries.en: On bingxu Sun Xingyou of Yiding, Feng Jiye of Lingzhou, and Zhe Deyi of Fuzhou were all advanced from acting Grand Guardian to acting Grand Tutor and raised in noble rank.
entries.literal: On bingxu, Sun Xingyou, Yiding military commissioner; Feng Jiye, Lingzhou military commissioner; and Zhe Deyi, Fuzhou military commissioner, were all advanced from acting Grand Guardian to acting Grand Tutor and given higher noble ranks.

entries.zh: 以延州留後、檢校太傅李萬全為延州節度使，進封開國公。
entries.en: Li Wanquan, acting Yanzhou administrator, became Yanzhou commissioner and was made Duke Who Opens the State.
entries.literal: Li Wanquan, acting Yanzhou administrator and acting Grand Tutor, was made Yanzhou military commissioner and advanced to Duke Who Opens the State.

entries.zh: 庚寅，皇弟特進檢校太保、左驍衛上將軍、燕國公、食邑三千戶宗讓加檢校太傅，進封曹王，改名熙讓；
entries.en: On gengyin the emperor's younger brother Zongrang, Duke of Yan with three thousand fief households, was given acting Grand Tutor, made Prince of Cao, and renamed Xirang;
entries.literal: On gengyin, the imperial younger brother Zongrang, specially advanced, acting Grand Guardian, General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards, Duke of Yan, with a fief income of three thousand households, was given acting Grand Tutor, advanced to Prince of Cao, and renamed Xirang;

entries.zh: 熙謹拜光祿大夫、檢校太保、右武衛大將軍，封紀王，食邑三千戶；
entries.en: Xijin was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Grand Guardian, made great general of the Right Martial Guards and Prince of Ji with three thousand fief households;
entries.literal: Xijin was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Guardian, and Great General of the Right Martial Guards, enfeoffed as Prince of Ji with a fief income of three thousand households;

entries.zh: 皇弟熙誨拜金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、左領衛大將軍，封蘄王，食邑三千戶。
entries.en: The emperor's younger brother Xihui was appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and acting Minister of Education, made great general of the Left Leading Guards and Prince of Qi with three thousand fief households.
entries.literal: The imperial younger brother Xihui was appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Minister of Education, and Great General of the Left Leading Guards, enfeoffed as Prince of Qi with a fief income of three thousand households.

entries.zh: 制下，即令所司擇日備禮冊命。
entries.en: Once the edict was issued, the relevant offices were ordered at once to choose a day and prepare the investiture rites.
entries.literal: When the edict was issued, the relevant offices were at once ordered to choose a day and prepare the rites of investiture.

entries.zh: 以晉國長公主張氏為晉國大長公主；
entries.en: Lady Zhang, Princess of Jin, was advanced to Grand Princess of Jin;
entries.literal: Lady Zhang, Princess of Jin, was made Grand Princess of Jin;

entries.zh: 以前陜州節度使、檢校太尉藥元福為曹州節度使，進階爵。
entries.en: Yao Yuanfu, former Shanzhou commissioner, became Caozhou commissioner and was advanced in noble rank.
entries.literal: Yao Yuanfu, former Shanzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Marshal, was made Caozhou military commissioner and given a higher noble rank.

entries.zh: 甲午，守司徒、同平章事、宏文館大學士、參知樞密院事範質加開府儀同三司，進封蕭國公；
entries.en: On jiawu Fan Zhi, grand councilor and participant in military affairs, received Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and was made Duke of Xiao;
entries.literal: On jiawu, Fan Zhi, Defender of Minister of Education, Concurrent Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and Participant in the Bureau of Military Affairs, was given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and advanced to Duke of Xiao;

entries.zh: 門下侍郎兼禮部尚書、同平章事、監修國史、參知樞密院事王溥加右僕射，進封開國公；
entries.en: Wang Pu, vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor, was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke Who Opens the State;
entries.literal: Wang Pu, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Minister of Rites, Concurrent Grand Councilor, overseer of the compilation of the National History, and Participant in the Bureau of Military Affairs, was given Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced to Duke Who Opens the State;

entries.zh: 樞密使、中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士魏仁浦加兼刑部尚書，依前樞密使；
entries.en: Wei Renpu, military-affairs commissioner and grand councilor, was given concurrent Minister of Justice while keeping his military-affairs post;
entries.literal: Wei Renpu, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was given Concurrent Minister of Justice, remaining Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

entries.zh: 檢校太傅、右驍衛上將軍吳延祚依前樞密使，進封慶國公；
entries.en: Wu Yanzuo, acting Grand Tutor and general of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guards, kept his military-affairs commission and was made Duke of Qing;
entries.literal: Wu Yanzuo, acting Grand Tutor and General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guards, remained Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was advanced to Duke of Qing;

entries.zh: 以左武衛上將軍史牷為左金吾上將軍致仕。
entries.en: Shi Quan, general of the Left Martial Guards, was retired as general of the Left Golden Crow Guards.
entries.literal: Shi Quan, General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guards, was made retired General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Crow Guards.

entries.zh: 乙未，以隴州防禦使王全斌為相州留後。
entries.en: On yiwei Wang Quanbin of Longzhou was made acting Xiangzhou administrator.
entries.literal: On yiwei, Wang Quanbin, Longzhou defense commissioner, was made acting Xiangzhou administrator.

entries.zh: 戊戌，宣徽南院使、判開封府事昝居潤，宣徽北院使、判三司張美，並加檢校太傅。
entries.en: On wuxu Zan Jurun of the Southern Palace Secretariat and Zhang Mei of the Northern Palace Secretariat were both given acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: On wuxu, Zan Jurun, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and overseer of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs, and Zhang Mei, Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and overseer of the Three Offices, were both given acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 己亥，前司空李穀加開府儀同三司、趙國公，以前太傅、少卿朱渭為太僕卿致仕。
entries.en: On jihai Li Gu, former Minister of Works, received Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and was made Duke of Zhao; Zhu Wei, former grand tutor and vice director, was retired as Director of the Imperial Stud.
entries.literal: On jihai, Li Gu, former Minister of Works, was given Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and made Duke of Zhao; Zhu Wei, former Grand Tutor and vice director, was made retired Director of the Imperial Stud.

entries.zh: 辛丑，左金吾上將軍致仕史牷卒。
entries.en: On xinchou Shi Quan, retired general of the Left Golden Crow Guards, died.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Shi Quan, retired General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Crow Guards, died.

entries.zh: 壬寅，高麗國遣使朝貢，兼進《別序孝經》一卷、《越王孝經新義》一卷、《皇靈孝經》一卷、《孝經雌圖》三卷。
entries.en: On renyin Goryeo sent tribute envoys who also presented one scroll each of Separate Preface to the Classic of Filial Piety, New Meaning of the Yue King's Classic of Filial Piety, and Imperial Spirit Classic of Filial Piety, and three scrolls of the Yin Diagram of the Classic of Filial Piety.
entries.literal: On renyin, Goryeo sent envoys to offer tribute and also presented one scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety with a Separate Preface, one scroll of the New Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety of the King of Yue, one scroll of the Imperial Spirit Classic of Filial Piety, and three scrolls of the Yin Diagram of the Classic of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 〈（《文昌雜錄》云：《別序》者，記孔子所生及弟子從學之事。
entries.en: (Miscellaneous Records from Wenchang: Separate Preface records Confucius's birthplace and his disciples' studies.
entries.literal: (Miscellaneous Records from Wenchang states: Separate Preface records where Confucius was born and matters of disciples following him in study.

entries.zh: 《新義》者，以越王為問目，釋疏文之義。
entries.en: New Meaning uses the King of Yue as interlocutor to explain the commentary.
entries.literal: New Meaning takes the King of Yue as the questioner and explains the meaning of the commentary text.

entries.zh: 《皇靈》者，止說延年避災之事及符文，乃道書也。
entries.en: Imperial Spirit deals only with prolonging life, avoiding disaster, and talismanic writings—it is a Daoist text.
entries.literal: Imperial Spirit speaks only of prolonging life and avoiding calamity and of talismanic writings—it is a Daoist book.

entries.zh: 《雌圖》者，止說日之環暈、星之彗孛，亦非奇書。）〉
entries.en: Yin Diagram discusses only solar halos and comets—hardly a remarkable book either.)〉
entries.literal: Yin Diagram speaks only of solar halos and comets and broom-stars—it too is no remarkable book.)〉

entries.zh: 冬十月癸酉朔，以司農卿致仕李鍇為太僕卿致仕，太常少卿致仕姚遂為將作監致仕。
entries.en: On the first day guiyou of the tenth winter month, Li Kai, retired director of agriculture, was made retired director of the imperial stud, and Yao Sui, retired vice director of ceremonies, retired director of palace construction.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day guiyou, Li Kai, retired Director of Agriculture, was made retired Director of the Imperial Stud, and Yao Sui, retired Vice Director of Ceremonies, was made retired Director of Palace Construction.

entries.zh: 丁亥，太子太師薛懷讓封杞國公。
entries.en: On dinghai Xue Huairang, grand preceptor of the heir apparent, was made Duke of Qi.
entries.literal: On dinghai, Xue Huairang, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

entries.zh: 壬辰，翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼撰進貞惠皇后廟歌辭。
entries.en: On renchen Dou Yan, Hanlin academician and overseer of ceremonies, presented the temple hymn for Empress Zhenhui.
entries.literal: On renchen, Dou Yan, Hanlin Academician and overseer of the Directorate of Ceremonies, drafted and presented the temple hymn text for Empress Zhenhui.

entries.zh: 丁酉，世宗皇帝靈駕發引。
entries.en: On dingyou Emperor Shizong's coffin set out on the funeral procession.
entries.literal: On dingyou, the imperial coffin of Emperor Shizong set out on the funeral procession.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以前相州留後王暉為右神武統軍。
entries.en: Wang Hui, former acting Xiangzhou administrator, became commander of the Right Divine Martial Guards.
entries.literal: Wang Hui, former acting Xiangzhou administrator, was made Commander of the Right Divine Martial Guards.

entries.zh: 辛丑，江南國主李景來告，世子宏冀卒，遣禦廚使張延範充吊祭使。
entries.en: On xinchou Li Jing of Jiangnan reported the death of his heir Hongji; Zhang Yanfan of the Imperial Kitchen was sent as condolence envoy.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Li Jing, lord of Jiangnan, came to report that the heir Hongji had died; Zhang Yanfan, commissioner of the Imperial Kitchen, was sent as condolence envoy.

entries.zh: 十一月壬寅朔，葬世宗皇帝於慶陵，以貞惠皇后劉氏祔焉。
entries.en: On the first day renyin of the eleventh month Emperor Shizong was buried at Qingling, with Empress Zhenhui, Lady Liu, interred beside him.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day renyin, Emperor Shizong was buried at Qingling, with Empress Zhenhui, Lady Liu, joined in burial.

entries.zh: 戊申，西京奏，太子太師致仕白文珂卒。
entries.en: On wushen the Western Capital reported the death of Bai Wenke, retired grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: On wushen, the Western Capital reported that Bai Wenke, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, had died.

entries.zh: 丙辰，日南至，百僚奉表稱賀。
entries.en: On bingchen, the winter solstice, the officials presented congratulatory memorials.
entries.literal: On bingchen, at the winter solstice, the hundred officials presented memorials of congratulation.

entries.zh: 戊午，廢兗州廣利軍，依舊為萊蕪監。
entries.en: On wuwu the Guangli Army of Yanzhou was abolished and restored to the Laiwu directorate.
entries.literal: On wuwu, the Guangli Army of Yanzhou was abolished and restored as the Laiwu Directorate.

entries.zh: 壬戌，升鳳州固鎮為雄勝軍。
entries.en: On renxu Guzhen in Fengzhou was elevated to the Xiongsheng Army command.
entries.literal: On renxu, Guzhen in Fengzhou was elevated to the Xiongsheng Army.

entries.zh: 丙寅，左羽林統軍馬希崇。
entries.en: On bingyin, Ma Xichong, commander of the Left Forest Cavalry.
entries.literal: On bingyin, Ma Xichong, Commander of the Left Forest of Cavalry.

entries.zh: 〈（案：此下有脫誤。）〉
entries.en: (Note: text is missing below.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: there is a lacuna below.)〉

entries.zh: 十二月壬申朔，史館奏，請差官修撰世宗實錄，從之。
entries.en: On the first day renshen of the twelfth month the Historiography Office asked that officials be assigned to compile Shizong's Veritable Records; the court approved.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day renshen, the Historiography Office memorialized requesting that officials be assigned to compile the Veritable Records of Shizong; it was approved.

entries.zh: 甲戌，改萬歲殿為紫宸殿。
entries.en: On jiaxu the Hall of Ten Thousand Years was renamed the Hall of Purple Serenity.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, the Hall of Ten Thousand Years was renamed the Hall of Purple Serenity.

entries.zh: 甲午，西京奏，左屯衛上將軍致仕李萼卒。
entries.en: On jiawu the Western Capital reported the death of Li E, retired general of the Left Garrison Guards.
entries.literal: On jiawu, the Western Capital reported that Li E, retired General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guards, had died.

entries.zh: 乙未，大霖，晝昏，凡四日而止，分命使臣賑給諸州遭水人戶。
entries.en: On yiwei torrential rain darkened the day for four days; envoys were then sent to relieve flood-stricken households across the prefectures.
entries.literal: On yiwei, heavy rain fell; day turned to dusk for four days before it stopped, and envoys were dispatched in turn to provide relief to households afflicted by flooding in the various prefectures.

entries.zh: 顯德七年春正月辛丑朔，文武百僚進名奉賀。
entries.en: On the first day xinchou in spring of Xiande 7, civil and military officials offered New Year congratulations.
entries.literal: In spring of the seventh year of Xiande, on the first day xinchou of the first month, civil and military officials presented their names in congratulation.

entries.zh: 鎮、定二州馳奏，契丹入寇，河東賊軍自土門東下與蕃寇合勢。
entries.en: Zhen and Ding sent urgent reports that Khitan forces had invaded and Hedong rebels had marched east through Tumen Pass to join them.
entries.literal: Zhen and Ding prefectures sent urgent reports that the Khitan had invaded, and rebel forces of Hedong had come down east from Tumen Pass and joined strength with the barbarian invaders.

entries.zh: 詔今上率兵北征。
entries.en: The court ordered the present sovereign to lead a northern campaign.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the Present Lord to lead troops on a northern campaign.

entries.zh: 癸卯，發京師，是夕宿於陳橋驛。
entries.en: On guimao he left the capital and lodged that night at Chenqiao Post.
entries.literal: On guimao, he set out from the capital; that evening he lodged at Chenqiao Post.

entries.zh: 未曙，軍變，將士大噪呼萬歲，擐甲將刃，推戴今上升大位，扶策升馬，擁迫南行。
entries.en: Before dawn the army mutinied; troops shouted "Long live the emperor!", donned armor and drew swords, and pressed the present sovereign onto the throne; they helped him mount and crowded him south.
entries.literal: Before dawn the army mutinied; officers and soldiers raised a great clamor shouting "Ten thousand years!", donned armor and drew blades, and pressed the Present Lord to ascend the great throne; they helped him mount his horse and crowded him southward.

entries.zh: 是日，詔曰：「天生蒸民，樹之司牧，二帝推公而禪位，三王乘時以革命，其極一也。
entries.en: That day an edict read: "Heaven bred the people and set rulers over them; Yao and Shun yielded the realm in the public interest, and the Three Kings changed the mandate when the time came—the principle is the same.
entries.literal: That day an edict said: "Heaven gave birth to the teeming people and set over them rulers and herdsmen; the Two Emperors yielded the public good and abdicated the throne, and the Three Kings seized the time to change the mandate—their ultimate principle is one.

entries.zh: 予末小子，遭家不造，人心已去，國命有歸。
entries.en: I am but a young and unworthy ruler; misfortune has struck my house, the people's hearts have turned away, and the mandate has found its new home.
entries.literal: I, an unworthy youth, have met with misfortune in my house; popular hearts have already departed, and the mandate of the state has found its destination.

entries.zh: 咨爾歸德軍節度使、殿前都點檢趙，
entries.en: I summon you, Zhao, military commissioner of the Guide Army and director of the Palace Front,
entries.literal: I summon you, Zhao, military commissioner of the Guide Army and Director of the Palace Front,

entries.zh: 〈（案：此下原本空二字。）〉
entries.en: (Note: the original text here omitted two characters.)
entries.literal: (Note: the original text here left two characters blank.)

entries.zh: 稟上聖之姿，有神武之略，佐我高祖，格於皇天，逮事世宗，功存納麓，東征西怨，厥績懋焉。
entries.en: You bear the stature of a supreme sage and a divinely martial mind; you aided our founding emperor and won Heaven's approval; you served Shizong to the end and secured the succession; your campaigns east and west won the realm—your achievements are great.
entries.literal: You possess the bearing of the supreme sage and a divinely martial strategy; you aided our High Ancestor and attained the approval of August Heaven; you served Emperor Shizong to the end, your merit preserved in receiving the succession; east and west you campaigned and won hearts—your achievements are abundant.

entries.zh: 天地鬼神享於有德，謳謠獄訟附於至仁，應天順民，法堯禪舜，如釋重負，予其作賓，嗚呼欽哉！
entries.en: Heaven, earth, and the spirits accept the offerings of the virtuous; the people's songs and lawsuits turn to supreme benevolence; answer Heaven and follow the people, yield as Yao did to Shun, cast off this heavy burden, and let me be your guest. Reverently!
entries.literal: Heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits enjoy offerings from the virtuous; songs of praise and lawsuits of the people attach to supreme benevolence; respond to Heaven and accord with the people, follow Yao in yielding to Shun, as if casting off a heavy burden—I shall be your guest. Alas, reverently!

entries.zh: 祗畏天命。」
entries.en: Reverently accept Heaven's mandate."
entries.literal: Reverently fear the mandate of Heaven."

entries.zh: 今上於是詣崇元殿受命，百官朝賀而退。
entries.en: The present sovereign then went to the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive the mandate; the officials offered congratulations and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Present Lord thereupon went to the Hall of Exalted Origin to receive the mandate; the hundred officials offered court congratulations and withdrew.

entries.zh: 制封周帝為鄭王，以奉周祀，正朔服色一如舊制，奉皇太后為周太后。
entries.en: An edict made the Zhou emperor Prince of Zheng to maintain Zhou rites; calendar, regalia, and colors stayed as before, and the empress dowager was honored as Zhou empress dowager.
entries.literal: An edict enfeoffed the Zhou emperor as Prince of Zheng to maintain Zhou sacrifices; the calendar, regalia, and colors were to remain as before, and the empress dowager was honored as Zhou Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 〈（《續通鑒長編》：建隆三年，周鄭王出居房州。）〉
entries.en: (Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In Jianlong 3 the Zhou Prince of Zheng was sent to live at Fangzhou.)〉
entries.literal: (Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the third year of Jianlong, the Zhou Prince of Zheng was sent to reside at Fangzhou.)〉

entries.zh: 皇朝開寶六年春，崩於房陵。
entries.en: In spring of Kaibao 6 he died at Fangling.
entries.literal: In spring of the sixth year of Kaibao of Our Dynasty, he died at Fangling.

entries.zh: 今上聞之震慟，發哀成服於便殿，百僚進名奉慰，尋遣中使監護其喪。
entries.en: The present sovereign was shaken with grief; he donned mourning in the side hall, officials offered condolences, and soon a palace envoy was sent to oversee the funeral.
entries.literal: When the Present Lord heard it he was shaken with grief; he put on mourning dress in the side hall, the hundred officials presented their names in condolence, and soon a palace envoy was sent to oversee the funeral.

entries.zh: 〈（《續通鑒長編》：開寶六年三月乙卯，房州上言，周鄭王殂，上素服發哀，輟視朝十日。）〉
entries.en: (Extended Comprehensive Mirror: On yimao in the third month of Kaibao 6, Fangzhou reported the Zhou Prince of Zheng's death; the emperor wore plain dress, mourned, and suspended court for ten days.)〉
entries.literal: (Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the third month of the sixth year of Kaibao, on yimao, Fangzhou reported that the Zhou Prince of Zheng had died; the emperor put on plain dress and mourned, suspending court audiences for ten days.)〉

entries.zh: 以其年十月，歸葬於世宗慶陵之側。
entries.en: That October he was buried beside Emperor Shizong at Qingling.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was returned for burial beside Emperor Shizong's Qingling.

entries.zh: 詔有司定謚曰恭皇帝，陵曰順陵。
entries.en: The court ordered his posthumous title set as Emperor Gong and his tomb named Shunling.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to fix his posthumous title as Emperor Gong and his tomb as Shunling.

entries.zh: 〈（《續通鑒長編》：仁宗嘉祐四年，詔有司取柴氏譜系，於諸房中推最長一人，令歲時奉周祀。）〉
entries.en: (Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In Jiayou 4 of Renzong, the court ordered the Chai genealogy searched and the eldest collateral-line descendant chosen to maintain Zhou sacrifices each year.)〉
entries.literal: (Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the fourth year of Jiayou of Emperor Renzong, an edict ordered the relevant offices to take the genealogy of the Chai clan, select the eldest man among the collateral lines, and charge him with maintaining Zhou sacrifices at the proper seasons.)〉

entries.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州龍崗人，世家豪右。
entries.en: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, born into the Chai clan of Longgang in Xingzhou, came from a family that had long ranked among the region's great houses.
entries.literal: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, née Chai, was a native of Longgang in Xingzhou; her family were for generations eminent local magnates.

entries.zh: 太祖微時，在洛陽聞後賢淑，遂聘之。
entries.en: While he was still obscure, he heard in Luoyang of her virtue and refinement and took her as his wife.
entries.literal: When the Emperor was still obscure, in Luoyang he heard that the lady was virtuous and refined, and thereupon took her in marriage.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張永德傳》云：周太祖柴後，本唐莊宗之嬪御也。
entries.en: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Zhang Yongde, states that Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.
entries.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Zhang Yongde》: the Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.

entries.zh: 莊宗沒，明宗遣歸其家，行至河上，父母迓之，會大風雨，止於逆旅數日。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong's death Mingzong sent her home; on the way to the Yellow River her parents came out to meet her, but a violent storm forced them to halt at an inn for several days.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong died, Mingzong sent her back to her family; on the road she reached the river, her parents came to meet her, and they were stopped by a great storm at an inn for several days.

entries.zh: 有一丈夫走過其門，衣弊不能自庇。
entries.en: A man ran past the door in tattered clothes that could scarcely keep off the weather.
entries.literal: A man ran past their door, his clothes in rags and unable to shelter himself.

entries.zh: 後見之，驚曰：「此何人邪？」
entries.en: The lady saw him and cried out in surprise, "Who is this?"
entries.literal: The lady saw him and said in astonishment, "Who is this man?"

entries.zh: 逆旅主人曰：「此馬步軍使郭雀兒者也。」
entries.en: The innkeeper answered, "That is Guo Que'er, commissioner of the horse-and-foot army."
entries.literal: The innkeeper said, "This is Guo Que'er, commissioner of the horse-and-foot army."

entries.zh: 後異其人，欲嫁之，請於父母。
entries.en: Struck by his bearing, she wished to marry him and pleaded with her parents.
entries.literal: The lady thought him extraordinary and wished to marry him; she asked her parents.

entries.zh: 父母恚曰：「汝帝左右人，歸當嫁節度使，奈何欲嫁此人？」
entries.en: Her parents were furious: "You had served at the emperor's side; now that you are home you should marry a military governor—why this man?"
entries.literal: Her parents said angrily, "You were a woman at the emperor's side; on returning home you ought to marry a military governor—why do you wish to marry this man?"

entries.zh: 後曰：「此貴人也，不可失也。
entries.en: She replied, "This man is destined for greatness; we must not let him slip away.
entries.literal: The lady said, "This man is of noble rank; he must not be let go.

entries.zh: 囊中裝分半與父母，我取其半。」
entries.en: She split her purse in two, gave half to her parents, and kept the rest."
entries.literal: She divided the contents of her purse in half for her parents and kept half for herself."

entries.zh: 父母知不可奪，遂成婚於逆旅中。
entries.en: Seeing they could not dissuade her, her parents consented and the wedding was held at the inn.
entries.literal: Her parents knew they could not prevail, and the marriage was completed at the inn.

entries.zh: 所謂郭雀兒，即周太祖也。）〉
entries.en: The Guo Que'er in question was none other than the future Emperor Taizu of Zhou.)〉
entries.literal: The so-called Guo Que'er was none other than Emperor Taizu of Zhou.)〉

entries.zh: 太祖壯年，喜飲博，好任俠，不拘細行，後規其太過，每有內助之力焉。
entries.en: In his prime he drank and gambled freely, loved bold adventure, and cared little for petty propriety; she checked his excesses and was a steady force within the household.
entries.literal: In his prime the Emperor loved drinking and gambling, delighted in chivalric adventure, and did not trouble over small proprieties; the lady admonished him when he went too far and often gave him strength within the household.

entries.zh: 世宗皇帝即後之侄也，幼而謹願，後甚憐之，故太祖養之為己子。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful even as a boy, he won her deep affection, and the Emperor therefore raised him as his own son.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful and prudent from youth, she pitied him deeply, so the Emperor raised him as his own son.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗寢，後見五色小蛇入顴鼻間，心異之，知其必貴，敬奉愈厚，未及貴而厭代。
entries.en: Once while he slept she saw a small five-colored serpent slip between his cheek and nose; struck by the omen and sure he was destined for greatness, she honored him all the more—yet she died before he rose to power.
entries.literal: Once when the Emperor was asleep, the lady saw a small serpent of five colors enter between his cheek and nose; her heart marveled at it, knowing he would surely become exalted, and she served him with ever greater respect, yet before he attained eminence she died.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，乃下制曰：「義之深無先於作配，禮之重莫大於追崇。
entries.en: After he took the throne he issued an edict: "In depth of righteousness nothing precedes the bond of marriage; in weight of ritual nothing surpasses posthumous honor.
entries.literal: When the Emperor took the throne he issued an edict saying, "In depth of righteousness nothing comes before taking a spouse; in weight of ritual nothing is greater than posthumous elevation.

entries.zh: 朕當寧載思，撫存懷舊。
entries.en: On the throne I dwell on her memory and cherish what we once shared.
entries.literal: On the throne I constantly reflect and cherish what was and what is past.

entries.zh: 河洲令德，猶傳荇菜之詩；
entries.en: Her virtue by the rivers still lives in the ode of the water shields;
entries.literal: Her virtue by the rivers reached far; still the ode of the water shields is recited;

entries.zh: 媯汭大名，不及珩璜之貴。
entries.en: yet her great name at Gui and Rui never matched the honor her jade regalia deserved.
entries.literal: Her great name at Gui and Rui did not yet attain the worth of her jade regalia.

entries.zh: 俾盛副笄之禮，以伸求劍之情。
entries.en: Let the full rites of the secondary pin be performed to express my longing to keep faith with her.
entries.literal: Let the full rites of the secondary pin be performed to express the longing for the sword.

entries.zh: 故夫人柴氏，代籍貽芳，湘靈集慶。
entries.en: Lady Chai of old, her clan's fragrance handed down through generations, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.
entries.literal: Thus Lady Chai, her clan's fragrance handed down, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.

entries.zh: 體柔儀而陳闕翟，芬若椒蘭；
entries.en: Gentle in bearing, she bore the regalia of rank, fragrant as pepper and orchid;
entries.literal: Gentle in bearing she displayed the falcon banner of office, fragrant as pepper and orchid;

entries.zh: 持貞操以選中珰，譽光圖史。
entries.en: steadfast in conduct, she was chosen within the palace, and her fame shines in the chronicles.
entries.literal: Holding steadfast conduct she was chosen within the palace gates, her fame shining in chronicles.

entries.zh: 懿範尚留於閨閫，昌言有助於箴規。
entries.en: Her fine example still lingers in the inner quarters; her wise words aided every admonition.
entries.literal: Her fine model still remained in the inner quarters; her good words aided in admonition.

entries.zh: 深惟望氣之艱，彌嘆藏舟之速，將開寶祚，俄謝璧臺。
entries.en: She had long read the hardship of fate's signs and sighed at how swiftly life passes—just as the precious succession was about to open, she suddenly left the jade terrace.
entries.literal: Deeply she considered the hardship of reading fate's signs; the more she sighed at how swiftly the boat is hidden—when the precious succession was about to open, she suddenly left the jade terrace.

entries.zh: 宜正號於軒宮，俾潛耀於坤象，可追命為皇后。
entries.en: Let her receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly realm; she is posthumously invested as Empress.
entries.literal: She should receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly trigram; she may be posthumously invested as Empress.

entries.zh: 仍令所司定謚，備禮冊命。」
entries.en: Let the relevant offices fix her posthumous title and complete the rites of investiture."
entries.literal: Let the relevant offices fix her posthumous title and complete the rites of investiture."

entries.zh: 既而有司上謚曰聖穆。
entries.en: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.
entries.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.

entries.zh: 顯德初，太祖神主入廟，以後祔於其室。
entries.en: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, she was enshrined beside him in his chamber.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, the lady was enshrined with him in his chamber.

entries.zh: 淑妃楊氏，鎮州真定人。
entries.en: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang, from Zhending in Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 父洪裕，真定少尹。
entries.en: Her father Hongyu served as Vice Magistrate of Zhending.
entries.literal: Her father Hongyu was Vice Magistrate of Zhending.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》云：父宏裕，少漁貂裘陂，有以二石雁授之者，其翼一掩左，一掩右，曰：「吾北嶽使也。」
entries.en: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Yang Tingzhang, relates that his father Hongyu fished as a youth at Diaojiuqi Pond when someone presented him with two stone geese, one wing covering the left and one the right, saying, "I am an envoy of the Northern Peak."
entries.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: his father Hongyu in youth fished at Diaojiuqi Pond; someone gave him two stone geese, one wing covering left and one covering right, saying, "I am an envoy of the Northern Peak."

entries.zh: 言訖不知所之。
entries.en: With those words he vanished, and no one knew where he had gone.
entries.literal: When the words were finished he vanished, none knew where.

entries.zh: 是年生女，為周太祖淑妃，明年生廷璋。）〉
entries.en: A daughter was born that year—the future Lady of Cultivated Virtue of Emperor Taizu of Zhou—and Tingzhang was born the year after.)〉
entries.literal: That year a daughter was born, who became Lady of Cultivated Virtue of Emperor Taizu of Zhou; the next year Tingzhang was born.)〉

entries.zh: 當河朔三鎮全盛之時，所屬封疆，制之於守帥，故韶顏美媛，皆被選於王宮。
entries.en: When the three Hebei circuits were at their height, each garrison commander controlled his own domain, and fair-faced beauties were routinely drafted into princely palaces.
entries.literal: When the three Hebei circuits were in full flower, their territories were controlled by the defending commanders, so fair-faced beauties were all selected for princely palaces.

entries.zh: 妃幼以良家子中選，事趙王王镕。
entries.en: Chosen in youth from a respectable family, she entered the service of Prince of Zhao Wang Rong.
entries.literal: The lady in youth was chosen as a girl of good family and served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 張文禮之亂，妃流離於外。
entries.en: During Zhang Wenli's rebellion she was cast adrift in the chaos.
entries.literal: In the turmoil of Zhang Wenli, the lady was cast adrift abroad.

entries.zh: 唐明宗在藩，錄其遺逸。
entries.en: While still a prince, Tang Mingzong gathered up those who had been left behind.
entries.literal: When Tang Mingzong was still in his princely domain, he recorded those left behind.

entries.zh: 安重誨保庇妃家，致其仕進，父母即以妃嫁於鄉人石光輔，不數年嫠居。
entries.en: An Chonghui protected her family and helped them advance in office; her parents then married her to a townsman named Shi Guangfu, and within a few years she was widowed.
entries.literal: An Chonghui sheltered her family and secured their advancement in office; her parents thereupon married the lady to a fellow townsman, Shi Guangfu, and within a few years she was widowed.

entries.zh: 太祖佐漢之初，屬聖穆皇后棄世，聞妃之賢，遂以禮聘之。
entries.en: Early in his service to the Later Han, after Empress Shenmu's death, he heard of the lady's virtue and took her as his wife with full ceremony.
entries.literal: At the beginning when the Emperor aided Han, as Empress Shenmu had passed away, hearing of the lady's virtue he took her in marriage with full rites.

entries.zh: 《宋史·楊廷璋傳》：有姊寡居京師，周祖微時欲聘之，姊不從。
entries.en: The 《History of Song》, Biography of Yang Tingzhang, notes that he had an elder sister, a widow in the capital; when the Zhou founder was still obscure he sought to marry her, but she refused.
entries.literal: 《History of Song·Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: He had an elder sister widowed in the capital; when the Zhou founder was still obscure he wished to marry her, and the sister would not consent.

entries.zh: 令媒氏傳言恐逼，姊以告廷璋。
entries.en: He sent the matchmaker back with words that sounded like threats; she told Tingzhang.
entries.literal: He had the matchmaker convey words of threat and coercion; the sister told Tingzhang.

entries.zh: 廷璋往見周祖，歸謂姊曰：「此人姿貌異常，不可拒。」
entries.en: Tingzhang went to see the Zhou founder and told his sister on returning, "This man's bearing is extraordinary; you must not refuse him."
entries.literal: Tingzhang went to see the Zhou founder and on returning said to his sister, "This man's bearing is extraordinary; he must not be refused."

entries.zh: 姊乃從之。）
entries.en: She then agreed.)
entries.literal: The sister then consented.)

entries.zh: 妃睦族撫孤，宜家內助，甚有力焉。
entries.en: She kept her clan in harmony and cared for orphans, and was a strong support within the household.
entries.literal: The lady harmonized her clan and nurtured orphans; within the household she was a great help.

entries.zh: 晉天福末，卒於太原，因留葬於晉郊。
entries.en: At the end of the Jin Tianfu era she died in Taiyuan and was buried in the Jin suburbs.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianfu of Jin she died in Taiyuan and was therefore left buried in the Jin suburbs.

entries.zh: 廣順元年九月，追冊為淑妃。
entries.en: In the ninth month of Guangshun 1 she was posthumously invested as Lady of Cultivated Virtue.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun she was posthumously invested as Lady of Cultivated Virtue.

entries.zh: 太祖凡一後三妃，及嵩陵就掩，皆議陪祔。
entries.en: The Emperor had one empress and three consorts in all; when Songling was sealed, each was considered for joint enshrinement.
entries.literal: The Emperor had in all one empress and three consorts; when Songling was closed, all were discussed for joint enshrinement.

entries.zh: 時以妃喪在賊境，未及遷窆，世宗乃詔有司於嵩陵之側，預營一冢以虛之，俟賊平即議襄事。
entries.en: Because her remains still lay in rebel-held territory and could not yet be moved, Shizong ordered the offices to prepare an empty tomb beside Songling, to be filled once the rebels were subdued.
entries.literal: At the time, as the lady's remains lay in rebel territory and had not yet been moved for burial, Shizong ordered the offices to prepare a tomb beside Songling to stand empty, to discuss the funeral rites once the rebels were pacified.

entries.zh: 顯德元年夏，世宗征河東，果成素誌焉。
entries.en: In summer of Xiande 1 Shizong campaigned in Hedong and at last fulfilled his long-held wish.
entries.literal: In summer of the first year of Xiande, Shizong campaigned in Hedong and indeed fulfilled his long-held wish.

entries.zh: 宣懿皇后符氏，祖存審，事後唐武皇、莊宗，位極將相，追封秦王。
entries.en: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu, was granddaughter of Cunshen, who served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong, rose to the highest ranks of general and minister, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
entries.literal: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu; her grandfather Cunshen served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong, rose to the summit of general and minister, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 父彥卿，天雄軍節度使，封魏王。
entries.en: Her father Yanqing was military governor of the Tianxiong army and held the title Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Her father Yanqing was military governor of the Tianxiong army and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 後初適李守貞之子崇訓。
entries.en: She was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.
entries.literal: The lady was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐中，守貞叛於河中，太祖以兵攻之，及城陷，崇訓自刃其弟妹，次將及後，後時匿於屏處，以帷箔自蔽，崇訓倉黃求後不及，遂自刎，後因獲免。
entries.en: During the Han Qianyou era Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and the Emperor besieged him. When the city fell, Chongxun killed his younger siblings and was about to kill her next; she had hidden behind a screen, shielded by curtains. He searched for her in panic but could not find her in time and cut his own throat, and she escaped.
entries.literal: In Qianyou of Han, Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; the Emperor attacked with troops, and when the city fell Chongxun himself slew his younger siblings; next he was about to reach the lady, but she was then hiding behind a screen, covering herself with curtains; Chongxun in haste sought the lady but could not reach her and thereupon cut his own throat—the lady thereby escaped harm.

entries.zh: 太祖入河中，令人訪而得之，即遣女使送於其父，自是後常感太祖大惠，拜太祖為養父。
entries.en: When the Emperor entered Hezhong he had her found and at once sent a female envoy to return her to her father. From then on she was deeply grateful for his kindness and acknowledged him as her adoptive father.
entries.literal: When the Emperor entered Hezhong he had men seek and obtain her, and at once sent a female envoy to deliver her to her father; from then on the lady always felt the Emperor's great kindness and acknowledged him as adoptive father.

entries.zh: 世宗鎮澶淵日，太祖為世宗聘之。
entries.en: When Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan, the Emperor betrothed her to him.
entries.literal: On the day when Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan, the Emperor betrothed her to Shizong.

entries.zh: 後性和惠，善候世宗之旨，世宗或暴怒於下，後必從容救解，世宗甚重之，及即位，冊為皇后。
entries.en: Gentle and kind by nature, she read Shizong's moods well; when he flew into rages at his subordinates she would calmly intercede on their behalf. He valued her deeply, and when he took the throne he invested her as Empress.
entries.literal: The lady's nature was gentle and kind; she was skilled at reading Shizong's intent; when Shizong sometimes raged at subordinates, the lady always calmly interceded and rescued them; Shizong greatly valued her, and when he took the throne she was invested as Empress.

entries.zh: 世宗將南征，後常諫止之，言甚切直，世宗亦為之動容，洎車駕駐於淮甸，久冒炎暑，後因憂恚成疾。
entries.en: When Shizong prepared to campaign south she often urged him to stay, speaking with blunt earnestness that moved him; but when the imperial train halted in the Huai region, long exposure to summer heat and anxiety brought on her illness.
entries.literal: When Shizong was about to campaign south, the lady often admonished and stopped him, her words very earnest and direct; Shizong was also moved by this; when the imperial carriage halted in the Huai region, long exposed to summer heat, the lady fell ill from worry and distress.

entries.zh: 顯德二年七月二十一日，崩於滋德殿，時年二十有六。
entries.en: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of Xiande 2 she died in Zide Hall at the age of twenty-six.
entries.literal: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of the second year of Xiande she died in Zide Hall—she was twenty-six.

entries.zh: 世宗甚悼之。
entries.en: Shizong mourned her deeply.
entries.literal: Shizong grieved for her deeply.

entries.zh: 既而有司上謚曰宣懿，葬於新鄭，陵曰懿陵。
entries.en: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Xuanyi; she was buried at Xinzheng in the tomb named Yiling.
entries.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Xuanyi; she was buried at Xinzheng, tomb named Yiling.

entries.zh: 〈（案：世宗有後符後，即宣懿之女弟也，薛史不為立傳，未免闕略。
entries.en: (Note: Shizong later had another consort, Lady Fu, the younger sister of Empress Xuanyi; Xue's History gives her no separate biography, which is a regrettable omission.
entries.literal: (Note: Shizong had a later consort, the later Lady Fu, who was the younger sister of Xuanyi; Xue's History did not compose a separate biography for her, which is somewhat an omission.

entries.zh: 《五代史補》：世宗皇后符氏，即魏王彥卿之女。
entries.en: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 states that Empress Fu of Shizong was the daughter of Prince of Wei Yanqing.
entries.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Empress Fu of Shizong was the daughter of Prince of Wei Yanqing.

entries.zh: 時有相工視之大驚，密告魏王曰：「此女貴不可言。」
entries.en: A physiognomist who examined her was greatly startled and told the Prince of Wei in secret, "This girl's destiny is beyond words."
entries.literal: At the time a physiognomist viewed her and was greatly startled, secretly telling the Prince of Wei, "This girl's nobility is beyond words."

entries.zh: 李守貞素有異志，因與子崇訓娶之，禮畢，守貞甚有喜色。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen, who had long harbored rebellious ambitions, had his son Chongxun marry her; when the wedding was complete he was visibly delighted.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen had long harbored rebellious intent and therefore had his son Chongxun marry her; when the rites were complete Shouzhen showed great pleasure.

entries.zh: 其後據河中叛，高祖為樞密使，受命出征。
entries.en: Later he seized Hezhong and rebelled; the High Ancestor, then Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was ordered to campaign against him.
entries.literal: Afterward he held Hezhong and rebelled; the High Ancestor was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and received orders to campaign.

entries.zh: 後知高祖與其父有舊，城破之際，據堂門而坐，叱諸軍曰：「我符魏王女也，魏王與樞密太尉，兄弟之不若，汝等慎勿無禮。」
entries.en: Knowing the High Ancestor and her father were old associates, when the city fell she sat in the hall doorway and shouted at the soldiers, "I am the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu; the Prince of Wei and the Grand Preceptor are as close as brothers—you must not treat me with disrespect."
entries.literal: The lady knew the High Ancestor and her father were old associates; as the city fell she sat by the hall door and shouted at the armies, "I am the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu; the Prince of Wei and the Grand Preceptor of the Bureau are as close as brothers—you must not be disrespectful."

entries.zh: 於是諸軍聳然引退。
entries.en: The soldiers drew back in awe.
entries.literal: Thereupon the armies drew back in awe.

entries.zh: 頃之，高祖至，喜曰：「此女於白刃紛之際保全，可謂非常人也。」
entries.en: Soon the High Ancestor arrived and said with delight, "This woman preserved herself amid flashing blades—she is truly extraordinary."
entries.literal: Before long the High Ancestor arrived and said with pleasure, "This girl preserved herself amid flashing blades—she may be called an extraordinary person."

entries.zh: 乃歸之魏王。
entries.en: He then returned her to the Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: He then returned her to the Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 至世宗即位，納為皇后。
entries.en: When Shizong took the throne he made her his Empress.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne she was taken in as Empress.

entries.zh: 既免河中之難，其母欲使出家，資其福壽，後不悅曰：「死生有命，誰能髡首跣足以求茍活也！」
entries.en: After she escaped the disaster at Hezhong, her mother wished to have her take Buddhist orders to secure blessings and long life; the lady refused angrily: "Life and death are fated—who would shave her head and go barefoot merely to cling to life!"
entries.literal: After escaping the peril at Hezhong, her mother wished to have her leave home and become a nun to secure blessings and long life; the lady was displeased and said, "Life and death have their allotted span—who would shave the head and go barefoot to seek a mean survival!"

entries.zh: 母度不可逼，遂止。
entries.en: Her mother saw she could not be forced and gave up the idea.
entries.literal: Her mother judged she could not be compelled and stopped.

entries.zh: 世宗素以後賢，又聞命不以出家為念，愈賢之，所以為天下母也。）〉
entries.en: Shizong had always known her for her virtue, and when he heard she would not take orders merely to prolong life, he esteemed her all the more—thus she became mother of the realm.)〉
entries.literal: Shizong had always regarded the lady as virtuous, and hearing she would not consider leaving home for the tonsure, valued her all the more—thus she became mother of the realm.)〉

entries.zh: 史臣曰：周室后妃凡六人，而追冊者四，故中闈內則，罕得而聞，惟董妃、符後之懿範，亦無愧於彤管矣。
entries.en: The historiographer remarks: The Zhou house had six consorts in all, four of them posthumously invested; little is therefore known of the inner palace and its rules—yet the exemplary conduct of Lady Dong and Empress Fu would not disgrace the red brush.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: The consorts of the Zhou house numbered six in all, of whom four were posthumously invested; hence the inner quarters and household rules are rarely heard of—only the fine models of Lady Dong and Empress Fu are without shame before the red brush.

entries.zh: 〈（案：薛史無外戚傳，考《五代會要》云：周太祖第三女樂安公主，為漢室所害，廣順元年二月追封，至顯德四年四月，又追封莒國長公主。
entries.en: (Note: Xue's History has no biography of maternal kin. The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that Emperor Taizu's third daughter, Princess Le'an, was killed during the Later Han; she was posthumously enfeoffed in Guangshun 1.2 and again as Grand Princess of Ju in Xiande 4.4.
entries.literal: (Note: Xue's History has no biography of maternal kin; consulting the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, it states that the third daughter of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, Princess Le'an, was killed by the Han court; she was posthumously enfeoffed in the second month of the first year of Guangshun, and in the fourth month of the fourth year of Xiande was again posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Ju.

entries.zh: 第四女壽安公主，降張永德，廣順元年四月封，至顯德元年，封晉國長公主。
entries.en: The fourth daughter, Princess Shou'an, married Zhang Yongde and was enfeoffed in Guangshun 1.4; by Xiande 1 she held the title Grand Princess of Jin.
entries.literal: The fourth daughter, Princess Shou'an, married Zhang Yongde and was enfeoffed in the fourth month of the first year of Guangshun; by the first year of Xiande she was enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Jin.

entries.zh: 第五女永寧公主，廣順元年九月追封，至顯德四年四月，又追封梁國長公主。）〉
entries.en: The fifth daughter, Princess Yongning, was posthumously enfeoffed in Guangshun 1.9 and again as Grand Princess of Liang in Xiande 4.4.)〉
entries.literal: The fifth daughter, Princess Yongning, was posthumously enfeoffed in the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun; by the fourth month of the fourth year of Xiande she was again posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the State of Liang.)〉

entries.zh: 貴妃張氏，恒州真定人也。
entries.en: Honored Consort Zhang was a native of Zhending in Hengzhou.
entries.literal: Honored Consort Zhang, a native of Zhending in Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 祖記，成德軍節度判官、檢校兵部尚書。
entries.en: Her grandfather Ji served as adjutant of the Chengde army and Acting Minister of War.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Ji was adjutant of the Chengde army and Acting Minister of War.

entries.zh: 父同芝，本州諮呈官、檢校工部尚書，事趙王王镕，歷職中要。
entries.en: Her father Tongzhi was the prefecture's reporting officer and Acting Minister of Works; he served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong and rose to posts in the central administration.
entries.literal: Her father Tongzhi was reporting officer of the prefecture and Acting Minister of Works; he served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong and held posts in the central administration.

entries.zh: 天祐末，趙將張文禮殺王镕，以鎮州歸梁，莊宗命將符存審討平之。
entries.en: At the end of Tianyou the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and surrendered Zhenzhou to Liang; Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunshen to suppress him.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianyou, the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and surrendered Zhenzhou to Liang; Zhuangzong ordered the general Fu Cunshen to pacify it.

entries.zh: 時妃年尚幼，有幽州偏將武從諫者，駐騑於家，見妃韶令，乃為其子聘之。
entries.en: She was still young when a subordinate commander from Youzhou named Wu Congjian was billeted at her home; struck by her grace, he betrothed her to his son.
entries.literal: At the time the lady was still young; a partial commander from Youzhou, Wu Congjian, was quartered at her home, saw her fair and comely, and betrothed her to his son.

entries.zh: 武氏家在太原。
entries.en: The Wu family lived in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: The Wu family lived in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 太祖從漢祖鎮並門，屬楊夫人以疾終，無何武氏子卒，太祖素聞妃之賢，遂納為繼室。
entries.en: When the Emperor followed the Han founder to garrison Bingmen, Lady Yang died of illness; soon afterward the Wu son died as well. Having long heard of the lady's virtue, he took her as his successor consort.
entries.literal: The Emperor followed the Han founder in garrisoning Bingmen; as Lady Yang died of illness, before long the Wu son also died; the Emperor had long heard of the lady's virtue and took her as his successor consort.

entries.zh: 太祖貴，累封至吳國夫人。
entries.en: As he rose in rank she was repeatedly ennobled, eventually to Lady of the State of Wu.
entries.literal: When the Emperor rose in rank, she was repeatedly ennobled up to Lady of the State of Wu.

entries.zh: 漢隱帝末，蕭墻變起，屠害大臣，太祖在鄴都被讒，妃與諸皇屬同日遇害於東京舊第。
entries.en: At the end of Han Yindi's reign palace intrigue erupted and ministers were slaughtered; slandered while in Ye, the Emperor could not save her—she and the imperial kin were killed on the same day at his old residence in the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: At the end of Han Yindi, trouble arose within the palace walls and ministers were slaughtered; the Emperor in Ye was slandered, and the lady with the imperial kin were killed on the same day at the old residence in the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 太祖踐阼，追冊為貴妃，發哀，故世宗有起復之命。
entries.en: After he took the throne he posthumously invested her as Honored Consort and proclaimed mourning; therefore there was an order for Shizong to leave mourning and resume office.
entries.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne he posthumously invested her as Honored Consort and proclaimed mourning; therefore Shizong had the order to resume office from mourning.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣位，以太祖舊宅即妃遇禍之地，因施為僧院，以皇建為名焉。
entries.en: After Shizong succeeded, the Emperor's old residence—where she had met her end—was converted into a Buddhist monastery called Huangjian.
entries.literal: When Shizong succeeded, as the Emperor's old residence was where the lady met disaster, it was converted into a Buddhist monastery named Huangjian.

entries.zh: 德妃董氏，常山靈壽人也。
entries.en: Virtuous Consort Dong was a native of Lingshou in Changshan.
entries.literal: Virtuous Consort Dong, a native of Lingshou in Changshan.

entries.zh: 祖文廣，唐深州錄事參軍。
entries.en: Her grandfather Wenguang had been Recorder of Shenzhou under Tang.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Wenguang was Recorder of Shenzhou in Tang.

entries.zh: 父光嗣，趙州昭慶尉。
entries.en: Her father Guangsi served as Commandant of Zhaoging in Zhao prefecture.
entries.literal: Her father Guangsi was Commandant of Zhaoging in Zhao prefecture.

entries.zh: 妃孩提穎悟，始能言聽，按絲管而能辨其聲。
entries.en: Even as a child she was quick and bright; as soon as she could speak she could play string and wind instruments and tell each tone apart.
entries.literal: As a child the lady was keen and bright; as soon as she could speak and listen, she could strike the strings and pipes and distinguish their sounds.

entries.zh: 年七歲，遇鎮州亂，親黨羈離，與妃相失。
entries.en: At seven she was caught in the turmoil at Zhenzhou; her kin were scattered and she was separated from her family.
entries.literal: At age seven she met the turmoil in Zhenzhou; kin were scattered and she was lost from her family.

entries.zh: 潞州牙將得之，匿於褚中。
entries.en: A guard officer from Lu prefecture seized her and hid her in a sack.
entries.literal: A Lu prefecture guard officer obtained her and hid her in a sack.

entries.zh: 其妻以息女不育，得妃憐之，過於所生，姆教師箴，功容克備。
entries.en: His wife, who had no daughter of her own that lived, took her in and loved her more than a birth child; nurses and tutors trained her until her manners were flawless.
entries.literal: His wife, who had no daughter that lived, obtained the lady and cherished her more than a birth child; nurse and tutor instructed her, and her deportment was fully complete.

entries.zh: 妃家悲念，其兄瑀諸處求訪，垂六七年。
entries.en: Her family mourned her loss; her elder brother Yu searched for her everywhere for nearly six or seven years.
entries.literal: The lady's family grieved and thought of her; her elder brother Yu sought her everywhere for nearly six or seven years.

entries.zh: 後潞將入官於朝，妃之鄉親頗有知者，瑀見潞將，欣歸之，時年十三。
entries.en: Later, when the Lu commander came to court, townsfolk who knew her recognized her; Yu met the commander and brought her home in joy—she was thirteen.
entries.literal: Later when the Lu commander entered office at court, several of the lady's townsfolk recognized her; Yu met the Lu commander and joyfully brought her home—she was then thirteen.

entries.zh: 妃歸逾年，嫁為里人劉進超之妻，進超為內職，及契丹破晉之歲，陷蕃歿焉，妃嫠居洛陽。
entries.en: A year after her return she married a townsman named Liu Jinchao, who held an inner-court post; when the Khitans overran Jin he died in captivity, and she was left a widow in Luoyang.
entries.literal: After more than a year at home the lady married Liu Jinchao, a fellow townsman; Jinchao held an inner-court post, and in the year the Khitans destroyed Jin he perished in captivity; the lady was widowed in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 太祖楊淑妃與妃鄉親，平居恒言妃賢德。
entries.en: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang, a fellow townsman, often spoke in daily life of the lady's virtue.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizu's Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang was a fellow townsman of the lady and in daily life always spoke of her virtue.

entries.zh: 太祖從漢祖幸洛，因憶淑妃之言，尋以禮納之。
entries.en: When the Emperor accompanied the Han founder to Luoyang, he recalled Lady Yang's praise and soon took her as his wife with full ceremony.
entries.literal: When the Emperor followed the Han founder to Luoyang, recalling the Cultivated Virtue lady's words, he soon took her in marriage with full rites.

entries.zh: 鼎命初建，張貴妃遇禍，中宮虛位，乃冊為德妃。
entries.en: When the dynasty was first founded, Honored Consort Zhang had been killed and the inner palace stood empty; she was invested as Virtuous Consort.
entries.literal: When the Mandate was first established, Honored Consort Zhang met disaster and the inner palace was vacant; she was then invested as Virtuous Consort.

entries.zh: 太祖自聖穆皇后蚤世以來屢失邦媛，中幃內助惟妃存焉，加以結珮脫簪，率由令範。
entries.en: Since Empress Shenmu's early death he had lost consort after consort; she alone remained to manage the inner household, and in every detail of dress and deportment she set the standard.
entries.literal: Since Empress Shenmu's early death the Emperor had repeatedly lost consorts of the state; within the inner curtain she alone remained as household help, and moreover in tying sashes and removing hairpins she always followed the fine model.

entries.zh: 廣順三年夏，遇疾，醫藥之際，屬太祖兗海之征，車駕將行，妃奏曰：「正當暑毒，勞陛下省巡，明發宵征，須人供侍，司簿已下典事者，各已處分從行。」
entries.en: In summer of Guangshun 3 she fell ill. While physicians attended her, the Emperor was about to set out on the Yanhai campaign. She memorialized: "This is the season of summer heat, yet Your Majesty will tour the provinces, marching at dawn and through the night—you will need attendants. I have already assigned the clerks and other officers in charge to accompany you."
entries.literal: In summer of the third year of Guangshun she fell ill; while physicians attended her, it fell when the Emperor was campaigning in Yanhai and the imperial carriage was about to depart; the lady memorialized, "It is just the season of summer heat; Your Majesty labors in inspection tours, setting out at dawn and marching by night—attendants are needed; clerks and below in charge of affairs have each been assigned to accompany the journey."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「妃疾未平，數令診視，此行在近，無繁內人。」
entries.en: He replied, "Your illness is not yet settled; I have ordered the physicians to watch you closely. This campaign is nearby—there is no need to trouble the inner household."
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "The lady's illness is not yet settled; I have repeatedly ordered examinations—this journey is nearby; do not trouble the inner household."

entries.zh: 及太祖駐蹕魯中，妃誌欲令內人進侍，發中使往來言之。
entries.en: After he halted in Lu, she still wished to send inner attendants to wait on him and dispatched palace envoys to urge it.
entries.literal: When the Emperor halted in Lu, the lady resolved to have inner attendants come to serve and sent palace envoys back and forth to speak of it.

entries.zh: 太祖手敕鄭仁誨曰：「切慮德妃以朕至兗州行營，津置內人承侍。
entries.en: The Emperor wrote in his own hand to Zheng Renhui: "I am concerned that the Virtuous Consort, learning that I have reached the Yanzhou field headquarters, will arrange for inner attendants to come and serve me.
entries.literal: The Emperor wrote by his own hand to Zheng Renhui: "I am deeply concerned that the Virtuous Consort, because I have reached the Yanzhou field headquarters, will arrange for inner attendants to come and serve.

entries.zh: 緣諸軍在野，不可自安，令鄭仁誨專心體候。
entries.en: With the armies in the field I cannot be at ease about such arrangements. Let Zheng Renhui attend to her with your full attention.
entries.literal: Because the armies are in the field, one cannot be at ease; order Zheng Renhui to attend to her with single-minded care.

entries.zh: 如德妃津置內人東來，便須上聞約住，或取索鞍馬，不得供應。
entries.en: If she arranges for inner attendants to come east, report at once and hold them back; if they demand saddles or horses, do not supply them.
entries.literal: If the Virtuous Consort arranges for inner attendants to come east, you must report upward and restrain them, or if they demand saddles and horses, do not supply them.

entries.zh: 如意堅確，即以手敕示之。」
entries.en: If she insists, show her this handwritten edict."
entries.literal: If she is firm and resolute, show her this handwritten edict."

entries.zh: 既而平定兗州，車駕還京，妃疾無減，俄卒於大內，時年三十九。
entries.en: Yanzhou was pacified and the Emperor returned to the capital, but her illness did not abate; she soon died in the inner palace at the age of thirty-nine.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yanzhou was pacified and the imperial carriage returned to the capital; the lady's illness did not lessen, and soon she died in the great inner palace—she was thirty-nine.
