entries.zh: 輟朝三日。
entries.en: Court was suspended for three days.
entries.literal: Court was suspended for three days.

entries.zh: 妃兄廷璋，蚤事太祖，即位累歷內職，出為晉州節度使。
entries.en: Her elder brother Tingzhang had served the Emperor from early on; after the founding he held a series of inner-court posts before being appointed military governor of Jin.
entries.literal: The lady's elder brother Tingzhang had long served the Emperor; when he took the throne Tingzhang successively held inner-court posts and was then sent out as military governor of Jin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 皇朝撫運，移鎮邢州，又改鄜州，受代歸闕，卒於私第。
entries.en: Under the new dynasty he was transferred to Xingzhou, then reassigned to Yanzhou; when his term ended he returned to the capital and died at home.
entries.literal: When the dynasty received Heaven's favor he was transferred to garrison Xing Prefecture, then reassigned to Yan Prefecture; after his term ended he returned to court and died at his private residence.

entries.zh: 世宗貞惠皇后劉氏，將家女也，幼歸於世宗。
entries.en: Empress Zhenhui of Emperor Shizong, née Liu, came from a military family and married Shizong in her youth.
entries.literal: Empress Zhenhui of Emperor Shizong, née Liu, was a daughter of a military family and in youth became Shizong's wife.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐中，世宗在西班，後始封彭城縣君。
entries.en: During the Han Qianyou era, while Shizong served in the western bureau, she was first ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng county.
entries.literal: In Qianyou of Han, Shizong was in the western class; the lady was first ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng county.

entries.zh: 世宗隨太祖在鄴，後留居邸第。
entries.en: When Shizong followed the Emperor to Ye, she remained at their residence.
entries.literal: Shizong followed the Emperor in Ye; the lady remained in the residence.

entries.zh: 漢末李業等作亂，後與貴妃張氏及諸皇族同日遇禍。
entries.en: At the end of Han, when Li Ye and others rose in revolt, she, Honored Consort Zhang, and the imperial kin were killed on the same day.
entries.literal: At the end of Han, Li Ye and others made trouble; the lady with Honored Consort Zhang and the imperial kin met disaster on the same day.

entries.zh: 國初，追封彭城郡夫人。
entries.en: At the founding of the dynasty she was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng commandery.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state she was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng commandery.

entries.zh: 顯德四年夏四月，追冊為皇后，謚曰貞惠，陵曰惠陵。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer of Xiande 4 she was posthumously invested as Empress with the posthumous title Zhenhui; her tomb was named Huiling.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the fourth year of Xiande she was posthumously invested as Empress, posthumous title Zhenhui, tomb named Huiling.

entries.zh: 剡王侗，太祖子，初名青哥，漢末遇害。
entries.en: Prince Tong of Shan was a son of Taizu; his childhood name was Qingge, and he was murdered in the final days of the Later Han.
entries.literal: Prince of Shan Tong, a son of Taizu, was originally named Qingge; he was killed at the end of the Later Han.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈太尉，賜名侗。
entries.en: After Taizu came to the throne, he ordered Tong posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and given the formal name Tong.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict posthumously conferred on him the rank of Grand Commandant and granted him the name Tong.

entries.zh: 顯德四年追封。
entries.en: He received a posthumous enfeoffment in the fourth year of the Xiande era.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he was posthumously enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 杞王信，太祖子，初名意哥，漢末遇害。
entries.en: Prince Xin of Qi was another son of Taizu; born Yige, he too was slain in the closing days of the Later Han.
entries.literal: Prince of Qi Xin, a son of Taizu, was originally named Yige; he was killed at the end of the Later Han.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈司空，賜名信。
entries.en: On his accession Taizu posthumously named him Xin and honored him as Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict posthumously conferred on him the rank of Minister of Works and granted him the name Xin.

entries.zh: 顯德四年追封。
entries.en: He too was enfeoffed posthumously in Xiande 4.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he was posthumously enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 〈（案：太祖諸子蚤歲遇害，本無事跡。
entries.en: Editor's note: Taizu's sons were murdered young and left virtually no deeds worth recording.
entries.literal: Annotation: the several sons of Taizu were killed in their early years and originally had no deeds to record.

entries.zh: 原本過於簡略，疑有刪節，今據《歐陽史·家人傳》云：初，帝舉兵於魏，漢以兵圍帝第，時張貴妃與諸子青哥、意哥，侄守筠、奉超、定哥皆被誅。
entries.en: The base text is so terse that passages may have been cut; the following is drawn from Ouyang Xiu's family biographies. When the future Taizu first took up arms in Wei, the Later Han besieged his household. The honored consort Zhang, the boys Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all put to death.
entries.literal: The original text is excessively brief and is suspected of having been abridged; now according to the "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History it says: at first, when the Emperor raised troops in Wei, the Han sent troops to besiege the Emperor's residence; at that time the Honored Consort Zhang and the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge, were all executed.

entries.zh: 青哥、意哥不知其母誰氏。
entries.en: The mothers of Qingge and Yige are unknown.
entries.literal: It is not known whose sons Qingge and Yige were by their mothers.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔故第二子青哥贈太尉，賜名侗；
entries.en: After Taizu acceded, he posthumously named his former second son Qingge Tong and honored him as Grand Commandant;
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict posthumously conferred on the former second son Qingge the rank of Grand Commandant and granted him the name Tong;

entries.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信。
entries.en: his third son Yige he named Xin and raised to Minister of Works.
entries.literal: the third son Yige was posthumously conferred Minister of Works and granted the name Xin.

entries.zh: 皇侄守筠贈左領軍衛將軍，以「筠」聲近「榮」，為世宗避，更名守願；
entries.en: The imperial nephew Shoujun was made General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty, but because "jun" sounded like "rong," to avoid Shizong's taboo he was renamed Shouyuan;
entries.literal: The imperial nephew Shoujun was posthumously made General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty; because the sound of "jun" was close to "rong," to avoid the taboo for Shizong he was renamed Shouyuan;

entries.zh: 奉超贈左監門衛將軍；
entries.en: Fengchao was honored as General of the Left Gate Guards;
entries.literal: Fengchao was posthumously made General of the Left Gate Guards;

entries.zh: 定哥贈左千牛衛將軍，賜名遜。
entries.en: and Dingge was made General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guards and given the name Xun.
entries.literal: Dingge was posthumously made General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guards and granted the name Xun.

entries.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月癸未，詔曰：「禮以緣情，恩以悼往，矧在友於之列，尤鐘惻愴之情。
entries.en: On guiwei day in the fourth month of Xiande 4, Shizong proclaimed: "Ritual springs from human feeling, and favor should mourn the dead—above all among brothers, where compassion runs deepest.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, in the fourth month, on the day guiwei, Shizong issued an edict saying: "Rites follow feeling; grace mourns what is past; how much more among the ranks of brotherly affection is there especially deep compassionate feeling.

entries.zh: 故皇弟贈太保侗、贈司空信，景運初啟，天年不登，俾予終鮮，實動予懷。
entries.en: My late brothers, Grand Guardian Tong and Minister of Works Xin, died just as fortune was turning and never lived out their years, leaving me alone among my kin—a grief that pierces me still.
entries.literal: The late imperial younger brothers, the posthumously titled Grand Guardian Tong and Minister of Works Xin, when the auspicious fortune had just begun, did not complete their allotted years, leaving me without brothers to the end—this truly moves my heart.

entries.zh: 侗可贈太傅，追封剡王；
entries.en: Let Tong be raised to Grand Tutor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shan;
entries.literal: Tong may be posthumously made Grand Tutor and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Shan;

entries.zh: 信司徒，杞王。」
entries.en: and Xin as Minister over the Masses and Prince of Qi."
entries.literal: Xin as Minister over the Masses, Prince of Qi."

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「故皇從弟贈左領軍衛將軍守願、贈左監門衛將軍奉超、贈左千牛衛將軍遜等，頃因季世，不享遐齡，每念非辜，難忘有慟。
entries.en: A second edict read: "My late cousins Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun—honored respectively as generals of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty, the Left Gate Guards, and the Left Thousand-Ox Guards—perished young in violent times. Remembering their undeserved deaths, I cannot lay grief aside.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "The late imperial cousins, the posthumously titled General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty Shouyuan, General of the Left Gate Guards Fengchao, and General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guards Xun and others, recently because of the troubled age did not enjoy long life; whenever I think of their innocence, I cannot forget my grief.

entries.zh: 守願可贈左衛大將軍，奉超右衛大將軍，遜右武衛大將軍。」）〉
entries.en: Shouyuan shall be Grand General of the Left Guard, Fengchao of the Right Guard, and Xun of the Right Martial Guard." (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: Shouyuan may be posthumously made Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard." (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 蘄王熙誨，世宗子，顯德六年封。
entries.en: Prince Xi Hui of Qi was enfeoffed in Xiande 6, likewise a son of Shizong.
entries.literal: Prince of Qi Xi Hui, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·家人傳》云：世宗子七人，長曰宜哥，次二皆未名，次曰恭皇帝，次曰熙讓，次曰熙謹，次曰熙誨，皆不知其母為誰氏，宜哥與其二皆為漢誅。
entries.en: Ouyang Xiu's family biographies record seven sons of Shizong: the eldest Yige, two younger boys still unnamed, then the future Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui. Their mothers are unknown. Yige and the two unnamed boys were killed by the Later Han.
entries.literal: The "Biographies of the Imperial Family" in Ouyang's History says: Shizong had seven sons; the eldest was called Yige, the next two were both unnamed, the next was the Emperor Gong, then Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui; it is not known who their mothers were; Yige and the other two were all executed by the Han.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔賜皇孫名，誼贈左驍衛大將軍，誠左武衛大將軍，諴左屯衛大將軍。
entries.en: When Taizu acceded he named his grandsons: Yi became Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Cheng of the Left Martial Guard, and Yan of the Left Garrison.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict granted names to the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Cheng Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, and Yan Grand General of the Left Garrison.

entries.zh: 顯德三年，君臣請封宗室，世宗以謂為國日淺，恩信未及於人，須功德大成，慶流於世，而後議之可也。
entries.en: In Xiande 3 the court asked to enfeoff the imperial clan. Shizong replied that the dynasty was still young, its grace had not yet won men's hearts, and titles should wait until great deeds had been done and blessings could be shared with the realm.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiande, ministers and subjects requested enfeoffment of the imperial clan; Shizong considered that the state was still young in days, that favor and trust had not yet reached the people, and that one must wait until merit and virtue were fully achieved and blessings flowed through the age before such matters could be discussed.

entries.zh: 明年夏四月癸未，先封太祖諸子。
entries.en: The following fourth month, on guiwei day, he enfeoffed Taizu's slain sons first.
entries.literal: In the summer of the next year, on the day guiwei of the fourth month, he first enfeoffed the several sons of Taizu.

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「父子之道，聖賢不忘，再思夭閼之端，愈動悲傷之抱。
entries.en: He also proclaimed: "The bond between father and son is what the sages never forget. To dwell again on a son's early death is to reopen the wound.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "The way of father and son—the sages do not forget it; thinking again of the beginning of untimely obstruction, one's embrace of grief and sorrow is stirred all the more.

entries.zh: 故皇子左驍衛大將軍誼、左武衛大將軍誠、左屯衛大將軍諴等，載惟往事，有足傷懷，宜增一字之封，仍贈三臺之秩。
entries.en: My sons Yi, Cheng, and Yan—honored as generals of the Left Valiant Cavalry, Martial Guard, and Garrison—deserve remembrance that still pains me. Let each receive a fuller princely title and a post in the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: The late princes, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Cheng, and Grand General of the Left Garrison Yan and others—reflecting on past events, there is ample cause for wounded feeling; they should receive an added character in their enfeoffment and still be granted ranks among the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 誼可贈太尉，追封越王；
entries.en: Yi shall be Grand Commandant and Prince of Yue;
entries.literal: Yi may be posthumously made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Yue;

entries.zh: 誠太傅，吳王；
entries.en: Cheng Grand Tutor and Prince of Wu;
entries.literal: Cheng as Grand Tutor, Prince of Wu;

entries.zh: 諴太保，韓王。」
entries.en: and Yan Grand Guardian and Prince of Han."
entries.literal: Yan as Grand Guardian, Prince of Han."

entries.zh: 而皇子在者皆不封。
entries.en: Living princes, however, received no titles.
entries.literal: Yet the princes who were still alive were all left without enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 六年，北復三關，遇疾還京師。
entries.en: In his sixth year Shizong reconquered the three northern passes, fell ill, and returned to the capital.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, recovering the three passes in the north, he fell ill and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 六月癸未，皇子宗訓特進左衛上將軍，封梁王，而宗讓亦拜左驍衛上將軍，封燕國公。
entries.en: On guiwei day in the sixth month Prince Zongxun was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Prince of Liang, while Zongrang became General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry and Duke of Yan.
entries.literal: On guiwei day of the sixth month, the prince Zongxun was specially advanced to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, while Zongrang was also appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

entries.zh: 後十日而世宗崩，梁王即位，是為恭皇帝。
entries.en: Ten days later Shizong died. The Prince of Liang succeeded him as Emperor Gong.
entries.literal: Ten days later Shizong died; the Prince of Liang took the throne—this was Emperor Gong.

entries.zh: 其年八月，宗讓更名熙讓，封曹王。
entries.en: That August Zongrang took the name Xi Rang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Zongrang was renamed Xi Rang and enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.

entries.zh: 熙謹、熙誨皆前未封爵，遂拜熙謹右武衛大將軍，封紀王；
entries.en: Xi Jin and Xi Hui had never held titles; now Xi Jin was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and Prince of Ji;
entries.literal: Xi Jin and Xi Hui had both previously received no noble rank; thereupon Xi Jin was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;

entries.zh: 熙誨左領軍衛大將軍，封蘄王。
entries.en: and Xi Hui Grand General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty and Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: Xi Hui was made Grand General of the Left Army of Inspired Majesty and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 乾德二年十月，熙謹卒，熙讓、熙誨不知其所終。）〉
entries.en: Xi Jin died in the tenth month of Qiande 2; what became of Xi Rang and Xi Hui is not recorded. (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Qiande, Xi Jin died; the final fates of Xi Rang and Xi Hui are unknown. (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 越王宗誼，世宗子，漢末遇害。
entries.en: Prince Zongyi of Yue was a son of Shizong who was murdered in the final days of the Later Han.
entries.literal: Prince of Yue Zongyi, a son of Shizong, was killed at the end of the Later Han.

entries.zh: 顯德四年追封。
entries.en: He received posthumous enfeoffment in Xiande 4.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he was posthumously enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 曹王宗讓，世宗子，顯德六年封。
entries.en: Prince Zongrang of Cao, another son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in Xiande 6.
entries.literal: Prince of Cao Zongrang, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande.

entries.zh: 紀王熙謹，世宗子，顯德六年封，皇朝乾德二年卒。
entries.en: Prince Xi Jin of Ji, also Shizong's son, was enfeoffed in Xiande 6 and died in the second year of the Song Qiande era.
entries.literal: Prince of Ji Xi Jin, a son of Shizong, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Xiande and died in the second year of Qiande of the present dynasty.

entries.zh: 趙暉，字重光，澶州人也。
entries.en: Zhao Hui, whose style was Chongguang, was a native of Chanzhou.
entries.literal: Zhao Hui, style name Chongguang, was a man of Chanzhou.

entries.zh: 弱冠以驍果應募，始隸於莊宗帳前，與大梁兵經百餘戰，以功遷馬直軍使。
entries.en: When he came of age he joined the elite shock troops and was first assigned to Emperor Zhuangzong's personal guard. He fought the armies of Later Liang in more than a hundred battles and, for his achievements, was promoted to commander of the imperial horse guard.
entries.literal: Upon reaching manhood he enlisted in the valiant corps, first serving under Emperor Zhuangzong's personal guard; he fought the armies of Great Liang in more than a hundred engagements and was promoted to commander of the horse guard for his merit.

entries.zh: 同光中，從魏王破蜀，命暉分統所部，南戍蠻陬。
entries.en: During the Tongguang reign he accompanied the Prince of Wei in the campaign that conquered Shu. He was then ordered to lead his own detachment south to guard the frontier against the southern tribes.
entries.literal: During the Tongguang era he followed the Prince of Wei in the conquest of Shu; Hui was ordered to take separate command of his unit and garrison the southern frontier against the barbarians.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，征還，授禁軍指揮使。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong acceded, Hui was recalled to court and made commander of the imperial guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Hui was recalled and appointed commander of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 晉有天下，參掌衛兵，從馬全節圍安陸，佐杜重威戰宗城，皆有功，改奉國指揮使。
entries.en: Under the Later Jin he helped command the palace guard, joined Ma Quanjie in the siege of Anlu, and aided Du Chongwei at the battle of Zongcheng, earning merit in each. He was then made commander of the Fengguo army.
entries.literal: When the Jin dynasty held the realm, he helped administer the palace troops; he followed Ma Quanjie in besieging Anlu and assisted Du Chongwei in the battle at Zongcheng, distinguishing himself in both, and was transferred to commander of the Fengguo army.

entries.zh: 開運末，以部兵屯於陜，屬契丹入汴，慨然有憤激之意。
entries.en: Near the end of the Kaiyun reign he encamped his division at Shaan. When the Khitans entered Bian, he was filled with angry determination.
entries.literal: At the end of the Kaiyun era he stationed his troops at Shaan; when the Khitans entered Bian, he was stirred by indignant resolve.

entries.zh: 及聞漢祖建義於並門，乃與部將王晏、侯章戮力葉謀，逐契丹所命官屬，據有陜州，即時馳騎聞於漢祖。
entries.en: Learning that the founder of Later Han had raised his standard at Taiyuan, he plotted together with his officers Wang Yan and Hou Zhang, drove out the officials the Khitans had installed, took control of Shaan prefecture, and immediately sent horsemen to inform the Han founder.
entries.literal: When he heard that the Han founder had raised the banner of righteousness at Bing Gate, he joined his subordinate commanders Wang Yan and Hou Zhang in concerted plotting, expelled the officials appointed by the Khitans, seized Shaan prefecture, and at once dispatched riders to report to the Han founder.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹主賜趙暉詔，即以為保義留後。
entries.en: (According to the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Khitan emperor issued an edict to Zhao Hui and immediately appointed him acting military governor of Baoyi.
entries.literal: (From the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Khitan ruler issued an edict to Zhao Hui and at once appointed him acting military governor of Baoyi.

entries.zh: 暉斬契丹使者，焚其詔，遣支使河間趙矩奉表晉陽。）〉
entries.en: Hui executed the Khitan envoy, burned the edict, and sent his staff officer Zhao Ju of Hejian to submit a memorial at Jinyang.)〉
entries.literal: Hui beheaded the Khitan envoy, burned the edict, and sent the staff officer Zhao Ju of Hejian to present a memorial at Jinyang.)〉

entries.zh: 漢祖乃命暉為保義軍節度、陜虢等州觀察處置等使。
entries.en: The Han founder then appointed Hui military governor of the Baoyi circuit and commissioner overseeing Shaan, Guo, and the adjoining prefectures.
entries.literal: The Han founder thereupon appointed Hui military governor of the Baoyi army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Shaan, Guo, and related prefectures.

entries.zh: 漢祖之幸東京，路出於陜，暉戎服朝於路左，手控六飛達於行宮，君臣之義如舊結焉，旋加檢校太尉。
entries.en: When the Han founder journeyed to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shaan. Hui, in full armor, paid his respects by the roadside, took the reins of the imperial carriage, and escorted it to the temporary palace. The bond between sovereign and minister seemed renewed, and he was soon given the honorary rank of Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: When the Han founder traveled to the Eastern Capital, his route passed through Shaan; Hui, in military dress, paid court on the left of the road, took the reins of the imperial carriage and escorted it to the traveling palace; the bond between ruler and minister was as if newly sealed, and he was soon made acting Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 乾祐初，移鎮鳳翔，加同平章事。
entries.en: At the start of the Qianyou reign he was transferred to Fengxiang and made a co-equal chief councilor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyou era he was transferred to Fengxiang and given the title of co-equal chief councilor.

entries.zh: 屬王景崇叛據岐山，及期不受代，朝廷即命暉為西南面行營都部署，統兵以討之。
entries.en: Wang Jingchong had rebelled and seized Qishan, and when his term ended he refused to step down. The court promptly named Hui overall commander of the southwestern campaign and sent him with an army to suppress him.
entries.literal: At this time Wang Jingchong rebelled and held Qishan; when his term expired he refused to be replaced, and the court at once appointed Hui overall commander of the southwestern campaign headquarters to lead troops against him.

entries.zh: 時李守貞叛於蒲，趙思綰據於雍，與景崇皆遞相為援，又引蜀軍出自大散關，勢不可遏。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen was in revolt at Pu, Zhao Siwan held Yong, and all three rebels supported one another. Shu forces were also brought through Dasan Pass, and the rebellion seemed unstoppable.
entries.literal: At the time Li Shouzhen rebelled at Pu, Zhao Siwan held Yong, and they all aided one another in turn with Jingchong; moreover Shu troops were brought out through Dasan Pass, and the momentum seemed unstoppable.

entries.zh: 暉領兵數千，數戰而勝，然後塹而圍之。
entries.en: Hui led several thousand men, won battle after battle, and then invested the city with trenches and a siege line.
entries.literal: Hui led several thousand troops, won repeated battles, and then dug trenches and laid siege.

entries.zh: 暉屢使人挑戰，賊終不出，乃潛使千餘人，於城南一舍之外，擐甲執兵，偽為蜀兵旗幟，循南山而下，詐令諸軍聲言川軍至矣。
entries.en: Hui repeatedly challenged the enemy to fight, but the rebels would not sally forth. He then secretly sent more than a thousand men a lodge's distance south of the city wall. They donned armor, took up weapons, and bore Shu banners and standards as they came down from the southern hills, while the main army shouted that Shu reinforcements had arrived.
entries.literal: Hui repeatedly sent men to offer battle, but the rebels never came out; he then secretly sent more than a thousand men, beyond one lodge south of the city, to don armor and take up weapons, feigning Shu banners and standards, and descend along the southern hills, ordering the army to cry out falsely that Shu troops had arrived.

entries.zh: 須臾，西南塵起，城中以為信，乃令數千人潰圍而出，以為應援，暉設伏而待，一鼓而盡殪之。
entries.en: Soon dust rose in the southwest. The garrison took this for truth and sent several thousand men out through a breach in the siege lines to meet the supposed allies. Hui's ambush was waiting; at a single drumbeat his men annihilated them.
entries.literal: In a moment dust rose in the southwest; the city believed it and sent several thousand men breaking out of the encirclement as supposed reinforcements; Hui had set an ambush and, at one drumbeat, slaughtered them all.

entries.zh: 自是景崇膽破，不復敢出。
entries.en: After that Jingchong lost heart and dared not venture out again.
entries.literal: From then on Jingchong's courage was broken and he no longer dared come out.

entries.zh: 明年春，拔之，加檢校太保、兼侍中。
entries.en: The following spring he took the city. He was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: The next spring he captured the place and was made acting Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 國初，就加兼中書令。
entries.en: At the founding of the Zhou dynasty he was further made concurrent Director of the Chancellery.
entries.literal: At the founding of the dynasty he was further given the concurrent title of Director of the Chancellery.

entries.zh: 三年春，拜章請覲，詔從之，入朝授歸德軍節度使。
entries.en: In the third year of the reign he submitted a memorial asking to come to court. The emperor assented, and on his arrival Hui was appointed military governor of the Guide circuit.
entries.literal: In the third spring he memorialized requesting an audience; an edict granted it, and on entering court he was appointed military governor of the Guide army.

entries.zh: 顯德元年，受代歸闕，以疾告老，授太子太師致仕，進封秦國公。
entries.en: In the first year of Xiande he was replaced and returned to court. Citing illness, he asked to retire and was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with honorable discharge, and was advanced in rank to Duke of Qin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was relieved and returned to the capital; citing illness he requested retirement and was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in honorable discharge, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin.

entries.zh: 尋卒於其第，年六十七。
entries.en: He soon died at his home, at the age of sixty-seven.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he died at his residence, aged sixty-seven.

entries.zh: 制贈尚書令。
entries.en: An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: By imperial order he was posthumously given the title of Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 王繼宏，冀州南宮人。
entries.en: Wang Jihong was a native of Nangong in Jizhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jihong, a man of Nangong in Jizhou.

entries.zh: 少嘗為盜，攻剽閭裏，為吏所拘，械系於鎮州獄，會赦免死，配隸本軍，時明宗作鎮，致之麾下。
entries.en: As a youth he had been a bandit who robbed the neighborhoods. Officials arrested him and he was shackled in the prison at Zhen prefecture. An amnesty spared his life and he was assigned to the local army. Mingzong was then military governor there and took him into his service.
entries.literal: In youth he had been a bandit, raiding neighborhoods; he was seized by officials and shackled in the prison of Zhen prefecture; he met with amnesty and escaped death, was assigned to serve in the local army, and at the time Mingzong held the post as military governor and brought him under his command.

entries.zh: 晉高祖為明宗將，署為帳中小校。
entries.en: When Jin Gaozu was still a general under Mingzong, he appointed Jihong a junior officer in his personal guard.
entries.literal: When Jin Gaozu was a general under Mingzong, he appointed him a junior officer in his personal guard.

entries.zh: 天福中，為六宅副使。
entries.en: During the Tianfu reign he served as deputy commissioner of the Six Residences.
entries.literal: During Tianfu he was deputy commissioner of the Six Residences.

entries.zh: 性負氣不遜，禁中與同列忿爭，出配義州軍。
entries.en: He was proud and defiant by nature. In the palace he quarreled violently with his colleagues and was banished to serve with the army at Yizhou.
entries.literal: By nature he was proud and insubordinate; in the palace he quarreled angrily with his peers and was sent out to serve with the army at Yizhou.

entries.zh: 歲餘，為奉國指揮使，從契丹主至相州，遂令以本軍戍守。
entries.en: After more than a year he became commander of the Fengguo army. He followed the Khitan emperor to Xiangzhou and was then ordered to garrison the city with his own troops.
entries.literal: After more than a year he became commander of the Fengguo army; he followed the Khitan ruler to Xiangzhou and was then ordered to garrison with his original army.

entries.zh: 契丹主留高唐英為相州節度使。
entries.en: The Khitan emperor left Gao Tangying as military governor of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler left Gao Tangying as military governor of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 唐英善待繼宏，每候其第，則升堂拜繼宏之母，贈遺甚厚，倚若親戚，又給以兵仗，略無猜忌。
entries.en: Tangying treated Jihong generously. Whenever he visited Jihong's home he would enter the hall and bow to Jihong's mother. He gave lavish gifts, treated Jihong like a kinsman, and even supplied him with arms and armor, showing scarcely any suspicion.
entries.literal: Tangying treated Jihong well; whenever he called at his residence he would ascend the hall and bow to Jihong's mother, gave lavish gifts, relied on him as if kin, and also supplied him with weapons and armor, with scarcely any suspicion.

entries.zh: 會契丹主死，漢祖趨洛，唐英遣使歸款，漢祖大悅，將厚待唐英。
entries.en: When the Khitan emperor died and the Han founder hurried to Luoyang, Tangying sent an envoy to submit. The Han founder was delighted and was about to reward Tangying generously.
entries.literal: When the Khitan ruler died and the Han founder hurried to Luo, Tangying sent an envoy to submit; the Han founder was greatly pleased and was about to treat Tangying generously.

entries.zh: 使未回，繼宏與指揮使樊暉等共殺唐英，繼宏自稱留後，令判官張易奉表於漢祖。
entries.en: Before the envoy returned, Jihong joined the commander Fan Hui and others in killing Tangying. Jihong proclaimed himself acting regent and had his judicial officer Zhang Yi submit a memorial to the Han founder.
entries.literal: Before the envoy returned, Jihong joined the commander Fan Hui and others in killing Tangying together; Jihong proclaimed himself acting regent and ordered the judicial officer Zhang Yi to present a memorial to the Han founder.

entries.zh: 人或責以見利忘義，繼宏曰：「吾儕小人也，若不因利乘便，以求富貴，畢世以來，未可得志也。」
entries.en: Some rebuked him for betraying a benefactor for gain. Jihong said, "We are petty men. If we do not seize the moment when fortune offers itself, we will never win wealth and rank in all our lives."
entries.literal: Some reproached him for forgetting righteousness at the sight of profit; Jihong said, "We are petty men; if we do not seize opportunity when profit offers itself to seek wealth and honor, we could never fulfill our ambitions in a lifetime."

entries.zh: 及漢祖征杜重威至德清軍，繼宏來朝，乃正授節旄。
entries.en: When the Han founder marched against Du Chongwei as far as Deqing, Jihong came to court and was formally granted the military commission.
entries.literal: When the Han founder campaigned against Du Chongwei as far as Deqing army, Jihong came to court and was then formally granted the military commission.

entries.zh: 是歲，就加檢校太傅。
entries.en: That year he was further made acting Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: That year he was further given the acting title of Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 節度判官張易，每見繼宏不法，必切言之，繼宏以為輕己。
entries.en: The circuit judicial officer Zhang Yi spoke bluntly whenever he saw Jihong break the law. Jihong took this as an insult.
entries.literal: The circuit judicial officer Zhang Yi, whenever he saw Jihong act unlawfully, always spoke sharply to him; Jihong took this as belittling himself.

entries.zh: 乾祐中，因事誣奏殺之，尋又害觀察推官張制。
entries.en: During the Qianyou reign he framed Zhang Yi on a false charge and had him killed. Soon afterward he also murdered the observation circuit investigating officer Zhang Zhi.
entries.literal: During Qianyou, on a pretext he submitted a false accusation and had him killed; soon afterward he also killed the observation circuit investigating officer Zhang Zhi.

entries.zh: 漢末，移鎮貝州，就加檢校太尉。
entries.en: Late in the Han dynasty he was transferred to Beizhou and further made acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: At the end of Han he was transferred to Beizhou and further given the acting title of Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 廣順初，加同平章事。
entries.en: Early in the Guangshun reign he was made a co-equal chief councilor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was made co-equal chief councilor.

entries.zh: 三年六月，移鎮河陽，會永壽節入覲，遇疾卒於京師，詔贈侍中。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the third year he was transferred to Heyang. He came to court for the Eternal Longevity festival, fell ill, and died in the capital. An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he was transferred to Heyang; when the Eternal Longevity festival brought him to court for an audience, he fell ill and died in the capital; an edict posthumously gave him the title of Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 盧文紀，字子持，京兆萬年人。
entries.en: Lu Wenji, courtesy name Zichi, came from Wannian in the Jingzhao commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Wenji, styled Zichi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 〈（案：此下原有闕文。）〉
entries.en: Note: The original text below was missing.
entries.literal: Note: The original text below was missing.

entries.zh: 長興末，為太常卿。
entries.en: Late in the Changxing reign he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: At the end of the Changxing era he served as Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 文紀形貌魁偉，語音高朗，占對鏗鏘，健於飲啖。
entries.en: Wenji was tall and imposing, spoke in a clear, carrying voice, answered audiences with ringing assurance, and ate and drank with hearty appetite.
entries.literal: Wenji had a tall, imposing physique, a high, clear voice, and a resonant manner in audience; he was hearty in eating and drinking.

entries.zh: 奉使蜀川，路由岐下，時唐末帝為岐帥，以主禮待之，觀其儀形旨趣，遇之頗厚。
entries.en: While on embassy to Shu he traveled through Qi, where the future Last Emperor of Tang held the Qi governorship and received him with a host's courtesy. Struck by Wenji's bearing and manner, he showed him exceptional regard.
entries.literal: On a mission to Shu he passed through Qi; at that time the Last Emperor of Tang was military governor of Qi and received him with the courtesy due a sovereign guest. Observing his bearing and intent, the governor treated him with marked favor.

entries.zh: 清泰初，中書闕輔相，末帝訪之於朝，左右曰：「臣見班行中所譽，當大拜者，姚顗、盧文紀、崔居儉耳。」
entries.en: Early in Qingtai, with no vice-chancellor in the Secretariat, the Last Emperor asked the court whom to appoint. Attendants said, "Of those the ranks most commend for great promotion, I see Yao Hao, Lu Wenji, and Cui Jujian."
entries.literal: Early in the Qingtai era the Secretariat lacked a chief counselor; the Last Emperor inquired of the court, and those at his side said, "Among those praised in the ranks whom Your Majesty should promote to high office, I see Yao Hao, Lu Wenji, and Cui Jujian."

entries.zh: 或品藻三人才行，其心愈惑。
entries.en: When others weighed the three men's character and ability, he grew only more uncertain.
entries.literal: When some appraised the three men's conduct and talent, his mind grew all the more unsettled.

entries.zh: 末帝乃俱書當時清望達官數人姓名，投琉璃瓶中，月夜焚香，禱請於天，旭旦以箸挾之，首得文紀之名，次即姚顗。
entries.en: The emperor wrote the names of several leading officials of the day, dropped them into a glass jar, burned incense under the moon, and prayed to Heaven. At dawn he drew with chopsticks: Wenji's name came first, then Yao Hao's.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor then wrote together the names of several eminent officials of the day, placed them in a glass jar, burned incense by moonlight, and prayed to Heaven; at dawn he drew lots with chopsticks—the first name drawn was Wenji's, the next Yao Hao's.

entries.zh: 末帝素已奇待，歡然命之，即授中書侍郎、同平章事，與姚顗同升相位。
entries.en: He had long held Wenji in special regard. Pleased, he appointed him Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery, elevating him to chief minister alongside Yao Hao.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor had long regarded him as extraordinary; delighted, he appointed him—at once Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery, rising to the chief ministership together with Yao Hao.

entries.zh: 時朝廷兵革之後，宗社甫寧，外寇內侵，強臣在境。
entries.en: The court had only just settled the realm after years of war; enemies threatened from without and powerful generals held the frontiers.
entries.literal: At that time, after years of warfare, the altars had only just been secured; foreign enemies pressed inward and powerful subjects held the borders.

entries.zh: 文紀處經綸之地，無輔弼之謀，所論者愛憎朋黨之小瑕，所糾者銓選擬掄之微颣。
entries.en: Though he occupied the seat of statecraft, Wenji offered no true ministerial counsel. He busied himself with petty factional grudges and trifling flaws in appointments and promotions.
entries.literal: Wenji stood in the place of statecraft yet offered no counsel fit for a helper; what he discussed were petty blemishes of factional love and hate, and what he impeached were slight faults in selection and appointment.

entries.zh: 時有蜀人史在德為太常丞，出入權要之門，評品朝士，多有譏彈，乃上章云：「文武兩班，宜選能進用。
entries.en: A Shu native, Shi Zaide, served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He haunted the powerful, judged courtiers, and often mocked them. He memorialized: "Both civil and military ranks should be filled by selecting the capable.
entries.literal: At the time a man of Shu named Shi Zaide was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he frequented the doors of the powerful, appraised court officials, and often cast ridicule. He submitted a memorial saying, "Both civil and military cohorts should be chosen and advanced on merit.

entries.zh: 見在軍都將校、朝廷士大夫，並請閱試澄汰，能者進用，否者黜退，不限名位高下。」
entries.en: All active army commanders and court grandees should be tested and winnowed: the able promoted, the unfit removed, with no regard to rank."
entries.literal: All serving army commanders and court grandees should be examined and sifted—the able promoted, the unfit dismissed, without limit of rank high or low."

entries.zh: 疏下中書，文紀以為非己，怒甚，召諫議大夫盧損為覆狀，辭旨蕪漫，為眾所嗤。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the Secretariat, Wenji took it as a personal attack and was furious. He had Remonstrance Officer Lu Sun draft a reply; the prose was vague and rambling, and everyone laughed at it.
entries.literal: When the memorial reached the Secretariat, Wenji took it as directed against himself and was furious. He summoned Remonstrance Officer Lu Sun to draft a rebuttal; the wording was muddled and diffuse, and the crowd mocked it.

entries.zh: 三年夏，晉祖引契丹拒命，既而大軍挫衄，官寨受圍。
entries.en: That summer in the third year, the Jin founder brought in Khitan forces in rebellion. The main army was soon broken and the imperial encampment surrounded.
entries.literal: In the summer of the third year the Jin Ancestor led the Khitans in defiance; soon the great army suffered defeat and the imperial camp was besieged.

entries.zh: 八月，親征，過徽陵，拜於闕下，休於仗舍。
entries.en: In the eighth month he took the field in person. At Huiling he bowed beneath the gate-tower and rested in the guard-house.
entries.literal: In the eighth month the emperor led the campaign in person; passing Huiling he bowed below the gate-tower and rested in the guard-house.

entries.zh: 文紀扈從，帝顧謂之曰：「朕聞主憂臣辱，予自鳳翔來，首命卿為宰相，聽人所論，將為便致太平，今寇孽紛紛，令萬乘自行戰賊，於汝安乎？」
entries.en: Wenji followed the campaign. The emperor turned to him and said, "They say the minister shares the ruler's shame. Since Fengxiang I made you chancellor first, believing men who said you would soon restore peace. Now rebels swarm and I must ride out to fight them myself—does that sit well with you?"
entries.literal: Wenji attended him; the emperor turned and said to him, "I have heard that when the ruler grieves, the minister is shamed. Since I came from Fengxiang I first named you chancellor, trusting men's talk that you would soon bring peace. Now rebels swarm and I must lead the imperial carriage to fight bandits myself—are you at ease with this?"

entries.zh: 文紀惶恐致謝。
entries.en: Wenji thanked him in terror.
entries.literal: Wenji thanked him in fear and trembling.

entries.zh: 時末帝季年，天奪其魄，聲言救寨，其實倦行。
entries.en: The Last Emperor was in his final years; Heaven had dimmed his vigor. He spoke of relieving the camp, but in truth he had grown weary of campaigning.
entries.literal: At that time the Last Emperor was in his declining years; Heaven had taken his spirit. He proclaimed rescue of the camp, but in truth he wearied of the march.

entries.zh: 初次河陽，召文紀、張延朗謀議。
entries.en: When he first reached Heyang he called Wenji and Zhang Yanlang to deliberate.
entries.literal: On first reaching Heyang he summoned Wenji and Zhang Yanlang for counsel.

entries.zh: 文紀曰：「敵騎倏往忽來，無利則去，大寨牢固，足以枝梧，況已有三處救兵，可以不戰而解。
entries.en: Wenji said, "Enemy cavalry strike and vanish; they withdraw when there is no profit. The main camp is strong enough to hold, and three relief forces are already moving. The siege can be raised without fighting.
entries.literal: Wenji said, "The enemy's horsemen come and go in a flash; when there is no gain they leave. The great camp is solid and can be braced against them; moreover three relief armies are already in place, so the siege may be lifted without battle.

entries.zh: 使人督促，責以成功，輿駕且駐河橋，詳觀事勢，況地處舟車之要，正當天下之心，必若未能解圍，去亦非晚。」
entries.en: Dispatch envoys to press them for results. Let the imperial train pause at Heqiao and observe events. The spot commands river and road traffic and the empire's attention. If relief fails, withdrawal will still be in time."
entries.literal: Send men to urge them and hold them to success; let the imperial carriage halt at Heqiao and watch how matters unfold. Moreover this place commands river and road traffic and holds the heart of the realm. If the siege cannot be raised, withdrawal will not be too late."

entries.zh: 會延朗與趙延壽款密，傍奏曰：「文紀之言是也。」
entries.en: Yanlang was then intimate with Zhao Yanshou. He whispered: "Wenji is right."
entries.literal: At that juncture Yanlang was on intimate terms with Zhao Yanshou; he spoke aside and said, "Wenji's words are right."

entries.zh: 故令延壽北行，末帝坐俟其敗。
entries.en: So Yanshou was sent north while the Last Emperor sat back expecting his failure.
entries.literal: So Yanshou was sent north, and the Last Emperor sat waiting for his defeat.

entries.zh: 晉祖入洛，罷相為吏部尚書，再遷太子少傅。
entries.en: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, Wenji left the chief ministership for director of the Ministry of Personnel, then was promoted again to junior tutor of the heir.
entries.literal: When the Jin Ancestor entered Luoyang, Wenji was removed from the chief ministership and made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted again to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 少帝嗣位，改太子太傅。
entries.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made grand tutor of the heir.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was changed to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 漢祖登極，轉太子太師。
entries.en: When the Han founder took the throne, he became grand mentor of the heir.
entries.literal: When the Han founder ascended the throne, he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 時朝官分司在洛，雖有留臺御史，紀綱亦多不整肅，遂敕文紀別令檢轄。
entries.en: Court officials then held branch offices in Luoyang. Though leave-behind censors existed, discipline was often lax, so Wenji was ordered to serve separately as special inspector.
entries.literal: At that time court officials with branch offices in Luoyang had leave-behind censors, yet discipline was often not strict; Wenji was therefore ordered to serve separately as special inspector.

entries.zh: 侍御史趙礪及糾分司朝臣中有行香拜表疏怠者，楊邠怒，凡疾病不在朝謁者，皆與致仕官。
entries.en: Attending Censor Zhao Li and others impeached Luoyang branch officials lax in incense rites and memorial audiences. Yang Bin grew angry and granted retirement to all who claimed illness and stayed away from court audiences.
entries.literal: Attending Censor Zhao Li and others impeached Luoyang branch officials lax in incense rites and memorial audiences. Yang Bin grew angry and granted retirement to all who claimed illness and stayed away from court audiences.

entries.zh: 時文紀別令檢轄之職，頗甚滋章，因疾請假，復為留臺所奏，遂以本官致仕。
entries.en: Wenji's special inspection duties grew increasingly burdensome. After he took sick leave, the leave-behind office impeached him again, and he retired at his original rank.
entries.literal: At the time Wenji's duties as special inspector grew increasingly burdensome. Taking sick leave, he was again impeached by the leave-behind office and retired at his original rank.

entries.zh: （《歐陽史》：周太祖入立，即拜司空於家。）
entries.en: (The History of Ouyang: When Zhou Taizu took power, Wenji was at once appointed Grand Master of Works at home.)
entries.literal: (The History of Ouyang: When Zhou Taizu took power, Wenji was at once appointed Grand Master of Works at home.)

entries.zh: 廣順元年夏卒，年七十六。
entries.en: He died in summer of the first year of Guangshun, aged seventy-six.
entries.literal: He died in summer of the first year of Guangshun, aged seventy-six.

entries.zh: 贈司徒，輟視朝一日。
entries.en: He was posthumously made minister over the masses and court audience was suspended one day.
entries.literal: Posthumously made Minister over the Masses; court audience was suspended one day.

entries.zh: 文紀平生積財巨萬，及卒，為其子龜齡所費，不數年間，以至蕩盡，由是多藏者以為誡焉。
entries.en: Wenji had amassed great wealth in life, but after his death his son Guiling spent it within a few years until nothing remained, and many hoarders thereafter took this as a warning.
entries.literal: Wenji had amassed great wealth in life; after his death his son Guiling spent it all within a few years until nothing remained—whereafter many hoarders took this as a warning.

entries.zh: 晉有天下，拜端明殿學士，兼判度支，轉戶部侍郎，會廢端明之職，復入翰林充承旨。
entries.en: When Jin held the realm he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and oversaw revenue, then vice minister of revenue. When that academy was abolished he returned to the Hanlin as chief drafter.
entries.literal: When Jin held the realm he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, concurrently overseeing the Revenue Bureau, then Vice Minister of Revenue; when the Brilliant Governance post was abolished he re-entered the Hanlin as Chief Drafter.

entries.zh: 晉祖每召問以時事，言皆稱旨。
entries.en: The Jin founder summoned him on affairs of state; his answers always pleased.
entries.literal: The Jin Ancestor whenever summoned him to ask about current affairs found his words all to the purpose.

entries.zh: 五年，拜中書侍郎平章事。
entries.en: In the fifth year he became vice minister of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 六年秋，晉高祖將幸鄴都，時襄州安從進反狀已彰，凝乃奏曰：「車駕離闕，安從進或有悖逆，何以待之？」
entries.en: In autumn of the sixth year Gaozu of Jin was bound for Yedu while An Congjin of Xiang showed open rebellion. Ning memorialized: "If the throne leaves the capital, Congjin may rebel—what is our plan?"
entries.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year Emperor Gaozu of Jin was about to visit Yedu; at that time An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture's rebellious intent was already clear, and Ning memorialized: "If the imperial carriage leaves the capital, An Congjin may turn disloyal—how shall we meet it?"

entries.zh: 晉高祖曰：「卿意如何？」
entries.en: Gaozu asked, "What do you advise?"
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "What is your view?"

entries.zh: 凝曰：「以臣料之，先人有奪人之心，臨事即不及也。
entries.en: Ning said, "By my estimate, one must seize the initiative before the other does; when the crisis arrives it is already too late.
entries.literal: Ning said, "By my estimate, men who seize others' possessions beforehand lack resolve when events come; they fall short.

entries.zh: 欲預出宣敕十數道，密付開封尹鄭王，令有緩急即旋填將校姓名，令領兵擊之。」
entries.en: Prepare a dozen blank edicts in secret for the Prince of Zheng as Kaifeng prefect: in crisis he can fill in commanders' names and send troops at once."
entries.literal: I wish to prepare a dozen or so edicts in advance and secretly entrust them to the Prince of Zheng as Prefect of Kaifeng, so that in urgency he may at once fill in officers' names and order them to lead troops to strike."

entries.zh: 晉高祖從之。
entries.en: Gaozu agreed.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu followed this.

entries.zh: 及聞唐、鄧奏報，鄭王如所敕，遣騎將李建崇、監軍焦繼勛等領兵討焉，相遇於湖陽，從進出於不意，甚訝其神速，以至於敗，由凝之力也。
entries.en: When Tang and Deng reported, the Prince of Zheng did as ordered, sending Li Jianchong, Jiao Jixun, and others. They met Congjin at Huyang; caught off guard by their speed, he was defeated—Ning's doing.
entries.literal: When reports came from Tang and Deng, the Prince of Zheng acted as commanded, sending Cavalry General Li Jianchong, Military Commissioner Jiao Jixun, and others to lead troops against him. They met at Huyang; Congjin, taken unawares, was greatly astonished at their speed and was defeated—through Ning's power.

entries.zh: 少帝嗣位，加右僕射。
entries.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded he was made right vice director.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded he was made Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 開運初，罷相守本官，未幾，轉左僕射。
entries.en: Early in Kaiyun he left the chief ministership but kept his post; soon he became left vice director.
entries.literal: Early in Kaiyun he was dismissed from the chief ministership and kept his original office; before long he was changed to Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 漢興，授太子太保。
entries.en: When Han arose he was made grand guardian of the heir.
entries.literal: When Han arose he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 國初，遷太子太傅。
entries.en: At the state's founding he became grand tutor of the heir.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state he was moved to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 顯德二年秋，以背疽卒於其第，年五十八。
entries.en: In autumn, Xiande year two, he died of a back carbuncle at home, aged fifty-eight.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Xiande he died of a back carbuncle at his residence, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 輟視朝兩日，詔贈侍中。
entries.en: Audience was suspended two days; he was posthumously made palace attendant.
entries.literal: Court audience was suspended two days; an edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 馬裔孫，字慶先，棣州商河人。
entries.en: Ma Yisun, courtesy name Qingxian, was from Shanghe in Dizhou.
entries.literal: Ma Yisun, styled Qingxian, was a native of Shanghe in Dizhou.

entries.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。）〉
entries.en: Note: Text is missing below.
entries.literal: Note: Text is missing below.

entries.zh: 唐末帝即位，用為翰林學士、戶部郎中、知制誥，賜金紫，未滿歲，改中書舍人、禮部侍郎，皆帶禁職。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor of Tang acceded, Yisun became Hanlin academician, revenue bureau director, and drafting officer for edicts, with gold-purple insignia. Within the year he was made secretariat drafter and vice minister of rites, retaining palace duties.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang took the throne, Yisun was made Hanlin Academician, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Drafting Officer for Imperial Edicts, with the gold-purple distinction. Before a year had passed he was changed to Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites, all with forbidden-office duties.

entries.zh: 尋拜中書侍郎、平章事。
entries.en: He was soon made vice minister of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 裔孫純儒，性多凝滯，遽登相位，未悉朝廷舊事。
entries.en: A bookish man, slow and obstructive by temperament, he was suddenly elevated to chief minister without mastering the court's old ways.
entries.literal: Yisun was a pure scholar, slow and obstructive by nature; suddenly raised to the chief ministership, he did not yet know the court's old practices.

entries.zh: 初，馮道罷同州入朝，拜司空。
entries.en: Earlier Feng Dao had left Tongzhou for court and been appointed Grand Master of Works.
entries.literal: Earlier, Feng Dao left Tongzhou and entered court, receiving appointment as Grand Master of Works.

entries.zh: 唐朝故事，三公為加官，無單拜者，是時朝議率爾命道，制出，或曰「三公正宰相，便合參大政」；
entries.en: Tang precedent treated the Three Excellencies as honorary posts without separate audiences. The court now appointed Dao offhand. When the order appeared, some said, "The three excellencies are true chancellors and should join great affairs at once";
entries.literal: By Tang precedent the Three Excellencies were supernumerary titles, with no separate audience; at that time the court's deliberation casually ordered Dao. When the edict issued, some said, "The Three Excellencies are true chancellors and ought at once to take part in great affairs";

entries.zh: 又云「合受冊」。
entries.en: others that "he should receive formal investiture."
entries.literal: others said he "ought to receive investiture."

entries.zh: 眾言藉藉。
entries.en: Rumor swirled through the court.
entries.literal: Talk buzzed everywhere.

entries.zh: 盧文紀又欲祭祀時便令掃除，馮道聞之曰：「司空掃除，職也，吾無所憚。」
entries.en: Lu Wenji also wanted Feng Dao to sweep the halls during sacrifices. Feng Dao heard and said, "Sweeping is the Grand Master of Works' duty; I do not shrink from it."
entries.literal: Lu Wenji also wished to have sweeping done at the time of sacrifices; when Feng Dao heard it he said, "Sweeping is the Grand Master of Works' duty—I have no fear of it."

entries.zh: 既而知非乃止。
entries.en: When he saw the proposal was wrong, he dropped it.
entries.literal: Once he knew it was wrong he stopped.

entries.zh: 劉句為僕射，性剛，群情嫉之，乃共贊右常侍孔昭序論行香次第，言：「常侍侍從之臣，行立合在僕射之前。」
entries.en: Liu Gou served as left vice director; his stiffness bred resentment. Courtiers backed Right Regular Attendant Kong Zhaoxu's memorial on incense order, arguing that "a regular attendant attends the sovereign and should walk before a vice director."
entries.literal: Liu Gou was Left Vice Director; stiff by nature, the crowd resented him. They jointly praised Right Regular Attendant Kong Zhaoxu for a memorial on the order of offering incense, saying, "The regular attendant is a attendant of the ruler and ought to walk and stand before the vice director."

entries.zh: 疏奏，下御史臺定例。
entries.en: The memorial went to the Censorate to fix precedent.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted it went down to the Censorate to fix precedent.

entries.zh: 同光已來，李琪、盧質繼為僕射，質性輕脫，不能守師長之體，故昭序輕言。
entries.en: Since Tongguang, Li Qi and Lu Zhi had held the post; Zhi was flighty and failed the senior's demeanor, which emboldened Zhaoxu.
entries.literal: Since Tongguang, Li Qi and Lu Zhi had in turn been vice directors; Zhi was light and unbridled and could not keep the demeanor of a senior, so Zhaoxu spoke lightly.

entries.zh: 裔孫以群情不悅劉句、馮道，欲微抑之，乃責臺司，須檢則例，而臺吏言：「舊不見例，據南北班位，即常侍在前。」
entries.en: Because the court disliked Liu Gou and Feng Dao, Yisun wished to humble them slightly. He rebuked the Censorate to find precedent; clerks replied, "No old case exists; by north-south court order the regular attendant precedes."
entries.literal: Yisun, because the crowd disliked Liu Gou and Feng Dao, wished to check them slightly; he therefore reproved the Censorate, demanding search of precedent, but the clerks said, "No old precedent is found; by north-south court order the regular attendant stands before."

entries.zh: 俄屬國忌，將就列未定，裔孫即判臺狀曰：「既有援據，足可遵行，各示本官。」
entries.en: When a national mourning observance came and ranks were not yet set, Yisun ruled on the censorial report: "With supporting authority, this may be followed—each official to his station."
entries.literal: Soon it was a national mourning day; as the ranks were about to form but not yet settled, Yisun at once ruled on the Censorate report: "Since there is supporting authority, it may fully be followed—show each official his place."

entries.zh: 劉句怒，揮袂而退。
entries.en: Liu Gou flung his sleeve and left in anger.
entries.literal: Liu Gou in anger swept his sleeve and withdrew.

entries.zh: 自後日責臺司定例，崔居儉謂南宮同列曰：「從昭序言語，是朝廷人總不解語也。
entries.en: Afterward he daily demanded the Censorate fix precedent. Cui Jujian told Southern Palace colleagues, "To follow Zhaoxu's words is to say the whole court cannot speak properly.
entries.literal: Thereafter he daily pressed the Censorate to fix precedent. Cui Jujian said to colleagues in the Southern Palace, "Following Zhaoxu's words—court men altogether fail to understand speech.

entries.zh: 且僕射師長也，中丞大夫就班修敬，常侍班在南宮六卿之下，況僕射乎。
entries.en: A vice director is a senior. Censors and grandees take station and show respect; a regular attendant ranks below the Southern Palace's six ministers—how much more below a vice director?
entries.literal: Moreover the vice director is a teacher; censors and grandees take their places and show respect—the regular attendant's rank stands below the Six Ministers of the Southern Palace, how much more below a vice director?

entries.zh: 已前騎省年深，望南宮二侍郎如仰霄漢，癡人舉止，何取笑之深耶！」
entries.en: Veterans of the Mounted Guard once looked up to the two vice ministers as to the Milky Way. What foolishness, and how deep the mockery!"
entries.literal: In former years the Mounted Guard was long in service; gazing at the Southern Palace's two vice ministers was like looking up at the Milky Way—what folly, and how deep the ridicule!"

entries.zh: 眾聞居儉言，紛議稍息。
entries.en: Hearing Jujian, the uproar slowly died down.
entries.literal: When the crowd heard Jujian's words, the clamor gradually subsided.

entries.zh: 文士哂裔孫堂判有「援據」二字，其中書百職，裔孫素未諳練，無能專決，但署名而已。
entries.en: Writers mocked Yisun's ruling for the phrase "supporting authority." Of the Secretariat's hundred duties he was unpracticed and decided nothing—only signed.
entries.literal: Literati mocked Yisun's desk ruling for the words "supporting authority"; of the Secretariat's hundred duties Yisun had never been practiced and could decide nothing—he only signed his name.

entries.zh: 又少見賓客，時人目之為「三不開」，謂口不開、印不開、門不開也。
entries.en: He rarely received guests. People called him the "Three Unopened": mouth, seal, and door.
entries.literal: He also rarely received guests; men of the time called him the "Three Unopened"—mouth unopened, seal unopened, door unopened.

entries.zh: 及太原事起，唐末帝幸懷州，裔孫留司在洛。
entries.en: When trouble broke at Taiyuan the Last Emperor went to Huai Prefecture; Yisun stayed in Luoyang as capital chief.
entries.literal: When the Taiyuan affair arose the Last Emperor of Tang went to Huai Prefecture; Yisun remained in Luoyang as chief of the capital office.

entries.zh: 未幾，趙德鈞父子有異志，官寨危急，君臣計無所出。
entries.en: Soon Zhao Dejun and his son showed disloyal intent. The camp was desperate and court and emperor found no plan.
entries.literal: Before long Zhao Dejun and his son harbored disloyal intent; the imperial camp was critical and ruler and ministers had no plan.

entries.zh: 俄而裔孫自洛來朝，眾相謂曰：「馬相此來，必有安危之策。」
entries.en: Suddenly Yisun came from Luoyang to court. All said, "Chancellor Ma must bring a policy for survival."
entries.literal: Suddenly Yisun came from Luoyang to audience; all said to one another, "Chancellor Ma's coming must mean a policy for safety or peril."

entries.zh: 既至，獻綾三百匹，卒無獻可之言。
entries.en: He presented three hundred bolts of silk—and no counsel worth taking.
entries.literal: When he arrived he presented three hundred bolts of silk and in the end offered no counsel worth adopting.

entries.zh: 晉祖受命，廢歸田里。
entries.en: When the Jin founder took the Mandate, Yisun was sent home.
entries.literal: When the Jin Ancestor received the Mandate, Yisun was dismissed to his home district.

entries.zh: 蘇禹珪，字元錫，其先出於武功，近世家高密，今為郡人也。
entries.en: Su Yugui, courtesy name Yuansi, traced descent to Wugong; his line had lately settled in Gaomi and were now men of the prefecture.
entries.literal: Su Yugui, styled Yuansi, was descended from Wugong; his family had lately settled in Gaomi and now were natives of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 父仲容，以儒學稱於鄉里，唐末舉《九經》，補廣文助教，遷輔唐令，累贈太師。
entries.en: Father Zhongrong was famed locally for scholarship. Late in Tang he passed the Nine Classics, became Broad Learning assistant, rose to magistrate of Futang, and was repeatedly enfeoffed grand preceptor.
entries.literal: His father Zhongrong was famed in the district for classical learning; late in Tang he passed the Nine Classics, was made assistant in the Broad Learning college, rose to magistrate of Futang, and was repeatedly enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 禹珪性謙和，虛襟接物，克構父業，以五經中第，辟遼州倅職，歷青、鄆從事，轉潞、並管記，累檢校官至戶部郎中。
entries.en: Yugui was modest and open, built on his father's learning, passed the Five Classics, served as aide in Liaozhou and staff in Qing and Yan, became recorder in Lu and Bing, and rose by inspection to revenue bureau director.
entries.literal: Yugui was modest and gentle, received others with open breast, built on his father's work, passed the Five Classics, was recruited as aide in Liaozhou, served as staff officer in Qing and Yan, became recorder in Lu and Bing, and by cumulative inspection reached Bureau Director in Revenue.

entries.zh: 漢高祖作鎮並門，奏為兼判。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu governed Bing Gate he had Yugui made concurrent overseer.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu held Bing Gate as military governor he memorialized for Yugui as concurrent overseer.

entries.zh: 開運末，契丹入汴，漢祖即位於晉陽，授中書侍郎平章事。
entries.en: At Kaiyun's end the Khitans entered Bian. Han Gaozu took the throne at Jinyang and made Yugui vice minister and grand councilor.
entries.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitans entered Bian; Han Ancestor took the throne at Jinyang and appointed Yugui Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 漢祖輗阼，兼刑部尚書，俄加右僕射、集賢殿大學士。
entries.en: On Han's accession he also became minister of punishments, then right vice director and grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
entries.literal: When Han Ancestor succeeded he was also Minister of Punishments; soon he was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

entries.zh: 漢祖大漸，與蘇逢吉、楊邠等受顧命，立少主。
entries.en: When Han fell gravely ill, he with Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and others received the deathbed charge and installed the young emperor.
entries.literal: When Han Ancestor fell gravely ill, together with Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and others he received the final charge and established the young ruler.

entries.zh: 明年，轉左僕射。
entries.en: The next year he became left vice director.
entries.literal: The next year he was made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 三年冬，太祖入平內難，禹珪遁入都城，為兵士所擄。
entries.en: In winter of year three Taizu entered to quell strife. Yugui fled into the capital and was seized by troops.
entries.literal: In the winter of the third year Taizu entered to quell internal strife; Yugui fled into the capital and was seized by soldiers.

entries.zh: 翌日，太祖令人求之，既見，撫慰甚至，尋復其位。
entries.en: Next day Taizu sent for him, comforted him deeply, and soon restored his post.
entries.literal: The next day Taizu sent men to seek him; when seen he was comforted to the utmost and soon restored to office.

entries.zh: 國初，加守司空，尋罷相守本官。
entries.en: At the founding he was made acting grand master of works; soon he left the chief ministership but kept his post.
entries.literal: At the founding he was made acting Grand Master of Works; soon dismissed from the chief ministership and kept his original office.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣位，封莒國公，未幾，受代歸第。
entries.en: When Shizong succeeded he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju; soon he retired home.
entries.literal: When Shizong succeeded he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju; before long he yielded office and returned home.

entries.zh: 顯德三年正月旦，與客對食之際，暴疾而卒，時年六十二。
entries.en: On New Year's Day, Xiande year three, dining with guests, he suddenly fell ill and died at sixty-two.
entries.literal: On the first day of the first month of the third year of Xiande, while dining with guests, he suddenly fell ill and died, aged sixty-two.

entries.zh: 禹珪純厚長者，遭遇漢祖，及蘇逢吉夷滅，禹珪恬然無咎，時人以為積善之報也。
entries.en: A pure, generous elder, he served Han Gaozu; when Su Fengji was destroyed he remained unscathed—men called it reward for virtue.
entries.literal: Yugui was a pure, generous elder; he met Han Ancestor's favor, and when Su Fengji was exterminated Yugui remained untroubled—men of the time took it as reward for accumulated goodness.

entries.zh: 裔孫好名，慕韓愈之為人，尤不重佛。
entries.en: Yisun loved fame, admired Han Yu, and especially despised Buddhism.
entries.literal: Yisun loved reputation and admired Han Yu's example, especially disdaining Buddhism.

entries.zh: 及廢居裏巷，追感唐末帝平昔之遇，乃依長壽僧舍讀佛書，冀申冥報。
entries.en: Dismissed to the lanes, he remembered the Last Emperor's kindness and read Buddhist texts at Longevity Monastery, hoping to repay him beyond the grave.
entries.literal: After dismissal he lived in lanes and alleys; recalling the Last Emperor's former kindness, he lodged at the Longevity Monastery to read Buddhist books, hoping to repay him in the unseen world.

entries.zh: 歲餘枕藉黃卷中，見《華嚴》、《楞嚴》，詞理富贍，由是酷賞之，仍抄撮之，相形於歌詠，謂之《法喜集》；
entries.en: A year among sutras brought him to the Avatamsaka and Surangama, rich in doctrine. He admired them, copied passages, and wove them into verse as Joy in the Dharma;
entries.literal: For more than a year, buried among yellow scrolls, he saw the Avatamsaka and Surangama Sutras, rich in doctrine and reason; he therefore admired them deeply, copied selections, and set them beside his songs, calling the collection Joy in the Dharma;

entries.zh: 又纂諸經要言為《佛國記》，凡數千言。
entries.en: and compiled essential passages as Record of the Buddha Land, several thousand words.
entries.literal: he also compiled essential passages of the scriptures as Record of the Buddha Land, several thousand words in all.

entries.zh: 或嘲之曰：「公生平以傅奕、韓愈為高識，何前倨而後恭，是佛佞公耶？
entries.en: Some teased him: "You held Fu Yi and Han Yu as models—why proud before and humble after? Is the Buddha fawning on you?
entries.literal: Some mocked him: "In life you took Fu Yi and Han Yu as your models of insight—why so proud before and so deferential after? Is the Buddha fawning on you?

entries.zh: 公佞佛耶？」
entries.en: Or are you fawning on the Buddha?"
entries.literal: Or are you fawning on the Buddha?"

entries.zh: 裔孫笑而答曰：「佛佞予則多矣。」
entries.en: Yisun smiled: "If the Buddha fawns on me, it has done so plenty."
entries.literal: Yisun answered with a smile, "If the Buddha fawns on me, it has done so often enough."

entries.zh: 李崧相晉，用李專美為贊善，裔孫以賓客致仕，專美轉少卿，裔孫得太子詹事。
entries.en: When Li Song served Jin, he made Li Zhuanmei aide to the heir; Yisun retired as guest, Zhuanmei rose to vice director, and Yisun became grand mentor of the heir.
entries.literal: When Li Song was chancellor of Jin he used Li Zhuanmei as aide; Yisun retired as a guest, Zhuanmei became vice director, and Yisun received Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 晉、漢公卿以裔孫好為文章，皆欣然待之。
entries.en: Grandees of Jin and Han, knowing his love of letters, welcomed him gladly.
entries.literal: Jin and Han grandees, because Yisun loved to write, all received him gladly.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，就加檢校禮部尚書、太子賓客，分司在洛。
entries.en: When Taizu acceded he was made inspector-general of rites and guest of the heir, with duty at Luoyang.
entries.literal: When the Taizu took the throne he was further made Inspector-General of the Ministry of Rites and Guest of the Heir Apparent, with office at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 每閉關養素，惟事謳吟著述。
entries.en: He shut his doors, lived simply, and devoted himself to verse and books.
entries.literal: He shut his doors to nurture simplicity and devoted himself only to chanting and writing.

entries.zh: 嗜八分書，題尺酬答，必親劄以炫其墨跡。
entries.en: He loved clerical script and always wrote titles and replies himself to show his brush.
entries.literal: He loved clerical script; for titles and replies on letters he always wrote in his own hand to display his brushwork.

entries.zh: 裔孫將卒之前，睹白虺緣於庭槐，驅之失所在，裔孫感賦鵬之文，作《槐蟲賦》以見誌。
entries.en: Before his death he saw a white serpent on the courtyard locust; driven off, it vanished. He wrote on the roc and composed Record of the Locust Worm to record his mood.
entries.literal: Before Yisun was to die he saw a white serpent on the courtyard locust; when driven off it vanished. Moved, he wrote an essay on the roc and composed Record of the Locust Worm to express his mind.

entries.zh: 廣順三年秋七月，卒於洛陽。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, Guangshun year three, he died in Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the third year of Guangshun he died in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 詔贈太子少傅，輟視朝一日。
entries.en: The throne posthumously made him junior tutor of the heir and suspended audience one day.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and suspended court audience for one day.

entries.zh: 景範，淄州長山人。
entries.en: Jing Fan was from Changshan in Zizhou.
entries.literal: Jing Fan was a native of Changshan in Zizhou.

entries.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。
entries.en: 〈Note: Text is missing below.
entries.literal: 〈Note: Text is missing below.

entries.zh: 據《世宗紀》，景範父名初，以戶部郎中致仕。）〉
entries.en: According to Shizong's annals, Fan's father was named Chu and retired as revenue bureau director.〉
entries.literal: According to the Basic Annals of Shizong, Fan's father's given name was Chu; he retired as Bureau Director in Revenue.〉

entries.zh: 世宗之北征也，命為東京副留守。
entries.en: On Shizong's northern campaign he was made vice guardian of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On Shizong's northern campaign Fan was ordered Vice Guardian of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 車駕回自河東，世宗以艱於國用，乃以範為中書侍郎平章事、判三司。
entries.en: Returning from Hedong, Shizong, pressed for revenue, made Fan vice minister, grand councilor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Hedong, Shizong, finding state revenue strained, made Fan Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.

entries.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》載：世宗即位，七月癸巳，制曰：「朕自履宸極，思平泰階，出一令慮下民之未從，行一事懼上穹之罔祐，晨興夕惕，終歲於茲。
entries.en: 〈The Imperial Tortoise Mirror records: On Shizong's accession, guisi of the seventh month, an edict said: "Since I took the throne I have sought to level the great stair. One order I fear the people have not followed; one act I fear Heaven has not blessed—diligent dawn to dusk the whole year through.
entries.literal: 〈The Imperial Tortoise Mirror records: When Shizong took the throne, on the day guisi of the seventh month an edict said: "Since I assumed the august pinnacle I have thought to level the great stair; issuing one order I fear the people have not yet followed, doing one thing I fear Heaven has not yet blessed it—rising early and resting late, the whole year thus.

entries.zh: 雖禮讓漸聞興行，而風雨未之咸若，豈刑政之所闕，而德教之未孚哉！
entries.en: Though courtesy is heard to rise, wind and rain are not yet harmonious—is government at fault, or teaching not yet trusted?
entries.literal: Though ritual yielding is gradually heard to arise, wind and rain have not all been harmonious—can it be that punishments and government are lacking, or that virtue and teaching have not won trust?

entries.zh: 由是進用良臣，輔宣皇化，雖朕志先定，亦輿情具瞻，爰擇佳辰，誕敷明命。
entries.en: Therefore I advance good ministers to proclaim the royal way; though my will was first, public sentiment also watches—I choose an auspicious day and proclaim a bright mandate.
entries.literal: Therefore I advance good ministers to assist and proclaim imperial transformation; though my will was set first, public sentiment also looks on all sides—choosing an auspicious day I proclaim a bright mandate.

entries.zh: 樞密院直學士、中大夫、尚書工部侍郎、上柱國、晉陽縣開國男、食邑三百戶、賜紫金魚袋範，昔佐先帝，每罄嘉謨，逮事眇躬，愈傾忠節，奉上得大臣之體，檢身為君子之儒。
entries.en: Fan, Direct Academician of the Privy Council, Grand Master of the Palace, Vice Minister of Works, Supreme Pillar of the State, Baron of Jinyang with three hundred households, bearer of the gold-purple fish tally—formerly aided the late emperor with every counsel fully offered; serving my slight person, his loyal resolve bends all the more; in serving his superiors he attains a great minister's form, in examining himself he is a gentleman's scholar.
entries.literal: Fan, Direct Academician of the Privy Council, Grand Master of the Palace, Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works, Supreme Pillar of the State, Baron of Jinyang with three hundred households' fief, bearer of the gold-purple fish tally—formerly aided the late emperor, every counsel fully offered; serving my slight person, his loyal resolve bends all the more; in serving the above he attains a great minister's form, in examining himself he is a gentleman's scholar.

entries.zh: 一昨戎輅親征，皇都是守，贊勛賢於留府，副征發於行營，軍政所需，國用無闕。
entries.en: When lately the emperor campaigned in person while the capital was guarded, he praised worthies at the rear capital office and assisted levies at the camp—military needs were met and revenue did not fail.
entries.literal: When lately the war carriage campaigned in person and the imperial capital was guarded, he praised the worthy at the rear capital office and assisted levy and dispatch at the campaign camp—military needs were met and state revenue unlacking.

entries.zh: 今則靈臺偃革，宣室圖功，思先朝欲用之言，成聖考得賢之美，俾參大政，仍掌利權。
entries.en: Now arms rest and merit is plotted; remembering the former court's wish to employ him, fulfilling the sage's gain of worth—let him share great government and hold fiscal power.
entries.literal: Now the Spirit Tower rests arms and the Hall of Proclamation plots merit; thinking of the former court's wish to employ him, fulfilling the sage's gain of the worthy—let him share great government and still hold fiscal power.

entries.zh: 爾其明聽朕言，往敷洪化，予欲則垂象而清品匯，爾則順天道以序彜倫，余欲恤刑名而息戰爭，爾則謹憲章而恢廟略。
entries.en: Hear my words and spread great transformation: when I wish, signs clear all ranks; you follow Heaven's way and order relations; when I ease punishments and still war, you keep statutes and restore strategy.
entries.literal: Clearly hear my words and go to spread great transformation: when I wish, the heavens show signs and all ranks grow clear; you shall follow Heaven's way and order human relations; when I wish to ease punishments and still war, you shall keep statutes and restore temple strategy.

entries.zh: 天人之際懸合，軍民之事罔渝，則國相之尊，非爾孰處，邦計之重，惟材是臧。
entries.en: When Heaven and man align and army and people hold firm, who but you for chief minister? For state accounts, only talent avails.
entries.literal: When Heaven and man hang together and army and people do not stray, then the state's chief minister—who but you? The state's accounts—only talent is stored.

entries.zh: 勉思倜儻以致君，勿效因循而保位，佇聞成績，用副虛懷。
entries.en: Strive boldly to serve the ruler; do not cling to routine and office—await achievement to match my hopes.
entries.literal: Strive with bold resolve to serve the ruler; do not imitate routine and cling to place—await achievement to match my open mind.

entries.zh: 可正議大夫、中書侍郎平章事，判三司。」）〉
entries.en: Appointed grand master of court discussion, vice minister, grand councilor, overseer of the Three Bureaus."〉
entries.literal: May be Grand Master of Court Discussion, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus."〉

entries.zh: 範為人厚重剛正，無所屈撓，然理繁治劇，非其所長，雖悉心盡瘁，終無稱職之譽。
entries.en: Fan was weighty and upright, yielding to none; yet complexity was not his strength—though he wore himself out, he won no praise for competence.
entries.literal: Fan as a man was weighty, upright, and bowed to nothing; yet governing complexity and urgency was not his strength—though he gave his heart and wore himself out, in the end he won no praise for competence.

entries.zh: 世宗知之，因其有疾，乃罷司計。
entries.en: Shizong knew it; when illness came he removed him from fiscal office.
entries.literal: Shizong knew this; because he was ill he dismissed him from fiscal office.

entries.zh: 尋以父喪罷相東歸。
entries.en: Soon his father's mourning took him from office eastward.
entries.literal: Soon on his father's mourning he left the chief ministership and returned east.

entries.zh: 顯德三年冬，以疾卒於鄉里。
entries.en: In winter, Xiande year three, he died of illness at home.
entries.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande he died of illness in his home district.

entries.zh: 優詔贈侍中，官為立碑焉。
entries.en: A gracious edict made him palace attendant posthumously, and the office raised a stele.
entries.literal: A gracious edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant, and the office erected a stele for him.

entries.zh: 楊凝式，華陰人也。
entries.en: Yang Ningshi came from Huayin.
entries.literal: Yang Ningshi was a native of Huayin.

entries.zh: 〈（《遊宦紀聞》載《凝式年譜》云：唐咸通十四年癸巳，凝式是年生，故題識多自稱癸巳人。
entries.en: (Records of Travel and Official Service records the Ningshi Chronological Record: He was born in 873, the guisi year of the Xiantong era, and often signed his works as a man of guisi.
entries.literal: (Records of Travel and Official Service carries the Ningshi Chronological Record, saying: In the guisi year, the fourteenth year of Xiantong of Tang, Ningshi was born that year, so inscriptions often call themselves persons of guisi.

entries.zh: 又，《別傳》云：凝式，字景度。）〉
entries.en: The Separate Biography also gives his style as Jingdu.)〉
entries.literal: Again, the Separate Biography says: Ningshi, styled Jingdu.)〉

entries.zh: 父涉，唐末梁初，再登臺席，罷相守左僕射卒。
entries.en: His father Yang She twice reached the chancellorship at the end of Tang and the beginning of Liang, then retired as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and died in that post.
entries.literal: His father She, at the end of Tang and the beginning of Liang, twice ascended the council seat, and after leaving the chancellorship guarded the post of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat until death.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·楊涉傳》云：祖收，父嚴。
entries.en: (Biography of Yang She in Ouyang Xiu's History names his grandfather as Shou and his father as Yan.
entries.literal: (Biography of Yang She in Ouyang's History says: grandfather Shou, father Yan.

entries.zh: 吳縝《纂誤》云：收與嚴乃兄弟，非父子也。
entries.en: Wu Zhen's Collected Corrections notes that Shou and Yan were brothers, not father and son.
entries.literal: Wu Zhen's Collected Corrections says: Shou and Yan were brothers, not father and son.

entries.zh: 又，《遊宦紀聞》載《楊氏家譜》云：唐修行楊氏，系出越公房，本出中山相結，次子繼生洛州刺史暉，暉生河間太守恩，恩生越恭公鈞，出居馮翊，至藏器徙潯陽。
entries.en: Records of Travel and Official Service also gives the Yang Clan Genealogy: the Xingxing Yangs descended from the house of the Duke of Yue in Zhongshan; through Ji, Hui of Luozhou, En of Hejian, and Jun the Respectful Duke of Yue, who settled in Fengyi, down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.
entries.literal: Again, Records of Travel and Official Service carries the Yang Clan Genealogy, saying: The Yang clan of Tang's Xingxing lineage descended from the house of the Duke of Yue, originally from Zhongshan Xiangjie; the second son Ji begot Hui, Prefect of Luozhou; Hui begot En, Administrator of Hejian; En begot Jun, the Respectful Duke of Yue, who moved out to dwell in Fengyi; down to Zangqi, who moved to Xunyang.

entries.zh: 唐相楊收之父曰遺直，生四子，名皆從「又」，曰發、假、收、嚴，以四時為義，故發之子名皆從「木」，假之子從「火」，收之子從「金」，嚴之子從「水」。
entries.en: The father of Tang chancellor Yang Shou was Yizhi, who had four sons named with the "you" radical—Fa, Jia, Shou, and Yan—after the four seasons; Fa's descendants used the wood radical, Jia's the fire radical, Shou's the metal radical, and Yan's the water radical.
entries.literal: The father of Tang chancellor Yang Shou was called Yizhi; he had four sons whose names all followed the "you" radical: Fa, Jia, Shou, and Yan, taking the four seasons as the meaning; therefore Fa's sons' names all followed "wood," Jia's sons followed "fire," Shou's sons followed "metal," and Yan's sons followed "water."

entries.zh: 嚴生涉，涉生凝式，而收乃藏器之兄、涉之伯也。
entries.en: Yan was She's father and She's son was Ningshi; Shou was the elder brother of Zangqi and She's uncle.
entries.literal: Yan begot She, She begot Ningshi, while Shou was the elder brother of Zangqi and the paternal uncle of She.

entries.zh: 《新五代史記·唐六臣傳》乃以收為涉之祖、嚴之父，非也。）〉
entries.en: The New History of the Five Dynasties' Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers wrongly makes Shou She's grandfather and Yan his father.)〉
