entries.literal: The New History of the Five Dynasties' Record, Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers, makes Shou She's grandfather and Yan She's father, which is incorrect.)〉

entries.zh: 凝式體雖蕞眇，而精神穎悟，
entries.en: Though slight in build, Ningshi was keen of mind,
entries.literal: Though Ningshi's physique was small and slight, his spirit was sharp and penetrating,

entries.zh: 〈（《宣和書譜》云：凝式形貌寢侻，然精神矍然，要大於身。）〉
entries.en: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Compendium: Ningshi looked frail, yet his spirit was vigorous and seemed larger than his frame.)〉
entries.literal: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Compendium says: Ningshi's form and appearance were slight and frail, yet his spirit was alert and vigorous, seeming greater than his body.)〉

entries.zh: 富有文藻，大為時輩所推。
entries.en: He was richly gifted in letters and highly esteemed by his contemporaries.
entries.literal: Rich in literary ornament, he was greatly esteemed by contemporaries.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗朝，登進士第，解褐授度支巡官，再遷秘書郎，直史館。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he took the jinshi degree, entered service as Revenue Circuit Inspector, was twice promoted to Secretary, and served in the History Office.
entries.literal: In the reign of Tang Zhaozong he passed the jinshi examination, left commoner's dress and was appointed Revenue Circuit Inspector, was twice transferred to Secretary, and served in the History Office.

entries.zh: 梁開平中，為殿中侍御史、禮部員外郎、三川守，齊王張宗奭見而嘉之，請以本官充留守巡官。
entries.en: In the Kaiping era of Liang he was Attending Censor, Vice Minister of Rites, and Administrator of the Three Rivers; Prince of Qi Zhang Zongshi admired him and asked that he serve as his protector's circuit inspector in his existing rank.
entries.literal: In the Kaiping era of Liang he served as Attending Censor within the Palace, Vice Minister of Rites, and Administrator of the Three Rivers; the Prince of Qi Zhang Zongshi saw and praised him and requested that he fill his original office as Protector Circuit Inspector.

entries.zh: 梁相趙光裔素重其才，奏為集賢殿直學士，改考功員外郎。
entries.en: Liang chancellor Zhao Guangyi had long valued his talent and had him appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
entries.literal: Liang chancellor Zhao Guangyi had long valued his talent and memorialized him as Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then changed him to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

entries.zh: 唐同光初，授比部郎中、知制誥。
entries.en: At the start of the Tang Tongguang era he was made Director of the Bureau of Review with charge of drafting edicts.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang of Tang he was granted Director of the Bureau of Review and Drafted Imperial Edicts.

entries.zh: 尋以心疾罷去，改給事中、史館修撰，判館事。
entries.en: Soon he resigned because of a mental disorder and was made Supervising Secretary and History Office compiler with charge of the office.
entries.literal: Shortly he was dismissed on account of heart illness, changed to Supervising Secretary and History Office Compiler, and judged office affairs.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，拜中書舍人，復以心疾不朝而罷。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne he was made Secretariat Drafter, but again left office because of his disorder and failure to attend court.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, and again was dismissed for heart illness and failure to attend court.

entries.zh: 長興中，歷右常侍、工戶二部侍郎，以舊恙免，改秘書監。
entries.en: During the Changxing era he served as Right Regular Attendant and Vice Ministers of Works and Revenue, then retired because of his old complaint and was made Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the Changxing era he successively served as Right Regular Attendant and Vice Ministers of the Works and Revenue Bureaus, was excused on account of old ailment, and was changed to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 清泰初，遷兵部侍郎。
entries.en: At the start of the Qingtai era he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 唐末帝按兵於懷覃，凝式在扈從之列，頗以心恙喧嘩於軍寨，末帝以其才名，優容之，詔遣歸洛。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor of Tang encamped at Huaizhen, Ningshi was in his retinue and often caused disturbances in camp because of his mental condition; the emperor indulged him for his reputation and ordered him back to Luoyang.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang held his army at Huaizhen, Ningshi was in the entourage column and rather often, on account of heart ailment, made uproar in the military camp; the Last Emperor, because of his talent and name, indulged him and by edict sent him back to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 晉天福初，改太子賓客，尋以禮部尚書致仕，閑居伊、洛之間，恣其狂逸，多所幹忤，自居守以降，咸以俊才耆德，莫之責也。
entries.en: At the start of the Jin Tianfu era he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, then retired as Minister of Rites and lived between the Yi and Luo rivers, indulging his eccentric ways and often giving offense; yet from prefects downward all treated him as a gifted elder and none held him accountable.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin he was changed to Guest of the Heir Apparent, and shortly retired as Minister of Rites; dwelling in leisure between Yi and Luo, he gave free rein to his wildness and license and often gave offense, yet from prefects and guards downward all regarded him as a man of outstanding talent and venerable virtue and none blamed him.

entries.zh: 晉開運中，宰相桑維翰知其絕俸，艱於家食，奏除太子少保，分司於洛。
entries.en: During the Jin Kaiyun era, Chancellor Sang Weihan learned that Ningshi had lost his salary and was struggling to feed his household; he memorialized to make him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with a post at Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the Kaiyun era of Jin, chancellor Sang Weihan knew that his stipend had ceased and that he was hard pressed for household food, and memorialized to appoint him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with separate duty at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐中，歷少傅、少師。
entries.en: Under the Later Han reign era Qianyou he served as Junior Tutor and then Junior Preceptor.
entries.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han he successively served as Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor.

entries.zh: 太祖總兵，凝式候於軍門，且以年老不任庶事上訴，太祖特為奏免之。
entries.en: When the future Taizu took command of the army, Ningshi waited at the camp gate and petitioned that age made him unfit for routine duties; Taizu had him specially excused by memorial.
entries.literal: When Taizu took command of the army, Ningshi waited at the army gate and moreover memorialized that he was old and unfit for miscellaneous duties; Taizu specially memorialized to exempt him.

entries.zh: 廣順中，表求致政，尋以右僕射得請。
entries.en: In the Guangshun era he petitioned to retire and soon received permission as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the Guangshun era he submitted a memorial requesting retirement from office, and shortly obtained it as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 顯德初，改左僕射，又改太子太保，並懸車。
entries.en: At the start of the Xiande era he was made Left Vice Director, then Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, retiring from each post.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was changed to Left Vice Director, then again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and in both cases hung up his carriage.

entries.zh: 元年冬，卒於洛陽，年八十五。
entries.en: He died at Luoyang in the winter of the first year, aged eighty-five.
entries.literal: In the winter of the first year he died at Luoyang, aged eighty-five.

entries.zh: 詔贈太子太傅。
entries.en: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: By edict he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 王朴，字文伯，東平人也。
entries.en: Wang Pu, whose style was Wenbo, came from Dongping.
entries.literal: Wang Pu, styled Wenbo, was a native of Dongping.

entries.zh: 父序，以朴貴，贈左諫議大夫。
entries.en: His father Wang Xu, on account of Pu's rise, was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Remonstrator.
entries.literal: His father Xu, because of Pu's eminence, was posthumously granted Left Remonstrator.

entries.zh: 朴幼警慧，好學善屬文。
entries.en: As a boy Pu was exceptionally bright, devoted to learning, and adept at literary writing.
entries.literal: Pu in youth was quick-witted and clever, fond of study and skilled at composition.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐中，擢進士第，解褐授校書郎，依樞密使楊邠，館於邠第。
entries.en: During the Later Han reign era Qianyou he took the jinshi degree, entered service as Collator, and served under Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Bin, living as a guest in Bin's household.
entries.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han he passed the jinshi examination, left the commoner's dress and was appointed Collator, attached to the Commissioner of Military Affairs Yang Bin, and lodged at Bin's residence.

entries.zh: 是時漢室浸亂，大臣交惡，朴度其必危，因乞告東歸。
entries.en: The Han court was then sliding into chaos and its leading ministers were feuding; Pu foresaw disaster and asked permission to go home to the east.
entries.literal: At that time the Han house was gradually falling into disorder and great ministers were at odds with one another; Pu judged that it would surely become perilous and therefore requested leave to return east.

entries.zh: 未幾，李業輩作亂，害邠等三族，凡遊其門下者，多被其禍，而朴獨免。
entries.en: Soon afterward Li Ye and his associates rebelled and wiped out Bin's clan and two related families; most who had associated with them perished, but Pu alone was spared.
entries.literal: Before long Li Ye and his faction raised a disturbance, killing the three clans of Bin and the like; all who had frequented their gates mostly suffered that calamity, yet Pu alone escaped.

entries.zh: 國初，世宗鎮澶淵，朝廷以朴為記室。
entries.en: Early in the Zhou dynasty, while the future Emperor Shizong held Chanyuan, the court named Pu his recorder.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the state, when Shizong was stationed at Chanyuan, the court appointed Pu as recorder.

entries.zh: 及世宗為開封尹，拜右拾遺，充開封府推官。
entries.en: When Shizong became Intendant of Kaifeng, Pu was made Right Reminder and assigned as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural government.
entries.literal: When Shizong became Intendant of Kaifeng, he was appointed Right Reminder and served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣位，授比部郎中，賜紫。
entries.en: After Shizong acceded, Pu was appointed Director of the Bureau of Review and awarded the purple robe of high office.
entries.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was granted Director of the Bureau of Review and presented with purple robes.

entries.zh: 二年夏，世宗命朝廷文學之士二十餘人，各撰策論一首，以試其才。
entries.en: In the summer of his second year Shizong directed more than twenty learned officials at court each to write a policy essay as a test of their ability.
entries.literal: In the summer of the second year Shizong ordered more than twenty literary men of the court each to compose one policy essay to test their talent.

entries.zh: 時朴獻《平邊策》，云：
entries.en: Pu then presented his "Strategy for Pacifying the Borders," which read:
entries.literal: At that time Pu submitted the "Strategy for Pacifying the Borders," saying:

entries.zh: 常思，字克恭，太原人也。
entries.en: Chang Si, whose style name was Kegong, came from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Chang Si, style name Kegong, was a native of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 父仁嶽，河東牙將，累贈太子太師。
entries.en: His father Ren Yue had served as a military adjutant in Hedong and was posthumously honored on several occasions as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: His father Ren Yue was a Hedong military adjutant and was repeatedly posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗之為晉王也，廣募勝兵，時思以趫悍應募，累從戎役，後為長直都校，歷捧聖軍使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong of Tang was still Prince of Jin, he recruited elite troops on a wide scale; Si enlisted then for his swift, fierce prowess, fought in campaign after campaign, later became chief officer of the Long-Duty Guard, and in time rose to command the Fengsheng Army.
entries.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong was Prince of Jin he widely recruited elite soldiers; Si at the time enlisted on account of his swift daring, took part repeatedly in campaigns, later became chief officer of the Long-Duty Guard, and successively served as commander of the Fengsheng Army.

entries.zh: 晉初，遷六軍都虞候。
entries.en: Early in the Jin period he was transferred to chief inspector of the Six Armies.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jin period he was promoted to chief inspector of the Six Armies.

entries.zh: 漢高祖出鎮並門，奏以思從行，尋表為河東牢城都指揮使，以勤幹見稱。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Han took up his post at Bing Gate, he had Si accompany him by memorial; Si was soon appointed commander of the Hedong fortress garrison and became known for his diligent, capable service.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu went out to govern Bingmen he memorialized that Si should accompany him; soon afterward he was recommended as commander of the Hedong fortress garrison and won praise for diligence and competence.

entries.zh: 漢國初建，授檢校太保，遙領鄧州。
entries.en: At the founding of the Han state he received the acting title Grand Guardian and was given nominal jurisdiction over Deng Prefecture.
entries.literal: When the Han state was first established he was appointed acting Grand Guardian and given nominal charge of Deng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 漢有天下，遷檢校太尉、昭義軍節度使。
entries.en: Once Han held the empire, he was promoted to acting Grand Marshal and appointed military governor of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: When Han held the realm he was transferred to acting Grand Marshal and made military governor of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 乾佑初，李守貞叛於河中，太祖征之，朝廷命思帥部兵以副焉。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianyou, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong; Taizu marched against him, and the court ordered Si to lead his division in support.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong; Taizu campaigned against him, and the court ordered Si to lead his troops as a supporting force.

entries.zh: 既而禦眾無能，勒歸舊藩。
entries.en: Before long he proved unable to handle the troops and was ordered to return to his former fief.
entries.literal: Before long he proved unable to command the troops and was ordered back to his former commandery.

entries.zh: 思在上黨凡五年，無令譽可稱，唯以聚斂為務，性又鄙吝，未嘗與賓佐有酒肴之會。
entries.en: Si spent five years in all at Shangdang without a reputation worth the name; he devoted himself solely to squeezing revenue, and by nature he was coarse and miserly—he never once shared food and wine with his staff.
entries.literal: Si spent five years altogether at Shangdang with no reputation worth mentioning; he devoted himself solely to extortion, and by nature he was mean and stingy, never once hosting his staff with food and wine.

entries.zh: 嘗有從事欲求謁見者，思覽刺而怒曰：「彼必是來獵酒也。」
entries.en: Once a staff member asked to see him; Si read the calling card and snapped, "He must be coming to scrounge wine."
entries.literal: Once a staff member sought an audience; Si read his calling card and said angrily, "He must be coming to hunt for wine."

entries.zh: 命典客者飲而遣之，其鄙吝也如是。
entries.en: He told the usher to give the man a drink and send him away—such was his meanness.
entries.literal: He ordered the usher to give him drink and send him away—such was his stinginess.

entries.zh: 太祖受命，就加平章事。
entries.en: When Taizu received the Mandate, Si was at once made a Councilor of State.
entries.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate he was immediately given the title of Councilor.

entries.zh: 初，太祖微時，以季父待思，及即位，遣其妻入覲，太祖拜之如家人之禮，仍呼曰叔母，其恩顧如是。
entries.en: In the old days, when Taizu was still obscure, he had treated Si as a younger uncle; after he took the throne he had Si's wife come to court, bowed to her with the courtesy of family, and still called her Aunt—such was the grace he showed them.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Taizu was still obscure, he had treated Si as a younger uncle; after his accession he sent Si's wife to court for an audience, and Taizu bowed to her with the courtesy due a kinswoman and still addressed her as Aunt—such was the favor shown him.

entries.zh: 廣順二年秋，思來朝，加兼侍中，移鎮宋州。
entries.en: In the autumn of Guangshun year two, Si came to court, was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, and was transferred to Song Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Guangshun, Si came to court, was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, and was transferred to govern Song Prefecture.

entries.zh: 三年夏，詔赴闕，改授平盧軍節度使。
entries.en: In the summer of year three he was summoned to court by edict and reassigned as military governor of Pinglu.
entries.literal: In the summer of the third year an edict summoned him to the capital and he was reassigned as military governor of Pinglu.

entries.zh: 思將赴鎮，奏太祖云：「臣在宋州出鎮，得絲十餘萬兩，謹以上進，請行征督。」
entries.en: As Si was about to leave for his new command he memorialized Taizu: "When I departed Song Prefecture I had more than a hundred thousand taels of silk, which I respectfully offer upward; please have it levied and collected."
entries.literal: As Si was about to take up his new post he memorialized Taizu, saying, "When I left my post at Song Prefecture I had more than a hundred thousand taels of silk, which I respectfully present to Your Majesty; please levy and collect it."

entries.zh: 太祖頷之，尋詔本州折券以諭其民。
entries.en: Taizu nodded, and soon an edict ordered that prefecture to cancel the tax bonds and notify the people.
entries.literal: Taizu nodded assent, and soon an edict ordered that prefecture to cancel the bonds and inform the people.

entries.zh: 及到鎮，未幾，染風痹之疾，上表請尋醫，既而舁疾歸洛。
entries.en: Not long after he reached his post he fell ill with wind paralysis; he memorialized asking permission to seek a physician, and was soon carried home to Luoyang on a litter.
entries.literal: After he reached his post, before long he contracted wind-paralysis; he memorialized asking to seek medical treatment and was soon carried home ill to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 顯德元年春卒，年六十有九。
entries.en: In the spring of Xiande year one he died, at the age of sixty-nine.
entries.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande he died, aged sixty-nine.

entries.zh: 贈中書令。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted the title Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 翟光鄴，字化基，濮州鄄城人。
entries.en: Di Guangye, whose style name was Huaji, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
entries.literal: Di Guangye, style name Huaji, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.

entries.zh: 父景珂，倜儻有膽氣。
entries.en: His father Jing Ke was bold and daring by nature.
entries.literal: His father Jing Ke was bold and free-spirited and had courage.

entries.zh: 梁貞明初，唐莊宗始駐軍於河上，景珂率聚邑人守永定驛，固守逾年，後為北軍所攻，景珂戰歿，眾潰。
entries.en: In the first year of Liang Zhenming, Zhuangzong of Tang first encamped his army on the Yellow River; Jing Ke led the people of his district to hold Yongding Post, held firm for more than a year, was later attacked by the northern army, fell in battle, and his force broke.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenming of Liang, Tang Zhuangzong first stationed his army on the Yellow River; Jing Ke led the people of his district to hold Yongding Post, defended it for more than a year, and was later attacked by the northern army; Jing Ke died in battle and the host scattered.

entries.zh: 光鄴時年十歲，為明宗軍所俘，以其穎悟，俾侍左右，字之曰永定。
entries.en: Guangye was then ten; Mingzong's army captured him, and because he was bright they had him wait at the ruler's side and gave him the style name Yongding.
entries.literal: Guangye was then ten years old; he was captured by Mingzong's army, and because he was clever they had him attend at the ruler's side and gave him the style name Yongding.

entries.zh: 既冠，沈毅有謀，蒞事寡過。
entries.en: Once he came of age he was grave, resolute, and resourceful, and rarely erred in office.
entries.literal: After he came of age he was steady and resolute, full of plans, and rarely erred in office.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，時深委遇，累遷至皇城使、檢校司空。
entries.en: When Mingzong acceded, Guangye enjoyed his deep trust and in time rose to Imperial City Commissioner and acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Guangye was deeply trusted and in time rose to Imperial City Commissioner and acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 長興中，樞密使安重誨得罪，時光鄴與中官孟小僧頗有力焉。
entries.en: During Changxing, when Chief Councilor An Chonghui fell from favor, Guangye and the eunuch Meng Xiaoseng had played a considerable part.
entries.literal: During Changxing, when Chief Councilor An Chonghui fell from favor, Guangye at the time had considerable influence together with the eunuch Meng Xiaoseng.

entries.zh: 居無何，出為耀州團練使。
entries.en: Before long he was sent out as regimental commissioner of Yao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Before long he was sent out as regimental commissioner of Yao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 清泰初，入為左監門衛大將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Qingtai he entered court service as Grand General of the Left Directorate of the Gate Guards.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingtai he entered service as Grand General of the Left Directorate of the Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，歷棣沂二州刺史、西京副留守。
entries.en: During Jin Tianfu he served in turn as prefect of Di and Yi and as deputy defender of the Western Capital.
entries.literal: During Jin Tianfu he successively served as prefect of Di and Yi prefectures and as deputy defender of the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 開運初，授宣徽使。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaiyun he was appointed Commissioner of the Palace Directorate.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun he was appointed Commissioner of the Palace Directorate.

entries.zh: 楊光遠叛滅，青州平，除為防禦使，朝廷以兵亂之後，人物雕弊，故命光鄴理之。
entries.en: After Yang Guangyuan's rebellion was crushed and Qingzhou pacified, he was made defense commissioner; the court, seeing how war had ravaged the region and thinned the population, put Guangye in charge of restoring it.
entries.literal: When Yang Guangyuan's rebellion was crushed and Qingzhou pacified, he was made defense commissioner; because after the military turmoil the population was devastated, the court ordered Guangye to administer the region.

entries.zh: 光鄴好聚書，重儒者，虛齋論議，惟求理道。
entries.en: Guangye loved to gather books, honored Confucian scholars, and in his quiet study held discussions aimed solely at principle.
entries.literal: Guangye loved to collect books, honored Confucian scholars, and in his empty study held discussions seeking only the Way.

entries.zh: 時郡民喪亡十之六七，而招懷撫諭，視之如傷，故期月之間，流亡載輯。
entries.en: Six or seven tenths of the prefecture's people had died, yet he recruited, comforted, and instructed the survivors as though tending the wounded, and within a month refugees were streaming back.
entries.literal: At the time six or seven tenths of the prefecture's people had perished, yet he recruited, comforted, and instructed them, treating their wounds as his own, so that within a month exiles were returning in crowds.

entries.zh: 契丹入汴，偽命權知曹州。
entries.en: When the Khitan entered Bian, a puppet regime named him acting prefect of Cao.
entries.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, a puppet appointment made him acting prefect of Cao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 李從益假號，以光鄴明宗舊臣，署為樞密使。
entries.en: Li Congyi took a false title; because Guangye was an old minister of Mingzong, he appointed him Chief Councilor.
entries.literal: Li Congyi assumed a false title and, because Guangye was an old minister of Mingzong, appointed him Chief Councilor.

entries.zh: 漢祖至汴，改左領衛大將軍。
entries.en: When the Han founder reached Bian, Guangye was reassigned as Grand General of the Left Leading Guard.
entries.literal: When the Han founder reached Bian he was changed to Grand General of the Left Leading Guard.

entries.zh: 乾祐初，遷右金吾衛大將軍，充街使、檢校太保。
entries.en: In Qianyou year one he was promoted to Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, made street commissioner, and given the acting title Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou he was promoted to Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, served as street commissioner, and was given the acting title Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 太祖踐阼，復授宣徽使、左千牛衛上將軍、檢校太傅。
entries.en: When Taizu acceded he was again made Commissioner of the Palace Directorate, Grand General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard, and acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he was again appointed Commissioner of the Palace Directorate, Grand General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard, and acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 數月，兼樞密副使。
entries.en: Several months later he was also made Deputy Chief Councilor.
entries.literal: Several months later he was also made Deputy Chief Councilor.

entries.zh: 會永興李洪信入朝，代知軍府事。
entries.en: When Li Hongxin of Yongxing came to court, Guangye acted in his stead administering the military government.
entries.literal: When Li Hongxin of Yongxing came to court, Guangye acted in his stead as administrator of the military government.

entries.zh: 廣順二年十月，卒於長安，時年四十六。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Guangshun year two he died at Chang'an, aged forty-six.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Guangshun he died at Chang'an, aged forty-six.

entries.zh: 曹英，字德秀，舊名犯今上御名，故改焉。
entries.en: Cao Ying, whose style name was Dexiu, bore an original given name that violated the present emperor's taboo and was therefore changed.
entries.literal: Cao Ying, style name Dexiu, had an original name that violated the present emperor's taboo name and was therefore changed.

entries.zh: 本常山鎮定人也。
entries.en: He was originally from Zhen in Changshan.
entries.literal: He was originally a native of Zhen in Changshan.

entries.zh: 父全武，事趙王王镕為列校，英因得隸於镕之帳下。
entries.en: His father Quanwu had served Prince Zhao Wang Rong as a company commander, and Ying came to serve in Rong's headquarters.
entries.literal: His father Quanwu served Prince Zhao Wang Rong as a company commander, and Ying thereby came to serve in Rong's headquarters.

entries.zh: 及張文禮之亂，唐莊宗奄有其地，乃錄镕之左右，署為散指揮使。
entries.en: When Zhang Wenli rebelled, Zhuangzong of Tang suddenly seized the region and enrolled Rong's attendants, appointing Ying a scattered commander.
entries.literal: When Zhang Wenli's rebellion broke out, Tang Zhuangzong suddenly seized that territory and enrolled Rong's attendants, appointing Ying a scattered commander.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，英侍於仗下，問其祖考，英以實對，明宗曰：「乃朕之舊也。」
entries.en: When Mingzong acceded, Ying stood attendance below the imperial halberds; the emperor asked about his forebears and Ying answered truthfully; Mingzong said, "So you are one of my old associates."
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Ying attended below the imperial halberds; the emperor asked about his forebears and Ying answered truthfully; Mingzong said, "So you are one of my old associates."

entries.zh: 擢為本班行首，每加顧遇。
entries.en: He was promoted to head of his guard company and won repeated favor.
entries.literal: He was promoted to head of his guard company and received repeated favor.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，遷弩手軍使。
entries.en: During Jin Tianfu he was transferred to commander of the Crossbow Hand Army.
entries.literal: During Jin Tianfu he was transferred to commander of the Crossbow Hand Army.

entries.zh: 平張從賓於汜水，以功授本軍都校。
entries.en: When Zhang Congbin was pacified at Sishui he was made company commander of his own army for his merit.
entries.literal: When Zhang Congbin was pacified at Sishui he was given command of his own army's company for merit.

entries.zh: 漢初，改奉國軍主，加檢校司徒，兼康州刺史。
entries.en: Early in Han he was made commander of the Fengguo Army, given the acting title of Situ, and concurrently prefect of Kang.
entries.literal: Early in Han he was made commander of the Fengguo Army, given the acting title of Situ, and concurrently made prefect of Kang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 乾祐初，李守貞據河中叛，授行營步軍都校。
entries.en: In Qianyou year one, when Li Shouzhen held Hezhong in rebellion, he was appointed company commander of the campaign army's foot soldiers.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou, when Li Shouzhen held Hezhong in rebellion, he was appointed company commander of the campaign army's infantry.

entries.zh: 河中平，遷本軍廂主，領岳州防禦使。
entries.en: When Hezhong was pacified he was made wing commander of his army and given nominal charge as defense commissioner of Yue.
entries.literal: When Hezhong was pacified he was transferred to commander of his army's wing and given nominal charge as defense commissioner of Yue Prefecture.

entries.zh: 隨太祖在魏，為北面行營步軍都校，從平內難。
entries.en: Following Taizu at Wei he served as company commander of the northern campaign army's foot soldiers and helped quell the internal crisis.
entries.literal: Following Taizu at Wei he served as company commander of the northern campaign army's infantry and took part in pacifying the internal crisis.

entries.zh: 國初，以翊戴功授昭武節度使、檢校太傅、侍衛步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: At the founding of the dynasty, for his merit in supporting the enthronement he was made military governor of Zhaowu, acting Grand Tutor, and commander of the palace guard foot soldiers.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state, for his merit in supporting the enthronement he was made military governor of Zhaowu, acting Grand Tutor, and commander of the palace guard infantry.

entries.zh: 二年春，總兵討慕容彥超於兗州，梯沖塹壘，頗有力焉。
entries.en: In the spring of year two he led troops against Murong Yanchao at Yan Prefecture; in scaling ladders, rams, ditches, and ramparts he played a major part.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year he led troops against Murong Yanchao at Yan Prefecture; in assault ladders, rams, ditches, and ramparts he contributed considerable strength.

entries.zh: 夏五月，太祖親征，因並兵攻陷其城，及凱旋，領彰信軍節度使，典軍如故。
entries.en: In the fifth month of summer Taizu campaigned in person; the armies were combined, the city stormed and taken; on the return in triumph he was given Zhangxin Army while keeping command of the troops as before.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer Taizu campaigned in person; the armies were combined and the city stormed and taken; on the triumphal return he was given charge of Zhangxin Army while retaining command of the troops as before.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣位，加同平章事，授成德軍節度使。
entries.en: When Shizong succeeded he was made a Councilor and military governor of Chengde.
entries.literal: When Shizong succeeded he was given the title of Councilor and made military governor of Chengde.

entries.zh: 車駕自太原回，加兼侍中。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage returned from Taiyuan he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Taiyuan he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 顯德元年冬，卒於鎮，時年四十九。
entries.en: In the winter of Xiande year one he died at his post, aged forty-nine.
entries.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xiande he died at his post, aged forty-nine.

entries.zh: 制贈中書令。
entries.en: An edict posthumously granted him the office of Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the office of Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 英性沈厚，謙恭有禮，雖衽席之際，接對賓客，亦未嘗造次。
entries.en: Ying was deep and steady by nature, humble and courteous; even beside his own mat he never treated guests with casual abruptness.
entries.literal: Ying's nature was deep and steady, humble and courteous; even at his own mat he never treated guests rashly when receiving them.

entries.zh: 及卒，搢紳之士亦皆惜之。
entries.en: When he died, men of the gentry mourned him as well.
entries.literal: When he died the gentry also all mourned him.

entries.zh: 李彥頵，字德循，太原人也。
entries.en: Li Yanyun, whose style name was Dexun, came from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Li Yanyun, style name Dexun, was a native of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 本以商賈為業，太祖鎮鄴，置之左右，及即位，歷綾錦副使、搉易使。
entries.en: He had originally been a merchant; when Taizu governed Ye he kept Yanyun at his side, and after the accession Yanyun served in turn as deputy commissioner of brocade and silk and as monopoly commissioner.
entries.literal: He had originally been a merchant; when Taizu governed Ye he placed him at his side, and after the accession he successively served as deputy commissioner of brocade and silk and as commissioner of the state monopoly.

entries.zh: 世宗嗣位，以彥頵有舊，超授內客省使。
entries.en: When Shizong succeeded, because Yanyun was an old associate he was abruptly made Commissioner of the Inner Guests Directorate.
entries.literal: When Shizong succeeded, because Yanyun was an old associate he was abruptly appointed Commissioner of the Inner Guests Directorate.

entries.zh: 未幾，知相州軍府事，尋改延州兵馬留後。
entries.en: Before long he was put in charge of Xiang Prefecture's military government; soon afterward he was made military commander of Yan.
entries.literal: Before long he was made administrator of Xiang Prefecture's military government; soon afterward he was changed to military commander of Yan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 到鎮，頗以殖貨為意，窺圖剩利，侵漁蕃漢部人，群情大擾。
entries.en: Once at his post he was much intent on amassing wealth, scheming for surplus profit and squeezing both tribal and Han subjects until the region was in uproar.
entries.literal: On reaching his post he was much intent on amassing wealth, scheming for surplus profit and plundering both tribal and Han subjects until popular feeling was greatly disturbed.

entries.zh: 會世宗南征，蕃部結聚，圍迫州城，彥頵閉壁自守，求援於鄰道，賴救兵至，乃解。
entries.en: When Shizong marched south the tribal peoples gathered and pressed the prefectural city; Yanyun shut the walls and held out, sought aid from neighboring circuits, and only when relief arrived was the siege lifted.
entries.literal: When Shizong marched south the tribal peoples gathered and pressed the prefectural city; Yanyun shut the walls and held out, sought aid from neighboring circuits, and only when relief troops arrived was the siege lifted.

entries.zh: 世宗不悅，征赴京師，然猶委曲庇護，竟不之責。
entries.en: Shizong was displeased and summoned him to the capital, yet still sheltered him tactfully and in the end did not hold him accountable.
entries.literal: Shizong was displeased and summoned him to the capital, yet still sheltered him tactfully and in the end did not punish him.

entries.zh: 尋為西京水南巡檢使，居無何，命權知泗州軍州事，改滄州兩使留後。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made inspector of the Western Capital's south-of-the-water circuit; before long he was ordered to act as military governor of Si and then made dual commissioner of Cang.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was made inspector of the Western Capital's south-of-the-water circuit; before long he was ordered to act as military governor of Si Prefecture and then made dual commissioner of Cang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 彥頵到任，處置乖方，大為物情所鄙。
entries.en: When Yanyun took up his post his arrangements were ill judged and public opinion held him in contempt.
entries.literal: When Yanyun took up his post his arrangements were ill judged and he was widely despised in public sentiment.

entries.zh: 顯德六年秋，受代歸闕，遇疾而卒，時年五十有二。
entries.en: In the autumn of Xiande year six he was relieved and returned to court; he fell ill on the way and died, aged fifty-two.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Xiande he was relieved and returned to court; he fell ill on the way and died, aged fifty-two.

entries.zh: 李暉，字順光，瀛州束城人。
entries.en: Li Hui, whose style name was Shunguang, came from Dongcheng in Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Hui, style name Shunguang, was a native of Dongcheng in Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 弱冠應募於龍驤軍，漢祖領河東，暉請從，因得署為河東牙將。
entries.en: In his youth he enlisted in the Dragon-Soaring Army; when the Han founder took charge of Hedong, Hui asked to follow him and was appointed a Hedong military adjutant.
entries.literal: In his youth he enlisted in the Dragon Soaring Army; when the Han founder took charge of Hedong, Hui asked to follow and was appointed a Hedong military adjutant.

entries.zh: 漢有天下，授檢校司徒、大內皇城使。
entries.en: When Han held the empire he was given the acting title of Situ and made commissioner of the Inner Imperial City.
entries.literal: When Han held the realm he was given the acting title of Situ and made commissioner of the Inner Imperial City.

entries.zh: 未幾，遷宣徽南院使。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred to Commissioner of the Southern Palace Directorate.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Commissioner of the Southern Palace Directorate.

entries.zh: 乾祐初，拜河陽節度使、檢校太傅。
entries.en: In Qianyou year one he was appointed military governor of Heyang and acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou he was appointed military governor of Heyang and acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 太祖登極，加同平章事，尋移鎮滄州。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne he was made a Councilor and soon transferred to Cang Prefecture.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he was given the title of Councilor and soon transferred to govern Cang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 顯德元年，就加兼侍中。
entries.en: In Xiande year one he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant in situ.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant on the spot.

entries.zh: 二年秋，以世宗誕慶節來朝，改邠州節度使。
entries.en: In the autumn of year two he came to court for Shizong's birthday celebration and was transferred to military governor of Bin.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year he came to court for Shizong's birthday celebration and was transferred to military governor of Bin.

entries.zh: 五年，移鎮鳳翔。
entries.en: In year five he was transferred to Fengxiang.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to govern Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 歲餘，卒於鎮。
entries.en: A little more than a year later he died at his post.
entries.literal: After a little more than a year he died at his post.

entries.zh: 優詔贈中書令。
entries.en: A gracious edict posthumously granted him the office of Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: A gracious edict posthumously granted him the office of Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 暉之儀貌不及於常人，而位極將相，年登耳順，袁、許之術，夫何恃哉！
entries.en: Hui's looks fell short of the ordinary, yet he rose to the summit of general and minister and lived to sixty—what need had he of the arts of Yuan and Xu!
entries.literal: Hui's bearing and appearance fell short of ordinary men, yet he rose to the summit of general and minister, lived to the age of sixty—what did he rely on from the arts of Yuan and Xu!

entries.zh: 然性貪鄙，而好小惠以邀虛譽，故在河陽及滄州日，民皆詣闕請立碑以頌其美，識者亦未之許也。
entries.en: Yet he was greedy and base by nature and liked petty favors to win empty praise; so while at Heyang and Cang the people all petitioned the court to erect steles praising his virtue, but the discerning did not approve.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he was greedy and base, and liked petty favors to win empty praise; therefore while at Heyang and Cang Prefecture the people all went to court asking to erect steles praising his virtue, yet the knowing did not approve.

entries.zh: 李建崇，潞州人。
entries.en: Li Jianchong came from Luzhou.
entries.literal: Li Jianchong was a native of Luzhou.

entries.zh: 少從軍，善騎射。
entries.en: In his youth he took up arms and was skilled at mounted archery.
entries.literal: In his youth he joined the army and was skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 初事唐武皇，為鐵林都將，轉突騎、飛騎二軍使。
entries.en: He first served Wuhuang of Tang as a commander of the Iron Forest Guard, then rose to command the Sudden Cavalry and Flying Cavalry armies.
entries.literal: He first served Tang Wuhuang as commander of the Iron Forest Guard, then became commander of the Sudden Cavalry and Flying Cavalry armies.

entries.zh: 從莊宗攻常山，阿保機來援，莊宗率親軍千騎，遇於滿城，兵少，為契丹所圍。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong attacked Changshan, Abaoji came to the enemy's aid; Zhuangzong led a thousand horse of his personal guard, met them at Mancheng with too few men, and was surrounded by the Khitan.
entries.literal: Following Zhuangzong's attack on Changshan, Abaoji came to their aid; Zhuangzong led a thousand horse of the personal army, met them at Mancheng, had too few troops, and was surrounded by the Khitan.

entries.zh: 時建崇為親將，與契丹格鬥，自午至申，會李嗣昭騎至，契丹乃解去。
entries.en: Jianchong was then a commander of the personal guard; he fought the Khitan from noon to late afternoon, until Li Sizhao's cavalry arrived and the Khitan broke off.
entries.literal: Jianchong was then a personal commander; he fought the Khitan from the noon hour to the shen hour; when Li Sizhao's cavalry arrived the Khitan withdrew.

entries.zh: 同光中，自龍武捧聖都指揮使，出歷襄、秦、徐、雍都指揮使。
entries.en: During Tongguang he rose from commander of the Dragon Martial Fengsheng Guard to serve in turn as army commander of Xiang, Qin, Xu, and Yong.
entries.literal: During Tongguang he rose from commander of the Dragon Martial Fengsheng Guard to successively serve as army commander of Xiang, Qin, Xu, and Yong.

entries.zh: 建崇性純厚，處身任遇，不能巧宦，以致久滯偏裨。
entries.en: Jianchong was plain and honest by nature; in how he carried himself and won appointments he could not play the courtier, and so long remained a subordinate officer.
entries.literal: Jianchong's nature was simple and honest; in conduct and appointment he could not practice clever office-holding, so he long remained at subordinate ranks.

entries.zh: 明宗嘗掌牙兵，與建崇共事，及即位，甚湣之，連授磁、沁二郡。
entries.en: Mingzong had once commanded the guard troops alongside Jianchong; when he took the throne he pitied him deeply and in succession gave him Ci and Qin.
entries.literal: Mingzong had once commanded the guard troops and worked with Jianchong; when he took the throne he pitied him greatly and successively gave him Ci and Qin prefectures.

entries.zh: 入晉為申州刺史。
entries.en: In Jin service he became prefect of Shen.
entries.literal: Entering Jin service he became prefect of Shen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 天福七年冬，襄州安從進構逆，率眾寇南陽，時建崇領步騎千餘屯於葉縣，開封尹鄭王遣宣徽使張從恩、皇城使焦繼勛率在京諸軍，會建崇軍拒賊，至湖陽縣之花山，遇從進軍，建崇接戰，大敗之，以功授亳州團練使。
entries.en: In the winter of Tianfu year seven, An Congjin of Xiangzhou rebelled and led troops against Nanyang; Jianchong then commanded more than a thousand foot and horse at Ye County; the Prince of Zheng, as Kaifeng intendant, sent Palace Commissioner Zhang Congen and Imperial City Commissioner Jiao Jixun with the capital armies to join Jianchong; at Huashan in Huyang they met Congjin's force, Jianchong gave battle and routed them, and for his merit was made regimental commissioner of Bo.
entries.literal: In the winter of the seventh year of Tianfu, An Congjin of Xiangyang plotted rebellion and led troops to raid Nanyang; Jianchong then led more than a thousand foot and horse stationed at Ye County; the Prince of Zheng as Kaifeng intendant sent Palace Commissioner Zhang Congen and Imperial City Commissioner Jiao Jixun to lead the capital armies, join Jianchong's force to resist the rebels, and at Huashan in Huyang County met Congjin's army; Jianchong engaged and routed them, and for merit was made regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

entries.zh: 襄陽平，遷安州防禦使。
entries.en: When Xiangyang was pacified he was transferred to defense commissioner of An.
entries.literal: When Xiangyang was pacified he was transferred to defense commissioner of An.

entries.zh: 歷河陽、邢州兵馬留後。
entries.en: He served in turn as military commander of Heyang and Xing.
entries.literal: He successively served as military commander of Heyang and Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 漢初，入為右衛大將軍。
entries.en: Early in Han he entered court service as Grand General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: Early in Han he entered service as Grand General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 年逾七十，神氣不衰。
entries.en: Past seventy, his spirit and vigor had not waned.
entries.literal: Past seventy, his spirit and vigor did not decline.

entries.zh: 建崇始自代北事武皇，至是四十餘年，前後所掌兵，麾下部曲多至節鉞，零落殆盡，惟建崇雖位不及藩屏，而康強自適，以至期耄。
entries.en: Jianchong had followed Wuhuang from the northern frontier; by now more than forty years had passed; of the troops he had led, many subordinates had risen to military governorships and nearly all were gone—only Jianchong, though he never reached a frontier command, stayed hale and content even to great old age.
entries.literal: Jianchong had served Wuhuang from the northern Dai region; by now more than forty years had passed; of the troops he had commanded, many subordinates had risen to military governorships and nearly all had fallen away—only Jianchong, though his rank never reached a frontier command, remained hale and at ease even to extreme old age.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，授左監門衛上將軍。
entries.en: When Taizu acceded he was appointed Grand General of the Left Directorate of the Gate Guards.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he was appointed Grand General of the Left Directorate of the Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 廣順三年春卒。
entries.en: In the spring of Guangshun year three he died.
entries.literal: In the spring of the third year of Guangshun he died.

entries.zh: 贈黔南節度使。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor of Qiannan.
entries.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as military governor of Qiannan.

entries.zh: 齊藏珍，少歷內職，累遷諸衛將軍。
entries.en: Qi Cangzhen in youth held inner-court posts and rose through the guard generalships.
entries.literal: Qi Cangzhen in youth held inner palace posts and rose through the various guard generalships.

entries.zh: 前後監押兵師在外，頗稱幹事，然險诐無行，殘忍辯給，無不畏其利口。
entries.en: He repeatedly supervised troops abroad and was called capable, yet he was treacherous, cruel, and glib, and all feared his sharp tongue.
entries.literal: He repeatedly supervised troops abroad and was praised as capable, yet he was treacherous and without conduct, cruel and glib, and none did not fear his sharp tongue.

entries.zh: 廣順中，奉命滑州界巡護河堤，以弛慢致河決，除名，配沙門島。
entries.en: During Guangshun he patrolled the Yellow River dikes on the Hua border; through negligence the river broke through; he was dismissed and exiled to Shamen Island.
entries.literal: During Guangshun he was ordered to patrol the Yellow River dikes on the Hua Prefecture border; through negligence the river broke its banks; he was dismissed from office and exiled to Shamen Island.

entries.zh: 世宗在西班時，與藏珍同列，每聆其談論，或剖判世務，似有可采。
entries.en: When Shizong sat in the western class he and Cangzhen were colleagues; Shizong often heard him discuss affairs and judge the times as though there were something worth taking.
entries.literal: When Shizong was in the western class he and Cangzhen were colleagues; whenever he heard Cangzhen's talk, whether dissecting cases or judging affairs of the age, it seemed there was something to glean.

entries.zh: 及即位，自流所征還。
entries.en: When he acceded he was recalled from exile.
entries.literal: When he took the throne he was recalled from exile.

entries.zh: 秦、鳳之役，令監偏師。
entries.en: In the Qin-Feng campaign he was ordered to supervise a detached column.
entries.literal: In the Qin-Feng campaign he was ordered to supervise a detached force.

entries.zh: 及淮上用兵，復委監護，與軍校何超領兵降下光州。
entries.en: When the Huai campaign began he was again entrusted to supervise; with army commander He Chao he led troops to take Guang Prefecture.
entries.literal: When troops were used on the Huai he was again entrusted with supervision; with army commander He Chao he led troops to reduce Guang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 藏珍欺隱官物甚多，超以為不可，藏珍曰：「沙門島已有屋數間，不妨再去矣。」
entries.en: Cangzhen concealed much government property; Chao objected; Cangzhen said, "Shamen Island already has several rooms—it would not hurt to go again."
entries.literal: Cangzhen concealed much government property; Chao thought this wrong; Cangzhen said, "Shamen Island already has several rooms—going again would not hurt."

entries.zh: 其不畏法也如此。
entries.en: Such was his contempt for the law.
entries.literal: Such was his fearlessness of the law.

entries.zh: 世宗既破紫金山寨，追吳寇室渦口，因與藏珍言及克捷之狀。
entries.en: After Shizong broke the Zijin Mountain camp and pursued the Wu enemy to Shiwokou, he spoke with Cangzhen about the victory.
entries.literal: After Shizong broke the Zijin Mountain camp and pursued the Wu enemy to Shiwokou, he spoke with Cangzhen of the victory.

entries.zh: 對曰：「陛下神武之功，近代無比，於文德則未光。」
entries.en: He replied, "Your Majesty's martial achievement is unmatched in recent times, yet your civil virtue has not yet shone."
entries.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's martial achievement is unmatched in recent times, yet your civil virtue has not yet shone."

entries.zh: 世宗頷之，又問以揚州之事，對曰：「揚州地實卑濕，食物例多腥腐。
entries.en: Shizong nodded and asked about Yangzhou; he replied, "Yangzhou's land is truly low and damp; food there is mostly rank and rotten.
entries.literal: Shizong nodded, and asked about Yangzhou; he replied, "Yangzhou's land is truly low and damp; food there is mostly rank and rotten.

entries.zh: 臣去歲在彼，人以鱔魚饋臣者，視其盤中虬屈，一如蛇虺之狀，假使鸛雀有知，亦應不食，豈況於人哉！」
entries.en: Last year when I was there, someone presented eel; in the dish they writhed like serpents—if storks and magpies had sense they would not eat it, how much less men!"
entries.literal: Last year when I was there, someone presented eel to me; looking at the dish they writhed like snakes—if even storks and magpies had sense they would not eat it, how much less men!"

entries.zh: 其敷奏大率多此類，聞者無不悚然。
entries.en: His memorials were mostly of this kind; hearers were all struck with dread.
entries.literal: His memorials were mostly of this sort; hearers were all struck with dread.

entries.zh: 一日，又奏云：「唐景思已為刺史，臣猶未蒙聖澤。」
entries.en: One day he memorialized again, "Tang Jingsi has already been made prefect, yet I have not yet received Your Majesty's grace."
entries.literal: One day he again memorialized, "Tang Jingsi has already been made prefect, yet I have not yet received the sage's grace."

entries.zh: 世宗俯而從之，時濠梁未下，即命為濠州行州刺史。
entries.en: Shizong assented; Hao and Liang had not yet fallen, and he was at once made acting prefect of Hao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Shizong bowed his head and assented; Hao and Liang had not yet fallen, and he was at once made acting prefect of Hao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 及張永德與李重進有間言，藏珍嘗遊說重進，洎壽陽兵回，諸將中有以藏珍之言上奏者。
entries.en: When Zhang Yongde and Li Chongjin fell out, Cangzhen once urged Chongjin; when the Shouyang army returned, some generals memorialized what Cangzhen had said.
entries.literal: When Zhang Yongde and Li Chongjin had a breach, Cangzhen once urged Chongjin; when the Shouyang army returned, among the generals some memorialized Cangzhen's words.

entries.zh: 世宗怒，急召赴闕。
entries.en: Shizong was angry and urgently summoned him to court.
entries.literal: Shizong was angry and urgently summoned him to court.

entries.zh: 四年夏，以其冒稱檢校官罪，按其事而斃之，蓋不欲暴其惡跡也。
entries.en: In the summer of year four, for falsely claiming an acting official title, his case was investigated and he was put to death—so as not to expose his wicked deeds openly.
entries.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, for the crime of falsely claiming an acting official title, his case was investigated and he was executed—so as not to expose his wicked deeds publicly.

entries.zh: 王環，本真定人。
entries.en: Wang Huan was originally from Zhending.
entries.literal: Wang Huan was originally a native of Zhending.

entries.zh: 唐天成初，孟知祥鎮西川，環往事之，及知祥建號，環累典軍衛，孟昶嗣位，環兼領左、右衛。
entries.en: In Tang Tiancheng year one Meng Zhixiang governed Western Chuan; Huan served him; when Zhixiang declared a state Huan rose through guard commands; when Meng Chang succeeded, Huan held both left and right guards.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tang Tiancheng, Meng Zhixiang governed the Western Chuan; Huan went to serve him; when Zhixiang declared a state Huan rose through military guard posts; when Meng Chang succeeded, Huan concurrently held the left and right guards.

entries.zh: 顯德二年秋，王師西伐，時環為鳳州節度使。
entries.en: In the autumn of Xiande year two the imperial army marched west; Huan was then military governor of Feng.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Xiande the imperial army campaigned west; Huan was then military governor of Feng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 初，偏師傅其城下，為環所敗，裨將胡立為環所擒。
entries.en: At first a detached column reached his walls and was defeated by Huan; deputy commander Hu Li was captured.
entries.literal: At first a detached force reached his walls and was defeated by Huan; deputy general Hu Li was captured by Huan.

entries.zh: 是冬，王師大集，急攻其城，蜀之援兵相次敗走。
entries.en: That winter the main army gathered and pressed the city; Shu relief armies were beaten in succession and fled.
entries.literal: That winter the main army gathered and pressed the city hard; Shu relief armies were defeated in succession and fled.

entries.zh: 環聞之，守備愈堅，王師攻擊數月方克。
entries.en: When Huan heard this his defense grew firmer; the imperial army attacked for months before the city fell.
entries.literal: When Huan heard this his defense grew firmer; the imperial army attacked for months before taking it.

entries.zh: 城陷，環就擒。
entries.en: When the city fell Huan was taken.
entries.literal: When the city fell Huan was captured.

entries.zh: 及到闕，世宗以忠於所事，釋其罪，授若驍衛大將軍。
entries.en: At court Shizong, because he had been loyal to his master, pardoned him and appointed him Grand General of the Xiao Guard.
entries.literal: When he reached court Shizong, because he had been loyal to his master, pardoned his crime and appointed him Grand General of the Xiao Guard.

entries.zh: 四年冬，世宗南征，環隨駕至泗州，遇疾而卒。
entries.en: In the winter of year four Shizong marched south; Huan followed to Si, fell ill, and died.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Shizong campaigned south; Huan followed the carriage to Si Prefecture, fell ill, and died.

entries.zh: 張彥超，本沙陀部人也。
entries.en: Zhang Yanchao was originally of the Shatuo tribe.
entries.literal: Zhang Yanchao was originally of the Shatuo tribe.

entries.zh: 素有郤克之疾，時號為「跛子」。
entries.en: He had long suffered Xi Ke's affliction and was known as "the Lame One."
entries.literal: He had long had Xi Ke's affliction and was at the time called "the Lame One."

entries.zh: 初，以騎射事唐莊宗為馬直軍使，莊宗入汴，授神武指揮使。
entries.en: At first, for mounted archery he served Zhuangzong of Tang as commander of the Horse Guard Army; when Zhuangzong entered Bian he was made commander of the Divine Martial Army.
entries.literal: At first, for his skill in mounted archery he served Tang Zhuangzong as commander of the Horse Guard Army; when Zhuangzong entered Bian he was appointed commander of the Divine Martial Army.

entries.zh: 明宗嘗以為養子。
entries.en: Mingzong once took him as a foster son.
entries.literal: Mingzong once took him as an adopted son.

entries.zh: 天成中，擢授蔚州刺史。
entries.en: During Tiancheng he was promoted to prefect of Yu.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng he was promoted and appointed prefect of Yu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 素與晉高祖不協，屬其總戎於太原，遂舉其城投於契丹，即以為雲州節度使。
entries.en: He had long been at odds with Gaozu of Jin; when Gaozu commanded at Taiyuan he surrendered his city to the Khitan, who made him military governor of Yun.
entries.literal: He had long been at odds with Jin Gaozu; when Gaozu commanded troops at Taiyuan he raised his city in surrender to the Khitan, who then made him military governor of Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 契丹之南侵也，彥超率部眾，頗為鎮、魏之患。
entries.en: When the Khitan marched south, Yanchao led his troops and became a serious scourge to Zhen and Wei.
entries.literal: When the Khitan invaded south, Yanchao led his troops and was a considerable trouble to Zhen and Wei.

entries.zh: 及契丹入汴，遷侍衛馬軍都校，尋授晉昌軍節度使。
entries.en: When the Khitan entered Bian he was made company commander of the palace guard horse army and soon military governor of Jinchang.
entries.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian he was transferred to company commander of the palace guard cavalry and soon appointed military governor of Jinchang.

entries.zh: 漢高祖入洛，彥超飛表輸誠，移授保大軍節度使。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Han entered Luoyang, Yanchao sent an urgent memorial pledging loyalty and was transferred to military governor of Baoda.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu entered Luoyang, Yanchao sent a swift memorial pledging loyalty and was transferred to military governor of Baoda.

entries.zh: 乾祐初，奉詔歸闕，止奉朝請而已。
entries.en: In Qianyou year one he was ordered back to court and held only the status of court petitioner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou he was ordered by edict to return to court and held only the status of court petitioner.

entries.zh: 太祖自鄴入平內難，隱帝令彥超董騎軍為拒，劉子陂兵亂，彥超先謁見太祖。
entries.en: When Taizu came from Ye to quell the internal crisis, the Hidden Emperor ordered Yanchao to command the cavalry against him; at the rout at Liuzi Slope, Yanchao was first to pay court to Taizu.
entries.literal: When Taizu entered from Ye to pacify the internal crisis, the Hidden Emperor ordered Yanchao to command the cavalry in resistance; at the disorder at Liuzi Slope, Yanchao was the first to call on Taizu.

entries.zh: 廣順中，授神武統軍。
entries.en: During Guangshun he was appointed commander-in-chief of the Divine Martial Army.
entries.literal: During Guangshun he was appointed commander-in-chief of the Divine Martial Army.

entries.zh: 顯德三年冬，以疾終於第。
entries.en: In the winter of Xiande year three he died of illness at home.
entries.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande he died of illness at his residence.

entries.zh: 制贈太子太師。
entries.en: By edict he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 張穎，太原人，駙馬都尉永德
entries.en: Zhang Ying came from Taiyuan; he was the father of Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household Yongde
entries.literal: Zhang Ying was a native of Taiyuan, father of Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household Yongde

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史》列傳：永德，并州陽曲人。
entries.en: (《Song History》 biographies: Yongde came from Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.
entries.literal: (《Song History》 biographies: Yongde was a native of Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 家世饒財，曾祖丕，尚氣節。
entries.en: His family had been wealthy for generations; his great-grandfather Pi was high-spirited and principled.
entries.literal: His family had been wealthy for generations; his great-grandfather Pi was high-spirited and principled.

entries.zh: 後唐武皇鎮太原，急於用度，多嚴選富家子掌帑庫，或調度不給，即坐誅，沒入資產。
entries.en: When Wuhuang of Later Tang governed Taiyuan and urgently needed funds, he often picked sons of rich families to manage the treasury; if supplies ran short they were executed and their assets seized.
entries.literal: When Later Tang Wuhuang governed Taiyuan and urgently needed funds, he often strictly selected sons of rich families to manage the treasury; if supplies fell short they were executed and their assets confiscated.

entries.zh: 丕為之滿歲，府財有餘。
entries.en: Pi held the post a full year and the prefectural treasury had a surplus.
entries.literal: Pi held the post a full year and the prefectural treasury had a surplus.

entries.zh: 宗人政當次補其任，率族屬泣拜，請丕濟其急，丕又為代掌一年，鄉里服其義。）〉
entries.en: A clansman Zheng was next in line; he led the clan in weeping and bowing, begging Pi to relieve their distress, and Pi again took charge for a year—the countryside admired his righteousness.)〉
entries.literal: A clansman Zheng was next in line for the post; he led the clan in weeping and bowing, asking Pi to relieve their distress, and Pi again took charge for a year—the countryside admired his righteousness.)〉

entries.zh: 之父也。
entries.en: who was his father.
entries.literal: was his father.

entries.zh: 累為藩郡列校，由內職歷諸衛將軍。
entries.en: He served in turn as a company commander in frontier prefectures and rose through inner service to the guard generalships.
entries.literal: He successively served as a company commander in frontier prefectures and rose through inner service to the various guard generalships.

entries.zh: 國初，以戚裏之故，自華州行軍司馬歷郢、懷二州刺史，遷安州防禦使。
entries.en: At the founding of the dynasty, through marriage kinship, he rose from march commander of Hua to prefect of Ying and Huai, then defense commissioner of An.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state, because of kin by marriage, he rose from march commander of Hua to prefect of Ying and Huai, then defense commissioner of An.

entries.zh: 穎性卞急峻刻，不容人之小過，雖左右親信，亦皆怨之。
entries.en: Ying was harsh, impatient, stern, and unforgiving of the smallest fault; even his trusted attendants resented him.
entries.literal: Ying's nature was harsh, impatient, stern, and unforgiving of the smallest fault; even close attendants on whom he relied all resented him.

entries.zh: 部曲曹澄有處女，穎逼而娶之，澄遂與不逞之徒數人，同謀害穎，中夜挾刃入於寢門，執穎而殺之，遂奔於金陵。
entries.en: His subordinate Cao Cheng had a virgin daughter; Ying forced her into marriage; Cheng then joined several unruly men to kill Ying; in the dead of night they entered the bedroom with blades, seized Ying and killed him, then fled to Jinling.
entries.literal: His subordinate Cao Cheng had a virgin daughter; Ying forced her and married her; Cheng then joined several unruly men in a plot to kill Ying; in the middle of the night they took blades into the bedroom door, seized Ying and killed him, then fled to Jinling.

entries.zh: 世宗征淮南，以永德之故，遣江南李景，令執澄等送行在。
entries.en: When Shizong campaigned against Huainan, for Yongde's sake he sent word to Li Jing of Jiangnan to deliver Cheng and the others to headquarters.
entries.literal: When Shizong campaigned against Huainan, because of Yongde he sent word to Li Jing of Jiangnan ordering Cheng and the others delivered to the imperial headquarters.

entries.zh: 及至，世宗以澄等賜永德，俾甘心而戮之。
entries.en: When they arrived Shizong gave Cheng and the others to Yongde to satisfy his heart by executing them.
entries.literal: When they arrived Shizong gave Cheng and the others to Yongde so he might satisfy his heart by executing them.

entries.zh: 劉仁贍，略通儒術，好兵書，在澤國甚有聲望。
entries.en: Liu Renshan had some mastery of Confucian learning, loved military books, and enjoyed great repute in the marsh country.
entries.literal: Liu Renshan had some mastery of Confucian learning, loved military books, and in the marsh country enjoyed great repute.

entries.zh: 吳主知之，累遷為偽右監門衛將軍，歷黃、袁二州刺史，所至稱治。
entries.en: The Wu ruler knew him and repeatedly promoted him to the illegitimate office of General of the Right Directorate of the Gate Guards; he served in turn as prefect of Huang and Yuan and wherever he went his rule was praised.
entries.literal: The Wu ruler knew him and repeatedly promoted him to the illegitimate office of General of the Right Directorate of the Gate Guards; he successively served as prefect of Huang and Yuan and wherever he went his rule was praised.

entries.zh: 洎李景僭襲偽位，俾掌親軍，遷鄂州節度使。
entries.en: When Li Jing usurped the false throne he put him in command of the personal army and made him military governor of E.
entries.literal: When Li Jing usurped the false throne he had him command the personal army and transferred him to military governor of E Prefecture.

entries.zh: 居數年，復以兵柄任之，改壽州節度使。
entries.en: After several years he again entrusted him with military authority and transferred him to military governor of Shou.
entries.literal: After several years he again entrusted him with military authority and changed him to military governor of Shou Prefecture.

entries.zh: 及王師渡淮，而仁贍固守甚堅。
entries.en: When the imperial army crossed the Huai, Renshan held firm in defense.
entries.literal: When the imperial army crossed the Huai, Renshan defended with great firmness.

entries.zh: 洎世宗駐蹕於其壘北，數道齊攻，填塹陷壁，晝夜不息，如是者累月。
entries.en: When Shizong encamped north of his ramparts, several columns attacked together, filling ditches and breaching walls day and night without cease for months.
entries.literal: When Shizong halted north of his ramparts, several columns attacked together, filling ditches and breaching walls, day and night without cease, for months on end.

entries.zh: 世宗臨城以諭之，而仁贍但遜詞以謝。
entries.en: Shizong came before the city to instruct him, but Renshan only answered with humble apologies.
entries.literal: Shizong came before the city to instruct him, but Renshan only answered with humble words of apology.

entries.zh: 及車駕還京，命李重進總兵守之，復乘間陷我南寨。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he ordered Li Chongjin to hold the siege; Renshan again seized an opening and stormed our southern camp.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he ordered Li Chongjin to command the troops holding the siege; Renshan again seized an opening and stormed our southern camp.

entries.zh: 自是圍之愈急，城中饑死者甚眾。
entries.en: From then the siege grew tighter and very many inside the city died of hunger.
entries.literal: From then the siege grew tighter; inside the city very many died of hunger.

entries.zh: 三年冬，淮寇復來救援，列寨於紫金山，夾道相屬，累然數十里，垂及壽壁，而重進兵幾不能支，世宗患之，遂復議親征。
entries.en: In the winter of year three Huai rebels came to relieve the siege, forming camps at Zijin Mountain in a line along the road for tens of li, nearly reaching the walls of Shou while Chongjin's army could hardly hold; Shizong was troubled and debated campaigning in person again.
entries.literal: In the winter of the third year Huai rebels came again to relieve the siege, forming camps at Zijin Mountain in a continuous line along the road for several tens of li, nearly reaching the walls of Shou while Chongjin's army could hardly hold; Shizong was troubled and debated campaigning in person again.

entries.zh: 車駕至壽春，命今上率師破紫金山之眾，擒其應援使陳承昭以獻。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage reached Shouchun he ordered the present emperor to lead troops to break the host at Zijin Mountain and capture relief commander Chen Chengzhao to present.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Shouchun he ordered the present emperor to lead troops to break the host at Zijin Mountain and capture their relief commander Chen Chengzhao to present.

entries.zh: 仁贍聞援兵既敗，計無所出，但扼腕浩嘆而已。
entries.en: When Renshan heard the relief army was defeated he had no plan left and could only wring his wrists and sigh.
entries.literal: When Renshan heard the relief army had been defeated he had no plan left and could only wring his wrists and sigh greatly.

entries.zh: 會世宗以紫金山之捷，飛詔以諭之，時仁贍臥疾已亟，因翻然納款，而城內諸軍萬計，皆屏息以聽其命。
entries.en: When Shizong sent a flying edict on the Zijin Mountain victory to instruct him, Renshan was already gravely ill; he suddenly submitted, and the tens of thousands of troops in the city all held their breath and obeyed his command.
entries.literal: When Shizong, on the victory at Zijin Mountain, sent a flying edict to instruct him, Renshan was already gravely ill in bed; he therefore suddenly submitted, and the troops in the city numbering in the tens of thousands all held their breath and obeyed his command.

entries.zh: 及見於行在，世宗撫之甚厚，賜與加等，復令入城養病，尋授天平軍節度使、兼中書令。
entries.en: When he was received at headquarters Shizong treated him very generously, gave him higher gifts, and again ordered him into the city to recover; soon he was appointed military governor of Tianping and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When he was received at headquarters Shizong treated him very generously, gave him gifts of higher grade, and again ordered him into the city to nurse his illness; soon he was appointed military governor of Tianping and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 制出之日，薨於其家，年五十八。
entries.en: On the day the appointment was issued he died at home, aged fifty-eight.
entries.literal: On the day the appointment was issued he died at his home, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 世宗聞之，遣使吊祭，命內臣監護喪事，追封彭城郡王。
entries.en: When Shizong heard he sent envoys to mourn, ordered inner attendants to supervise the funeral, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng.
entries.literal: When Shizong heard he sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, ordered inner attendants to supervise the funeral, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 後以其子崇讃為懷州刺史。
entries.en: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai.
entries.literal: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai.

entries.zh: 仁贍輕財重士，法令嚴肅，重圍之中，其子崇諫犯軍禁，即令斬之，故能以一城之眾，連年拒守。
entries.en: Renshan was light with wealth and heavy toward scholars; his laws were stern; in the tight siege his son Chongjian violated military law and he at once had him beheaded—therefore with one city's troops he could hold out for years.
entries.literal: Renshan was light with wealth and heavy toward scholars; his laws were stern; in the tight siege his son Chongjian violated military prohibition and he at once ordered him beheaded—therefore with the troops of one city he could hold out for years.

entries.zh: 逮其來降，而其下未敢竊議者，保其後嗣，抑有由焉。
entries.en: When he surrendered his subordinates did not dare whisper in private—he had secured his descendants, and there was reason in that.
entries.literal: When he came to surrender his subordinates did not dare whisper in private—he secured his descendants, and there was reason for that.

entries.zh: 王峻，字秀峰，相州安陽人也。
entries.en: Wang Jun, courtesy name Xiufeng, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
entries.literal: Wang Jun, style name Xiufeng, was a man of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父豐，本郡樂營使。
entries.en: His father Feng served as director of the commandery music camp.
entries.literal: His father Feng was Music Camp commissioner of the native commandery.

entries.zh: 峻幼慧黠善歌，梁貞明初，張筠鎮相州，憐峻敏惠，遂畜之。
entries.en: As a boy Jun was clever, quick-witted, and skilled at singing. In the early Zhenming reign of Liang, Zhang Yun was posted to Xiang Prefecture; taking pity on the boy's intelligence, he took him in and raised him.
entries.literal: Jun in youth was clever and sharp and good at song; early in Liang Zhenming, Zhang Yun held Xiang Prefecture, pitied Jun's quick wit, and thereupon reared him.

entries.zh: 及莊宗入魏州，筠棄鎮南渡，以峻自隨。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Weizhou, Yun abandoned his command and fled south, taking Jun with him.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Weizhou, Yun abandoned the post and crossed south, taking Jun with himself.

entries.zh: 時租庸使趙巖訪筠於其第，筠召峻聲歌以侑酒，巖悅，筠因以贈之，頗得親愛。
entries.en: At that time Zhao Yan, commissioner for rent and corvée labor, called on Yun at his mansion. Yun had Jun sing to enliven the wine. Yan was delighted, and Yun presented Jun to him as a gift; he soon won Zhao's warm regard.
entries.literal: At that time Rent-and-Corvée Commissioner Zhao Yan visited Yun at his residence; Yun summoned Jun to sing by voice to assist the wine; Yan was pleased; Yun thereupon presented him, and won no small affection.

entries.zh: 梁亡，趙氏族滅，峻流落無依，寄食於符離陳氏之家，久之彌窘，乃事三司使張延朗，所給甚薄。
entries.en: When Liang fell and the Zhao clan was destroyed, Jun was cast adrift with nowhere to turn. He lived on the Chen family's charity at Fuli; as months passed his plight grew worse, and he entered the service of Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the three fiscal agencies—but the pay was meager indeed.
entries.literal: Liang perished; the Zhao clan was extinguished; Jun drifted without support, lodged for food at the Chen house in Fuli; after long time grew still more straitened, then served Three Agencies Commissioner Zhang Yanlang; what was given was very thin.

entries.zh: 清泰末，延朗誅，漢祖盡得延朗之資產仆從，而峻在籍中，從歷數鎮，常為典客。
entries.en: Near the end of the Qingtai era Yanlang was put to death. The Han founder Liu Zhiyuan seized all his property and retainers; Jun was listed among them and followed him through several provincial postings, usually as protocol officer.
entries.literal: Late Qingtai, Yanlang was executed; Han Founder wholly obtained Yanlang's assets and attendants, while Jun was on the registers; he followed through several posts, constantly as protocol officer.

entries.zh: 漢祖踐阼，授客省使，奉使荊南，留於襄、漢為監軍，入為內客省使。
entries.en: When Liu Zhiyuan took the throne he made Jun commissioner of the guest bureau, then sent him on embassy to Jingnan. He was left behind as military supervisor at Xiangyang and Hanzhong, and later recalled to serve as inner commissioner of the guest bureau.
entries.literal: Han Founder ascended the throne, appointed Guest Bureau commissioner, sent on mission to Jingnan, left at Xiang and Han as military supervisor, entered as Inner Guest Bureau commissioner.

entries.zh: 及趙思綰作亂於永興，漢隱帝命郭從義討之，以峻為兵馬都監。
entries.en: When Zhao Siwan rose in rebellion at Yongxing, Emperor Yindi of Later Han ordered Guo Congyi to crush him and appointed Jun director of armies and cavalry.
entries.literal: When Zhao Sixian rebelled at Yongxing, Han Emperor Yindi ordered Guo Congyi to suppress him, with Jun as army-and-horse chief supervisor.

entries.zh: 從義與峻不協，甚如水火。
entries.en: Congyi and Jun could not work together—they were as incompatible as water and fire.
entries.literal: Congyi and Jun were not in accord, very like water and fire.

entries.zh: 未幾，改宣徽北院使。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred to commissioner of the northern directorate of the palace secretariat.
entries.literal: Before long, changed to Palace Secretariat Northern Directorate commissioner.

entries.zh: 賊平，加檢校太傅，轉南院使。
entries.en: After the rebels were subdued he was given the honorary title Grand Mentor and moved to commissioner of the southern directorate.
entries.literal: Rebels pacified, added honorary Grand Mentor, turned to southern directorate commissioner.

entries.zh: 慕容彥超，
entries.en: Murong Yanchao,
entries.literal: Murong Yanchao,

entries.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。）〉
entries.en: (Editorial note: There is lacuna below this point.)〉
entries.literal: (Editorial note: There is lacuna below this point.)〉

entries.zh: 為兗州節度使，彥超即漢高祖之同產弟也。
entries.en: He served as military governor of Yan Prefecture; Yanchao was a younger brother of the same mother as the Han founder Liu Zhiyuan.
entries.literal: He was military governor of Yan Prefecture; Yanchao was the full younger brother of the Han founder.

entries.zh: 嘗冒姓閻氏，體黑麻面，故謂之閻昆侖。
entries.en: He had once passed himself off under the Yan surname; dark-skinned and pockmarked, men called him "Yan the Kunlun."
entries.literal: He once took the surname Yan by false pretense; his body was black and his face pitted like hemp, hence he was called Yan the Kunlun.

entries.zh: 彥超鎮兗州，漢隱帝欲殺周太祖，召彥超，方食，釋匕箸而就道。
entries.en: While Yanchao governed Yan Prefecture, Emperor Yindi of Later Han plotted to kill Guo Wei and summoned him. Yanchao was in the middle of a meal but set down his utensils and set out at once.
entries.literal: When Yanchao held Yan Prefecture, Han Emperor Yindi wished to kill the Zhou founder and summoned Yanchao; he was at his meal and set down spoon and chopsticks to take the road.

entries.zh: 周兵犯京師，隱帝出勞軍，太后使彥超衛帝，彥超曰：「北兵何能為，當於陣上唱坐使歸營。」
entries.en: When Zhou troops marched on the capital, Yindi went out to review the army. The empress dowager ordered Yanchao to protect the emperor. Yanchao said, "What can northern soldiers do? I will stand on the field and call the commissioner to return to camp."
entries.literal: Zhou troops attacked the capital; Yindi went out to encourage the army; the empress dowager had Yanchao guard the emperor; Yanchao said: "What can the northern troops do? One should on the battlefield call out and send the commissioner back to camp."

entries.zh: 彥超敗，奔兗，隱帝遇弒。
entries.en: Yanchao was beaten, fled to Yan, and Yindi was murdered.
entries.literal: Yanchao was defeated, fled to Yan; Yindi met assassination.

entries.zh: 周太祖時，彥超進呈鄆州節度使高行周來書，其書意即行周毀讟太祖結連彥超之意，帝覽之，笑曰：「此必是彥超之詐也。」
entries.en: Under the Zhou founder, Yanchao submitted a letter purportedly from Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Yun Prefecture, whose wording suggested that Xingzhou had slandered the emperor and was conspiring with Yanchao. Guo Wei read it and laughed: "This must be Yanchao's trick."
entries.literal: In the time of the Zhou founder, Yanchao presented a letter from Yan Prefecture military governor Gao Xingzhou; the letter's intent was that Xingzhou slandered the founder and was in league with Yanchao; the emperor read it and laughed, saying: "This must surely be Yanchao's fraud."

entries.zh: 試令驗之，果然。
entries.en: He had it examined, and it proved to be a forgery.
entries.literal: He tried ordering it verified, and so it proved.

entries.zh: 其鄆州印元有缺，文不相接，其為印即無缺處，帝尋令賫書示諭行周，行周上表謝恩。
entries.en: The genuine Yunzhou seal had a flaw where the characters did not meet; the forged seal had no such gap. The emperor soon sent the letter to Xingzhou to show him the truth, and Xingzhou memorialized his thanks.
entries.literal: The Yan Prefecture seal originally had a gap; the characters did not connect; the forged seal had no gap; the emperor soon ordered the letter carried to show and instruct Xingzhou; Xingzhou submitted a memorial thanking grace.

entries.zh: 先是，填星初至角、亢，占者曰：角，鄭分，兗州屬焉。
entries.en: Earlier the planet Saturn had entered the lodges Horn and Neck. Diviners said, "Horn is the astral allotment of Zheng, and Yan Prefecture falls within it."
entries.literal: Earlier, the Saturn had first reached Horn and Neck; the diviner said: Horn is Zheng's allotment; Yan Prefecture belongs to it.

entries.zh: 彥超即率軍府賓佐，步出州西門三十里致祭，迎於開元寺，塑像以事之，謂之「菩薩」，日至祈禱，又令民家豎黃幡以禳之。
entries.en: Yanchao led his staff on foot thirty li beyond the west gate to offer sacrifice, welcomed the omen at Kaiyuan Temple, and set up an image to worship, calling it the "Bodhisattva." He prayed daily and ordered households to raise yellow banners to ward off ill fortune.
entries.literal: Yanchao thereupon led the military prefecture's guests and aides, on foot left the prefecture's west gate thirty li to perform sacrifice, received at Kaiyuan Temple, set up an image to serve it, calling it "Bodhisattva"; day by day he prayed, and again ordered households to raise yellow banners to avert it.

entries.zh: 及城陷，彥超方在土星院燃香，急乃馳去。
entries.en: When the city fell, Yanchao was still burning incense in the Saturn Courtyard; he galloped away in alarm.
entries.literal: When the city fell, Yanchao was just burning incense in the Saturn Courtyard; in haste he galloped away.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：慕容彥超素有鉤距。
entries.en: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Murong Yanchao had long been a master of schemes.
entries.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Murong Yanchao had always been full of stratagems.

entries.zh: 兗州有盜者，詐為大官從人，跨驢於衢中，市羅十餘匹，價值既定，引物主詣一宅門，以驢付之，曰：「此本宅使，汝且在此，吾為汝上白於主以請值。」
entries.en: At Yan Prefecture a thief posed as a great official's retainer, rode a donkey through the market, and bought more than ten bolts of silk. Once the price was set he led the seller to a mansion gate, handed him the donkey, and said, "This is our house messenger—wait here while I go in and ask the master for payment."
entries.literal: In Yan Prefecture there was a thief who pretended to be a great official's attendant, rode a donkey in the middle of the street, bought more than ten bolts of silk; the price fixed, he led the owner to a mansion gate, handed him the donkey, saying: "This is our mansion's messenger—you wait here; I will go up and report to the master to request payment."

entries.zh: 物主許之。
entries.en: The seller agreed.
entries.literal: The owner of the goods assented.

entries.zh: 既而聲跡悄然，物主怒其不出，叩門呼之，則空宅也。
entries.en: Before long all was silent. The seller, angry that no one came out, knocked and called at the gate—and found an empty house.
entries.literal: Before long sound and trace grew still; the owner of the goods, angry that he did not come out, knocked on the gate and called— it was an empty house.

entries.zh: 於是連叫「賊」，巡司至，疑其詐，兼以驢收之詣府。
entries.en: He then cried "Thief!" again and again. The patrol came, suspected him of fraud, and took him and the donkey to the prefectural office.
entries.literal: Thereupon he repeatedly shouted "Thief!"; the patrol arrived, suspected his fraud, and also took the donkey with him to the prefecture.

entries.zh: 彥超憫之，且曰：「勿憂，吾為汝擒此賊。」
entries.en: Yanchao took pity on him and said, "Do not worry—I will catch the thief for you."
entries.literal: Yanchao pitied him and said: "Do not worry; I will catch this thief for you."

entries.zh: 乃留物主府中，復戒廄卒高系其驢，通宵不與水草，然後密召親信者，牽於通衢中放之，且曰：「此盜者之驢耳，自昨日不與水草，其饑渴者甚矣，放之必奔歸家，但可躡蹤而觀之，盜無不獲也。」
