entries.en: He kept the seller at the yamen, told the stable hand to tie the donkey high and withhold fodder and water all night, then secretly sent a trusted man to lead it into the main street and turn it loose, saying, "This is the thief's donkey—it has had no food or water since yesterday and must be desperate with hunger and thirst. Turn it loose and it will run home; follow its tracks and watch—the thief cannot escape."
entries.literal: He then kept the owner of the goods in the prefecture, again warned the stable groom to tie the donkey high, all night gave it no fodder or water, then secretly summoned a trusted man, led it out in the main thoroughfare and released it, saying: "This is the thief's donkey; since yesterday it has had no fodder or water—it must be very hungry and thirsty; release it and it will surely run home; you need only follow its tracks and watch—the thief cannot fail to be taken."

entries.zh: 親信者如其言隨之，其驢果入一小巷，轉數曲，忽有兒戲於門側，視其驢，連呼曰：「驢歸，驢歸。」
entries.en: The man did as told. The donkey entered a small lane and wound through several turns. A child playing by a gate saw it and cried again and again, "The donkey's back! The donkey's back!"
entries.literal: The trusted man followed as he said; the donkey indeed entered a small lane, turned several bends; suddenly a child played by the gate, saw its donkey, and repeatedly called: "The donkey's back, the donkey's back."

entries.zh: 盜者聞之，欣然出視，遂擒之。
entries.en: The thief heard, came out gladly to look, and was seized.
entries.literal: The thief heard, came out gladly to look, and was seized.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，改乾祐為廣順。
entries.en: When the founder took the throne he changed the era name from Qianyou to Guangshun.
entries.literal: When the founder ascended the throne, he changed Qianyou to Guangshun.

entries.zh: 是年，兗州慕容彥超反。
entries.en: That year Murong Yanchao rebelled at Yan Prefecture.
entries.literal: That year, Murong Yanchao of Yan Prefecture rebelled.

entries.zh: 高祖親征，城將破，忽夜夢一人，狀貌甚偉異，被王者之服，謂高祖曰：「陛下明日當得城。」
entries.en: The founder marched in person. As the city was about to fall, he dreamed at night of a man of strange and imposing mien in kingly robes who said to him, "Your Majesty will take the city tomorrow."
entries.literal: The founder campaigned in person; the city was about to fall; suddenly at night he dreamed of a man, his appearance very strange and grand, wearing kingly robes, who said to the founder: "Your Majesty tomorrow will take the city."

entries.zh: 及覺，天猶未曉。
entries.en: When he woke, dawn had not yet broken.
entries.literal: When he awoke, heaven had not yet brightened.

entries.zh: 高祖私謂征兆如此，可不預備乎！
entries.en: The founder said to himself: With an omen like this, how could he fail to prepare!
entries.literal: The founder privately said: With an omen like this, how can one not prepare!

entries.zh: 於是躬督將士，戮力急攻，至午而城陷。
entries.en: He then personally directed his generals in a fierce assault, and by noon the city had fallen.
entries.literal: Thereupon he personally directed the generals and soldiers, exerted strength in urgent attack; by noon the city fell.

entries.zh: 車駕將入，有司請由生方鳴鞘而進，遂取別巷，轉數曲，見一處門墻甚高大，問之，雲夫子廟。
entries.en: As the imperial carriage was about to enter, the officials asked that he enter by the "live" route with swords drawn in their scabbards. He took another lane instead, wound through several turns, and came upon a gate and walls of great height. Inquiring, he was told it was the temple of Confucius.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage was about to enter; the relevant offices requested entry by the live route with sounding scabbard; he therefore took another lane, turned several bends, saw a place whose gate and wall were very lofty; asked, and was told it was the temple of the Master.

entries.zh: 高祖意豁然，謂近臣曰：「寡人所夢，得非夫子乎？
entries.en: His mind cleared at once. He said to his close ministers, "Was the figure in my dream none other than the Master?
entries.literal: The founder's mind suddenly cleared; he said to close ministers: "Could the one in my dream be the Master?

entries.zh: 不然，何取路於此也。」
entries.en: If not, why should we have come by this road?"
entries.literal: If not, why take the road here?"

entries.zh: 因下馬觀之，方升堂，睹其聖像，一如夢中所見者，於是大喜，叩首再拜。
entries.en: He dismounted to look. As he entered the hall he saw the sage's image—just as in his dream. Overjoyed, he bowed twice.
entries.literal: He thereupon dismounted to view it; just as he ascended the hall he beheld the sage's image, exactly like the one seen in the dream; he was greatly pleased and bowed his head twice.

entries.zh: 近臣或諫，以為天子不合拜異世陪臣。
entries.en: Some close ministers objected that the Son of Heaven ought not bow to a minister of another age.
entries.literal: Close ministers some remonstrated, holding that the Son of Heaven should not bow to a companion minister of another age.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「夫子聖人也，百王取則，而又夢告寡人，得非夫子幽贊所及耶？
entries.en: The founder said, "The Master is a sage whom a hundred kings take as their model. He warned me in a dream—was that not his hidden blessing at work?
entries.literal: The founder said: "The Master is a sage; the hundred kings take him as model; moreover he announced himself to me in a dream—could it not be that the Master's hidden aid reached this?

entries.zh: 安得不拜！」
entries.en: How could I not bow!"
entries.literal: How could one not bow!"

entries.zh: 仍以廟側數十家為灑掃戶，命孔氏襲文宣王者長為本縣。
entries.en: He assigned several dozen households near the temple to its upkeep and appointed the Kong descendant who carried on King Wenxuan's line as magistrate of the local county.
entries.literal: He further made several dozen households beside the temple responsible for sprinkling and sweeping, and ordered the Kong descendant who inherited King Wenxuan's line to govern the local county.

entries.zh: 慕容彥超之被圍也，乘城而望，見高祖親臨矢石，其勢不可當，退而憂之，因勉其麾下曰：「汝等宜為吾盡命，吾庫中金銀如山積，若全此城，吾盡以為賜，汝等勿患富貴。」
entries.en: While Murong Yanchao was under siege he climbed the wall and saw the founder himself in the hail of arrows and stones. The assault could not be withstood. He withdrew in dread and urged his men: "Fight to the death for me. Gold and silver in my treasury are heaped like mountains—if we hold the city I will give it all to you. You need not fear for wealth or rank."
entries.literal: When Murong Yanchao was besieged, he mounted the wall and looked; he saw the founder personally under arrows and stones; the momentum could not be withstood; he withdrew and was anxious, and therefore exhorted his subordinates: "You ought to give your lives for me; the gold and silver in my treasury are piled like mountains; if this city is preserved, I will give it all as reward—you need not worry about wealth and honor."

entries.zh: 頃之，有卒私言曰：「我知侍中銀皆鐵胎，得之何用？」
entries.en: Soon a soldier muttered, "I know the commander's silver is all iron at the core—what good is that?"
entries.literal: Before long a soldier privately said: "I know the attendant's silver is all iron core—what use is getting it?"

entries.zh: 於是諸軍聞之，稍稍解體，未幾城陷。
entries.en: The troops heard it, and morale slowly crumbled. Before long the city fell.
entries.literal: Thereupon the armies heard it; gradually their unity dissolved; before long the city fell.

entries.zh: 及高祖之入也，有司閱其庫藏，其間銀鐵胎者果十有七八。
entries.en: When the founder entered, officials inspected the treasury. Seven or eight tenths of the silver proved to be iron at the core.
entries.literal: When the founder entered, the relevant offices examined his treasury stores; among them iron-core silver indeed made up seven or eight tenths.

entries.zh: 初，彥超常令人開質庫，有以鐵胎銀質錢者，經年後，庫吏始覺，遂言之於彥超。
entries.en: Earlier Yanchao had often run a pawnshop. Some customers pawned silver that was iron at the core. Years passed before a clerk noticed and told Yanchao.
entries.literal: Earlier, Yanchao often had men open a pawn office; some pawned iron-core silver for cash; after years the office clerk first noticed, and reported to Yanchao.

entries.zh: 初甚怒，頃之謂吏曰：「此易致耳，汝宜偽竇刂庫墻，凡金銀器用暨縑帛等，速皆藏匿，仍亂撤其餘以為賊踐，然後申明，吾當擒此輩矣。」
entries.en: At first he was furious; then he told the clerk, "This is easy to turn to account. Pretend thieves have broken through the treasury wall. Hide all gold and silver vessels and silks at once, scatter the rest as if robbers had trampled them, then report it—I will catch the culprits."
entries.literal: At first he was very angry; presently he told the clerk: "This is easy to obtain—you should falsely bore through the treasury wall; all gold and silver vessels and silk damask and the like, quickly hide them, still scatter the rest in disorder as if thieves had trampled, then report openly—I will catch this lot."

entries.zh: 庫吏如其教，於是彥超下令曰：「吾為使長典百姓，而又不謹，遭賊竇刂去，其過深矣。
entries.en: The clerk obeyed. Yanchao then proclaimed, "As commissioner I am charged with the people, yet I was careless—thieves broke in and stole goods. The fault is grave.
entries.literal: The treasury clerk followed his instruction; Yanchao thereupon issued an order: "I am commissioner charged with the people, yet was not careful; thieves bored through and took goods—the fault is deep.

entries.zh: 今恐百姓疑彥超隱其物，宜令三日內各投狀，明言質物色，自當陪償之，不爾者有過。」
entries.en: I fear the people think I have hidden their goods. Within three days each of you must file a statement describing your pawned goods by kind, and I will repay you in full—otherwise you will be at fault."
entries.literal: Now I fear the people suspect Yanchao of hiding their goods; they should within three days each submit a statement, clearly stating pawned goods by kind; I will compensate in full—otherwise there is fault."

entries.zh: 百姓以為然，於是投狀相繼，翌日鐵胎銀主果出。
entries.en: The people believed him. Statements poured in, and the next day the owners of the iron-core silver came forward.
entries.literal: The people thought it so; statements were submitted in succession; the next day the owners of iron-core silver indeed came forward.

entries.zh: 於是擒之，置之深屋中，使教部曲輩晝夜造，用廣府庫，此銀是也。）〉
entries.en: He seized them, shut them in a back room, and made them teach his personal troops to forge day and night, swelling the prefectural treasury—that was the source of the silver.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon they were seized, placed in a deep room, and made to teach his personal troops day and night to forge, to enlarge the prefectural treasury—this was that silver.)〉

entries.zh: 太祖鎮鄴，兼北面兵馬，峻為監軍，留駐鄴城。
entries.en: When Guo Wei was military governor at Ye and also commanded the northern armies, Jun served as his military supervisor and remained garrisoned at Ye.
entries.literal: Taizu held Ye, also northern armies; Jun was military supervisor, left garrisoned at Ye city.

entries.zh: 隱帝蕭墻變起，峻亦為群小所構，舉家見害。
entries.en: When the palace coup struck under Emperor Yindi, Jun too was framed by petty schemers, and his entire household was slaughtered.
entries.literal: Yindi's coup within the palace walls arose; Jun too was framed by petty men; the whole household was killed.

entries.zh: 從太祖赴闕，綢繆帷幄，贊成大事，峻居首焉。
entries.en: He followed Guo Wei to the capital, worked closely with him in the command tent, and helped bring the great enterprise to success—Jun ranked foremost among them.
entries.literal: Following Taizu to the capital, intimate in the command tent, assisted the great achievement; Jun stood first.

entries.zh: 京師平定，受漢太后令，充樞密使。
entries.en: Once the capital was secured he received orders from the Han empress dowager and was appointed director of the bureau of military affairs.
entries.literal: Capital pacified, received Han Empress Dowager's order, filled Bureau of Military Affairs director.

entries.zh: 太祖北征，至澶州，為諸軍擁迫，峻與王殷在京聞變，乃遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使郭崇往宋州，前申州刺史馬鐸往許州，以防他變，二州安然，亦峻之謀也。
entries.en: When Guo Wei marched north and reached Chanzhou, the armies pressed him to take the throne. Jun and Wang Yin, hearing the news in the capital, dispatched Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou and the former prefect of Shen, Ma Duo, to Xuzhou to forestall any other upheaval. Both prefectures stayed calm—another stroke planned by Jun.
entries.literal: Taizu marched north, reached Chanzhou, was pressed by the armies; Jun and Wang Yin in the capital heard the change, then sent Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou, former Shen prefect Ma Duo to Xuzhou, to guard against other changes; the two prefectures were secure—also Jun's plan.

entries.zh: 太祖踐阼，加平章事，尋兼右僕射、門下侍郎平章事，監修國史。
entries.en: When Guo Wei became emperor, Jun was made grand councilor; soon he also held the posts of right vice director of the imperial secretariat, vice minister of the gate department and grand councilor, and supervisor for the compilation of the national history.
entries.literal: Taizu ascended the throne, added Grand Councilor; soon also Right Vice Director, Gate Department vice minister Grand Councilor, supervised compilation of national history.

entries.zh: 時朝廷初建，四方多故，峻夙夜奉事，知無不為，每侍太祖商榷軍事，未嘗不移時而退，甚有裨益。
entries.en: The dynasty was new and troubles pressed on every side. Jun attended day and night, leaving nothing undone that he could attempt. Whenever he sat with the emperor to weigh military affairs he would not withdraw until hours had passed—his counsel proved of real benefit.
entries.literal: At that time the court was newly founded, the four quarters had many affairs; Jun day and night served; what he knew he did not leave undone; each time he attended Taizu to discuss military affairs, never withdrew before hours had shifted; very beneficial.

entries.zh: 然為性輕躁，舉措率易，以天下之事為己任，每有啟請，多自任情。
entries.en: Yet he was by nature flighty and rash, careless in his bearing, and treated the affairs of the realm as his personal burden. When he petitioned the throne he usually followed whim rather than rule.
entries.literal: Yet by nature light and rash, conduct careless and easy, took the realm's affairs as his own charge; whenever he submitted requests, mostly followed his own mood.

entries.zh: 太祖從而順之，則忻然而退；
entries.en: If the emperor agreed, he would withdraw well pleased.
entries.literal: Taizu followed and assented, then withdrew in pleasure.

entries.zh: 稍未允可，則應聲而慍，不遜之語隨事輒發。
entries.en: If assent fell even slightly short, anger flared on the spot and insubordinate words spilled out at every turn.
entries.literal: Slightly not granted, then at the sound grew angry; insubordinate words with each matter would burst forth.

entries.zh: 太祖素知其為人，且以佐命之故，每優容之。
entries.en: Guo Wei had long known his temper, and for his merit in founding the dynasty showed him forbearance time and again.
entries.literal: Taizu long knew his person, and because of founding merit, each time showed forbearance.

entries.zh: 峻年長於太祖二歲，太祖雖登大位，時以兄呼之，有時呼表字，不忘布衣之契也。
entries.en: Jun was two years older than the emperor. Though Guo Wei now wore the throne, he would sometimes address him as elder brother, sometimes call him Xiufeng—never forgetting their bond as men in plain cloth.
entries.literal: Jun was two years older than Taizu; Taizu though he ascended the great position, at times called him elder brother, at times called the style name, not forgetting the plain-cloth bond.

entries.zh: 峻以此益自負焉。
entries.en: Jun grew all the more prideful on that account.
entries.literal: Jun by this grew still more self-conceited.

entries.zh: 初，峻降制除青州，有司制造旌節，以備迎授。
entries.en: Earlier, when the edict appointed Jun to Qingzhou, the offices forged the commission banners in readiness for his investiture.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the edict appointed Jun to Qingzhou, the relevant offices manufactured the banner-credentials in preparation for his reception and investiture.

entries.zh: 前一夕，其旄有聲甚異，聞者駭之。
entries.en: On the eve of his departure the staff of the banner gave a strange sound; those who heard it were shaken.
entries.literal: The night before, its banner-staff made sounds very strange; those who heard were alarmed.

entries.zh: 主者曰：「昔安重誨授河中節，亦有此異焉。」
entries.en: The keeper of the regalia said: "When An Chonghui received the Hezhong commission, the same omen appeared."
entries.literal: The person in charge said: "In the past when An Chonghui received the Hezhong commission, there was also this strangeness."

entries.zh: 又所居堂陛，忽然隱起如堆。
entries.en: Moreover, the steps of his hall suddenly bulged upward like a heap of earth.
entries.literal: Moreover, the steps of his hall suddenly swelled up hidden, like a mound.

entries.zh: 又夢被官府追攝入司簿院，既寤，心惡之，以是尤加狂躁。
entries.en: He also dreamed that officials seized him and dragged him into the Bureau of Registers. When he woke his heart was full of dread, and from that day he grew only more frantic.
entries.literal: Moreover he dreamed he was seized and taken into the Bureau of Registers; when he awoke, his heart was adverse toward it; because of this he became all the more frenzied and rash.

entries.zh: 峻才疏位重，輕躁寡謀，聽人穿鼻，既國權在手，而射利者曲為指畫，乃啖餌虎臣，離間親舊，加以善則稱己，無禮於君，欲求無罪，其可得乎！
entries.en: Jun's talent did not match his rank: rash, shallow in counsel, led by the nose. Once power was his, profiteers bent schemes to his will; he baited fierce ministers and turned kin and old friends against one another; whatever credit there was, he claimed for himself; toward his sovereign he showed no ritual propriety. To expect innocence from such a man—how could that be?
entries.literal: Jun's talent was shallow yet his position heavy; he was light and rash, lacking in counsel; he let others lead him by the nose. Once state power was in his hands, those who sought profit twisted out plans for him; he fed and baited fierce ministers, sundered kin and old friends; add to this that when there was good he claimed it for himself, and his lack of ritual toward the ruler—if he wished to be without guilt, how could that be obtained!

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：廣順初，河東劉崇引契丹攻晉州。
entries.en: (Lost Text of the History of the Five Dynasties: Early in Guangshun, Liu Chong of Hedong brought Khitan forces against Jin Prefecture.
entries.literal: (Lost Text of the History of the Five Dynasties: Early in Guangshun, Liu Chong of Hedong led the Khitans to attack Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 遣王峻率師赴援，峻頓兵於陜。
entries.en: The court sent Wang Jun with an army to relieve the city; Jun halted his troops at Shan.
entries.literal: He dispatched Wang Jun to lead an army to rush to the relief; Jun encamped at Shan.

entries.zh: 周祖親征，遣使諭之。
entries.en: The Zhou founder took the field in person and sent an envoy to instruct him.
entries.literal: The Zhou Founder personally campaigned and sent an envoy to instruct him.

entries.zh: 峻見使受宣訖，謂使曰：「與某馳還，附奏陛下，言晉州城堅，未易可破，劉崇兵鋒方銳，不可與力爭，所以駐兵者，待其氣衰耳，非臣怯也。
entries.en: When Jun met the envoy and received the imperial message, he told him: "Ride back with me at once and report to His Majesty that Jin Prefecture's walls are strong and not easily taken, that Liu Chong's troops are at the height of their ardor and cannot be met head-on. I hold my army here only to wait until their spirit flags—not from cowardice.
entries.literal: When Jun saw the envoy and finished receiving the imperial order, he said to the envoy: "Ride back swiftly with me and submit a memorial to Your Majesty, saying that Jinzhou's walls are firm and not easily taken; Liu Chong's military edge is just sharp—it cannot be contested by force. The reason for halting the army is to wait until their spirit declines—that is all; it is not that your subject is cowardly.

entries.zh: 陛下新即位，不宜輕舉。
entries.en: Your Majesty has only lately taken the throne; you should not venture lightly.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended; you should not act lightly.

entries.zh: 今朝中受聖知者，惟李蒨、範質而已，陛下若車駕出汜水，則慕容彥超以賊軍入汴，大事去矣。」
entries.en: Of those the court trusts today, only Li Qian and Fan Zhi enjoy the emperor's confidence. If Your Majesty's carriage crosses Sishui, Murong Yanchao will bring rebel troops into Bian and the cause will be lost."
entries.literal: In the court today, those who enjoy the sage's trust are only Li Qian and Fan Zhi. If Your Majesty's carriage goes out beyond Sishui, then Murong Yanchao will enter Bian with rebel troops and the great affair will be lost."

entries.zh: 使還具奏，周祖自以手提其耳曰：「幾敗吾事。」）〉
entries.en: The envoy returned and reported every word. The Zhou founder clutched his own ear and said, "He nearly ruined everything.")〉
entries.literal: The envoy returned and reported in full. The Zhou Founder himself said, taking his ear: "He nearly ruined my affair.")〉

entries.zh: 廣順元年冬，劉崇與契丹圍晉州，峻請行應援，太祖用為行營都部署，以徐州節度使王彥超為副。
entries.en: In the winter of the first year of Guangshun, Liu Chong and the Khitan besieged Jin Prefecture. Jun asked to lead the relief army; Guo Wei appointed him overall commander of the field headquarters, with Wang Yanchao, military governor of Xuzhou, as his deputy.
entries.literal: Guangshun first year winter, Liu Chong with Khitan besieged Jinzhou; Jun requested to march in relief; Taizu used him as field headquarters overall commander, with Xuzhou military governor Wang Yanchao as deputy.

entries.zh: 詔諸軍並取峻節度，許峻以便宜從事，軍行資用仰給於官，隨行將吏得自選擇。
entries.en: An edict ordered every army to obey Jun's command, allowed him to act at his own discretion, promised that campaign expenses would be met from the treasury, and let him choose his own staff of officers and clerks.
entries.literal: Edict: all armies alike take Jun's command; permitted Jun discretionary action; campaign expenses looked to the state; accompanying officers and clerks might choose themselves.

entries.zh: 將發之前，召宴於滋德殿，太祖出女樂以寵之。
entries.en: On the eve of departure the court feasted him in the Hall of Nurturing Virtue, and the emperor sent out female musicians to honor him.
entries.literal: Before setting out, summoned to feast in Zide Hall; Taizu sent out female musicians to honor him.

entries.zh: 奉辭之日，恩賜優厚，不拘常制。
entries.en: On the day he took formal leave, imperial gifts were lavish beyond the usual scale.
entries.literal: On the day of taking leave, grace and gifts were generous, not bound by usual rules.

entries.zh: 及發，太祖幸西莊，親臨宴餞，別賜御馬玉帶，執手而別。
entries.en: As the army set out, Guo Wei went to the Western Villa and personally feasted him on his departure, then gave him an imperial horse and jade belt and clasped his hands in farewell.
entries.literal: When he marched, Taizu visited the Western Villa, personally came to feast him on departure, separately bestowed imperial horse and jade belt, clasped hands and parted.

entries.zh: 峻至陜駐留數夕，劉崇攻晉州甚急，太祖憂其不可支，議親征，取澤州路入，與峻會合，先令諭峻。
entries.en: Jun reached Shan and halted several nights. Liu Chong's assault on Jin Prefecture was fierce; the emperor feared the city could not stand and considered leading the campaign himself along the Ze Prefecture road to join Jun, and first sent word to inform him.
entries.literal: Jun reached Shan and halted several nights; Liu Chong attacked Jinzhou very urgently; Taizu feared it could not hold, deliberated personal campaign, taking the Ze Prefecture route in, to join Jun; first ordered Jun informed.

entries.zh: 峻遣驛騎馳奏，請車駕不行幸。
entries.en: Jun sent a courier with an urgent memorial begging the emperor not to take the field in person.
entries.literal: Jun sent relay rider with urgent memorial, requesting the imperial carriage not proceed on campaign.

entries.zh: 時已降御劄，行有日矣，會峻奏至，乃止。
entries.en: An imperial rescript had already been issued and the departure was only days away—but when Jun's memorial arrived, the journey was called off.
entries.literal: At that time the imperial letter had already been issued; departure had a set day; then Jun's memorial arrived, and it was stopped.

entries.zh: 峻軍既過絳郡，距平陽一舍，賊軍燔營，狼狽而遁。
entries.en: Once Jun's army had passed Jiang Prefecture and was a day's march from Pingyang, the enemy burned their camps and fled in disorder.
entries.literal: Jun's army had already passed Jiang Prefecture, one stage from Pingyang; the rebel army burned camps, fled in disarray.

entries.zh: 峻入晉州，或請追賊，必有大利，峻猶豫久之，翌日方遣騎軍襲賊，信宿而還。
entries.en: Jun entered Jin Prefecture. Some urged him to pursue, promising a rich prize; he hesitated for a long while. Only the next day did he send cavalry after the enemy, and they returned after two nights on the road.
entries.literal: Jun entered Jinzhou; some urged pursuing the rebels, saying great gain was certain; Jun hesitated long; only next day sent cavalry to strike the rebels; after two nights returned.

entries.zh: 向使峻極力追躡，則並、汾之孽，無噍類矣。
entries.en: Had Jun pressed the pursuit with all his strength, the rebel survivors of Bing and Fen would have been wiped out to the last man.
entries.literal: Had Jun pursued with all his might, then the remnant rebels of Bing and Fen would have had none left to devour.

entries.zh: 峻亦深恥無功，因計度增修平陽故城而回。
entries.en: Deeply shamed at accomplishing so little, he planned and enlarged the repairs on the old walls of Pingyang, then marched home.
entries.literal: Jun also deeply shamed at no achievement, therefore planned and enlarged repairs on Pingyang's old walls and returned.

entries.zh: 時永興軍節度使李洪信，漢室之密戚也，自太祖踐阼，恒有憂沮之意，而本城軍不滿千，峻出征至陜州，以救援晉州為辭，抽起數百人，及劉崇北遁，又遣禁兵千餘人，屯於京兆，洪信懼，遂請入朝。
entries.en: Li Hongxin, military governor of Yongxing, was a close kinsman of the Han house. Since Guo Wei took the throne he had shown constant unease, yet his city garrison numbered fewer than a thousand. When Jun marched out and reached Shan, he used the relief of Jin Prefecture as a pretext to draft several hundred men from him; and when Liu Chong fled north, Jun sent more than a thousand palace guards to garrison Jingzhao. Hongxin was terrified and petitioned to come to court.
entries.literal: At that time Yongxing military governor Li Hongxin was a close kinsman of Han; since Taizu ascended the throne he constantly had anxious dismay, while the city's troops did not reach a thousand; Jun on campaign reached Shan, on the pretext of relieving Jinzhou drafted several hundred men; when Liu Chong fled north, again sent over a thousand imperial guards to garrison Jingzhao; Hongxin feared and thereupon requested to enter court.

entries.zh: 峻軍回，太祖厚加優賜。
entries.en: When Jun's army returned, the emperor showered him with generous rewards.
entries.literal: Jun's army returned; Taizu heaped generous rewards.

entries.zh: 時慕容彥超叛於兗州，已遣侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英、客省使向訓率兵攻之。
entries.en: Murong Yanchao had rebelled at Yan Prefecture; the court had already sent Palace Guard infantry commander Cao Ying and guest-bureau commissioner Xiang Xun to attack him.
entries.literal: At that time Murong Yanchao rebelled at Yanzhou; already sent Palace Guard infantry commander Cao Ying and guest-bureau commissioner Xiang Xun to lead troops against him.

entries.zh: 峻意欲自將兵討賊，累言於太祖曰：「慕容劇賊，曹英不易與之敵耳。」
entries.en: Jun wanted to take the field himself. Again and again he told the emperor, "Murong is a ferocious rebel—Cao Ying will not easily stand against him."
entries.literal: Jun wished to lead troops himself to crush the rebels, repeatedly said to Taizu: 'Murong is a fierce outlaw; Cao Ying will not easily be his match.'

entries.zh: 太祖默然。
entries.en: The emperor said nothing.
entries.literal: Taizu was silent.

entries.zh: 未幾親征，命峻為隨駕一行都部署，破賊之日，峻督軍在城南，其眾先登，頗有得色。
entries.en: Before long the emperor marched in person and named Jun overall commander of the entire retinue. On the day the rebels were broken, Jun directed the southern wing; his men were first over the wall, and he could not hide his satisfaction.
entries.literal: Before long the emperor campaigned in person, appointed Jun overall commander of the entire accompanying column; on the day the rebels were broken, Jun directed the army on the south; his troops were first to scale; he wore considerable satisfaction.

entries.zh: 從駕還京，未幾貢表乞解樞機，即時退歸私第。
entries.en: He returned with the imperial train to the capital; before long he memorialized asking to be relieved of the bureau of military affairs and at once retired to his private mansion.
entries.literal: Following the imperial procession back to the capital, before long submitted memorial begging release from the keys of state, at once withdrew to private residence.

entries.zh: 是歲，戶部侍郎趙上交權知貢舉，上交嘗詣峻，峻言及一童子，上交不達其旨，榜出之日，童子不第，峻銜之。
entries.en: That year Zhao Shangjiao, Vice Minister of Revenue, oversaw the examinations. Shangjiao had once visited Jun, who mentioned a certain candidate; Shangjiao did not take his meaning. When the results were posted the youth failed. Jun bore a grudge.
entries.literal: That year, Zhao Shangjiao, Vice Minister of Revenue, acted as supervisor of the examinations. Shangjiao had once called on Jun; Jun spoke of a certain youth; Shangjiao did not grasp his intent. On the day the results were posted, the youth failed to pass. Jun harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 及貢院申中書門下，取日過堂，峻知印，判定過日。
entries.en: When the examination office reported to the Secretariat to schedule the Hall ceremony, Jun held the seal and fixed the date himself.
entries.literal: When the examination compound reported to the Directorate of the Middle Secretariat and Below to set a day for the Hall ceremony, Jun held the seal and determined the day of passage.

entries.zh: 及上交引新及第人至中書，峻在政事堂厲聲曰：「今歲選士不公，當須覆試。」
entries.en: When Shangjiao brought the new graduates to the Secretariat, Jun shouted in the Hall of Administration: "This year's examination was unfair. There must be a re-test."
entries.literal: When Shangjiao led the newly passed candidates to the Secretariat, Jun in the Hall of Administration said in a stern voice: "This year's selection of scholars was unjust—it must be re-examined."

entries.zh: 諸相曰：「但緣已行指揮行過，臨事不欲改移，況未敕下，覆試非晚。」
entries.en: The chief ministers said: "Orders have already gone out and been executed; one does not change course at the last moment. Besides, the edict has not yet been issued—a re-examination can wait."
entries.literal: The chief councillors said: "It is only because orders have already been issued and carried out; at the last moment one does not wish to change. Moreover, the edict has not yet been promulgated—a re-examination is not too late."

entries.zh: 峻愈怒，詬責上交，聲聞於外。
entries.en: Jun grew angrier, reviled Shangjiao, and his shouting was heard outside the hall.
entries.literal: Jun grew angrier still, reviled and blamed Shangjiao; his voice carried outside.

entries.zh: 少頃，竟令引過。
entries.en: A moment later he nevertheless had the graduates presented.
entries.literal: After a brief while, he ultimately ordered them brought through after all.

entries.zh: 及罷，上交詣本廳謝峻，峻又延之飲酌從容。
entries.en: When the ceremony ended, Shangjiao went to Jun's office to apologize; Jun received him again and shared wine at ease.
entries.literal: When it was over, Shangjiao went to his own bureau to apologize to Jun; Jun again received him and drank wine at leisure.

entries.zh: 翌日，峻奏上交知舉不公，請致之於法，太祖頷之而已。
entries.en: The next day Jun memorialized that Shangjiao had run the examinations unfairly and asked that he be punished by law. Taizu only nodded.
entries.literal: The next day, Jun memorialized that Shangjiao's supervision of the examinations was unjust and requested that he be brought to justice; Taizu merely nodded.

entries.zh: 又奏請以顏愆、陳觀代範質、李穀為相。
entries.en: He also asked that Yan Yan and Chen Guan replace Fan Zhi and Li Gu as chief ministers.
entries.literal: He also memorialized requesting that Yan Yan and Chen Guan replace Fan Zhi and Li Gu as chief councillors.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「進退宰輔，未可倉卒，待徐思之。」
entries.en: Taizu said: "The appointment and removal of chief ministers must not be rushed. Let us consider it at leisure."
entries.literal: Taizu said: "The advancement and dismissal of chief ministers cannot be done in haste; wait and think on it carefully."

entries.zh: 峻論列其事，奏對不遜。
entries.en: Jun pressed the case point by point; in memorial and reply he showed no deference.
entries.literal: Jun enumerated and laid out the matter; in memorial and response he was not deferential.

entries.zh: 太祖未食，日將亭午，諍之不已。
entries.en: Taizu had not yet eaten; the sun was nearly at noon, yet Jun argued without stopping.
entries.literal: Taizu had not eaten; the sun was nearly at noon; Jun remonstrated without cease.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「節假之內，未欲便行，已俟假開，即依所奏。」
entries.en: Taizu said: "During the holiday I did not wish to act at once. When the holiday ends I will do as you ask."
entries.literal: Taizu said: "Within the festival holiday, I did not wish to act immediately; already I have waited until the holiday ends, then I will follow what you memorialized."

entries.zh: 峻退至中書。
entries.en: Jun withdrew to the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Jun withdrew to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 是月，吏部選人過門下，峻當其事，頗疑選部不公，其擬官選人落下者三十餘人。
entries.en: That month, as Ministry of Personnel candidates passed through the Secretariat, Jun handled the review. Convinced the selection office was unfair, he struck more than thirty nominees from the list.
entries.literal: That month, candidates of the Ministry of Personnel passed through the Secretariat gate; Jun was in charge of the matter. He greatly suspected the selection bureau of injustice and struck down more than thirty proposed appointees.

entries.zh: 次日寒食時節，臣僚各歸私第。
entries.en: The next day was Cold Food; the officials each went home.
entries.literal: The next day was the Cold Food Festival; the officials each returned to their private residences.

entries.zh: 午時，宣召宰臣、樞密使，及入，幽峻於別所。
entries.en: At noon the chief ministers and the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs were summoned; when they arrived, Jun was held apart in another room.
entries.literal: At noon, the chief councillors and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs were summoned; when they entered, Jun was secluded in a separate place.

entries.zh: 太祖見馮道已下，泣曰：「峻淩朕頗甚，無禮太過，擬欲盡去左右臣僚，翦朕羽翼。
entries.en: Taizu met Feng Dao and the others and wept: "Jun bullies me cruelly and shows outrageous disrespect. He means to drive away every minister at my side and cut off my wings.
entries.literal: Taizu, meeting Feng Dao and those below, wept and said: "Jun bullies Us greatly; his lack of ritual is excessive. He intends to remove all Our close ministers entirely and clip Our wings.

entries.zh: 朕兒在外，專意阻隔，暫令到闕，即懷怨望。
entries.en: My son is abroad, and Jun blocks him at every turn. When I briefly summoned him to court, Jun at once nursed resentment.
entries.literal: Our son is outside; he deliberately obstructs and blocks; when We briefly ordered him to come to court, he at once harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 豈有既總樞機，又兼宰相，堅求重鎮，尋亦授之，任其襟懷，尚未厭足，如此無君，誰能甘忍！」
entries.en: He already commands the pivot of state, serves also as chief minister, pressed for a great prefecture and got it—yet given his way, he is still not satisfied. A subject so faithless to his ruler—who could endure it!"
entries.literal: How can there be one who already holds overall charge of the pivot, also serves concurrently as chief councillor, obstinately demanded a weighty prefecture—and shortly it was granted—yet given free rein to his heart, he is still not satisfied? Such lack of regard for the ruler—who could bear it willingly!"

entries.zh: 即召翰林學士徐臺符等草制。
entries.en: He at once summoned the Hanlin academician Xu Taifu and others to draft the demotion edict.
entries.literal: At once he summoned the Hanlin Academician Xu Taifu and others to draft the edict.

entries.zh: 其日，退朝宣制，貶授商州司馬，差供奉官蔣光遠援送赴商州。
entries.en: That day, after court, the edict was proclaimed: Jun was demoted to Sima of Shangzhou, and the palace officer Jiang Guangyuan was sent to escort him there.
entries.literal: That day, after court was dismissed the edict was proclaimed: Jun was demoted and appointed Sima of Shangzhou; the tribute officer Jiang Guangyuan was dispatched to escort him to Shangzhou.

entries.zh: 未幾，死於貶所，時廣順三年三月也。
entries.en: Before long he died in exile, in the third month of the third year of Guangshun.
entries.literal: Before long he died at his place of exile—it was the third month of Guangshun year 3.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：峻至商州，得腹疾，帝猶湣之，命其妻往視之，未幾而卒。）〉
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: When Jun reached Shangzhou he fell ill with a griping belly. The emperor still pitied him and sent his wife to see him; he died soon after.)〉
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: When Jun reached Shangzhou he developed abdominal illness. The Emperor still pitied him and ordered his wife to visit him; before long he died.)〉

entries.zh: 太祖平兗州，詔曰：「閻宏魯、崔周度，死義之臣，禮加二等，所以滲漏澤而賁黃泉也。
entries.en: When the founder pacified Yan Prefecture, an edict said, "Yan Honglu and Cui Zhoudu died for righteousness. Their rites shall be raised two grades, that seeping favor may reach them even in the yellow springs.
entries.literal: When the founder pacified Yan Prefecture, an edict said: "Yan Honglu and Cui Zhoudu were ministers who died for righteousness; ritual is raised two grades, thereby letting seeping moisture reach the yellow springs.

entries.zh: 爾等貞節昭彰，正容肅厲，以從順為己任，以立義作身謀，履此禍機，並罹冤橫，宜伸贈典，以慰貞魂。
entries.en: Your steadfast loyalty shines forth; your bearing was upright and stern. You took obedience as your duty and righteousness as your life's aim, yet fell into this calamity and met wrongful death together. Posthumous honors are fitting to comfort your faithful spirits.
entries.literal: Your loyal integrity shines clear, your upright bearing stern and grave; you took obedience as your charge and establishing righteousness as your life's plan; you trod this snare of calamity and together met wrongful death—fitting to extend posthumous honors to comfort your faithful spirits.

entries.zh: 宏魯可贈左驍衛大將軍，周度可贈秘書少監。」
entries.en: Honglu shall be posthumously made General of the Left Brave Guards; Zhoudu shall be posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat."
entries.literal: Honglu may be posthumously awarded General of the Left Brave Guards; Zhoudu may be posthumously awarded Vice Director of the Secretariat."

entries.zh: 峻貪權利，多機數，好施小惠，喜人附己。
entries.en: Jun was greedy for power, full of schemes, fond of small favors, and happiest when men clustered about him.
entries.literal: Jun was greedy for power and profit, full of stratagems, fond of dispensing small favors, pleased when men attached to him.

entries.zh: 太祖登極之初，務存謙抑，潛龍將佐未甚進用，其後鄭仁誨、李重進、向訓等稍遷要職，峻心忌之，至是求退，蓋偵太祖之意也。
entries.en: Early in Guo Wei's reign he had kept his former companions in check and advanced them slowly. Later Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, Xiang Xun, and others were gradually promoted to high office. Jun resented it. His request to retire was largely a probe of the emperor's mind.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taizu's reign he preserved humility; hidden-dragon companions were not much advanced; afterward Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, Xiang Xun and others were gradually moved to key posts; Jun's heart envied them; at this time he sought withdrawal, largely probing Taizu's intent.

entries.zh: 未陳請之前，多發外諸侯書以求保證，旬浹之內，諸道馳騎進納峻書，聞者驚駭其事。
entries.en: Even before he filed the petition he had sent letters far and wide to regional commanders seeking pledges of support. Within a fortnight relay riders from every circuit galloped in with his letters. All who heard of it were shocked.
entries.literal: Before stating the petition, he sent many letters to outer commanderies seeking pledges; within ten days and more, every circuit sent relay riders bearing Jun's letters; hearers were appalled at the affair.

entries.zh: 峻連貢三章，中使宣諭無虛日，太祖嚴駕將幸其第，峻聞之，即馳馬入見，太祖慰勞久之，復令視事。
entries.en: Jun sent up three memorials in a row. Palace envoys came day after day with the emperor's word. Guo Wei in full procession was about to visit his mansion; Jun heard of it and galloped straight to court. The emperor comforted him at length and ordered him back to office.
entries.literal: Jun submitted three memorials in succession; palace envoys announced imperial will without an idle day; Taizu in full state was about to visit his residence; Jun heard and at once galloped in for audience; Taizu consoled him long, again ordered him back to duties.

entries.zh: 峻又於本院之東，別建公署，廓廡廳事，高廣華侈。
entries.en: Jun also built a new official compound east of his bureau, with corridors and reception halls lofty, spacious, and sumptuous.
entries.literal: Jun also east of his bureau separately built an official compound; corridors and halls lofty, broad, and lavish.

entries.zh: 及土木之功畢，請太祖臨幸，恩賜甚厚。
entries.en: When the building was finished he invited the emperor to visit in person, and the gifts showered on him were exceedingly rich.
entries.literal: When the earth-and-timber work was finished, he requested Taizu to visit in person; grace and gifts were very thick.

entries.zh: 其後內園新起小殿，峻視之，奏曰：「宮室已多，何用於此？」
entries.en: Later, when a small hall was built in the imperial park, Jun saw it and memorialized: "There are already more than enough palaces—why build this?"
entries.literal: Afterward, in the inner park a small hall was newly raised. Jun looked upon it and memorialized, saying: "Palaces and chambers are already numerous—what use is there in this?"

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「樞密院舍宇不少，公更自興造何也？」
entries.en: Taizu replied: "The Bureau of Military Affairs already has ample quarters—why are you building more on your own?"
entries.literal: Taizu said: "The halls and chambers of the Bureau of Military Affairs are not few—why has the Duke undertaken further construction on his own?"

entries.zh: 峻慚默而退。
entries.en: Jun said nothing more, withdrew in shame, and held his tongue.
entries.literal: Jun, ashamed, fell silent and withdrew.

entries.zh: 時峻以前事趙巖，頗承寵愛，至是欲希贈官立碑。
entries.en: Jun had once served Zhao Yan and enjoyed his favor; now he hoped to win a posthumous office and a commemorative stele.
entries.literal: At that time, because Jun had formerly served Zhao Yan, he had received considerable favor and affection; by then he wished to hope for a posthumous title and the erection of a stele.

entries.zh: 或謂峻曰：「趙巖以諂佞事君，破壞梁室，至今言者無不切齒，茍如所欲，必貽物議。」
entries.en: Someone warned him: "Zhao Yan flattered his sovereign and ruined the Liang house; men still speak of him with clenched teeth. If you have your way, you will invite scandal."
entries.literal: Someone said to Jun: "Zhao Yan, through flattery and obsequiousness in serving his lord, destroyed the house of Liang; to this day those who speak of him gnash their teeth without exception—if you obtain what you desire, you will surely bring upon yourself public criticism."

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: He dropped the matter.
entries.literal: He then stopped.

entries.zh: 巖侄崇勛，居於陳郡，峻為求官田宅以賜之，太祖亦從之。
entries.en: Yan's nephew Chongxun lived in Chen commandery; Jun secured official land and a mansion for him as a gift, and Taizu agreed.
entries.literal: Yan's nephew Chongxun dwelt in Chen commandery; Jun sought official fields and a residence to bestow upon him, and Taizu also assented.

entries.zh: 三年春，修利河堤，大興土功，峻受詔檢校。
entries.en: In the spring of the third year the court repaired the river dikes on a vast scale; Jun was ordered to supervise the works.
entries.literal: In the spring of the third year, river dikes were repaired for benefit and earthworks were launched on a great scale; Jun received an edict to inspect and oversee.

entries.zh: 既而世宗自澶州入覲，峻素憚世宗之聰明英果，聞其赴闕，即自河次歸朝。
entries.en: Soon afterward Shizong came from Chanzhou to attend court. Jun had long feared his intelligence and resolve; hearing that he was on his way to the capital, Jun left the river works at once and returned.
entries.literal: Before long Shizong came from Chanzhou to present himself at court. Jun had always feared Shizong's intelligence and martial resolve; hearing that he was proceeding to the capital, he at once returned to court from his post on the river.

entries.zh: 居無何，邀求兼領青州，太祖不得已而授之。
entries.en: Before long he pressed to hold Qingzhou as well; Taizu, unable to refuse, granted the post.
entries.literal: After not long, he pressed to be appointed concurrently as governor of Qingzhou; Taizu, having no alternative, granted it.

entries.zh: 既受命，求暫赴任，奏借左藏綾絹萬匹，從之。
entries.en: After accepting the commission he asked leave to take up the post and requested ten thousand bolts of damask from the Left Treasury; the request was granted.
entries.literal: Once he had received the appointment, he requested a temporary leave to take up his post and memorialized to borrow ten thousand bolts of silk damask from the Left Treasury; this was granted.

entries.zh: 閻宏魯者，後唐邢州節度使寶之子也。
entries.en: Yan Honglu was the son of Yan Bao, military governor of Xing Prefecture under Later Tang.
entries.literal: Yan Honglu was the son of Bao, Later Tang military governor of Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 寶，《唐書》有傳。
entries.en: Bao has a biography in the Tang History.
entries.literal: Bao has a biography in the Tang History.

entries.zh: 宏魯事唐明宗、晉高祖，累歷事任。
entries.en: Honglu served under Emperor Mingzong of Tang and the Jin founder, rising through a series of offices.
entries.literal: Honglu served Tang Mingzong and Jin Founder, accumulating posts through successive offices.

entries.zh: 家本魯中，洎告疾歸裏，慕容彥超初臨，禮待極厚。
entries.en: His family was from central Shandong. When he fell ill and went home, Murong Yanchao on first taking Yan treated him with the greatest courtesy.
entries.literal: His family was originally from central Lu; when he reported illness and returned home, Murong Yanchao on first arrival treated him with extreme courtesy.

entries.zh: 及謀大逆，以宏魯子希俊為鎮寧軍節度副使，在世宗幕下而惡之。
entries.en: When Yanchao plotted rebellion he made Honglu's son Xijun deputy military governor of Zhenning—but Xijun was on Shizong's staff, and Yanchao resented him.
entries.literal: When he plotted great treason, he made Honglu's son Xijun deputy military governor of Zhenning Army; Xijun was on Shizong's staff and Yanchao hated him.

entries.zh: 聞朝廷出兵堤防，即責宏魯曰：「爾教兒捍我於朝，將覆吾族耶！」
entries.en: Hearing that the court was sending troops, he at once rebuked Honglu: "You taught your son to oppose me at court—do you mean to destroy my whole clan?"
entries.literal: Hearing that the court had sent troops on guard, he at once blamed Honglu: "You taught your son to resist me at court—will you overthrow my clan!"

entries.zh: 故罹其禍。
entries.en: For this he suffered death.
entries.literal: Therefore he suffered this calamity.

entries.zh: 王延，字世美，鄚州長豐人也。
entries.en: Wang Yan, whose courtesy name was Shimei, came from Changfeng in Mozhou.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shimei, was a native of Changfeng in Mozhou.

entries.zh: 少為儒，善詞賦，會鄉曲離亂，不獲從鄉薦，因客於浮陽，隨滄帥戴思遠入梁。
entries.en: In youth he studied the classics and excelled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home region fell into chaos he could not obtain a local recommendation, so he lodged in Fuyang and followed the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang service.
entries.literal: In youth he was a Confucian scholar, skilled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home district was torn by disorder he could not obtain local recommendation, and therefore lodged in Fuyang, following the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang.

entries.zh: 嘗以所為賦謁梁相李琪，琪覽之，欣然曰：「此道近難其人，王生升我堂矣。」
entries.en: He once presented a fu he had written to Liang Chancellor Li Qi, who read it and said with delight, "This art has lately lacked a true master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my level."
entries.literal: He once presented a fu he had written to the Liang chancellor Li Qi; Qi read it and said with pleasure, "In recent times this art has lacked its master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my hall."

entries.zh: 繇是人士稱之。
entries.en: From that time men of letters spoke highly of him.
entries.literal: From this men of letters praised him.

entries.zh: 尋薦為即墨縣令，歷徐、宋、鄆、青四鎮從事。
entries.en: He was soon recommended as magistrate of Jimo and went on to serve as aide in the Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing circuits.
entries.literal: Soon he was recommended as magistrate of Jimo and successively served as aide in the four circuits of Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing.

entries.zh: 長興初，鄉人馮道、趙鳳在相位，擢拜左補闕。
entries.en: Early in the Changxing era his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were chief ministers; he was promoted to left supplementer.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Changxing his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng held the chief ministership; he was promoted and appointed left supplementer.

entries.zh: 逾年，以水部員外知制誥遷中書舍人，賜金紫。
entries.en: A year later he moved from vice director of the Water Ministry with responsibility for drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and received the gold-and-purple insignia.
entries.literal: After a year he was transferred from vice director of the Water Ministry with charge of drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and was granted gold-and-purple.

entries.zh: 清泰末，以本官權知貢舉。
entries.en: Near the end of the Qingtai era he was appointed in his existing post to oversee the civil examinations.
entries.literal: At the end of Qingtai he was appointed in his existing office to act as director of the civil examinations.

entries.zh: 時有舉子崔頎者，故相協之子也。
entries.en: Among the candidates was Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.
entries.literal: At the time there was an examinee named Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.

entries.zh: 協素與吏部尚書盧文紀不睦，及延將入貢院，文紀謂延曰：「舍人以謹重聞於時，所以去冬老夫在相位時，與諸相首以長者聞奏，用掌文衡。
entries.en: Xie had long been at odds with Minister of Personnel Lu Wenji. As Yan was about to enter the examination hall, Wenji told him, "You are known for your caution and gravity; that is why last winter, when I was chief minister, I was the first among the ministers to recommend a man of mature reputation to oversee the examinations.
entries.literal: Xie had long been on bad terms with the minister of Personnel Lu Wenji; as Yan was about to enter the examination compound, Wenji said to him, "You, Drafter, are known in the age for caution and weight; therefore last winter, when this old man was chief minister, I reported first among the ministers that a man of mature reputation should be appointed to hold the literary scales.

entries.zh: 然貢闈取士，頗多面目。
entries.en: Yet in selecting candidates for the examinations, personal connections often play a large part.
entries.literal: Yet in selecting scholars in the examination compound, there are often many personal connections.

entries.zh: 說者云：『越人善泅，生子方晬，乳母浮之水上。
entries.en: As the saying goes: "The people of Yue are skilled swimmers; when a child is barely a month old, the wet nurse floats him on the water."
entries.literal: Storytellers say: "The people of Yue are skilled at swimming; when a child is just one month old, the wet nurse floats him on the water."

entries.zh: 或駭然止之，乳母曰，其父善泅，子必無溺。』
entries.en: Someone alarmed tries to stop her; the wet nurse says, "His father is a skilled swimmer—the child will surely not drown."
entries.literal: Someone in alarm tries to stop it; the wet nurse says, "His father is skilled at swimming—the child will surely not drown."

entries.zh: 今若以名下取士，即此類也。
entries.en: If you choose candidates today by family name and reputation alone, it is exactly this sort of thing.
entries.literal: If today one selects scholars by name, it is just this sort of thing.

entries.zh: 舍人當求實才，以副公望。」
entries.en: You, as Drafter, should seek genuine talent to live up to the reputation you enjoy."
entries.literal: You, Drafter, ought to seek real talent, to fulfill public expectation.

entries.zh: 延退而謂人曰：「盧公之言，蓋為崔頎也。
entries.en: Yan withdrew and told others, "Master Lu's remarks were surely directed at Cui Qi.
entries.literal: Yan withdrew and said to others, "Master Lu's words were surely aimed at Cui Qi.

entries.zh: 縱與其父不悅，致意何至此耶！」
entries.en: Even if he bore ill will toward the boy's father, why make his meaning so plain!"
entries.literal: Even if he was displeased with the man's father, why carry the hint to such an extent!

entries.zh: 來春，以頎登甲科。
entries.en: The next spring, Cui Qi placed in the highest tier of the examinations.
entries.literal: The following spring, Hao passed in the top tier of the examinations.

entries.zh: 其年，改御史中丞，歲滿，轉尚書右丞。
entries.en: That same year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, and when his term ended he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.
entries.literal: That year he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.

entries.zh: 奉使兩浙，吳人深重之。
entries.en: While serving as envoy to the Two Zhes, he won the deep respect of the people of Wu.
entries.literal: On a mission to the Two Zhes, the people of Wu held him in deep esteem.

entries.zh: 復命，授吏部侍郎，改尚書左丞，拜太常卿，歷工、禮、刑三尚書。
entries.en: After reporting back, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and went on to hold the ministries of Works, Rites, and Punishments in succession.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and served successively as Minister of Works, Rites, and Punishments.

entries.zh: 以疾求分司西洛，授太子少保。
entries.en: He pleaded illness and asked for a post in the Luoyang branch office in the west, and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Citing illness, he requested a post in the western Luoyang branch office and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 既而連月請告，為留臺所糾，改少傅致仕。
entries.en: Before long he took medical leave month after month, was censured by the Luoyang branch office, and was reassigned as Junior Preceptor before retiring from office.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he repeatedly took leave for months on end and was censured by the Luoyang branch office; he was changed to Junior Preceptor and retired.

entries.zh: 廣順二年冬卒，時年七十有三。
entries.en: He died in the winter of the second year of Guangshun, at the age of seventy-three.
entries.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged seventy-three.

entries.zh: 子億，仕皇朝為殿中丞。
entries.en: His son Yi served the present dynasty as a Director in the Palace Bureau.
entries.literal: His son Yi served the present dynasty as Director in the Palace Bureau.

entries.zh: 劉皞，字克明，晉丞相譙國公句之弟也。
entries.en: Liu Hao, whose courtesy name was Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.
entries.literal: Liu Hao, courtesy name Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.

entries.zh: 句，《晉書》有傳。
entries.en: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.
entries.literal: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.

entries.zh: 皞少離鄉里，唐天祐中，梁將劉鄩襲太原，軍至樂平，時皞客於縣舍，為鄩軍所俘。
entries.en: Hao had left his hometown while still young. During the Tianyou reign of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun attacked Taiyuan; when his army reached Leping, Hao was staying at the county inn and was taken prisoner by Xun's forces.
entries.literal: Hao left his native place while still young. In the Tianyou era of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun raided Taiyuan; when the army reached Leping, Hao was lodging at the county guesthouse and was captured by Xun's troops.

entries.zh: 謝彥章見之，知其儒者，待之以禮，謂其鄉人劉去非曰：「為君得一宗人。」
entries.en: When Xie Yanzhang saw him, he recognized a man of learning and treated him courteously. He told his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."
entries.literal: Xie Yanzhang saw him, knew he was a scholar, and treated him with courtesy. He said to his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."

entries.zh: 即令皞見之，去非詢其爵裏，乃親族也，對泣久之，自是隨去非客於彥章門下。
entries.en: He then had Hao brought to meet him. Qufei inquired into his title and home district and found they were relatives; the two wept together for a long while. Thereafter Hao followed Qufei as a client in Yanzhang's entourage.
entries.literal: He then had Hao brought before him. Qufei asked about his rank and native place and found they were kin; the two wept together for a long time. From then on Hao followed Qufei as a guest in Yanzhang's household.

entries.zh: 彥章得罪，去非為郢州刺史，皞隨之郡。
entries.en: After Yanzhang fell from grace, Qufei was appointed prefect of Yingzhou, and Hao went with him to the prefecture.
entries.literal: When Yanzhang fell from favor, Qufei became prefect of Yingzhou, and Hao accompanied him to the prefecture.

entries.zh: 莊宗平河洛，去非以嘗從劉守奇歸梁，深懼獲罪，乃棄郡投高季興於荊南，皞累為荊州攝官。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the central plains, Qufei—who had once followed Liu Shouqi in defecting to Liang—feared severe punishment. He abandoned his post and threw in his lot with Gao Jixing in southern Jing; Hao served repeatedly as acting official in Jingzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the Yellow River region, Qufei, having once followed Liu Shouqi in surrendering to Liang, greatly feared punishment. He abandoned his prefecture and went to Gao Jixing in Jingnan; Hao repeatedly served as acting official in Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 既而兄句明宗朝為學士，遣人召歸。
entries.en: Later his elder brother Gou became a Hanlin academician under Emperor Mingzong and sent for him to return.
entries.literal: Later his elder brother Gou became an academician in the court of Emperor Mingzong and sent someone to summon him home.

entries.zh: 梁漢颙鎮鄧州，辟為從事，入為監察御史，歷水部員外郎、史館修撰。
entries.en: Liang Hanyong, military governor of Dengzhou, took him on as an aide. He then entered the capital as investigating censor and went on to serve as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
entries.literal: Liang Hanyong governed Dengzhou and recruited him as an aide; he entered the capital as investigating censor, then served as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

entries.zh: 長興末，宰臣趙鳳鎮邢臺，表為節度判官。
entries.en: Near the end of the Changxing era, Chief Minister Zhao Feng was posted to Xingtai and recommended him as adjutant to the military commissioner.
entries.literal: At the end of the Changxing era, the chief minister Zhao Feng governed Xingtai and recommended him as military commissioner adjutant.

entries.zh: 清泰初，入為起居郎，改駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事，移河南少尹、兵部郎中，轉太府卿。
entries.en: Early in the Qingtai era he entered court as recorder of imperial activity, then became vice director of the Transport Ministry while also serving as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business. He was later posted as vice director of Henan, director of the War Ministry, and finally minister of the Grand Treasury.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he entered service as recorder of the emperor's movements, was transferred to vice director of the Transport Ministry, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs. He was moved to vice director of Henan, director of the War Ministry, and then minister of the Grand Treasury.

entries.zh: 漢祖受命，用為宗正卿。
entries.en: When the founder of Later Han took the throne, he was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.
entries.literal: When the Han founder received the mandate, Hao was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 周初，改衛尉卿。
entries.en: Early in the Zhou dynasty he was made minister of the Palace Guard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was transferred to minister of the Palace Guard.

entries.zh: 從嚴，茂貞之長子也。
entries.en: Congyan was Maozhen's eldest son.
entries.literal: Congyan was Maozhen's eldest son.

entries.zh: 未冠，授諮議參軍，賜緋魚袋，尋還領彭州副使、鳳翔衙內都指揮使。
entries.en: Before he came of age he was made advisory staff officer and granted the crimson fish tally pouch; he soon returned to serve as deputy commissioner of Pengzhou and overall commander of the Fengxiang headquarters guard.
entries.literal: Before he came of age he was appointed Advisory Staff Officer, granted the crimson fish tally pouch, and soon returned to hold the posts of deputy commissioner of Peng Prefecture and overall commander within the Fengxiang yamen.

entries.zh: 天復中，自秦王府行軍司馬、檢校太傅出為涇州兩使留後。
entries.en: During Tianfu he left his posts as campaigning marshal of the Qin princely mansion and acting Grand Mentor to become acting commissioner of Jingzhou.
entries.literal: During Tianfu, from his posts as campaigning marshal of the Prince of Qin's mansion and acting Grand Mentor he went out to serve as acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs in Jing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 茂貞尋承制加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼待中，四鎮北庭行軍、彰義軍節度使。
entries.en: Maozhen soon, by delegated imperial authority, conferred on him the titles of opening an office with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
entries.literal: Maozhen soon by delegated authority added to him the titles of opening an office with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.

entries.zh: 及唐莊宗平梁，茂貞令從嚴入覲，制加從嚴兼中書令。
entries.en: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Maozhen sent Congyan to court, and an ordinance made him concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Liang, Maozhen ordered Congyan to come to court for an audience; by ordinance Congyan was additionally made concurrent Zhongshu Ling.

entries.zh: 俄而茂貞薨，遣奏權知鳳翔軍府事，詔起復，授鳳翔節度、管內觀察處置等使。
entries.en: Soon after Maozhen died he memorialized to take provisional charge of Fengxiang headquarters; the court ordered him to resume office from mourning and appointed him military commissioner of Fengxiang with full circuit authority.
entries.literal: Soon Maozhen died; he sent a memorial requesting provisional authority over Fengxiang military headquarters affairs; an edict ordered him to resume office from mourning; he was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit.

entries.zh: 三年九月，以魏王繼岌伐蜀，詔充供軍轉運應接使。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the third year, when Prince of Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu, an edict appointed Congyan commissioner for supply, transport, and liaison.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, as Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, an edict appointed him commissioner for supplying armies, transport, and liaison.

entries.zh: 四年正月，蜀平，繼岌命部署王衍一行東下，至岐，監軍使柴重厚不與符印，促令赴闕。
entries.en: In the first month of the fourth year Shu was pacified; Jiji ordered Wang Yan and his party escorted east; at Qi, army supervisory commissioner Chai Zhonghou withheld their tally seals and urged them on to the capital.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Shu was pacified; Jiji ordered the escort of Wang Yan and his party eastward; when they reached Qi, the army supervisory commissioner Chai Zhonghou would not give them tally seals and urged them to proceed to court.

entries.zh: 從嚴至華下，聞內難歸鎮，明宗詔誅重厚，從嚴以軍民不擾，重厚之力也，不以前事為隙，上表論救，事雖不允，時議嘉之。
entries.en: Congyan reached Huazhou, heard of turmoil at court, and returned to his post; Emperor Mingzong ordered Chai Zhonghou executed; Congyan credited Zhonghou with keeping the region calm and, without holding the earlier incident against him, memorialized in his defense; though the plea was denied, contemporaries praised him.
entries.literal: Congyan reached the area below Hua; hearing of internal turmoil he returned to his post; Emperor Mingzong ordered Chai Zhonghou executed; Congyan said that because soldiers and civilians were undisturbed, this was Zhonghou's merit; he did not hold the previous affair against him and submitted a memorial arguing for his rescue; though the matter was not granted, public opinion praised him.

entries.zh: 天成元年五月，制落起復，加檢校太師。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng an ordinance ended his mourning resumption and promoted him to acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng, by ordinance he was removed from mourning resumption and promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 其年九月，敕曰：「李從嚴等世聯宗屬，任重藩宣，慶善有稱，忠勤甚著。
entries.en: That ninth month an imperial command said: "Li Congyan and others are of long imperial kinship, bear heavy frontier responsibilities, are praised for their virtue, and are notably loyal and diligent.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of that year an imperial command said: "Li Congyan and others are linked by imperial clan kinship for generations, bear heavy responsibility in frontier governorship and proclamation, are praised for celebrating goodness, and are notably loyal and diligent.

entries.zh: 既預維城之列，宜新定體之文，是降寵光，以隆惇敘，俾煥成家之美，貴從猶子之規，宜於『嚴』、『昶』、『照』上改稱『從』。」
entries.en: As members of the imperial clan who shore up the realm, new forms of address are fitting; favor is therefore bestowed to exalt kinship and complete the family's honor according to the rule for younger imperial clansmen: the character Cong should replace Yan, Chang, and Zhao in their names."
entries.literal: Since they already belong to the ranks that shore up the realm, proper new forms of address should be established; therefore favor and glory are bestowed to exalt kinship ties, so that the beauty of family completion may shine forth and the honored rule for younger imperial clansmen may be observed; on the characters Yan, Chang, and Zhao the character Cong should be used instead."

entries.zh: 自長興元年，明宗有事於南郊，從嚴入覲，禮畢，移鎮汴州。
entries.en: From the first year of Changxing, when Mingzong performed the southern suburban rites, Congyan came to court; when the rites ended he was transferred to Bianzhou.
entries.literal: From the first year of Changxing, when Emperor Mingzong performed the southern suburban rites, Congyan came to court for an audience; when the rites were completed, he was transferred to govern Bian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四年，復入覲，改天平軍節度使。
entries.en: In the fourth year he again came to court and was made military commissioner of the Tianping army.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he again came to court for an audience and was changed to military commissioner of the Tianping Army.

entries.zh: 及唐末帝起兵於岐下，盡取從嚴家財器仗，以助軍須。
entries.en: When the last Tang emperor raised troops below Qi, he seized all of Congyan's family wealth and weapons for the army.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang raised troops below Qi, he took all of Congyan's family wealth and weapons to supply military needs.

entries.zh: 末帝發離岐城，吏民扣馬，乞以從嚴為帥，末帝許之。
entries.en: When the last emperor prepared to leave Qi, officials and commoners seized his horse's bridle and begged that Congyan be made commander; the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor set out to leave Qi city, officials and commoners seized his horse's bridle and begged that Congyan be made commander; the Last Emperor agreed.

entries.zh: 清泰初，即以從嚴復為鳳翔節度使，仍封秦國公。
entries.en: Early in Qingtai he was restored as military commissioner of Fengxiang and continued as Duke of Qin.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Congyan was at once restored as military commissioner of Fengxiang and still enfeoffed as Duke of Qin.

entries.zh: 晉高祖登極，繼封秦王、岐王，累食邑至一萬五千戶，食實封一千五百戶。
entries.en: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, Congyan was successively enfeoffed as Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi; his cumulative fief households reached fifteen thousand, with one thousand five hundred actual fief households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Jin ascended the throne, he was successively enfeoffed as Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi; his cumulative fief households reached fifteen thousand, with actual fief households of one thousand five hundred.

entries.zh: 少帝嗣位，加守太保。
entries.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made acting Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was added as acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 開運三年冬，卒於鎮，年四十有九。
entries.en: He died at his post in the winter of the third year of Kaiyun, aged forty-nine.
entries.literal: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun he died at his post; he was forty-nine years old.

entries.zh: 李茂貞，本姓宋，名文通，深州博野人。
entries.en: Li Maozhen was born Song Wentong, a native of Boye in Shenzhou.
entries.literal: Li Maozhen, original surname Song, personal name Wentong, a native of Boye in Shen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 祖鐸，父端。
entries.en: His grandfather was Duo and his father Duan.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Duo; his father was Duan.

entries.zh: 唐乾符中，鎮州有博野軍，宿衛京師，屯於奉天，文通時隸本軍為市巡，累遷至隊長。
entries.en: During the Qianfu reign of Tang, the Boye Army from Zhenzhou served as capital guards and was posted at Fengtian; Wentong then belonged to that unit as a market patrolman and rose in stages to company commander.
entries.literal: In the Qianfu era of Tang, Zhen Prefecture had the Boye Army, which garrisoned the capital as palace guards and was stationed at Fengtian; at that time Wentong served in this army as a market patrol officer and was promoted step by step to company commander.

entries.zh: 黃巢犯闕，博野軍留於鳳翔，時鄭畋理兵於岐下，畋遣文通以本軍敗尚讓之眾於龍尾坡，以功為神策軍指揮使。
entries.en: When Huang Chao stormed the capital, the Boye Army stayed at Fengxiang; Zheng Tian was then marshaling forces in the Qi region and sent Wentong with his own troops to rout Shang Rang at Longwei Slope, for which he was appointed commander of the Shence Army.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital, the Boye Army remained at Fengxiang; at that time Zheng Tian was organizing troops below Qi, and Tian sent Wentong with his native army to defeat Shang Rang's forces at Longwei Slope; for this merit he was made commander of the Shence Army.

entries.zh: 朱玫之亂，唐僖宗再幸興元，文通扈蹕山南，論功第一，遷檢校太保、同平章事、洋蓬壁等州節度使，賜姓，名茂貞，僖宗親為制字曰正臣。
entries.en: In Zhu Mei's revolt, when Emperor Xizong again fled to Xingyuan, Wentong escorted the court into the southern mountains and was judged foremost in merit; he was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi, made military commissioner of Yang, Peng, Bi and other prefectures, granted the surname Li and the name Maozhen, and given characters composed by Xizong himself reading "Loyal Minister."
entries.literal: During Zhu Mei's rebellion, Emperor Xizong of Tang again went to Xingyuan; Wentong escorted the imperial procession south of the mountains and ranked first in merit; he was promoted to acting Grand Guardian, Tongping Zhangshi, and military commissioner of Yang, Peng, Bi and other prefectures; he was granted the surname Li and the name Maozhen; Emperor Xizong personally composed characters for him reading "loyal minister."

entries.zh: 光啟二年，王行瑜殺朱玫於京師，李昌符擁兵於岐下，詔茂貞與陳佩等討之。
entries.en: In the second year of Guangqi, Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei at the capital while Li Changfu massed troops in the Qi region; the court ordered Maozhen, Chen Pei, and others to campaign against him.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei in the capital; Li Changfu held troops below Qi; an edict ordered Maozhen together with Chen Pei and others to attack him.

entries.zh: 三年，誅昌符，車駕還京，以茂貞為鳳翔節度使，加檢校太尉、兼待中、隴西郡王。
entries.en: The next year Changfu was put to death and the emperor returned to the capital; Maozhen was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and further honored as acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Longxi.
entries.literal: In the third year, Changfu was executed; the imperial carriage returned to the capital; Maozhen was made military commissioner of Fengxiang, with additional appointment as acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Longxi Commandery.

entries.zh: 光化元年三月，令其長子襲滄州，盧彥威委城而遁，遂兼有滄、景、德三郡，以守文為留後，請節鉞於朝。
entries.en: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua (898) he sent his eldest son to seize Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. Rengong then held Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and petitioned the court for the command baton.
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua he ordered his eldest son to attack Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. He then held the three prefectures of Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and requested the command baton from court.

entries.zh: 昭宗怒其擅興，不時與之。
entries.en: Emperor Zhaozong, angered by this unauthorized aggression, withheld the commission.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was angry at this unauthorized campaign and did not promptly grant it.

entries.zh: 會中使至范陽，仁恭私之曰：「旄節吾自有，但要長安本色耳，何以累章見阻？
entries.en: When a court envoy reached Fanyang, Rengong told him privately, "I already hold the command in fact—I only need the proper insignia from Chang'an. Why should repeated memorials stand in my way?
entries.literal: When a court messenger reached Fanyang, Rengong told him privately: "The command baton I already have myself—I only need the proper insignia from Chang'an. Why block me with repeated memorials?

entries.zh: 為吾言之。」
entries.en: Say as much for me there."
entries.literal: Speak for me on this."

entries.zh: 其悖戾如此。
entries.en: Such was the arrogance and perversity of the man.
entries.literal: His arrogance and perversity were such as this.

entries.zh: 仁恭兵鋒益盛，每戰多捷，以為天贊，遂有吞噬河朔之志。
entries.en: Rengong's armies grew ever stronger and he won battle after battle; taking this as Heaven's blessing, he set his sights on swallowing the whole Hebei region.
entries.literal: Rengong's martial power grew ever stronger and he won victory in most battles; he took this as Heaven's favor and formed the ambition to swallow up the north of the Yellow River.

entries.zh: 二年正月，仁恭率幽、滄步騎十萬，號三十萬，將兼並魏博、鎮定。
entries.en: In the first month of the second year he led a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry from You and Cang—claiming three hundred thousand—with the aim of annexing Weibo and Zhending.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year Rengong led a hundred thousand foot and horse from You and Cang, claiming three hundred thousand, intending to annex Weibo and Zhending.

entries.zh: 師次貝州，一鼓而拔，無少長皆屠之，清水為之不流。
entries.en: His army reached Beizhou and took it at the first assault, slaughtering every soul regardless of age until the Clearwater ran red and ceased to flow.
entries.literal: His army halted at Beizhou and took it at the first assault, slaughtering every person without distinction of age; the clear water ceased to flow.

entries.zh: 羅紹威求援於汴，汴將李思安、葛從周赴之，思安屯內黃。
entries.en: Luo Shaowei appealed to Bian for aid; Liang generals Li Si'an and Ge Congzhou marched to his relief, and Si'an encamped at Neihuang.
entries.literal: Luo Shaowei sought aid from Bian; Liang generals Li Si'an and Ge Congzhou went to help. Si'an encamped at Neihuang.

entries.zh: 仁恭兵圍魏州，聞汴軍在內黃，戒其子守文曰：「李思安怯懦，汝之智勇，比之十倍，當先殄此鼠輩，次擄紹威。」
entries.en: Rengong besieged Weizhou. Learning that Bian troops were at Neihuang, he told his son Shouwen, "Li Si'an is a coward; in wit and courage you are ten times his better. Destroy these vermin first, then take Shaowei prisoner."
entries.literal: Rengong besieged Weizhou. Hearing that Bian troops were at Neihuang, he admonished his son Shouwen: "Li Si'an is cowardly—in wit and courage you are ten times his match. First destroy these rats, then capture Shaowei."

entries.zh: 守文與單可及率漁陽精甲五萬，夾清水而上。
entries.en: Shouwen and Shan Keji then led fifty thousand crack troops from Yuyang up the Clearwater.
entries.literal: Shouwen and Shan Keji led fifty thousand elite troops from Yuyang up the Clearwater.

entries.zh: 思安設伏於內黃清水之左，袁象先設伏於內黃清水之右。
entries.en: Si'an posted an ambush on the left bank of the Clearwater at Neihuang, and Yuan Xiangxian another on the right.
entries.literal: Si'an laid an ambush on the left bank of the Clearwater at Neihuang; Yuan Xiangxian laid an ambush on the right.

entries.zh: 思安逆戰於繁陽城，偽不勝，徐退，燕人追躡，至於內黃，思安步兵成列，回擊之。
entries.en: Si'an gave battle at Fanyang, feigning defeat and drawing back slowly. The Yan troops pursued to Neihuang, where Si'an's infantry formed line and wheeled to counterattack.
entries.literal: Si'an met them in battle at Fanyang city, feigning defeat and slowly withdrawing. The Yan men pursued to Neihuang; Si'an's infantry formed ranks and wheeled to strike.

entries.zh: 燕人將引退，左右伏兵發，燕軍大敗，臨陣斬單可及，守文單騎僅免，五萬之眾無生還者。
entries.en: As the Yan were about to pull back, the ambushers on both flanks struck; the Yan army was shattered. Shan Keji was killed in the field; Shouwen alone escaped on horseback. Of fifty thousand men, not one returned alive.
entries.literal: As the Yan were about to withdraw, the ambushers on both flanks sprang forth; the Yan army was utterly routed. Shan Keji was killed in the battle; Shouwen escaped alone on horseback. Of the fifty thousand, none returned alive.

entries.zh: 時葛從周率邢、洺之眾入魏州，與賀德倫、李暉出擊賊營。
entries.en: Meanwhile Ge Congzhou had entered Weizhou with troops from Xing and Ming and, with He Delun and Li Hui, struck the enemy camp.
entries.literal: At that time Ge Congzhou had entered Weizhou at the head of troops from Xing and Ming, and with He Delun and Li Hui struck the rebel camp.

entries.zh: 是夜，仁恭燒營遁走，汴人長驅追擊，自魏至長河數百里，僵屍蔽地，敗旗折戟，累累於路。
entries.en: That night Rengong burned his camp and fled. The Liang pursued at full gallop from Wei to the Changhe—for hundreds of li the dead covered the earth, and broken banners and snapped halberds lay heaped along the road.
entries.literal: That night Rengong burned his camp and fled. The Liang men pursued at full speed from Wei to the Changhe—for several hundred li the dead lay covering the ground; broken banners and snapped halberds littered the road.

entries.zh: 鎮人又邀擊於東境，燕軍復敗。
entries.en: Zhending forces ambushed them again on the eastern frontier, and the Yan army was beaten a second time.
entries.literal: Zhen troops ambushed them again on the eastern border and the Yan army was defeated once more.

entries.zh: 仁恭自是垂翅不振者累年。
entries.en: From that day Rengong's wings were clipped, and for years he could not regain his strength.
entries.literal: From then on Rengong's wings were clipped and he did not recover for years.

entries.zh: 汴人乘勝攻滄州，仁恭率師援之，營於乾寧軍。
entries.en: The Liang pressed their victory against Cangzhou; Rengong marched to relieve it and encamped at Qianning Army.
entries.literal: The Liang took advantage of victory to attack Cangzhou. Rengong led troops to rescue and encamped at Qianning Army.

entries.zh: 汴將氏叔琮逆戰，燕軍逗撓，退保瓦橋，乃卑辭厚禮乞師於晉，武皇遣兵逼邢、洺以應之。
entries.en: Liang general Shi Shucong gave battle; the Yan army faltered, fell back to Wa Bridge, and then sent humble pleas and rich gifts begging Jin for aid. The Prince sent troops to threaten Xing and Ming in reply.
entries.literal: Liang general Shi Shucong met them in battle; the Yan army hesitated and stalled, fell back to defend Wa Bridge, then sent humble words and rich gifts begging troops from Jin. The Prince sent forces to press Xing and Ming in response.

entries.zh: 十月，汴人陷瀛、鄚二州，晉將周德威將兵出飛狐，仁恭復修好於晉。
entries.en: In the tenth month the Liang took Ying and Mo; Jin general Zhou Dewei marched out through Flying Fox Pass, and Rengong renewed his alliance with Jin.
entries.literal: In the tenth month the Liang took Ying and Mo; Jin general Zhou Dewei led troops out through Flying Fox Pass, and Rengong renewed friendly relations with Jin.

entries.zh: 守光性本庸昧，以父兄失勢，謂天所助，淫虐滋甚。
entries.en: Shouguang was by nature dull and foolish. Seeing his father and brother fall, he took it as Heaven's aid and grew ever more cruel and debauched.
entries.literal: Shouguang was by nature dull and foolish. Because his father and brother had lost power he thought Heaven was aiding him, and his cruelty and debauchery grew ever worse.

entries.zh: 每刑人必以鐵籠盛之，薪火四逼，又為鐵刷劀剔人面。
entries.en: Whenever he punished someone he placed the victim in an iron cage with fire closing in on all sides, and used an iron brush to scrape the face raw.
entries.literal: Whenever he punished a man he would place him in an iron cage with fires pressing in on all four sides, and also use an iron brush to scrape the man's face.

entries.zh: 嘗衣赭黃袍，顧謂將吏曰：「當今海內四分五裂，吾欲南面以朝天下，諸君以為何如？」
entries.en: Once he put on an ochre-yellow robe and asked his officers, "The realm is torn apart; I mean to face south and receive the homage of the empire—what do you think?"
