entries.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year, the great general of Zhenzhou Zhang Wenli murdered his commander Wang Rong; Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against him. At that time Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou conspired with Wenli and sent the Weisai Army commissioner Wang Yu to again lead the Khitan as reinforcements.

entries.zh: 十二月，安巴堅傾塞入寇，攻圍幽州，李紹宏以兵城守。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Abaoji invaded in force, besieged Youzhou, and Li Shaohong held the city with the garrison.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Abaoji poured across the frontier in invasion, attacked and besieged Youzhou, and Li Shaohong defended the city with troops.

entries.zh: 契丹長驅陷涿郡，執刺史李嗣弼，進攻易、定，至新樂，渡沙河，王都遣使告急。
entries.en: The Khitan swept south, took Zhuo, captured Prefect Li Sibi, and pressed Yi and Ding. They reached Xinle, crossed the Sha River, and Wang Du sent desperate appeals for help.
entries.literal: The Khitan drove straight through and took Zhuo commandery, seized Prefect Li Sibi, advanced to attack Yi and Ding, reached Xinle, crossed the Sha River, and Wang Du sent envoys in urgent appeal.

entries.zh: 時莊宗在鎮州行營，聞前鋒報日「敵渡沙河」，軍中鹹恐，議者請權釋鎮州之圍以避之。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was then at his field camp before Zhenzhou. When the vanguard reported, "The enemy has crossed the Sha River," panic spread through the army, and some urged him to raise the siege of Zhenzhou and withdraw.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Zhuangzong was at the field headquarters in Zhenzhou; hearing the vanguard report say "the enemy has crossed the Sha River," the army all feared, and advisers asked temporarily to lift the siege of Zhenzhou to avoid them.

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「霸王舉事，自有天道，契丹其如我何！
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "When a true conqueror takes the field, Heaven itself is on his side. What can the Khitan do to me?
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said: "When a hegemon-king undertakes affairs, Heaven has its own way — what can the Khitan do to me!

entries.zh: 國初，突厥入寇，至於渭北，高祖欲棄長安，遷都樊、鄧，太守曰：「獫狁孔熾，自古有之，未聞遷移都邑。
entries.en: At the founding of Tang, when the Turks raided as far as the north bank of the Wei, Gaozu wanted to abandon Chang'an for Fan and Deng. Taizong said, "The northern tribes have always been fierce. That is no reason to move the capital.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state, the Turks invaded and reached north of the Wei; Gaozu wished to abandon Chang'an and move the capital to Fan and Deng. Taizong said: "The Xianyun have always burned fiercely — from antiquity it has been so; one has never heard of moving the capital.

entries.zh: 霍去病，漢廷將帥，猶且誌滅匈奴，況帝王應運，而欲移都避寇哉！」
entries.en: Huo Qubing was only a Han general, yet he burned to destroy the Xiongnu. How could an emperor who holds Heaven's mandate think of fleeing the capital before mere raiders?"
entries.literal: Huo Qubing, a general of the Han court, still aspired to destroy the Xiongnu — how much more a sovereign who receives Heaven's mandate, yet would move the capital to flee bandits!"

entries.zh: 文皇雄武，不數年俘二突厥為衛士。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong was bold in war. Within a few years he had captured both Turk khans and made them his palace guards.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong was heroic and martial; within a few years he captured both Turks and made them palace guards.

entries.zh: 今吾以數萬之眾安集山東，王德明廝養小人，阿保機生長邊地，豈有退避之理，吾何面視蒼生哉！
entries.en: I hold Shandong secure with tens of thousands of men. Wang Deming is a groom's lackey, and Abaoji is a frontier barbarian. Why should I retreat? How could I face the people of this land?
entries.literal: Now I with tens of thousands of men have settled Shandong in peace — Wang Deming is a menial groom's petty man, Abaoji grew up on the frontier; is there any reason to retreat? How could I face the black-haired people!

entries.zh: 爾曹但駕馬同行，看吾破敵。」
entries.en: Mount up and ride with me. Watch me break the enemy."
entries.literal: You lot need only mount your horses and come along — watch me break the enemy."

entries.zh: 莊宗親禦鐵騎五千，至新城北，遇契丹前鋒萬騎，莊宗精甲自桑林突出，光明照日，諸部愕然緩退，莊宗分二廣以乘之，敵騎散退。
entries.en: He personally led five thousand armored horsemen to the north of Xincheng and met ten thousand Khitan vanguard troops. His elite cavalry burst from Mulberry Grove, armor flashing in the sun. The Khitan clans faltered and fell back. Zhuangzong split his force in two wings, routed them, and the enemy scattered.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong personally led five thousand iron cavalry to north of Xincheng, met ten thousand Khitan vanguard horsemen; Zhuangzong's picked armor burst from Mulberry Grove, light shining on the sun, the tribes stunned and slowing their retreat; Zhuangzong divided two wings to strike them, and the enemy horsemen scattered and withdrew.

entries.zh: 時沙河微冰，其馬多陷，安巴堅退保望都。
entries.en: The Sha River had only thin ice, and many Khitan horses foundered. Abaoji fell back to Wangdu.
entries.literal: At that time the Sha River had thin ice; many of their horses sank in; Abaoji withdrew to defend Wangdu.

entries.zh: 是夜，莊宗次定州，翌日出戰，遇奚長托諾五千騎，莊宗親軍千騎與之鬥，為其所圍，外救不及，莊宗挺馬奮躍，出入數四，酣戰不解。
entries.en: That night he camped at Dingzhou. The next day he gave battle and met the Xi chief Tuonuo with five thousand horsemen. A thousand of Zhuangzong's personal guard engaged them, were surrounded, and no relief could reach them in time. Zhuangzong spurred his horse and charged in and out of the ring four times, fighting on without pause.
entries.literal: That night Emperor Zhuangzong halted at Dingzhou; the next day he went out to battle, met the Xi chief Tuonuo with five thousand horsemen; Zhuangzong's personal guard of one thousand horsemen fought them, was surrounded by them, outside rescue could not reach in time; Zhuangzong spurred his horse and leaped fiercely, going in and out four times, fighting fiercely without resolution.

entries.zh: 李嗣昭聞其急也，灑泣而往，攻破敵陣，掖莊宗而歸。
entries.en: Li Sizhao, hearing that he was in peril, rode forward in tears, broke the enemy line, and brought Emperor Zhuangzong back to safety.
entries.literal: Li Sizhao, hearing he was in peril, went with tears streaming, broke the enemy formation, and supported Emperor Zhuangzong back.

entries.zh: 時契丹值大雪，野無所掠，馬無芻草，凍死者相望於路。
entries.en: Heavy snow fell on the Khitan. Nothing remained to plunder in the fields, fodder ran out, and frozen corpses lined the road as far as the eye could see.
entries.literal: At that time the Khitan encountered great snow; in the wilds there was nothing to plunder, horses had no fodder grass, and those frozen to death lined the road in sight of one another.

entries.zh: 安巴堅召盧文進，以手指天謂之曰：「天未令我到此。」
entries.en: Abaoji summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed to the sky, and said, "Heaven did not will me to come this far."
entries.literal: Abaoji summoned Lu Wenjin, pointed to Heaven with his finger and said to him: "Heaven has not yet willed me to come here."

entries.zh: 乃引眾北去。
entries.en: He then led his army north.
entries.literal: He then led the host north away.

entries.zh: 莊宗率精兵騎躡其後，每經安巴堅野宿之所，布稭在地，方而環之，雖去，無一莖亂者，莊宗謂左右曰：「蕃人法令如是，豈中國所及！」
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong pursued with elite cavalry. At every camp Abaoji had used, the straw was laid in neat squares and rings; even after the Khitan had gone, not a stalk was out of place. Zhuangzong told his attendants, "Their discipline is like this. China cannot match it."
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong led picked cavalry in pursuit behind them; wherever he passed Abaoji's camps in the wild, straw was spread on the ground in squares and circled — though they had gone, not a single stalk was disordered. Emperor Zhuangzong said to those at his side: "Barbarian law and order are like this — how could China match it!"

entries.zh: 莊宗至幽州，發二百騎偵之，皆為契丹所獲，莊宗乃還。
entries.en: He reached Youzhou and sent two hundred horsemen to scout. The Khitan captured them all, and he turned back.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong reached Youzhou, sent out two hundred horsemen to scout — all were captured by the Khitan — and Zhuangzong then returned.

entries.zh: 天祐末，安巴堅乃自稱皇帝，署中國官號。
entries.en: Late in the Tianyou era Abaoji proclaimed himself emperor and created offices on the Chinese model.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianyou, Abaoji then styled himself emperor and appointed Chinese official titles.

entries.zh: 其俗舊隨畜牧，素無邑屋，得燕人所教，乃為城郭宮室之制於漠北，距幽州三千里，名其邑曰西樓邑，屋門皆東向，如車帳之法。
entries.en: They had always lived as nomads and built no permanent towns until men from Yan taught them. Abaoji then raised walled cities and palaces in the northern steppe three thousand li from Youzhou. He called his capital Western Tower. Every doorway faced east, as with their wagon tents.
entries.literal: Their custom had long followed pastoral herding and they had never had towns or houses; taught by men of Yan, they then made the system of walled cities and palaces in the northern desert, three thousand li from Youzhou, naming their settlement Western Tower Settlement; house doors all faced east, like the method of cart tents.

entries.zh: 城南別作一城，以實漢人，名曰漢城，城中有佛寺三，僧尼千人。
entries.en: South of the capital he built a separate city for Han subjects called Han City. It held three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.
entries.literal: South of the city they separately built another city to house Han people, called Han City; within the city were three Buddhist temples and a thousand monks and nuns.

entries.zh: 其國人號安巴堅為天皇王。
entries.en: His people called Abaoji the Heavenly Emperor King.
entries.literal: The people of his state called Abaoji the Heavenly Emperor King.

entries.zh: 同光中，安巴堅深著辟地之志，欲收兵大舉，慮渤海踵其後。
entries.en: During Tongguang, Abaoji was bent on expansion and meant to gather his armies for a major campaign, but he feared that Bohai would strike at his rear.
entries.literal: In the Tongguang era, Abaoji deeply harbored ambition to open territory, wished to gather troops for a great campaign, and feared Bohai would follow at his heels.

entries.zh: 三年，舉其眾討渤海之遼東，令禿餒、盧文進據營、平等州，擾我燕薊。
entries.en: In year three he marched in force against Bohai's Liaodong. He left Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying, Ping, and neighboring prefectures and raid Yan and Ji.
entries.literal: In the third year he raised his host to campaign against Bohai's Liaodong, ordered Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying and Ping and other prefectures, and harass our Yan and Ji.

entries.zh: 明宗初纂嗣，遣供奉官姚坤奉書告哀，至西樓邑，屬阿保機在渤海，又徑至慎州，崎嶇萬里。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong first took the throne, he sent the palace attendant Yao Kun with a letter of condolence. Kun reached Western Tower, learned that Abaoji was campaigning in Bohai, and pressed on to Shenzhou across ten thousand li of hard country.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong first succeeded to the throne, he sent the palace attendant Yao Kun to present a letter announcing mourning; he reached Western Tower Settlement — it happened that Abaoji was in Bohai — and again went straight to Shenzhou, ten thousand li of rugged travel.

entries.zh: 既至，謁見阿保機，延入穹廬，阿保機身長九尺，被錦袍，大帶垂後，與妻對榻引見坤。
entries.en: When he arrived he was received by Abaoji in the royal tent. Abaoji stood nine chi tall, wore a brocade robe with a great belt hanging behind him, and with his wife on a facing couch received Kun.
entries.literal: When he arrived he had audience with Abaoji, who invited him into the domed tent; Abaoji was nine chi in height, wore a brocade robe, a great belt hanging behind, and with his wife on facing couches received and introduced Kun.

entries.zh: 坤未致命，阿保機先問曰：「聞爾漢土河南、河北各有一天子，信乎？」
entries.en: Before Kun could deliver his message, Abaoji asked, "I hear that your Han lands now have one Son of Heaven south of the Yellow River and another north of it. Is that true?"
entries.literal: Before Kun could deliver his charge, Abaoji first asked: "I hear that in your Han lands south of the river and north of the river each has a Son of Heaven — is it true?"

entries.zh: 坤曰：「河南天子，今年四月一日洛陽軍變，今兇問至矣。
entries.en: Kun said, "The Son of Heaven south of the river died in a military mutiny at Luoyang on the first day of the fourth month this year. The grievous news has only now reached us.
entries.literal: Kun said: "The Son of Heaven south of the river — this year on the first day of the fourth month there was a military mutiny at Luoyang; now the grievous news has arrived.

entries.zh: 河北總管令公，比為魏州軍亂，先帝詔令除討，既聞內難，軍眾離心，及京城無主，上下堅冊令公，請主社稷，今已順人望登帝位矣。」
entries.en: The chief commander north of the river, Lord Ling, had lately been ordered by the late emperor to suppress the Weizhou mutiny. When he heard of the turmoil in the capital, his troops lost heart. With the throne empty, his officers and men pressed him to take the throne, and he has now ascended in accord with their will."
entries.literal: The Chief Commander north of the river, Lord Ling — recently because of the Weizhou military mutiny the late emperor issued an edict ordering him to suppress it; once he heard of internal troubles, the army and masses lost heart, and when the capital had no lord, high and low firmly enthroned Lord Ling and asked him to preside over the altars of soil and grain — he has now followed the people's hope and ascended the imperial throne."

entries.zh: 阿保機號咷，聲淚俱發，曰：「我與河東先世約為兄弟，河南天子吾兒也。
entries.en: Abaoji broke into loud wailing, voice and tears together, and said, "Your late sovereign of Hedong and I were sworn brothers. The Son of Heaven south of the river was my son.
entries.literal: Abaoji wailed aloud, voice and tears together bursting forth, and said: "I and the late lord of Hedong pledged brotherhood — the Son of Heaven south of the river was my son.

entries.zh: 近聞漢地兵亂，點得甲馬五萬騎，比欲自往洛陽救助我兒，又緣渤海未下，我兒果致如此，冤哉！」
entries.en: When I heard of the turmoil in your lands I gathered fifty thousand horsemen and was about to ride to Luoyang myself to save my son, but Bohai was not yet conquered. And now my son has come to this. How unjust!"
entries.literal: Recently hearing of military turmoil in Han lands, I mustered fifty thousand armored horses and had just intended to go myself to Luoyang to rescue my son, but again because Bohai was not yet subdued, my son truly came to this — how unjust!"

entries.zh: 泣下不能已。
entries.en: He wept without cease.
entries.literal: Tears fell and he could not stop.

entries.zh: 又謂坤曰：「今漢土天子，初聞洛陽有難，不急救，致令及此。」
entries.en: He told Kun again, "Your new emperor heard of the disaster at Luoyang and did not hurry to help. That is how things came to this pass."
entries.literal: He again said to Kun: "Now the Son of Heaven of Han lands, when he first heard of trouble at Luoyang, did not rush to rescue — causing it to reach this."

entries.zh: 坤曰：「非不急切，地遠阻隔不及也。」
entries.en: Kun said, "It was not for lack of urgency. The distance was too great and we could not arrive in time."
entries.literal: Kun said: "It was not that we were not urgent — the distance was far and barriers blocked; we could not arrive in time."

entries.zh: 又曰：「我兒既殂，當合取我商量，安得自便！」
entries.en: He said again, "Now that my son is dead, you should have consulted me. How could you decide on your own?"
entries.literal: He again said: "Since my son has died, you ought to have consulted me — how could you act on your own!"

entries.zh: 坤曰：「吾皇將兵二十年，位至大總管，所部精兵三十萬，眾口一心，聖堅推戴，違之則立見禍生，非不知稟天皇王意旨，無奈人心何。」
entries.en: Kun said, "Our emperor has led armies for twenty years and commands three hundred thousand elite troops. Every man under him spoke as one. They pressed him to the throne, and to refuse would have brought immediate ruin. We do not ignore the Heavenly Emperor King's wishes, but we could not defy the will of the army."
entries.literal: Kun said: "Our emperor has commanded troops for twenty years, risen to Great Chief Commander, has three hundred thousand picked troops under him, every mouth with one heart — the sage was firmly pushed to the throne; to disobey would at once bring disaster — it is not that we did not know to defer to the Heavenly Emperor King's intent, but we were helpless before the people's will."

entries.zh: 其子托雲在側，謂坤曰：「漢使勿多談。」
entries.en: His son Tuoyun, standing beside him, said to Kun, "Han envoy, say no more."
entries.literal: His son Tuoyun was at his side and said to Kun: "Han envoy, do not talk overmuch."

entries.zh: 因引左氏牽牛蹊田之說以折坤，坤曰：「應天順人，不同匹夫之義，只如天皇王初領國事，豈是強取之耶！」
entries.en: He cited the Zuo Commentary tale of the oxherd who trampled another's fields to rebuke Kun. Kun replied, "To follow Heaven and win the people's assent is not the same as a private quarrel. When you first took power, Heavenly Emperor King, was that by force alone?"
entries.literal: He then cited from the Zuo Commentary the story of the oxherd trampling fields to refute Kun; Kun said: "Answering Heaven and following the people is not the same as a common man's righteousness — just as when the Heavenly Emperor King first took charge of state affairs, was it by force that he took it!"

entries.zh: 阿保機因曰：「理當如此，我漢國兒子致有此難，我知之矣。
entries.en: Abaoji said, "That is only right. I know now why my Han son came to this end.
entries.literal: Abaoji then said: "It ought to be so — my Han-state son brought this trouble on himself; I understand it now.

entries.zh: 聞此兒有宮婢二千，樂官千人，終日放鷹走狗，耽酒嗜色，不惜人民，任使不肖，致得天下皆怒。
entries.en: I hear he kept two thousand palace women and a thousand musicians, spent his days hawking and hunting, drowned himself in wine and women, wasted the people, and put worthless men in office until the whole realm turned against him.
entries.literal: I heard this son had two thousand palace maids and a thousand music officers, all day released hawks and coursed dogs, indulged in wine and favored women, did not cherish the people, employed the unworthy at will, and thereby made all under Heaven angry.

entries.zh: 我自聞如斯，常憂傾覆，一月前已有人來報，知我兒有事，我便舉家斷酒，解放鷹犬，休罷樂官。
entries.en: When I heard such things I feared ruin for my own house. A month ago a messenger told me my son was in danger. I forbade wine in my household, released my hawks and dogs, and dismissed my musicians.
entries.literal: When I myself heard it was so, I constantly feared overthrow; a month ago someone had already come to report, knowing my son was in trouble — I then had the whole household cut off wine, released hawks and dogs, and dismissed the music officers.

entries.zh: 我亦有諸部家樂千人，非公宴未嘗妄舉。
entries.en: I too have a thousand household musicians among the tribes, and I never call for music except at state feasts.
entries.literal: I too have a thousand household musicians of the tribes, and except at public feasts I never raise them rashly.

entries.zh: 我若所為似我兒，亦應不能持久矣，從此願以為戒。」
entries.en: If I acted as my son did, I could not have endured either. From this day I take his fate as my warning."
entries.literal: If what I did were like my son, I too could not have lasted long — from now on I wish to take this as a warning.

entries.zh: 又曰：「漢國兒與我雖父子，亦曾彼此讎敵，俱有惡心，與爾今天子無惡，足得歡好。
entries.en: He said again, "That Han son and I were father and son in name, yet we were enemies at heart. With your present emperor there is no such ill will. We can be good friends.
entries.literal: He again said: "The Han-state son and I, though father and son, were also once mutual enemies — both had ill will; with your present Son of Heaven there is no ill will — enough to be on friendly terms.

entries.zh: 爾先復命，我續將馬萬騎至幽、鎮以南，與爾家天子面為盟約，我要幽州，令漢兒把捉，更不復侵入漢界。」
entries.en: Return first with your report. I will follow with ten thousand horsemen south of You and Zhen to swear alliance with your emperor in person. I want Youzhou held by Han men, and I will not cross the Han frontier again."
entries.literal: You first return with your report; I will then lead ten thousand horses south of You and Zhen to make a face-to-face covenant with your house's Son of Heaven — I want Youzhou and will have Han men hold it, and will no longer invade Han territory."

entries.zh: 又問：「漢收得西川，信不？」
entries.en: He asked again, "Is it true that you have taken western Shu?"
entries.literal: He again asked: "The Han have taken western Shu — is it true?"

entries.zh: 坤曰：「去年九月出兵，十一月十六日收下東、西川，得兵馬二十萬，金帛無算。
entries.en: Kun said, "Our armies marched last year in the ninth month and on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month took both eastern and western Shu. We gained two hundred thousand troops and horses and untold gold and silks.
entries.literal: Kun said: "Last year in the ninth month troops were sent out; on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month eastern and western Shu were taken, obtaining two hundred thousand troops and horses, gold and silks beyond counting.

entries.zh: 皇帝初即位，未辦送來，續當遣使至矣。」
entries.en: The emperor has only just taken the throne and has not yet been able to send tribute, but envoys will follow soon."
entries.literal: The emperor has just ascended the throne and has not yet been able to send them; envoys will be dispatched presently."

entries.zh: 阿保機忻然曰：「聞西有劍閣，兵馬從何過得？」
entries.en: Abaoji said with delight, "I have heard of Sword Pass in the west. How could an army pass it?"
entries.literal: Abaoji said with pleasure: "I hear in the west there is Sword Pass — how could troops and horses get through?"

entries.zh: 坤曰：「川路雖險，然先朝收復河南，有精兵四十萬，良馬十萬騎，但通人行處，便能去得，視劍閣如平地耳。」
entries.en: Kun said, "The Shu roads are steep, but when the former dynasty recovered Henan it had four hundred thousand elite troops and one hundred thousand fine horses. Wherever a man can walk, an army can go. Sword Pass is level ground to us."
entries.literal: Kun said: "Though the Shu roads are perilous, yet when the former dynasty recovered Henan it had four hundred thousand picked troops and one hundred thousand fine horses — wherever a man can pass, one can go; Sword Pass is regarded as level ground."

entries.zh: 阿保機善漢語，謂坤曰：「吾解漢語，歷口不敢言，懼部人效我，令兵士怯弱故也。」
entries.en: Abaoji was fluent in Chinese. He told Kun, "I understand your language, but I have never dared speak it openly, lest my tribes imitate me and my warriors grow soft."
entries.literal: Abaoji was skilled in Han speech and said to Kun: "I understand Han speech, but through all my days I dared not speak it, fearing the tribes would imitate me and make the soldiers timid and weak."

entries.zh: 坤至止三日，阿保機病傷寒。
entries.en: Kun had been there only three days when Abaoji fell ill with a fever.
entries.literal: Kun had been there only three days when Abaoji fell ill with cold damage.

entries.zh: 一夕，大星殞於其帳前，俄而卒於扶餘城，時天成元年七月二十七日也。
entries.en: One night a great star fell before his tent. Soon afterward he died at Fuyu city, on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of Tiancheng 1.
entries.literal: One night a great star fell before his tent; shortly he died at Fuyu city — the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month of Tiancheng 1.

entries.zh: 其妻舒嚕氏自率眾護其喪歸西樓，坤亦從行，得報而還。
entries.en: His wife Lady Shulü led the funeral train back to Western Tower. Kun accompanied them, received word of the death, and returned.
entries.literal: His wife Lady Shulü herself led the host to escort the bier back to Western Tower; Kun also followed on the journey, received the report, and returned.

entries.zh: 既而舒嚕氏立其次子德光為渠帥，以總國事，尋遣使告哀，明宗為之輟朝。
entries.en: Lady Shulü then installed her second son Deguang as chief to govern the state. She soon sent envoys to announce the death, and Emperor Mingzong suspended court in mourning.
entries.literal: Shortly Lady Shulü enthroned her second son Deguang as tribal chief to oversee state affairs; soon she sent envoys to announce mourning, and Emperor Mingzong suspended court for it.

entries.zh: 明年正月，葬阿保機於木葉山，偽謚曰「大聖皇帝」。
entries.en: In the first month of the following year they buried Abaoji on Mount Muye and gave him the posthumous title "Great Sage Emperor."
entries.literal: In the first month of the following year they buried Abaoji on Mount Muye; his false posthumous title was "Great Sage Emperor."

entries.zh: 阿保機凡三子，皆雄偉。
entries.en: Abaoji had three sons, all imposing men.
entries.literal: Abaoji had three sons in all, all imposing in stature.

entries.zh: 長曰人皇王突然，即東丹王也；
entries.en: The eldest was called Human Emperor King Turan, the King of Eastern Dan;
entries.literal: The eldest was called Human Emperor King Turan — that is, the King of Eastern Dan;

entries.zh: 次曰元帥太子，即德光也；
entries.en: the second was Marshal Crown Prince Deguang;
entries.literal: the second was called Marshal Crown Prince — that is, Deguang;

entries.zh: 幼曰阿安端君。
entries.en: the youngest was Lord Aanduan.
entries.literal: the youngest was called Lord Aanduan.

entries.zh: 德光本名耀屈之，後慕中華文字，遂改焉。
entries.en: Deguang had originally been named Yaokuizhi, but later he admired Chinese writing and took a new name.
entries.literal: Deguang's original name was Yaokuizhi; later he admired Chinese script and therefore changed it.

entries.zh: 唐天成初，阿保機死，其母令德光權主牙帳，令少子安端少君往渤海國代突欲。
entries.en: Early in Tiancheng, when Abaoji died, his mother had Deguang govern the tribal camp in his stead and sent the youngest son, Young Lord Anduan, to Bohai to replace Tuyu.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tang's Tiancheng, when Abaoji died, his mother had Deguang provisionally preside over the tribal encampment and sent the younger son Young Lord Anduan to the Bohai state to replace Tuyu.

entries.zh: 突欲將立，而德光素為部族所服，又其母亦常鐘愛，故因而立之。
entries.en: Tuyu had been expected to succeed, but the tribes had long respected Deguang, and his mother favored him, so Deguang was enthroned instead.
entries.literal: Tuyu was about to be installed, but Deguang had long been obeyed by the tribes, and his mother also constantly favored him, and therefore he was installed instead.

entries.zh: 明宗時，德光遣使摩琳等三十餘人來修好，又遣使為父求碑石，明宗許之，賜與甚厚，並賜其母瓔珞錦彩。
entries.en: During Mingzong's reign Deguang sent more than thirty envoys led by Molin to renew relations and asked for a memorial stele for his father. Mingzong agreed, lavished gifts upon them, and sent brocades and jeweled necklaces to Deguang's mother.
entries.literal: In Emperor Mingzong's time, Deguang sent envoys Molin and more than thirty others to renew friendly relations, and again sent envoys to seek a stone stele for his father; Emperor Mingzong granted it, gifts were very generous, and he also bestowed on his mother necklaces and brocades.

entries.zh: 自是山北安靜，蕃漢不相侵擾。
entries.en: From that time the country north of the mountains was at peace, and Khitan and Han did not raid one another.
entries.literal: From then on the lands north of the mountains were quiet, and barbarians and Han did not harass each other.

entries.zh: 十五日，漢高祖建號於晉陽，德光聞之，削奪漢祖官爵。
entries.en: On the fifteenth day the Han founder proclaimed his reign at Jinyang. Deguang heard of it and stripped him of all titles.
entries.literal: On the fifteenth day the Han Founder established his reign title at Jinyang; Deguang heard of it and stripped the Han ancestor of office and rank.

entries.zh: 是月，晉州、潞州並歸河東。
entries.en: That month Jin and Lu prefectures both went over to Hedong.
entries.literal: That month Jin and Lu prefectures both returned to Hedong.

entries.zh: 時盜賊所在群起，攻劫州郡，斷澶州浮梁。
entries.en: Bandits rose everywhere, raided the prefectures, and destroyed the pontoon bridge at Chanzhou.
entries.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere in groups, attacked and plundered prefectures and commanderies, and cut the Chanzhou pontoon bridge.

entries.zh: 契丹大恐，沿河諸藩鎮並以腹心鎮之。
entries.en: The Khitan were terrified and posted trusted commanders along the river.
entries.literal: The Khitan were greatly afraid; all military governors along the river garrisoned them with trusted men.

entries.zh: 三月朔日，德光坐崇元殿，行入閣之禮，睹漢家儀法之盛，大悅。
entries.en: On the first day of the third month he sat in Chongyuan Hall for the entering-the-pavilion ceremony. Delighted by the grandeur of Chinese court ritual, he was in high spirits.
entries.literal: On the first day of the third month Deguang sat in Chongyuan Hall and performed the entering-the-pavilion rite; seeing the splendor of Han ritual and law, he was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 以其大將蕭翰為汴州節度使。
entries.en: He appointed his general Xiao Han military governor of Bianzhou.
entries.literal: He appointed his great general Xiao Han military governor of Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 十七日，德光北還。
entries.en: On the seventeenth day Deguang marched north.
entries.literal: On the seventeenth day Deguang returned north.

entries.zh: 發離東京，宿於赤岡，有大聲如雷，起於牙帳之下，契丹自黎陽濟河，次湯陰縣界，有一岡，土人謂之愁死岡，德光憩於其上，謂宣徽使高勛曰：「我在上國，以打圍食肉為樂，自及漢地，每每不快，我若得歸本土，死亦無恨。」
entries.en: Leaving the Eastern Capital he camped at Chigang. Thunder sounded beneath his tent. The Khitan crossed the river at Liyang and halted in Tangyin county at a hill the locals called Sorrow-Death Mound. Resting there, Deguang told Palace Secretariat commissioner Gao Xun, "At home I took joy in the hunt and fresh meat. Since I came to Han lands I have known little pleasure. If I can reach my own country again, I will die content."
entries.literal: Setting out from the Eastern Capital, he lodged at Chigang; a great sound like thunder rose beneath the tent headquarters. The Khitan crossed the river from Liyang, halted at the border of Tangyin county; there was a hillock the locals called Sorrow-Death Mound; Deguang rested upon it and said to the Palace Secretariat commissioner Gao Xun: "In my upper country I take joy in hunting and eating meat; since reaching Han lands I am often displeased — if I can return to my native soil, death will hold no regret."

entries.zh: 勛退而謂人曰：「其語偷，殆將死矣。」
entries.en: When Xun withdrew he told others, "His words were evasive. He is near death."
entries.literal: Xun withdrew and said to others: "His words are furtive — he is probably about to die."

entries.zh: 時賊帥梁暉據相州，德光親率諸部以攻之。
entries.en: The bandit Liang Hui held Xiangzhou, and Deguang led his tribes against him in person.
entries.literal: At that time the bandit chief Liang Hui held Xiangzhou; Deguang personally led the tribes to attack him.

entries.zh: 四月四日，屠其城而去。
entries.en: On the fourth day of the fourth month he massacred the city and marched on.
entries.literal: On the fourth day of the fourth month he slaughtered the city and departed.

entries.zh: 德光聞河陽軍亂，謂蕃漢臣僚曰：「我有三失：殺上國兵士，打草谷，一失也；
entries.en: Hearing of the mutiny at Heyang, Deguang told his Khitan and Han officials, "I have committed three errors. I killed my own soldiers and let them plunder the countryside. That is the first.
entries.literal: Deguang heard of the Heyang army mutiny and said to barbarian and Han officials: "I have three faults: killing soldiers of the upper country and raiding for fodder — the first fault;

entries.zh: 天下括錢，二失也；
entries.en: I seized money from the whole realm. That is the second.
entries.literal: levying money throughout the realm — the second fault;

entries.zh: 不尋遣節度使歸藩，三失也。」
entries.en: I did not send the military governors back to their posts at once. That is the third."
entries.literal: not promptly sending military governors back to their circuits — the third fault."

entries.zh: 十六日，次於欒城縣殺虎林之側，時德光已得寒熱疾數日矣，命部人賫酒脯，禱於得疾之地。
entries.en: On the sixteenth day he halted beside Tiger-Slaying Grove in Luancheng county. He had been feverish for days and ordered his men to offer wine and meat at the spot where he had fallen ill.
entries.literal: On the sixteenth day he halted beside Tiger-Slaying Grove in Luancheng county; by then Deguang had had alternating chills and fever for several days and ordered tribesmen to carry wine and dried meat, praying at the place where he had fallen ill.

entries.zh: 十八日晡時，有大星落於穹廬之前，若迸火而散，德光見之，西望而唾，連呼曰：「劉知遠滅，劉知遠滅！」
entries.en: Late on the eighteenth day a great star fell before his tent like a burst of fire. Deguang looked west, spat, and cried again and again, "Liu Zhiyuan is finished! Liu Zhiyuan is finished!"
entries.literal: At the si hour on the eighteenth day a great star fell before the domed tent, as if bursting fire and scattering; Deguang saw it, looked west and spat, crying repeatedly: "Liu Zhiyuan is destroyed, Liu Zhiyuan is destroyed!"

entries.zh: 是月二十一日卒，時年四十六，主契丹凡二十二年。
entries.en: He died on the twenty-first day of that month at the age of forty-six, having ruled the Khitan for twenty-two years.
entries.literal: On the twenty-first day of that month he died, aged forty-six; he ruled the Khitan for twenty-two years in all.

entries.zh: 契丹人破其屍，摘去腸胃，以鹽沃之，載而北去，漢人目之為「帝羓」焉。
entries.en: The Khitan opened his body, removed the entrails, packed it in salt, and carried it north. The Han called it "the emperor's cured meat."
entries.literal: The Khitan broke open his corpse, removed the entrails, poured salt upon it, and carried it north — Han people regarded it as "emperor's cured meat."

entries.zh: 〈（案「以下原本闕佚」。
entries.en: (Note: "The text below was originally missing from the received edition."
entries.literal: (Note: "The text below was originally missing."

entries.zh: 據《五代會要》云：四月十八日，德光卒於欒城。
entries.en: According to the Essentials of the Five Dynasties, Deguang died at Luancheng on the eighteenth day of the fourth month.
entries.literal: According to the "Essentials of the Five Dynasties" it says: on the eighteenth day of the fourth month Deguang died at Luancheng.

entries.zh: 五月，宣遣制，以永康王襲位。
entries.en: In the fifth month an edict proclaimed Prince Yongkang as successor.
entries.literal: In the fifth month an edict was proclaimed appointing Prince Yongkang to succeed to the throne.

entries.zh: 永康王者，東丹王之長子，以其月二十一日領部族歸國，改會同十年為天祿元年，自稱天授皇帝。
entries.en: Prince Yongkang was the eldest son of the King of Eastern Dan. On the twenty-first day of that month he led the tribes home, proclaimed the Tianlu era in place of Huitong 10, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Granted.
entries.literal: Prince Yongkang was the eldest son of the King of Eastern Dan; on the twenty-first day of that month he led the tribes back to the state, changed Huitong 10 to Tianlu 1, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Granted.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐三年十一月，率騎數萬，陷邢州之內丘縣、深州之饒陽縣。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Han Ganyou 3 he led tens of thousands of horsemen and took Neiqiu in Xingzhou and Raoyang in Shenzhou.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of Han Ganyou 3 he led tens of thousands of horsemen and took Neiqiu county of Xingzhou and Raoyang county of Shenzhou.

entries.zh: 周廣順元年正月，太祖命左千牛衛將軍朱憲往修和好，永康王亦遣使報命，獻良馬四匹，太祖復遣尚書左丞田敏、供奉官蔣光遂銜命往聘。
entries.en: In the first month of Zhou Guangshun 1 the Zhou founder sent Left Thousand-Ox Guard general Zhu Xian to restore relations. Prince Yongkang replied with envoys and four fine horses. The founder then sent Secretariat Director Tian Min and palace attendant Jiang Guangsui on a formal mission.
entries.literal: In the first month of Zhou Guangshun 1 the Founder ordered Left Thousand-Ox Guard general Zhu Xian to go restore friendly relations; Prince Yongkang also sent envoys in reply, presenting four fine horses; the Founder again sent Left Secretariat Director Tian Min and palace attendant Jiang Guangsui bearing credentials on a mission.

entries.zh: 其年四月，田敏等回，永康王遣使獻碧玉金鍍銀裹鞍轡，並馬四十匹。
entries.en: When Tian Min returned that fourth month, Prince Yongkang sent envoys with jade saddlery plated in gold and silver and forty horses.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of that year Tian Min and the others returned; Prince Yongkang sent envoys presenting jade-and-gold, silver-plated saddle trappings, and forty horses besides.

entries.zh: 其月，太祖又命左金吾將軍姚漢英、左神武將軍華光裔往使。
entries.en: That same month the founder sent Left Golden Crow Guard general Yao Hanying and Left Divine Martial Guard general Hua Guangyi as envoys.
entries.literal: That month the Founder again ordered Left Golden Crow Guard general Yao Hanying and Left Divine Martial Guard general Hua Guangyi on a mission.

entries.zh: 其年九月，永康王為部下太寧王所弒，德光之子勒所部兵誅太寧王自立，稱應歷元年，號天順皇帝。
entries.en: In the ninth month Prince Yongkang was murdered by his subordinate Prince Taining. Deguang's son Le killed Taining, seized the throne, proclaimed the Yingli era, and styled himself Emperor Heaven-Compliant.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of that year Prince Yongkang was murdered by his subordinate Prince Taining; Deguang's son Le led his troops to execute Prince Taining and install himself, proclaiming Yingli 1 and styling himself Emperor Heaven-Compliant.

entries.zh: 顯德元年春，太原劉崇將圖南寇，契丹將楊兗率騎萬餘以助之。
entries.en: In the spring of Xiande 1 Liu Chong of Taiyuan prepared to invade the south, and the Khitan general Yang Yan led more than ten thousand horsemen to help him.
entries.literal: In the spring of Xiande 1 Liu Chong of Taiyuan was about to scheme a southern raid; the Khitan general Yang Yan led more than ten thousand horsemen to assist him.

entries.zh: 三月，世宗親征，與崇戰於潞州高平縣之南原，崇軍大敗，契丹眾棄甲而遁。
entries.en: In the third month Emperor Shizong marched in person and met Chong on the southern plain of Gaoping in Luzhou. Chong's army was routed and the Khitan threw down their armor and fled.
entries.literal: In the third month Emperor Shizong campaigned in person; he fought Chong on the southern plain of Gaoping county in Luzhou; Chong's army was greatly defeated, and the Khitan host cast off armor and fled.

entries.zh: 二年三月，命許州節度使王彥超等築壘於李晏口，與契丹數千騎戰於安平縣，敗之。）〉
entries.en: In the third month of the second year he ordered Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou. They fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.
entries.literal: In the third month of the second year he ordered Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao and others to build fortifications at Li Yankou; they fought several thousand Khitan horsemen at Anping County and defeated them.

entries.zh: 契丹者，古匈奴之種也。
entries.en: The Khitan were descended from the ancient Xiongnu.
entries.literal: The Khitan are the stock of the ancient Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 代居遼澤之中，潢水南岸，南距榆關一千一百里，榆關南距幽州七百里，本鮮卑之舊地也。
entries.en: For generations they lived in the Liao marshes on the south bank of the Huang River. Yuguan lay eleven hundred li to their south, and Youzhou another seven hundred li beyond the pass — lands that had once belonged to the Xianbei.
entries.literal: For generations they dwelt amid the Liao marshes, on the south bank of the Huang River; one thousand one hundred li south to Yuguan, and seven hundred li south from Yuguan to Youzhou — the old territory of the Xianbei.

entries.zh: 其風土人物，世代君長，前史載之詳矣。
entries.en: Earlier histories already describe their land and customs, their people, and the succession of their chieftains at length.
entries.literal: Their customs, land, and people, and their successive chieftains, earlier histories record in detail.

entries.zh: 至五代時，吐蕃已微弱，回鶻、党項諸羌夷分侵其地，而不有其人民。
entries.en: By the Five Dynasties Tubo had already waned. The Uyghurs, Tangut, and other Qiang and frontier peoples carved up and raided its territory yet did not truly hold its people.
entries.literal: By the Five Dynasties period Tubo had already grown weak; the Huihu, Tangut, and various Qiang and Yi peoples divided and encroached on its lands without holding its populace.

entries.zh: 值中國衰亂，不能撫有，惟甘、涼、瓜、沙四州常自通於中國。
entries.en: With the central realm in turmoil and unable to assert control, only Gan, Liang, Gua, and Sha—the four prefectures—continued to keep contact with China on their own.
entries.literal: As China fell into decline and disorder and could not govern them, only the four prefectures of Gan, Liang, Gua, and Sha regularly maintained their own contact with China.

entries.zh: 甘州爲回鶻牙帳，而涼、瓜、沙三州將吏猶稱唐官，數來請命。
entries.en: Gan Prefecture became the seat of the Uyghur royal camp, but the commanders and clerks of Liang, Gua, and Sha still called themselves Tang officials and came again and again to seek imperial appointment.
entries.literal: Ganzhou served as the Huihu royal encampment, while the officers of Liang, Gua, and Sha still styled themselves Tang officials and came repeatedly to request commissions.

entries.zh: 自梁太祖時，常以靈武節度使兼領河西節度，而觀察甘、肅、威等州，然雖有其名，而涼州自立守將。
entries.en: From the reign of the Liang founder onward, the military governor of Lingwu was routinely given concurrent command of Hexi and oversight of Gan, Su, Wei, and neighboring prefectures. In name the post existed, but Liangzhou kept its own defending commander.
entries.literal: From the time of Emperor Taizu of Liang, the military governor of Lingwu was usually also made military governor of Hexi and overseer of Gan, Su, Wei, and other prefectures; yet though the title existed, Liangzhou maintained its own defending commander.

entries.zh: 唐長興四年，涼州留後孫超遣大將拓拔承謙及僧道士耆老楊通信等至京師，明宗拜孫超節度使。
entries.en: In the fourth year of the Later Tang Changxing era, Sun Chao, acting governor of Liangzhou, sent his senior general Tuoba Chengqian together with monks, Daoists, and elders led by Yang Tongxin to the capital. Emperor Mingzong then invested Sun Chao as military governor.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Later Tang, Liangzhou acting governor Sun Chao sent the great general Tuoba Chengqian and the monk, Daoist, and elder Yang Tongxin and others to the capital; Emperor Mingzong appointed Sun Chao military governor.

entries.zh: 清泰元年，留後李文謙來請命。
entries.en: In the first year of Qingtai, acting governor Li Wenqian came to seek imperial appointment.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, acting governor Li Wenqian came to request a commission.

entries.zh: 後數年，涼州人逐出文謙，靈武馮暉遣牙將吳繼興代文謙爲留後，是時天福七年。
entries.en: A few years later the people of Liangzhou expelled Wenqian. Feng Hui of Lingwu dispatched his adjutant Wu Jixing to replace him as acting governor. This was in the seventh year of Tianfu.
entries.literal: Several years later the people of Liangzhou drove out Wenqian; Feng Hui of Lingwu sent his adjutant Wu Jixing to replace Wenqian as acting governor—this was in the seventh year of Tianfu.

entries.zh: 明年，晉高祖遣涇州押牙陳延暉齎詔書安撫涼州，涼州人共劫留延暉，立以爲刺史。
entries.en: The following year Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Chen Yanhui, adjutant of Jing Prefecture, with an edict to reassure Liangzhou. The people of Liangzhou seized him and made him their prefect.
entries.literal: The next year Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Chen Yanhui, adjutant of Jingzhou, bearing an edict to pacify Liangzhou; the people of Liangzhou together detained Yanhui by force and installed him as prefect.

entries.zh: 至漢隱帝時，涼州留後折逋嘉施來請命，漢即以爲節度使。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yindi of Later Han, Zhebo Jiashi, acting governor of Liangzhou, came to seek appointment, and the Han court at once made him military governor.
entries.literal: By the time of Emperor Yindi of Han, Liangzhou acting governor Zhebo Jiashi came to request a commission, and Han immediately appointed him military governor.

entries.zh: 嘉施，土豪也。
entries.en: Jiashi was a local magnate.
entries.literal: Jiashi was a local strongman.

entries.zh: 周廣順二年，嘉施遣人市馬京師。
entries.en: In the second year of Guangshun under the Zhou, Jiashi sent agents to purchase horses in the capital.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, Jiashi sent men to buy horses in the capital.

entries.zh: 是時樞密使王峻用事，峻故人申師厚者，少起盜賊，爲兗州牙將，與峻相友善。
entries.en: At that time Privy Councilor Wang Jun dominated the court. An old friend of his, Shen Shihou, had begun life as a bandit and later became adjutant of Yan Prefecture; he and Jun were close.
entries.literal: At that time Privy Councilor Wang Jun held power; Jun's old acquaintance Shen Shihou had risen from banditry in youth, became adjutant of Yanzhou, and was on friendly terms with Jun.

entries.zh: 後峻貴，師厚弊衣蓬首，日候峻出，馬前訴以饑寒，峻未有以發。
entries.en: After Jun rose to power, Shihou would appear in ragged clothes with hair in disarray, wait each day for Jun to leave his residence, and plead before his horse of hunger and cold. Jun had no means to help him.
entries.literal: Later, when Jun became eminent, Shihou in ragged clothes and unkempt hair daily waited for Jun to go out and pleaded before his horse of hunger and cold; Jun had no way to reward him.

entries.zh: 而嘉施等來請帥，峻即建言，涼州深入夷狄，中國未嘗命吏，請帥募府率供奉官能往者。
entries.en: When Jiashi and his party came to request a commander, Jun immediately proposed that Liangzhou lay far within barbarian territory and that the central court had never stationed officials there. He asked that a commander be recruited from among palace attendants willing to go.
entries.literal: When Jiashi and others came to request a commander, Jun at once proposed that Liangzhou lay deep among the barbarians and China had never appointed officials there, and asked that a commander be recruited from palace attendants able to go.

entries.zh: 月餘，無應募者，乃奏起師厚爲左衛將軍，已而拜河西節度使。
entries.en: After more than a month without a single volunteer, he memorialized to recall Shihou as general of the Left Guard, and soon afterward Shihou was appointed military governor of Hexi.
entries.literal: After more than a month with no volunteers, he memorialized to recall Shihou as Left Guard General, and shortly afterward Shihou was appointed military governor of Hexi.

entries.zh: 師厚至涼州，奏薦押牙副使崔虎心、陽妃谷首領沈念般等，及中國留人子孫王廷翰、溫崇樂、劉少英爲將吏，又自安國鎮至涼州立三州以控扼諸羌，用其酋豪爲刺史。
entries.en: On reaching Liangzhou, Shihou recommended adjutant deputy commissioner Cui Huxin, the Yangfei Valley chieftain Shen Nianban, and others, together with Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying—descendants of Chinese who had stayed behind—as officers. He also set up three prefectures from Anguo Town to Liangzhou to hold the Qiang in check, installing their chieftains as prefects.
entries.literal: When Shihou reached Liangzhou he memorialized recommending adjutant deputy commissioner Cui Huxin, Yangfei Valley chieftain Shen Nianban, and others, and the descendants of Chinese who had remained—Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying—as officers; he also established three prefectures from Anguo Town to Liangzhou to control the various Qiang, appointing their chieftains as prefects.

entries.zh: 然涼州夷夏雜處，師厚小人，不能撫有，至世宗時，師厚留其子而逃歸，涼州遂絕於中國。
entries.en: But Liangzhou was a mixed region of barbarians and Chinese, and Shihou, a man of small character, could not hold it. By Emperor Shizong's reign he abandoned his son and fled home, and Liangzhou was lost to the central realm thereafter.
entries.literal: Yet Liangzhou was a mixed land of barbarians and Chinese; Shihou was a petty man and could not govern it. By the time of Emperor Shizong, Shihou left his son behind and fled back, and Liangzhou was thereafter cut off from China.

entries.zh: 獨瓜、沙二州，終五代常來。
entries.en: Only Gua and Sha continued to send envoys throughout the Five Dynasties.
entries.literal: Only Gua and Sha, the two prefectures, came regularly throughout the Five Dynasties.

entries.zh: 晉天福三年十月，遣使都督李萬全等朝貢，以萬全爲歸義大將軍，監使雷福德爲順化將軍。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the third year of Tianfu of Jin they sent commissioner Li Wanquan and others to court with tribute; Wanquan was made Great General of Returning Allegiance and overseer Lei Fude Compliant Transformation General.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Tianfu of Jin they sent commissioner Li Wanquan and others to court with tribute; Wanquan was made Great General of Returning Allegiance and overseer Lei Fude Compliant Transformation General.

entries.zh: 四年三月，又遣都督拽里敦來朝，兼貢方物。
entries.en: In the third month of the fourth year they sent commissioner Zhailidun to court again, bearing local products as tribute.
entries.literal: In the third month of the fourth year they again sent commissioner Zhailidun to court, also presenting local products.

entries.zh: 其月，命衛尉卿邢德昭持節就冊爲奉化可汗。
entries.en: That same month Minister of the Guard Xing Dezhao was sent with credentials to invest him as Khan of Reverent Transformation.
entries.literal: That month Minister of the Guard Xing Dezhao was ordered to bear credentials on the spot and invest him as Khan of Reverent Transformation.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》：「晉高祖時，又加冊命，阿咄欲不知其爲狄銀親疏，亦不知其立卒，而仁裕訖五代常來朝貢，史亦失其紀。」
entries.en: The Ouyang History states: "Under Emperor Gaozu of Jin further investiture was granted. Whether Atouyu was near or distant kin to Diyin is unknown, as are the circumstances of his rise and death, whereas Renyu continued to send tribute throughout the Five Dynasties—yet the histories have lost the record of his reign as well."
entries.literal: The Ouyang History states: "Under Emperor Gaozu of Jin additional investiture was granted; whether Atouyu was close or distant kin to Diyin is unknown, as are his accession and death, while Renyu came to court with tribute throughout the Five Dynasties—the histories also lose his record."

entries.zh: 五年正月，遣都督石海金等來貢良馬百駟，並白玉團、白玉鞍轡等，謝其封冊。
entries.en: In the first month of the fifth year they sent commissioner Shi Haijin and others with one hundred teams of fine horses, white jade balls, white jade saddles and bridles, and the like, to thank the court for their investiture.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifth year they sent commissioner Shi Haijin and others to present one hundred teams of fine horses, together with white jade balls, white jade saddles and bridles, and the like, in thanks for their investiture.

entries.zh: 沙州，梁開平中，有節度使張奉，自號「金山白衣天子」。
entries.en: At Sha Prefecture, during the Liang Kaiping era, military governor Zhang Feng styled himself "the White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain."
entries.literal: In Sha Prefecture, during Kaiping of Liang, there was military governor Zhang Feng, who styled himself "White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain."

entries.zh: 至唐莊宗時，回鶻來朝，沙州留後曹義金亦遣使附回鶻以來，莊宗拜義金爲歸義軍節度使、瓜沙等州觀察處置等使。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, when the Uyghurs came to court, Cao Yijin, acting governor of Sha Prefecture, sent envoys along with the Uyghur mission. Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and commissioner overseeing Gua, Sha, and the other prefectures.
entries.literal: By the time of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, when the Huihu came to court, Sha Prefecture acting governor Cao Yijin also sent envoys attached to the Huihu mission; Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and commissioner for observation and disposition of Gua, Sha, and other prefectures.

entries.zh: 晉天福五年，義金卒，子元德立。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianfu under Jin, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded him.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded.

entries.zh: 至七年，沙州曹元忠、瓜州曹元深皆遣使來。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Cao Yuanzhong of Sha and Cao Yuanshen of Gua each dispatched envoys.
entries.literal: By the seventh year, Cao Yuanzhong of Sha and Cao Yuanshen of Gua both sent envoys.

entries.zh: 周世宗時，又以元忠爲歸義軍節度使，元恭爲瓜州團練使。
entries.en: Under Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Yuanzhong was again appointed military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and Yuangong regimental commissioner of Gua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Yuanzhong was again made military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and Yuangong regimental trainer of Gua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 其所貢碙砂、羚羊角、波斯錦、安西白絺、金星礬、大鵬砂、眊褐、玉團，皆因其來者以名見，而其卒立世次，史皆失其紀。
entries.en: They presented ammoniac, antelope horn, Persian brocade, Anxi white silk, golden-star alum, great peng sand, mao-brown cloth, and jade balls—each item recorded as it arrived—but the chronology of their deaths and successions has been lost to history.
entries.literal: Their tribute of ammoniac, antelope horn, Persian brocade, Anxi white silk, golden-star alum, great peng sand, mao-brown cloth, and jade balls—all were named as they came; but their deaths, successions, and generations are all lost in the records.

entries.zh: 周廣順元年二月，遣使並摩尼貢玉團七十有七，白絺、貂皮、犛牛尾、藥物等。
entries.en: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou, envoys came with the Manichaean mission bearing seventy-seven jade balls, white silk, sable pelts, yak tails, medicines, and other goods.
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou, envoys together with the Manichaean mission presented seventy-seven jade balls, white silk, sable pelts, yak tails, medicines, and the like.

entries.zh: 先是，晉、漢已來，回鶻每至京師，禁民以私市易，其所有寶貨皆鬻之入官，民間市易者罪之。
entries.en: Previously, from the Jin and Han dynasties onward, whenever Uyghur missions reached the capital the people were forbidden to trade with them privately. All their valuables had to be sold to the government, and anyone who traded privately was punished.
entries.literal: Previously, from Jin and Han onward, whenever the Uyghurs reached the capital private trade with the populace was forbidden; all their valuables had to be sold to the government, and private traders were punished.

entries.zh: 至是，周太祖命除去舊法，每回鶻來者，聽私下交易，官中不得禁詰，由是玉之價直十損七八。
entries.en: Thereupon Emperor Taizu of Zhou abolished the old rules. Whenever Uyghurs came, private trade was allowed and officials were forbidden to interfere. As a result the price of jade fell by seven or eight tenths.
entries.literal: At this point Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered the old regulations abolished: whenever Uyghurs came, private trade was permitted and officials might not prohibit or interrogate them; from this the price of jade fell by seven or eight tenths.

entries.zh: 顯德六年二月，又遣使朝貢，獻玉並碙砂等物，皆不納，所入馬量給價錢。
entries.en: In the second month of the sixth year of Xiande they sent envoys again with jade, ammoniac, and other goods. The court refused them all and paid only for the horses they accepted.
entries.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Xiande they again sent envoys to court, presenting jade, ammoniac, and other goods; all were refused, and for horses brought in payment was given by measure.

entries.zh: 時世宗以玉雖稱寶，無益國用，故因而卻之。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong held that although jade was prized as treasure it did not serve the needs of state, and on that account he refused it.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Shizong held that although jade was called a treasure, it did not benefit state needs, and therefore rejected it on that account.

entries.zh: 吐蕃 回鶻 高麗 渤海靺鞨 黑水靺鞨 新羅 党項 昆明部落 于闐 占城 牂牁蠻
entries.en: Tubo, the Uyghurs, Goryeo, the Bohai Mohe, the Heishui Mohe, Silla, the Tangut, the Kunming tribes, Yutian, Champa, and the Zangke Man.
entries.literal: Tubo, Huihu, Goryeo, Bohai Mohe, Heishui Mohe, Silla, Tangut, Kunming tribes, Yutian, Champa, Zangke Man.

entries.zh: 梁太祖乾化元年，正月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianhua under Liang Taizu, on the new moon of the first month (bingxu), the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the first day of the first month (bingxu), there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 時言事諸臣，多引漢高祖末年日蝕於歲首，太祖甚惡之，於是素服避正殿，百官各守本司。
entries.en: The remonstrating ministers of the day mostly invoked the solar eclipse at the year's opening in the closing years of Han Gaozu; Taizu took this as a very bad omen, put on undyed robes, withdrew from the main audience hall, and ordered every official to remain at his post.
entries.literal: At the time the remonstrating officials mostly cited the solar eclipse at the year's beginning in the final years of Emperor Gaozu of Han; Taizu greatly detested this, and therefore wore plain garments and avoided the main hall; the hundred officials each remained at their offices.

entries.zh: 是日，有司奏：「雲初陰晦，事同不蝕。」
entries.en: That day the responsible offices reported: "Clouds were dark from the outset, so in effect no eclipse was seen."
entries.literal: On that day the responsible offices reported: "At first the clouds were dark and overcast; the matter is the same as if there were no eclipse."

entries.zh: 百僚奉表稱賀。
entries.en: The entire bureaucracy submitted memorials of congratulation.
entries.literal: The hundred officials submitted memorials offering congratulations.

entries.zh: 乾化二年，五月壬戌，熒惑犯心大星，去心四度，順行。
entries.en: In the second year of Qianhua, on renxu of the fifth month Mars encroached on the chief star of the Heart asterism, four degrees from the Heart, in direct motion.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianhua, on renxu of the fifth month, Mars encroached upon the great star of the Heart mansion, four degrees from the Heart, moving in direct motion.

entries.zh: 占曰：「心為帝王之星。」
entries.en: The omen text reads: "The Heart is the star of the sovereign."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "The Heart is the star of the Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 其年六月五日，帝崩。
entries.en: That year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, the emperor died.
entries.literal: In that year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, the emperor died.

entries.zh: 梁太祖開平四年，十二月十四日夜，先是，司天奏：「是日月蝕，不宜用兵。」
entries.en: In the fourth year of Kaiping under Liang Taizu, on the night of the fourteenth of the twelfth month, the astronomical office had reported in advance: "A lunar eclipse is due; troops should not be deployed."
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the night of the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "On this day there will be a lunar eclipse; it is not appropriate to use the army."

entries.zh: 時王景仁方總大軍北伐，追之不及。
entries.en: Wang Jingren was already leading the main army north; the warning could not reach him in time.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Jingren was just then commanding the great army on a northern campaign; [the order] could not overtake him.

entries.zh: 至五年正月二日，果為後唐莊宗大敗於柏鄉。
entries.en: On the second day of the first month of the fifth year he was indeed routed by Later Tang Zhuangzong at Boxiang.
entries.literal: By the second day of the first month of the fifth year, he was indeed greatly defeated by Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang at Boxiang.

entries.zh: 唐明宗天成元年，十一月，月暈匝火、木。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiancheng under Tang Mingzong, in the eleventh month the moon showed a halo ringed around the stations of Fire and Wood.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, in the eleventh month, the moon had a halo encircling the Fire and Wood [planetary stations].

entries.zh: ◎彗孛梁太祖乾化二年，四月甲戌夜，彗見於靈臺之西。
entries.en: Comets and Broom Stars. In the second year of Qianhua under Liang Taizu, on the night of jiaxu in the fourth month, a comet appeared west of the Observatory Terrace.
entries.literal: ◎ Comets and Broom Stars. In the second year of Qianhua of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the night of jiaxu of the fourth month, a comet appeared west of the Observatory Terrace.

entries.zh: 周太祖顯德三年，正月壬戌夜，有星孛於參角，其芒指於東南。
entries.en: In the third year of Xiande under Zhou Taizu, on the night of renxu in the first month a broom star appeared at the corner of the Three Stars asterism, its rays toward the southeast.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on the night of renxu of the first month, there was a broom star at the corner of the Three Stars mansion; its rays pointed toward the southeast.

entries.zh: ◎五星淩犯梁太祖開平二年，正月乙亥，歲星犯月。
entries.en: Encroachments of the Five Planets. In the second year of Kaiping under Liang Taizu, on yihai of the first month Jupiter crossed the moon's path.
entries.literal: ◎ Encroachments of the Five Planets. In the second year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on yihai of the first month, the Year Star encroached upon the moon.

entries.zh: 晉高祖天福二年，七月丙寅，月蝕。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu under Jin Gaozu, on bingyin of the seventh month there was a lunar eclipse.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, on bingyin of the seventh month, the moon was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 五年，十一月丁丑，月蝕鶉首之分。
entries.en: In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month the moon was eclipsed within the Quail's Head celestial division.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, on dingchou of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed within the Quail's Head asterism division.

entries.zh: 少帝開運元年，三月戊子，月蝕。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaiyun under the Young Emperor, on wuzi of the third month there was a lunar eclipse.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun of the Young Emperor, on wuzi of the third month, the moon was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 九月丙戌，月蝕。
entries.en: On bingxu of the ninth month there was a lunar eclipse.
entries.literal: On bingxu of the ninth month, the moon was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 漢高祖天福十二年，十二月乙未，月食。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Tianfu under Han Gaozu, on yiwei of the twelfth month the moon was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Han, on yiwei of the twelfth month, there was a lunar eclipse.

entries.zh: 晉高祖天福二年，正月乙卯，先是，司天奏：「正月二日，太陽虧蝕，宜避正殿，開諸營門，蓋藏兵器，半月不宜用軍。」
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu under Jin Gaozu, on yimao of the first month, the astronomical office had reported in advance: "On the second day of the first month the sun will be eclipsed; the emperor should withdraw from the main hall, the camp gates should be opened, arms should be stored away, and troops should not be employed for half a month."
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, on yimao of the first month, beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "On the second day of the first month the sun will suffer eclipse; it is appropriate to avoid the main hall, open the gates of the various camps, cover and store weapons, and for half a month it is not appropriate to use the army."

entries.zh: 是日太陽虧，十分內食三分，在尾宿十七度。
entries.en: That day the sun was eclipsed: three parts in ten were covered, at the seventeenth degree of the Tail asterism.
entries.literal: On that day the sun was eclipsed; within ten parts, three parts were eaten, at the seventeenth degree of the Tail mansion.

entries.zh: 日出東方，以帶蝕三分，漸生，至卯時復滿。
entries.en: The sun rose in the east with a three-part belt eclipse, then waxed back until by the mao hour it was whole again.
entries.literal: The sun rose in the east with a belt-like eclipse of three parts; it gradually regenerated, and by the mao hour was full again.

entries.zh: 三年，正月戊申朔，司天先奏，其日日蝕。
entries.en: In the third year, on the new moon of the first month (wushen), the astronomical office had foretold an eclipse for that day.
entries.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the first month (wushen), the Directorate of Astronomy had reported in advance that on that day the sun would be eclipsed.

entries.zh: 至是日不蝕，內外稱賀。
entries.en: When the day arrived there was no eclipse, and court and capital alike offered congratulations.
entries.literal: When that day came there was no eclipse; inside and outside the court offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 四年，七月庚子朔，時中書門下奏：「謹按舊禮：日有變，天子素服避正殿，太史以所司救日於社，陳五兵、五鼓、五麾，東戟西矛，南弩北楯，中央置鼓，服從其位，百職廢務，素服守司，重列於庭，每等異位，向日而立，明復而止。
entries.en: In the fourth year, on the new moon of the seventh month (gengzi), the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "According to the ancient rites, when the sun shows an anomaly the emperor puts on undyed robes and leaves the main hall; the chief astrologer performs the sun-rescue rite at the soil altar, arraying five kinds of arms, five drums, and five banners—halberds east, spears west, crossbows south, shields north, with a drum in the center—each in prescribed dress; all offices suspend business, wear plain clothes and keep their posts, and line up in the courtyard by rank, each grade in its place, facing the sun until full daylight returns.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, on the first day of the seventh month (gengzi), at the time the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "We respectfully examine the old rites: when the sun undergoes change, the Son of Heaven wears plain garments and avoids the main hall; the Grand Astrologer, according to his office, performs the rite to rescue the sun at the altar of the soil, displaying the five weapons, five drums, and five banners—halberds to the east, spears to the west, crossbows to the south, shields to the north, with a drum placed in the center—garments according to position; the hundred offices suspend duties, wear plain garments and remain at their offices, arrayed in ranks in the court, each grade in a different position, standing facing the sun until brightness is restored, then stopping.

entries.zh: 今所司法物，鹹不能具，去歲正旦日食，唯謹藏兵仗，皇帝避正殿素食，百官守司。
entries.en: The ritual implements now in the keeping of the offices cannot all be supplied; at last year's New Year eclipse we could only store arms with care, have the emperor withdraw to plain fare in a side hall, and keep officials at their posts.
entries.literal: The ritual objects in the charge of the offices today cannot all be provided; at last year's New Year's Day solar eclipse, we only carefully stored away weapons, the emperor avoided the main hall and ate plain food, and the hundred officials remained at their offices.

entries.zh: 今且欲依近禮施行。」
entries.en: We propose to follow the simplified rites used in recent years."
entries.literal: For now we wish to carry out the recent rites."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was adopted.
entries.literal: [The memorial] was approved.

entries.zh: 七年，四月甲寅朔，是日百官守司，太陽不蝕，上表稱賀。
entries.en: In the seventh year, on the new moon of the fourth month (jiayin), officials kept their posts as ordered; the sun was not eclipsed, and congratulatory memorials were sent up.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, on the first day of the fourth month (jiayin), on that day the hundred officials remained at their offices; the sun was not eclipsed, and memorials of congratulation were submitted.

entries.zh: 八年，四月戊申朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the eighth year, on the new moon of the fourth month (wushen), the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, on the first day of the fourth month (wushen), there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 晉高祖天福六年，九月，有彗星長丈餘。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianfu under Jin Gaozu, in the ninth month a comet appeared more than ten feet long.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, in the ninth month, there was a comet more than a zhang in length.

entries.zh: 八年，十月庚戌夜，有彗見於東方，西指，尾長一丈，在角九度。
entries.en: In the eighth year, on the night of gengxu in the tenth month, a comet appeared in the east with its tail toward the west, ten feet long, at the ninth degree of the Horn asterism.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, on the night of gengxu of the tenth month, a comet was seen in the east, pointing west; its tail was one zhang in length, at the ninth degree of the Horn mansion.

entries.zh: 周太祖廣順二年，四月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou Taizu, on the new moon of the fourth month (bingxu), the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on the first day of the fourth month (bingxu), there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 月食
entries.en: Lunar Eclipses
entries.literal: Lunar Eclipses

entries.zh: 周世宗顯德三年，正月戊申，月蝕。
entries.en: In the third year of Xiande under Zhou Shizong, on wushen of the first month, there was a lunar eclipse.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, on wushen of the first month, the moon was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 五年，十一月辛未，月蝕。
entries.en: In the fifth year, on xinwei of the eleventh month, there was a lunar eclipse.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, on xinwei of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed.

entries.zh: ◎月暈
entries.en: Lunar Halos
entries.literal: ◎ Lunar Halos

entries.zh: 晉天福初，高祖將建義於太原，日傍多有五色雲，如蓮芰之狀。
entries.en: At the start of the Tianfu era, as Jin Gaozu prepared to raise his banner at Taiyuan, five-colored clouds like lotus pods gathered beside the sun.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin, when Gaozu was about to raise righteous arms at Taiyuan, beside the sun there were many five-colored clouds shaped like lotus seed-pods.

entries.zh: 二年，正月丙辰，一鼓初，北方有赤氣，向西至戌亥地，東北至醜地已來向北，闊三丈餘，狀如火光。
entries.en: In the second year, on bingchen of the first month, at the first watch red vapor appeared in the north, stretching west toward the xu-hai quarter and from the northeast through the chou quarter northward, more than thirty feet wide and like blazing fire.
entries.literal: In the second year, on bingchen of the first month, at the beginning of the first drum, in the north there was red vapor extending west to the xu and hai regions, and from the northeast to the chou region turning northward, more than three zhang in breadth, shaped like firelight.

entries.zh: 赤氣內見紫微宮共北斗諸星，其氣乍明乍暗。
entries.en: Within the red glow the Purple Forbidden Enclosure and the stars of the Northern Dipper could be seen, the vapor brightening and fading by turns.
entries.literal: Within the red vapor could be seen the Purple Forbidden Palace together with the stars of the Northern Dipper; the vapor was now bright, now dim.

entries.zh: 至三點後，後有白氣數條，相次西行，直至三鼓後散。
entries.en: After the third point of the watch several streaks of white vapor followed one another westward until they dispersed after the third watch.
entries.literal: After the third point, there were afterward several streaks of white vapor, one after another streaming west, until after the third drum they dispersed.

entries.zh: 天文志
entries.en: Astronomical Treatise
entries.literal: Treatise on Astronomy

entries.zh: 古先哲王，受命而帝天下者，必先觀象以垂法，治曆以明時，使萬物服其化風，四海同其正朔，然後能允釐下土，欽若上天。
entries.en: The sage-kings of antiquity who received the Mandate and ruled the world always began by reading the heavens to establish law, and by fixing the calendar to mark the seasons, so that all creation bowed to their civilizing influence and the four seas kept a single calendar—only then could they truly govern the earth below and stand in reverent harmony with Heaven.
entries.literal: Ancient sage-kings who received the Mandate and took Heaven as emperor over all under Heaven must first observe the signs to hand down models, regulate the calendar to clarify the seasons, make the myriad things submit to their transforming wind, and make the four seas share one new-year reckoning—only then could they truly bring order to the lands below and reverently accord with Heaven above.

entries.zh: 故虞舜之紹唐堯，先齊七政；
entries.en: Thus when Shun succeeded Yao, his first act was to align the seven luminaries;
entries.literal: Therefore when Yu Shun succeeded Tang Yao, he first aligned the Seven Regulators;

entries.zh: 武王之得箕子，首敘九疇。
entries.en: and when King Wu received Jizi, he began by expounding the Nine Categories.
entries.literal: when King Wu obtained Jizi, he first set forth the Nine Categories.

entries.zh: 皇極由是而允興，人時以之而不忒。
entries.en: The royal norm was thereby truly established, and the seasons of human affairs kept true to it without deviation.
entries.literal: The Supreme Norm was thereby truly established, and human seasons through it were without error.

entries.zh: 歷代已降，何莫由斯。
entries.en: Every dynasty since has followed this same path.
entries.literal: From successive generations downward, which did not proceed from this.

entries.zh: 及晉祖肇位，司天監馬重績始造新曆，奉表上之，云：「臣聞為國者，正一氣之元，宣萬邦之命，爰資曆以立章程。
entries.en: When the Jin founder ascended the throne, Ma Chongji of the Directorate of Astronomy devised a new calendar and presented a memorial, writing: "I have heard that to rule a state is to fix the origin of cosmic breath and proclaim the mandate of all peoples—and for this one must rely on the calendar to set the standards of government.
entries.literal: When the Jin founder first took the throne, the Director of the Astronomy Bureau Ma Chongji first devised a new calendar and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that to govern a state is to rectify the origin of the single qi and proclaim the mandate of the myriad states—one relies on the calendar to establish regulations.

entries.zh: 《長慶宣明》，雖氣朔不渝，即星躔罕驗；
entries.en: The Changqing Xuanming calendar kept its solar terms and new moons steady, yet its star positions seldom matched observation;
entries.literal: The Changqing Xuanming Calendar, though its qi and new moon did not change, yet its stellar positions were rarely verified;

entries.zh: 《景福崇元》，縱五曆甚正，而年差一日。
entries.en: while the Jingfu Chongyuan, though its five reckonings were largely sound, drifted a full day in the annual count.
entries.literal: the Jingfu Chongyuan Calendar, though its five reckonings were very correct, yet differed by one day in the year.

entries.zh: 今以《宣明》氣朔，《崇元》星緯，二曆相參，方得符合。
entries.en: Only by taking the solar terms and new moons from Xuanming and the star tracks from Chongyuan, and cross-checking the two, could a satisfactory fit be achieved.
entries.literal: Now, taking the qi and new moon of the Xuanming and the stellar tracks of the Chongyuan, the two calendars cross-referenced, only then could they accord.

entries.zh: 自古諸曆，皆以天正十一月為歲首，循太古甲子為上元，積歲彌多，差闊至甚。
entries.en: Since antiquity every calendar had taken the eleventh month as the year's beginning and traced its origin back to the primordial jiazi year—yet as centuries piled up, the error grew enormous.
entries.literal: From antiquity all calendars took the eleventh month of the celestial standard as the year's head, following the ancient jiazi as the superior origin; as accumulated years grew ever more, the discrepancy became very great.

entries.zh: 臣改法定元，創為新曆一部二十一卷，七章上下經二卷，算草八卷，立成十二卷，取唐天寶十四載乙未，立為近元，以雨水正月朔為歲首。
entries.en: I have revised the constants and fixed a new origin, composing a calendar in twenty-one scrolls—two of canonical text in upper and lower parts, eight of computational drafts, and twelve of ready tables—taking the yiwei year of Tianbao 14 as the near origin and making the new moon of the first month at Rain Water the start of the year.
entries.literal: Your subject has revised the law and fixed the origin, creating a new calendar in one set of twenty-one scrolls: two scrolls of the upper and lower classics of the seven chapters, eight scrolls of calculation drafts, and twelve scrolls of ready reckonings, taking the yiwei year of the fourteenth year of Tang Tianbao as the near origin and making the new moon of the first month at Rain Water the year's head.

entries.zh: 謹詣閣門上進。」
entries.en: I respectfully present it at the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat."
entries.literal: I respectfully proceed to the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat to present it."

entries.zh: 〈（《玉海》：《調元曆》，蓋仿曹士蒍小曆之舊。
entries.en: (Jade Sea: The Tiaoyuan Calendar largely followed the tradition of Cao Shuxun's small calendar.
entries.literal: (Jade Sea: The Tiaoyuan Calendar largely followed the old small calendar of Cao Shuxun.

entries.zh: 唐建中時，曹士蒍始變古法，以顯慶五年為上元，雨水為歲首。
entries.en: In Tang's Jianzhong era, Cao Shuxun first broke with ancient practice, taking Xianqing 5 as the superior origin and Rain Water as the year's beginning.
entries.literal: In the Jianzhong era of Tang, Cao Shuxun first altered the ancient method, taking the fifth year of Xianqing as the superior origin and Rain Water as the year's head.

entries.zh: 世謂之小曆。）〉
entries.en: Contemporaries called this the small calendar.)〉
entries.literal: The age called it the small calendar.)〉

entries.zh: 晉高祖命司天少監趙仁锜、張文皓，秋官正徐皓，天文參謀趙延乂、杜升、杜崇龜等，以新曆與《宣明》、《崇元》考核得失。
entries.en: Jin Gaozu ordered Vice Directors Zhao Renqi and Zhang Wenhao of the Astronomy Bureau, Xu Hao of the Autumn Office, and astronomical advisers Zhao Yanyi, Du Sheng, and Du Chonggui to compare the new calendar against Xuanming and Chongyuan and judge its merits.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Jin ordered the Vice Directors of the Astronomy Bureau Zhao Renqi and Zhang Wenhao, the Director of the Autumn Office Xu Hao, and the astronomical advisers Zhao Yanyi, Du Sheng, and Du Chonggui and others to test the new calendar against the Xuanming and Chongyuan calendars for gains and losses.

entries.zh: 俾有司奉而行之，因賜號《調元曆》，仍命翰林學士承旨和凝撰序。
entries.en: The responsible offices were ordered to adopt and implement it; it was given the name Tiaoyuan Calendar, and Academician Expositor He Ning was commissioned to write its preface.
entries.literal: He had the responsible offices receive and implement it, and accordingly bestowed the name Tiaoyuan Calendar, further ordering Academician Expositor He Ning to compose the preface.

entries.zh: 其後數載，法度浸差。
entries.en: Within a few years its constants began to slip.
entries.literal: Several years afterward, the standards gradually drifted.

entries.zh: 至周顯德二年，世宗以端明殿學士、左散騎常侍王樸明於曆算，乃命樸考而正之。
entries.en: In Zhou Xiande 2, Shizong, finding Wang Pu—Academician of the Duanming Hall and Left Regular Attendant—expert in calendrical science, commissioned him to review and revise the calendar.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xiande of Zhou, Shizong, because Wang Pu, Academician of the Duanming Hall and Left Regular Attendant, was skilled in calendrical calculation, ordered Pu to examine and correct it.

entries.zh: 樸奉詔歲餘，撰成《欽天曆》十五卷，上之。
entries.en: After more than a year at the task, Pu completed the Qintian Calendar in fifteen scrolls and presented it to the throne.
entries.literal: Pu received the edict for more than a year and completed the Qintian Calendar in fifteen scrolls, presenting it.

entries.zh: 表云：
entries.en: His memorial read:
entries.literal: The memorial said:

entries.zh: 世宗覽之，親為制序，仍付司天監行用，以來年正旦為始，自前諸曆並廢。
entries.en: Shizong reviewed it, composed the preface himself, and ordered the Astronomy Bureau to implement it from new year's dawn of the coming year, abolishing all previous calendars.
entries.literal: Shizong reviewed it and personally composed the preface, further handing it to the Directorate of Astronomy for implementation, taking the new year's dawn of the coming year as the beginning; all previous calendars were abolished.

entries.zh: 〈（《玉海》：《欽天》於朔分之下，立小分謂之杪。
entries.en: (Jade Sea: The Qintian Calendar, below the new-moon parts, establishes small parts called miao.
entries.literal: (Jade Sea: The Qintian Calendar, below the new-moon parts, establishes small parts called miao.

entries.zh: 說者謂前代謂曆朔余未有杪者。
entries.en: Commentators say that in former ages calendar new-moon remainders had no miao.
entries.literal: Expositors say that in former ages calendar new-moon remainders had no miao.

entries.zh: 若可用杪，何待求日法以齊朔分也。）〉
entries.en: If miao sufficed, why seek the day method to align new-moon parts?)〉
entries.literal: If miao could be used, why wait to seek the day method to align new-moon parts?)〉

entries.zh: 其曆經一卷，今聊紀於後，以備太史氏之周覽焉。
entries.en: Its one-scroll calendar classic is briefly recorded below for the Grand Astrologer's comprehensive review.
entries.literal: Its calendar classic of one scroll is now briefly recorded below, to supply the Grand Astrologer's comprehensive perusal.

entries.zh: 自唐而下，凡曆數朝，亂日失天，垂將百載，天之曆數，汩陳而已矣。
entries.en: From Tang onward, dynasty after dynasty let the calendar fall into chaos; for nearly a century Heaven's reckoning was nothing but confusion and decay.
entries.literal: From Tang downward, through several dynasties of calendars, days were disordered and Heaven was lost; for nearly a hundred years the celestial calendar was merely muddled and stale.

entries.zh: 今陛下順考古道，寅畏上天，咨詢庶官，振舉墜典。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty follows the ancient Way, stands in reverent awe of Heaven, consults his ministers, and revives fallen institutions.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty follows and examines the ancient Way, stands in reverent awe of Heaven above, consults the various officials, and revives fallen statutes.

entries.zh: 以臣薄遊曲藝，嘗涉舊史，遂降述作之命，俾究迎推之要，雖非能者，敢不奉詔。
entries.en: Finding in me only a modest acquaintance with these minor arts and some reading in the old histories, Your Majesty has charged me to compose a calendar and master the essentials of astronomical calculation—no master of the craft, yet how could I refuse the edict.
entries.literal: Because your subject has lightly wandered in minor arts and once traversed old histories, you thereupon bestowed the command to compose and investigate, ordering me to plumb the essentials of welcoming and pushing forward—though no adept, how dare I not receive the edict.

entries.zh: 乃包萬象以立法，齊七政以立元，測圭箭以候氣，審朓朒以定朔，明九道以步月，校遲疾以推星，考黃道之斜正，辨天勢之升降，而交蝕詳焉。
