entries.en: I have embraced the myriad phenomena to frame the law, aligned the seven luminaries to fix the origin, measured gnomon and clepsydra to track the seasons, refined waxing and waning to set the new moon, clarified the nine paths to pace the moon, calibrated planetary motion to reckon the stars, examined the obliquity of the ecliptic and the incline of the celestial sphere—and so made eclipses calculable in full detail.
entries.literal: Thereupon embracing the myriad images to establish law, aligning the Seven Regulators to fix the origin, measuring the gnomon and clepsydra to await the qi, examining waxing and waning to fix the new moon, clarifying the Nine Paths to pace the moon, checking slow and fast to push the stars, examining the oblique and straight of the Yellow Path, distinguishing the rising and falling of Heaven's disposition—and eclipses are thereby detailed.

entries.zh: 昔在唐堯，欽若昊天。
entries.en: Of old, Yao of Tang reverently conformed to august Heaven.
entries.literal: Of old, under Tang Yao, he reverently conformed to august Heaven.

entries.zh: 陛下親降聖謨，考曆象日月星辰。
entries.en: Your Majesty has personally bestowed sacred counsel, examining the calendar and the images of sun, moon, stars, and constellations.
entries.literal: Your Majesty personally bestowed sacred counsel, examining the calendar and the images of sun, moon, stars, and constellations.

entries.zh: 唐堯之道也，其曆謹以「顯德欽天」為名。
entries.en: This is the Way of Yao of Tang; the calendar is respectfully named "Xiande Qintian."
entries.literal: This is the Way of Tang Yao; the calendar respectfully takes "Xiande Qintian" as its name.

entries.zh: 天道元遠，非微臣之所盡知，但竭兩端，以奉明詔。
entries.en: The Heavenly Way is profoundly remote—beyond your humble servant's full knowledge; I can only give my utmost to serve the enlightened edict.
entries.literal: The Heavenly Way is profoundly remote—not what your humble servant can fully know; I can only exhaust both ends to serve the enlightened edict.

entries.zh: 疏略乖謬，甘俟罪戾。
entries.en: If it is coarse or mistaken, I willingly await punishment.
entries.literal: If coarse and mistaken, I willingly await punishment.

entries.zh: 乃以一篇步日，一篇步月，一篇步星，
entries.en: He then set one chapter to pace the sun, one to pace the moon, and one to pace the stars,
entries.literal: Thereupon taking one chapter to pace the sun, one chapter to pace the moon, and one chapter to pace the stars,

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下脫「一篇步發斂」五字。
entries.en: (Note: The five characters "one chapter pacing emergence and retraction" are missing below.
entries.literal: (Note: Below, the five characters "one chapter pacing emergence and retraction" are missing.

entries.zh: 下云「以卦候沒滅，為之下篇」者，言為步發斂之下篇。
entries.en: The phrase below, "taking hexagram periods and extinction as the lower chapter," refers to the lower chapter on pacing emergence and retraction.
entries.literal: Where below it says "taking hexagram periods and extinction as the lower chapter," this means the lower chapter for pacing emergence and retraction.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》約其文，稱「謹以步日、步月、步星、步發斂為四篇」，是也。）〉
entries.en: The Ouyang History condenses the text to read, "respectfully taking pacing the sun, moon, stars, and emergence and retraction as four chapters"—which is correct.)〉
entries.literal: The Ouyang History abridges the text, saying "respectfully taking pacing the sun, pacing the moon, pacing the stars, and pacing emergence and retraction as four chapters"—which is correct.)〉

entries.zh: 以卦候沒滅，為之下篇，都四篇，為曆經一卷，曆十一卷，草三卷，《顯德三年七政細行曆》一卷。
entries.en: With hexagram periods and extinction as the lower chapter, four chapters in all formed one scroll of the calendar classic, eleven of calendar, three of draft, and one scroll of the Detailed Motion of the Seven Regulators for Xiande 3.
entries.literal: Taking hexagram periods and extinction as the lower chapter—in all four chapters—forming one scroll of the calendar classic, eleven scrolls of calendar, three scrolls of draft, and one scroll of the Detailed Motion of the Seven Regulators for the third year of Xiande.

entries.zh: 演紀上元甲子，距今顯德三年丙辰，積七千二百六十九萬八千四百五十二。
entries.en: Projecting the era from supreme origin jiazi to the present Xiande 3 bingchen: accumulated 72,698,452.
entries.literal: Projecting the era: supreme origin jiazi, from the present third year of Xiande bingchen, accumulated 72,698,452.

entries.zh: 《欽天》統法：七千二百《欽天》經法：七十二
entries.en: 《Qintian》 comprehensive method: 7,200. 《Qintian》 canonical method: 72.
entries.literal: Qintian comprehensive method: 7,200. Qintian canonical method: 72.

entries.zh: 昔武王克商，以箕子歸，作《洪範》。
entries.en: In ancient times, after King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, he brought Jizi home and composed the 《Great Plan》.
entries.literal: In antiquity, when King Wu conquered Shang, he brought Jizi back and composed the 《Hong Fan》.

entries.zh: 其九疇之序，一曰五行，所以紀休咎之征，窮天人之際。
entries.en: Of the nine divisions in sequence, the first is the Five Elements, meant to record omens of blessing and calamity and to probe the relationship between Heaven and humanity.
entries.literal: Among the nine categories in order, the first is called the Five Elements, by which to record signs of fortune and misfortune and to exhaust the boundary between Heaven and man.

entries.zh: 故後之修史者，咸有其說焉。
entries.en: For this reason, later historians all set forth their own accounts of it.
entries.literal: Therefore later compilers of histories all have their explanations thereof.

entries.zh: 蓋欲使後代帝王見災變而自省，責躬修德，崇仁補過，則禍消而福至，此大略也。
entries.en: The aim was broadly to teach later rulers that when they witnessed disasters and portents they should reflect on themselves, take personal responsibility, cultivate virtue, cherish benevolence, and remedy their faults—then misfortune would fade and good fortune follow. Such is the general idea.
entries.literal: It is broadly intended to make later emperors, on seeing disasters and anomalies, examine themselves, blame their own persons and cultivate virtue, esteem benevolence and repair faults—then calamity is dispelled and blessing arrives; this is the general purport.

entries.zh: 今故按五代之簡編，記五行之災沴，追為此誌，以示將來。
entries.en: I have therefore drawn on the brief annals of the Five Dynasties to record disasters associated with the Five Elements, compiled this treatise for posterity, and set it forth for those who come after.
entries.literal: Now therefore, following the brief annals of the Five Dynasties, I record disasters and calamities of the Five Elements, compile this treatise retrospectively, and present it to posterity.

entries.zh: 其於京房之舊說，劉向之緒言，則前史敘之詳矣，此不復引以為證焉。
entries.en: As for the older theories of Jing Fang and the introductory remarks of Liu Xiang, earlier histories have already treated them at length, and they are not cited again here as evidence.
entries.literal: As for the old doctrines of Jing Fang and the prefatory remarks of Liu Xiang, earlier histories have narrated them in detail; here they are not cited again as proof.

entries.zh: 晉天福初，高祖將建義於太原，城中數處井泉暴溢。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Tianfu era of Later Jin, as the High Ancestor was preparing to raise his banner at Taiyuan, wells and springs in several parts of the city suddenly burst forth.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin, when the High Ancestor was about to raise righteous forces at Taiyuan, wells and springs in several places within the city suddenly overflowed.

entries.zh: 四年七月，西京大水，伊、洛、、澗皆溢，壞天津橋。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year the Western Capital was inundated. The Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian rivers all overflowed and destroyed the Tianjin Bridge.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, the Western Capital suffered great flooding; the Yi, Luo, —, and Jian all overflowed and destroyed the Tianjin Bridge.

entries.zh: 八月，河決博平，甘陵大水。
entries.en: In the eighth month the Yellow River broke through at Boping, and Ganling was severely flooded.
entries.literal: In the eighth month the Yellow River burst its banks at Boping; Ganling suffered great flooding.

entries.zh: 六年九月，河決於滑州，一概東流。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the sixth year the Yellow River broke through at Hua Prefecture and shifted entirely to an eastward course.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year the Yellow River burst its banks at Hua Prefecture and entirely flowed eastward.

entries.zh: 居民登丘冢，為水所隔。
entries.en: Residents took refuge on mounds and burial knolls, cut off by the floodwaters.
entries.literal: Residents climbed mounds and tombs and were cut off by the water.

entries.zh: 詔所在發舟楫以救之。
entries.en: An edict ordered local authorities to dispatch boats for rescue.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that wherever this occurred boats be dispatched to rescue them.

entries.zh: 兗州、濮州界皆為水所漂溺，命鴻臚少卿魏比、將作少監郭廷讓、右金吾衛將軍安濬、右驍衛將軍田峻於滑、濮、澶、鄆四州，檢河水所害稼，並撫問遭水百姓。
entries.en: The border regions of Yan and Pu prefectures were inundated. Wei Bi, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Guo Tingrang, Assistant Director of Imperial Construction; An Jun, General of the Right Golden Crow Guard; and Tian Jun, General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard, were dispatched to Hua, Pu, Chan, and Yun prefectures to inspect flood-damaged crops and to comfort the afflicted populace.
entries.literal: The borders of Yan and Pu prefectures were all swept and drowned by water; Honglu Vice Minister Wei Bi, Assistant Director of Imperial Construction Guo Tingrang, General of the Right Golden Crow Guard An Jun, and General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Tian Jun were ordered in the four prefectures of Hua, Pu, Chan, and Yun to inspect crops damaged by the river water and also to comfort and inquire after the common people who suffered flooding.

entries.zh: 兗州又奏，河水東流，闊七十里。
entries.en: Yan Prefecture further reported that the river had shifted eastward and was seventy li wide.
entries.literal: Yan Prefecture further reported that the river water flowed eastward, seventy li in breadth.

entries.zh: 至七年三月，命宋州節度使安彥威率丁夫塞之。
entries.en: By the third month of the seventh year Military Governor An Yanwei of Song Prefecture was ordered to lead laborers in blocking the breach.
entries.literal: By the third month of the seventh year, Military Governor of Song Prefecture An Yanwei was ordered to lead laborers to block it.

entries.zh: 河平，建碑立廟於河決之所。
entries.en: Once the river was brought under control, a stele and shrine were erected at the site of the breach.
entries.literal: When the river was pacified, a stele was erected and a shrine established at the place of the breach.

entries.zh: 周顯德五年四月，吳越王錢俶奏，十日夜，杭州火，焚燒府署殆盡。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Xiande of Later Zhou, King Qian Chu of Wuyue reported that on the night of the tenth, fire at Hangzhou had burned the government offices nearly to the ground.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, King Qian Chu of Wuyue reported that on the night of the tenth day, Hangzhou had fire that burned the government offices nearly to completion.

entries.zh: 世宗命中使賫詔撫問。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong dispatched a palace envoy bearing an edict of consolation and inquiry.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered a palace envoy to carry an edict in consolation and inquiry.

entries.zh: 梁開平三年春正月，潞州軍前李思安奏，壺關縣庶穰鄉村人因伐樹倒，自分為兩片，內有六字，皆如左書，曰「天十四載石進」，乃圖其狀以進。
entries.en: In the first month of spring of the third year of Kaiping of Later Liang, Li Si'an at the Lu Prefecture front memorialized that villagers of Shurang Township in Huguan County, while felling a tree, saw it fall and split in two; inside were six characters in clerical script reading "Heaven, the fourteenth year, Shi Jin." He painted its form and submitted the report.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year of Kaiping of Liang, Li Si'an at the front of the Lu Prefecture army memorialized: villagers of Shurang Township in Huguan County, while felling a tree, saw it fall and split of itself into two pieces; within were six characters, all written like clerical script, reading "Heaven, the fourteenth year, Shi Jin." He painted its form and submitted it.

entries.zh: 梁祖異之，命示百官，莫有詳其義者，及晉高祖即位，人以為雖有圖姓，計其甲子則二十有九年矣。
entries.en: The Liang Founder regarded it as strange and ordered it shown to the hundred officials, but none could explain its meaning. When the Later Jin High Ancestor took the throne, people reckoned that although the diagram bore a surname, counting by the sexagenary cycle it had been twenty-nine years.
entries.literal: The Liang Founder regarded it as strange and ordered it shown to the hundred officials; none could explain its meaning. When the Jin High Ancestor took the throne, people thought that although there was a surname in the diagram, counting by the sexagenary cycle it was twenty-nine years.

entries.zh: 識者曰：「『天』字取『四』字中兩畫加之於傍，則『丙』字也；
entries.en: Those versed in omens said: "Take the character for 'heaven' and add to its side the two strokes from the middle of the character for 'four,' and one gets the character for 'bing';
entries.literal: Those with insight said: "Taking the character 'tian' and adding to its side the two strokes from the middle of the character 'si,' one gets the character 'bing';

entries.zh: 『四』字去中間兩畫加『十』字，則『申』字也。
entries.en: remove the middle two strokes from the character for 'four,' add the character for 'ten,' and one gets the character for 'shen.'
entries.literal: removing the middle two strokes from the character 'si' and adding the character 'shi,' one gets the character 'shen.'

entries.zh: 晉祖即位之年，乃丙申也。」
entries.en: The year in which the Jin Ancestor took the throne was indeed bingshen."
entries.literal: The year in which the Jin Ancestor took the throne was indeed bingshen."

entries.zh: 唐天祐五年，長柳巷田家有僵桃樹，經年舊坎猶在，其仆木一朝屹然而起，行數十步，復於舊坎，其家駭異，倉皇散走。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianyou of Later Tang, a farmer's home in Changliu Lane had a dead peach tree whose old root hollow still remained. One morning the fallen trunk suddenly stood upright, moved several dozen paces, and settled back into the old hollow. The household fled in terror.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianyou of Tang, at a farmer's home in Changliu Lane there was a stiff peach tree; the old pit from years past still remained; its fallen trunk one morning stood upright abruptly, walked several tens of paces, and returned to the old pit; the household was terrified and astonished and fled in haste.

entries.zh: 議者以漢昭帝時，上林仆木起生枝，時蟲蠹成文而宣帝興。
entries.en: Commentators cited the reign of Emperor Zhao of Han, when a fallen tree in Shanglin Park rose and put forth branches while insects bored characters into its wood, presaging the rise of Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: Discussants cited that in the time of Emperor Zhaodi of Han, a fallen tree in Shanglin Park rose and sprouted branches; at the time insects bored patterns into it and Emperor Xuandi rose.

entries.zh: 今木理成文，仆而重起，乃莊宗中興之兆也。
entries.en: Now the grain of the wood had formed characters, and a fallen tree had risen again—an omen of Emperor Zhuangzong's restoration of the Tang.
entries.literal: Now the wood grain formed characters, fallen yet rising again—this was an omen of Emperor Zhuangzong's restoration.

entries.zh: 五行志
entries.en: Treatise on the Five Elements
entries.literal: Treatise on the Five Elements

entries.zh: 臣讀十四代史書，見二千年故事，觀諸家宗廟，都無始祖之稱，唯商、周二代，以稷、契為太祖。
entries.en: I have read the histories of fourteen dynasties and reviewed two thousand years of precedent; in every dynasty's ancestral temples there is no title of founding ancestor—only in the Shang and Zhou were Ji and Qi taken as Taizu.
entries.literal: I have read the histories of fourteen dynasties and reviewed two thousand years of precedent; in every dynasty's ancestral temples there is no title of founding ancestor—only in the Shang and Zhou were Ji and Qi taken as Taizu.

entries.zh: 《禮記》曰：「天子七廟，三昭、三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
entries.en: The Record of Rites states: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Taizu temple—seven in all."
entries.literal: The 《Record of Rites》 says: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Taizu temple—seven in all."

entries.zh: 鄭玄註：「此周制也。
entries.en: Zheng Xuan's annotation: "This is the Zhou system.
entries.literal: Zheng Xuan's annotation: "This is the Zhou system.

entries.zh: 七者，太祖後稷及文王、武王與四親廟。」
entries.en: The seven are the Taizu Hou Ji, Kings Wen and Wu, and the four collateral-line temples."
entries.literal: The seven are the Taizu Hou Ji, Kings Wen and Wu, and the four collateral-line temples."

entries.zh: 又曰：「商人六廟，契及成湯與二昭、二穆也。
entries.en: It further states: "The Shang had six temples: Qi and Cheng Tang, together with two zhao and two mu chambers.
entries.literal: It further says: "The Shang had six temples: Qi and Cheng Tang, together with two zhao and two mu chambers.

entries.zh: 夏後氏立五廟，不立太祖，惟禹與二昭、二穆而已。」
entries.en: The Xia Hou clan established five temples and did not establish a Taizu—only Yu together with two zhao and two mu chambers."
entries.literal: The Xia Hou clan established five temples and did not establish a Taizu—only Yu together with two zhao and two mu chambers."

entries.zh: 據《王制》鄭玄所釋，即商、周以稷、契為太祖，夏後無太祖，亦無追謚之廟。
entries.en: According to Zheng Xuan's explanation of the Royal Regulations, the Shang and Zhou took Ji and Qi as Taizu; the Xia Hou had no Taizu and also no posthumously enshrined temple.
entries.literal: According to Zheng Xuan's explanation of the 《Royal Regulations》, the Shang and Zhou took Ji and Qi as Taizu; the Xia Hou had no Taizu and also no posthumously enshrined temple.

entries.zh: 自商、周以來，時更十代，皆於親廟之中，以有功者為太祖，無追崇始祖之例。
entries.en: Since the Shang and Zhou, ten dynasties have passed; all, within the collateral temples, took the meritorious figure as Taizu—there is no precedent for posthumously honoring a founding ancestor.
entries.literal: Since the Shang and Zhou, ten dynasties have passed; all, within the collateral temples, took the meritorious figure as Taizu—there is no precedent for posthumously honoring a founding ancestor.

entries.zh: 具引今古，即恐詞繁，事要證明，須陳梗概。
entries.en: To cite ancient and modern cases in full would make the language prolix; since the matter requires proof, I must set forth the outline.
entries.literal: To cite ancient and modern cases in full would make the language prolix; since the matter requires proof, I must set forth the outline.

entries.zh: 漢以高祖父太上皇執嘉無社稷功，不立廟號，高帝自為高祖。
entries.en: The Han, because the great-grandfather the Supreme Emperor Zhijia had no merit for the state, did not establish a temple title; the High Emperor himself served as Gaozu.
entries.literal: The Han, because the great-grandfather the Supreme Emperor Zhijia had no merit for the altars of soil and grain, did not establish a temple title; the High Emperor himself served as Gaozu.

entries.zh: 魏以曹公相漢，垂三十年，始封於魏，故為太祖。
entries.en: The Wei, because Duke Cao served as chancellor of Han for nearly thirty years and was first enfeoffed in Wei, made him Taizu.
entries.literal: The Wei, because Duke Cao served as chancellor of Han for nearly thirty years and was first enfeoffed in Wei, made him Taizu.

entries.zh: 晉以宣王輔魏有功，立為高祖，以景帝始封晉，故為太祖。
entries.en: The Jin, because the Xuan King assisted Wei with merit, established him as Gaozu; because the Jing Emperor was first enfeoffed in Jin, he was made Taizu.
entries.literal: The Jin, because the Xuan King assisted Wei with merit, established him as Gaozu; because the Jing Emperor was first enfeoffed in Jin, he was made Taizu.

entries.zh: 宋氏先世，官閥卑微，雖追崇帝號，劉裕自為高祖。
entries.en: The Song clan's earlier generations were of humble official standing; although imperial titles were posthumously conferred, Liu Yu himself served as Gaozu.
entries.literal: The Song clan's earlier generations were of humble official standing; although imperial titles were posthumously conferred, Liu Yu himself served as Gaozu.

entries.zh: 南齊高帝之父，位至右將軍，生無封爵，不得為太祖，高帝自為太祖。
entries.en: The Southern Qi Gaodi's father rose to Right General; in life he received no enfeoffment and could not be Taizu—the Gaodi himself served as Taizu.
entries.literal: The Southern Qi Gaodi's father rose to Right General; in life he received no enfeoffment and could not be Taizu—the Gaodi himself served as Taizu.

entries.zh: 梁武帝父順之，佐佑齊室，封侯，位至領軍、丹陽尹，雖不受封於梁，亦為太祖。
entries.en: Liang Wudi's father Shunzhi assisted the Qi court, was enfeoffed as marquis, and rose to Area Commander and Danyang Intendant; although he received no enfeoffment from Liang, he was made Taizu.
entries.literal: Liang Wudi's father Shunzhi assisted the Qi court, was enfeoffed as marquis, and rose to Area Commander and Danyang Intendant; although he received no enfeoffment from Liang, he was made Taizu.

entries.zh: 陳武帝父文贊，生無名位，以武帝功，梁室贈侍中，封義興公，及武帝即位，亦追為太祖。
entries.en: Chen Wudi's father Wenzan had no rank in life; because of the Wudi's merit, the Liang court posthumously granted him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yixing; when the Wudi ascended the throne, he was also posthumously made Taizu.
entries.literal: Chen Wudi's father Wenzan had no rank in life; because of the Wudi's merit, the Liang court posthumously granted him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yixing; when the Wudi ascended the throne, he was also posthumously made Taizu.

entries.zh: 周閔帝以父泰相西魏，經營王業，始封於周，故為太祖。
entries.en: Northern Zhou Emperor Min, because his father Tai served as chancellor of Western Wei, built the royal enterprise, and was first enfeoffed in Zhou, made him Taizu.
entries.literal: Northern Zhou Emperor Min, because his father Tai served as chancellor of Western Wei and built the royal enterprise and was first enfeoffed in Zhou, made him Taizu.

entries.zh: 隋文帝父忠，輔周室有大功，始封於隋，故為太祖。
entries.en: Sui Wendi's father Zhong assisted the Zhou court with great merit and was first enfeoffed in Sui; therefore he was made Taizu.
entries.literal: Sui Wendi's father Zhong assisted the Zhou court with great merit and was first enfeoffed in Sui; therefore he was made Taizu.

entries.zh: 唐高祖神堯祖父虎為周八柱國，隋代追封唐公，故為太祖。
entries.en: Tang Gaozu Shenyao's grandfather Hu was one of the Zhou Eight Pillars; the Sui dynasty posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Tang; therefore he was made Taizu.
entries.literal: Tang Gaozu Shenyao's grandfather Hu was one of the Zhou Eight Pillars; the Sui dynasty posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Tang; therefore he was made Taizu.

entries.zh: 唐末梁室朱氏有帝位，亦立四廟，朱公先世無名位，雖追冊四廟，不立太祖，朱公自為太祖。
entries.en: At the end of Tang the Liang Zhu clan held the imperial throne and also established four temples; the Zhu lord's earlier generations had no rank; although four temples were posthumously enrolled, no Taizu was established—the Zhu lord himself served as Taizu.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang the Liang Zhu clan held the imperial throne and also established four temples; the Zhu lord's earlier generations had no rank; although four temples were posthumously enrolled, no Taizu was established—the Zhu lord himself served as Taizu.

entries.zh: 此則前代追冊太祖，不出親廟之成例也。
entries.en: This shows that in former ages posthumous enrollment as Taizu did not depart from the established precedent of the collateral temples.
entries.literal: This shows that in former ages posthumous enrollment as Taizu did not depart from the established precedent of the collateral temples.

entries.zh: 三年九月，將有事於南郊，議於東京別建太廟。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the third year, with a southern-suburb sacrifice impending, officials deliberated building a separate imperial ancestral temple at the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, when the southern suburb ceremony was to be performed, it was deliberated to separately build an imperial ancestral temple at the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 時太常禮院言：「準洛京廟室一十五間，分為四室，東西各有夾室，四神門，每方屋一間，各三門，戟二十四，別有齋宮神廚屋宇。
entries.en: The Court of Imperial Rites reported: "According to the Luoyang model, the temple comprises fifteen bays divided into four main chambers, with side chambers on east and west, four spirit gates, one bay per cardinal direction with three gates each, twenty-four halberds, and separate buildings for the fasting palace and spirit kitchen.
entries.literal: At the time the Court of Imperial Rites said: "According to the Luoyang capital, the temple chambers number fifteen bays, divided into four chambers; east and west each have side chambers; four spirit gates; each direction has one bay with three gates each; twenty-four halberds; separately there are fasting-palace and spirit-kitchen buildings.

entries.zh: 準禮，左宗廟，右社稷，在國城內，請下所司修奉。」
entries.en: By rite the ancestral temple stands to the left and the altars of soil and grain to the right, within the capital walls; we request that the responsible offices be ordered to restore and maintain them."
entries.literal: According to rites, the ancestral temple is to the left and the altars of soil and grain to the right, within the capital walls; we request dispatch to the relevant offices to restore and maintain them."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 其月，太常禮院奏：「迎太廟社稷神主到京，其日未審皇帝親出郊外迎奉否。
entries.en: That same month, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "When the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain are brought to the capital, it remains undecided whether the emperor should personally go out beyond the city to receive them.
entries.literal: That month, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "When welcoming the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain to the capital, it is not yet determined whether on that day the emperor will personally go out beyond the suburbs to receive them.

entries.zh: 檢討故事，元無禮例，伏請召三省官集議。」
entries.en: A search of precedents turns up no established ritual; we humbly request that officials of the Three Departments be convened to deliberate."
entries.literal: Examining precedents, originally there is no ritual example; we humbly request summoning the Three Departments' officials to assemble and deliberate."

entries.zh: 敕：「宜令尚書省四品以上、中書門下五品已上同參議。」
entries.en: An edict ordered: "Officials of the fourth rank and above in the Secretariat, together with officials of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery, shall jointly deliberate."
entries.literal: An edict: "It is fitting to order officials of the fourth rank and above in the Secretariat and of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery to participate jointly in deliberation."

entries.zh: 司徒竇貞固、司空蘇禹珪等議：「按吳主孫休即位，迎祖父神主於吳郡，人祔太廟，前一日出城野次，明日常服奉迎，此其例也。」
entries.en: Minister over the Masses Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works Su Yugui, and others argued: "When Sun Xiu of Wu took the throne, he welcomed his grandfather's spirit tablet from Wu Commandery for enshrinement in the ancestral temple; the day before he went out of the city and encamped in the open country, and the next day received the tablet in ordinary dress. That is the precedent."
entries.literal: Minister over the Masses Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works Su Yugui, and others deliberated: "According to the precedent when Lord Sun Xiu of Wu acceded, he welcomed his grandfather's spirit tablet from Wu Commandery and had it enshrined in the imperial ancestral temple; the day before he went out of the city to encamp in the open country, and the next day in ordinary dress received and escorted it—this is the example."

entries.zh: 遂署狀言車駕出城奉迎為是，請下禮儀使草定儀註。
entries.en: They then signed a memorial recommending that the emperor go out of the city to receive the tablets, and requested that the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol draft the ceremonial regulations.
entries.literal: Thereupon they signed a memorial stating that the imperial carriage going out of the city to receive and escort was correct, and requested dispatch to the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol to draft the ritual regulations.

entries.zh: 至十月，禮儀使奏：「太祖神主將至，前一日儀仗出城掌次，於西禦莊東北設神主行廟幄幕，面南。
entries.en: In the tenth month, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized: "When Taizu's spirit tablet is about to arrive, on the preceding day the guard of honor will go out of the city to prepare the encampment, and a traveling-temple canopy for the spirit tablet shall be erected northeast of the Western Imperial Estate, facing south.
entries.literal: By the tenth month, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized: "When Taizu's spirit tablet is about to arrive, on the day before the guard of honor goes out of the city to manage the encampment, a traveling-temple canopy for the spirit tablet is set up northeast of the Western Imperial Estate, facing south.

entries.zh: 其日放朝，群臣早出西門，皇帝常服出城詣行宮，群臣起居畢，就次。
entries.en: On that day court is suspended; the officials assemble early at the Western Gate; the emperor goes out of the city in ordinary dress to the traveling palace; after the officials have paid their respects, they take their stations.
entries.literal: On that day court is dismissed; the hundred officials go out early through the Western Gate; the emperor in ordinary dress goes out of the city to the traveling palace; when the hundred officials have finished paying respects, they take their places.

entries.zh: 神主將至，群臣班定，皇帝立於班前。
entries.en: As the spirit tablet approaches, the officials form their ranks and the emperor stands before them.
entries.literal: When the spirit tablet is about to arrive, the hundred officials' ranks are set; the emperor stands before the ranks.

entries.zh: 神主至，太常卿請皇帝再拜，群臣俱拜。
entries.en: When the spirit tablet arrives, the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites asks the emperor to bow twice, and all the officials bow with him.
entries.literal: When the spirit tablet arrives, the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites requests the emperor to bow twice; the hundred officials all bow.

entries.zh: 神主就行廟幄幕座，設常饌，群臣班於神幄前。
entries.en: The spirit tablet is conducted to its seat in the traveling-temple canopy; ordinary offerings are laid out, and the officials form ranks before the spirit canopy.
entries.literal: The spirit tablet proceeds to the seat within the traveling-temple canopy; ordinary offerings are set out; the hundred officials rank before the spirit canopy.

entries.zh: 侍中就次，請皇帝謁神主。
entries.en: The Palace Attendant takes his station and asks the emperor to approach the spirit tablet.
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant takes his place and requests the emperor to visit the spirit tablet.

entries.zh: 既至，群臣再拜，皇帝進酒畢再拜，群臣俱拜。
entries.en: When he arrives, the officials bow twice; after the emperor presents wine and bows again, all the officials bow with him.
entries.literal: When he has arrived, the hundred officials bow twice; when the emperor has finished presenting wine he bows twice again; the hundred officials all bow.

entries.zh: 皇帝還幄，群臣先赴太廟門外立班，俟皇帝至起居。
entries.en: The emperor returns to the canopy; the officials go ahead to form ranks outside the ancestral temple gate and wait for the emperor to arrive and pay his respects.
entries.literal: The emperor returns to the canopy; the hundred officials first go to stand in ranks outside the gate of the imperial ancestral temple, awaiting the emperor's arrival to pay respects.

entries.zh: 俟神主至，群臣班於廟門外，皇帝立於班前，太常卿請皇帝再拜，群臣俱拜。
entries.en: When the spirit tablet arrives, the officials form ranks outside the temple gate; the emperor stands before them; the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites asks the emperor to bow twice, and all the officials bow with him.
entries.literal: Awaiting the spirit tablet's arrival, the hundred officials rank outside the temple gate; the emperor stands before the ranks; the Director of the Court of Imperial Rites requests the emperor to bow twice; the hundred officials all bow.

entries.zh: 皇帝還幄，群臣就次，宮闈令安神主於本室訖，群臣班於廟庭。
entries.en: The emperor returns to the canopy and the officials take their stations; the Director of the Inner Palace installs the spirit tablet in its proper chamber; when this is done, the officials form ranks in the temple courtyard.
entries.literal: The emperor returns to the canopy; the hundred officials take their places; the Director of the Inner Palace installs the spirit tablet in its proper chamber; when finished, the hundred officials rank in the temple courtyard.

entries.zh: 太常卿請皇帝於四室奠饗，逐室皇帝再拜，群臣俱拜。
entries.en: The Director of the Court of Imperial Rites asks the emperor to offer sacrifice in each of the four chambers; at every chamber the emperor bows twice and all the officials bow with him.
entries.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Rites requests the emperor to set out offerings and feast in the four chambers; at each chamber the emperor bows twice and the hundred officials all bow.

entries.zh: 四室祔饗畢，皇帝還宮。
entries.en: When the enshrinement offerings in all four chambers are complete, the emperor returns to the palace.
entries.literal: When the enshrinement feasting in the four chambers is finished, the emperor returns to the palace.

entries.zh: 前件儀註，望付中書門下宣下。」
entries.en: We request that these ritual regulations be issued through the Secretariat and Chancellery."
entries.literal: The foregoing ritual regulations are requested to be transmitted by the Secretariat and Chancellery for promulgation."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 禮志上
entries.en: Rites Treatise, Part One
entries.literal: Treatises on Rites, Part One

entries.zh: 〈（案：《禮志序》，原本闕佚。）〉
entries.en: (Editor's note: The preface to the Treatise on Rites is no longer extant in the original.)
entries.literal: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Rites is missing from the original text.)

entries.zh: 後唐長興元年九月，太常禮院奏：「來年四月孟夏，禘饗於太廟。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the first year of Changxing of Later Tang, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "In the fourth month of next year—the first month of summer—a di offering is to be performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Changxing of Later Tang, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: "In the fourth month of next year, the first month of summer, the di sacrifice will be offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 謹按禮經，三年一祫以孟冬，五年一禘以孟夏。
entries.en: The ritual classics prescribe a collective ancestral sacrifice every three years in mid-winter, and a di sacrifice every five years in mid-summer.
entries.literal: According to the ritual classics, there is one he/xia sacrifice every three years in the first month of winter, and one di sacrifice every five years in the first month of summer.

entries.zh: 已毀未毀之主，並合食於太祖之廟，逐廟功臣，配饗於太廟之庭。
entries.en: Tablets of ancestors whose shrines had been closed down and those still active were all to share a meal in the Grand Ancestor's hall, while meritorious officials from each shrine received secondary offerings in the temple courtyard.
entries.literal: Spirit tablets of ancestors whose temples have been destroyed and those not yet destroyed are all to dine together in the temple of the Grand Ancestor; meritorious ministers of each temple are to receive paired offerings in the court of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 本朝寶應元年定禮，奉景皇帝為始封之祖。
entries.en: In Baoying 1 of our dynasty the rites were codified, with Emperor Jing honored as the founding ancestor of the original enfeoffment.
entries.literal: In the first year of Baoying of this dynasty ritual was fixed, and Emperor Jing was honored as the founding ancestor of the first enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 既廟號太祖，百代不遷，每遇禘祫，位居東向之尊，自代祖元皇帝、高祖、太宗已下，列聖子孫，各序昭穆南北相向，合食於前。
entries.en: With the temple name Grand Ancestor, his place would never be moved; at every di or collective sacrifice he held the seat of honor facing east. From the Yuan Emperor of Dai through the High Ancestor and Great Ancestor and below, successive imperial descendants were arranged in zhao-mu order north and south, sharing the feast before him.
entries.literal: Since his temple title was Grand Ancestor, for a hundred generations he would not be moved; whenever di and he/xia sacrifices occurred he held the seat of honor facing east; from the Yuan Emperor, dynastic ancestor of Dai, down through the High Ancestor and Great Ancestor, successive sage descendants were each arranged in zhao and mu order facing north and south, and dined together before him.

entries.zh: 聖朝中興，重修宗廟，今太廟見饗高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗、獻祖、太祖、莊宗七廟，太祖景皇帝在祧廟之數，不列廟饗。
entries.en: After the dynasty's revival the ancestral shrines were rebuilt; the Imperial Temple now served seven halls—the High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Yizong, Zhaozong, Xianzu, Taizu, and Zhuangzong—while Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing was relegated to the distant-lineage shrine and no longer received regular temple offerings.
entries.literal: When the sacred court restored the dynasty and rebuilt the ancestral temples, the Imperial Ancestral Temple now offers sacrifices to seven temples: the High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Yizong, Zhaozong, Xianzu, Taizu, and Zhuangzong. The Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing is counted among the distant ancestral temples and is not listed for temple sacrifice.

entries.zh: 將來禘禮，若奉高祖居東向之尊，則禘饗不及於太祖、代祖；
entries.en: If the upcoming di rite placed the High Ancestor in the seat of honor facing east, the di offering would not include the Grand Ancestor or the Dai ancestor;
entries.literal: For the upcoming di ritual, if the High Ancestor were placed in the seat of honor facing east, the di offering would not reach the Grand Ancestor and the Dai ancestor;

entries.zh: 若以祧廟太祖居東向之位，則又違於禮意。
entries.en: yet placing Grand Ancestor from the distant shrine in the east-facing seat would likewise violate ritual propriety.
entries.literal: If the Grand Ancestor in the distant temple were placed in the east-facing position, this would again violate ritual intent.

entries.zh: 今所司修奉祧廟神主，及諸色法物已備，合預請參詳，事須具狀申奏。」
entries.en: The responsible offices had already prepared the distant-shrine tablets and all ritual implements; advance deliberation was needed, and a full memorial should be submitted."
entries.literal: The responsible offices have now prepared the spirit tablets of the distant temple and various ritual implements; it is appropriate to request advance deliberation, and the matter must be reported in a full memorial."

entries.zh: 敕下尚書省集百官詳議。
entries.en: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to gather all officials for full deliberation.
entries.literal: An imperial edict was issued to the Department of State Affairs to assemble all officials for detailed deliberation.

entries.zh: 戶部尚書韓彥惲等奏議曰：「伏以本朝尊受命之祖景皇帝為始封之君，百代不遷，長居廟食，自貞觀至於天祐，無所改更，聖祖神孫，左昭右穆。
entries.en: Minister of Revenue Han Yanhun and others submitted their opinion: "Our dynasty honors Emperor Jing, the ancestor who received the Mandate, as the founding lord of the first enfeoffment—his place unmoved for a hundred generations, with perpetual temple offerings. From Zhenguan through Tianyou nothing was altered; sage forebears and divine descendants were arranged with zhao on the left and mu on the right.
entries.literal: Minister of Revenue Han Yanhun and others memorialized in deliberation: "Your subjects observe that this dynasty honors Emperor Jing, the ancestor who received the Mandate, as the founding enfeoffment lord; for a hundred generations unmoved, he has long held temple sacrifice. From Zhenguan to Tianyou nothing was changed; sage ancestors and divine descendants were arranged left in zhao and right in mu.

entries.zh: 自中興國祚，再議宗祊，以太祖景皇帝在祧廟之數，不列祖宗，欲尊太祖之位，將行東向之儀，爰命群臣，同議可否。
entries.en: Since the dynasty's revival the ancestral shrines had been reconsidered; because Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing was counted among the distant lineage and excluded from the main ancestral roster, the court wished to honor his position with the east-facing rite and ordered the ministers to debate whether this was proper.
entries.literal: Since the revival of the dynastic fortune, the ancestral shrines were again deliberated; because Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing is counted among the distant temples and is not listed among the ancestors, wishing to honor the Grand Ancestor's position, the east-facing rite was to be performed, and all ministers were ordered to deliberate together on whether this was permissible.

entries.zh: 伏詳本朝列聖之舊典，明皇定禮之新規，開元十年，特立九廟，子孫遵守，歷代無虧。
entries.en: We have examined the old statutes of our dynasty's successive emperors and the new ritual regulations established under Emperor Ming; in Kaiyuan 10 nine temples were specially established, and descendants have observed this through the generations without lapse.
entries.literal: Your subjects have examined in detail the old statutes of the successive sage emperors of this dynasty and the new regulations for fixing ritual under Emperor Ming; in the tenth year of Kaiyuan nine temples were specially established, observed by descendants through the generations without impairment.

entries.zh: 今既行定禮之規，又以祧太祖之室。
entries.en: The court now follows the fixed ritual regulations while also drawing on the distant-lineage hall of the Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Now that the regulations for fixed ritual are being followed, yet the hall of the Grand Ancestor in the distant lineage is also being used.

entries.zh: 昔德宗朝，將行禘祫之禮，顏真卿議請奉獻祖居東向之位，景皇帝暫居昭穆之列，考之於貞元，則以為誤，行之於今日，正得其禮。
entries.en: In Dezong's reign, when di and collective sacrifices were planned, Yan Zhenqing proposed placing Xianzu in the east-facing seat and Emperor Jing temporarily in the zhao-mu ranks; judged by Zhenyuan standards that had been an error, but applied today it would be exactly proper ritual.
entries.literal: In the reign of Dezong, when the di and he/xia rituals were to be performed, Yan Zhenqing proposed that Xianzu be placed in the east-facing position and Emperor Jing temporarily placed in the zhao-mu ranks; examining this in the Zhenyuan era it was deemed an error, but carrying it out today would be exactly in accord with ritual.

entries.zh: 今欲請每遇禘祫之歲，暫奉景皇帝居東向之尊，自元皇帝以下，敘列昭穆。」
entries.en: We therefore propose that in every year of di or collective sacrifice, Emperor Jing temporarily hold the seat of honor facing east, with the Yuan Emperor and below arranged in zhao-mu order."
entries.literal: We now wish to request that in every year of di and he/xia sacrifice, Emperor Jing temporarily hold the seat of honor facing east, and from the Yuan Emperor down be arranged in zhao-mu order."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: The proposal was approved.

entries.zh: 八月戊申，明宗服兗冕，禦文明殿，追冊昭宣光烈孝皇帝。
entries.en: On the day wushen of the eighth month, Mingzong wore the yan cap and robe, took the throne at the Hall of Civilization, and posthumously enregistered the August, Illustrious, Bright, and Majestic Filial Emperor.
entries.literal: On the day wushen of the eighth month, Mingzong wore the yan cap and robe, took the throne at the Hall of Civilization, and posthumously enregistered the August, Illustrious, Bright, and Majestic Filial Emperor.

entries.zh: 禮畢，冊使兵部尚書盧質押冊出應天門登車，鹵簿鼓吹前導，入都亭驛，翌日，登車赴曹州。
entries.en: When the rite concluded, enregistration envoy Minister of War Lu Zhi escorted the tablet out through the Gate of Responding to Heaven and mounted his carriage; armed escort and music led the way to the Capital Pavilion Post Station, and the next day he proceeded to Cao Prefecture.
entries.literal: When the rite was concluded, the enregistration envoy, Minister of War Lu Zhi, escorted the tablet out through the Gate of Responding to Heaven and mounted the carriage; armed escort and music led the way; he entered the Capital Pavilion Post Station, and the next day mounted the carriage and proceeded to Cao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 時議者以追尊則可，立之為宗，不入太廟，深為失禮。
entries.en: Contemporary commentators held that posthumous elevation was permissible, but establishing him as 'zong' without entering the Imperial Ancestral Temple was a serious lapse in ritual.
entries.literal: Contemporaries who deliberated held that posthumous elevation was permissible, but establishing him as 'zong' without entering the Imperial Ancestral Temple was deeply a lapse in ritual.

entries.zh: 夫言宗者，功業纂於祖禰，德澤被於生民，發號申令可也。
entries.en: To speak of 'zong' means that achievements are gathered upon ancestors and fathers, and virtue and bounty extend over the living people—issuing commands and proclaiming orders is fitting.
entries.literal: To speak of 'zong' means that achievements are gathered upon ancestors and fathers, and virtue and bounty extend over the living people—issuing commands and proclaiming orders is fitting.

entries.zh: 且輝王纂嗣之日，國命出於賊臣，君父銜冤，母後塗炭，遭罹放逐，鼎祚覆亡，追謚易名，當循故實。
entries.en: Moreover, when King Hui succeeded to the throne, the nation's mandate issued from treacherous ministers; father and lord bore wrong, the empress dowager suffered ruin, he met exile, and the dynasty fell—posthumous titles should follow established precedent.
entries.literal: Moreover, on the day when King Hui succeeded to the throne, the nation's mandate issued from treacherous ministers; father and lord bore wrong, the empress dowager suffered ruin, he met with exile, and the imperial vessel was overturned—posthumous titles and changed names should follow established precedent.

entries.zh: 如漢之沖、質，晉之閔、懷，但尊稱而無廟號；
entries.en: Such as Han's Chong and Zhi, Jin's Min and Huai—only honored titles without temple names;
entries.literal: Such as Han's Chong and Zhi, Jin's Min and Huai—only honored titles without temple names;

entries.zh: 前代亡國者周赧、漢獻、魏陳留，亦不稱宗；
entries.en: former dynasties' fallen rulers—Zhou's Nan, Han's Xian, Wei's Chenliu—were also not called 'zong';
entries.literal: former dynasties' fallen states—Zhou's Nan, Han's Xian, Wei's Chenliu—were also not called 'zong';

entries.zh: 中興之追謚者孺子嬰，光武竟無追宗之典。
entries.en: among those posthumously titled at dynastic revival, the Infant Lord Ying—Emperor Guangwu ultimately had no precedent of posthumous 'zong.'
entries.literal: among those posthumously titled at dynastic revival, the Infant Lord Ying—Emperor Guangwu ultimately had no precedent of posthumous 'zong.'

entries.zh: 設如自我作古，酌於人情，則謂之為「景宣光烈」，深不稱也。
entries.en: Suppose one were to create new precedent and weigh human sentiment—then to call him 'Jing Xuan Guang Lie' would be deeply unfitting.
entries.literal: Suppose one were to create new precedent and weigh human sentiment—then to call him 'Jing Xuan Guang Lie' would be deeply unfitting.

entries.zh: 古之周景、漢景、周宣、漢宣，皆中興再造之主。
entries.en: In antiquity Zhou's Jing, Han's Jing, Zhou's Xuan, and Han's Xuan were all rulers of revival who restored their dynasties.
entries.literal: In antiquity Zhou's Jing, Han's Jing, Zhou's Xuan, and Han's Xuan were all lords of revival who restored the dynasty.

entries.zh: 至如國朝，太祖曰景皇帝，以受命而有唐室，宣宗皇帝以隔代承運，皇綱復振故也。
entries.en: In our dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuanzong because he received the fortune across generations and restored the imperial norm.
entries.literal: As for our dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuanzong because he received the fortune across generations and the imperial norm was restored.

entries.zh: 今輝王亡國墜業，謂之「宣景」，得無謬乎！
entries.en: Now King Hui lost the state and let the enterprise fall—calling him 'Xuan Jing'—is this not absurd!
entries.literal: Now King Hui lost the state and let the enterprise fall—calling him 'Xuan Jing'—is this not absurd!

entries.zh: 先是，太常既奏，下尚書省集議，雖有智者，依違不言。
entries.en: Earlier, after the Court of Imperial Rites had memorialized and the matter was sent to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation, although there were wise men, they wavered and did not speak.
entries.literal: Earlier, after the Court of Imperial Rites had memorialized and the matter was sent to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation, although there were wise men, they wavered and did not speak.

entries.zh: 至是，既立為景宗，陵號溫陵，乃於曹州置廟，以時告享，仍以本州刺史以下為三獻官。
entries.en: By then he had been established as Jingzong, with tomb designation Wenling; a temple was set up in Cao Prefecture for timely offerings, with the prefect and officials below serving as the three-offering officials.
entries.literal: By this time, having been established as Jingzong, with tomb designation Wenling, a temple was set up in Cao Prefecture for timely announcement and offering; the prefect of that prefecture and below were made the three-offering officials.

entries.zh: 後宰臣知其非，奏去廟號。
entries.en: Later the chief ministers knew this was wrong and memorialized to remove the temple name.
entries.literal: Later the chief ministers knew this was wrong and memorialized to remove the temple name.

entries.zh: 晉天福四年十一月，太常禮院奏：議立唐朝帝廟，引武德年故事，祀隋三帝。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Tianfu 4 of Jin, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized on establishing temples to Tang emperors, citing the Wude-era precedent of sacrificing to the three Sui emperors.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, the Court of Imperial Rites memorialized: deliberating on establishing temples to Tang emperors, citing the precedent of the Wude era when the three Sui emperors were sacrificed to.

entries.zh: 今請立近朝莊宗、明宗、閔帝三廟，庶合前規。
entries.en: We now request establishing three temples to the recent Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min, thus following former regulations.
entries.literal: It is now requested to establish three temples to the recent Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min, thus approximating former regulations.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「德莫盛於繼絕，禮莫重於奉先。
entries.en: An edict stated: "No virtue is greater than continuing a severed line; no ritual is weightier than honoring ancestors.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "No virtue is greater than continuing a severed line; no ritual is weightier than honoring ancestors.

entries.zh: 莊宗立興復之功，明宗垂光大之業，逮乎閔帝，實繼本枝，然則丕緒洪源，皆尊唐室。
entries.en: Zhuangzong established the achievement of revival; Mingzong handed down the enterprise of glorious expansion; reaching Emperor Min, he truly continued the main branch—the great line and vast source all honor the Tang house.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong established the achievement of revival; Mingzong handed down the enterprise of glorious expansion; reaching Emperor Min, he truly continued the main branch—thus the great line and vast source all honor the Tang house.

entries.zh: 繼周者須崇後稷，嗣漢者必奉高皇，將啟嚴祠，當崇茂典。
entries.en: He who continues Zhou must honor Hou Ji; he who succeeds Han must serve the High Emperor—about to open solemn sacrifice, the abundant canon should be honored.
entries.literal: He who continues Zhou must honor Hou Ji; he who succeeds Han must serve the High Emperor—about to open solemn sacrifice, the abundant canon should be honored.

entries.zh: 宜立唐高祖、太宗及莊宗、明宗、閔帝五廟。」
entries.en: Five temples should be established to Tang's High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min."
entries.literal: Five temples should be established to Tang's High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, and Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min."

entries.zh: 其月，太常禮院又奏：「唐廟制度，請以至德宮正殿隔為五室，三分之，南去地四尺，以石為坷，中容二主。
entries.en: That month, the Court of Imperial Rites again memorialized: "For the Tang temple regulations, the main hall of the Zhide Palace should be partitioned into five chambers in thirds; four chi south from the ground, stone platforms—each holding two spirit tablets in the center.
entries.literal: That month, the Court of Imperial Rites again memorialized: "For the regulations of the Tang temples, the main hall of the Zhide Palace should be partitioned into five chambers, divided in thirds; four chi south from the ground, stone platforms—each holding two spirit tablets in the center.

entries.zh: 廟之南一屋三門，門戟二十有四；
entries.en: The southern chamber of the temple has three doors with twenty-four halberds;
entries.literal: The southern chamber of the temple has three doors, with twenty-four halberds at the doors;

entries.zh: 東西一屋一門，門無棨戟。
entries.en: the eastern and western chambers each have one door without ceremonial halberds.
entries.literal: the eastern and western chambers each have one door, without ceremonial halberds at the doors.

entries.zh: 四仲之祭，一羊一豕，如其中祠，幣帛牲牢之類，光祿主之。
entries.en: For sacrifices in the four mid-season months, one sheep and one pig as for medium sacrifices; silks, victims, and the like are managed by the Court of Imperial Commissary.
entries.literal: For sacrifices in the four mid-season months, one sheep and one pig, as for medium sacrifices; silks, victims, and the like are managed by the Court of Imperial Commissary.

entries.zh: 祠祝之文，不進不署，神廚之具，鴻臚督之。
entries.en: Prayer texts for the sacrifice are not advanced or signed; spirit kitchen implements are supervised by the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
entries.literal: Prayer texts for the sacrifice are not advanced and not signed; implements of the spirit kitchen are supervised by the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 五帝五後，凡十主，未遷者六，未立者四，未謚者三。
entries.en: Five emperors and five empresses—ten spirit tablets in all: six not yet moved, four not yet established, three not yet given posthumous titles.
entries.literal: Five emperors and five empresses—ten spirit tablets in all: six not yet moved, four not yet established, three not yet given posthumous titles.

entries.zh: 高祖、太宗與其後暨莊宗、明宗，凡六主在清化裏之寢宮，祭前二日，以殿中傘扇二十，迎置新廟以享祀。
entries.en: The High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, and their empresses together with Zhuangzong and Mingzong—six tablets in the sleeping palace at Qinghua Lane; two days before the sacrifice, twenty palace umbrellas and fans welcome and install them in the new temple for the offering.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, and their empresses together with Zhuangzong and Mingzong—six tablets in all in the sleeping palace at Qinghua Lane; two days before the sacrifice, twenty palace umbrellas and fans are used to welcome and install them in the new temple for the offering.

entries.zh: 閔皇帝、莊宗明宗二後及魯國孔夫人神主四座，請修制祔廟，及三後請定謚法。」
entries.en: Emperor Min, the two empresses of Zhuangzong and Mingzong, and Lady Kong of Lu—four spirit tablets—we request drafting regulations for enshrinement in the temple, and fixing posthumous title procedures for the three empresses."
entries.literal: Emperor Min, the two empresses of Zhuangzong and Mingzong, and Lady Kong of Lu—four spirit tablets—it is requested to draft regulations for enshrinement in the temple, and for the three empresses posthumous title procedures should be fixed."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approval was granted.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 周廣順元年二月，太常禮院上言：「準敕，遷漢廟入升平宮。
entries.en: In the second month of Guangshun 1 of Later Zhou, the Court of Imperial Rites submitted: "By imperial decree, the Han ancestral temples should be moved into Shengping Palace.
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun of Zhou, the Court of Imperial Rites submitted: "By imperial decree, the Han ancestral temples should be moved into Shengping Palace.

entries.zh: 其唐、晉兩朝，皆止五廟遷移，今漢七廟，未審總移，為復只移五廟？
entries.en: For both the Tang and Jin dynasties, only five temples were moved; Han now has seven temples—it is unclear whether all should be moved, or only five temples?
entries.literal: For both the Tang and Jin dynasties, only five temples were moved; Han now has seven temples—it is unclear whether all should be moved, or only five temples?

entries.zh: 敕宜準前敕，並移於升平宮。
entries.en: The decree should follow the previous decree, and all should be moved to Shengping Palace.
entries.literal: The decree should follow the previous decree, and all should be moved to Shengping Palace.

entries.zh: 其法物、神廚、齋院、祭服、祭器、饌料，皆依中祠例，用少牢，光祿等寺給；
entries.en: Ritual implements, spirit kitchens, purification lodges, sacrificial robes, sacrificial vessels, and food supplies should all follow medium-sacrifice precedent, using the shao lao offering, supplied by the Court of Imperial Commissary and related offices;
entries.literal: Ritual implements, spirit kitchens, purification lodges, sacrificial robes, sacrificial vessels, and food supplies should all follow medium-sacrifice precedent, using the shao lao offering, supplied by the Court of Imperial Commissary and related offices;

entries.zh: 其讀文太祝及奉禮郎，太常寺差。
entries.en: The Grand Invoker who reads the text and the Ceremonial Attendant should be assigned by the Court of Imperial Rites.
entries.literal: The Grand Invoker who reads the text and the Ceremonial Attendant should be assigned by the Court of Imperial Rites.

entries.zh: 每仲饗，以漢宗子為三獻。」
entries.en: For each mid-season offering, a Han imperial clansman should serve as thrice-presenter."
entries.literal: For each mid-season offering, a Han imperial clansman should serve as thrice-presenter."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approval was granted.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 周廣順三年九月，南郊，禮儀使奏：「郊祀所用珪璧制度，準禮，祀上帝以蒼璧；
entries.en: In the ninth month of Guangshun 3 of Later Zhou, at the southern suburban altar, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "The regulations for gui and bi disks used in suburban sacrifice—according to ritual, the Supreme Lord is worshipped with a green bi disk;
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, at the southern suburb, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "The regulations for gui and bi disks used in suburban sacrifice—according to ritual, the Supreme Lord is sacrificed to with a green disk;

entries.zh: 祀地祇以黃琮；
entries.en: the earthly spirits with a yellow cong;
entries.literal: the earthly spirits are sacrificed to with a yellow cong;

entries.zh: 祀五帝以珪璋琥璜琮，其玉各依本方正色，祀日月以珪璋，祀神州以兩珪有邸。
entries.en: the Five Emperors with gui, zhang, hu, huang, and cong, each jade in the proper color of its direction; the sun and moon with gui and zhang; the sacred land with two gui bearing pedestals.
entries.literal: the Five Emperors are sacrificed to with gui, zhang, hu, huang, and cong; each jade follows the proper color of its direction; the sun and moon are sacrificed to with gui and zhang; the sacred land is sacrificed to with two gui with pedestals.

entries.zh: 其用幣，天以蒼色，地以黃色，配帝以白色，日月五帝各從本方之色，皆長一丈八尺。
entries.en: Silks used: azure for Heaven, yellow for Earth, white for the paired emperor; sun, moon, and Five Emperors each in the color of their direction—all one zhang and eight chi long.
entries.literal: Silks used: for Heaven azure color, for Earth yellow, for the paired emperor white; sun, moon, and Five Emperors each follow the color of their direction—all one zhang and eight chi in length.

entries.zh: 其珪璧之狀，譬圓而琮八方，珪上銳而下方，半珪曰璋，琥為虎形，半璧曰璜，其珪璧琮璜皆長一尺二寸四。
entries.en: The forms: the bi is round, the cong eight-sided; the gui pointed above and square below; half a gui is a zhang; hu is tiger-shaped; half a bi is a huang; gui, bi, cong, and huang are each one chi, two cun, and four fen long.
entries.literal: The forms of gui and bi: the bi is round and the cong eight-sided; the gui is pointed above and square below; half a gui is called zhang; hu is in the shape of a tiger; half a bi is called huang; gui, bi, cong, and huang are all one chi, two cun, and four fen in length.

entries.zh: 珪有邸，邸，本也，珪著於璧而整肅也。
entries.en: Gui may bear a pedestal; di means foundation—the gui is set upon the bi to complete the solemn arrangement.
entries.literal: Gui may have a pedestal; di means foundation—the gui is set upon the bi and made whole and solemn.

entries.zh: 日月星辰以珪璧五寸，前件珪璧雖有圖樣，而長短之說或殊。
entries.en: For sun, moon, and stars, gui and bi of five cun; although the aforesaid gui and bi have illustrated patterns, accounts of their dimensions differ.
entries.literal: For sun, moon, and stars, gui and bi of five cun; although the aforesaid gui and bi have illustrated patterns, accounts of their length differ.

entries.zh: 按唐開元中，玄宗詔曰：「祀神以玉，取其精潔，比來用瑉，不可行也。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan of Tang, Emperor Xuanzong decreed: "Spirits are worshipped with jade for its purity and refinement; the recent use of min stone cannot be permitted.
entries.literal: According to Kaiyuan of Tang, Emperor Xuanzong decreed: "To sacrifice to the spirits with jade is to take its purity and refinement; recently min stone has been used—this cannot be permitted.

entries.zh: 如或以玉難辦，寧小其制度，以取其真。」
entries.en: If jade is hard to obtain, it is better to reduce the prescribed dimensions than sacrifice authenticity."
entries.literal: If jade is difficult to obtain, it is better to reduce the scale of the regulations so as to preserve authenticity."

entries.zh: 今郊廟所修珪璧，量玉大小，不必皆從古制，伏請下所司修制。」
entries.en: The gui and bi now prepared for suburban and temple sacrifice should be sized according to available jade and need not all follow ancient regulations; we respectfully request that the responsible offices be ordered to manufacture them."
entries.literal: The gui and bi now prepared for suburban and temple sacrifice should be sized according to available jade and need not all follow ancient regulations; your subjects respectfully request that the responsible offices be ordered to manufacture them."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approval was granted.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 四年五月，中書門下奏：「先據太常寺定少帝謚昭宣光烈孝皇帝，號景宗者。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the fourth year, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "Previously the Court of Imperial Rites fixed the Lesser Emperor's posthumous title as the August, Illustrious, Bright, and Majestic Filial Emperor, with the designation Jingzong.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "Previously, according to the Court of Imperial Rites, the Lesser Emperor's posthumous title was fixed as the August, Illustrious, Bright, and Majestic Filial Emperor, with the designation Jingzong.

entries.zh: 伏以景宗生曾為帝，饗乃承祧，既號景宗，合入宗廟，如不入宗廟，難以言宗。
entries.en: We observe that Jingzong in life was once emperor; offerings continue the ancestral line—having been called Jingzong, he should enter the ancestral temple; if he does not, the title 'zong' is hard to justify.
entries.literal: Your subjects observe that Jingzong in life was once emperor; offerings continue the ancestral line—having been called Jingzong, he should enter the ancestral temple; if he does not enter the ancestral temple, it is difficult to speak of 'zong.'

entries.zh: 於理而論，祧一遠廟，安少帝神主於太廟，即昭穆序而宗祀正。
entries.en: In principle, removing one distant temple and installing the Lesser Emperor's tablet in the Imperial Ancestral Temple would set zhao-mu order aright and make ancestral worship correct.
entries.literal: In terms of principle, removing one distant temple and installing the Lesser Emperor's spirit tablet in the Imperial Ancestral Temple would set zhao-mu order aright and make ancestral worship correct.

entries.zh: 今或且居別廟，即請不言景宗，但雲昭宣光烈孝皇帝。
entries.en: If for now he dwells in a separate temple, we request not using the name Jingzong but only the August, Illustrious, Bright, and Majestic Filial Emperor.
entries.literal: If for now he dwells in a separate temple, it is requested not to speak of Jingzong but only of the August, Illustrious, Bright, and Majestic Filial Emperor.

entries.zh: 兼冊文內有『基』字，是玄宗廟諱，雖尋常詔敕皆不回避，少帝是繼世之孫，不欲斥列聖之諱，今改『基』為『宗』字。」
entries.en: Moreover, the writ contains the character 'ji,' the temple taboo of Emperor Xuanzong; although ordinary edicts do not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a descendant in succession and we do not wish to pronounce the taboos of successive sages—'ji' is now changed to 'zong.'"
entries.literal: Moreover, within the writ text is the character 'ji,' which is the temple taboo of Emperor Xuanzong; although ordinary edicts do not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a descendant in succession and we do not wish to pronounce the taboos of successive sages—now 'ji' is changed to the character 'zong."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approval was granted.
entries.literal: Approval was granted.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：《風俗通》陳孔璋云：尊卑有敘，喪祭哀敬，各有攸終，欲令言著而可遵，事施而不犯。
entries.en: (The Wudai huiyao: Chen Kongzhang in the Comprehensive Account of Popular Customs says: High and low have order; mourning and sacrifice have grief and reverence, each with its proper end, wishing that words be set forth so they may be followed and affairs carried out without violation.
entries.literal: (The Wudai huiyao: Chen Kongzhang in the Comprehensive Account of Popular Customs says: High and low have order; mourning and sacrifice have grief and reverence, each with its proper end, wishing that words be set forth so they may be followed and affairs carried out without violation.

entries.zh: 《禮》云：「卒哭之後，宰執木鐸徇於宮，曰舍故而諱新。」
entries.en: The Rites say: "After the end of wailing, the steward takes a wooden clapper and announces through the palace, saying 'Abandon the old taboo and observe the new.'"
entries.literal: The Rites say: "After the end of wailing, the steward takes a wooden clapper and announces through the palace, saying 'Abandon the old taboo and observe the new.'"

entries.zh: 故，謂毀廟之主也，恩遠屬絕，名不可諱。
entries.en: 'Old' means the lord of a destroyed temple; when favor is distant and kinship severed, the name need not be tabooed.
entries.literal: 'Old' means the lord of a destroyed temple; when favor is distant and kinship severed, the name need not be tabooed.

entries.zh: 今昭宣上去玄宗十四世，奏改冊文，非典故也。）〉
entries.en: From the August and Illustrious up to Emperor Xuanzong are fourteen generations; memorializing a change to the writ text is not according to precedent.)〉
entries.literal: Now from the August and Illustrious up to Emperor Xuanzong are fourteen generations; to memorialize changing the writ text is not according to precedent.)〉

entries.zh: 周廣順三年冬十月，禮儀使奏：「郊廟祝文，禮例云：古者文字皆書於冊，而有長短之差。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, Guangshun 3 of Later Zhou, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "Regarding prayer texts for suburban and temple sacrifices, ritual precedent holds that in antiquity all texts were written on tablets, which varied in length.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter of the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, the Commissioner of Ritual memorialized: "Regarding prayer texts for suburban and temple sacrifices, ritual precedent states: in antiquity all writing was inscribed on tablets, and there were differences in length.

entries.zh: 魏、晉郊廟祝文書於冊。
entries.en: Under Wei and Jin, suburban and temple prayer texts were written on bound tablets.
entries.literal: In Wei and Jin, suburban and temple prayer texts were written on tablets.

entries.zh: 唐初悉用祝版，唯陵廟用玉冊，玄皇親祭郊廟，用玉為冊。
entries.en: Early Tang used prayer boards exclusively; only imperial tombs and temples used jade tablets, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade tablets were employed.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tang all used prayer boards; only imperial tombs and temples used jade tablets, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade was used for tablets.

entries.zh: 德宗朝，博士陸淳議，準禮用祝版，祭已燔之，可其議。
entries.en: In Dezong's reign, Erudite Lu Chun argued that ritual required prayer boards to be burned after the sacrifice; his proposal was approved.
entries.literal: In the reign of Dezong, Erudite Lu Chun proposed that according to ritual prayer boards should be used and burned after the sacrifice; his proposal was approved.

entries.zh: 貞元六年親祭，又用竹冊，當司準《開元禮》，並用祝版。
entries.en: In Zhenyuan 6 bamboo tablets were used again for a personal sacrifice, but the responsible office, following the Kaiyuan Ritual, employed prayer boards throughout.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan for a personal sacrifice, bamboo tablets were again used; the responsible office, following the Kaiyuan Ritual, used prayer boards throughout.

entries.zh: 梁朝依禮行之，至明宗郊天，又用竹冊。
entries.en: The Liang dynasty followed ritual practice; by Emperor Mingzong's suburban sacrifice to Heaven, bamboo tablets were used again.
entries.literal: The Liang dynasty followed ritual in practice; by the time of Emperor Mingzong's suburban sacrifice to Heaven, bamboo tablets were again used.

entries.zh: 今詳酌禮例，允以祝版為宜。」
entries.en: Having reviewed ritual precedent in detail, prayer boards are deemed appropriate."
entries.literal: Having now examined ritual precedent in detail, prayer boards are approved as appropriate."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: An edict approved the proposal.
entries.literal: An edict approved this.

entries.zh: 顯德二年秋八月，兵部尚書張昭上言：「今月十二日，伏蒙宸慈召對，面奉聖旨，每年祀祭，多用太牢，念其耕稼之勞，更備犧牲之用，比諸豢養，特可湣傷，令臣等討故事，可以佗牲代否。
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn, Xiande 2, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial: "On the twelfth of this month I was graciously summoned for audience and received the sacred command in person: yearly sacrifices mostly use the grand offering; considering the labor of plowing and sowing and the further provision of sacrificial animals, compared with ordinary rearing this is especially pitiable—order us to investigate precedent on whether other victims may be substituted.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the second year of Xiande, Minister of War Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial: "On the twelfth day of this month your subject was graciously summoned for audience and received the sacred command in person: yearly sacrifices mostly use the grand offering; considering the labor of plowing and sowing and the further provision of sacrificial animals, compared with ordinary rearing this is especially pitiable—order your subjects to investigate precedent on whether other victims may be substituted.

entries.zh: 臣仰稟綸言，退尋禮籍，其三牲八簋之制，五禮六樂之文，著在典彜，叠相沿襲，累經朝代，無所改更。
entries.en: I received the imperial words and, retiring, searched the ritual records: the regulations for the three victims and eight gui, the texts of the five rites and six music—all recorded in canonical vessels, handed down through successive dynasties without change.
entries.literal: Your subject received the imperial words and, retiring, searched the ritual records: the regulations for the three victims and eight gui, the texts of the five rites and six music—all are recorded in canonical vessels, handed down in succession through successive dynasties without change.

entries.zh: 臣聞古者燔黍捭豚，尚多質略，近則梁武面牲竹脯，不可宗師，雖好生之德則然，於奉先之儀太劣。
entries.en: I have heard that in antiquity roasted millet and split pig were offered in a largely plain and simple way; recently Emperor Wu of Liang used bamboo effigies of victims and dried meat—this cannot serve as a model; although the virtue of cherishing life is admirable, for rites honoring ancestors it is far too inferior.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that in antiquity roasted millet and split pig were offered, still largely plain and simple; recently Emperor Wu of Liang used bamboo effigies of victims and dried meat—this cannot be taken as a model; although the virtue of cherishing life is admirable, for rites honoring ancestors it is far too inferior.

entries.zh: 蓋禮主於信，孝本因心，黍稷非馨，鬼神饗德，不必牲牢之巨細，籩豆之方圓，茍血祀長保於宗祧，而牲俎何須於繭栗。
entries.en: Ritual chiefly rests on sincerity; filial piety originates in the heart. Grain offerings are not fragrant—the spirits feast on virtue. Victims need not be large or small, nor platters round or square; if blood sacrifice long preserves the ancestral line, what need for silkworm cocoons and chestnuts on the victim table?
entries.literal: Ritual chiefly rests on sincerity; filial piety originates in the heart. Millet and millet stalks are not fragrant—the spirits feast on virtue. It is not necessary that victims be large or small, or platters round or square; if blood sacrifice long preserves the ancestral line, what need is there for silkworm cocoons and chestnuts on the victim table?

entries.zh: 但以國之大事，儒者久行，易以佗牢，恐未為便。
entries.en: Yet because this is a great affair of state long practiced by Confucian scholars, changing to another grand offering would perhaps be inconvenient.
entries.literal: Yet because this is a great affair of state long practiced by Confucian scholars, to change to another grand offering would perhaps be inconvenient.

entries.zh: 以臣愚見，其南北郊、宗廟社稷、朝日夕月等大祠，如皇帝親行事，備三牲；
entries.en: In my humble view, for great sacrifices such as the southern and northern suburbs, ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, morning sun and evening moon—if the emperor personally performs the rite, the three victims should be provided;
entries.literal: In your subject's humble view, for great sacrifices such as the southern and northern suburbs, ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, morning sun and evening moon—if the emperor personally performs the rite, the three victims should be provided;

entries.zh: 如有司攝行事，則用少牢已下。
entries.en: if officials perform the rite by proxy, then the lesser offering or below should be used.
entries.literal: if officials perform the rite by proxy, then the lesser offering or below should be used.

entries.zh: 雖非舊典，貴減牲牛。」
entries.en: Although this departs from the old statute, it would reduce the use of sacrificial oxen."
entries.literal: Although this is not the old statute, it is valuable for reducing sacrificial oxen."

entries.zh: 是時太常卿田敏又奏云：
entries.en: At this time Director of the Court of Imperial Rites Tian Min also memorialized:
entries.literal: At this time Director of the Court of Imperial Rites Tian Min also memorialized:

entries.zh: 天成三年十一月，太常定唐少帝為昭宣光烈考皇帝，廟號景宗。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Tiancheng 3, the Court of Imperial Rites fixed the posthumous title of the Tang Lesser Emperor as the August and Illustrious, Bright and Majestic Imperial Father, with temple name Jingzong.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Tiancheng, the Court of Imperial Rites fixed the posthumous title of the Tang Lesser Emperor as the August and Illustrious, Bright and Majestic Imperial Father, with temple name Jingzong.

entries.zh: 博士呂朋龜奏：「謹按禮經，臣不誄君，稱天以謚之，是以本朝故事，命太尉率百僚奉謚冊告天於圜丘，回讀於靈座前，並在七月之內，謚冊入陵。
entries.en: Erudite Lü Penggui memorialized: "According to the ritual classics, subjects do not bestow posthumous titles on their lord; Heaven is invoked to confer the title. Thus our dynasty orders the Grand Commandant to lead the hundred officials in presenting the posthumous tablet to Heaven at the Round Mound, returning to read it before the spirit seat—all within the seventh month, and the tablet enters the tomb.
entries.literal: Erudite Lü Penggui memorialized: "According to the ritual classics, subjects do not bestow posthumous titles on their lord; Heaven is invoked to confer the title. Thus the precedent of this dynasty orders the Grand Commandant to lead the hundred officials in presenting the posthumous tablet to announce to Heaven at the Round Mound, returning to read it before the spirit seat—all within the seventh month, and the posthumous tablet enters the tomb.

entries.zh: 若追尊定謚，命太尉讀謚冊於太廟，藏冊於本廟。
entries.en: If posthumous elevation and fixing of the title are pursued, the Grand Commandant reads the posthumous tablet at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and stores it in that emperor's temple.
entries.literal: If posthumous elevation and fixing of the title are pursued, the Grand Commandant is ordered to read the posthumous tablet at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and store the tablet in that emperor's temple.

entries.zh: 伏以景宗皇帝，頃負沈冤，歲月深遠，園陵已修，不祔於廟，則景宗皇帝親在七廟之外。
entries.en: We observe that Emperor Jingzong long bore a deep wrong; years have passed and the imperial tomb has been repaired—if he is not enshrined in the temple, he remains outside the seven temples.
entries.literal: Your subjects observe that Emperor Jingzong long bore a deep wrong; the years are distant; the imperial tomb has been repaired—if he is not enshrined in the temple, then Emperor Jingzong's person remains outside the seven temples.

entries.zh: 今聖朝申冤，追尊定謚，重新帝號，須撰禮儀。
entries.en: Now the court redresses the wrong, pursues posthumous elevation, and renews the imperial designation—ritual procedures must be drafted.
entries.literal: Now the sacred court redresses the wrong, pursues posthumous elevation and fixes the title, and renews the imperial designation—ritual procedures must be drafted.

entries.zh: 又，《禮》云：君不逾年不入宗廟。
entries.en: Moreover, the Rites state: a lord who has not completed a full year does not enter the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Rites state: a lord who has not completed a full year does not enter the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 且漢之殤、沖、質，君臣已成，晉之惠、懷、湣，俱負艱難，皆不列高食，止祀於園寢。
entries.en: Moreover, Han's Shang, Chong, and Zhi—lord and subject relations were already formed; Jin's Hui, Huai, and Min—all bore hardship; none received offerings in the main temple and were worshipped only at the garden mausoleum.
entries.literal: Moreover, Han's Shang, Chong, and Zhi—lord and subject relations were already formed; Jin's Hui, Huai, and Min—all bore hardship; none were listed for high offerings and were worshipped only at the garden mausoleum.

entries.zh: 臣等切詳故實，欲請立景宗皇帝廟於園所，命使奉冊書寶綬，上謚於廟，便奉太牢祀之，其四時委守奉薦。
entries.en: We have examined precedent in detail and request establishing Emperor Jingzong's temple at the mausoleum grounds, ordering envoys to present the tablet, writ, seal, and cord, confer the posthumous title at the temple, and offer the grand sacrifice; guardians shall perform seasonal offerings through the four seasons.
entries.literal: Your subjects have examined precedent in detail and wish to request establishing Emperor Jingzong's temple at the mausoleum grounds, ordering envoys to present the tablet, writ, seal, and cord, confer the posthumous title at the temple, and immediately offer the grand sacrifice; the four seasons shall be entrusted to guardians for seasonal offerings.

entries.zh: 請下尚書省集三省官詳議施行。」
entries.en: We request that the Department of State Affairs assemble officials of the Three Departments for detailed deliberation and implementation."
entries.literal: It is requested that the Department of State Affairs assemble officials of the Three Departments for detailed deliberation and implementation."

entries.zh: 右散騎常侍蕭希甫等議請依禮院所奏。
entries.en: Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xifu and others deliberated and requested following the Court of Imperial Rites' memorial.
entries.literal: Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Household Xiao Xifu and others deliberated and requested following the Court of Imperial Rites' memorial.

entries.zh: 奉敕：宜令本州城內選地起廟。
entries.en: By imperial command: a site within the prefectural city should be selected and a temple erected.
entries.literal: By imperial command: a site within the prefectural city should be selected and a temple erected.

entries.zh: 乃於曹州立廟。
entries.en: A temple was then established in Cao Prefecture.
entries.literal: A temple was then established in Cao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 禮志下
entries.en: Treatises on Rites, Part Two
entries.literal: Treatises on Rites, Lower

entries.zh: 古之王者，理定制禮，功成作樂，所以昭事天地，統和人神，歷代已來，舊章斯在。
entries.en: The kings of old established ritual once order was settled and composed music once their achievements were complete, thereby making clear their service to Heaven and Earth and harmonizing the realms of human and spirit. From age to age, those ancient regulations have endured.
entries.literal: The ancient kings, when order was settled established ritual, when achievements were complete made music, thereby to manifest service to Heaven and Earth and harmonize human and divine beings; from successive ages onward, the old regulations have remained in place.

entries.zh: 洎唐季之亂，鹹、鎬為墟；
entries.en: When the late Tang fell into chaos, the ritual centers at Xian and Hao were reduced to ruins;
entries.literal: When the disorder of the late Tang came, Xian and Hao became ruins;

entries.zh: 梁運雖興，《英》、《莖》掃地。
entries.en: and though the Liang dynasty rose in their place, the ancient pieces Ying and Jing vanished entirely.
entries.literal: though the fortune of Liang arose, the Ying and Jing pieces were swept clean from the earth.
