entries.zh: 莊宗起於朔野，經始霸圖，其所存者，不過邊部鄭聲而已，先王雅樂，殆將泯絕。
entries.en: Zhuangzong rose from the northern marches and set about his bid for dominion, yet all that survived in his court was the vulgar Zheng music of the frontier; the elegant music of former kings was all but lost.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong rose from the northern frontier and began his hegemonic design; what he preserved was nothing but the Zheng music of the borderlands, while the elegant music of the former kings was nearly extinguished.

entries.zh: 當同光、天成之際，或有事清廟，或祈祀泰壇，雖簨虡猶施，而宮商孰辨？
entries.en: During the Tongguang and Tiancheng reigns, rites were still held at the imperial temple or prayers offered at the great altar, but though ritual frames and plumes were set in place, who could tell one pitch from another?
entries.literal: In the Tongguang and Tiancheng eras, sometimes there were rites at the Clear Temple or prayers at the great altar; though feathered frames were still set up, who could distinguish gong from shang?

entries.zh: 遂使磬襄、鼗武，入河、漢而不歸；
entries.en: Thus masters such as Qixiang and Taowu went off to the Yellow and Han and never came back;
entries.literal: Thus masters like Qixiang and Taowu entered the Yellow and Han rivers and did not return;

entries.zh: 湯、舜韶，混陵谷而俱失。
entries.en: and the Shao music of Tang of Shang and Shun of Yu was swallowed up with the hills and valleys, lost without trace.
entries.literal: the Shao music of Tang and Shun was mingled with hills and valleys and lost together.

entries.zh: 洎晉高祖奄登大寶，思迪前規，爰詔有司，重興二舞。
entries.en: When Jin Gaozu at last took the throne, he sought to follow the precedents of old and ordered the responsible offices to revive the two ritual dances.
entries.literal: When Jin Gaozu suddenly ascended the great throne, he thought to follow the former regulations and thereupon ordered the responsible offices to revive the two dances.

entries.zh: 旋屬烽火為亂，明法罔修，漢祚幾何，無暇制作。
entries.en: Soon war-fires blazed again, proper law went untended, and the Later Han mandate lasted only a few years—there was no time to complete the work.
entries.literal: Soon afterward war-fires arose in disorder, bright laws went unrepaired, and the Han mandate lasted but briefly, with no leisure for composition.

entries.zh: 周顯德五年冬，將立歲仗，有司以崇牙樹羽，宿設於殿庭。
entries.en: In the winter of the fifth year of Xiande under the Zhou, as the year-end guard ceremony was being prepared, the responsible offices erected lofty frames with plumes and set them up overnight in the palace courtyard.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, when the year-end guard ceremony was to be established, the responsible offices set up lofty teeth and planted feathers overnight in the palace courtyard.

entries.zh: 世宗因親臨樂懸，試其聲奏，見鐘磬之類，有設而不擊者，訊於工師，皆不能對。
entries.en: Shizong went in person to inspect the suspended instruments and test their sound. He found bells and chimes set out but left unplayed, and when he questioned the craftsmen, none could explain why.
entries.literal: Shizong thereupon personally inspected the suspended music, tested its sound and performance, and saw that among bells, chimes, and the like some were set up but not struck; he questioned the craftsmen, and none could answer.

entries.zh: 世宗惻然，乃命翰林學士、判太常寺事竇儼參詳其制，又命樞密使王樸考正其聲。
entries.en: Deeply troubled, Shizong ordered the Hanlin academician and acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Dou Yan, to review the regulations in detail, and the Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu to correct the pitches.
entries.literal: Shizong was moved with concern and thereupon ordered Hanlin academician and acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Yan to examine the regulations in detail, and also ordered Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu to correct the pitches.

entries.zh: 樸乃用古累黍之法，以審其度，造成律準，其狀如琴而巨，凡設十三弦以定六律、六呂旋相為宮之義。
entries.en: Pu applied the ancient method of stacking millet grains to determine the measures and built a pitch standard shaped like an oversized zither, with thirteen strings arranged to establish the six lü and six lü alternately generating the tonic.
entries.literal: Pu then used the ancient method of stacking millet grains to determine the measures, and constructed a pitch standard shaped like a large zither, setting thirteen strings in all to fix the meaning of the six lü and six lü alternately generating the tonic.

entries.zh: 世宗善之，申命百官議而行之。
entries.en: Shizong approved the design and directed all officials to deliberate and put it into effect.
entries.literal: Shizong approved it and ordered all officials to deliberate and put it into practice.

entries.zh: 今亦備紀於後，以誌五代雅樂沿革之由焉。
entries.en: What follows records these matters in full, tracing how elegant music evolved through the Five Dynasties.
entries.literal: Now these are also fully recorded below, to mark the reasons for the evolution of elegant music in the Five Dynasties.

entries.zh: 晉高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《咸和之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Jin Gaozu, the Sheng Wen, Zhang Wu, Ming De, Xiao Emperor, the Dance of Universal Harmony was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Jin Gaozu, the Sheng Wen, Zhang Wu, Ming De, Xiao Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Universal Harmony.

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: Approved.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·崔棁傳》：高祖詔太常復文武二舞，詳定正冬朝會禮及樂章。
entries.en: (Ouyang's History [New History of the Five Dynasties], Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.
entries.literal: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Cui Zhuo: Gaozu ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to restore the civil and military dances and to fix in detail the rites of the winter court assembly and the music sections.

entries.zh: 自唐末之亂，禮樂制度亡失已久，棁與御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允等草定之。
entries.en: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost. Zhuo, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others, drafted regulations for them.
entries.literal: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, ritual and music institutions had long been lost; Zhuo together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and others drafted regulations for them.

entries.zh: 其年冬至，高祖會朝崇元殿，廷設宮懸，二舞在北，登歌在上。
entries.en: That year at the winter solstice, Gaozu held court at Chongyuan Hall. Court suspended bells and chimes were set up in the hall, with the two dances to the north and ascending song above.
entries.literal: That year at the winter solstice, Gaozu held court at Chongyuan Hall; court suspended bells and chimes were set up in the hall, the two dances to the north, ascending song above.

entries.zh: 文舞郎八佾六十有四人，冠進賢。
entries.en: Sixty-four civil dancers in eight rows wore the forward-virtue cap.
entries.literal: Sixty-four civil dancers in eight rows, wearing the forward-virtue cap.

entries.zh: 黃紗袍，白中單，白練𧞔襠，白布大口袴，革帶履，左執枿，右秉翟，執纛引者二人。
entries.en: They wore yellow gauze robes, white undergarments, white silk overskirt panels, white cloth wide-legged trousers, leather belts and shoes; in the left hand they held the yue flute, in the right they grasped plumes, and two men holding battle standards led.
entries.literal: Yellow gauze robes, white undergarments, white silk overskirt panels, white cloth wide-legged trousers, leather belts and shoes; in the left hand they hold the yue flute, in the right they grasp plumes; two men holding battle standards lead.

entries.zh: 武舞郎八佾六十有四人，服平巾幘，緋絲布大袖繡襠，甲金飾，白練𧞔襠，錦騰蛇起梁帶，豹文大口袴，烏靴，左執幹，右執戚，執旌引者二人。
entries.en: Sixty-four military dancers in eight rows wore plain kerchiefs, crimson silk large sleeves with embroidered panels, gold-trimmed armor ornaments, white silk overskirt panels, brocade belts with rising snake patterns, leopard-pattern wide-legged trousers, and black boots. In the left hand they held shields, in the right battle-axes, and two men holding pennants led.
entries.literal: Sixty-four military dancers in eight rows wore plain kerchiefs, crimson silk large sleeves with embroidered panels, gold-trimmed armor ornaments, white silk overskirt panels, brocade belts with rising snake patterns, leopard-pattern wide-legged trousers, and black boots; in the left hand they held shields, in the right battle-axes; two men holding pennants led.

entries.zh: 加鼓吹十二案，負以熊豹，以象百獸率舞。
entries.en: Twelve sets of wind-and-percussion were added, borne on bear and leopard figures, to symbolize the hundred beasts leading the dance.
entries.literal: Twelve sets of wind-and-percussion were added, borne on bear and leopard figures, to symbolize the hundred beasts leading the dance.

entries.zh: 案設羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌簫、笳各二人。
entries.en: Each set had one feathered-canopy drum, one great drum, one metal chun, and two each for singing pipes and reed pipes.
entries.literal: Each set had one feathered-canopy drum, one great drum, one metal chun, and two each for singing pipes and reed pipes.

entries.zh: 王公上壽，天子舉爵，奏《元同》；
entries.en: When princes and nobles offered longevity wishes, the Son of Heaven raised his cup and they played "Primary Unity";
entries.literal: When princes and nobles offered longevity wishes, the Son of Heaven raised his cup and they played "Primary Unity";

entries.zh: 二舉，登歌奏《文同》；
entries.en: At the second raising, ascending song played "Literary Unity";
entries.literal: At the second raising, ascending song played "Literary Unity";

entries.zh: 舉食，文舞《昭德》，武舞《成功》之曲。
entries.en: When food was served, the civil dance played "Manifest Virtue" and the military dance the piece "Accomplishment."
entries.literal: When food was served, the civil dance played "Manifest Virtue" and the military dance the piece "Accomplishment."

entries.zh: 禮畢，高祖大悅，賜棁金帛，群臣左右睹者皆贊嘆之。
entries.en: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo. All the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.
entries.literal: When the rites were complete, Gaozu was greatly pleased and bestowed gold and silk on Zhuo; all the ministers and onlookers praised and marveled at it.

entries.zh: 然禮樂廢久，而制作簡繆，又繼以龜茲部《霓裳法曲》，參亂雅音。
entries.en: Yet ritual and music had long been abandoned, and what was made was simple and flawed. Moreover they added the Kucha section's "Rainbow Skirt Law Piece," mingling and disrupting elegant music.
entries.literal: Yet ritual and music had been abandoned for long, and what was made was simple and flawed; moreover they added the Kucha section's "Rainbow Skirt Law Piece," mingling and disrupting elegant music.

entries.zh: 其樂工舞郎，多教坊伶人、百工商賈、州縣避役之人，又無老師良工教習。
entries.en: The musicians and dancers were mostly entertainment-bureau performers, artisans and merchants, and people evading corvée duty from prefectures and districts. Moreover there were no veteran masters or skilled craftsmen to teach them.
entries.literal: The musicians and dancers were mostly entertainment-bureau performers, artisans and merchants, and people evading corvée duty from prefectures and districts; moreover there were no veteran masters or skilled craftsmen to teach them.

entries.zh: 明年正旦，復奏於庭，而登歌發聲，悲離煩慝，如《薤露》、《虞殯》之音，舞者行列進退，皆不應節，聞者皆悲憤。
entries.en: The next year at New Year's Day they again performed in court, but when ascending song sounded it was mournful, troubled, and grievous, like the tones of "Wild Leek Dew" and "Yu Funereal." The dancers' ranks advancing and retreating all failed to match the beat, and all who heard it felt grief and anger.
entries.literal: The next year at New Year's Day they again performed in court, but when ascending song sounded it was mournful, troubled, and grievous, like the tones of "Wild Leek Dew" and "Yu Funereal"; the dancers' ranks advancing and retreating all failed to match the beat; all who heard it felt grief and anger.

entries.zh: 開運二年，太常少卿陶穀奏廢二舞。）〉
entries.en: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the two dances.)〉
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tao Gu memorialized to abolish the two dances.)〉

entries.zh: 晉天福四年十二月，禮官奏：「來歲正旦，王公上壽，皇帝舉酒，請奏《元同之樂》；
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tianfu under Jin, the ritual officials memorialized: "For next year's New Year's Day, when the princes and dukes offer birthday felicitations and the emperor raises his cup, Music of Primal Unity should be played;
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Tianfu of Jin, the ritual officials memorialized: "Next year's New Year's Day, when the princes and dukes offer longevity wishes and the emperor raises his cup, please perform Music of Primal Unity;

entries.zh: 再舉酒，奏《文同之樂》。」
entries.en: when he raises his cup a second time, Music of Cultural Unity should be played."
entries.literal: when the cup is raised a second time, perform Music of Cultural Unity."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: This was approved.

entries.zh: 五年，始議重興二舞，詔曰：「正冬二節，朝會舊儀，廢於離亂之時，興自和平之代。
entries.en: In the fifth year, deliberations began on reviving the two dances. An edict declared: "The two mid-winter festivals and the court assembly rites of old were abandoned in times of turmoil and are to be restored in an age of peace.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, they first deliberated on reviving the two dances. An edict stated: "The two mid-winter festivals and the court assembly rites of old were abandoned in times of disorder and are to be revived in an age of peace.

entries.zh: 將期備物，全系用心；
entries.en: We expect every implement to be prepared in full, and that depends entirely on devoted effort;
entries.literal: We expect to prepare the implements in full, which depends entirely on devoted effort;

entries.zh: 須議擇人，同為定制。
entries.en: we must deliberate and choose the right men to establish these regulations together.
entries.literal: we must deliberate and select personnel to establish these regulations together.

entries.zh: 其正冬朝會禮節、樂章、二舞行列等事宜，差太常卿崔棁、御史中丞竇貞固、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允與太常寺官一一詳定。
entries.en: Concerning the mid-winter court assembly ritual procedures, hymns, formations of the two dances, and related matters, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, and officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are commissioned to determine each point in detail.
entries.literal: As for the mid-winter court assembly ritual procedures, hymns, formations of the two dances, and related matters, commission Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Justice Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, together with officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to determine each in detail.

entries.zh: 禮從新意，道在舊章，庶知治世之和，漸見移風之善。」
entries.en: Ritual may take on new forms, but the Way lies in the old regulations; we hope thereby to manifest the harmony of a well-governed age and gradually to see customs transformed for the better."
entries.literal: Ritual may follow new intentions, but the Way lies in the old regulations; we hope thereby to know the harmony of a well-governed age and gradually see the goodness of transforming customs."

entries.zh: 其年秋，棁等具述制度上奏云：
entries.en: That autumn, Zhi and his colleagues submitted a full account of the regulations, stating:
entries.literal: That autumn, Zhi and the others fully set forth the regulations and memorialized, stating:

entries.zh: 慶祖章肅皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《觀成之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Qing Zu, the Zhang Su Emperor, the Dance of Observing Accomplishment was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Qing Zu, the Zhang Su Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Observing Accomplishment.

entries.zh: 登歌樂章各一首。
entries.en: Each chamber had one hymn for the ascending song.
entries.literal: One hymn each for the ascending song.

entries.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《明德之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Taizu, the Sheng Shen, Gong Su, Wen Wu, Xiao Emperor, the Dance of Bright Virtue was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Taizu, the Sheng Shen, Gong Su, Wen Wu, Xiao Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Bright Virtue.

entries.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《定功之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Shizong, the Rui Wu, Xiao Wen Emperor, the Dance of Fixing Merit was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Shizong, the Rui Wu, Xiao Wen Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Fixing Merit.

entries.zh: 登歌樂章各一首。
entries.en: Each chamber had one hymn for the ascending song.
entries.literal: One hymn each for the ascending song.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：太祖廟室樂章，太常卿田敏撰。
entries.en: (According to the Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium, the hymns for Taizu's temple chamber were composed by Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tian Min.
entries.literal: (The Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium states: the hymns for Taizu's temple chamber were composed by Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tian Min.

entries.en: Those for Shizong's temple chamber were composed by Hanlin academician and acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Yan.)〉

entries.zh: 樂章詞多不錄。
entries.en: Most of the hymn texts are not recorded here.
entries.literal: Most of the hymn texts are not recorded.

entries.zh: 梁開平初，太祖受禪，始建宗廟，凡四室，每室有登歌、酌獻之舞：肅祖宣元皇帝室曰《大合之舞》。
entries.en: Early in Kaiping of the Liang, when Taizu accepted the abdication, he established the ancestral temple with four chambers. Each chamber had dances for the ascending song and the libation offering: the chamber of Sole Ancestor Emperor Xuan Yuan used the Dance of Great Harmony.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping of Liang, when Taizu received the abdication, he first established the ancestral temple, four chambers in all; each chamber had dances for ascending song and libation offering: the chamber of Sole Ancestor Emperor Xuan Yuan was called the Dance of Great Harmony.

entries.zh: 敬祖光憲皇帝室曰《象功之舞》。
entries.en: The chamber of Revered Ancestor Emperor Guang Xian used the Dance of Symbolizing Merit.
entries.literal: The chamber of Revered Ancestor Emperor Guang Xian was called the Dance of Symbolizing Merit.

entries.zh: 憲祖昭武皇帝室曰《來儀之舞》。
entries.en: The chamber of Ancestor of the Constitution Emperor Zhao Wu used the Dance of Coming Rites.
entries.literal: The chamber of Ancestor of the Constitution Emperor Zhao Wu was called the Dance of Coming Rites.

entries.zh: 烈祖文穆皇帝室曰《昭德之舞》。
entries.en: The chamber of Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu used the Dance of Manifest Virtue.
entries.literal: The chamber of Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu was called the Dance of Manifest Virtue.

entries.zh: 登歌樂章各一首。
entries.en: Each chamber had one hymn for the ascending song.
entries.literal: For ascending song, one hymn each.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：太常少卿楊煥撰。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium, these were composed by Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yang Huan.)〉
entries.literal: (The Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium states: composed by Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yang Huan.)〉

entries.zh: 二年春，梁祖將議郊禋，有司撰進樂名、舞名：樂曰《慶和之樂》。
entries.en: In the spring of the second year, as the Liang founder prepared to discuss the suburban sacrifice, the responsible offices submitted proposed names for the music and dances: the music was to be called Music of Celebrating Harmony.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year, when the Liang founder was about to deliberate on suburban sacrifice, the responsible offices drafted and presented music names and dance names: the music was called Music of Celebrating Harmony.

entries.zh: 漢高祖受命之年，秋九月，權太常卿張昭上疏，奏改一代樂名，其略曰？
entries.en: In the year when Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial requesting changes to the music names of the dynasty. Stated in summary:
entries.literal: In the year when Han Gaozu received the Mandate, in the ninth month of autumn, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial requesting changes to the music names of the dynasty; stated in summary:

entries.zh: 翼祖昭獻皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《顯仁之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Yi Zu, the Zhao Xian Emperor, the Dance of Manifest Benevolence was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Yi Zu, the Zhao Xian Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Manifest Benevolence.

entries.zh: 顯祖章聖皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《章慶之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Xian Zu, the Zhang Sheng Emperor, the Dance of Manifest Celebration was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Xian Zu, the Zhang Sheng Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Manifest Celebration.

entries.zh: 登歌樂章各一首。
entries.en: Each chamber had one hymn for the ascending song.
entries.literal: One hymn each for the ascending song.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：太常卿張昭撰。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium, they were composed by Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao.)〉
entries.literal: (The Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium states: composed by Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Zhao.)〉

entries.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝廟室酌獻，舞《觀德之舞》。
entries.en: For the libation offering at the temple chamber of Gaozu, the Rui Wen, Sheng Wu, Zhao Su, Xiao Emperor, the Dance of Observing Virtue was performed.
entries.literal: At the libation offering in the temple chamber of Gaozu, the Rui Wen, Sheng Wu, Zhao Su, Xiao Emperor, the dance was the Dance of Observing Virtue.

entries.zh: 昔周朝奏六代之樂，即今二舞之類是也。
entries.en: Formerly the Zhou court played the music of the six ages—the same kind as today's two dances.
entries.literal: Formerly the Zhou court played the music of the six ages—this is the same kind as today's two dances.

entries.zh: 其賓祭常用，別有《九夏之樂》，即《肆夏》、《皇夏》等是也，梁武帝善音樂，改《九夏》為《十二雅》，前朝祖孝孫改雅為和，示不相沿也。
entries.en: For guest rites and sacrifices in common use there were separately the "Nine Summers Pieces," such as "Free Summer" and "August Summer." Emperor Wu of Liang was skilled in music and changed the "Nine Summers" to the "Twelve Elegances." In the previous dynasty Zu Xiaosun changed elegance to harmony, showing that one should not simply follow precedent.
entries.literal: For guest rites and sacrifices in common use there were separately the "Nine Summers Pieces," such as "Free Summer" and "August Summer"; Emperor Wu of Liang was skilled in music and changed the "Nine Summers" to the "Twelve Elegances"; in the previous dynasty Zu Xiaosun changed elegance to harmony, showing that one should not simply follow precedent.

entries.zh: 臣今改和為成，取《韶》樂九成之義也。
entries.en: Your subject now changes harmony to accomplishment, taking the meaning of the nine accomplishments of Shao music.
entries.literal: Your subject now changes harmony to accomplishment, taking the meaning of the nine accomplishments of Shao music.

entries.zh: 《十二成樂曲》名：祭天神奏《豫和之樂》，請改為《禋成》；
entries.en: Names of the "Twelve Accomplishment Pieces": for sacrificing to Heaven they play "Music of Forethought and Harmony"—please change to "Accomplishment of the Smoke Offering";
entries.literal: Names of the "Twelve Accomplishment Pieces": for sacrificing to Heaven they play "Music of Forethought and Harmony," please change to "Accomplishment of the Smoke Offering";

entries.zh: 祭地祇奏《順和》，請改為《順成》；
entries.en: for sacrificing to earthly spirits they play "Compliance and Harmony"—please change to "Compliance Accomplished";
entries.literal: for sacrificing to earthly spirits they play "Compliance and Harmony," please change to "Compliance Accomplished";

entries.zh: 祭宗廟奏《永和》，請改為《裕成》；
entries.en: for sacrificing at the ancestral temple they play "Everlasting Harmony"—please change to "Abundant Accomplishment";
entries.literal: for sacrificing at the ancestral temple they play "Everlasting Harmony," please change to "Abundant Accomplishment";

entries.zh: 祭天地、宗廟，登歌奏《肅和》，請改為《肅成》；
entries.en: for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and at the ancestral temple, ascending song plays "Solemn Harmony"—please change to "Solemn Accomplishment";
entries.literal: for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and at the ancestral temple, ascending song plays "Solemn Harmony," please change to "Solemn Accomplishment";

entries.zh: 皇帝臨軒奏《太和》，請改為《政成》；
entries.en: when the emperor presides at court they play "Grand Harmony"—please change to "Government Accomplished";
entries.literal: when the emperor presides at court they play "Grand Harmony," please change to "Government Accomplished";

entries.zh: 王公出入奏《舒和》，請改為《弼成》；
entries.en: when princes and nobles enter and leave they play "Easy Harmony"—please change to "Assisting Accomplishment";
entries.literal: when princes and nobles enter and leave they play "Easy Harmony," please change to "Assisting Accomplishment";

entries.zh: 皇帝食舉及飲宴奏《休和》，請改為《德成》；
entries.en: when the emperor raises food and at drinking banquets they play "Restful Harmony"—please change to "Virtue Accomplished";
entries.literal: when the emperor raises food and at drinking banquets they play "Restful Harmony," please change to "Virtue Accomplished";

entries.zh: 皇帝受朝、皇后入宮奏《正和》，請改為《骍成》；
entries.en: when the emperor receives court and the empress enters the palace they play "Correct Harmony"—please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";
entries.literal: when the emperor receives court and the empress enters the palace they play "Correct Harmony," please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";

entries.zh: 皇太子軒懸出入奏《承和》，請改為《允成》；
entries.en: when the crown prince with suspended bells and chimes enters and leaves they play "Receiving Harmony"—please change to "Sincere Accomplishment";
entries.literal: when the crown prince with suspended bells and chimes enters and leaves they play "Receiving Harmony," please change to "Sincere Accomplishment";

entries.zh: 元日、冬至皇帝禮會，登歌奏《昭和》，請改為《慶成》；
entries.en: at New Year's Day and the winter solstice when the emperor holds ceremonial assembly, ascending song plays "Bright Harmony"—please change to "Celebration Accomplished";
entries.literal: at New Year's Day and the winter solstice when the emperor holds ceremonial assembly, ascending song plays "Bright Harmony," please change to "Celebration Accomplished";

entries.zh: 郊廟俎入奏《雍和》，請改為《骍成》；
entries.en: when sacrificial stands enter at suburban and temple rites they play "Harmonious Unity"—please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";
entries.literal: when sacrificial stands enter at suburban and temple rites they play "Harmonious Unity," please change to "Sacrificial Accomplishment";

entries.zh: 皇帝祭享、酌獻、讀祝文及飲福、受胙奏《壽和》，請改為《壽成》。
entries.en: when the emperor sacrifices, pours the offering, reads the prayer text, drinks the blessing wine, and receives the sacrificial meat they play "Longevity Harmony"—please change to "Longevity Accomplished."
entries.literal: when the emperor sacrifices, pours the offering, reads the prayer text, drinks the blessing wine, and receives the sacrificial meat they play "Longevity Harmony," please change to "Longevity Accomplished."

entries.en: Treatise on Music, Part One
entries.literal: Treatise on Music, Part One

entries.zh: 周廣順元年，太祖初即大位，惟新庶政，時太常卿邊蔚上疏請改舞名，其略云：「前朝改祖孝孫所定二舞名，文舞曰《治安之舞》，武舞曰《振德之舞》，今請改《治安》為《政和之舞》，《振德》為《善勝之舞》。
entries.en: In the first year of Later Zhou's Guangshun reign, when Taizu first ascended the throne and set about renewing government, Director of Imperial Sacrifices Bian Wei memorialized the throne to rename certain court dances. In brief he wrote: "The previous dynasty had altered the two dances that Zu Xiaosun had established—the civil dance Pacifying the Realm and the martial dance Stirring Virtue. We ask that Pacifying the Realm be renamed Harmonious Governance and Stirring Virtue be renamed Good Victory.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangshun of Zhou, when the Taizu first assumed the great position and renewed all government affairs, at that time the Director of Imperial Sacrifices Bian Wei submitted a memorial requesting to change dance names. The gist said: "The previous dynasty changed the two dance names fixed by Zu Xiaosun: the civil dance was called Dance of Pacifying the Realm, the martial dance was called Dance of Stirring Virtue. We now request to change Pacifying the Realm to Dance of Harmonious Governance, and Stirring Virtue to Dance of Good Victory.

entries.zh: 前朝改貞觀中二舞名，文舞曰《觀象之舞》，武舞曰《講功之舞》，今請改《觀象》為《崇德之舞》，《講功》為《象成之舞》。
entries.en: He further noted that the previous dynasty had renamed two dances from the Zhenguan period—the civil Observing the Images and the martial Expounding Merit—and asked that Observing the Images become Honoring Virtue and Expounding Merit become Image Accomplished.
entries.literal: The previous dynasty also changed the two dance names of the Zhenguan era: the civil dance was called Dance of Observing the Images, the martial dance was called Dance of Expounding Merit. We now request to change Observing the Images to Dance of Honoring Virtue, and Expounding Merit to Dance of Image Accomplished.

entries.zh: 又議改《十二成》，今改為順。
entries.en: He also proposed retitling the Twelve Accomplishments suite, substituting shun ("accord") for cheng ("accomplishment") throughout.
entries.literal: He also discussed changing the Twelve Accomplishments, now to substitute shun (accord) in their titles.

entries.zh: 《十二順樂曲》名：祭天神奏《禋成》，請改為《昭順之樂》；
entries.en: Among the Twelve Shun pieces: for sacrifices to Heaven, where Yin Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Zhao Shun;
entries.literal: Names of the Twelve Shun music pieces: when sacrificing to Heaven, Yin Accomplished is played; request to change it to Zhao Shun music;

entries.zh: 祭地祗奏《順成》，請改為《寧順之樂》；
entries.en: for sacrifices to earthly spirits, where Shun Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Ning Shun;
entries.literal: when sacrificing to earthly spirits, Shun Accomplished is played; request to change it to Ning Shun music;

entries.zh: 祭宗廟奏《裕成》，請改為《肅順之樂》；
entries.en: for ancestral temple sacrifices, where Yu Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Su Shun;
entries.literal: when sacrificing at the ancestral temple, Yu Accomplished is played; request to change it to Su Shun music;

entries.zh: 祭天地、宗廟，登歌奏《肅成》，今請改為《感順之樂》；
entries.en: for sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple, where the ascending hymn Su Accomplished was used, he asked that it be renamed Gan Shun;
entries.literal: when sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple, the ascending song plays Su Accomplished; we now request to change it to Gan Shun music;

entries.zh: 皇帝臨軒奏《政成》，請改為《治順之樂》；
entries.en: when the emperor held court, where Zheng Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Zhi Shun;
entries.literal: when the emperor presides at the hall, Zheng Accomplished is played; request to change it to Zhi Shun music;

entries.zh: 王公出入奏《弼成》，請改為《忠順之樂》；
entries.en: when princes and dukes entered and left the palace, where Bi Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Zhong Shun;
entries.literal: when princes and dukes enter and exit, Bi Accomplished is played; request to change it to Zhong Shun music;

entries.zh: 皇帝食舉奏《德成》，請改為《康順之樂》；
entries.en: at the emperor's meals, where De Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Kang Shun;
entries.literal: when the emperor's meal is served, De Accomplished is played; request to change it to Kang Shun music;

entries.zh: 皇帝受朝、皇后入宮奏《扆成》，請改為《雍順之樂》；
entries.en: when the emperor received court and the empress entered the palace, where Yi Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Yong Shun;
entries.literal: when the emperor receives the court assembly and the empress enters the palace, Yi Accomplished is played; request to change it to Yong Shun music;

entries.zh: 皇太子軒懸出入奏《胤成》，請改為《溫順之樂》；
entries.en: when the crown prince entered and left with his full bell ensemble, where Yin Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Wen Shun;
entries.literal: when the crown prince with suspended bells enters and exits, Yin Accomplished is played; request to change it to Wen Shun music;

entries.zh: 元日、冬至皇帝禮會，登歌奏《慶成》，請改為《禮順之樂》；
entries.en: at the emperor's New Year and winter solstice assemblies, where the ascending hymn Qing Accomplished was used, he asked that it be renamed Li Shun;
entries.literal: on New Year's Day and the winter solstice at the emperor's ceremonial assembly, the ascending song plays Qing Accomplished; request to change it to Li Shun music;

entries.zh: 郊廟俎入奏《骍成》，請改為《禋順之樂》；
entries.en: when sacrificial stands were brought in at suburban and temple rites, where Xing Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Yin Shun;
entries.literal: when the sacrificial stands enter at suburban and temple rites, Xing Accomplished is played; request to change it to Yin Shun music;

entries.zh: 皇帝祭享、酌獻、讀祝及飲福、受胙奏《壽成》，請改為《福順之樂》。
entries.en: during the emperor's sacrificial offering, libation, reading of prayers, drinking of the blessing wine, and receiving of sacrificial meat, where Shou Accomplished was played, he asked that it be renamed Fu Shun.
entries.literal: when the emperor offers sacrifice, pours libation, reads the prayer, drinks the blessing, and receives the sacrificial meat, Shou Accomplished is played; request to change it to Fu Shun music.

entries.zh: 梁武帝改《九夏》為《十二雅》，以協陽律、陰呂、十二管旋宮之義，祖孝孫改為《十二和》。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang had replaced the Nine Summers with the Twelve Elegances to align with the yang pitches, yin notes, and the twelve-pipe system of circulatory tonality; Zu Xiaosun later renamed them the Twelve Harmonies.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang changed the Nine Summers to the Twelve Elegances, to accord with the meaning of yang pitches, yin notes, and the twelve tubes of circulatory tonality; Zu Xiaosun changed them to the Twelve Harmonies.

entries.zh: 開元中，乃益三和，前朝去二和，改一雅。
entries.en: During the Kaiyuan reign three pieces were added to the Harmonies; the previous dynasty removed two Harmonies and retitled one Elegance.
entries.literal: In the Kaiyuan era three harmonies were added; the previous dynasty removed two harmonies and changed one elegance.

entries.zh: 今去雅，只用《十二順》之曲。
entries.en: He proposed dropping the Elegances altogether and using only the Twelve Shun pieces.
entries.literal: Now the elegances are removed, and only the Twelve Shun pieces are used.

entries.zh: 祭孔宣父、齊太公廟降神奏《師雅》，請同用《禮順之樂》；
entries.en: for spirit-descent rites at the temples of Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi, where Master Elegance was played, he asked that Li Shun be used instead;
entries.literal: when invoking the spirits at the temples of Confucius and Duke Tai of Qi, Master Elegance is played; request likewise to use Li Shun music;

entries.zh: 三公升殿、會訖下階履行同用《弼成》，請同用《忠順之樂》；
entries.en: when the three highest ministers ascended the hall and when they left after an assembly, both occasions used Bi Accomplished; he asked that Zhong Shun be used for both;
entries.literal: when the three dukes ascend the hall, and when the assembly ends and they descend the steps to walk, Bi Accomplished is used for both; request likewise to use Zhong Shun music;

entries.zh: 享先農及籍田同用《順成》，請同用《寧順之樂》。」
entries.en: offerings to the spirit of agriculture and the ceremonial plowing both used Shun Accomplished; he asked that Ning Shun be used for both."
entries.literal: offerings to the spirit of agriculture and the plowing ceremony both use Shun Accomplished; request likewise to use Ning Shun music."

entries.zh: 曲詞文多不載。
entries.en: The lyrics of these pieces are largely omitted from the record.
entries.literal: The texts of the song lyrics are mostly not recorded.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：邊蔚請添召樂師，令在寺習樂。
entries.en: (According to the Institutional History of the Five Dynasties: Bian Wei asked to recruit additional music masters and have them train at the Directorate of Sacrifices.
entries.literal: (Institutional History of the Five Dynasties: Bian Wei requested to recruit additional music masters and have them practice music at the temple.

entries.zh: 敕太常寺見管兩京雅樂節級樂工共四十人外，更添六十人，內三十八人宜抽教坊貼部樂官兼充，餘二十二人宜令本寺照名充填。
entries.en: An edict directed that beyond the forty graded court musicians already under the Directorate in both capitals, sixty more were to be added—thirty-eight drawn from attached chiefs of the Music Bureau to serve concurrently, and the remaining twenty-two filled from the directorate's own roster.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that beyond the forty graded musicians of court music in the two capitals already under the Directorate of Sacrifices, sixty more were to be added; of these, thirty-eight should be drawn from the Music Bureau's attached section chiefs to serve concurrently, and the remaining twenty-two should be filled by name from the directorate itself.

entries.zh: 仍令三司定支春冬衣糧，月報聞奏。
entries.en: The Three Departments were to set their spring and winter clothing and grain allowances, with monthly reports to the throne.
entries.literal: The Three Departments were also ordered to fix spring and winter clothing and grain allowances, with monthly reports submitted to the throne.

entries.zh: 其舊管四十人，亦量添請。）〉
entries.en: The existing staff of forty were likewise to receive proportionate increases in allowance.)〉
entries.literal: The original forty under its charge were also to receive proportional increases in allowance.)〉

entries.zh: 世宗顯德元年即位，有司上太祖廟室酌獻，奏《明德之舞》。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne in the first year of Xiande, the responsible officials offered libations at Taizu's temple hall to the accompaniment of the Dance of Bright Virtue.
entries.literal: When Shizong assumed the throne in the first year of Xiande, the responsible officials presented libations at the Taizu temple hall, and the Dance of Bright Virtue was performed.

entries.zh: 昔帝鴻氏之制樂也，將以範圍天地，協和人神，候八節之風聲，測四時之正氣。
entries.en: When the Di Hong clan first established music, it was meant to encompass Heaven and Earth, harmonize humanity and the spirits, observe the winds of the eight seasonal nodes, and measure the correct qi of the four seasons.
entries.literal: Of old, when the Di Hong clan established music, it was to bound Heaven and Earth, harmonize human beings and spirits, observe the wind sounds of the eight seasonal nodes, and measure the correct qi of the four seasons.

entries.zh: 氣之清濁不可以筆授，聲之善否不可以口傳，故鳧氏鑄金，伶倫截竹。
entries.en: The clarity and turbidity of qi cannot be conveyed in writing; the quality of sound cannot be passed on by word of mouth. Therefore the Fu clan cast bells and Ling Lun cut bamboo pipes.
entries.literal: The clear and muddy of qi cannot be handed down by brush; the good and bad of sound cannot be transmitted by mouth. Therefore the Fu clan cast metal, and Ling Lun cut bamboo.

entries.zh: 為律呂相生之算，宮商正和之音。
entries.en: They worked out the mathematics of mutual pitch generation and the properly harmonized tones of gong and shang.
entries.literal: They made the calculation of mutual generation among pitches, and the properly harmonized sounds of gong and shang.

entries.zh: 乃播之於管弦，宣之於鐘石，然後覆載之情訢合，陰陽之氣和同，八風從律而不奸，五聲成文而不亂。
entries.en: They spread the system among strings and pipes and proclaimed it on bells and stones; only then did the sentiments of Heaven and Earth unite, yin and yang harmonize, the eight winds follow the pitches without straying, and the five tones form ordered patterns.
entries.literal: Then they spread it among strings and pipes and proclaimed it on bells and stones; only then did the feelings of that which covers and bears unite in joy, the qi of yin and yang harmonize, the eight winds follow the pitches without deviation, and the five sounds form patterns without disorder.

entries.zh: 空桑、孤竹之韻，足以禮神；
entries.en: the melodies of Kongsang and Guzhu sufficed to honor the spirits;
entries.literal: the tones of Kongsang and Guzhu sufficed to honor the spirits;

entries.zh: 《雲門》、《大夏》之容，無虧觀德。
entries.en: the dances Cloud Gate and Great Xia did not fall short as displays of virtue.
entries.literal: the forms of Cloud Gate and Great Xia did not fall short in displaying virtue.

entries.zh: 然月律有旋宮之法，備於太師之職。
entries.en: Yet the monthly pitches included the method of circulatory tonality, which fell within the Grand Music Master's charge.
entries.literal: Yet the monthly pitches had the method of circulatory tonality, fully provided for in the office of the Grand Master.

entries.zh: 經秦滅學，雅道淩夷。
entries.en: When Qin suppressed learning, the elegant tradition declined.
entries.literal: After Qin extinguished learning, the elegant Way declined.

entries.zh: 漢初制氏所調，惟存鼓舞，旋宮十二均更用之法，世莫得聞。
entries.en: In early Han only the Zhi clan's drum-and-dance music survived; the method of rotating among the twelve keys was lost to the world.
entries.literal: In early Han what the Zhi clan tuned survived only as drum-and-dance; the method of rotating use among the twelve keys of circulatory tonality, the world could no longer hear.

entries.zh: 漢元帝時，京房善《易》、別音，探求古義，以《周官》均法，每月更用五音，乃立準調，旋相為宮，成六十調。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan of Han, Jing Fang, skilled in the Changes and expert in pitch, sought the ancient meaning and, following the key method of the Offices of Zhou, rotated the five notes month by month; he established a pitch standard, set the circulating tonics, and produced sixty modes.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Yuan of Han, Jing Fang was skilled in the Changes and distinguished in pitch, sought ancient meaning, and by the key method of the Offices of Zhou changed use of the five notes each month; he then established a pitch standard, rotated as tonics, and formed sixty modes.

entries.zh: 又以日法析為三百六十，傳於樂府，而編懸復舊，律呂無差。
entries.en: He also divided the day-cycle into three hundred sixty parts and transmitted the system to the Music Bureau; the chime ensemble was restored and the pitches aligned without error.
entries.literal: He also divided the day method into three hundred sixty parts, transmitted it to the Music Bureau, and the chime ensemble was restored to the old state, with pitches and notes without discrepancy.

entries.zh: 遭漢中微，雅音淪缺，京房準法，屢有言者，事終不成。
entries.en: When Han fell into mid-dynasty decline, elegant music was lost; advocates repeatedly urged adoption of Jing Fang's pitch-standard method, but the effort never succeeded.
entries.literal: When Han declined in the middle period, elegant music was lost and deficient; Jing Fang's pitch-standard method was repeatedly advocated, but the matter in the end was not accomplished.

entries.zh: 錢樂空記其名，沈重但條其說，六十律法，寂寥不傳。
entries.en: Qian Yue recorded only names in vain; Shen Chong merely summarized the theories; the sixty pitch laws fell silent and were never transmitted.
entries.literal: Qian Yue merely recorded their names in vain; Shen Chong only listed their theories; the sixty pitch laws were desolate and not transmitted.

entries.zh: 梁武帝素精音律，自造四通十二笛，以鼓八音。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang, himself expert in pitch theory, devised four sitong pitch-standards and twelve flutes to sound the eight categories of instruments.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was by nature skilled in pitch and law; he himself made twelve four-way flutes to sound the eight kinds of tone.

entries.zh: 又引古五正、二變之音，旋相為宮，得八十四調，與律準所調，音同數異。
entries.en: He also applied the ancient five regular and two altered tones, rotating them as tonics to produce eighty-four modes—matching the pitch standard in sound though differing in numerical arrangement.
entries.literal: He also drew on the ancient five regular and two altered notes, rotating as tonics to obtain eighty-four modes; with those tuned by the pitch standard, the sound was the same but the numbers differed.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，其音又絕，隋朝初定雅樂，群黨沮議，歷載不成。
entries.en: Hou Jing's rebellion extinguished the tradition again; when Sui first sought to fix court music, factional obstruction delayed the work for years.
entries.literal: In the rebellion of Hou Jing its music was again extinguished; when Sui first fixed court music, factions obstructed deliberation, and for years it was not accomplished.

entries.zh: 而沛公鄭譯，因龜茲琵琶七音，以應月律，五正、二變，七調克諧，旋相為宮，復為八十四調。
entries.en: Duke of Pei Zheng Yi then adapted the seven notes of Kucha pipa to the monthly pitches; combining the five regular and two altered tones into seven harmonious modes and rotating them as tonics, he restored the eighty-four modes.
entries.literal: But Duke of Pei Zheng Yi, taking the seven notes of Kucha pipa, matched them to monthly pitches; the five regular and two altered notes, seven modes harmoniously joined, rotated as tonics, and again formed eighty-four modes.

entries.zh: 工人萬寶常又減其絲數，稍令古淡。
entries.en: The craftsman Wan Baochang further reduced the number of strings, giving the music a somewhat plainer, more archaic character.
entries.literal: The craftsman Wan Baochang further reduced the number of strings, making it somewhat ancient and plain.

entries.zh: 隋高祖不重雅樂，令儒官集議。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu of Sui did not esteem court music and ordered Confucian officials to deliberate the matter.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Sui did not value court music and ordered Confucian officials to assemble for deliberation.

entries.zh: 博士何妥駁奏，其鄭、萬所奏八十四調並廢。
entries.en: Academician He Tuo submitted a counter-memorial, and the eighty-four modes proposed by Zheng and Wan were abolished entirely.
entries.literal: Academician He Tuo submitted a refuting memorial, and the eighty-four modes presented by Zheng and Wan were all abolished.

entries.zh: 隋氏郊廟所奏，惟黃鐘一均，與五郊迎氣，雜用蕤賓，但七調而已，其餘五鐘，懸而不作。
entries.en: Sui suburban and temple music used only the yellow-bell key; the five suburban qi-welcoming rites mixed in luxuriant guest—seven modes in all—while the remaining five bells hung unused.
entries.literal: What the Sui performed at suburban and temple rites was only the single key of yellow bell, and at the five suburban rites welcoming the qi, luxuriant guest was mixed in—only seven modes; the remaining five bells hung in suspension but were not struck.

entries.zh: 三朝宴樂，用縵樂九部，迄於革命，未能改更。
entries.en: Banquet music at the three courts relied on the nine divisions of slow music, and through the dynastic transition no change was made.
entries.literal: For the three courts' banquet music, the nine divisions of slow music were used; down to the dynastic change, they could not be altered.

entries.zh: 唐太宗爰命舊工祖孝孫、張文收整比鄭譯、萬寶常所均七音八十四調，方得絲管並施，鐘石俱奏，七始之音復振，四廂之韻皆調。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong of Tang ordered veteran masters Zu Xiaosun and Zhang Wenshou to reconcile the seven-note, eighty-four-mode system of Zheng Yi and Wan Baochang; only then could strings and pipes sound together with bells and stones, the seven foundational tones revive, and harmony return to all four sides of the ensemble.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang then ordered the veteran craftsmen Zu Xiaosun and Zhang Wenshou to collate the seven notes and eighty-four modes harmonized by Zheng Yi and Wan Baochang; only then could strings and pipes be used together and bells and stones played together, the seven initial sounds revived, and the tones of the four sides all tuned.

entries.zh: 自安、史亂離，鹹秦蕩覆。
entries.en: After the An and Shi rebellion, the heartland was laid waste.
entries.literal: From the separation of the An and Shi rebellion, all Qin lands were overturned.

entries.zh: 崇牙樹羽之器，掃地無餘；
entries.en: the lofty-toothed, feather-decked instruments were swept away without a trace;
entries.literal: instruments with lofty teeth and planted feathers were swept clean, nothing remaining;

entries.zh: 戛擊搏拊之工，窮年不嗣。
entries.en: craftsmen skilled in tapping, striking, and clapping went years without successors.
entries.literal: craftsmen of tapping, striking, and clapping went years without successors.

entries.zh: 郊廟所奏，何異南箕，波蕩不遷，知音始絕。
entries.en: suburban and temple performances were as meaningless as the southern Winnowing Basket constellation—adrift without direction, until those who understood music vanished entirely.
entries.literal: what was performed at suburban and temple rites differed little from the southern Winnowing Basket; drifting without change, those who understood pitch were finally extinct.

entries.zh: 臣等竊以音之所起，出自人心，夔、曠不能長存，人事不能常泰，人亡則音息，世亂則樂崩，若不深知禮樂之情，安能明制作之本。
entries.en: We hold that music arises from the human heart; masters like Kui and Kuang cannot endure forever, and human affairs cannot always prosper—when men die, music falls silent; when the age is chaotic, music collapses. Without deep understanding of ritual and music, how can one grasp the foundations of cultural order?
entries.literal: We your servants consider privately that where sound arises, it comes from the human heart; Kui and Kuang cannot long endure, human affairs cannot always be peaceful; when men perish sound ceases, when the age is chaotic music collapses—if one does not deeply know the sentiments of ritual and music, how can one clarify the root of establishment and regulation?

entries.zh: 陛下心苞萬化，學富三雍。
entries.en: Your Majesty's heart embraces all transformations, and your learning is steeped in the classics of the three Yong halls.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's heart embraces the myriad transformations; your learning is rich in the three Yong halls.

entries.zh: 觀兵耀武之功，已光鴻業；
entries.en: your military achievements have already glorified the great enterprise;
entries.literal: in displaying military achievement and martial glory, you have already illumined the great enterprise;

entries.zh: 尊祖禮神之致，尤軫皇情。
entries.en: your reverence for ancestors and the spirits moves your imperial heart above all.
entries.literal: in honoring ancestors and worshipping spirits, your imperial feeling is especially moved.

entries.zh: 乃眷奉常，痛淪樂職，親閱四懸之器，思復九奏之音，爰命廷臣，重調鐘律。
entries.en: You turned to the Directorate of Sacrifices, grieved at the collapse of its musical duties, personally inspected the four suspended ensembles, sought to restore the ninefold performance, and ordered court ministers to retune the bells and pitches.
entries.literal: You then turned affection to the Directorate of Constant Offerings, grieved at the fall of musical offices, personally inspected the four suspended ensembles, thought to restore the sound of nine performances, and thereupon ordered court ministers to retune bells and pitches.

entries.zh: 樞密使王樸，采京房之準法，練梁武之通音，考鄭譯、寶常之七均，校孝孫、文收之九變，積黍累以審其度，聽聲詩以測其情，依權衡嘉量之前文，得備數和聲之大旨，施於鐘虡，足洽《簫韶》。
entries.en: Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu drew on Jing Fang's pitch standard, mastered Emperor Wu of Liang's universal tones, studied the seven keys of Zheng Yi and Wan Baochang and the nine transformations of Zu Xiaosun and Zhang Wenshou, calibrated measures with millet grains, tested pitches against the Sound Poems, followed ancient standards of weight and measure, recovered the principle of numbered harmony, and applied it to bells and stands until it matched the legendary Xiao-Shao music.
entries.literal: Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu adopted Jing Fang's pitch-standard method, mastered Emperor Wu of Liang's universal tones, examined the seven keys of Zheng Yi and Baochang, collated the nine transformations of Xiaosun and Wenshou, piled millet to verify the measure, listened to the Sound Poems to gauge the sentiment, followed the prior texts of weights and the fine measure, obtained the great purport of complete numbers and harmonized sound, applied it to bells and stands, and sufficed to accord with Xiao-Shao.

entries.zh: 臣等今月十九日於太常寺集，命太樂令賈峻奏王樸新法黃鐘調七均，音律和諧，不相淩越。
entries.en: On the nineteenth of this month we assembled at the Directorate and had Grand Music Master Jia Jun perform Wang Pu's new seven keys in yellow-bell mode; the pitches were harmonious, with no note overpowering another.
entries.literal: We your servants on the nineteenth day of this month assembled at the Directorate of Sacrifices and ordered Grand Music Master Jia Jun to perform Wang Pu's new-method seven keys of the yellow-bell mode; pitches and notes were harmonious and did not encroach on one another.

entries.zh: 其餘十一管諸調，望依新法教習，以備禮寺施用。
entries.en: We ask that the remaining eleven pipes and their modes be taught by the new method, so the ritual directorate may put them into use.
entries.literal: The remaining eleven tubes and various modes, we hope, will be taught according to the new method to prepare for use by the ritual directorate.

entries.zh: 其五郊天地、宗廟、社稷、三朝大禮，合用十二管諸調，並載唐史、《開元禮》，近代常行。
entries.en: The five suburban rites, sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, the altars of soil and grain, and the great ceremonies of the three courts all require the full twelve pipes and their modes, as recorded in Tang histories and the Kaiyuan Rites and practiced in recent times.
entries.literal: For the five suburban rites, Heaven and Earth, ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, and great rites of the three courts, all twelve tubes and various modes should be used together; these are recorded in Tang histories and the Kaiyuan Rites, and have been regularly practiced in recent times.

entries.zh: 廣順中，太常卿邊蔚奉敕定前件祠祭朝會舞名、樂曲、歌詞，寺司合有薄籍，伏恐所定與新法曲調聲韻不協，請下太常寺檢詳校試。
entries.en: During Guangshun, Director Bian Wei was ordered to fix the dance names, pieces, and lyrics for those sacrifices and assemblies; the directorate should hold the records on file. We fear they may not match the new pitch system and ask that the directorate examine and test them.
entries.literal: In Guangshun, Director of Sacrifices Bian Wei, by imperial order, fixed the dance names, musical pieces, and song lyrics for the aforesaid sacrifices, assemblies, and court meetings; the directorate should have registers on file. We humbly fear that what was fixed may not accord in tune and sound with the new method, and request that the Directorate of Sacrifices be ordered to examine and test them in detail.

entries.zh: 如或乖舛，請本寺依新法聲調，別撰樂章舞曲，令歌者誦習，永為一代之法，以光六樂之書。
entries.en: If discrepancies are found, we ask the directorate to compose new pieces and dances to the new tones, have the singers learn them by heart, and establish them as the permanent standard of our age—to honor the tradition of the six classical musics.
entries.literal: If there are discrepancies, we request that this directorate, according to the new-method tones, separately compose musical chapters and dance pieces, have singers memorize and practice them, and make them the law of the age forever, to glorify the book of the six musics.

entries.zh: 世宗善之，詔尚書省集百官詳議。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong approved the proposal and ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene all officials for full deliberation.
entries.literal: Shizong approved it and ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble all officials for detailed deliberation.

entries.zh: 兵部尚書張昭等議曰：
entries.en: Minister of War Zhang Zhao and others submitted their deliberation, saying:
entries.literal: Minister of War Zhang Zhao and others deliberated, saying:

entries.zh: 世宗覽奏，善之。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong read the memorial and approved it.
entries.literal: Shizong reviewed the memorial and approved it.

entries.zh: 乃下詔曰：「禮樂之重，國家所先。
entries.en: He then issued an edict: "Ritual and music are what the state must put first.
entries.literal: He then issued an edict saying: "The weight of ritual and music is what the state puts first.

entries.zh: 近朝以來，雅音廢墜，雖時運之多故，亦官守之因循。
entries.en: In recent reigns court music has fallen into ruin—partly because of the turmoil of the times, but also because officials clung to routine.
entries.literal: In recent courts elegant music has been abandoned and fallen; though there have been many vicissitudes of the times, it is also due to officials' routine conformity.

entries.zh: 遂使擊拊之音，空留梗概；
entries.en: so that the sounds of drums and clappers retain only a bare outline;
entries.literal: thus the sounds of striking and clapping retain only a bare outline;

entries.zh: 旋相之法，莫究指歸。
entries.en: the method of rotating tonics—no one could trace its principles.
entries.literal: the method of rotating tonics—no one could trace where it led.

entries.zh: 樞密使王仆，博識古今，懸通律呂，討尋舊典，撰集新聲，定六代之正音，成一朝之盛事。
entries.en: Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu, learned in antiquity and the present, master of pitch and mode, has searched the old canons and compiled new music, restored the correct tones of six dynasties, and achieved a crowning accomplishment of our reign.
entries.literal: Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu is broadly learned in ancient and modern matters, thoroughly versed in pitches and notes, has sought old canons and compiled new sounds, fixed the correct tones of the six dynasties, and accomplished a grand event of the age.

entries.zh: 其王樸所奏旋宮之法，宜依張昭等議狀行。
entries.en: Wang Pu's method of circulatory tonality should be implemented as Zhang Zhao and his colleagues recommended.
entries.literal: Wang Pu's presented method of circulatory tonality should be implemented according to the deliberation memorial of Zhang Zhao and others.

entries.zh: 仍令有司依調制曲，其間或有疑滯，更委王樸裁酌施行。」
entries.en: The responsible offices are to compose pieces according to the modes; any difficulties that arise are to be referred to Wang Pu for final decision."
entries.literal: Let the responsible offices further compose pieces according to the modes; if there are doubts or delays in the process, entrust Wang Pu again to judge and implement."

entries.zh: 自是雅樂之音，稍克諧矣。
entries.en: From that point the sound of court music gradually achieved harmony.
entries.literal: From this time the sound of court music was somewhat able to harmonize.

entries.zh: 五年六月，命中書舍人竇儼參詳太常雅樂。
entries.en: In the sixth month of his fifth year, he ordered Secretariat Drafter Dou Yi to review the directorate's court music.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, the Secretariat Drafter Dou Yi was ordered to examine and revise the court music of the Directorate of Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 十一月，翰林學士竇儼上疏論禮樂刑政之源，其一曰：「請依《唐會要》所分門類，上自五帝，迄於聖朝，凡所施為，悉命編次，凡關禮樂，無有闕漏，名之曰大周通禮，俾禮院掌之。」
entries.en: In the eleventh month, Hanlin Academician Dou Yi memorialized on the foundations of ritual, music, penal law, and governance. His first proposal read: "Following the topical divisions of the Tang Institutional Compendium, let everything enacted from the age of the Five Emperors down to our own dynasty be compiled in full, with nothing omitted concerning ritual and music. Call the work Comprehensive Rites of Great Zhou and place it under the Ritual Office."
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, Hanlin Academician Dou Yi submitted a memorial discussing the origins of ritual, music, penal law, and government. The first proposal said: "We request that according to the categories divided in the Tang Institutional Compendium, from the Five Emperors down to the sacred dynasty, all that has been enacted be ordered for compilation; everything pertaining to ritual and music, without omission, is to be named Comprehensive Rites of Great Zhou, and entrusted to the Ritual Office for custody."

entries.zh: 其二曰：「伏請命博通之士，上自五帝，迄於聖朝，凡樂章沿革，總次編錄，系於歷代樂錄之後，永為定式，名之曰大周正樂，俾樂寺掌之。
entries.en: His second proposal read: "I humbly ask that learned scholars compile the entire history of musical pieces from the Five Emperors to our dynasty, arranged in order and appended to the music records of previous ages as a permanent standard, to be called Correct Music of Great Zhou and placed under the Music Directorate.
entries.literal: The second said: "We humbly request that broadly learned scholars be appointed, from the Five Emperors down to the sacred dynasty, to compile in full order all changes in musical pieces, appended after the music records of successive dynasties, to serve permanently as the fixed standard, named Correct Music of Great Zhou, and entrusted to the Music Directorate for custody.

entries.zh: 依文教習，務在齊肅。」
entries.en: Training should follow the written scores, with uniformity and solemnity as the goal."
entries.literal: Instruction is to follow the text, with the aim of uniformity and solemnity."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「竇儼所上封章，備陳政要，舉當今之急務，疾近世之因循，器識可嘉，辭理甚當，故能立事，無愧蒞官。
entries.en: An edict replied: "Dou Yi's memorial sets forth the essentials of governance, identifies the urgent tasks of our day, and deplores the slavish conformity of recent times. His judgment is commendable and his reasoning sound; he is fit to take on such work without disgracing his office.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The sealed memorial submitted by Dou Yi sets forth the essentials of government in full, raises the urgent tasks of the present age, and deplores the routine conformity of recent times. His capacity and insight are commendable, and his reasoning is very apt; thus he can accomplish affairs without shame in holding office.

entries.zh: 所請編集大周通禮、大周正樂，宜依。
entries.en: His request to compile the Comprehensive Rites of Great Zhou and Correct Music of Great Zhou is approved.
entries.literal: His request to compile the Comprehensive Rites of Great Zhou and Correct Music of Great Zhou is approved.

entries.zh: 仍令於內外職官前資前名中，選擇文學之士，同共編集，具名以聞。
entries.en: Literary scholars are to be chosen from among qualified officials inside and outside the court to join the compilation, and their names reported to the throne.
entries.literal: Let literary scholars be selected from among civil and military officials of prior qualification and prior appointment to compile together, and their names reported in full.

entries.zh: 委儼總領其事。
entries.en: Dou Yi was placed in overall charge of the project.
entries.literal: Dou Yi is entrusted to take overall charge of the matter.

entries.zh: 所須紙筆，下有司供給。」
entries.en: Paper and writing materials are to be supplied by the appropriate offices."
entries.literal: Paper and brushes required are to be supplied by the responsible offices."

entries.zh: 六年春正月，樞密使王樸奉詔詳定雅樂十二律旋相為宮之法，並造律準，上之。
entries.en: In the first month of spring of his sixth year, Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu was ordered to work out the method by which the twelve court-music pitches circulate as tonics, and to construct a pitch standard, which he then presented to the throne.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of the sixth year, Privy Council Commissioner Wang Pu, by imperial order, thoroughly determined the method by which the twelve pitches of court music circulate as tonics, and also constructed a pitch standard, which he presented to the throne.

entries.zh: 其奏疏略曰：
entries.en: His memorial, in summary, read:
entries.literal: His memorial in summary said:

entries.zh: 陛下天縱文武，奄宅中區，思復三代之風，臨視樂懸，親自考聽，知其亡失，深動上心。
entries.en: Your Majesty, endowed with civil and martial gifts from Heaven, has taken the central realm and seeks to restore the culture of the Three Dynasties. Inspecting the court ensemble in person, you heard its losses for yourself and were deeply moved.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is endowed by Heaven with civil and martial excellence, has taken possession of the central realm, and seeks to restore the customs of the Three Dynasties. Observing the suspended music, you personally examined and listened, knew its losses, and were deeply moved at heart.

entries.zh: 乃命中書舍人竇儼參詳太常樂事，不逾月調品八音，粗加和會。
entries.en: You then ordered Secretariat Drafter Dou Yi to review the directorate's music; within a month the eight categories of instruments were tuned into rough harmony.
entries.literal: You then ordered Secretariat Drafter Dou Yi to examine the music affairs of the Directorate of Sacrifices; within a month the eight kinds of sound were tuned and roughly harmonized.

entries.zh: 以臣嘗學律歷，宣示古今樂錄，令臣討論，臣雖不敏，敢不奉詔。
entries.en: Because I have studied pitch theory and calendrics, I was shown the music records of past and present and ordered to investigate them. Though I am not clever, how could I refuse the command?
entries.literal: Because your servant has studied pitch and calendrics, the music records ancient and modern were displayed and your servant was ordered to discuss them. Though your servant is not clever, how dare he not obey the edict?

entries.zh: 遂依周法，以黍校定尺度，長九寸，虛徑三分，為黃鐘之管，與見在黃鐘之聲相應。
entries.en: I followed Zhou methods, using millet grains to calibrate the measure—a tube nine inches long with an inner diameter of three tenths—and produced a yellow-bell pipe that matched the yellow-bell pitch already in use.
entries.literal: I then followed Zhou methods, using millet to calibrate the measure: length nine inches, inner diameter three tenths, making the yellow-bell tube, which corresponded to the present yellow-bell sound.

entries.zh: 以上下相生之法推之，得十二律管。
entries.en: By the method of mutual generation I derived the full set of twelve pitch tubes.
entries.literal: By the method of mutual generation above and below I derived twelve pitch tubes.

entries.zh: 以為眾管互吹，用聲不便，乃作律準，十三弦宣聲，長九尺張弦，各如黃鐘之聲。
entries.en: Because blowing many tubes against one another was impractical, I constructed a pitch standard—a nine-foot frame with thirteen strings, each tuned to the yellow-bell pitch.
entries.literal: Considering that blowing many tubes against one another was inconvenient in use, I then made a pitch standard: thirteen strings to give forth sound, nine feet long with strings stretched, each like the yellow-bell sound.

entries.zh: 以第八弦六尺，設柱為林鐘；
entries.en: on the eighth string at six feet, a bridge was set for forest bell;
entries.literal: on the eighth string at six feet, a bridge was set for forest bell;

entries.zh: 第三弦八尺，設柱為大簇；
entries.en: on the third string at eight feet, a bridge was set for great cluster;
entries.literal: on the third string at eight feet, a bridge was set for great cluster;

entries.zh: 第十弦五尺三寸四分，設柱為南呂；
entries.en: on the tenth string at five feet, three inches, and four tenths, a bridge was set for southern lü;
entries.literal: on the tenth string at five feet three inches and four tenths, a bridge was set for southern lü;

entries.zh: 第五弦七尺一寸三分，設柱為姑洗；
entries.en: on the fifth string at seven feet, one inch, and three tenths, a bridge was set for maiden wash;
entries.literal: on the fifth string at seven feet one inch and three tenths, a bridge was set for maiden wash;

entries.zh: 第十二弦四尺七寸五分，設柱為應鐘；
entries.en: on the twelfth string at four feet, seven inches, and five tenths, a bridge was set for responding bell;
entries.literal: on the twelfth string at four feet seven inches and five tenths, a bridge was set for responding bell;

entries.zh: 第七弦六尺三寸三分，設柱為蕤賓；
entries.en: on the seventh string at six feet, three inches, and three tenths, a bridge was set for luxuriant guest;
entries.literal: on the seventh string at six feet three inches and three tenths, a bridge was set for luxuriant guest;

entries.zh: 第二弦八尺四寸四分，設柱為太呂；
entries.en: on the second string at eight feet, four inches, and four tenths, a bridge was set for great lü;
entries.literal: on the second string at eight feet four inches and four tenths, a bridge was set for great lü;

entries.zh: 第九弦五尺六寸三分，設柱為夷則；
entries.en: on the ninth string at five feet, six inches, and three tenths, a bridge was set for yi rule;
entries.literal: on the ninth string at five feet six inches and three tenths, a bridge was set for yi rule;

entries.zh: 第四弦七尺五寸一分，設柱為夾鐘；
entries.en: on the fourth string at seven feet, five inches, and one tenth, a bridge was set for pressed bell;
entries.literal: on the fourth string at seven feet five inches and one tenth, a bridge was set for pressed bell;

entries.zh: 第十一弦五尺一分，設柱為無射；
entries.en: on the eleventh string at five feet and one inch, a bridge was set for wu she;
entries.literal: on the eleventh string at five feet one inch, a bridge was set for wu she;

entries.zh: 第六弦六尺六寸八分，設柱為中呂；
entries.en: on the sixth string at six feet, six inches, and eight tenths, a bridge was set for central lü;
entries.literal: on the sixth string at six feet six inches and eight tenths, a bridge was set for central lü;

entries.zh: 第十三弦四尺五寸，設柱為黃鐘之清聲。
entries.en: on the thirteenth string at four feet and five inches, a bridge was set for the higher octave of yellow bell.
entries.literal: on the thirteenth string at four feet five inches, a bridge was set for the clear sound of yellow bell.

entries.zh: 十二律中，旋用七聲為均，為均之主者，宮也，徵、商、羽、角、變宮、變徵次焉，發其均主之聲，歸乎本音之律，七聲叠應而不亂，乃成其調。
entries.en: Among the twelve pitches, seven notes rotate as the basis of each key; gong is the governing note, followed by zhi, shang, yu, jue, and the altered tones. When the governing note sounds, it resolves to its home pitch; the seven notes answer one another in layers without confusion, and a mode is thereby formed.
entries.literal: Among the twelve pitches, seven notes are used in rotation as keys; the lord of the key is gong, followed by zhi, shang, yu, jue, altered gong, and altered zhi. When the lord note of the key is sounded, it returns to its fundamental pitch; the seven notes respond in layers without disorder, and thus the mode is formed.

entries.zh: 均有七調，聲有十二均，合八十四調，歌奏之曲，由之出焉。
entries.en: Each key has seven modes, and there are twelve keys in all, yielding eighty-four modes from which all ceremonial songs and performances derive.
entries.literal: Each key has seven modes; there are twelve keys in sound, totaling eighty-four modes; the pieces for song and performance issue from these.

entries.zh: 樂誌下
entries.en: Treatise on Music, Part Two
entries.literal: Music Treatise, Part Two

entries.zh: 梁祖之開國也，屬黃巢大亂之後。
entries.en: When the Liang founding emperor established his dynasty, the realm was still reeling from Huang Chao's great rebellion.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor of Liang established the state, it fell in the period after Huang Chao's great rebellion.

entries.zh: 以夷門一鎮，外嚴烽侯，內辟汙萊，厲以耕桑，薄以租賦，士雖苦戰，民則樂輸，二紀之間，俄成霸業。
entries.en: From the single stronghold of Yimen he tightened frontier defenses abroad and reclaimed wasteland at home, promoted farming and silk production, and kept rents and levies light. Soldiers bore the hardships of war, but the people paid their dues willingly; within two twenty-year cycles he had built a hegemonic power almost overnight.
entries.literal: With a single prefecture at Yimen, outwardly he tightened beacon and frontier defense, inwardly he opened wasteland and marshes, urged farming and sericulture, and kept rents and levies light; though the warriors suffered in battle, the people gladly paid taxes, and within two twenty-year cycles he swiftly achieved hegemony.

entries.zh: 及末帝與莊宗對壘於河上，河南之民，雖困於輦運，亦未至流亡，其義無他，蓋賦斂輕而丘園可戀故也。
entries.en: When the last Liang emperor and Emperor Zhuangzong faced each other across the Yellow River, the people of Henan were strained by transport corvée, yet they did not take to flight—for no other reason than that levies remained light and they still had homes and fields worth holding on to.
entries.literal: When the last emperor of Liang and Emperor Zhuangzong faced each other in stalemate on the Yellow River, the people of Henan, though worn down by cart transport levies, still did not flee into exile; the reason was none other than that tax collections were light and they could still cherish their homes and fields.

entries.zh: 及莊宗平定梁室，任吏人孔謙為租庸使，峻法以剝下，厚斂以奉上，民產雖竭，軍食尚虧。
entries.en: After Emperor Zhuangzong overthrew the Liang, he put the clerk Kong Qian in charge of land tax and corvée. Kong applied harsh laws to squeeze the populace and heavy exactions to fill the court's coffers; even when civilian wealth was drained dry, army rations still fell short.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the Liang house, he appointed the clerk Kong Qian as commissioner of land tax and corvée; with harsh laws he stripped those below, with heavy exactions he enriched those above, and though the people's wealth was exhausted, military provisions were still deficient.

entries.zh: 加之以兵革，因之以饑饉，不三四年，以致顛隕，其義無他，蓋賦役重而寰區失望故也。
entries.en: War and famine followed, and within three or four years the dynasty collapsed—for no other reason than that taxes and corvée had grown crushing and the empire had lost faith in the regime.
entries.literal: Added to this were warfare and famine; in less than three or four years he came to ruin. The reason was none other than that taxes and corvée were heavy and the whole realm lost hope.

entries.zh: 〈（案：以上見《容齋三筆》所引《薛史》，繹其文義，當系《食貨志序》，今錄於卷首。）〉
entries.en: (Editorial note: The passage above is quoted from the History of Xue in Hong Mai's Third Collection of Rong Studio Notes. By its sense it belongs to the preface of the Treatise on Finance and Economics and is placed here at the opening of the chapter.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: The foregoing appears in the History of Xue as quoted in Hong Mai's Third Collection of Rong Studio Notes. Interpreting its meaning, it should belong to the preface of the Treatise on Food and Commodities; it is now recorded at the head of the scroll.)〉

entries.zh: 顯德元年十二月，世宗謂侍臣曰：「朕覽食末鹽州郡，犯私鹽多於顆鹽界分，蓋卑濕之地，易為刮鹼煎造，豈惟違我榷法，兼又汙我好鹽。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Xiande 1, Emperor Shizong told his attendants: 'I have reviewed the fine-salt prefectures and find private-salt violations exceed those in crystal-salt zones, because low-lying damp lands make it easy to scrape alkali and boil salt. This not only violates our monopoly law but also taints our good salt.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Xiande, Emperor Shizong said to his attendants: 'I have reviewed the prefectures consuming fine salt and find that private-salt violations exceed those in crystal-salt zones, because low-lying damp lands make it easy to scrape alkali and boil salt. This not only violates our monopoly law but also taints our good salt.

entries.zh: 況末鹽煎煉，般運費用倍於顆鹽。
entries.en: Moreover, boiling and transporting fine salt costs twice as much as crystal salt.
entries.literal: Moreover, boiling fine salt costs twice as much to transport as crystal salt.

entries.zh: 今宜分割十餘州，令食顆鹽，不惟輦運省力，兼且少人犯禁。」
entries.en: More than ten prefectures should now be set apart to consume crystal salt—this would save transport labor and reduce violations."
entries.literal: Now more than ten prefectures should be divided off and made to consume crystal salt; this would not only save cart transport labor but also reduce violations.'

entries.zh: 自是曹、宋已西十餘州，皆盡食顆鹽。
entries.en: From this time Cao, Song, and more than ten prefectures to the west all switched entirely to crystal salt.
entries.literal: From this time Cao, Song, and more than ten prefectures to the west all consumed crystal salt entirely.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：顯德二年八月二十四日，宣頭節文：「改立鹽法如後：一、贍國軍堂場務、邢洺州鹽務，應有見垛貯鹽貨處，並煎鹽場竈及應是鹼地，並須四面修置墻塹。
entries.en: (Five Dynasties Essentials: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month of Xiande 2, a memorial edict: 'The revised salt law is as follows: 1. At the Zhan'guo Army hall offices and the Xing and Mo prefecture salt offices, wherever stored salt, salt-boiling fields and furnaces, and alkali lands exist, walls and ditches must be built on all four sides.
entries.literal: (Records of the Five Dynasties: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month of the second year of Xiande, a memorial edict: 'The revised salt law is as follows: 1. At the Zhan'guo Army hall offices and the Xing and Mo prefecture salt offices, wherever stored salt exists, salt-boiling fields and furnaces, and all alkali lands, walls and ditches must be built on all four sides.

entries.zh: 如是地裏遙遠，難為修置墻塹，即作壕籬為規隔。
entries.en: If the land is too remote for walls and ditches, trenches and fences shall serve as barriers.
entries.literal: If the land is remote and walls and ditches are hard to build, trenches and fences shall serve as barriers.

entries.zh: 如是人於壕籬內偷盜，夾帶官鹽，兼於壕籬外煎造鹽貨，便仰收捉，及許諸色人陳告。
entries.en: Anyone who steals within the trench-fence while concealing official salt, or boils salt outside it, shall be arrested, and denunciation by persons of any category is permitted.
entries.literal: If anyone steals within the trench-fence, carrying official salt concealed, or boils salt goods outside the trench-fence, they shall be arrested, and persons of all categories may denounce them.

entries.zh: 所犯不計多少斤兩，並決重杖一頓，處死。
entries.en: Regardless of weight, all receive one heavy beating and execution.
entries.literal: Regardless of how many jin or liang are involved, all receive one heavy beating and are put to death.

entries.zh: 其經歷地分及門司節級人員，並當量罪勘斷。
entries.en: Local officials through whose jurisdiction they passed and gate officers at every level shall all be punished in proportion to their offense.
entries.literal: Local officials through whose jurisdiction they passed and gate officers at every level shall all be punished in proportion to their offense.

entries.zh: 所有捉事、告事人賞錢，一兩以上至一斤，賞錢二十千；
entries.en: Reward money for informants and accusers: from one liang up to one jin, twenty strings;
entries.literal: Reward money for informants and accusers: from one liang up to one jin, reward money of twenty strings;

entries.zh: 一斤已上至十斤，賞錢三十千；
entries.en: from one jin up to ten jin, thirty strings;
entries.literal: from one jin up to ten jin, reward money of thirty strings;

entries.zh: 一十斤已上，賞錢五十千。
entries.en: ten jin or more, fifty strings.
entries.literal: ten jin or more, reward money of fifty strings.

entries.zh: 一、應有不系官中煎鹽處鹼地，並須標識，委本州府差公幹職員與巡檢節級、村保、地主、鄰人，同共巡檢。
entries.en: 1. All alkali lands not under official salt production must be marked; the prefecture shall dispatch duty officers together with patrol officers, village mutual-supervision groups, landowners, and neighbors to patrol jointly.
entries.literal: 1. All alkali lands not under official salt production must be marked; the prefecture shall dispatch duty officers together with patrol officers, village mutual-supervision groups, landowners, and neighbors to patrol jointly.

entries.zh: 若諸色人偷刮鹵地，便仰收捉，及許人陳告。
entries.en: If persons of any category secretly scrape brine lands, they shall be arrested, and denunciation is permitted.
entries.literal: If persons of any category secretly scrape brine lands, they shall be arrested, and denunciation is permitted.

entries.zh: 若勘逐不虛，捉事人每獲一人，賞絹一十匹；
entries.en: If investigation proves true, for each person seized the arresting party receives ten bolts of silk;
entries.literal: If investigation proves true, for each person seized the arresting party receives ten bolts of silk;

entries.zh: 獲二人，賞絹二十匹；
entries.en: for two persons seized, twenty bolts of silk;
entries.literal: for two persons seized, twenty bolts of silk;

entries.zh: 獲三人已上，不計人數，賞絹五十匹。
entries.en: for three or more persons seized, regardless of number, fifty bolts of silk.
entries.literal: for three persons or more seized, regardless of number, fifty bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 刮鹼煎鹽人並知情人，所犯不計多少斤兩，並決重杖一頓，處死。
entries.en: Those who scrape alkali to boil salt and those who knew of it, regardless of weight, all receive one heavy beating and execution.
entries.literal: Those who scrape alkali to boil salt and those who knew of it, regardless of how many jin or liang are involved, all receive one heavy beating and are put to death.

entries.zh: 其刮鹼處地分，並刮鹼人住處巡檢、節級、所由、村保等，各徒二年半，令眾一月，依舊勾當。
entries.en: Patrol officers, local officers, agents, and village mutual-supervision groups at the scraping site and at the scraper's residence each receive two and a half years of penal servitude, one month of public humiliation, and then return to duty.
entries.literal: Patrol officers, local officers, agents, and village mutual-supervision groups at the scraping site and at the scraper's residence each receive two and a half years of penal servitude, public humiliation for one month, and then return to duty as before.
