entries.zh: 刮堿處地主，不切檢校，徒二年，令眾一月。
entries.en: Landowners at the scraping site who failed to inspect diligently receive two years of penal servitude and one month of public humiliation.
entries.literal: Landowners at the scraping site who failed to inspect diligently receive two years of penal servitude and public humiliation for one month.

entries.zh: 一、顆鹽地分界內，有人刮鹼煎煉鹽貨，所犯並依前法。
entries.en: 1. Within crystal-salt territorial boundaries, anyone who scrapes alkali to boil salt is punished under the preceding law.
entries.literal: 1. Within crystal-salt territorial boundaries, anyone who scrapes alkali and boils salt goods is punished under the preceding law.

entries.zh: 一、今緣改價賣鹽，慮有別界分鹽貨遞相侵犯，及將鹽入城，諸色犯鹽人，令下三司，依下項條流科斷；
entries.en: 1. Because salt prices are being changed, lest salt from other zones encroach and salt be brought into cities, all salt violators shall be sentenced by the Three Departments under the following articles;
entries.literal: 1. Because salt prices are being changed, lest salt goods from other zones encroach upon one another and salt be brought into cities, all salt violators are ordered sent down to the Three Departments to be sentenced under the following articles;

entries.zh: 其犯鹽人隨行物色，給與本家，其鹽沒納入官。
entries.en: the violator's traveling goods go to his household; the salt is confiscated to the state.
entries.literal: the violator's traveling goods are given to his household; the salt is confiscated to the state.

entries.zh: 所經歷地分節級人員，並行勘斷。
entries.en: Local officials at every level through whose jurisdiction they passed shall all be investigated and punished.
entries.literal: Local officials at every level through whose jurisdiction they passed shall all be investigated and punished.

entries.zh: 一兩至一斤，決臀杖十五，令眾半月，捉事、告事人賞錢五千；
entries.en: from one liang to one jin: fifteen buttock strokes, half a month of public humiliation, five thousand cash reward for informants and accusers;
entries.literal: from one liang to one jin, fifteen buttock strokes, public humiliation for half a month, reward money of five thousand cash for informants and accusers;

entries.zh: 一斤已上至一十斤，徒一年半，令眾一月，捉事、告事人賞錢七千；
entries.en: from one jin up to ten jin: one and a half years of penal servitude, one month of public humiliation, seven thousand cash reward for informants and accusers;
entries.literal: from one jin up to ten jin, one and a half years of penal servitude, public humiliation for one month, reward money of seven thousand cash for informants and accusers;

entries.zh: 十斤已上，不計多少，徒二年，配發運務役一年，捉事、告事人賞錢十千。
entries.en: ten jin or more, regardless of amount: two years of penal servitude, one year of corvée at transport offices, ten thousand cash reward for informants and accusers.
entries.literal: ten jin or more, regardless of amount, two years of penal servitude, one year of corvée at transport offices, reward money of ten thousand cash for informants and accusers.

entries.zh: 一、諸州府人戶所請蠶鹽，不得於鄉村衷私貨賣，及信團頭、腳戶、縣司、請鹽節級、所由等克折糶賣，如有犯者，依諸色犯鹽例科斷。
entries.en: 1. Silkworm salt allocated to prefectural households may not be privately sold in villages, nor may group leaders, porters, county clerks, salt-allocation officers, or local agents skim and resell it; violators are punished under general salt rules.
entries.literal: 1. Silkworm salt allocated to prefectural households may not be privately sold in villages, nor may group leaders, porters, county clerks, salt-allocation officers, and local agents skim and resell grain; if there are violators, they are punished under the rules for all salt violations.

entries.zh: 一、如有人於河東界將鹽過來，及自家界內有人往彼興販鹽貨，所犯者並處斬。
entries.en: 1. Anyone who brings salt across from the Hedong border, or sells salt from this zone into that border, shall be executed.
entries.literal: 1. If anyone brings salt across from the Hedong border, or anyone within this zone goes there to trade in salt goods, all violators are executed.

entries.zh: 其犯鹽人隨行驢畜資財，並與捉事人充賞。」
entries.en: The violator's donkeys, livestock, and property go to the arresting party as reward.'
entries.literal: The violator's traveling donkeys, livestock, and property all go to the arresting party as reward.'

entries.zh: 「慶州青白榷稅院，元有透稅條流，所有隨行驢畜物色，一半支與捉事人充賞，其餘一半並鹽，並納入官。
entries.en: 'The green-and-white monopoly tax office at Qing Prefecture originally had smuggling articles: half of the traveling donkeys, livestock, and goods go to the arresting party as reward; the rest, together with the salt, goes to the state.
entries.literal: 'The green-and-white monopoly tax office at Qing Prefecture originally had articles on tax evasion: half of the traveling donkeys, livestock, and goods go to the arresting party as reward; the remaining half together with the salt are all turned in to the state.

entries.zh: 欲並且依舊一斗已上至三斗杖七十，三斗已上至五斗徒一年，五斗已上處死。
entries.en: It is desired to retain as before: from one dou up to three dou, seventy staff blows; from three dou up to five dou, one year of penal servitude; five dou or more, execution.
entries.literal: It is desired to retain as before: from one dou up to three dou, seventy staff blows; from three dou up to five dou, one year of penal servitude; five dou or more, put to death.

entries.zh: 安邑、解縣兩池榷鹽院，河府節度使兼判之時申到畫一事件條流等，準敕牒，兩池所出鹽，舊日苦無文榜，如擅將一斤一兩，準元敕條，並處極法。
entries.en: The two pool monopoly salt offices at Anyi and Jie counties—when the Hedong governor concurrently judged, unified case articles were submitted; per edict, salt from the two pools formerly had no posted regulations, and unauthorized removal of even one jin or one liang carries the maximum penalty under the original edict articles.
entries.literal: The two pool monopoly salt offices at Anyi and Jie counties—when the Hedong circuit governor concurrently judged, unified articles on cases were submitted; according to the edict, salt from the two pools formerly had no posted regulations, and unauthorized removal of even one jin or one liang is punished under the original edict articles with the extreme penalty.

entries.zh: 其犯鹽人應有錢物，並與捉事人充賞者。
entries.en: The violator's money and goods go to the arresting party as reward.
entries.literal: The violator's money and goods all go to the arresting party as reward.

entries.zh: 切以兩池禁棘峻阻，不通人行，四面各置場門弓射，分擘鹽池地分居住，並在棘圍裏面，更不別有差遣，只令巡護鹽池。
entries.en: The two pools are strictly fenced with thorns and impassable to travelers; armed guards are posted at field gates on all four sides; residents assigned to salt-pool zones live inside the fence with no other duty but guarding the pools.
entries.literal: Strictly speaking, the two pools are fenced with thorns, steep and impassable to travelers; armed guards are posted at field gates on all four sides; residents assigned to salt-pool zones live inside the thorn enclosure, with no other duty assigned, only guarding the salt pools.

entries.zh: 如此後有人偷盜官鹽一斤一兩出池，其犯鹽人並準元敕條流處分，應有隨行錢物並納入官，其捉事人依下項定支優給。
entries.en: If anyone later steals even one jin or one liang of official salt from the pools, the violator is punished under the original edict articles; traveling money and goods go to the state; the arresting party receives the stipulated generous reward.
entries.literal: If hereafter anyone steals one jin or one liang of official salt out of the pools, the violator is punished under the original edict articles; traveling money and goods are all turned in to the state; the arresting party receives the generous reward stipulated below.

entries.zh: 若是巡檢、弓射、池場門子，自不專切巡察，致有透漏到棘圍外，被別人捉獲，及有糾告，兼同行反告，官中更不坐罪，陳告人亦依捉事人支賞。
entries.en: If patrol officers, archers, or pool gatekeepers fail to inspect diligently and leakage reaches outside the fence where others capture or report the thief, or if colleagues counter-accuse one another, the state does not punish them further; the accuser receives the same reward as an arresting party.
entries.literal: If patrol officers, archers, or pool gatekeepers fail to inspect diligently, allowing leakage outside the thorn enclosure where others capture the thief, or if there is denunciation, and colleagues counter-accuse one another, the government does not punish them further; the accuser also receives reward like an arresting party.

entries.zh: 應有知情偷盜官鹽之人，亦依犯鹽人一例處斷。
entries.en: Anyone knowingly assisting theft of official salt is punished like the salt violator.
entries.literal: All who knowingly assist in stealing official salt are punished like salt violators.

entries.zh: 其不知情關連人，臨時酌情定罪。
entries.en: Unwitting associates are sentenced at discretion on the spot.
entries.literal: Unwitting associates are sentenced at discretion on the spot.

entries.zh: 所有透漏地分弓射及池場門子，如是透漏出鹽一十斤已下，徒一年半。
entries.en: Archers and pool gatekeepers in the leaking zone: if ten jin or less of salt leaked out, one and a half years of penal servitude.
entries.literal: For archers and pool gatekeepers in the leaking zone, if ten jin or less of salt leaked out, one and a half years of penal servitude.

entries.zh: 一十斤已上至二十斤，支賞錢一十千；
entries.en: from ten jin up to twenty jin, reward money of ten thousand cash;
entries.literal: from ten jin up to twenty jin, reward money of ten thousand cash;

entries.zh: 二十斤已上至五十斤，支賞錢二十千；
entries.en: from twenty jin up to fifty jin, reward money of twenty thousand cash;
entries.literal: from twenty jin up to fifty jin, reward money of twenty thousand cash;

entries.zh: 五十斤已上至一百斤，支賞錢三十千；
entries.en: from fifty jin up to one hundred jin, reward money of thirty thousand cash;
entries.literal: from fifty jin up to one hundred jin, reward money of thirty thousand cash;

entries.zh: 一百斤已上，支賞錢五十千。
entries.en: one hundred jin or more, reward money of fifty thousand cash.
entries.literal: one hundred jin or more, reward money of fifty thousand cash.

entries.zh: 前項所定奪到鹽法條流，其應屬州府捉獲抵犯之人，便委本州府檢條流科斷訖申奏，別報省司。
entries.en: Under the salt-law articles established above, offenders caught by prefectures shall be sentenced by the local prefecture under the articles and reported upward; the provincial office shall be separately notified.
entries.literal: For the salt-law articles established above, offenders caught who fall under prefectural jurisdiction shall be sentenced by the local prefecture under the articles and reported upward upon completion; separately notify the provincial office.

entries.zh: 其屬省院捉到犯鹽之人，幹死刑者，即勘情罪申上，候省司指揮。
entries.en: Offenders caught by provincial offices who warrant capital punishment shall have circumstances examined and reported upward pending provincial orders.
entries.literal: Offenders caught by provincial offices who warrant the death penalty shall have circumstances and guilt examined and reported upward, awaiting provincial orders.

entries.zh: 不至極刑者，便委務司準條流決放訖申報。」）〉
entries.en: Those not warranting the maximum penalty shall be sentenced and released by the office under the articles and reported.' )〉
entries.literal: Those not reaching the extreme penalty shall be sentenced and released by the office under the articles and reported upon completion.' )〉

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court approved.
entries.literal: The court approved.

entries.zh: 周顯德二年正月，世宗謂侍臣曰：「轉輸之物，向來皆給斗耗，自晉、漢已來，不與支破。
entries.en: In the first month of Zhou Xiande 2, Emperor Shizong told his attendants: 'For transport goods, allowance for handling loss was always granted; since Jin and Han it has not been paid out.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xiande of Zhou, Emperor Shizong said to his attendants: 'For goods in transport, allowance for handling loss was always granted; since Jin and Han it has not been paid out.

entries.zh: 倉廩所納新物，尚除省耗，況水路所般，豈無損折？
entries.en: New goods stored in granaries still deduct official handling loss—how can water transport suffer no breakage?
entries.literal: New goods received in granaries still deduct official handling loss—how can water transport suffer no breakage?

entries.zh: 起今後每石宜與耗一斗。」
entries.en: Henceforth one dou of allowance per shi shall be granted.'
entries.literal: From now on one dou of allowance per shi should be granted.'

entries.zh: 三年十月，敕：「漳河已北州府管界，元是官場糶鹽，今後除城郭草市內，仍舊禁法，其鄉村並許鹽貨通商。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the third year, an edict: 'In prefectural jurisdictions north of the Zhang River, where salt was formerly sold by official monopoly, the old prohibition remains in force within city walls and grass markets; in villages salt goods may be freely traded.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, an edict: 'In prefectural jurisdictions north of the Zhang River, where salt was formerly sold by official monopoly, hereafter except within city walls and grass markets the old prohibition remains in force; in villages salt goods may be freely traded.

entries.zh: 逐處有鹼鹵之地，一任人戶煎煉，興販則不得逾越漳河，入不通商地界。」
entries.en: Wherever alkali brine lands exist, households may boil freely; trade may not cross the Zhang River into non-trade zones.'
entries.literal: Wherever alkali brine lands exist, households may boil freely; in trade they may not cross the Zhang River into non-trade zones.'

entries.zh: 〈（《文獻通考》：五年，既取江北諸州，唐主奉表入貢，因白帝以江南無鹵田，願得海陵鹽監南屬以贍軍。
entries.en: (Comprehensive Examination of Documents: In the fifth year, after the Jiangbei prefectures were taken, the Tang ruler submitted tribute and told the emperor that Jiangnan had no brine fields and requested the Hailing salt monopoly in the south to support the army.
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Examination of Documents: In the fifth year, after the Jiangbei prefectures were taken, the Tang ruler submitted tribute and told the emperor that Jiangnan had no brine fields and requested that the Hailing salt monopoly be placed under the south to support the army.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「海陵在江北難以交居，當別有處分。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'Hailing is north of the river and difficult to share jointly; separate arrangements will be made.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Hailing is north of the river and difficult to share jointly; separate arrangements will be made.'

entries.zh: 乃詔歲支鹽二十萬斛以給江南，士卒稍稍歸之。）〉
entries.en: An edict was then issued to supply Jiangnan two hundred thousand hu of salt annually; soldiers gradually returned.)〉
entries.literal: An edict was then issued to supply Jiangnan two hundred thousand hu of salt annually; soldiers gradually returned to it.)〉

entries.zh: 食貨志
entries.en: Treatise on Finance and Economics
entries.literal: Treatise on Food and Commodities

entries.zh: 梁太祖開平三年十一月，詔太常卿李燕、御史蕭頃、中書舍人張兗、戶部侍郎崔沂、大理卿王鄯、刑部郎中崔誥，共刪定律令格式。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping, Emperor Taizu of Liang ordered Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan, Censor Xiao Qing, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Minister of Justice Wang Shan, and Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cui Gao to revise the statutes, ordinances, formats, and regulations together.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, an edict ordered Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan, Censor Xiao Qing, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Minister of Justice Wang Shan, and Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cui Gao jointly to revise the statutes, ordinances, formats, and regulations.

entries.zh: 四年十二月，宰臣薛貽矩奏：「太常卿李燕等重刊定律令三十卷，式二十卷，格一十卷，並目錄一十三卷，律疏三十卷，凡五部一十帙，共一百三卷。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Chief Minister Xue Yiju reported: "Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan and his colleagues have newly printed and fixed the statutes in thirty scrolls, formats in twenty, regulations in ten, a table of contents in thirteen, and the statutory commentary in thirty—five parts in ten fascicles, one hundred and three scrolls in all.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Chief Minister Xue Yiju memorialized: "Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Yan and others have newly printed and fixed the statutes in thirty scrolls, the formats in twenty scrolls, the regulations in ten scrolls, together with a table of contents in thirteen scrolls and the commentary on the statutes in thirty scrolls, altogether five parts in ten fascicles, comprising one hundred and three scrolls in all.

entries.zh: 敕中書舍人李仁儉詣閣門奉進，伏請目為《大梁新定格式律令》，仍頒下施行。」
entries.en: We ask that Secretariat Drafter Li Renjian be sent to present them at the Palace Gate, and that they be titled The Newly Fixed Statutes, Ordinances, Formats, and Regulations of Great Liang and promulgated for enforcement."
entries.literal: We request that Secretariat Drafter Li Renjian be ordered to present them at the Palace Gate; we bow and ask that they be titled The Newly Fixed Statutes, Ordinances, Formats, and Regulations of Great Liang, and that they be issued for enforcement."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court approved.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 〈（原註：是時，大理卿李保殷進所撰《刑律總要》十二卷。）〉
entries.en: (Original note: At this time Minister of Justice Li Baoyin presented the twelve-scroll General Essentials of Penal Law that he had compiled.)〉
entries.literal: (Original note: At this time Minister of Justice Li Baoyin presented the General Essentials of Penal Law in twelve scrolls that he had compiled.)〉

entries.zh: 唐莊宗同光元年十二月，御史臺奏：「當司刑部、大理寺本朝法書，自朱溫僭逆，刪改事條，或重貨財，輕入人命，或自徇枉過，濫加刑罰。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tongguang, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang received a memorial from the Censorate: "The law books of our bureau, the Ministry of Justice, and the Court of Judicial Review—ever since Zhu Wen's usurpation—have had their articles revised, sometimes treating property crimes more harshly than loss of life, sometimes indulging personal bias and imposing punishments arbitrarily.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, the Censorate memorialized: "The penal codes of our bureau, the Ministry of Justice, and the Court of Judicial Review in this dynasty's law books—since Zhu Wen's usurpation, article after article was revised, sometimes making property offences heavy and human life light, sometimes indulging personal wrongs and adding punishments at will.

entries.zh: 今見在三司收貯刑書，並是偽廷刪改者，兼偽廷先下諸道追取本朝法書焚毀，或經兵火所遺，皆無舊本節目。
entries.en: The penal codes now in the archives of the three offices are all versions the usurping court had revised; that court had also ordered the circuits to seize and burn our dynasty's law books, and what survived the wars no longer preserves the original section headings.
entries.literal: The penal books now held in storage by the three offices are all versions revised by the usurping court; moreover the usurping court earlier ordered the circuits to seize and burn this dynasty's law books, and those that survived war and fire lack the old section headings.

entries.zh: 只定州敕庫有本朝法書具在，請敕定州節度使速寫副本進納，庶刑法令式，並合本朝舊制。」
entries.en: Only the edict archive at Dingzhou still holds our dynasty's law books intact. We ask that the military governor of Dingzhou be ordered to copy and submit duplicates at once, so that penal statutes, ordinances, and formats may again follow our dynasty's former system."
entries.literal: Only the edict archive of Dingzhou still has this dynasty's law books intact; we request an edict ordering the military governor of Dingzhou speedily to copy and submit duplicates, so that the statutes, ordinances, and formats of penal law may all accord with this dynasty's former system."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court approved.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 未幾，定州王都進納唐朝格式律令，凡二百八十六卷。
entries.en: Soon afterward Wang Du of Dingzhou submitted the Tang regulations, formats, statutes, and ordinances—two hundred and eighty-six scrolls in all.
entries.literal: Before long, Wang Du of Dingzhou submitted the Tang dynasty's regulations, formats, statutes, and ordinances, altogether two hundred and eighty-six scrolls.

entries.zh: 二年二月，刑部尚書盧價奏，纂集《同光刑律統類》凡一十三卷，上之。
entries.en: In the second month of the second year, Minister of Justice Lu Jia reported that he had compiled the thirteen-scroll Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Penal Statutes and submitted them to the throne.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year, Minister of Justice Lu Jia memorialized that he had compiled the Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Penal Statutes in thirteen scrolls and presented them.

entries.zh: 周太祖廣順元年六月，敕侍御史盧億、刑部員外郎曹匪躬、大理正段濤同議定重寫法書一百四十八卷。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the first year of Guangshun, Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered Attending Censor Lu Yi, Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cao Feigong, and Senior Rectifier Duan Tao of the Court of Judicial Review to deliberate together and rewrite the law books in one hundred and forty-eight scrolls.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Guangshun of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, an edict ordered Attending Censor Lu Yi, Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cao Feigong, and Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review Duan Tao jointly to deliberate and rewrite the law books in one hundred and forty-eight scrolls.

entries.zh: 先是，漢隱帝末，因兵亂法書亡失，至是大理奏重寫律令格式、統類編敕，凡改點畫及義理之誤字凡二百一十有四，以晉、漢及國初事關刑法敕條，凡二十六件，分為二卷，附於編敕，目為《大周續編敕》，命省、寺行用焉。
entries.en: Earlier, at the end of the Han reign of Emperor Yin, the law books had been lost in the wars. The Court of Judicial Review now memorialized for a rewrite of the statutes, ordinances, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts, correcting two hundred and fourteen mistaken characters in form or meaning, and gathering twenty-six edict articles on penal law from the Jin and Han periods and the founding of the state into two scrolls appended to the compiled edicts under the title Great Zhou Supplementary Compiled Edicts, with orders for the ministries and courts to put them into use.
entries.literal: Earlier, at the end of Emperor Yin of Han, the law books were lost in the turmoil of war; thereupon the Court of Judicial Review memorialized for the rewriting of statutes, ordinances, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts, correcting in all two hundred and fourteen erroneous characters in strokes and meaning, and taking twenty-six edict articles concerning penal law from Jin, Han, and the opening of the state, divided into two scrolls, appended to the compiled edicts, titled the Great Zhou Supplementary Compiled Edicts, and ordered the ministries and courts to employ them.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史》：盧億，周初為侍御史，漢末兵亂，法書亡失，至是大理奏重寫律令格式、統類編敕，乃詔億與刑部員外曹匪躬、大理正段濤同加議定舊本，以京兆府改同五府，開封、大名府改同河南府，長安、萬年改為次赤縣，開封、浚儀、大名、元城改為赤縣，又定東京諸門薰風等為京城門，明德等為皇城門，啟運等為宮城門，升龍等為宮門，崇元等為殿門，廟諱書不成字，凡改點畫及義理之誤字二百一十有四。
entries.en: (History of Song: Lu Yi served as Attending Censor in early Zhou. At the end of Han the law books were lost in the wars, and when the Court of Judicial Review memorialized for a rewrite of the statutes, ordinances, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts, the court ordered Yi, Vice Director Cao Feigong of the Bureau of Punishments, and Senior Rectifier Duan Tao to revise the old text together. Jingzhao Prefecture was raised to rank with the Five Prefectures; Kaifeng and Daming were made equivalent to Henan Prefecture; Chang'an and Wannian became secondary red counties and Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng became red counties. The gates of the Eastern Capital were classified—Xunfeng and the like as capital-city gates, Mingde as imperial-city gates, Qiyun as palace-city gates, Shenglong as palace gates, and Chongyuan as hall gates. Taboo forms for temple names were written incompletely. In all, two hundred and fourteen mistaken characters in form or meaning were corrected.
entries.literal: (History of Song: Lu Yi, in early Zhou served as Attending Censor; at the end of Han the law books were lost in military disorder; thereupon the Court of Judicial Review memorialized for rewriting statutes, ordinances, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts, and an edict ordered Yi together with Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments Cao Feigong and Senior Rectifier Duan Tao jointly to deliberate on the old text, changing Jingzhao Prefecture to rank with the Five Prefectures, Kaifeng and Daming prefectures to rank with Henan Prefecture, Chang'an and Wannian to secondary red counties, Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng to red counties, and further fixing the gates of the Eastern Capital such as Xunfeng as capital-city gates, Mingde as imperial-city gates, Qiyun as palace-city gates, Shenglong as palace gates, and Chongyuan as hall gates; taboo characters for temple names were written incompletely; altogether two hundred and fourteen erroneous characters in strokes and meaning were corrected.

entries.zh: 又以晉、漢及周初事關刑法敕條者，分為二卷，附編敕，目為《大周續編敕》。
entries.en: Edict articles on penal law from the Jin and Han periods and early Zhou were also divided into two scrolls, appended to the compiled edicts under the title Great Zhou Supplementary Compiled Edicts.
entries.literal: Further, edict articles concerning penal law from Jin, Han, and early Zhou were divided into two scrolls, appended to the compiled edicts, and titled the Great Zhou Supplementary Compiled Edicts.

entries.zh: 詔行之。）〉
entries.en: An edict ordered them promulgated.)〉
entries.literal: An edict ordered them put into effect.)〉

entries.zh: 周廣順三年四月乙亥，敕：「朕以時當化育，氣屬炎蒸，乃思縲紲之人，是軫哀矜之念，慮其非所，案鞫淹延，或枉濫窮屈而未得申宣，或饑渴疾病而無所控告。
entries.en: On the day yihai of the fourth month of the third year of Guangshun, an edict declared: "As the season is for nurturing transformation and the qi belongs to blazing heat, We think of those in fetters and are moved by compassionate concern. We fear that they are not in their proper place, that case examination is delayed, that some wrongfully oppressed cannot make their grievance known, or that hunger, thirst, and illness leave them with no means of appeal.
entries.literal: On the day yihai of the fourth month of the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, an edict stated: "We, as the season is for nurturing transformation and the qi belongs to blazing heat, think of those in fetters and bonds and are moved by compassionate concern, fearing that they are not in their proper place, that case examination is delayed, that some wrongfully oppressed and exhausted cannot make their grievance known, or that hunger, thirst, and illness leave them with no means of appeal.

entries.zh: 以罪當刑者，惟彼自召，法不可移；
entries.en: Those whose crime deserves punishment have only themselves to blame; the law cannot be shifted;
entries.literal: Those whose crime deserves punishment have only themselves to blame; the law cannot be shifted;

entries.zh: 非理受苦者，為上不明，安得無慮。
entries.en: but those who suffer without reason do so because the ruler above is not clear—how can We not be concerned?
entries.literal: those who suffer without reason do so because the ruler above is not clear—how can we not be concerned?

entries.zh: 欽恤之道，夙宵靡寧。
entries.en: The way of compassionate rule leaves Us uneasy from early morning to late night.
entries.literal: The way of reverent compassion leaves us uneasy from early morning to late night.

entries.zh: 應諸道州府見系罪人，宜令官吏疾速推鞫，據輕斷遣，不得淹滯。
entries.en: All offenders now detained in every circuit are to be investigated at once by officials, sentenced according to severity, and released without delay.
entries.literal: All offenders now detained in the prefectures of all circuits should be ordered by officials to investigate speedily, sentence according to severity, and release them, without delay.

entries.zh: 仍令獄吏，灑掃牢獄，當令虛歇；
entries.en: Prison officers are further ordered to clean the prisons and keep them properly vacant;
entries.literal: Prison officers are further ordered to sprinkle and sweep the prisons and keep them properly vacant;

entries.zh: 洗滌枷械，無令蚤虱；
entries.en: wash the cangues and fetters and permit no fleas or lice;
entries.literal: wash the cangues and fetters and do not permit fleas and lice;

entries.zh: 供給水漿，無令饑渴。
entries.en: supply water and drink and permit no hunger or thirst.
entries.literal: supply water and drink and do not permit hunger or thirst.

entries.zh: 如有疾患，令其家人看承，囚人無主，官差醫工診候，勿致病亡。
entries.en: If prisoners fall ill, their families are to attend them; for those without kin, official physicians are to examine them, and death from disease is not permitted.
entries.literal: If there is illness, order their families to attend them; for prisoners without kin, assign physicians to examine them and do not permit death from disease.

entries.zh: 循典法之成規，順長嬴之時令，俾無淹滯，以致治平。」
entries.en: Following the established regulations of the canonical law and conforming to the seasonal order of full summer, cause there to be no delay, thereby achieving ordered peace."
entries.literal: Following the established regulations of the canonical law and conforming to the seasonal order of full summer, cause there to be no delay and detention, thereby achieving ordered peace."

entries.zh: 又，賜諸州詔曰：「朕以敷政之勤，惟刑是重，既未能化人於無罪，則不可為上而失刑。
entries.en: Further, edicts were sent to the prefectures: "In the diligence of governing, We hold punishment supremely weighty. Having been unable to transform all people into innocence, We cannot as ruler fail to apply the law.
entries.literal: Further, edicts were granted to the prefectures stating: "We, in the diligence of spreading government, hold punishment supremely weighty; having been unable to transform people into innocence, we cannot as ruler above fail to apply punishment.

entries.zh: 況時當長嬴，事貴清適，念囹圄之閉固，復桎梏之拘縻，處於炎蒸，何異焚灼。
entries.en: Moreover, the season is full summer, when clarity and ease are prized. To think of prisons shut fast and shackles binding prisoners in blazing heat is no different from burning them.
entries.literal: Moreover, the season is full summer, when affairs value clarity and ease; thinking of the closed solidity of prisons and again the binding restraint of shackles, to be placed in blazing heat is no different from being burned.

entries.zh: 在州及所屬刑獄見系罪人，卿可躬親錄問，省略區分。
entries.en: For offenders now detained in your prefecture and its subordinate prisons, you may question them in person and abbreviate procedural distinctions.
entries.literal: Offenders now detained in the prefecture and its subordinate prisons—you may personally record and question them and abbreviate distinctions.

entries.zh: 於入務不行者，令俟務開系；
entries.en: Those for whom proceedings cannot proceed during court recess are to await reopening of court;
entries.literal: Those for whom proceedings cannot proceed during court recess are to await reopening of court;

entries.zh: 有理須伸者，速期疏決。
entries.en: those with merit requiring redress are to be tried and released at once.
entries.literal: those with merit requiring redress should speedily be tried and released.

entries.zh: 俾皆平允，無至滯淹。
entries.en: Thus all cases are to be fair and even, without delay.
entries.literal: Thus causing all to be fair and even, without reaching delay and detention.

entries.zh: 又以獄吏逞任情之奸，囚人被非法之苦，宜加檢察，勿縱侵欺。
entries.en: Because prison officers indulge wilful wrongdoing and prisoners suffer unlawful hardship, inspection should be increased and oppression must not be indulged.
entries.literal: Further, because prison officers indulge wilful wrongdoing and prisoners suffer unlawful hardship, inspection should be increased and oppression must not be indulged.

entries.zh: 常令凈掃獄房，洗刷枷匣，知其饑渴，供與水漿，有病者聽骨肉看承，無主者遣醫工救療，勿令非理致斃，以致和氣有傷。
entries.en: Prison rooms are to be kept swept clean and cangues washed; hunger and thirst are to be relieved with water and drink. The ill may be attended by kin; those without kin are to be treated by physicians. Unlawful death that harms harmonious qi is not permitted.
entries.literal: Constantly order the prison rooms swept clean, cangues and cases washed, know their hunger and thirst and supply water and drink; when ill, permit kin to attend; when without kin, send physicians to treat them; do not permit unlawful death that harms harmonious qi.

entries.zh: 卿忠幹分憂，仁明蒞事，必能奉詔，體我用心，眷委於茲，興寐無已。
entries.en: You are loyal and capable in sharing Our cares and benevolent and clear in office—you will surely obey the edict and embody Our intent. In entrusting this commission to you, We think of it waking and sleeping without end.
entries.literal: You are loyal and capable in sharing our cares, benevolent and clear in attending to affairs—you will surely be able to obey the edict, embody our intent, and in this commission entrusted to you, we think of it waking and sleeping without end.

entries.zh: 余從敕命處分。」
entries.en: Act according to the edict."
entries.literal: Act according to the edict's disposition."

entries.zh: 世宗顯德四年五月，中書門下奏：「準宣，法書行用多時，文意古質，條目繁細，使人難會，兼前後敕格，互換重疊，亦難詳定。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Xiande, Emperor Shizong received a memorial from the Secretariat: "As the throne has directed, the law books have been in force for many years. Their language is archaic and their articles minute and numerous, so that readers struggle to grasp them; edicts and regulations from different periods also overlap and repeat, making reliable application difficult.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Xiande of Emperor Shizong, the Secretariat memorialized: "According to the imperial pronouncement, the law books have been in use for a long time; their language is archaic and their articles numerous and minute, making them hard to understand; moreover edicts and regulations before and after overlap and duplicate one another, and are also hard to fix with certainty.

entries.zh: 宜令中書門下並重刪定，務從節要，所貴天下易為詳究者。
entries.en: The Secretariat should be ordered to revise them again, aiming for brevity and essentials so that the whole realm can study and apply them with ease.
entries.literal: It is fitting to order the Secretariat again to revise them, striving for brevity and essentials, so that throughout the realm they may easily be studied in detail.

entries.zh: 伏以刑法者御人之銜勒，救弊之斧斤，故鞭撲不可一日弛之於家，刑法不可一日廢之於國，雖堯、舜淳古之代，亦不能舍此而致理矣。
entries.en: Penal law is the bridle by which people are governed and the tool by which abuses are cut away. Flogging cannot be relaxed for a day in the household, nor penal law abandoned for a day in the state—even the pure antiquity of Yao and Shun could not achieve good order without it.
entries.literal: We submit that penal law is the bridle by which people are governed and the axe by which abuses are remedied; therefore flogging cannot for a single day be relaxed in the household, nor penal law for a single day be abandoned in the state—even in the pure antiquity of Yao and Shun one could not discard this and achieve good order.

entries.zh: 今奉制旨刪定律令，有以見聖君欽恤明罰敕法之意也。
entries.en: In obeying the imperial order to revise the statutes and ordinances, we see the sage ruler's intent to temper punishment with compassion and to make the law clear.
entries.literal: Now in receiving the imperial order to revise statutes and ordinances, one may see the sage ruler's intent of reverent compassion, clear punishment, and instructing the law.

entries.zh: 竊以律令之書，政理之本，經聖賢之損益，為古今之章程，歷代以來，謂之彜典。
entries.en: Books of statutes and ordinances are the foundation of government. Revised by sages through the ages, they form the enduring institutions of past and present and have long been regarded as the constant canon.
entries.literal: We venture to consider that books of statutes and ordinances are the root of government and order, having passed through the additions and subtractions of sages, serving as institutions for past and present; through successive ages they have been called the constant canon.

entries.zh: 今朝廷之所行用者律一十二卷、律疏三十卷、式二十卷、令三十卷、《開成格》一十卷、《大中統類》一十二卷、後唐以來至漢末編敕三十二卷及皇朝制敕等。
entries.en: The court now applies twelve scrolls of statutes, thirty of statutory commentary, twenty of formats, thirty of ordinances, ten of the Kaicheng Regulations, twelve of the Dazhong Comprehensive Categories, thirty-two scrolls of compiled edicts from Later Tang through the end of Han, and the regulatory edicts of the present dynasty.
entries.literal: What the court now employs are twelve scrolls of statutes, thirty scrolls of statutory commentary, twenty scrolls of formats, thirty scrolls of ordinances, ten scrolls of the Kaicheng Regulations, twelve scrolls of the Dazhong Comprehensive Categories, thirty-two scrolls of compiled edicts from Later Tang down to the end of Han, and the present dynasty's regulatory edicts, and so forth.

entries.zh: 折獄定刑，無出於此。
entries.en: Nothing lies outside these books when cases are decided and punishments fixed.
entries.literal: In deciding cases and fixing punishments, nothing lies outside these.

entries.zh: 律令則文辭古質，看覽者難以詳明；
entries.en: The statutes and ordinances are couched in archaic language that readers struggle to master;
entries.literal: Statutes and ordinances have archaic language, and those who read them find it hard to understand them fully;

entries.zh: 格敕則條目繁多，檢閱者或有疑誤。
entries.en: the regulations and edicts are so numerous that those who consult them may easily go astray.
entries.literal: regulations and edicts have numerous articles, and those who consult them may harbor doubt or error.

entries.zh: 加之邊遠之地，貪猾之徒，緣此為奸，浸以成弊。
entries.en: In remote regions, moreover, the greedy and cunning exploit the confusion to commit abuses that gradually become entrenched.
entries.literal: Added to this, in remote regions greedy and cunning persons take advantage of this to commit wrongdoing, and the abuse gradually becomes entrenched.

entries.zh: 方屬盛明之運，宜伸畫一之規，所冀民不陷刑，吏知所守。
entries.en: In this flourishing age it is fitting to enforce a single uniform rule, so that the people do not fall into punishment through ignorance and officials know what to uphold.
entries.literal: Now that we belong to an era of flourishing brilliance, it is fitting to extend a uniform rule, in the hope that the people will not fall into punishment and officials will know what to uphold.

entries.zh: 臣等商量，望準聖旨施行，仍差侍御史知雜事張湜、太子右庶子劇可久、殿中侍御史率汀、職方郎中鄧守中、倉部郎中王瑩、司封員外郎賈比、太常博士趙礪、國子博士李光贊、大理正蘇曉、太子中允王伸等一十人，編集新格，勒成部帙。
entries.en: We have deliberated and ask to carry out the imperial will by assigning Attending Censor Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyou, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Director Deng Shouzhong of the Bureau of Appointments, Director Wang Ying of the Bureau of Granaries, Vice Director Jia Bi of the Bureau of Seals, Erudite Zhao Li of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Erudite Li Guangzan of the Directorate of Education, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, Junior Mentor Wang Shen—ten men in all—to compile new regulations and bind them into fascicles.
entries.literal: Your subjects have deliberated and ask to carry out the sage edict, and further request that Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyou, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Director of the Bureau of Appointments Deng Shouzhong, Director of the Bureau of Granaries Wang Ying, Vice Director of the Bureau of Seals Jia Bi, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Li, Erudite of the Directorate of Education Li Guangzan, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, and Junior Mentor Wang Shen—ten men in all—be assigned to compile new regulations and bind them into fascicles.

entries.zh: 律令之有難解者，就文訓釋；
entries.en: Where statutes and ordinances are obscure, they should be glossed in the text itself;
entries.literal: Where statutes and ordinances are hard to understand, gloss them according to the text;

entries.zh: 格敕之有繁雜者，隨事刪除。
entries.en: where regulations and edicts are redundant, articles should be cut as the subject requires.
entries.literal: where regulations and edicts are redundant, delete them according to the matter.

entries.zh: 止要諧理省文，兼且直書易會。
entries.en: The aim is coherent reasoning and concise language, written plainly so that readers can grasp it at once.
entries.literal: We need only harmonize reason and economize language, and moreover write plainly so that they are easy to grasp.

entries.zh: 其中有輕重未當，便於古而不便於今，矛盾相違，可於此而不可於彼，盡宜改正，無或牽拘。
entries.en: Where penalties are ill matched, what suited antiquity no longer suits the present, or provisions contradict one another, everything should be corrected without undue constraint.
entries.literal: Among them, where severity and leniency are inappropriate, what suited antiquity does not suit the present, or provisions contradict and conflict, what applies here does not apply there—all should be corrected without being bound by constraint.

entries.zh: 候編集畢日，委御史臺、尚書省四品以上及兩省五品以上官參詳可否，送中書門下議定，奏取進止。」
entries.en: When the compilation is finished, officials of the fourth rank and above in the Censorate and Department of State Affairs and of the fifth rank and above in the Two Departments should review it, the Secretariat should deliberate and fix the text, and a memorial should be submitted for the throne's decision."
entries.literal: When compilation is finished, commission officials of the fourth rank and above in the Censorate and Department of State Affairs and of the fifth rank and above in the Two Departments to examine whether it is feasible, send it to the Secretariat for deliberation and fixation, and memorialize for imperial decision."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict approved the proposal.
entries.literal: An edict approved.

entries.zh: 自是湜等於都省集議刪定，仍令大官供膳。
entries.en: Thereafter Chi and his colleagues met at the capital offices to revise the code, and the Court of Imperial Entertainments was ordered to supply their meals.
entries.literal: Thereafter Chi and the others met at the capital offices to deliberate and revise, and the Court of Imperial Entertainments was ordered to provide meals.

entries.zh: 顯德元年十一月，帝謂侍臣曰：「天下所奏獄訟，多追引證，甚致淹延，有及百餘日而未決者。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the first year of Xiande, the emperor said to his attendants: "Of lawsuits reported throughout the realm, many require pursuing collateral witnesses and testimony, causing serious delays, with some cases unresolved for more than a hundred days.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Xiande, the emperor said to his attendants: "Of lawsuits reported throughout the realm, many require pursuing collateral witnesses and testimony, causing serious delay, with some cases unresolved for more than a hundred days.

entries.zh: 其中有徒黨反告者，劫主陳訴者及妄遭牽引者，慮獄吏作幸遲留，致生人休廢活業，朕每念此，彌切疚懷。
entries.en: Among them are cases where accomplices lodge counter-accusations, robbery victims bring complaints, and persons are wrongly implicated. I fear prison officers deliberately delay proceedings, causing people to abandon their livelihoods. Whenever I think of this, my guilt grows ever keener.
entries.literal: Among them are cases where accomplices lodge counter-accusations, victims robbed bring complaints, and persons are wrongly implicated—I fear prison officers deliberately delay proceedings, causing people to abandon their livelihoods. Whenever I think of this, my sense of guilt grows ever keener.

entries.zh: 此後宜條貫所在藩郡，令選明幹僚吏，當其訴訟。
entries.en: Henceforth regulations should be drawn up in each feudatory commandery, ordering the selection of capable and competent subordinate officials to handle their lawsuits.
entries.literal: Henceforth regulations should be drawn up in each feudatory commandery, ordering the selection of capable and competent subordinate officials to handle their lawsuits.

entries.zh: 如獄不滯留，人無枉撓，明具聞奏，量與甄獎。」
entries.en: If cases are not detained and no one is wrongfully abused, report this clearly in memorial and grant rewards in appropriate measure."
entries.literal: If cases are not detained and no one is wrongfully abused, report this clearly in memorial and grant rewards in appropriate measure."

entries.zh: 五年七月，中書門下奏：「侍御史知雜事張湜等九人，奉詔編集刑書，悉有條貫，兵部尚書張昭等一十人，參詳旨要，更加損益。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the Secretariat reported: "Attending Censor Zhang Chi and eight others, acting on the imperial edict to compile the penal code, have brought every article into systematic order; Minister of War Zhang Zhao and nine others have reviewed the essentials and made further revisions.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the Secretariat memorialized: "Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters Zhang Chi and eight others, receiving the edict to compile the penal books, have arranged them all in systematic order; Minister of War Zhang Zhao and nine others have examined the essential points and further added revisions.

entries.zh: 臣質、臣溥據文評議，備見精審。
entries.en: Your subjects Zhi and Pu have examined the text and find the work throughout refined and thorough.
entries.literal: Your subjects Zhi and Pu have judged by the text and find it throughout refined and thorough.

entries.zh: 其所編集者，用律為正；
entries.en: The compilation takes the statutes as its standard;
entries.literal: What they have compiled takes the statutes as the standard;

entries.zh: 辭旨之有難解者，釋以疏意；
entries.en: where the wording is obscure, it is explained by the commentary;
entries.literal: where the wording is hard to understand, it is explained by the sense of the commentary;

entries.zh: 義理之有易了者，略其疏文。
entries.en: where the meaning is plain, the commentary is abbreviated.
entries.literal: where the meaning is easy to grasp, the commentary text is abbreviated.

entries.zh: 式令之有附近者次之，格敕之有廢置者又次之。
entries.en: Relevant formats and ordinances follow next, then regulations and edicts that have been abolished or set aside.
entries.literal: Formats and ordinances that are relevant come next; regulations and edicts that have been abolished or set aside come after that.

entries.zh: 事有不便於今、該說未盡者，別立新條於本條之下；
entries.en: Where present conditions make an article inconvenient or the explanation is incomplete, new articles are added beneath the original;
entries.literal: Matters inconvenient for the present or not fully covered in explanation have new articles set up beneath the original article;

entries.zh: 其有文理深古、慮人疑惑者，別以朱字訓釋。
entries.en: where the language is profoundly archaic and likely to perplex readers, glosses in red characters are supplied.
entries.literal: where the language is profoundly archaic and readers might be perplexed, separate glosses in red characters are provided.

entries.zh: 至於朝廷之禁令，州縣之常科，各以類分，悉令編附。
entries.en: Court prohibitions and the standing statutes of prefectures and counties are each classified by type and all appended to the compilation.
entries.literal: As for court prohibitions and the standing statutes of prefectures and counties, each is classified by category and all are ordered compiled and appended.

entries.zh: 所冀發函展卷，綱目無遺，究本討源，刑政咸在。
entries.en: The hope is that on opening the case and unrolling the scrolls, no heading is missing and the whole of penal administration, traced to its roots, lies within.
entries.literal: The hope is that on opening the case and unrolling the scrolls, no heading or item is missing, and tracing root and source, all penal administration is contained therein.

entries.zh: 其所編集，勒成一部，別有目錄，凡二十一卷。
entries.en: The compilation is bound as one work with a separate table of contents, twenty-one scrolls in all.
entries.literal: What they have compiled is bound into one work, with a separate table of contents, twenty-one scrolls in all.

entries.zh: 刑名之要，盡統於茲，目之為《大周刑統》，欲請頒行天下，與律疏令式通行。
entries.en: The essentials of penal nomenclature are all gathered here under the title Great Zhou Penal Compendium. We ask that it be promulgated throughout the realm and applied together with the statutes, commentary, ordinances, and formats.
entries.literal: The essentials of penal nomenclature are all gathered here; it is titled the Great Zhou Penal Compendium; we wish to request that it be promulgated throughout the realm and applied together with the statutes, commentary, ordinances, and formats.

entries.zh: 其《刑法統類》、《開成格》、編敕等，采掇既盡，不在法司行使之限，自來有宣命指揮公事及三司臨時條法，州縣見今施行，不在編集之數。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Categories of Penal Law, the Kaicheng Regulations, compiled edicts, and the like have been fully drawn upon and lie outside what the judicial offices enforce on their own. Imperial orders on official business and provisional regulations of the three offices that prefectures and counties now apply are not included in the compilation.
entries.literal: The Comprehensive Categories of Penal Law, the Kaicheng Regulations, compiled edicts, and the like, having been fully drawn upon, lie outside the scope of what the judicial offices may enforce; as for imperial orders directing official business and provisional regulations of the three offices that prefectures and counties are now applying, they are not included in the compilation.

entries.zh: 應該京百司公事，逐司各有見行條件，望令本司刪集，送中書門下詳議聞奏。」
entries.en: Each capital office has regulations now in force for its own affairs; we ask that each office revise and compile them and submit them to the Secretariat for deliberation and report to the throne."
entries.literal: As for the official business of the hundred offices of the capital, each office has its own regulations now in force; we hope each office may be ordered to revise and compile them and send them to the Secretariat for detailed deliberation and report."

entries.zh: 敕宜依，仍頒行天下。
entries.en: The edict approved the proposal, and the work was promulgated throughout the realm.
entries.literal: An edict approved, and it was further promulgated throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 乃賜侍御史知雜事張湜等九人各銀器二十兩，雜彩三十匹，賞刪定《刑統》之勞也。
entries.en: Zhang Chi and the eight other compilers were each rewarded with twenty taels of silver vessels and thirty bolts of mixed silks for their labor in revising the Penal Compendium.
entries.literal: Thereupon Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters Zhang Chi and eight others were each granted twenty taels of silver vessels and thirty bolts of mixed silks, rewarding their labor in revising the Penal Compendium.

entries.zh: 刑法志
entries.en: Treatise on Punishment and Law
entries.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law

entries.zh: 〈（案：《刑法志序》，《永樂大典》原闕。）〉
entries.en: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Punishment and Law was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Punishment and Law was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.)〉

entries.zh: 梁開平三年三月，詔升尚書令為正一品。
entries.en: In the third month of Kaiping 3 of Liang, an edict raised the Director of the Department of State Affairs to first rank, upper grade.
entries.literal: In the third month of Kaiping 3 of Liang, an edict promoted the Director of the Department of State Affairs to the first rank, upper grade.

entries.zh: 按《唐六典》，尚書令正二品，是時以將授趙州王镕此官，故升之。
entries.en: Under the Tang Six Institutions the Director of the Department of State Affairs had been second rank, upper grade; the rank was raised because the post was about to be conferred on Wang Rong, military governor of Zhao.
entries.literal: According to the Tang Six Institutions, the Director of the Department of State Affairs was second rank, upper grade; at this time the office was about to be granted to Wang Rong of Zhao prefecture, so it was raised.

entries.zh: 職官誌
entries.en: Treatise on Official Posts
entries.literal: Treatise on Official Posts

entries.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝諱綱，字世纘，小字六通，高祖第三子，昭明太子母弟也。
entries.en: Taizong Emperor Jianwen, personal name Gang, courtesy name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong, was Gaozu's third son and Zhaoming Crown Prince's younger brother by the same mother.
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor Jianwen was tabooed Gang, style name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong; he was the third son of the Gaozu and a uterine younger brother of Crown Prince Zhaoming.

entries.zh: 天監二年十月丁未，生於顯陽殿。
entries.en: On dingwei in the tenth month of Tianjian 2 he was born in Xianyang Hall.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, day dingwei, year 2 of Tianjian, he was born in Xianyang Hall.

entries.zh: 五年，封晉安王，食邑八千戶。
entries.en: In year 5 he was made Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.
entries.literal: In year 5 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an with a fief of eight thousand households.

entries.zh: 八年，為雲麾將軍，領石頭戍軍事，量置佐吏。
entries.en: In year 8 he became General of the Cloud Banner, took charge of Shitou garrison affairs, and had aides appointed as required.
entries.literal: In year 8 he was made General of the Cloud Banner, supervising military affairs at the Shitou garrison, with assistant officials appointed as needed.

entries.zh: 九年，遷使持節、都督南北兗青徐冀五州諸軍事、宣毅將軍、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: In year 9 he was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the five Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji provinces, General Who Proclaims Resolution, and South Yanzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In year 9 he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the five provinces North and South Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji, made General Who Proclaims Resolution and South Yanzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 十二年，入為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: In year 12 he entered court as General Who Proclaims Grace and intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: In year 12 he entered the capital as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 十三年，出為使持節、都督荊雍梁南北秦益寧七州諸軍事、南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Jing, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, Yi, and Ning, Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, and Jingzhou inspector, retaining his generalship.
entries.literal: In year 13 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Jing, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Yi, and Ning, made Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and Jingzhou Inspector, his generalship unchanged.

entries.zh: 十四年，徙為都督江州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、江州刺史，持節如故。
entries.en: In year 14 he was reassigned commander of Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner, and Jiangzhou inspector, still Bearer of the Staff.
entries.literal: In year 14 he was reassigned as Commander over military affairs in Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Banner and Jiangzhou Inspector, Bearer of the Staff unchanged.

entries.zh: 十七年，徵為西中郎將、領石頭戍軍事，尋復為宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，加侍中。
entries.en: In year 17 he was recalled as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West with Shitou garrison duties, then again General Who Proclaims Grace and Danyang intendant, with Palace Attendant added.
entries.literal: In year 17 he was summoned as Leader of the Palace Gentlemen of the West, supervising the Shitou garrison; soon restored as General Who Proclaims Grace and Intendant of Danyang, additionally made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 普通元年，出為使持節、都督益寧雍梁南北秦沙七州諸軍事、益州刺史；
entries.en: In Putong 1 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and Sha, and Yi province inspector;
entries.literal: In year 1 of Putong he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in the seven provinces Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, and Sha, and made Yi Province Inspector;

entries.zh: 未拜，改授雲麾將軍、南徐州刺史。
entries.en: before taking office he was reassigned General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou inspector.
entries.literal: before assuming the post, he was reassigned as General of the Cloud Banner and South Xuzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 四年，徙為使持節、都督雍梁、南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事，平西將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
entries.en: In year 4 he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, the two Qin, and related districts, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In year 4 he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in Yong and Liang, North and South Qin, the four provinces, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Su commandery, made General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of Pacified Barbarians, and Yongzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 五年，進號安北將軍。
entries.en: In year 5 he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: In year 5 he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 七年，權進都督荊、益、南梁三州諸軍事。
entries.en: In year 7 he was provisionally made commander of Jing, Yi, and South Liang.
entries.literal: In year 7 he was provisionally advanced as Commander over military affairs in Jing, Yi, and South Liang.

entries.zh: 是歲，丁所生穆貴嬪喪，上表陳解，詔還攝本任。
entries.en: That year, when his birth mother Honored Consort Mu died, he asked to resign but was ordered back to his post.
entries.literal: That year, on mourning for his birth mother Honored Consort Mu, he submitted a memorial requesting release; an edict ordered him to resume his original duties.

entries.zh: 中大通元年，詔依先給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: In Zhongdatong 1 an edict granted him the usual suite of drums and pipes.
entries.literal: In year 1 of Zhongdatong an edict granted him one suite of drums and pipes as before.

entries.zh: 二年，徵為都督南揚、徐二州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史。
entries.en: In year 2 he was recalled as commander of South Yang and Xu, General of Agile Cavalry, and Yangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: In year 2 he was summoned as Commander over military affairs in South Yang and Xu, made General of Agile Cavalry and Yangzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 三年四月乙巳，昭明太子薨。
entries.en: On yisi in the fourth month of year 3 Crown Prince Zhaoming died.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, day yisi, year 3, Crown Prince Zhaoming died.

entries.zh: 五月丙申，詔曰：「非至公無以主天下，非博愛無以臨四海。
entries.en: On bingshen in the fifth month an edict said, "Without utmost fairness one cannot hold the realm; without universal love one cannot govern the four seas.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, day bingshen, an edict said: "Without utmost fairness one cannot rule all under Heaven; without universal love one cannot oversee the four seas.

entries.zh: 所以堯舜克讓，惟德是與；
entries.en: Therefore Yao and Shun yielded the throne, giving it only to the virtuous;
entries.literal: Therefore Yao and Shun could yield, bestowing office only on virtue;

entries.zh: 文王舍伯邑考而立武王，格于上下，光于四表。
entries.en: King Wen passed over Bo Yi Kao and installed King Wu, harmonizing above and below and shining across the four quarters.
entries.literal: King Wen set aside Bo Yi Kao and established King Wu, reaching above and below, shining to the four quarters.

entries.zh: 今岱宗牢落，天步艱難，淳風猶鬱，黎民未乂，自非克明克哲，允武允文，豈能荷神器之重，嗣龍圖之尊。
entries.en: Now the sacred mountain is empty and the heavenly steps are hard; pure custom is still troubled and the people unrested—without brightness, wisdom, martial merit, and culture, who could bear the sacred regalia and succeed to the dragon throne?
entries.literal: Now Mount Tai stands desolate and the heavenly course is hard; pure custom still is troubled and the people are not settled—unless one is bright and wise, truly martial and cultured, how could one bear the weight of the sacred vessel and inherit the dragon throne?

entries.zh: 晉安王綱，文義生知，孝敬自然，威惠外宣，德行內敏，羣后歸美，率土宅心。
entries.en: Prince Gang of Jin'an was gifted in letters and principles, naturally filial and respectful, his authority and kindness known abroad and his virtue keen within; the lords praised him and the realm took him to heart.
entries.literal: Prince of Jin'an Gang, gifted in letters and right by nature, filial and respectful by instinct, his authority and kindness proclaimed abroad and virtue and conduct keen within, the feudal lords admired him and all the land took him to heart.

entries.zh: 可立為皇太子。」
entries.en: He is to be established as crown prince."
entries.literal: He may be established as crown prince."

entries.zh: 七月乙亥，臨軒策拜，以脩繕東宮，權居東府。
entries.en: On yihai in the seventh month he was invested at the throne hall; while the Eastern Palace was repaired he lodged temporarily at the Eastern Mansion.
entries.literal: On yihai in the seventh month, the enthronement ceremony was held at the imperial hall; because the Eastern Palace was under repair, he temporarily resided at the Eastern Mansion.

entries.zh: 四年九月，移還東宮。
entries.en: In the ninth month of year 4 he returned to the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of year 4 he moved back to the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 太清三年五月丙辰，高祖崩。
entries.en: On bingchen in the fifth month of Taiqing 3 Gaozu died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, day bingchen, year 3 of Taiqing, the Gaozu died.

entries.zh: 辛巳，卽皇帝位。
entries.en: On xinsi he took the throne.
entries.literal: On xinsi he ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕以不造，夙丁閔凶。
entries.en: An edict said, "Ill-fated as I am, I have long borne this grief.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Our lack of fortune afflicts us; from early we suffered this calamity.

entries.zh: 大行皇帝奄棄萬國，攀慕號躃，厝身靡所。
entries.en: The late emperor has suddenly left the myriad realms; in longing and wailing I have nowhere to set myself.
entries.literal: The late emperor suddenly abandoned the myriad realms; we cling and wail and have nowhere to place ourselves.

entries.zh: 猥以寡德，越居民上，煢煢在疚，罔知所託，方賴籓輔，社稷用安。
entries.en: With slight virtue I have undeservedly risen above the people; alone in grief I know not whom to trust, and must rely on the feudatories to keep the altars secure.
entries.literal: Unworthily with slight virtue we have crossed above the people; alone in anguish we know not where to lean, yet rely on the feudal helpers that the altars may be secure.

entries.zh: 謹遵先旨，顧命遺澤，宜加億兆。
entries.en: Respectfully following the prior command and the grace of the deathbed charge, the hundred millions should receive added benefit.
entries.literal: Respectfully following the prior will and the bequeathed grace of the final charge, benefit should be added for the hundred millions.

entries.zh: 可大赦天下。」
entries.en: A general amnesty is proclaimed for the empire."
entries.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed for the empire."

entries.zh: 壬午，詔曰：「育物惟寬，馭民惟惠，道著興王，本非隸役。
entries.en: On renwu an edict said, "In nurturing things be broad; in governing the people be kind—the Way of founding kings was never meant for servitude.
entries.literal: On renwu an edict said: "In nourishing creatures be only broad; in governing the people be only kind—the Way that marks a founding king was never bondage in origin.

entries.zh: 或開奉國，便致擒虜，或在邊疆，濫被抄劫。
entries.en: Some who opened their gates in loyalty were seized at once; some on the borders were wantonly raided.
entries.literal: Some opened their gates to serve the state and at once were taken captive; some on the frontiers were wantonly plundered in raids.

entries.zh: 二邦是競，黎元何罪！
entries.en: Two states contend—what crime have the common people!
entries.literal: Two realms contend—what crime have the common people!

entries.zh: 朕以寡昧，創承鴻業，旣臨率土，化行宇宙，豈欲使彼獨為匪民。
entries.en: I, slight and dull, have newly received the great enterprise; now that I rule all within the seas and my transforming influence fills the cosmos, how could I wish them alone to be outcasts?
entries.literal: We, slight and dull, newly inherit the great enterprise; having come to rule all within the four seas and spread transformation through the cosmos, how could we wish them alone to be outlaws?

entries.zh: 諸州見在北人為奴婢者，並及妻兒，悉可原放。」
entries.en: Northerners now held as slaves and maidservants in the provinces, with wives and children, may all be released."
entries.literal: Northerners now held as slaves and maidservants in the various provinces, together with wives and children, may all be released and forgiven."

entries.zh: 癸未，追諡妃王氏為簡皇后。
entries.en: On guiwei Consort Wang was posthumously titled Empress Jian.
entries.literal: On guiwei posthumous title was given to Consort Wang as Empress Jian.

entries.zh: 大寶元年春正月辛亥朔，以國哀不朝會。
entries.en: On xinhai, the new-year's day of Dabao 1, national mourning prevented the court assembly.
entries.literal: On xinhai, the first day of the first month of spring in year 1 of Dabao, because of national mourning there was no court assembly.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「蓋天下者，至公之神器，在昔三五，不獲已而臨蒞之。
entries.en: An edict said, "All under Heaven is the sacred vessel of utmost fairness; in antiquity the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors took the throne only when they could not refuse.
entries.literal: An edict said: "All under Heaven is the sacred vessel of utmost fairness; in ages past the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors took the throne only because they had no choice.

entries.zh: 故帝王之功，聖人之餘事。
entries.en: Thus the work of emperors and kings is what sages leave as surplus.
entries.literal: Thus the achievement of emperors and kings is what sages leave over.

entries.zh: 軒冕之華，儻來之一物。
entries.en: Chariot and cap are adornments that come by chance alone.
entries.literal: The glory of chariot and cap is something that came by chance.

entries.zh: 太祖文皇帝含光大之量，啓西伯之基。
entries.en: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor held vast hidden brilliance and laid the foundation of the Western Earl.
entries.literal: Grand Ancestor the Literary Emperor embraced a great measure of hidden light and opened the foundation of the Western Earl.

entries.zh: 高祖武皇帝道洽二儀，智周萬物。
entries.en: Gaozu the Martial Emperor made the Way fill the two principles and his wisdom encompass the myriad things.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor, the Gaozu, made the Way pervade the two principles and wisdom compass the myriad things.

entries.zh: 屬齊季薦瘥，彝倫剝喪，同氣離入苑之禍，元首懷無厭之欲，乃當樂推之運，因億兆之心，承彼掎角，雪茲讎恥。
entries.en: When Qi neared its end pestilence returned and moral order collapsed, kin suffered the calamity of the park, and the ruler nursed insatiable desires—then came the fortune of willing elevation, the hearts of the hundred millions were followed, their allied strength was taken up, and this shame was avenged.
entries.literal: When the late Qi era brought repeated pestilence and constant norms were stripped away, flesh-and-blood kin suffered the calamity of entering the park, and the ruler harbored insatiable desire—then we met the fortune of the people's willing elevation, drew on the hearts of the hundred millions, received their allied support, and avenged this shame.

entries.zh: 事非為己，義寔從民。
entries.en: The deed was not for oneself; in righteousness one truly followed the people.
entries.literal: The affair was not for oneself; in righteousness one truly followed the people.

entries.zh: 故功成弗居，卑宮菲食，大慈之業普薰，汾陽之詔屢下。
entries.en: Therefore when the work was done he did not keep it, dwelt in low halls and ate plain food, great compassion spread widely, and edicts like those of Fenyang were issued again and again.
entries.literal: Therefore when achievement was done he did not dwell on it, lived in low halls and plain food, the great compassionate enterprise broadly perfumed, and edicts like those of Fenyang were repeatedly issued.

entries.zh: 于茲四紀，無得而稱。
entries.en: For four reign cycles there has been no fully fitting praise.
entries.literal: For four reign cycles now, none can fully praise it.

entries.zh: 朕以寡昧，哀煢孔棘，生靈已盡，志不圖全，僶俛視陰，企承鴻緒。
entries.en: I, slight and dull, am in deepest grief and distress; the living are exhausted and my will does not aim at wholeness; bowing low I await shade and hope to inherit the great succession.
entries.literal: We, slight and dull, in deepest grief and distress—the living souls are spent and our will does not plan for wholeness; we bend low and look to shade, hoping to inherit the great thread.

entries.zh: 懸旌履薄，未足云喻。
entries.en: Banners hang over thin ice—words can scarcely tell it.
entries.literal: Suspended banners over thin ice—words barely suffice.

entries.zh: 痛甚愈遲，諒闇彌切。
entries.en: Pain deepens as recovery is slow; mourning seclusion grows keener still.
entries.literal: Pain grows deeper as healing delays; the period of hidden mourning is all the keener.

entries.zh: 方當玄默在躬，栖心事外。
entries.en: I should keep dark silence within and lodge my mind outside affairs.
entries.literal: We should keep dark silence within and lodge the mind in matters beyond.

entries.zh: 卽王道未直，天步猶艱，式憑宰輔，以弘庶政。
entries.en: Yet the kingly Way is not yet straight and the heavenly steps still hard; I must rely on chief ministers to broaden the myriad affairs of state.
entries.literal: Yet the kingly Way is not yet straight and the heavenly course still hard—we must rely on chief ministers to expand the myriad administrations.

entries.zh: 履端建號，仰惟舊章。
entries.en: At the year's beginning I establish the era name, looking up to the old statutes.
entries.literal: Observing the year's beginning, we establish the era name, looking up to the old statutes.

entries.zh: 可大赦天下，改太清四年為大寶元年。」
entries.en: A general amnesty is proclaimed and Taiqing 4 is changed to Dabao 1."
entries.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed; Taiqing year 4 is changed to Dabao year 1."

entries.zh: 丁巳，天雨黃沙。
entries.en: On dingsi yellow sand fell from the sky.
entries.literal: On dingsi yellow sand rained from the sky.

entries.zh: 己未，太白經天，辛酉乃止。
entries.en: On jiwei Venus crossed the heavens; on xinyou it stopped.
entries.literal: On jiwei Venus crossed the sky; on xinyou it ceased.

entries.zh: 西魏寇安陸，執司州刺史柳仲禮，盡沒漢東之地。
entries.en: Western Wei raided Anlu, seized Sizhou inspector Liu Zhongli, and took all the lands east of the Han.
entries.literal: Western Wei raided Anlu, seized Sizhou Inspector Liu Zhongli, and wholly took the lands east of the Han.

entries.zh: 丙寅，月晝見。
entries.en: On bingyin the moon was visible by day.
entries.literal: On bingyin the moon was seen in daytime.

entries.zh: 癸酉，前江都令祖皓起義，襲廣陵，斬賊南兗州刺史董紹先。
entries.en: On guiyou former Jiangdu magistrate Zu Hao rose, attacked Guangling, and beheaded the rebel South Yanzhou inspector Dong Shaoxian.
entries.literal: On guiyou former Jiangdu magistrate Zu Hao rose in revolt, struck Guangling, and beheaded the rebel South Yanzhou Inspector Dong Shaoxian.

entries.zh: 侯景自帥水步軍擊皓。
entries.en: Hou Jing personally led land and river forces against Hao.
entries.literal: Hou Jing personally led infantry and naval forces to attack Hao.

entries.zh: 太宗幼而敏睿，識悟過人，六歲便屬文，高祖驚其早就，弗之信也。
entries.en: Taizong from childhood was quick and perceptive, his insight beyond others; at six he could write, and Gaozu marveled at his early gift but did not believe it.
entries.literal: Taizong from youth was keen and perceptive, his understanding surpassing others; at six he could compose texts, and Gaozu marveled at his early maturity but did not believe it.

entries.zh: 乃於御前面試，辭采甚美。
entries.en: He was tested before the throne, and his literary grace was superb.
entries.literal: He was then tested before the imperial presence, and his literary color was very fine.

entries.zh: 高祖歎曰：「此子，吾家之東阿。」
entries.en: Gaozu sighed and said, "This boy is our family's Dong'e."
entries.literal: Gaozu sighed and said: "This boy is our family's Dong'e."

entries.zh: 旣長，器宇寬弘，未嘗見慍喜。
entries.en: When he grew up, his bearing was broad and calm; anger and delight never showed on his face.
entries.literal: When he grew up, his bearing was broad and magnanimous; he was never seen angry or pleased.

entries.zh: 方頰豊下，須鬢如畫，眄睞則目光燭人。
entries.en: Square of cheek and full below, beard and temples like painted lines; a sidelong glance lit upon men like fire.
entries.literal: Square of cheek and full below, his beard and temples like a painting; when he glanced sidelong his gaze lit upon men.

entries.zh: 讀書十行俱下。
entries.en: In reading he took in ten lines at a glance.
entries.literal: In reading he took in ten lines at once.

entries.zh: 九流百氏，經目必記；
entries.en: Of the nine schools and hundred thinkers, whatever passed his eye he remembered;
entries.literal: Of the nine schools and the hundred clans, what passed his eye he always remembered;

entries.zh: 篇章辭賦，操筆立成。
entries.en: in essays, rhapsodies, and verse he took up the brush and finished on the spot.
entries.literal: in essays, rhapsodies, and verse he took up the brush and finished at once.

entries.zh: 博綜儒書，善言玄理。
entries.en: He mastered Confucian classics and was skilled in Neo-Daoist discourse.
entries.literal: Broadly versed in Confucian books, skilled in discoursing on Dark Learning.

entries.zh: 自年十一，便能親庶務，歷試蕃政，所在有稱。
entries.en: From age eleven he could handle routine affairs himself; repeatedly tried in frontier posts, wherever he went he won praise.
entries.literal: From age eleven he could personally attend to the multitude of affairs; repeatedly tested in frontier administration, wherever he went he won praise.

entries.zh: 在穆貴嬪憂，哀毀骨立，晝夜號泣不絕聲，所坐之席，沾濕盡爛。
entries.en: Mourning Noble Consort Mu, grief wasted him to bone; day and night he wept without pause, and the mat he sat on rotted from wetting.
entries.literal: In mourning for Noble Consort Mu, his grief wasted him to bone; day and night his weeping never ceased, and the mat he sat on was soaked through and rotted.

entries.zh: 在襄陽拜表北伐，遣長史柳津、司馬董當門，壯武將軍杜懷寶、振遠將軍曹義宗等衆軍進討，剋平南陽、新野等郡，魏南荊州刺史李志據安昌城降，拓地千餘里。
entries.en: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign and sent chief clerk Liu Jin, marshal Dong Dangmen, martial valor general Du Huaibao, far-shaking general Cao Yizong, and others with the armies; they took Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies, Wei's south Jingzhou inspector Li Zhi surrendered Anchang fortress, and territory expanded more than a thousand li.
entries.literal: At Xiangyang he memorialized for a northern campaign; he sent Chief Clerk Liu Jin, Marshal Dong Dangmen, Martial Valor General Du Huaibao, Far-Shaking General Cao Yizong, and others with the massed armies on expedition, conquering Nanyang, Xinye, and other commanderies; Wei's South Jingzhou Inspector Li Zhi, holding Anchang fortress, surrendered, and territory was extended more than a thousand li.

entries.zh: 及居監撫，多所弘宥，文案簿領，纖毫不可欺。
entries.en: As regent he was broadly lenient in many matters, yet in documents and ledgers not the finest thread could be falsified.
entries.literal: When he held the regency he was broadly indulgent in many matters, yet in documents and ledgers not the finest thread could be deceived.

entries.zh: 引納文學之士，賞接無倦，恒討論篇籍，繼以文章。
entries.en: He welcomed literary men and rewarded them tirelessly, constantly discussing texts and then writing himself.
entries.literal: He drew in men of letters and rewarded them without weariness, constantly discussing texts and following with compositions.

entries.zh: 高祖所制《五經講疏》，嘗於玄圃奉述，聽者傾朝野。
entries.en: When Gaozu composed his Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once lectured on them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.
entries.literal: When Gaozu composed Expositions on the Five Classics, Taizong once presented them at the Dark Garden; listeners filled court and countryside.

entries.zh: 雅好題詩，其序云：「余七歲有詩癖，長而不倦。」
entries.en: He loved poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote, "At seven I had a poetry mania, and as I grew I never tired of it."
entries.literal: He loved composing poetry by nature; in his preface he wrote: "At seven I had a poetry mania, and in growing up I never tired of it."

entries.zh: 然傷於輕豔，當時號曰「宮體」。
entries.en: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age called it the "Palace Style."
entries.literal: Yet he was faulted for frivolous ornament, and his age styled this the "Palace Style."

entries.zh: 所著《昭明太子傳》五卷，《諸王傳》三十卷，《禮大義》二十卷，《老子義》二十卷，《莊子義》二十卷，《長春義記》一百卷，《法寶連璧》三百卷，並行於世焉。
entries.en: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his day.
entries.literal: His works included Biography of the Heir Apparent Zhaoming in five scrolls, Biographies of the Princes in thirty scrolls, Great Meaning of the Rites in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Laozi in twenty scrolls, Meaning of the Zhuangzi in twenty scrolls, Recorded Meaning of Eternal Spring in one hundred scrolls, and Treasured Laws Linked Pearls in three hundred scrolls—all circulated in his time.

entries.zh: 秋七月甲寅，廣州刺史元景仲謀應侯景，西江督護陳霸先起兵攻之，景仲自殺，霸先迎定州刺史蕭勃為刺史。
entries.en: On jiayin in the seventh month of autumn Guangzhou inspector Yuan Jingzhong plotted to join Hou Jing; West River Protector Chen Baxian rose against him; Jingzhong killed himself and Baxian installed Dingzhou inspector Xiao Bo as inspector.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, day jiayin, Guangzhou Inspector Yuan Jingzhong plotted to join Hou Jing; West River Protector Chen Baxian raised troops and attacked him; Jingzhong killed himself and Baxian welcomed Dingzhou Inspector Xiao Bo as inspector.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以吳郡置吳州，以安陸王大春為刺史。
entries.en: On wuchen Wu commandery was made Wu province, with Prince Dachun of Anlu as inspector.
entries.literal: On wuchen Wu commandery was made into Wu province, with Prince of Anlu Dachun as inspector.

entries.zh: 庚午，以司空南康嗣王會理兼尚書令，南海王大臨為揚州刺史，新興王大莊為南徐州刺史。
entries.en: On gengwu the heir of Nankang Prince Huili, Minister of Works, also became Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Dalin of Nanhai became Yangzhou inspector; Prince Dazhuang of Xinxing became South Xuzhou inspector.
entries.literal: On gengwu the Heir of Nankang Prince Huili, Minister of Works, additionally became Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince of Nanhai Dalin was made Yangzhou Inspector; Prince of Xinxing Dazhuang was made South Xuzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 是月，九江大饑，人相食十四五。
entries.en: That month Jiujiang suffered great famine; four or five out of ten people ate human flesh.
entries.literal: That month in Jiujiang there was great famine; one person in fourteen or fifteen ate another.

entries.zh: 八月甲午，湘東王繹遣領軍將軍王僧辯率衆逼郢州。
entries.en: On jiawu in the eighth month Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent Army Inspector General Wang Sengbian with troops to press Yingzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, day jiawu, Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Army Inspector General Wang Sengbian leading the host to press Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 乙亥，侯景自進位相國，封二十郡為漢王。
entries.en: On yihai Hou Jing made himself Chancellor of State and enfeoffed twenty commanderies as King of Han.
entries.literal: On yihai Hou Jing advanced himself to Chancellor of State and enfeoffed over twenty commanderies as King of Han.

entries.zh: 邵陵王綸棄郢州走。
entries.en: Prince Lun of Shaoling abandoned Yingzhou and fled.
entries.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun abandoned Yingzhou and fled.

entries.zh: 冬十月乙未，侯景又逼太宗幸西州曲宴，自加宇宙大將軍、都督六合諸軍事。
entries.en: On yiwei in the tenth month of winter Hou Jing again forced Taizong to a banquet at Xizhou and made himself Grand General of the Cosmos and commander of the Six Harmonized Directions.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, day yiwei, Hou Jing again compelled the Taizong to attend a banquet at Xizhou, and himself added Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander over military affairs in the Six Harmonized Directions.

entries.zh: 立皇子大鈞為西陽郡王，大威為武寧郡王，大球為建安郡王，大昕為義安郡王，大摯為綏建郡王，大圜為樂梁郡王。
entries.en: The princes Dagun, Dawei, Daqiu, Daxin, Dazhi, and Dayuan were enfeoffed as princes of Xiyang, Wuning, Jian'an, Yi'an, Suijian, and Yuele commanderies.
entries.literal: Imperial sons Dagun, Dawei, Daqiu, Daxin, Dazhi, and Dayuan were enfeoffed as princes of Xiyang, Wuning, Jian'an, Yi'an, Suijian, and Yuele commanderies.

entries.zh: 壬寅，景害南康嗣王會理。
entries.en: On renyin Hou Jing killed the heir of Nankang Prince Huili.
entries.literal: On renyin Jing killed the Heir of Nankang Prince Huili.

entries.zh: 三月，侯景自帥衆西寇。
entries.en: In the third month Hou Jing personally led his army west on campaign.
entries.literal: In the third month Hou Jing personally led his host westward on campaign.

entries.zh: 丁未，發京師，自石頭至新林，舳艫相接。
entries.en: On dingwei day he marched from the capital; from Shitou to Xinlin, boats stretched bow to stern without a break.
entries.literal: On dingwei, he set out from the capital; from Shitou to Xinlin, war vessels linked stem to stern.

entries.zh: 八月丙午，晉熙人王僧振、鄭寵起兵襲郡城，偽晉州刺史夏侯威生、儀同任延遁走。
entries.en: On bingwu in the eighth month Wang Sengzhen and Zheng Chong of Jinxi rose and stormed the commandery seat; the rebel Jinzhou inspector Xiahou Weisheng and formation companion Ren Yan fled.
