entries.literal: After crossing the Yangtze he served as aide to the chancellor and as attendant to the crown prince.

entries.zh: 穆之少方雅，有識鑒。
entries.en: Muzhi in youth was upright and elegant, with keen judgment.
entries.literal: Muzhi in youth was square and refined, with discernment.

entries.zh: 宋元嘉中，爲員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: In Song's Yuanjia era he became an outer member of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: In Yuanjia of Song he was made Outer Member of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 與吏部尚書江湛、太子左率袁淑善，淑薦之於始興王濬，濬深引納焉。
entries.en: He was close to Minister of the Civil Service Jiang Zhan and the heir's left leader Yuan Shu; Shu recommended him to Prince Jun of Shixing, and Jun took him in warmly.
entries.literal: He was on good terms with Minister of the Civil Service Jiang Zhan and Left Leader of the Heir's Household Yuan Shu; Shu recommended him to Prince Jun of Shixing, and Jun warmly received him.

entries.zh: 穆之鑒其禍萌，思違其難，言於湛求外出。
entries.en: Muzhi saw trouble brewing and sought a way out; he asked Zhan to post him away.
entries.literal: Muzhi saw the disaster sprouting and thought to escape the trouble; he spoke to Zhan asking to be sent out.

entries.zh: 湛將用爲東縣，固乞遠郡，久之，得爲寧遠將軍、交阯太守。
entries.en: Zhan meant to place him in an eastern county, but he begged for a distant commandery and, after long delay, became General Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Jiaozhi.
entries.literal: Zhan was about to use him in an eastern county; he firmly begged for a distant commandery, and after long delay became General Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Jiaozhi.

entries.zh: 治有異績。
entries.en: He governed with outstanding results.
entries.literal: His administration showed exceptional achievement.

entries.zh: 會刺史死，交土大亂，穆之威懷循拊，境內以寧。
entries.en: When the inspector died, Jiaozhi erupted in chaos; Muzhi won men by authority and kindness, and the region grew calm.
entries.literal: When the inspector died, Jiaozhi fell into great disorder; Muzhi by awe and kindness guided and comforted them, and within the borders there was peace.

entries.zh: 宋文帝聞之嘉焉，將以爲交州刺史，會病卒。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Song heard and praised him and was about to make him Inspector of Jiaozhi, but Muzhi fell ill and died.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Song heard and praised this, and was about to make him Inspector of Jiaozhi, but Muzhi fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 子弘籍，字真藝，齊初爲鎮西參軍，卒於官。
entries.en: His son Hongji, styled Zhenyi, in early Qi served as staff officer to the Pacify West army and died in office.
entries.literal: His son Hongji, styled Zhenyi, in early Qi was staff officer to the Pacify West army and died in office.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，追贈穆之光祿大夫，加金章。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Muzhi was posthumously made Glory Grand Master with a gold seal.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Muzhi was posthumously made Glory Grand Master with gold seal.

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「亡舅齊鎮西參軍，素風雅猷，夙肩名輩，降年不永，早世潛輝。
entries.en: Another edict said: "My late uncle, Qi's Pacify West staff officer, bore pure taste and fine counsel and long stood among eminent men; his years were short and his light went under early.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "The deceased uncle, Qi staff officer to the Pacify West army, had pure style and elegant counsel, from of old shoulder to shoulder with famous men; his years were not long, early leaving the world his light hid.

entries.zh: 朕少離苦辛，情地彌切，雖宅相克成，輅車靡贈，興言永往，觸目慟心。
entries.en: I knew bitter separation in youth and feel the bond all the more; though tombs were raised, no carriage of gifts went forth, and every thought of his going wrings the heart.
entries.literal: I in youth parted from bitter hardship, kin feeling ever keener; though dwelling tombs were mutually accomplished, touring carriage had no gift-offering, words rising at eternal parting, the eye touched brings anguished heart.

entries.zh: 可追贈廷尉卿。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously made Minister of Justice."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Minister of Justice."

entries.zh: 弘籍無子，從父弟弘策以第三子纘爲嗣，別有傳。
entries.en: Hongji had no son; his cousin Hongce made his third son Zuan the heir—see the separate biography.
entries.literal: Hongji had no son; his father's younger brother's son Hongce made his third son Zuan heir—treated in a separate biography.

entries.zh: 高祖郗皇后
entries.en: Empress Xi of Gaozu
entries.literal: Empress Xi of Gaozu

entries.zh: 高祖德皇后郗氏，諱徽，高平金鄉人也。
entries.en: Gaozu's Virtuous Empress Xi, taboo name Hui, came from Jinxiang in Gaoping.
entries.literal: Gaozu's Virtuous Empress, the Xi clan, taboo name Hui, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.

entries.zh: 祖紹，國子祭酒，領東海王師。
entries.en: Her grandfather Shao was Sacrificer of the Imperial Academy and tutor to the Prince of Donghai.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Shao was Sacrificer of the Imperial Academy and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Donghai.

entries.zh: 父燁，太子舍人，早卒。
entries.en: Her father Ye was a crown prince attendant and died young.
entries.literal: Her father Ye was attendant to the crown prince and died early.

entries.zh: 后幼而明慧，善隸書，讀史傳。
entries.en: From childhood she was clever and bright, skilled at clerical script, and read histories.
entries.literal: The empress from childhood was clever and bright, skilled at clerical script, and read histories and records.

entries.zh: 女工之事，無不閑習。
entries.en: Of women's crafts there was none she had not mastered.
entries.literal: Women's crafts—there was none she did not know intimately.

entries.zh: 宋後廢帝將納爲后；
entries.en: The deposed emperor of Later Song meant to make her empress;
entries.literal: Deposed Emperor of Later Song was about to take her as empress;

entries.zh: 齊初，安陸王緬又欲婚：郗氏並辭以女疾，乃止。
entries.en: in early Qi Prince Mian of Anlu also sought her hand; the Xi clan pleaded illness both times, and the matches ended.
entries.literal: in early Qi Prince Mian of Anlu also wished to marry her: the Xi clan both declined on grounds of the daughter's illness, and it stopped.

entries.zh: 建元未，高祖始娉焉。
entries.en: Near the end of Jianyuan Gaozu first took her as his wife.
entries.literal: At the end of Jianyuan Gaozu first betrothed her.

entries.zh: 生永興公主玉姚，永世公主玉婉，永康公主玉嬛。
entries.en: She bore Princess Yuyao of Yongxing, Princess Yuwan of Yongshi, and Princess Yuhuan of Yongkang.
entries.literal: She bore Princess Yuyao of Yongxing, Princess Yuwan of Yongshi, Princess Yuhuan of Yongkang.

entries.zh: 建武五年，高祖爲雍州刺史，先之鎮，後乃迎后。
entries.en: In Jianwu 5, when Gaozu became inspector of Yongzhou, he went to his post first and welcomed the empress afterward.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu, when Gaozu became inspector of Yongzhou, he first went to his garrison and only afterward welcomed the empress.

entries.zh: 至州未幾，永元元年八月殂于襄陽官舍，時年三十二。
entries.en: Not long after reaching the province, she died in the official residence at Xiangyang in the eighth month of Yongyuan 1, aged thirty-two.
entries.literal: Not long after she reached the province, in the eighth month of the first year of Yongyuan, she died at the official residence in Xiangyang, aged thirty-two.

entries.zh: 其年歸葬南徐州南東海武進縣東城里山。
entries.en: That year her remains were returned for burial on Dongchengli Mountain in Wujin county, South Donghai commandery, South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: That year she was returned for burial at Dongchengli Mountain in Wujin county, South Donghai, South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 中興二年，齊朝進高祖位相國，封十郡，梁公，詔贈后爲梁公妃。
entries.en: In Zhongxing 2, the Qi court advanced Gaozu to chancellor of state and enfeoffed him over ten commanderies as Duke of Liang; by edict, she was posthumously made consort of the Duke of Liang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, the Qi court advanced Gaozu to the post of chancellor of state and enfeoffed him over ten commanderies as Duke of Liang; an edict posthumously presented the empress as consort of the Duke of Liang.

entries.zh: 高祖踐阼，追崇爲皇后。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, she was posthumously honored as empress.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, she was posthumously exalted as empress.

entries.zh: 有司議諡，吏部尚書兼右僕射臣約議曰：「表號垂名，義昭不朽。
entries.en: When the offices deliberated on her posthumous title, your servant Yue, minister of personnel and acting right vice director, argued: "To set forth a title and pass down a name makes the principle of immortality clear.
entries.literal: The responsible offices deliberated on her posthumous title, and your servant Yue, minister of personnel and acting right vice director, stated in deliberation: "To display a title and transmit a name is a principle that makes immortality manifest.

entries.zh: 先皇后應祥月德，比載坤靈，柔範陰化，儀形自遠。
entries.en: The late empress answered auspicious signs and lunar virtue, bearing the spirit of Earth; her gentle model and womanly influence formed an example that reached far.
entries.literal: The former empress answered auspiciousness and lunar virtue, matched and bore the spirit of Earth; her gentle model and yin transformation, her form and example, reached far of themselves.

entries.zh: 俔天作合，義先造舟，而神猷夙掩，所隔升運。
entries.en: Heaven made the match and the rite preceded the crossing, yet her divine course was hidden early, cutting her off from the dynasty's rising fortune.
entries.literal: As Heaven made the match, the rite preceded the building of boats, yet her divine plan was early hidden, and she was separated from the rising fortune.

entries.zh: 宜式遵景行，用昭大典。
entries.en: We should follow her luminous conduct as our model and make the great ceremony clear.
entries.literal: It is proper to follow her bright conduct as a model and thereby make the great ceremony manifest.

entries.zh: 謹按《諡法》，忠和純備曰德，貴而好禮曰德。
entries.en: According to the Rules for Posthumous Titles, one loyal, harmonious, pure, and complete is called De; one noble and fond of ritual is also called De.
entries.literal: I respectfully note that according to the Rules for Posthumous Titles, loyal, harmonious, pure, and complete is called De; noble yet loving ritual is called De.

entries.zh: 宜崇曰德皇后。」
entries.en: She should be honored as Empress De."
entries.literal: She should be exalted as Empress De."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict followed this recommendation.
entries.literal: The edict followed this.

entries.zh: 陵曰脩陵。
entries.en: Her mausoleum was called Xiuling.
entries.literal: Her mausoleum was called Xiuling.

entries.zh: 父騫，字思寂，本名玄成，與齊高帝偏諱同，故改焉。
entries.en: Her father Qian, styled Siji, was originally named Xuancheng; because the name clashed with Qi Gaozu's partial taboo, he changed it.
entries.literal: Her father Qian, styled Siji, original name Xuancheng, shared a partial taboo with Qi Gaozu and therefore changed it.

entries.zh: 以公子起家員外郎，遷太子洗馬，襲封南昌縣公，出爲義興太守。
entries.en: He entered office as a noble's son, became an outer member, then attendant for the heir's wash horses, succeeded as Marquis of Nanchang county, and went out as Administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: Entering office as son of a noble he was outer member, promoted attendant to wash horses of the heir, succeeded as Marquis of Nanchang county, went out as Administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 還爲驃騎諮議，累遷黃門郎，司徒右長史。
entries.en: On return he advised the Rapid Cavalry general, then rose through Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate to Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: Returning he became advisory officer to the Rapid Cavalry general, rising through posts to Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 性凝簡，不狎當世。
entries.en: By nature he was austere and plain and kept aloof from his times.
entries.literal: By nature he was reserved and simple, not familiar with the age.

entries.zh: 嘗從容謂諸子曰：「吾家門戶，所謂素族，自可隨流平進，不須苟求也。」
entries.en: Once he told his sons at ease: "Our house is a plain clan; one may drift with the current and advance evenly—there is no need to scramble for rank."
entries.literal: Once at leisure he told his sons: "Our family's gate is what is called a plain clan; one may simply drift with the stream and advance evenly—there is no need to seek advancement recklessly."

entries.zh: 永元末，遷侍中，不拜。
entries.en: At the end of Yongyuan he was offered Palace Attendant but refused the post.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was moved to Palace Attendant but did not accept.

entries.zh: 高祖霸府建，引爲大司馬諮議參軍，俄遷侍中，領越騎校尉。
entries.en: When Gaozu set up his hegemony office, Qian was called in as Grand Marshal adviser, soon made Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Gaozu established his hegemony office, Qian was summoned as advisory officer to the Grand Marshal, soon promoted Palace Attendant and concurrently Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，詔曰：「庭堅世祀，靡輟於宗周，樂毅錫壤，乃昭於洪漢。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, an edict said: "Jianting's line was never cut off in the Zhou royal house; Yue Yi received a fief and shone in great Han.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the mandate, an edict said: "Jianting's generations of sacrifice never ceased in the Zhou of the clan; Yue Yi received lands and shone forth in great Han.

entries.zh: 齊故太尉南昌公，含章履道，草昧興齊，謨明翊贊，同符在昔。
entries.en: Qi's former Grand Commandant, Duke of Nanchang, bore talent and walked the Way, helped raise Qi from the wilds, and counseled with bright support like men of old.
entries.literal: Qi's former Grand Commandant Duke of Nanchang bore his talent and trod the Way, in the wilds he raised Qi, his counsels bright and supportive, matching those of old.

entries.zh: 雖子房之蔚爲帝師，文若之隆比王佐，無以尚也。
entries.en: Though Zifang became the emperor's teacher and Wenruo rose as the king's right hand, none surpass him.
entries.literal: Though Zifang stood eminent as emperor's teacher, Wenruo towered like king's helper—they cannot be surpassed.

entries.zh: 朕膺歷受圖，惟新寶命，莘莘玉帛，升降有典。
entries.en: I have received the mandate and renewed the imperial charge; gifts of silk now rise and fall by fixed ritual.
entries.literal: I have received the mandate and renewed the jade command; the multitudes of silk offerings rise and fall with fixed ritual.

entries.zh: 永言前代，敬惟徽烈，匪直懋勳，義兼懷樹。
entries.en: Speaking always of former times, I revere his great glory—not for merit alone, but also in gratitude, as one cherishes a tree.
entries.literal: Forever speaking of former ages, reverently thinking on his great glory—not only for meritorious toil, the meaning also embraces cherished trees.

entries.zh: 可降封南昌公爲侯，食邑千戶。」
entries.en: Let Duke of Nanchang be reduced to marquis with a fief of one thousand households."
entries.literal: Duke of Nanchang may be demoted to marquis, fief of one thousand households."

entries.zh: 騫襲爵，遷度支尚書。
entries.en: Qian inherited the title and was made Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: Qian succeeded to the title, was moved to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 天監四年，出爲東陽太守，尋徙吳郡。
entries.en: In Tianjian year 4 he went out as Administrator of Dongyang, then was moved to Wu commandery.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian he went out as Administrator of Dongyang, soon transferred to Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 八年，入爲太府卿，領后軍將軍，遷太常卿。
entries.en: In year 8 he entered as Minister of the Palace Treasury and Rear Army General, then became Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he entered as Minister of the Palace Treasury, concurrently Rear Army General, then Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 十一年，遷中書令，加員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: In year 11 he became Palace Scribe with added outer membership in the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was moved to Palace Scribe, with added Outer Member of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 時高祖於鐘山造大愛敬寺，騫舊墅在寺側，有良田八十餘頃，卽晉丞相王導賜田也。
entries.en: Gaozu was building the Great Temple of Filial Reverence on Zhong Mountain; Qian's old villa lay beside it, with more than eighty qing of fine fields—the very grant of Jin chancellor Wang Dao.
entries.literal: At the time Gaozu at Zhong Mountain built the Great Temple of Filial Reverence; Qian's old villa stood beside the temple, with more than eighty qing of good farmland—that very land the Jin chancellor Wang Dao had been granted.

entries.zh: 高祖遣主書宣旨就騫求市，欲以施寺。
entries.en: Gaozu sent a palace clerk with an imperial message to buy the land for the temple.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent a palace clerk with imperial words to Qian to seek to buy it, intending to give it to the temple.

entries.zh: 騫答旨云：「此田不賣；
entries.en: Qian answered: "This land is not for sale;
entries.literal: Qian answered the decree: "This land is not for sale;

entries.zh: 若是敕取，所不敢言。」
entries.en: if Your Majesty takes it by command, I dare not object."
entries.literal: if it is taken by command, I dare say nothing."

entries.zh: 酬對又脫略。
entries.en: His replies were curt and careless besides.
entries.literal: His replies were also curt and offhand.

entries.zh: 高祖怒，遂付市評田價，以直逼還之。
entries.en: Gaozu grew angry, had the market price assessed, and seized the land outright in return.
entries.literal: Gaozu was angry, had the market assess the land price, and by direct seizure returned it.

entries.zh: 由是忤旨，出爲吳興太守。
entries.en: For this he lost favor and was sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: For this he offended the will and was sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 在郡臥疾不視事。
entries.en: In the commandery he took to his bed and left affairs unattended.
entries.literal: In the commandery he lay ill and did not attend to affairs.

entries.zh: 徵還，復爲度支尚書，加給事中，領射聲校尉。
entries.en: Recalled, he again became Minister of Revenue, with added Supervising Censor and Colonel of the Archer Sound.
entries.literal: Summoned back, again Minister of Revenue, with added Supervising Censor, concurrently Colonel of the Archer Sound.

entries.zh: 以母憂去職。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 高祖丁貴嬪
entries.en: Noble Consort Ding of Gaozu
entries.literal: Noble Consort Ding of Gaozu

entries.zh: 高祖丁貴嬪，諱令光，譙國人也，世居襄陽。
entries.en: Gaozu's Noble Consort Ding, taboo name Lingguang, came from Qiao and had long lived at Xiangyang.
entries.literal: Gaozu's Noble Consort Ding, taboo name Lingguang, was a native of Qiao state, her family for generations dwelling at Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 貴嬪生于樊城，有神光之異，紫煙滿室，故以「光」爲名。
entries.en: She was born at Fancheng amid a marvel of divine light and purple mist filling the room, and so "Guang" was placed in her name.
entries.literal: The Noble Consort was born at Fancheng; there was a divine-light marvel, purple mist filling the chamber, and so "Guang" was put in her name.

entries.zh: 相者云：「此女當大貴。」
entries.en: A physiognomist said, "This girl will rise to great honor."
entries.literal: A physiognomist said: "This girl will attain great honor."

entries.zh: 高祖臨州，丁氏因人以聞。
entries.en: When Gaozu held the province, the Ding clan sent word through others.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was inspector of the province, the Ding clan had someone bring word.

entries.zh: 貴嬪時年十四，高祖納焉。
entries.en: The Noble Consort was then fourteen, and Gaozu took her in.
entries.literal: The Noble Consort was then fourteen; Gaozu took her in.

entries.zh: 初，貴嬪生而有赤痣在左臂，治之不滅，至是無何忽失所在。
entries.en: At birth she had a red mole on her left arm that medicine could not erase; now, without cause, it suddenly vanished.
entries.literal: At first the Noble Consort had been born with a red mole on her left arm; treatment could not remove it—now suddenly and for no reason it vanished.

entries.zh: 事德皇后小心祗敬，嘗於供養經案之側，彷彿若見神人，心獨異之。
entries.en: Serving the Virtuous Empress, she was careful and reverent; once beside the sutra offerings she seemed to see a spirit, and her heart alone was struck.
entries.literal: In serving the Virtuous Empress she was careful and reverent; once beside the sutra case where offerings were made, it was as if she saw a spirit being, and her heart alone felt it strange.

entries.zh: 高祖義師起，昭明太子始誕育，貴嬪與太子留在州城。
entries.en: When Gaozu's righteous army rose and Crown Prince Zhaoming was newly born, the Noble Consort stayed in the provincial city with the heir.
entries.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army rose, the Crown Prince Zhaoming was first born; the Noble Consort with the heir remained in the provincial city.

entries.zh: 京邑平，乃還京都。
entries.en: When the capital was pacified, she returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When the capital region was pacified, she returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 天監元年五月，有司奏爲貴人，未拜；
entries.en: In the fifth month of Tianjian year 1 the relevant office memorialized to make her Honored Person, but the investiture had not yet been performed;
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tianjian the relevant office memorialized to make her Honored Person—not yet invested;

entries.zh: 其年八月，又爲貴嬪，位在三夫人上，居于顯陽殿。
entries.en: that same year in the eighth month she became Noble Consort, ranking above the Three Consorts and dwelling in Xianyang Palace.
entries.literal: that same year in the eighth month she became Noble Consort, rank above the Three Consorts, dwelling in Xianyang Palace.

entries.zh: 及太子定位，有司奏曰：
entries.en: When the crown prince's place was settled, the relevant office memorialized:
entries.literal: When the crown prince's position was fixed, the relevant office memorialized:

entries.zh: 貴嬪性仁恕，及居宮內，接馭自下，皆得其歡心。
entries.en: The honored consort was by nature kind and forgiving; once she dwelt within the palace, she received and guided those below and won all their hearts.
entries.literal: The honored consort was by nature kind and forgiving; once she dwelt within the palace, she received and guided those below and won all their hearts.

entries.zh: 不好華飾，器服無珍麗，未嘗爲親戚私謁。
entries.en: She did not care for ornate dress; utensils and garments had no lavish gems; she never received private audiences for kin.
entries.literal: She did not care for ornate dress; utensils and garments had no lavish gems; she never received private audiences for kin.

entries.zh: 及高祖弘佛教，貴嬪奉而行之，屏絕滋腴，長進蔬膳。
entries.en: When Gaozu spread Buddhism, the honored consort followed it, banishing rich foods and keeping to vegetables long term.
entries.literal: When Gaozu spread Buddhism, the honored consort followed it, banishing rich foods and keeping to vegetables long term.

entries.zh: 受戒日，甘露降于殿前，方一丈五尺。
entries.en: On the day she received the precepts, sweet dew fell before the hall, a square of one zhang and five chi.
entries.literal: On the day she received the precepts, sweet dew fell before the hall, a square of one zhang and five chi.

entries.zh: 高祖所立經義，皆得其指歸。
entries.en: Of the sutra meanings Gaozu established, she grasped every import.
entries.literal: Of the sutra meanings Gaozu established, she grasped every import.

entries.zh: 尤精《淨名經》。
entries.en: She was especially versed in the Vimalakirti Sutra.
entries.literal: She was especially versed in the Vimalakirti Sutra.

entries.zh: 所受供賜，悉以充法事。
entries.en: All stipends and gifts she received went entirely to Buddhist rites.
entries.literal: All stipends and gifts she received went entirely to Buddhist rites.

entries.zh: 高祖阮脩容
entries.en: Gaozu's Ruan Xiurong
entries.literal: Gaozu's Ruan Xiurong

entries.zh: 高祖阮脩容諱令嬴，本姓石，會稽餘姚人也。
entries.en: Gaozu's Ruan Xiurong, taboo name Lingying, born a Shi of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Gaozu's Ruan Xiurong, taboo name Lingying, originally surname Shi, was of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 齊始安王遙光納焉。
entries.en: Qi's Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, took her to wife.
entries.literal: Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang of Qi took her in marriage.

entries.zh: 遙光敗，入東昏宮。
entries.en: When Yaoguang fell, she was taken into the Depraved Emperor's palace.
entries.literal: When Yaoguang was defeated, she entered the Depraved Emperor's palace.

entries.zh: 建康城平，高祖納爲彩女。
entries.en: When Jiankang fell, Gaozu took her as a painted attendant.
entries.literal: When Jiankang fell, Gaozu took her as a painted attendant.

entries.zh: 天監七年八月，生世祖。
entries.en: In the eighth month, year 7 of Tianjian, she bore Shizu.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, year 7 of Tianjian, she bore Shizu.

entries.zh: 尋拜爲脩容，常隨世祖出蕃。
entries.en: Soon she was appointed Xiurong, and often followed Shizu when he went out to his fief.
entries.literal: Soon she was appointed Xiurong, and often followed Shizu when he went out to his fief.

entries.zh: 大同六年六月，薨于江州內寢，時年六十七。
entries.en: In the sixth month, year 6 of Datong, she died in the inner chamber at Jiang Province; age sixty-seven.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, year 6 of Datong, she died in the inner chamber at Jiang Province; age sixty-seven.

entries.zh: 其年十一月，歸葬江寧縣通望山。
entries.en: That year in the eleventh month she was returned for burial at Tongwang Mountain in Jiangning county.
entries.literal: That year in the eleventh month she was returned for burial at Tongwang Mountain in Jiangning county.

entries.zh: 諡曰宣。
entries.en: Posthumous title: Xuan.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Xuan.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，有司奏追崇爲文宣太后。
entries.en: When Shizu took the throne, the responsible offices memorialized to posthumously honor her as Empress Dowager Wenxuan.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, the responsible offices memorialized to posthumously honor her as Empress Dowager Wenxuan.

entries.zh: 世祖徐妃
entries.en: Shizu's Consort Xu
entries.literal: Shizu's Consort Xu

entries.zh: 世祖徐妃，諱昭佩，東海郯人也。
entries.en: Shizu's consort Xu, taboo name Zhaopei, was from Tan in Donghai.
entries.literal: Shizu's consort Xu, taboo name Zhaopei, was from Tan in Donghai.

entries.zh: 祖孝嗣，太尉、枝江文忠公。
entries.en: grandfather Xiaosi, Grand Commandant, Duke of Zhijiang the Cultured and Loyal.
entries.literal: grandfather Xiaosi, Grand Commandant, Duke of Zhijiang the Cultured and Loyal.

entries.zh: 父緄，侍中、信武將軍。
entries.en: father Chun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Trustworthy Martial General.
entries.literal: father Chun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Trustworthy Martial General.

entries.zh: 天監十六年十二月，拜湘東王妃。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, year 16 of Tianjian, she was appointed consort of the Prince of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, year 16 of Tianjian, she was appointed consort of the Prince of Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 生世子方等、益昌公主含貞。
entries.en: She bore the heir Fangdeng and Princess Yichang Hanzhen.
entries.literal: She bore the heir Fangdeng and Princess Yichang Hanzhen.

entries.zh: 太清三年五月，被譴死，葬江陵瓦官寺。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Taiqing year 3 she was put to death by imperial reproof and buried at Jiangling's Waguan Temple.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Taiping year 3, she was condemned to death and buried at Waguan Temple in Jiangling.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：后妃道贊皇風，化行天下，蓋取《葛覃》、《關雎》之義焉。
entries.en: The historian writes: Empresses and consorts should uphold the court's moral influence and civilize the realm, following the spirit of "Ge Tan" and "Kuan-chiu."
entries.literal: The historian says: The Way of empresses and consorts commends the royal wind and transforms the realm under Heaven—this broadly takes the meaning of "Ge Tan" and "Kuan-chiu."

entries.zh: 至於穆貴嬪，徽華早著，誕育元良，德懋六宮，美矣。
entries.en: Of Consort Mu the Precious: her merit shone early, she bore the heir apparent, and her virtue filled the six palaces—admirable indeed.
entries.literal: As for Consort Mu the Precious, her fine splendor showed early; she bore the heir apparent; her virtue enriched the six palaces—beautiful indeed.

entries.zh: 世祖徐妃之無行，自致殲滅，宜哉。
entries.en: Shizu's Consort Xu, for her misdeeds, destroyed herself—as was fitting.
entries.literal: As for Shizu's Consort Xu, her want of conduct brought destruction on herself—fitting indeed.

entries.zh: 太宗簡皇后王氏，諱靈賓，琅邪臨沂人也。
entries.en: Taizong's Honored Empress Wang, taboo name Lingbin, came from Linyi in Langye.
entries.literal: Taizong's Honored Empress, the Wang clan, taboo name Lingbin, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

entries.zh: 祖儉，太尉、南昌文憲公。
entries.en: Her grandfather Jian was Grand Commandant and Duke of Nanchang, posthumous name Wenxian.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Jian was Grand Commandant and Duke of Nanchang, posthumous name Wenxian.

entries.zh: 太宗王皇后
entries.en: Empress Wang of Taizong
entries.literal: Empress Wang of Taizong

entries.zh: 后幼而柔明淑德，叔父暕見之曰：「吾家女師也。」
entries.en: From youth the empress was gentle, intelligent, and virtuous. When her uncle Jian saw her, he said, "She is the model woman of our house."
entries.literal: From youth the empress was gentle, bright, and virtuous; when her uncle Jian saw her, he said, "She is the female model of our house."

entries.zh: 天監十一年，拜晉安王妃。
entries.en: In Tianjian 11, she was appointed consort of the Prince of Jin'an.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianjian, she was appointed consort of the Prince of Jin'an.

entries.zh: 生哀太子大器，南郡王大連，長山公主妙䂮。
entries.en: She bore Daqi, Crown Prince Ai, Dalian, Prince of Nanjun, and the Princess of Changshan, whose personal name was written Miao followed by the rare graph U+40AE.
entries.literal: She gave birth to Crown Prince Ai Daqi, Prince Dalian of Nanjun, and the Princess of Changshan, whose personal name was written Miao followed by the rare graph U+40AE.

entries.zh: 中大通三年十月，拜皇太子妃。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Zhongdatong 3, she was appointed crown princess.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Zhongdatong, she was appointed crown princess.

entries.zh: 太清三年三月，薨于永福省，時年四十五。
entries.en: In the third month of Taiqing 3, she died at Yongfu Office, aged forty-five.
entries.literal: In the third month of the third year of Taiqing, she died at Yongfu Office, aged forty-five.

entries.zh: 其年，太宗卽位，追崇爲皇后，諡曰簡。
entries.en: That year Taizong took the throne and posthumously honored her as empress, with the title Jian.
entries.literal: That year, when Taizong took the throne, she was posthumously exalted as empress, with the posthumous title Jian.

entries.zh: 大寶元年九月，葬莊陵。
entries.en: In the ninth month of Dabao 1, she was buried in Zhuangling.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Dabao, she was buried in Zhuangling.

entries.zh: 先是詔曰：「簡皇后窀穸有期。
entries.en: Before this, an edict said: "The time has been set for Empress Jian's burial.
entries.literal: Before this, an edict said: "The interment of Empress Jian has its appointed time.

entries.zh: 昔西京霸陵，因山爲藏；
entries.en: In the past, Baling in the Western Capital used the mountain itself as the tomb;
entries.literal: Formerly, at Baling of the Western Capital, the mountain was used as the tomb;

entries.zh: 東漢壽陵，流水而已。
entries.en: at Shouling of the Eastern Han, there was nothing more than flowing water.
entries.literal: at Shouling of the Eastern Han, there was only flowing water.

entries.zh: 朕屬值時艱，歲饑民弊，方欲以身率下，永示敦朴。
entries.en: We have met difficult times: the year is hungry and the people worn down. We wish to lead those below by personal example and show lasting sincerity and simplicity.
entries.literal: We have encountered hard times; the year is hungry and the people exhausted. We now wish to lead those below by Our own person and forever show sincerity and simplicity.

entries.zh: 今所營莊陵，務存約儉。」
entries.en: In building Zhuangling, keep strictly to restraint and frugality."
entries.literal: Now in constructing Zhuangling, be sure to preserve restraint and frugality."

entries.zh: 又詔金紫光祿大夫蕭子范爲哀策文。
entries.en: Another edict ordered Xiao Zifan, grand master for splendid happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon, to compose the mourning elegy.
entries.literal: Another edict ordered Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon Xiao Zifan to compose the mourning elegy.

entries.zh: 昭明太子 哀太子 愍懷太子
entries.en: Crown Prince Zhaoming; the Grieving Crown Prince; the Lamenting Crown Prince
entries.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming; Crown Prince Ai; Crown Prince Minhuai

entries.zh: 昭明太子統字德施，高祖長子也。
entries.en: Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong, styled Deshi, was Gaozu's eldest son.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong, styled Deshi, was Gaozu's eldest son.

entries.zh: 母曰丁貴嬪。
entries.en: His mother was Honored Concubine Ding.
entries.literal: His mother was Honored Concubine Ding.

entries.zh: 初，高祖未有男，義師起，太子以齊中興元年九月生于襄陽。
entries.en: At first Gaozu had no sons; when the righteous army arose, the crown prince was born at Xiangyang in the ninth month of Qi Zhongxing 1.
entries.literal: At first Gaozu had no sons; when the righteous army arose, the crown prince was born at Xiangyang in the ninth month of Qi Zhongxing 1.

entries.zh: 高祖旣受禪，有司奏立儲副，高祖以天下始定，百度多闕，未之許也。
entries.en: After Gaozu accepted the abdication, the offices memorialized asking to establish an heir. Because the realm had only just been settled and many institutions were still lacking, Gaozu did not yet approve it.
entries.literal: After Gaozu accepted the abdication, the offices memorialized asking to establish an heir. Because the realm had only just been settled and many institutions were still lacking, Gaozu did not yet approve it.

entries.zh: 羣臣固請，天監元年十一月，立爲皇太子。
entries.en: The assembled ministers insisted, and in the eleventh month of Tianjian 1 he was established as crown prince.
entries.literal: The assembled ministers insisted, and in the eleventh month of Tianjian 1 he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 時太子年幼，依舊居於內，拜東宮官屬文武，皆入直永福省。
entries.en: At the time the crown prince was young and continued, as before, to live inside the palace; the civil and military officials appointed to the Eastern Palace all entered on duty in Yongfu Office.
entries.literal: At the time the crown prince was young and continued, as before, to live inside the palace; the civil and military officials appointed to the Eastern Palace all entered on duty in Yongfu Office.

entries.zh: 三年三月，寢疾。
entries.en: In the third year, third month, he fell ill and took to his bed.
entries.literal: In the third year, third month, he took to his bed with illness.

entries.zh: 恐貽高祖憂，敕參問，輒自力手書啓。
entries.en: Lest he burden Gaozu with worry, he had his attendants questioned but always wrote memorials by hand himself.
entries.literal: Fearing to burden Gaozu with worry, he ordered his attendants questioned and always personally wrote memorials by hand.

entries.zh: 及稍篤，左右欲啓聞，猶不許，曰「云何令至尊知我如此惡」，因便嗚咽。
entries.en: As the illness worsened, his attendants wished to report it, but he forbade them, saying, "How can I let His Majesty know I am so gravely ill?" and wept.
entries.literal: When his illness grew somewhat severe, those beside him wished to report it, but he still would not allow it, saying "How could I let the Supreme Sovereign know I am so gravely ill," and thereupon sobbed.

entries.zh: 四月乙巳薨，時年三十一。
entries.en: On yisi of the fourth month he died, aged thirty-one.
entries.literal: On yisi of the fourth month he passed away, age thirty-one.

entries.zh: 高祖幸東宮，臨哭盡哀。
entries.en: Gaozu came to the Eastern Palace and wept there with full grief.
entries.literal: Gaozu visited the Eastern Palace and mourned there with full grief.

entries.zh: 詔斂以袞冕。
entries.en: By edict he was to be enshrouded in full imperial mourning dress.
entries.literal: Edict: bury him in full imperial mourning dress.

entries.zh: 諡曰昭明。
entries.en: His posthumous name was Zhaoming, "Luminous."
entries.literal: Posthumous name Zhaoming.

entries.zh: 五月庚寅，葬安寧陵。
entries.en: On gengyin of the fifth month he was buried at Anning Mausoleum.
entries.literal: On gengyin of the fifth month he was buried at Anning Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 詔司徒左長史王筠爲哀冊文曰：
entries.en: An edict charged Wang Yun, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, to compose the funeral elegy. It read:
entries.literal: Edict ordered Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Yun to compose the lamentation text, saying:

entries.zh: 太子美姿貌，善舉止。
entries.en: The crown prince was handsome in face and graceful in bearing.
entries.literal: The crown prince had a fine countenance and graceful bearing.

entries.zh: 讀書數行並下，過目皆憶。
entries.en: He read several lines at a glance and remembered whatever passed his eyes.
entries.literal: In reading, several lines came down together; what passed his eye he all remembered.

entries.zh: 每游宴祖道，賦詩至十數韻。
entries.en: At feasts or parting rites he would compose poems in as many as ten rhyme groups.
entries.literal: Whenever at feasts or parting rites he composed poetry to as many as ten rhyme groups.

entries.zh: 或命作劇韻賦之，皆屬思便成，無所點易。
entries.en: Sometimes ordered to improvise rhymed verse, he finished at once as thought came, without a single revision.
entries.literal: Sometimes he was ordered to make impromptu rhyme compositions and would complete them as thought flowed, with nothing to change.

entries.zh: 高祖大弘佛教，親自講說；
entries.en: Gaozu greatly promoted Buddhism and lectured on it himself;
entries.literal: Gaozu greatly spread Buddhism and personally lectured on it;

entries.zh: 太子亦崇信三寶，遍覽衆經。
entries.en: the crown prince also revered the Three Treasures and read through all the sutras.
entries.literal: the crown prince also deeply believed in the Three Treasures and read through all the sutras.

entries.zh: 乃於宮內別立慧義殿，專爲法集之所。
entries.en: He then built Huiyi Hall within the palace, set apart solely for Dharma gatherings.
entries.literal: He then within the palace separately established Huiyi Hall, devoted solely to assemblies of the Dharma.

entries.zh: 招引名僧，談論不絕。
entries.en: He drew in eminent monks, and doctrinal discussion never ceased.
entries.literal: He drew in famous monks; discussions never ceased.

entries.zh: 太子自立二諦、法身義，並有新意。
entries.en: The crown prince himself framed doctrines of the Two Truths and the Dharma-body, each with fresh insight.
entries.literal: The crown prince himself set forth doctrines of the Two Truths and Dharma-body, both with fresh meaning.

entries.zh: 普通元年四月，甘露降于慧義殿，咸以爲至德所感焉。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Putong year one sweet dew fell on Huiyi Hall; all deemed it a response to supreme virtue.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Putong, sweet dew fell on Huiyi Hall; all took it as a response to supreme virtue.

entries.zh: 太子仁德素著，及薨，朝野惋愕。
entries.en: The crown prince's humane virtue was long renowned; at his death court and countryside alike were stricken with grief.
entries.literal: The crown prince's humane virtue had long been manifest; when he passed away, court and commoners were stunned with regret.

entries.zh: 京師男女，奔走宮門，號泣滿路。
entries.en: Men and women of the capital rushed to the palace gates, wailing until the roads were full.
entries.literal: Men and women of the capital ran to the palace gates, wailing and filling the roads.

entries.zh: 四方氓庶，及疆徼之民，聞喪皆慟哭。
entries.en: Commoners in every quarter, even people on the frontier marches, wept bitterly when they heard of the mourning.
entries.literal: Common folk of the four quarters, and people of the frontier marches, hearing of the mourning all wept bitterly.

entries.zh: 所著文集二十卷；
entries.en: His collected literary works ran to twenty juan;
entries.literal: His collected literary works numbered twenty juan;

entries.zh: 又撰古今典誥文言，爲《正序》十卷；
entries.en: he also compiled ancient and modern edicts in literary language as Correct Sequence in ten juan;
entries.literal: he also compiled ancient and modern canonical edicts in literary language, making Correct Sequence in ten juan;

entries.zh: 五言詩之善者，爲《文章英華》二十卷；
entries.en: his finest five-character poems he gathered as Literary Flowers in twenty juan;
entries.literal: the finest of his five-character poems he made Literary Flowers in twenty juan;

entries.zh: 《文選》三十卷。
entries.en: Literary Selections in thirty juan.
entries.literal: Literary Selections in thirty juan.

entries.zh: 性寬和容衆，喜慍不形於色。
entries.en: By nature magnanimous and accommodating, pleasure and anger never showed on his face.
entries.literal: By nature magnanimous and accommodating the multitude, pleasure and anger never showed on his face.

entries.zh: 引納才學之士，賞愛無倦。
entries.en: He drew in men of talent and learning and cherished them without tiring.
entries.literal: He drew in talented and learned men and cherished and rewarded without tiring.

entries.zh: 恒自討論篇籍，或與學士商榷古今；
entries.en: He constantly discussed texts himself, or weighed past and present with academicians;
entries.literal: He constantly himself discussed books and records, or with academicians weighed past and present;

entries.zh: 閒則繼以文章著述，率以爲常。
entries.en: in leisure he wrote, taking composition as his daily habit.
entries.literal: in leisure he followed with literary composition and writing, taking it as his constant way.

entries.zh: 于時東宮有書幾三萬卷，名才並集，文學之盛，晉、宋以來未之有也。
entries.en: The Eastern Palace then held nearly thirty thousand volumes; eminent talents gathered; literary brilliance unmatched since Jin and Song.
entries.literal: At that time the Eastern Palace had books approaching thirty thousand volumes; famous talents all gathered; the flourishing of letters had not been seen since Jin and Song.

entries.zh: 太子生而聰叡，三歲受《孝經》、《論語》，五歲遍讀五經，悉能諷誦。
entries.en: The crown prince was bright from birth; at three he studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, at five he had read the Five Classics through and could recite them all.
entries.literal: From birth the crown prince was clever and perspicacious; at three he received the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, at five he read through the Five Classics in full and could all chant them from memory.

entries.zh: 五年五月庚戌，始出居東宮。
entries.en: In year five, on the fifth month's gengxu day, he first took up residence in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, fifth month, day gengxu, he first went out to dwell in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 太子性仁孝，自出宮，恒思戀不樂。
entries.en: By nature the crown prince was humane and filial; once he left the palace grounds he pined constantly and was never at ease.
entries.literal: The crown prince by nature was humane and filial; from leaving the palace he constantly thought longingly and was unhappy.

entries.zh: 高祖知之，每五日一朝，多便留永福省，或五日三日乃還宮。
entries.en: Gaozu knew it: court was held every five days, and he often kept the heir at Yongfu Ward—or only let him return after three or five days.
entries.literal: Gaozu knew this; every fifth day he attended court once, often keeping him at Yongfu Ward, sometimes five days or three before returning to the palace.

entries.zh: 八年九月，於壽安殿講《孝經》，盡通大義。
entries.en: In the ninth month of year eight he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Shou'an Hall and mastered its main meaning.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year, at Shou'an Hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and fully penetrated its great meaning.

entries.zh: 講畢，親臨釋奠于國學。
entries.en: When the lecture ended he personally offered the libation sacrifice at the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: When the lecture ended, he personally performed the libation sacrifice at the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 三年十一月，始興王憺薨。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of year three Prince Dan of Shixing died.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, Prince Dan of Shixing died.

entries.zh: 舊事，以東宮禮絕傍親，書翰並依常儀。
entries.en: Formerly, because Eastern Palace ritual severs collateral kin, letters and memorials all followed ordinary usage.
entries.literal: By former precedent, because Eastern Palace ritual cuts off collateral kin, letters and memorials all followed ordinary rites.

entries.zh: 太子意以爲疑，命僕劉孝綽議其事。
entries.en: The crown prince found this doubtful and ordered his secretary Liu Xiaochuo to deliberate it.
entries.literal: The crown prince thought this doubtful and ordered his secretary Liu Xiaochuo to deliberate the matter.

entries.zh: 孝綽議曰：「案張鏡撰《東宮儀記》，稱『三朝發哀者，逾月不舉樂；
entries.en: Xiaochuo wrote: "Zhang Jing's Eastern Palace Ritual Record says, 'For mourning begun at the three audiences, for more than a month music is not performed;
entries.literal: Xiaochuo's deliberation said: "According to Zhang Jing's compilation Eastern Palace Ritual Record, it states, 'For those who begin mourning at the three audiences, for more than a month music is not performed;

entries.zh: 鼓吹寢奏，服限亦然』。
entries.en: drums and pipes cease, and the dress limit is the same.'"
entries.literal: drums and pipes cease performance, and the limit on dress is likewise.'"

entries.zh: 尋傍絕之義，義在去服，服雖可奪，情豈無悲？
entries.en: The sense of severing collateral kin is that mourning dress ends; dress may be removed, but feeling cannot be stripped of grief.
entries.literal: Seeking the meaning of cutting off collateral kin, the meaning lies in removing mourning dress; dress may be stripped away, but can feeling be without grief?

entries.zh: 鐃歌輟奏，良亦爲此。
entries.en: Halting gongs and songs is truly for this reason as well.
entries.literal: The striking of gongs and songs ceasing performance is truly also for this.

entries.zh: 旣有悲情，宜稱兼慕，卒哭之後，依常舉樂，稱悲竟，此理例相符。
entries.en: Where grief remains, one should call it combined mourning; after the wailing sacrifice music may resume as usual, grief being ended—principle and precedent agree.
entries.literal: Since there is feeling of grief, one should style it "combined mourning"; after the wailing sacrifice, follow custom in performing music, calling grief ended—this principle and precedent accord.

entries.zh: 謂猶應稱兼慕，至卒哭。」
entries.en: He held that combined mourning should still be named until the wailing sacrifice."
entries.literal: It is held that one should still style it combined mourning until the wailing sacrifice."

entries.zh: 僕射徐勉、左率周舍、家令陸襄並同孝綽議。
entries.en: Vice Director Xu Mian, Left Leader Zhou She, and Household Intendant Lu Xiang all sided with Xiaochuo.
entries.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian, Left Leader Zhou She, and Household Intendant Lu Xiang all agreed with Xiaochuo's deliberation.

entries.zh: 太子令曰：「張鏡《儀記》云『依《士禮》，終服月稱慕悼』。
entries.en: The crown prince ordered: "Zhang Jing's Ritual Record says, 'Per the Rites of the Scholar, after full mourning for a month one styles mourning tribute.
entries.literal: The crown prince's order said: "Zhang Jing's Ritual Record says, 'According to the Rites of the Scholar, after full mourning for a month one styles mourning tribute.

entries.zh: 又云『凡三朝發哀者，逾月不舉樂』。
entries.en: It also says, 'For all who begin mourning at the three audiences, for more than a month music is not performed.'"
entries.literal: It also says, 'For all who begin mourning at the three audiences, for more than a month music is not performed.'"

entries.zh: 劉僕議，云『傍絕之義，義在去服，服雖可奪，情豈無悲，卒哭之後，依常舉樂，稱悲竟，此理例相符』。
entries.en: Secretary Liu says, 'Severing collateral kin means mourning dress ends; dress may go, but grief cannot; after the wailing sacrifice music resumes as usual, grief ended—principle and precedent agree.'"
entries.literal: Secretary Liu's deliberation says, 'The meaning of cutting off collateral kin lies in removing mourning dress; dress may be stripped away, but can feeling be without grief? After the wailing sacrifice, follow custom in performing music, calling grief ended—this principle and precedent accord.'"

entries.zh: 尋情悲之說，非止卒哭之後，緣情爲論，此自難一也。
entries.en: On feeling grief, the issue is not only after the wailing sacrifice; arguing from feeling alone, this is hard to unify.
entries.literal: Seeking the doctrine of feeling grief, it is not only after the wailing sacrifice; taking feeling as the argument, this itself is hard to unify.

entries.zh: 用張鏡之舉樂，棄張鏡之稱悲，一鏡之言，取捨有異，此自難二也。
entries.en: To take Zhang Jing's music while dropping his grief styling—in one author's words the choices conflict; this is the second difficulty.
entries.literal: To use Zhang Jing's performing of music while abandoning Zhang Jing's styling of grief—in one mirror's words, taking and discarding differ; this itself is hard, second.

entries.zh: 陸家令止云『多歷年所』，恐非事證；
entries.en: Lu the Household Intendant only cited 'many years'—I fear that is not proof;
entries.literal: Household Intendant Lu only said 'for many years'—I fear this is not evidence of the matter;

entries.zh: 雖復累稔所用，意常未安。
entries.en: though long in use, the mind has never been easy with it.
entries.literal: though used for accumulated years, in mind one has never been at ease.

entries.zh: 近亦常經以此問外，由來立意，謂猶應有慕悼之言。
entries.en: Lately this has often been asked outside court; from the first the intent has been that mourning tribute should still be named.
entries.literal: Recently one has also often passed this question outward; from the outset the established intent has been that there should still be words of mourning tribute.

entries.zh: 張豈不知舉樂爲大，稱悲事小；
entries.en: Surely Zhang knew performing music was the greater matter and styling grief the lesser.
entries.literal: How could Zhang not know that performing music is great and styling grief a small matter?

entries.zh: 所以用小而忽大，良亦有以。
entries.en: He used the lesser and set aside the greater for good reason.
entries.literal: The reason for using the small and neglecting the great truly also has its grounds.

entries.zh: 至如元正六佾，事爲國章；
entries.en: As for New Year's six rows of dancers, the affair is a state statute;
entries.literal: As for the first of the year with six rows of dancers, the affair is a statute of the state;

entries.zh: 雖情或未安，而禮不可廢。
entries.en: though feeling may be uneasy, ritual cannot be set aside.
entries.literal: though feeling may not be at ease, ritual cannot be abandoned.

entries.zh: 鐃吹軍樂，比之亦然。
entries.en: Gongs, pipes, and military music stand on the same footing.
entries.literal: Gongs, pipes, and military music are comparable in the same way.

entries.zh: 書疏方之，事則成小，差可緣心。
entries.en: Letters and memorials are the smaller affair and may somewhat follow the heart.
entries.literal: Compared with letters and memorials, the affair is then smaller and may somewhat follow the heart.

entries.zh: 聲樂自外，書疏自內，樂自他，書自己。
entries.en: Music comes from outside; letters come from within—music from others, letters from oneself.
entries.literal: Music and sound come from without; letters and memorials come from within; music from others, letters from oneself.

entries.zh: 劉僕射之議，卽情未安。
entries.en: Vice Director Liu's view leaves feeling uneasy.
entries.literal: Vice Director Liu's deliberation—feeling is not at ease.

entries.zh: 可令諸賢更共詳衷。」
entries.en: Let the worthies deliberate further to the end."
entries.literal: Let the various worthies together deliberate further to the end."

entries.zh: 司農卿明山賓、步兵校尉朱异議，稱「慕悼之解，宜終服月」。
entries.en: Director of Agriculture Ming Shanbin and Colonel of Footsoldiers Zhu Yi deliberated, stating, "The interpretation of mourning tribute should run through the month of full mourning."
entries.literal: Director of Agriculture Ming Shanbin and Colonel of Footsoldiers Zhu Yi deliberated, stating, "The interpretation of mourning tribute should run through the month of full mourning."

entries.zh: 於是令付典書遵用，以爲永凖。
entries.en: The order was then handed to the Director of Documents for permanent use as standard.
entries.literal: Thereupon the order was handed to the Director of Documents to follow in use, taken as everlasting standard.

entries.zh: 十四年正月朔旦，高祖臨軒，冠太子于太極殿。
entries.en: At dawn on New Year's Day of year fourteen Gaozu faced the hall and capped the crown prince in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: On the first morning of the first month of the fourteenth year, Gaozu faced the hall and capped the crown prince in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 舊制，太子著遠遊冠，金蟬翠緌纓；
entries.en: By old custom the crown prince wore the Far-Wandering cap with golden cicada and emerald tassels and ribbons;
entries.literal: By old regulation the crown prince wore the Far-Wandering cap, with golden cicada and emerald tassels and ribbons;

entries.zh: 至是，詔加金博山。
entries.en: now an edict added the golden Boshan ornament.
entries.literal: at this time an edict added the golden Boshan ornament.

entries.zh: 太子自加元服，高祖便使省萬機，內外百司，奏事者填塞於前。
entries.en: After his capping Gaozu had him review myriad affairs; memorialists from every office filled the forecourt.
entries.literal: From the time the crown prince himself added the capping ceremony, Gaozu had him review the myriad affairs; within and without the hundred offices, those memorializing filled the space before him.

entries.zh: 太子明於庶事，纖毫必曉，每所奏有謬誤及巧妄，皆卽就辯析，示其可否，徐令改正，未嘗彈糾一人。
entries.en: The crown prince knew common affairs down to the finest strand; whenever a memorial erred or lied, he analyzed it on the spot, showed what stood, ordered correction without haste, and never punished anyone.
entries.literal: The crown prince was clear on common affairs; the finest strand he always understood. Whenever what was memorialized had error or crafty falsehood, he at once went to analyze and show what might or might not be so, slowly ordered correction, and never once punished a person.

entries.zh: 平斷法獄，多所全宥，天下皆稱仁。
entries.en: In judging legal cases he often spared lives; all under Heaven called him humane.
entries.literal: In leveling and deciding legal cases he often fully pardoned; all under Heaven called him humane.

entries.zh: 七年十一月，貴嬪有疾，太子還永福省，朝夕侍疾，衣不解帶。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of year seven the honored consort fell ill; the crown prince returned to Yongfu Ward and tended her day and night without loosening his belt.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year the honored consort fell ill; the crown prince returned to Yongfu Ward, attending her morning and evening, his clothes' belt never loosened.

entries.zh: 及薨，步從喪還宮，至殯，水漿不入口，每哭輒慟絕。
entries.en: When she died he walked behind the coffin back to the palace; through the lying-in-state he took no food or drink, and each cry ended in collapse.
entries.literal: When she died he walked behind the coffin back to the palace; until the lying-in-state he took no food or drink, and each lament ended in fainting.

entries.zh: 高祖遣中書舍人顧協宣旨曰：「毀不滅性，聖人之制。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Palace Secretary Gu Xie with an edict: "Self-destruction does not extinguish nature—the sage's rule.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Palace Secretary Gu Xie to proclaim the intent: "Destroying oneself does not extinguish one's nature—this is the sage's regulation.

entries.zh: 《禮》，不勝喪比於不孝。
entries.en: The Rites say failing to bear mourning ranks with unfilial conduct.
entries.literal: The Rites say that not bearing up under mourning is classed with unfilial conduct.

entries.zh: 有我在，那得自毀如此！
entries.en: While I still live, how can you destroy yourself so!
entries.literal: While I am here, how can you destroy yourself thus!

entries.zh: 可卽強進飲食。」
entries.en: Force yourself to eat and drink at once."
entries.literal: You must at once force yourself to take food and drink."

entries.zh: 太子奉勅，乃進數合。
entries.en: The crown prince obeyed and took a few mouthfuls.
entries.literal: The crown prince received the command and then took several mouthfuls.

entries.zh: 自是至葬，日進麥粥一升。
entries.en: From then until burial he took only one sheng of wheat porridge a day.
entries.literal: From then until the burial he daily took one sheng of wheat porridge.

entries.zh: 高祖又勅曰：「聞汝所進過少，轉就羸瘵。
entries.en: Gaozu commanded again: "I hear you eat too little and grow wasted and ill.
entries.literal: Gaozu again commanded: "I hear what you take is too little and you are turning wasted and ill.

entries.zh: 我比更無餘病，正爲汝如此，胸中亦圮塞成疾。
entries.en: I have no other sickness—only because of you my chest clogs into illness.
entries.literal: I lately have no other illness—only because of you thus does my breast also clog and become diseased.

entries.zh: 故應強加饘粥，不使我恒爾懸心。」
entries.en: So force more gruel and porridge on yourself and do not keep my heart always suspended."
entries.literal: Therefore you should force yourself to take more gruel and porridge, and not make me always hang my heart thus."

entries.zh: 雖屢奉勅勸逼，日止一溢，不嚐菜果之味。
entries.en: Though repeatedly urged by edict, daily he took only one yi and tasted no vegetables or fruit.
entries.literal: Though repeatedly receiving commands to urge and compel, daily he stopped at one yi and did not taste vegetables or fruit.

entries.zh: 體素壯，腰帶十圍，至是減削過半。
entries.en: His frame had been sturdy, his waist ten encirclements; by then more than half was gone.
entries.literal: His constitution had been robust, his waist belt ten encirclements; by then it was reduced by more than half.

entries.zh: 每入朝，士庶見者莫不下泣。
entries.en: Whenever he entered court, officials and commoners who saw him wept.
entries.literal: Whenever he entered court, scholars and commoners who saw him none failed to weep below.

entries.zh: 吳興郡屢以水災失收，有上言當漕大瀆以瀉浙江。
entries.en: Wuxing commandery repeatedly lost its harvest to floods; a memorial proposed dredging the Grand Canal to drain the Zhe River.
entries.literal: Wuxing commandery repeatedly because of flood disaster lost harvest; someone memorialized that the Grand Canal should be dredged to drain into the Zhe River.

entries.zh: 中大通二年春，詔遣前交州刺史王弁假節，發吳郡、吳興、義興三郡民丁就役。
entries.en: In spring of Zhongdatong year two an edict sent former Inspector of Jiaozhou Wang Bian with credentials to levy labor from Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing commanderies.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year of Zhongdatong, an edict sent former Inspector of Jiaozhou Wang Bian with credentials to mobilize civilian labor from the three commanderies Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing for the work.

entries.zh: 太子上疏曰：「伏聞當發王弁等上東三郡民丁，開漕溝渠，導泄震澤，使吳興一境，無復水災，誠矜恤之至仁，經略之遠旨。
entries.en: The crown prince memorialized: "I hear Wang Bian and others are to levy labor from the three eastern commanderies, open canals, drain Zhen Marsh, and end floods in Wuxing commandery—truly utmost humane care and far-sighted policy.
entries.literal: The crown prince memorialized: "I hear that Wang Dan and others are to be sent to mobilize civilian labor from the three eastern commanderies, open and dredge canals and ditches, guide and release Zhen Marsh, so that within Wu commandery there will never again be flood disaster—truly the utmost humane care and a far-reaching plan of statecraft.

entries.zh: 暫勞永逸，必獲後利。
entries.en: Temporary toil for lasting ease will surely bring later profit.
entries.literal: Temporary labor for lasting ease—surely afterward benefit will be obtained.

entries.zh: 未萌難覩，竊有愚懷。
entries.en: What has not yet sprouted is hard to foresee; I venture a humble thought.
entries.literal: What is not yet sprouted is hard to see; I venture a foolish thought.

entries.zh: 所聞吳興累年失收，民頗流移。
entries.en: I hear Wuxing commandery has lost harvest year after year and many people have wandered away.
entries.literal: What I hear is that Wu commandery for successive years has lost harvest and the people have quite wandered away.

entries.zh: 吳郡十城，亦不全熟。
entries.en: Of Wu commandery's ten cities, not all ripened fully.
entries.literal: Of Wu commandery's ten cities, not all fully ripened.

entries.zh: 唯義興去秋有稔，復非常役之民。
entries.en: Only Yixing had a full harvest last autumn, and even there the people are not those of ordinary corvée.
entries.literal: Only Yixing last autumn had a full harvest, yet again not people of ordinary corvée.

entries.zh: 卽日東境穀稼猶貴，劫盜屢起，在所有司，不皆聞奏。
entries.en: Just now grain in the eastern region is still dear and banditry keeps arising; not every office reports it.
entries.literal: Just now in the eastern region grain is still dear and robbery repeatedly arises; those in office everywhere do not all hear and report.

entries.zh: 今征戍未歸，強丁疏少，此雖小舉，竊恐難合，吏一呼門，動爲民蠹。
entries.en: Now the garrisons have not returned and strong men are few; though this is a small levy, I fear it will not cohere—one shout from an official at the door becomes a plague on the people.
entries.literal: Now the expedition garrisons have not returned and strong men are few and scattered; though this is a small mobilization, I fear it will be hard to combine—one call from an official at the door and it moves as a plague on the people.

entries.zh: 又出丁之處，遠近不一，比得齊集，已妨蠶農。
entries.en: Also the places levying labor lie at uneven distances; by the time men are gathered, silkworm season is already harmed.
entries.literal: Also the places sending out labor are far and near not one; by the time they are gathered together, silkworm farming is already harmed.

entries.zh: 去年稱爲豊歲，公私未能足食；
entries.en: Last year was called abundant, yet public and private stores were still not full;
entries.literal: Last year was called a abundant year, yet public and private could not yet fully eat;

entries.zh: 如復今茲失業，慮恐爲弊更深。
entries.en: if this year loses livelihood again, I fear the harm will go deeper.
entries.literal: if again this year loses livelihood, I fear the harm will be deeper.

entries.zh: 且草竊多伺候民間虛實，若善人從役，則抄盜彌增，吳興未受其益，內地已罹其弊。
entries.en: Moreover bandits often watch whether the people are weak or strong; if good men are conscripted, robbery only increases—Wuxing commandery will not yet gain, while the interior will already suffer.
entries.literal: Moreover grass bandits often watch the people's emptiness and fullness; if good people go to corvée, then robbery and plunder increase all the more—Wu commandery will not yet receive the benefit, while the interior will already suffer the harm.

entries.zh: 不審可得權停此功，待優實以不？
entries.en: Might this work be paused for now until prosperity returns?
entries.literal: I do not know whether this work may be temporarily halted, to wait until prosperity is full or not?

entries.zh: 聖心垂矜黎庶，神量久已有在。
entries.en: The sovereign heart cherishes the common people; divine foresight already has its place.
entries.literal: The sage heart bends in pity on the black-haired people; divine measure long since already has its place.

entries.zh: 臣意見庸淺，不識事宜，苟有愚心，願得上啓。」
entries.en: My views are shallow and I scarcely grasp affairs of state; yet if I may offer whatever poor counsel I have, I beg leave to submit it."
entries.literal: Your servant's views are shallow and dull, ignorant of what the times require; if there is any foolish thought, I wish to present it above."

entries.zh: 高祖優詔以喻焉。
entries.en: Gaozu replied with a gracious edict explaining his intent.
entries.literal: Gaozu issued a gracious edict to explain his intent.

entries.zh: 性愛山水，於玄圃穿築，更立亭館，與朝士名素者遊其中。
entries.en: He loved landscape; in the Mystic Garden he excavated and built pavilions and lodges, roaming with noted courtiers.
entries.literal: He loved mountains and waters; in the Mystic Garden he dug and built, further establishing pavilions and lodges, roaming there with court gentlemen of established name.

entries.zh: 嘗泛舟後池，番禺侯軌盛稱「此中宜奏女樂。」
entries.en: Once boating on the rear pool, the Marquis of Panyu Gui said, "This is the place for female musicians."
entries.literal: Once he floated on the rear pool; the Marquis of Panyu Gui greatly praised, "Here one ought to present female music."

entries.zh: 太子不答，詠左思《招隱詩》曰：「何必絲與竹，山水有清音。」
entries.en: The crown prince did not answer but recited Zuo Si's "Summoning the Recluse": "Why silk and bamboo? Mountains and waters have clear sound."
entries.literal: The crown prince did not answer but chanted Zuo Si's "Summoning the Recluse": "Why need silk and bamboo? Mountains and waters have clear sound."

entries.zh: 侯慚而止。
entries.en: The marquis, ashamed, fell silent.
entries.literal: The marquis, ashamed, stopped.

entries.zh: 出宮二十餘年，不畜聲樂。
entries.en: For more than twenty years after leaving the palace he kept no musicians.
entries.literal: For more than twenty years after leaving the palace he kept no music.

entries.zh: 少時，敕賜太樂女妓一部，略非所好。
entries.en: In youth an edict granted him a troupe of imperial music girls—barely to his taste.
entries.literal: In youth an edict granted him one troupe of the Grand Music Office's female performers—barely what he favored.

entries.zh: 普通中，大軍北討，京師穀貴，太子因命菲衣減膳，改常饌爲小食。
entries.en: During Putong the great army marched north, grain in the capital grew dear, and the crown prince ordered plain dress and frugal meals, changing his usual fare to small repasts.
entries.literal: In Putong, the great army campaigned north; in the capital grain was dear; the crown prince therefore ordered plain clothes and reduced meals, changing the usual fare to small repasts.

entries.zh: 每霖雨積雪，遣腹心左右，周行閭巷，視貧困家，有流離道路，密加振賜。
entries.en: Whenever rain or snow lingered, he sent trusted aides through lanes and alleys to find the poor and those wandering the roads and secretly gave relief.
entries.literal: Whenever long rain accumulated snow, he sent trusted intimates left and right to circle the lanes and alleys, viewing poor households; where any wandered the roads, he secretly added relief and gifts.

entries.zh: 又出主衣綿帛，多作襦袴，冬月以施貧凍。
entries.en: He also issued palace silk and cloth, made many jackets and trousers, and in winter gave them to the poor and cold.
entries.literal: He also issued the palace's silk and cloth, making many jackets and trousers, in winter months giving them to the poor and frozen.

entries.zh: 若死亡無可以斂者，爲備棺槥。
entries.en: For those who died with nothing to enshroud them, he provided coffins.
entries.literal: If any died with nothing to enshroud them, he prepared coffins.

entries.zh: 每聞遠近百姓賦役勤苦，輒斂容色。
entries.en: Whenever he heard of the people's tax and corvée burdens near or far, his face grew grave.
entries.literal: Whenever he heard that common people far and near suffered bitter labor from taxes and corvée, he immediately composed his countenance.

entries.zh: 常以戶口未實，重於勞擾。
entries.en: He constantly worried that household registers were incomplete and that labor pressed too hard.
entries.literal: He constantly took household registers as not yet full and weighed heavily on labor and disturbance.

entries.zh: 太子孝謹天至，每入朝，未五鼓便守城門開。
entries.en: The crown prince was naturally filial and dutiful; before the fifth watch each morning he was already waiting at the city gate for it to open.
entries.literal: The crown prince was filial, careful, and heaven-endowed in nature; each time he entered court, before the fifth watch he was already waiting at the city gate for it to open.

entries.zh: 東宮雖燕居內殿，一坐一起，恒向西南面臺。
entries.en: Even in the Eastern Palace's inner halls at ease, he always faced southwest toward the terrace whenever he sat or rose.
entries.literal: Though residing at leisure in the inner halls of the Eastern Palace, with every sitting and rising he always faced southwest toward the terrace.

entries.zh: 宿被召當入，危坐達旦。
entries.en: When summoned the night before an audience, he sat upright until dawn.
entries.literal: If summoned to enter on the eve before, he sat upright through until dawn.

entries.zh: 蜃輅俄軒，龍驂跼步；
entries.en: The shell-bedecked carriage rises; dragon-harnessed steeds pace in solemn tread;
entries.literal: The clam-shell carriage swiftly lifts; dragon-trained steeds step in constrained pace;

entries.zh: 羽翿前驅，雲旂北御。
entries.en: feathered fans lead the way; cloud banners bear him north.
entries.literal: feather fans proceed before; cloud banners drive northward.

entries.zh: 皇帝哀繼明之寢耀，痛嗣德之殂芳；
entries.en: The emperor mourns his heir's fading radiance and the withering of a successor's virtue;
entries.literal: The emperor mourns the waning radiance of the heir apparent, grieves the withering fragrance of the successor's virtue;

entries.zh: 御武帳而淒慟，臨甲觀而增傷。
entries.en: he stands desolate beneath the martial canopy; sorrow deepens before the armored watchtower.
entries.literal: before the martial canopy he is desolate in grief; before the armored watchtower his sorrow deepens.

entries.zh: 式稽令典，載揚鴻烈；
entries.en: He consults the established canon and raises his great merit;
entries.literal: Consulting the established canon, he raises the great merit;

entries.zh: 詔撰德於旌旒，永傳徽於舞綴。
entries.en: an edict commands his virtue inscribed on the pennants, his emblem forever borne in the dance tassels.
entries.literal: edict commands virtue to be written on the pennants, that his emblem may forever be transmitted in the dance tassels.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The text reads:
entries.literal: The text says:

entries.zh: 皇情悼愍，切心纏痛；
entries.en: The emperor's heart is stricken with grief, wound about in pain;
entries.literal: The emperor's heart is stricken with grief, his heart wound about in pain;

entries.zh: 胤嗣長號，跗萼增慟。
entries.en: the heir's descendants wail long; calyx and petals add to the grief.
entries.literal: the heir's descendants wail long, the calyx and petals add to the grief.

entries.zh: 慕結親遊，悲動氓衆；
entries.en: Longing binds close companions; grief moves the common people;
entries.literal: Longing binds close companions, grief moves the common people;

entries.zh: 憂若殄邦，懼同折棟。
entries.en: sorrow as if the state were perishing; fear as if the ridgepole were breaking.
entries.literal: sorrow as if the state were perishing, fear as if the ridgepole were breaking.

entries.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
entries.en: Alas, how mournful!
entries.literal: Alas, how mournful!

entries.zh: 太清二年十月，侯景寇京邑，敕太子爲臺內大都督。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Taqing year 2 Hou Jing attacked the capital; by edict the crown prince became Grand Commander within the Terrace.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of Taqing year 2, Hou Jing raided the capital; an edict made the crown prince Grand Commander within the Terrace.

entries.zh: 三年五月，太宗卽位。
entries.en: In the fifth month of year 3 Taizong took the throne.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Taizong took the throne.

entries.zh: 六月丁亥，立爲皇太子。
entries.en: On dinghai of the sixth month he was established crown prince.
entries.literal: On dinghai of the sixth month he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 大寶二年八月，賊景廢太宗，將害太子，時賊黨稱景命召太子，太子方講《老子》，將欲下床，而刑人掩至。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Dabao year 2 the rebel Jing deposed Taizong and meant to kill the crown prince; Jing's men claimed an order from Jing summoned him. The crown prince was lecturing on the Laozi and was rising from his couch when executioners burst in.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Dabao year 2 the rebel Jing deposed Taizong and was about to kill the crown prince; at that time Jing's partisans claimed Jing's order summoned the crown prince. The crown prince was lecturing on the Laozi and was about to rise from the couch when the executioners suddenly arrived.

entries.zh: 太子顏色不變，徐曰：「久知此事，嗟其晚耳。」
entries.en: The crown prince's face did not change; he said calmly, "I have long known this—only that it comes so late."
entries.literal: The crown prince's countenance did not change; he said slowly: "I have long known this—alas that it comes so late."

entries.zh: 刑者欲以衣帶絞之。
entries.en: The executioners meant to strangle him with his sash.
entries.literal: The executioners wished to strangle him with his sash.

entries.zh: 太子曰：「此不能見殺。」
entries.en: The crown prince said, "That will not do to kill me."
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "That cannot serve to kill me."

entries.zh: 乃指繫帳竿下繩，命取絞之而絕，時年二十八。
entries.en: He pointed to the rope on the tent pole and ordered them to take it and strangle him; he was twenty-eight.
entries.literal: He then pointed to the rope beneath the tent pole and ordered it taken to strangle him to death; he was then twenty-eight.

entries.zh: 太子性寬和，兼神用端嶷，在於賊手，每不屈意。
entries.en: By nature the crown prince was mild and harmonious, with a dignified spirit and bearing; even in rebel hands he never bent his will.
entries.literal: The crown prince by nature was mild and harmonious, and also of dignified spirit and bearing; in the rebels' hands he never bent his will.

entries.zh: 初，侯景西上，攜太子同行，及其敗歸，部伍不復整肅，太子所乘船居後，不及賊衆，左右心腹並勸因此入北。
entries.en: At first, when Hou Jing marched west he took the crown prince along; when defeated on his return the ranks were no longer disciplined. The crown prince's boat fell behind the rebel host, and his close attendants all urged him to seize the chance and flee north.
entries.literal: At first, when Hou Jing marched west, he took the crown prince with him; when he was defeated and returned, the ranks were no longer in good order. The crown prince's boat lagged behind and could not keep up with the rebel host; his close attendants and trusted followers all urged him to take this chance to flee north.

entries.zh: 太子曰：「家國喪敗，志不圖生；
entries.en: The crown prince said, "House and state are ruined—I have no wish to live;
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "House and state are ruined—I have no thought of living;

entries.zh: 主上蒙塵，寧忍違離？
entries.en: the sovereign is lost in hardship—how could I bear to leave him?
entries.literal: the sovereign suffers dust and hardship—how could I bear to leave him?

entries.zh: 吾今逃匿，乃是叛父，非謂避賊。」
entries.en: If I flee and hide now, I rebel against my father; it is not merely to avoid bandits."
entries.literal: If I flee and hide now, I am rebelling against my father, not merely avoiding bandits."

entries.zh: 便涕泗鳴咽，令卽前進。
entries.en: He wept aloud and ordered them to press forward at once.
entries.literal: Thereupon he wept and sobbed aloud and ordered them to press forward at once.

entries.zh: 賊以太子有器度，每常憚之，恐爲後患，故先及禍。
entries.en: The rebels, seeing the crown prince's bearing and capacity, always feared him; dreading future trouble, they struck at him first.
entries.literal: The rebels, because the crown prince had bearing and capacity, always feared him and, dreading future trouble, struck at him first.

entries.zh: 承聖元年四月，追諡哀太子。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Chengsheng year 1 he was posthumously titled Lamented Crown Prince.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Chengsheng year 1 he was posthumously titled Lamented Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 愍懷太子方矩，字德規，世祖第四子也。
entries.en: Crown Prince Minhuai, Fangju, styled Degui, was Shizu's fourth son.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Fangju, styled Degui, was Shizu's fourth son.

entries.zh: 初封南安縣侯，隨世祖在荊鎮。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an county and accompanied Shizu at his Jingzhou garrison.
entries.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an county and accompanied Shizu at his Jingzhou garrison.

entries.zh: 太清初，爲使持節、督湘郢桂寧成合羅七州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taiqing, he became Envoy Holding Credentials, commander of military affairs in the seven provinces of Xiang, Ying, Gui, Ning, Cheng, He, and Luo, General Who Pacifies the South, and inspector of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing, he became Envoy Holding Credentials, commander of military affairs in the seven provinces of Xiang, Ying, Gui, Ning, Cheng, He, and Luo, General Who Pacifies the South, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 尋𢖜爲侍中、中衛將軍，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was soon summoned to be Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Guard, and was granted one corps of drummers and pipers.
entries.literal: He was soon summoned to be Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Guard, and was granted one corps of drummers and pipers.

entries.zh: 世祖承制，拜王太子，改名元良。
entries.en: When Shizu acted under imperial mandate, he appointed him princely heir and changed his name to Yuanliang.
entries.literal: When Shizu acted under imperial mandate, he appointed him princely heir and changed his name to Yuanliang.

entries.zh: 承聖元年十一月丙子，立爲皇太子。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Chengsheng 1, on bingzi day, he was established as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of Chengsheng 1, on bingzi day, he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: 及西魏師陷荊城，太子與世祖同爲魏人所害。
entries.en: When the Western Wei army captured Jingcheng, the crown prince and Shizu were both killed by the Wei.
entries.literal: When the Western Wei army captured Jingcheng, the crown prince and Shizu were both killed by the Wei.

entries.zh: 太子聰穎，頗有世祖風，而凶暴猜忌。
entries.en: The crown prince was clever and keen, much in Shizu's manner, yet fierce, violent, and suspicious.
entries.literal: The crown prince was clever and keen, quite in Shizu's manner, yet fierce, violent, and suspicious.

entries.zh: 敬帝承制，追諡愍懷太子。
entries.en: Emperor Jing, acting on imperial mandate, posthumously titled him Crown Prince Minhuai.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing, acting under imperial mandate, posthumously titled him Crown Prince Minhuai.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第八 列傳第二
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume Eight, Biographies, Second
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 8, Biographies 2

entries.zh: 茂年數歲，爲大父深所異，常謂親識曰：「此吾家之千里駒，成門戶者必此兒也。」
entries.en: While Mao was still a child, his grandfather Shen singled him out and often told friends: "This boy is our thousand-li colt—the one who will uphold our house."
entries.literal: When Mao was only a few years old, his grandfather Shen regarded him as extraordinary and often told acquaintances: "This boy is our family's thousand-li colt; he who will uphold our house must be this child."

entries.zh: 及長，好讀兵書，駁略究其大旨。
entries.en: When he came of age he loved military texts and broadly mastered their essentials.
entries.literal: When he grew up, he loved reading books of war and broadly grasped their main purport.

entries.zh: 性沈隱，不妄交遊，身長八尺，潔白美容觀。
entries.en: Reserved by nature, he made no casual friendships; eight chi tall, fair and striking in looks.
entries.literal: By nature reserved and self-contained, he did not casually associate; he stood eight chi tall, fair-skinned and handsome in appearance.

entries.zh: 齊武帝布衣時，見之歎曰：「王茂年少，堂堂如此，必爲公輔之器。」
entries.en: Before Emperor Wu of Qi took the throne, he saw Mao and sighed: "So young, yet so imposing—he will surely reach the highest offices."
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Qi was still in plain dress, seeing him he sighed and said: "Wang Mao is young, yet so imposing; he will surely be minister and counselor material."

entries.zh: 宋昇明末，起家奉朝請，歷後軍行參軍，司空騎兵，太尉中兵參軍。
entries.en: At the end of Song's Shengming era he entered office as an Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, cavalry officer to the Minister of Works, and aide for inner troops to the Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and went on to serve as Rear Army Aide, Cavalry Officer to the Minister of Works, and Inner Troops Aide to the Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 魏將李烏奴寇漢中，茂受詔西討。
entries.en: When the Wei general Li Wunu raided Hanzhong, Mao was ordered west to attack him.
entries.literal: When Wei general Li Wunu raided Hanzhong, Mao received orders for a western campaign.

entries.zh: 魏軍退，還爲鎮南司馬，帶臨湘令。
entries.en: After the Wei withdrew he became Pacify the South major, also serving as magistrate of Linxiang.
entries.literal: The Wei army withdrew; he returned as Pacify the South Major, concurrently holding the magistracy of Linxiang.

entries.zh: 入爲越騎校尉。
entries.en: He then entered court as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 魏寇兗州，茂時以寧朔將軍長史鎮援北境，入爲前軍將軍江夏王司馬。
entries.en: When Wei struck Yanzhou, Mao was chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the North on the northern frontier; he then entered court as major to the Front Army General and Prince of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: When Wei raided Yanzhou, Mao at the time was chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the North, garrisoning the northern border in relief; he entered court as Front Army General's major to the Prince of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 又遷寧朔將軍、江夏內史。
entries.en: He was again made General Who Pacifies the North and interior administrator of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 建武初，魏圍司州，茂以郢州之師救焉。
entries.en: Early in Jianwu the Wei besieged Sizhou, and Mao led Yingzhou troops to its relief.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Wei besieged Sizhou; Mao led the Yingzhou army to relieve it.

entries.zh: 高祖率衆先登賢首山，魏將王肅、劉昶來戰，茂從高祖拒之，大破肅等。
entries.en: Gaozu led the army up Xianshou Mountain first; when Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang attacked, Mao followed Gaozu and routed them.
entries.literal: Gaozu led the host first to mount Xianshou; Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang came to give battle, and Mao followed Gaozu to resist them, greatly defeating Su and the rest.

entries.zh: 魏軍退，茂還郢，仍遷輔國長史、襄陽太守。
entries.en: The Wei withdrew; Mao returned to Ying and was made Support-the-State chief clerk and administrator of Xiangyang.
