entries.literal: The Wei army withdrew; Mao returned to Ying and was then transferred to Support-the-State chief clerk and Administrator of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 高祖義師起，茂私於張弘策，勸高祖迎和帝，高祖以爲不然，語在《高祖紀》。
entries.en: When Gaozu raised the righteous army, Mao privately urged Zhang Hongce to have Gaozu welcome Emperor He; Gaozu disagreed, as told in the Annals of Gaozu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army rose, Mao privately told Zhang Hongce to urge Gaozu to welcome Emperor He; Gaozu thought otherwise—the account is in the Annals of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖發雍部，每遣茂爲前驅。
entries.en: Whenever Gaozu marched out of Yong, he sent Mao ahead as vanguard.
entries.literal: When Gaozu launched from the Yong region, each time he sent Mao as vanguard.

entries.zh: 師次郢城，茂進平加湖，破光子衿、吳子陽等，斬馘萬計，還獻捷于漢川。
entries.en: When the army reached Yingcheng, Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guang Ziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.
entries.literal: When the army halted at Ying city, Mao advanced and pacified Jiahu, defeated Guang Ziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, and decapitations numbered in the tens of thousands; he returned and presented the victory at Hanchuan.

entries.zh: 郢、魯旣平，從高祖東下，復爲軍鋒。
entries.en: Once Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed Gaozu east and again led the van.
entries.literal: After Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed Gaozu east and again served as the army's spearhead.

entries.zh: 師次秣陵，東昏遣大將王珍國，盛兵朱雀門，衆號二十萬，度航請戰。
entries.en: At Moling, Dong Hun sent Grand General Wang Zhenguo with a host said to number two hundred thousand at Zhuque Gate; they crossed the floating bridge and offered battle.
entries.literal: When the army reached Moling, Dong Hun sent Grand General Wang Zhenguo, who massed troops at Zhuque Gate; the host was said to number two hundred thousand, and they crossed the floating bridge to request battle.

entries.zh: 茂與曹景宗等會擊，大破之。
entries.en: Mao joined Cao Jingzong and others in a combined strike and routed them.
entries.literal: Mao joined Cao Jingzong and others in the attack and greatly defeated them.

entries.zh: 縱兵追奔，積屍與航欄等，其赴淮死者，不可勝算。
entries.en: He drove the pursuit until corpses stood level with the bridge rails; the dead in the Huai were beyond counting.
entries.literal: He released troops in pursuit; corpses piled level with the bridge railings, and those who drowned in the Huai were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 長驅至宣陽門。
entries.en: The army swept on to Xuanyang Gate.
entries.literal: They drove in long columns to Xuanyang Gate.

entries.zh: 建康城平，以茂爲護軍將軍，俄遷侍中、領軍將軍。
entries.en: After Jiankang fell, Mao was made Guard Army General, then soon Palace Attendant and Army Inspector General.
entries.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Mao was made Guard Army General; soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Army Inspector General.

entries.zh: 羣盜之燒神虎門也，茂率所領到東掖門應赴，爲盜所射，茂躍馬而進，羣盜反走。
entries.en: When bandits set fire to Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his men to answer the alarm at the East Side Gate. Though struck by an arrow, he spurred his horse forward, and the bandits turned and fled.
entries.literal: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his command to the East Side Gate to answer the alarm; shot by bandits, he leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.

entries.zh: 茂以不能式遏姦盜，自表解職，優詔不許。
entries.en: Unable to stop the outlaws, Mao asked to resign; a gracious edict refused.
entries.literal: Because he could not restrain the wicked bandits, Mao memorialized to resign; a gracious edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 加鎮軍將軍，封望蔡縣公，邑二千三百戶。
entries.en: He was also made General Who Guards the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.
entries.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Guards the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.

entries.zh: 是歲，江州刺史陳伯之舉兵叛，茂出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督江州諸軍事、征南將軍、江州刺史，給鼓吹一部，南討伯之。
entries.en: That year Chen Bozhi rebelled as Jiangzhou inspector; Mao went out with staff insignia as Scattered Cavalry Attendant, area commander, Pacify the South General, and Jiangzhou inspector, with drums and pipes, to attack him.
entries.literal: That year Jiangzhou Inspector Chen Bozhi raised troops in rebellion; Mao went out as Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Area Commander of Jiangzhou military affairs, Pacify the South General, and Jiangzhou Inspector, granted one suite of drums and pipes, and marched south to attack Bozhi.

entries.zh: 伯之奔于魏。
entries.en: Bozhi fled to Wei.
entries.literal: Bozhi fled to Wei.

entries.zh: 時九江新罹軍寇，民思反業，茂務農省役，百姓安之。
entries.en: Jiujiang had just been ravaged by war and the people wanted to farm again; Mao pushed farming and cut levies, and the region grew calm.
entries.literal: At the time Jiujiang had newly suffered military disaster and the people longed to return to their livelihoods; Mao devoted himself to farming and reducing corvee, and the common people were at peace.

entries.zh: 四年，魏侵漢中，茂受詔西討，魏乃班師。
entries.en: In year four Wei invaded Hanzhong; Mao was ordered west, and the Wei army withdrew.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Wei invaded Hanzhong; Mao received orders for a western campaign, and Wei then withdrew its army.

entries.zh: 六年，遷尚書右僕射，常侍如故。
entries.en: In year six he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing while keeping his Palace Attendant post.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, his Palace Attendant post remaining as before.

entries.zh: 固辭不拜，改授侍中、中衛將軍，領太子詹事。
entries.en: He firmly declined; the appointment was changed to Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and Crown Prince Steward.
entries.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept; he was instead appointed Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and concurrent Crown Prince Steward.

entries.zh: 七年，拜車騎將軍，太子詹事如故。
entries.en: In year seven he was made Chariots and Cavalry General, still Crown Prince Steward.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Chariots and Cavalry General, Crown Prince Steward remaining as before.

entries.zh: 八年，以本號開府儀同三司、丹陽尹，侍中如故。
entries.en: In year eight he kept his title but received open office equal to the Three Excellencies and became Danyang intendant, remaining Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, under his original title, he received Open Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies and became Danyang Intendant, Palace Attendant as before.

entries.zh: 時天下無事，高祖方信仗文雅，茂心頗怏怏，侍宴醉後，每見言色，高祖常宥而不之責也。
entries.en: The realm was at peace and Gaozu favored literary men; Mao was ill at ease, and after banquets, drunk, he often showed it in face and speech—yet Gaozu always forgave him.
entries.literal: At the time the realm was at peace and Gaozu was just then trusting literary elegance; Mao's heart was rather displeased, and after feasts when drunk he often showed it in words and countenance—yet Gaozu always pardoned him without blame.

entries.zh: 十一年，進位司空，侍中、尹如故。
entries.en: In year eleven he was promoted to Minister of Works, keeping Palace Attendant and the intendant post.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced to Minister of Works, Palace Attendant and Intendant as before.

entries.zh: 茂辭京尹，改領中權將軍。
entries.en: Mao declined the capital intendant post and took the concurrent Central Authority Generalship instead.
entries.literal: Mao declined the Capital Intendant post and was instead made concurrent Central Authority General.

entries.zh: 初，茂以元勳，高祖賜以鐘磬之樂。
entries.en: Earlier, as a founding merit-holder, Mao had been granted bells and chimes from Gaozu.
entries.literal: Earlier, because Mao was a founding merit-holder, Gaozu had granted him the music of bells and chimes.

entries.zh: 茂在江州，夢鐘磬在格，無故自墮，心惡之。
entries.en: In Jiangzhou he dreamed the bells and chimes on their stand fell for no reason, and he took it ill.
entries.literal: While Mao was in Jiangzhou, he dreamed that the bells and chimes on their rack fell for no reason; his heart was troubled.

entries.zh: 及覺，命奏樂。
entries.en: When he woke he ordered the music played.
entries.literal: On waking he ordered the music performed.

entries.zh: 旣成列，鐘磬在格，果無故編皆絕，墮地。
entries.en: When the musicians were in place, every cord on the bells and chimes broke without cause and they crashed to the floor.
entries.literal: When the array was complete, the bells and chimes on the rack indeed, for no reason, had all their cords break and fell to the ground.

entries.zh: 茂謂長史江詮曰：「此樂，天子所以惠勞臣也。
entries.en: Mao told Chief Clerk Jiang Quan, "This music is what the Son of Heaven grants to reward his ministers.
entries.literal: Mao said to Chief Clerk Jiang Quan: "This music is what the Son of Heaven uses to grace and comfort his ministers.

entries.zh: 樂旣極矣，能無憂乎！」
entries.en: When music has reached its limit, can there be no foreboding!"
entries.literal: When music reaches its utmost—can there be no worry!"

entries.zh: 俄而病，少日卒。
entries.en: Soon after he fell ill and died within days.
entries.literal: Soon after he fell ill, and within a few days died.

entries.zh: 茂性寬厚，居官雖無譽，亦爲吏民所安。
entries.en: By nature generous and easy, he won little fame in office, yet officials and people alike trusted him.
entries.literal: Mao was generous and forbearing by nature; though in office he won no special praise, officials and commoners alike were at ease with him.

entries.zh: 居處方正，在一室衣冠儼然，雖僕妾莫見其惰容。
entries.en: At home he kept himself square; even alone in one room his dress was formal, and servants never saw him look lax.
entries.literal: In his dwelling he was upright: cap and robes dignified even in a single room, and even concubines never saw him slack in appearance.

entries.zh: 姿表瓖麗，鬚眉如畫。
entries.en: He was splendid in bearing, with beard and brows like painted lines.
entries.literal: His bearing was splendid and fine; beard and brows were like painted.

entries.zh: 出入朝會，每爲衆所瞻望。
entries.en: Whenever he attended court, all eyes followed him.
entries.literal: Entering and leaving court assemblies, each time he was gazed upon by the multitude.

entries.zh: 明年，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、開府同三司之儀、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史。
entries.en: The next year he went out with staff insignia as Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General with open office equal to the Three Excellencies, area commander, and Jiangzhou inspector.
entries.literal: The next year he went out as Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General, Open Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, Area Commander of Jiangzhou military affairs, and Jiangzhou Inspector.

entries.zh: 視事三年，薨于州，時年六十。
entries.en: After three years in office he died in the province, aged sixty.
entries.literal: He administered affairs three years and died in the province at age sixty.

entries.zh: 高祖甚悼惜之，賻錢三十萬，布三百匹。
entries.en: Gaozu mourned him deeply and granted three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth for the funeral.
entries.literal: Gaozu deeply mourned him, granting funeral money of three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「旌德紀勳，哲王令軌；
entries.en: An edict said, "To honor virtue and record merit is the enlightened king's true measure;
entries.literal: An edict said: "To honor virtue and record merit is the enlightened king's excellent standard;

entries.zh: 念終追遠，前典明誥。
entries.en: to remember the dead and reach back to the ancestors is the clear charge of former canons.
entries.literal: to think of the end and pursue the distant is the former canon's clear charge.

entries.zh: 故使持節、散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史茂，識度淹廣，器宇凝正。
entries.en: The late Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General, Open Office Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Jiangzhou Inspector Mao was broad in judgment and firm in bearing.
entries.literal: The late Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General, Open Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, and Jiangzhou Inspector Mao had discernment broad and deep and bearing firm and upright.

entries.zh: 爰初草昧，盡誠宣力，綢繆休戚，契闊屯夷。
entries.en: From the first days of hardship he gave loyal service, sharing joy and sorrow and every trial.
entries.literal: From the first in hardship and obscurity he devoted loyalty and proclaimed his effort, binding himself in joy and sorrow and sharing ordeals in difficulty.

entries.zh: 方賴謀猷，永隆朝寄；
entries.en: We meant to rely on his counsel and long entrust him with the court;
entries.literal: We were about to rely on his strategies and forever exalt the court's trust;

entries.zh: 奄至薨殞，朕用慟于厥心。
entries.en: yet suddenly he died, and Our heart is stricken.
entries.literal: suddenly he died, and We are grieved in Our heart.

entries.zh: 宜增禮數，式昭盛烈。
entries.en: His rites should be raised to show forth his great merit.
entries.literal: It is fitting to increase the rites and manifest his splendid merit.

entries.zh: 可贈侍中、太尉，加班劍二十人，鼓吹一部。
entries.en: Let him be granted posthumously Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with twenty Office Swords and one suite of drums and pipes.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with twenty Office Swords and one suite of drums and pipes.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠烈。」
entries.en: Posthumous name Loyal and Ardent."
entries.literal: Posthumous name Loyal and Ardent."

entries.zh: 建武二年，魏主托跋宏寇赭陽，景宗爲偏將，每衝堅陷陣，輒有斬獲，以勳除遊擊將軍。
entries.en: In Jianwu year two Tuoba Hong of Wei raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a flank commander, broke the line each time he charged, and was made Guerrilla General for merit.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei ruler Tuoba Hong raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a supporting general and each charge broke the enemy line, with beheadings each time; by merit he was made Guerrilla General.

entries.zh: 四年，太尉陳顯達督衆軍北圍馬圈，景宗從之，以甲士二千設伏，破魏援托跋英四萬人。
entries.en: In year four Grand Commandant Chen Xianda besieged Maquan in the north; Jingzong followed with two thousand armored men in ambush and routed forty thousand Wei troops under Tuoba Ying.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Grand Commandant Chen Xianda commanded the armies north to besiege Maquan; Jingzong followed him and, with two thousand armored men, set an ambush and defeated Wei relief under Tuoba Ying—forty thousand men.

entries.zh: 及剋馬圈，顯達論功，以景宗爲後，景宗退無怨言。
entries.en: When Maquan fell, Xianda ranked the merit and put Jingzong last; Jingzong withdrew without a word.
entries.literal: When Maquan was taken, Xianda assessed merit and ranked Jingzong last; Jingzong withdrew without complaint.

entries.zh: 魏主率衆大至，顯達宵奔，景宗導入山道，故顯達父子獲全。
entries.en: The Wei ruler came in force; Xianda fled by night, and Jingzong led him through the mountains, so Xianda and his son escaped whole.
entries.literal: The Wei ruler led a great army up; Xianda fled by night, and Jingzong guided him into mountain paths—therefore Xianda and his son were wholly saved.

entries.zh: 五年，高祖爲雍州刺史，景宗深自結附，數請高祖臨其宅。
entries.en: In year five Gaozu was inspector of Yongzhou; Jingzong courted him closely and often asked him to his house.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Gaozu was Yongzhou Inspector; Jingzong attached himself deeply and repeatedly invited Gaozu to his residence.

entries.zh: 時天下方亂，高祖亦厚加意焉。
entries.en: The realm was in turmoil, and Gaozu in turn treated him generously.
entries.literal: At the time the realm was in disorder, and Gaozu also greatly favored him.

entries.zh: 永元初，表爲冠軍將軍、竟陵太守。
entries.en: At the start of Yongyuan he was recommended as Champion General and administrator of Jingling.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was memorialized as Champion General and Administrator of Jingling.

entries.zh: 及義師起，景宗聚衆，遣親人杜思沖勸先迎南康王於襄陽卽帝位，然後出師，爲萬全計。
entries.en: When the righteous army rose, Jingzong mustered troops and sent his kinsman Du Sichong to urge welcoming the Prince of Nankang at Xiangyang as emperor before marching— a plan for perfect safety.
entries.literal: When the righteous army rose, Jingzong gathered troops and sent his kinsman Du Sichong to urge that they first welcome the Prince of Nankang at Xiangyang to ascend the throne and then march— a plan for complete security.

entries.zh: 高祖不從，語在《高祖紀》。
entries.en: Gaozu refused, as told in the Annals of Gaozu.
entries.literal: Gaozu did not follow—the account is in the Annals of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖至竟陵，以景宗與冠軍將軍王茂濟江，圍郢城，自二月至於七月，城乃降。
entries.en: At Jingling Gaozu sent Jingzong and Champion General Wang Mao across the river to besiege Ying; from the second month to the seventh month the city surrendered.
entries.literal: When Gaozu reached Jingling, he made Jingzong and Champion General Wang Mao cross the river and besiege Ying city; from the second month to the seventh the city then surrendered.

entries.zh: 復帥衆前驅至南州，領馬步軍取建康。
entries.en: He again led the van to Nanzhou and commanded horse and foot against Jiankang.
entries.literal: He again led troops as vanguard to Nanzhou and commanded horse and foot to take Jiankang.

entries.zh: 道次江寧，東昏將李居士以重兵屯新亭，是日選精騎一千至江寧行頓，景宗始至，安營未立；
entries.en: At Jiangning, Dong Hun's general Li Jushi held Xinting with a heavy force; that day he sent a thousand picked horsemen to Jingzong's halt—Jingzong had just arrived and his camp was not yet pitched;
entries.literal: Passing Jiangning, Dong Hun's general Li Jushi held Xinting with heavy troops; that day he selected a thousand elite cavalry to Jiangning marching halt—Jingzong had just arrived and his camp was not yet set;

entries.zh: 且師行日久，器甲穿弊，居士望而輕之，因鼓噪前薄景宗。
entries.en: and the column had marched long, its arms in tatters; Jushi saw this, despised them, and charged with drums and shouts straight at Jingzong.
entries.literal: moreover the army had marched long and weapons and armor were worn through; Jushi seeing this despised them and therefore beat drums, clamored, and pressed forward close on Jingzong.

entries.zh: 景宗被甲馳戰，短兵裁接，居士棄甲奔走，景宗皆獲之，因鼓而前，徑至皁莢橋築壘。
entries.en: Jingzong armored and rode to meet them; in close fight Jushi threw off his armor and ran; Jingzong took them all, drummed forward, and built a rampart at Zaojia Bridge.
entries.literal: Jingzong donned armor and galloped to battle; in close combat they had barely joined when Jushi abandoned his armor and fled; Jingzong captured them all, then drummed forward and went straight to Zaojia Bridge to build a rampart.

entries.zh: 景宗又與王茂、呂僧珍掎角，破王珍國於大航。
entries.en: Jingzong again joined Wang Mao and Lu Sengzhen in a pincer and defeated Wang Zhenguo at the Great Floating Bridge.
entries.literal: Jingzong again joined Wang Mao and Lu Sengzhen in a pincer attack and defeated Wang Zhenguo at the Great Floating Bridge.

entries.zh: 茂衝其中堅，應時而陷，景宗縱兵乘之。
entries.en: Mao broke the enemy center and it collapsed at once; Jingzong drove the troops to press the rout.
entries.literal: Mao charged the hard center and it fell at once; Jingzong released troops to exploit the victory.

entries.zh: 景宗軍士皆桀黠無賴，御道左右，莫非富室，抄掠財物，略奪子女，景宗不能禁。
entries.en: Jingzong's men were violent and lawless; along the imperial way every house was rich, and they plundered goods and seized women and children—Jingzong could not stop them.
entries.literal: Jingzong's soldiers were all fierce and unbridled ruffians; along the imperial avenue, right and left, there were none but wealthy houses—they looted goods and seized women and children, and Jingzong could not forbid it.

entries.zh: 及高祖入頓新城，嚴申號令，然後稍息。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered and encamped at Xincheng, he enforced orders strictly, and only then did the turmoil subside.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered and encamped at Xincheng, he strictly enforced orders, and only then did things gradually quiet.

entries.zh: 復與衆軍長圍六門。
entries.en: He again joined the armies in a long siege of the Six Gates.
entries.literal: He again joined the massed armies in a long siege of the Six Gates.

entries.zh: 城平，拜散騎常侍、右衛將軍，封湘西縣侯，食邑一千六百戶。
entries.en: When the city fell, he was made Regular Attendant and Right Guard General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangxi with a fief of sixteen hundred households.
entries.literal: When the city fell, Jingzong was appointed Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangxi with a fief of one thousand six hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍遷持節、都督郢司二州諸軍事、左將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: He was then made Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of Ying and Si provinces, Left General, and inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ying and Si provinces, Left General, and Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 天監元年，進號平西將軍，改封竟陵縣侯。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjian he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingling.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Jingling.

entries.zh: 景宗在州，鬻貨聚斂。
entries.en: While holding the province, Jingzong trafficked in goods and amassed wealth.
entries.literal: While Jingzong held the province, he trafficked in goods and amassed wealth.

entries.zh: 於城南起宅，長堤以東，夏口以北，開街列門，東西數里，而部曲殘橫，民頗厭之。
entries.en: South of the city he built a mansion; east of the Long Embankment and north of Xiakou he laid out streets and gates for miles east and west, while his retainers ran wild—the people deeply resented it.
entries.literal: South of the city he built a mansion; east of the Long Embankment and north of Xiakou he opened streets and set gates for several li east and west, while his retainers were brutal and overbearing—the people greatly resented it.

entries.zh: 二年十月，魏寇司州，圍刺史蔡道恭。
entries.en: In the tenth month of year 2, Wei raided Si province and besieged the inspector Cai Daogong.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, Wei raided Si province and besieged Inspector Cai Daogong.

entries.zh: 時魏攻日苦，城中負板而汲，景宗望門不出，但耀軍遊獵而已。
entries.en: As the Wei assault grew harsher by the day, people in the city drew water under shield; Jingzong watched from the gate and would not emerge, parading his troops in hunts alone.
entries.literal: As Wei's assault grew daily harsher, the cityfolk carried boards on their backs to draw water; Jingzong watched from the gate and would not go out, but only displayed his troops in hunts.

entries.zh: 及司州城陷，爲御史中丞任昉所奏。
entries.en: When Si province fell, Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang impeached him.
entries.literal: When Si province's city fell, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang.

entries.zh: 高祖以功臣寢而不治，徵爲護軍。
entries.en: Because Jingzong was a meritorious minister, Gaozu shelved the case without punishing him and summoned him to serve as Protector of the Army.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because he was a meritorious minister who had grown lax and gone unpunished, summoned him to be Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 旣至，復拜散騎常侍、右衛將軍。
entries.en: On arrival he was again made Regular Attendant and Right Guard General.
entries.literal: Once he arrived, he was again appointed Regular Attendant and Right Guard General.

entries.zh: 五年，魏托跋英寇鐘離，圍徐州刺史昌義之。
entries.en: In year 5, Tuoba Ying of Wei raided Zhongli and besieged Xuzhou inspector Chang Yizhi.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Tuoba Ying of Wei raided Zhongli and besieged Xuzhou Inspector Chang Yizhi.

entries.zh: 高祖詔景宗督衆軍援義之，豫州刺史韋叡亦預焉，而受景宗節度。
entries.en: Gaozu ordered Jingzong to command the armies to relieve Yizhi; Yuzhou inspector Wei Rui joined as well, under Jingzong's command.
entries.literal: Gaozu ordered Jingzong to command the massed armies to relieve Yizhi; Yuzhou Inspector Wei Rui also took part, but was placed under Jingzong's command.

entries.zh: 詔景宗頓道人洲，待衆軍齊集俱進。
entries.en: He ordered Jingzong to encamp at Daoren Isle and wait for the armies to gather before advancing together.
entries.literal: He ordered Jingzong to encamp at Daoren Isle and wait until all the armies had gathered to advance together.

entries.zh: 景宗固啓，求先據邵陽洲尾，高祖不聽。
entries.en: Jingzong repeatedly petitioned to seize the end of Shaoyang Isle first; Gaozu refused.
entries.literal: Jingzong repeatedly memorialized, asking to seize the tail of Shaoyang Isle first; Gaozu would not listen.

entries.zh: 景宗欲專其功，乃違詔而進，值暴風卒起，頗有渰溺，復還守先頓。
entries.en: Wishing to keep the glory for himself, Jingzong disobeyed the edict and advanced; a sudden storm drowned many, and he fell back to his former camp.
entries.literal: Jingzong wished to monopolize the merit, so he disobeyed the edict and advanced; a sudden storm arose and many were drowned, and he returned to hold his former camp.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，曰：「此所以破賊也。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard, he said, "This is how we break the enemy.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard of it, he said: "This is how the enemy will be broken.

entries.zh: 景宗不進，蓋天意乎！
entries.en: Jingzong holding back—surely that is Heaven's will!
entries.literal: If Jingzong does not advance, is it not Heaven's will!

entries.zh: 若孤軍獨往，城不時立，必見狼狽。
entries.en: Had he marched alone, the fort would not have risen in time and the army would have come to grief.
entries.literal: If a lone army went alone, the ramparts would not be raised in time and one would surely be reduced to disarray.

entries.zh: 今得待衆軍同進，始大捷矣。」
entries.en: Now we can wait for every army to advance together, and the great victory will come."
entries.literal: Now that all the armies may advance together, there will truly be a great victory."

entries.zh: 及韋叡至，與景宗進頓邵陽洲，立壘去魏城百餘步。
entries.en: When Wei Rui arrived, he and Jingzong advanced to Shaoyang Isle and built ramparts a little over a hundred paces from the Wei city.
entries.literal: When Wei Rui arrived, he and Jingzong advanced and encamped at Shaoyang Isle, building ramparts within a hundred-odd paces of the Wei city.

entries.zh: 魏連戰不能却，殺傷者十二三，自是魏軍不敢逼。
entries.en: Wei attacked again and again but could not drive them back; casualties ran to two or three in ten, and thereafter the Wei army did not dare close in.
entries.literal: Wei fought repeatedly but could not drive them off; those killed and wounded were two or three in ten, and from then on the Wei army did not dare press close.

entries.zh: 景宗等器甲精新，軍儀甚盛，魏人望之奪氣。
entries.en: Jingzong and the rest had bright new arms and armor and a splendid array; the Wei troops looked on and lost heart.
entries.literal: Jingzong and the others had armor and weapons fresh and fine, and their military array was very grand; the Wei men gazed upon them and lost heart.

entries.zh: 魏大將楊大眼對橋北岸立城，以通糧運，每牧人過岸伐芻槁，皆爲大眼所略。
entries.en: Wei's great general Yang Dayan built a city on the north bank opposite the bridge to keep supplies moving; whenever herders crossed to cut fodder, Dayan seized them.
entries.literal: Wei's great general Yang Dayan built a city on the north bank opposite the bridge to keep grain transport open; whenever herders crossed the bank to cut fodder, Dayan seized them all.

entries.zh: 景宗乃募勇敢士千餘人，徑渡大眼城南數里築壘，親自舉築。
entries.en: Jingzong then recruited more than a thousand brave men, crossed several li south of Dayan's city, and built a rampart, piling earth with his own hands.
entries.literal: Jingzong then recruited more than a thousand brave men, crossed straight over several li south of Dayan's city, and built a rampart, raising the earthworks himself.

entries.zh: 大眼率衆來攻，景宗與戰破之，因得壘成。
entries.en: Dayan led his troops to attack; Jingzong fought and broke him, and the rampart was finished.
entries.literal: Dayan led his host to attack; Jingzong fought and defeated him, and so the rampart was completed.

entries.zh: 使別將趙草守之，因謂爲趙草城，是後恣芻牧焉。
entries.en: He left the separate commander Zhao Cao to hold it, and the place was called Fort Zhao Cao; thereafter they grazed fodder freely.
entries.literal: He sent the separate commander Zhao Cao to hold it, and therefore called it Fort Zhao Cao; thereafter they grazed fodder at will.

entries.zh: 大眼時遣抄掠，輒反爲趙草所獲。
entries.en: Whenever Dayan sent raiders, Zhao Cao captured them instead.
entries.literal: Whenever Dayan sent parties to raid, they were in turn captured by Zhao Cao.

entries.zh: 先是，高祖詔景宗等逆裝高艦，使與魏橋等，爲火攻計。
entries.en: Earlier Gaozu had ordered Jingzong and the others to fit out tall warships in advance, level with the Wei bridges, for a fire attack.
entries.literal: Earlier, Gaozu had ordered Jingzong and the others to fit out tall warships in advance, to match the Wei bridges in height, for a fire-attack plan.

entries.zh: 令景宗與叡各攻一橋，叡攻其南，景宗攻其北。
entries.en: He ordered Jingzong and Rui each to take one bridge—Rui the south, Jingzong the north.
entries.literal: He ordered Jingzong and Rui each to attack one bridge—Rui the south, Jingzong the north.

entries.zh: 六年三月，春水生，淮水暴長六七尺。
entries.en: In the third month of year 6 the spring flood came and the Huai rose six or seven feet overnight.
entries.literal: In the third month of the sixth year the spring waters rose and the Huai surged six or seven feet.

entries.zh: 叡遣所督將馮道根、李文釗、裴邃、韋寂等乘艦登岸，擊魏洲上軍盡殪。
entries.en: Rui sent Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and other generals under his command to land from the ships and slaughter the Wei troops on the isle.
entries.literal: Rui sent the generals under his command—Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and others—to board the warships, land, and annihilate the Wei troops on the isle.

entries.zh: 景宗因使衆軍皆鼓噪亂登諸城，呼聲震天地，大眼於西岸燒營，英自東岸棄城走。
entries.en: Jingzong then had every army drum and shout and swarm the walls; the roar shook heaven and earth; Dayan burned his camp on the west bank, and Ying abandoned his city and fled from the east.
entries.literal: Jingzong then had all the armies drum and shout and scramble up the walls in disorder; the clamor shook heaven and earth; Dayan burned his camp on the west bank, and Ying abandoned his city and fled from the east bank.

entries.zh: 諸壘相次土崩，悉棄其器甲，爭投水死，淮水爲之不流。
entries.en: Rampart after rampart crumbled; all cast off arms and armor and threw themselves into the water to die—the Huai was so choked it would not flow.
entries.literal: Rampart after rampart collapsed like earthworks; all cast away arms and armor and strove to throw themselves into the water and die—the Huai was choked so that it would not flow.

entries.zh: 景宗令軍主馬廣躡大眼至濊水上，四十餘里，伏屍相枕。
entries.en: Jingzong ordered the army commander Ma Guang to pursue Dayan to the Huishui for more than forty li; the dead lay heaped along the way.
entries.literal: Jingzong ordered the army commander Ma Guang to pursue Dayan to the Huishui River for more than forty li; corpses lay pillow to pillow.

entries.zh: 義之出逐英至洛口，英以匹馬入梁城。
entries.en: Yizhi pursued Ying to Luokou; Ying entered Liang city on a single horse.
entries.literal: Yizhi went out in pursuit of Ying to Luokou; Ying entered Liang city on a single horse.

entries.zh: 緣淮百餘里，屍骸枕藉，生擒五萬餘人，收其軍糧器械，積如山岳，牛馬驢騾，不可勝計。
entries.en: For more than a hundred li along the Huai the dead lay piled; more than fifty thousand were captured alive; grain and arms heaped like mountains; cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules beyond count.
entries.literal: For more than a hundred li along the Huai, corpses lay pillow to pillow; more than fifty thousand were taken alive; grain, weapons, and equipment were gathered in heaps like mountains; oxen, horses, donkeys, and mules were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 景宗乃搜軍所得生口萬餘人，馬千匹，遣獻捷，高祖詔還本軍，景宗振旅凱入，增封四百，並前爲二千戶，進爵爲公。
entries.en: Jingzong gathered more than ten thousand captives and a thousand horses from the army's takings and sent word of victory; Gaozu ordered him back to his command; Jingzong marched home in triumph, his fief was increased by four hundred households to two thousand in all, and he was advanced to duke.
entries.literal: Jingzong then searched out more than ten thousand captives and a thousand horses from what the army had taken, sent them to report victory, and Gaozu ordered him back to his original command; Jingzong led his troops home in triumph, his fief was increased by four hundred households to two thousand in all, and he was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 詔拜侍中、領軍將軍，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: By edict he was made Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with one set of martial pipes and drums.
entries.literal: By edict he was appointed Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with one set of martial pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 景宗爲人自恃尚勝，每作書，字有不解，不以問人，皆以意造焉。
entries.en: Jingzong was proud and always had to win; when he wrote, any character he did not know he would not ask about but invent as he saw fit.
entries.literal: Jingzong was by nature self-reliant and fond of outdoing others; whenever he wrote letters, if he did not understand a character he would not ask anyone, but invent it as he pleased.

entries.zh: 雖公卿無所推揖；
entries.en: He showed no deference even to dukes and ministers;
entries.literal: Though among dukes and ministers he showed no deference;

entries.zh: 惟韋叡年長，且州里勝流，特相敬重，同宴御筵，亦曲躬謙遜，高祖以此嘉之。
entries.en: only Wei Rui, who was older and a leading man of their district, he specially honored; at imperial banquets he bowed with humble courtesy as well—Gaozu praised him for it.
entries.literal: only Wei Rui was older and a leading figure of their native district, and he specially respected him; at banquets on the imperial mat he too bowed with humble courtesy—Gaozu praised him for this.

entries.zh: 景宗好內，妓妾至數百，窮極錦繡。
entries.en: Jingzong loved women; his concubines and singing girls numbered in the hundreds, and he exhausted every brocade and embroidery.
entries.literal: Jingzong was fond of women; his singing girls and concubines numbered in the hundreds, and he exhausted brocades and embroideries.

entries.zh: 性躁動，不能沈默，出行常欲褰車帷幔，左右輒諫以位望隆重，人所具瞻，不宜然。
entries.en: Restless by nature, he could not keep still; on the road he always wanted to throw back the carriage curtains, and his attendants would warn him that with his rank and dignity all eyes were on him—he should not.
entries.literal: By nature restless, he could not keep silent; when he went out he always wanted to lift the carriage curtains, and those at his side would remonstrate that his rank and standing were weighty and that all eyes were upon him—he ought not do so.

entries.zh: 景宗謂所親曰：「我昔在鄉里，騎快馬如龍，與年少輩數十騎，拓弓弦作霹靂聲，箭如餓鴟叫。
entries.en: Jingzong told his intimates: "Back home I rode a swift horse like a dragon, with several dozen young men at my side, drawing the bowstring till it thundered, arrows screaming like hungry kites.
entries.literal: Jingzong said to those close to him: "In the old days at home I rode a swift horse like a dragon, with several dozen young fellows, drawing the bowstring till it cracked like thunder, arrows shrieking like hungry kites.

entries.zh: 平澤中逐麞，數肋射之，渴飲其血，饑食其肉，甜如甘露漿。
entries.en: On the open marsh we chased deer; I shot them through the ribs again and again, drank their blood when thirsty, ate their flesh when hungry—sweet as nectar.
entries.literal: In the open marsh we chased deer; I shot them through the ribs several times, drank their blood when thirsty and ate their flesh when hungry—sweet as sweet dew.

entries.zh: 覺耳後風生，鼻頭出火，此樂使人忘死，不知老之將至。
entries.en: Wind rose behind my ears, fire seemed to burst from my nostrils—joy like that makes you forget death and never feel old age draw near.
entries.literal: I felt wind rise behind my ears and fire burst from my nostrils—such joy makes one forget death and not know that old age is coming.

entries.zh: 今來揚州作貴人，動轉不得，路行開車幔，小人輒言不可。
entries.en: Now I have come to Yangzhou to play the great man and cannot move; on the road I lift the carriage curtain and little men say I must not.
entries.literal: Now I have come to Yangzhou to be a great man and cannot stir; on the road I open the carriage curtains and petty men say I must not.

entries.zh: 閉置車中，如三日新婦。
entries.en: Shut in the carriage like a bride on her third day.
entries.literal: Shut up in the carriage like a bride of three days.

entries.zh: 遭此邑邑，使人無氣。」
entries.en: This suffocation steals a man's breath."
entries.literal: To suffer such vexation takes the breath from a man."

entries.zh: 爲人嗜酒好樂，臘月於宅中，使作野虖逐除，遍往人家乞酒食。
entries.en: He loved wine and music; in the twelfth month at his mansion he staged the wilderness howl for the year-end expulsion, going door to door begging wine and food.
entries.literal: He was by nature addicted to wine and fond of music; in the twelfth month at his mansion he had a wilderness howl performed for the year-end expulsion, going from house to house begging wine and food.

entries.zh: 本以爲戲，而部下多剽輕，因弄人婦女，奪人財貨。
entries.en: It was meant as sport, but many of his men were violent and took liberties with women and seized property.
entries.literal: He had meant it as sport, but many of his subordinates were violent and light-minded, and so molested other men's wives and seized people's goods.

entries.zh: 高祖頗知之，景宗乃止。
entries.en: Gaozu learned of it, and Jingzong then stopped.
entries.literal: Gaozu came to know of it fairly well, and Jingzong then stopped.

entries.zh: 高祖數讌見功臣，共道故舊，景宗醉後謬忘，或誤稱下官，高祖故縱之，以爲笑樂。
entries.en: Gaozu often feasted his merit-holders and talked of old times; drunk, Jingzong would forget himself and sometimes call himself "your servant"; Gaozu indulged it and laughed.
entries.literal: Gaozu often feasted the meritorious ministers and talked over old times together; after wine Jingzong would forget himself in error and sometimes wrongly call himself "your servant"; Gaozu deliberately indulged him and took it as laughter.

entries.zh: 高祖之臨雍州，問京兆人杜惲求州綱，惲舉慶遠。
entries.en: When Gaozu took Yongzhou, he asked Du Yun of Jingzhao for the province's leading men; Yun recommended Qingyuan.
entries.literal: When Gaozu came to Yongzhou, he asked the man of Jingzhao, Du Yun, for the province's leading men; Yun recommended Qingyuan.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「文和吾已知之，所問未知者耳。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "I already know Wenhe; I was asking about what I did not yet know."
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "I already know Wenhe; what I asked about was what I did not yet know."

entries.zh: 因辟別駕從事史。
entries.en: Thereupon he summoned him as aide-de-camp attendant.
entries.literal: Thereupon he summoned him as Aide-de-Camp Attendant.

entries.zh: 齊方多難，慶遠謂所親曰：「方今天下將亂，英雄必起，庇民定霸，其吾君乎？」
entries.en: Qi was then in turmoil; Qingyuan told his intimates, "The realm will soon fall into disorder; heroes are sure to rise—he who shelters the people and settles hegemony, is he not our lord?"
entries.literal: Qi was then beset by many troubles; Qingyuan said to those close to him: "The realm under heaven will soon fall into disorder; heroes are sure to rise—he who shelters the people and settles hegemony, is he not our lord?"

entries.zh: 因盡誠協贊。
entries.en: Thereupon he gave himself wholly to loyal support.
entries.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself fully in loyal support.

entries.zh: 及義兵起，慶遠常居帷幄爲謀主。
entries.en: When the righteous army rose, Qingyuan constantly stayed in the command tent as chief strategist.
entries.literal: When the righteous army rose, Qingyuan constantly remained within the command tent as chief strategist.

entries.zh: 霸府建，以爲太尉從事中郎。
entries.en: When the hegemon's administration was established, he was appointed Attending Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff.
entries.literal: When the hegemon's administration was established, he was made Attending Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，遷散騎常侍、右衛將軍，加征虜將軍，封重安侯，食邑千戶。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Qingyuan was made Regular Attendant and Right Guard General, additionally General Who Subdues Captives, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Qingyuan was transferred to Regular Attendant and Right Guard General, with the additional title General Who Subdues Captives, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 母憂去職，以本官起之，固辭不拜。
entries.en: He left office for his mother's mourning, was recalled to his former post, and firmly declined.
entries.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning, was recalled to his former post, and firmly declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 天監二年，遷中領軍，改封雲杜侯。
entries.en: In Tianjian year 2 he was made Commander of the Army and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yundu.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was transferred to Commander of the Army and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yundu.

entries.zh: 四年，出爲使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州諸軍事、征虜將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
entries.en: In year 4 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of Yong, Liang, and northern and southern Qin, General Who Subdues Captives, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Yong, Liang, and the northern and southern Qin provinces, General Who Subdues Captives, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖餞於新亭，謂曰：「卿衣錦還鄉，朕無西顧之憂矣。」
entries.en: Gaozu saw him off at Xinting and said, "You return home in brocade; I need no longer look west with worry."
entries.literal: Gaozu saw him off at Xinting and said: "You return home in brocade; I have no more worry for the west."

entries.zh: 中興元年，西臺選爲黃門郎，遷冠軍將軍、征東長史。
entries.en: In Zhongxing 1, the western court selected him as Yellow Gate Gentleman; he was transferred to Champion General and chief clerk of the General Who Campaigns East.
entries.literal: In Zhongxing 1, the western court selected him as Yellow Gate Gentleman; he was transferred to Champion General and chief clerk of the General Who Campaigns East.

entries.zh: 從軍東下，身先士卒。
entries.en: He accompanied the army eastward and personally went ahead of the officers and troops.
entries.literal: He accompanied the army eastward and personally went ahead of the officers and troops.

entries.zh: 高祖行營壘，見慶遠頓舍嚴整，每歎曰：「人人若是，吾又何憂。」
entries.en: When Gaozu inspected the camps and saw Qingyuan's quarters arranged in strict order, he often sighed, "If everyone were like this, what would I have to worry about?"
entries.literal: When Gaozu inspected the camps and saw Qingyuan's quarters arranged in strict order, he often sighed, "If everyone were like this, what would I have to worry about?"

entries.zh: 建康城平，入爲侍中，領前軍將軍，帶淮陵、齊昌二郡太守。
entries.en: After Jiankang was pacified, Qingyuan entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently General of the Front Army and administrator of Huailing and Qichang commanderies.
entries.literal: After Jiankang was pacified, Qingyuan entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently General of the Front Army and administrator of Huailing and Qichang commanderies.

entries.zh: 城內嘗夜失火，禁中驚懼，高祖時居宮中，悉斂諸鑰，問「柳侍中何在」。
entries.en: Once a fire broke out in the city at night and those inside the palace were alarmed. Gaozu was then living in the palace; he gathered all the keys and asked, "Where is Attendant Liu?"
entries.literal: Once a fire broke out in the city at night and those inside the palace were alarmed. Gaozu was then living in the palace; he gathered all the keys and asked, "Where is Attendant Liu?"

entries.zh: 慶遠至，悉付之。
entries.en: When Qingyuan arrived, Gaozu handed them all over to him.
entries.literal: When Qingyuan arrived, Gaozu handed them all over to him.

entries.zh: 其見任如此。
entries.en: Such was the trust placed in him.
entries.literal: Such was the trust placed in him.

entries.zh: 七年，徵爲護軍將軍，領太子庶子。
entries.en: In year 7 he was summoned to be Protector of the Army and concurrent steward of the crown prince.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned to be Protector of the Army and Concurrent Steward of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 未赴職，仍遷通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍，領右驍騎將軍。
entries.en: Before taking up the post he was transferred to Unhampered Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and concurrent General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: Before he took up the post he was transferred to Unhampered Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and Concurrent General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 至京都，值魏宿預城請降，受詔爲援，於是假節守淮陰。
entries.en: On reaching the capital, Wei's Suyu city asked to surrender; ordered to relieve it, he was given the staff pro tem to hold Huaiyin.
entries.literal: When he reached the capital, it happened that Wei's Suyu city asked to surrender; he received orders to go to its relief, and was given the staff pro tem to hold Huaiyin.

entries.zh: 魏軍退。
entries.en: The Wei army withdrew.
entries.literal: The Wei army withdrew.

entries.zh: 八年，還京師，遷散騎常侍、太子詹事、雍州大中正。
entries.en: In year 8 he returned to the capital and was made Regular Attendant, steward of the crown prince, and chief rectifier of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he returned to the capital and was transferred to Regular Attendant, Steward of the Crown Prince, and Chief Rectifier of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 十年，遷侍中、領軍將軍，給扶，幷鼓吹一部。
entries.en: In year 10 he was made Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with a cane and one set of martial pipes and drums.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with a cane and one set of martial pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 十二年，遷安北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
entries.en: In year 12 he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 慶遠重爲本州，頗厲清節，士庶懷之。
entries.en: Qingyuan again held his home province and was strict in integrity; officials and commoners cherished him.
entries.literal: Qingyuan again held his native province and was quite strict in integrity; scholars and commoners cherished him.

entries.zh: 明年春，卒，時年五十七。
entries.en: The next spring he died, aged fifty-seven.
entries.literal: The next spring he died, aged fifty-seven.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「念往篤終，前王令則；
entries.en: An edict said, "To honor the past and cherish the dead is the ancient kings' enduring rule;
entries.literal: Edict: "To recall the past and show depth at life's end is the former kings' settled norm;

entries.zh: 式隆寵數，列代恒規。
entries.en: to heighten favor and rank is the constant practice of every age.
entries.literal: to heighten favor and ranks is the constant practice of successive ages.

entries.zh: 使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、安北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、雲杜縣開國侯柳慶遠，器識淹曠，思懷通雅。
entries.en: Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of Yong, Liang, northern and southern Qin, Jingling in Yingzhou, and Suixiang in Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, inspector of Yongzhou, and founding marquis of Yundu, Liu Qingyuan—his talent and insight are broad, his mind humane and refined.
entries.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Yong, Liang, northern and southern Qin, Jingling in Yingzhou, and Suixiang in Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Marquis Who Founded the State of Yundu, Liu Qingyuan—his capacity and insight are broad and far-reaching, his thought humane and refined.

entries.zh: 爰初草昧，預屬經綸；
entries.en: From the first days of the founding struggle he shared in planning the enterprise;
entries.literal: From the first in the founding struggle he shared in planning the enterprise;

entries.zh: 遠自升平，契闊禁旅。
entries.en: from long service in peaceful times he was bound to the palace guard.
entries.literal: from distant days in the age of peace he was bound to service in the palace guard.

entries.zh: 重牧西籓，方弘治道，奄至殞喪，傷慟于懷。
entries.en: Again he governed the western marches and was about to spread good rule, when death came suddenly—grief wounds my breast.
entries.literal: Again he governed the western marches and was about to spread good rule, when suddenly death came—grief wounds my breast.

entries.zh: 宜追榮命，以彰茂勳。
entries.en: Let posthumous honors be granted to display his abundant merit.
entries.literal: He should receive posthumous honors to display his abundant merit.

entries.zh: 可贈侍中、中軍將軍、開府儀同三司，鼓吹、侯如故。
entries.en: Let him be posthumously made Palace Attendant, Central Army General, and Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes; martial pipes and drums and his marquisate remain as before.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, Central Army General, and Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes; martial pipes and drums and his marquisate are to remain as before.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠惠。
entries.en: Posthumous name Zhonghui, "Loyal and Kind."
entries.literal: Posthumous name Zhonghui.

entries.zh: 賻錢二十萬，布二百匹。」
entries.en: Funerary gift: two hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of cloth."
entries.literal: Funerary gift: two hundred thousand in cash and two hundred bolts of cloth."

entries.zh: 及喪還京師，高祖出臨哭。
entries.en: When the coffin returned to the capital, Gaozu went out in person to mourn.
entries.literal: When the coffin returned to the capital, Gaozu went out in person to mourn.

entries.zh: 子津嗣。
entries.en: His son Jin succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Jin succeeded.

entries.zh: 梁書卷第九 列傳第三
entries.en: Book of Liang, Volume Nine, Biographies, Third
entries.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 9, Biographies 3

entries.zh: 弘策與高祖年相輩，幼見親狎，恒隨高祖游處。
entries.en: Hongce was Gaozu's contemporary; as youths they were close, and Hongce was always at Gaozu's side.
entries.literal: Hongce was of an age with Gaozu; from youth they were intimate, and he constantly followed Gaozu in his comings and goings.

entries.zh: 每入室，常覺有雲煙氣，體輒肅然，弘策由此特敬高祖。
entries.en: Each time he stepped into a room he seemed to sense cloud and mist; his bearing turned grave, and from that he revered Gaozu the more.
entries.literal: Whenever he entered a room he would feel as though cloud and mist were present; his person would at once grow solemn, and from this Hongce came to hold Gaozu in special regard.

entries.zh: 建武末，弘策從高祖宿，酒酣，徙席星下，語及時事。
entries.en: Late in Jianwu, Hongce lodged with Gaozu; drunk, they shifted their seats beneath the stars and talked of the age.
entries.literal: At the end of Jianwu, Hongce kept overnight with Gaozu; when wine was deep they moved their mats under the stars and spoke of the times.

entries.zh: 弘策因問高祖曰：「緯象云何？
entries.en: Hongce asked Gaozu, "What do the omens say?
entries.literal: Hongce then asked Gaozu: "What do the celestial signs say?

entries.zh: 國家故當無恙？」
entries.en: Will the realm truly be safe?"
entries.literal: Will the state in fact be unharmed?"

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「其可言乎？」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Can such things be said aloud?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "Can that be spoken?"

entries.zh: 弘策因曰：「請言其兆。」
entries.en: Hongce said, "Then tell me the signs."
entries.literal: Hongce said: "Please speak the omens."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「漢北有失地氣，浙東有急兵祥。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "North of the Han the land will slip away; east of Zhe urgent armies will rise.
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "North of Han there is an omen of lost territory; east of Zhe there is an omen of urgent arms.

entries.zh: 今冬初，魏必動；
entries.en: Early this winter Wei will surely stir;
entries.literal: This coming early winter Wei is certain to move;

entries.zh: 若動則亡漢北。
entries.en: and if it moves, the north of Han is gone.
entries.literal: if it moves, the north of Han will be lost.

entries.zh: 帝今久疾，多異議，萬一伺釁，稽部且乘機而作，是亦無成，徒自驅除耳。
entries.en: The emperor has been ill long, and talk runs every way; if someone seizes the moment, Kuaiji may rise too—yet it will win nothing, only purge itself in vain.
entries.literal: The emperor is now long ill, and many dissenting voices are heard; should anyone seize the chance, the Kuaiji region too will rise—but it will accomplish nothing, only drive men to destroy one another.

entries.zh: 明年都邑有亂，死人過於亂麻，齊之歷數，自茲亡矣。
entries.en: Next year the capital will fall into chaos; corpses will outnumber knotted hemp; Qi's fate ends with this.
entries.literal: Next year the capital will know disorder; the dead will outnumber tangled hemp; Qi's allotted span ends here.

entries.zh: 梁、楚、漢當有英雄興。」
entries.en: In Liang, Chu, and Han heroes will rise."
entries.literal: Liang, Chu, and Han will see heroes rise."

entries.zh: 弘策曰：「英雄今何在？
entries.en: Hongce said, "Where is that hero now?
entries.literal: Hongce said: "Where is the hero now?

entries.zh: 爲已富貴，爲在草茅？」
entries.en: Already rich and honored, or still in the grass?"
entries.literal: Already in wealth and rank, or still in the thatched hut?"

entries.zh: 高祖笑曰：「光武有云：『安知非僕』。」
entries.en: Gaozu laughed. "Guangwu said, 'How do you know it is not me?'"
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "Guangwu once said, 'How do you know it is not I?'"

entries.zh: 弘策起曰：「今夜之言，是天意也。
entries.en: Hongce stood. "Tonight's speech is Heaven's decree.
entries.literal: Hongce rose and said: "Tonight's words are Heaven's will.

entries.zh: 請定君臣之分。」
entries.en: Let us settle lord and minister now."
entries.literal: Please fix lord and minister's roles."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「舅欲效鄧晨乎？」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "Uncle—do you mean to play Deng Chen?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said: "Uncle, do you wish to imitate Deng Chen?"

entries.zh: 是冬，魏軍寇新野，高祖將兵爲援，且受密旨，仍代曹虎爲雍州。
entries.en: That winter Wei struck Xinye; Gaozu marched to relieve it and, on secret orders, took Yongzhou in place of Cao Hu.
entries.literal: That winter Wei troops raided Xinye; Gaozu led an army in relief and, on a secret order, replaced Cao Hu as inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 弘策聞之心喜，謂高祖曰：「夜中之言，獨當驗矣。」
entries.en: Hongce was delighted and told Gaozu, "What we said that night is about to come true."
entries.literal: Hongce heard it with joy and told Gaozu: "The words of that night should alone be proved."

entries.zh: 高祖笑曰：「且勿多言。」
entries.en: Gaozu laughed. "Say no more—for now."
entries.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "For now, say no more."

entries.zh: 弘策從高祖西行，仍參帷幄，身親軍役，不憚辛苦。
entries.en: Hongce followed Gaozu west, served in the command tent, and shared the hardships of every campaign.
entries.literal: Hongce followed Gaozu west, still taking part in the command tent, personally sharing in campaigns and not shirking hardship.

entries.zh: 義師將起，高祖夜召弘策、呂僧珍入宅定議，旦乃發兵，以弘策爲輔國將軍、軍主，領萬人督後部軍事。
entries.en: As the righteous army gathered, Gaozu called Hongce and Lü Sengzhen to his house by night to settle the plan; at dawn he marched, making Hongce Supporting State general and army commander over ten thousand men in charge of the rear.
entries.literal: When the righteous army was about to rise, Gaozu at night summoned Hongce and Lü Sengzhen to his house to fix the plan; at dawn he sent out the troops, making Hongce Supporting State General and army commander, commanding ten thousand men to supervise rear-area military affairs.

entries.zh: 西臺建，爲步兵校尉，遷車騎諮議參軍。
entries.en: When the western headquarters was set up, he became colonel of foot soldiers, then cavalry and chariots advisory staff officer.
entries.literal: When the Western Headquarters was established, he was made Colonel of Foot Soldiers and transferred to Cavalry and Chariots Advisory Staff Officer.

entries.zh: 及郢城平，蕭穎達、楊公則諸將皆欲頓軍夏口，高祖以爲宜乘勢長驅，直指京邑，以計語弘策，弘策與高祖意合。
entries.en: After Ying fell, Xiao Yingda and Yang Gongze wanted to camp at Xiakou; Gaozu meant to drive the victory straight to the capital and told Hongce, who agreed.
entries.literal: When Ying city was pacified, Xiao Yingda, Yang Gongze, and the other generals all wished to halt the army at Xiakou; Gaozu held that they should press the advantage in a long drive straight at the capital, and he spoke the plan to Hongce—Hongce agreed with Gaozu.

entries.zh: 又訪寧遠將軍庾域，域又同。
entries.en: He also asked Pacify the Distant general Yu Yu, who agreed as well.
entries.literal: He also consulted Pacify the Distant General Yu Yu; Yu too agreed.
